````rust
 1: use std::error::Error;
 2: use std::fmt::{Display, Formatter};
 3: 
 4: /// Default finite reach of baked fixture light, measured in world units.
 5: ///
 6: /// Six units keeps ordinary 3.2--5.4 unit rooms illuminated while still
 7: /// reaching zero before distant fixtures can flatten a whole streamed scene.
 8: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS: f32 = 6.0;
 9: 
10: /// Physical sampling settings for one voxel-light bake.
11: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
12: pub struct VoxelLightingSettings {
13:     voxel_size_world_units: f32,
14:     max_range_world_units: f32,
15: }
16: 
17: impl VoxelLightingSettings {
18:     /// Creates validated settings. Both values are lengths in the same world
19:     /// coordinate system used by generated architecture and runtime lights.
20:     pub fn new(
21:         voxel_size_world_units: f32,
22:         max_range_world_units: f32,
23:     ) -> Result<Self, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings> {
24:         if !voxel_size_world_units.is_finite() || voxel_size_world_units <= 0.0 {
25:             return Err(InvalidVoxelLightingSettings::VoxelSize);
26:         }
27:         if !max_range_world_units.is_finite() || max_range_world_units <= 0.0 {
28:             return Err(InvalidVoxelLightingSettings::MaxRange);
29:         }
30:         Ok(Self {
31:             voxel_size_world_units,
32:             max_range_world_units,
33:         })
34:     }
35: 
36:     /// Uses the engine's ordinary finite fixture range with an exact scene
37:     /// voxel size supplied by the generation configuration.
38:     pub fn with_default_range(
39:         voxel_size_world_units: f32,
40:     ) -> Result<Self, InvalidVoxelLightingSettings> {
41:         Self::new(voxel_size_world_units, DEFAULT_MAX_LIGHT_RANGE_WORLD_UNITS)
42:     }
43: 
44:     pub fn voxel_size_world_units(self) -> f32 {
45:         self.voxel_size_world_units
46:     }
47: 
48:     pub fn max_range_world_units(self) -> f32 {
49:         self.max_range_world_units
50:     }
51: }
52: 
53: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
54: pub enum InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {
55:     VoxelSize,
56:     MaxRange,
57: }
58: 
59: impl Display for InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {
60:     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
61:         match self {
62:             Self::VoxelSize => {
63:                 formatter.write_str("voxel size must be finite and greater than zero")
64:             }
65:             Self::MaxRange => {
66:                 formatter.write_str("maximum light range must be finite and greater than zero")
67:             }
68:         }
69:     }
70: }
71: 
72: impl Error for InvalidVoxelLightingSettings {}
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/voxel_neighborhood.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
 2: 
 3: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 4: pub(crate) struct VoxelCoord {
 5:     pub(crate) x: usize,
 6:     pub(crate) y: usize,
 7:     pub(crate) z: usize,
 8: }
 9: 
10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
11: pub(crate) struct GridDimensions {
12:     pub(crate) width: usize,
13:     pub(crate) height: usize,
14:     pub(crate) depth: usize,
15: }
16: 
17: impl GridDimensions {
18:     pub(crate) fn of(grid: &VoxelGrid) -> Self {
19:         Self {
20:             width: grid.width(),
21:             height: grid.height(),
22:             depth: grid.depth(),
23:         }
24:     }
25: 
26:     pub(crate) fn volume(self) -> usize {
27:         self.width * self.height * self.depth
28:     }
29: 
30:     /// Matches `VoxelGrid`'s y-major, then z, then x storage order without
31:     /// exposing the entity's backing vectors to the use case.
32:     pub(crate) fn index(self, coord: VoxelCoord) -> usize {
33:         coord.y * (self.width * self.depth) + coord.z * self.width + coord.x
34:     }
35: }
36: 
37: pub(crate) fn for_each_voxel(dimensions: GridDimensions, mut visit: impl FnMut(VoxelCoord)) {
38:     for z in 0..dimensions.depth {
39:         for y in 0..dimensions.height {
40:             for x in 0..dimensions.width {
41:                 visit(VoxelCoord { x, y, z });
42:             }
43:         }
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// Visits the six face-sharing cells in a fixed order. The order makes the
48: /// implementation reproducible, while shortest integer distances make the
49: /// result independent of which equally short route was visited first.
50: pub(crate) fn for_each_face_neighbor(
51:     coord: VoxelCoord,
52:     dimensions: GridDimensions,
53:     mut visit: impl FnMut(VoxelCoord),
54: ) {
55:     if coord.x + 1 < dimensions.width {
56:         visit(VoxelCoord {
57:             x: coord.x + 1,
58:             ..coord
59:         });
60:     }
61:     if coord.x > 0 {
62:         visit(VoxelCoord {
63:             x: coord.x - 1,
64:             ..coord
65:         });
66:     }
67:     if coord.y + 1 < dimensions.height {
68:         visit(VoxelCoord {
69:             y: coord.y + 1,
70:             ..coord
71:         });
72:     }
73:     if coord.y > 0 {
74:         visit(VoxelCoord {
75:             y: coord.y - 1,
76:             ..coord
77:         });
78:     }
79:     if coord.z + 1 < dimensions.depth {
80:         visit(VoxelCoord {
81:             z: coord.z + 1,
82:             ..coord
83:         });
84:     }
85:     if coord.z > 0 {
86:         visit(VoxelCoord {
87:             z: coord.z - 1,
88:             ..coord
89:         });
90:     }
91: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/bake_voxel_lighting/world_space_attenuation.rs
````rust
 1: use super::exposed_emissive_faces::EmissionProfile;
 2: use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;
 3: 
 4: /// Adds one emission class after finite-range linear attenuation.
 5: ///
 6: /// `cell_offsets` accounts for the half-cell from an emitting face to its
 7: /// first air center. Air samples use 0.5. A solid receiver adds the second
 8: /// half-cell from its neighboring air center to the receiving face and uses
 9: /// 1.0. Those two halves make equal physical gaps agree at 0.1 and 0.2 unit
10: /// voxel sizes instead of differing by one resolution-dependent cell center.
11: pub(crate) fn accumulate_attenuated(
12:     accumulated: &mut [f32; 3],
13:     profile: EmissionProfile,
14:     distance_steps: u32,
15:     cell_offsets: f32,
16:     settings: VoxelLightingSettings,
17: ) {
18:     let distance_world = (distance_steps as f32 + cell_offsets) * settings.voxel_size_world_units();
19:     let remaining = (1.0 - distance_world / settings.max_range_world_units()).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
20:     for channel in 0..3 {
21:         accumulated[channel] += profile.rgb[channel] * remaining;
22:     }
23: }
24: 
25: pub(crate) fn pack_rgb(accumulated: [f32; 3]) -> [u8; 3] {
26:     accumulated.map(|channel| channel.round().clamp(0.0, 15.0) as u8)
27: }
28: 
29: pub(crate) fn pack_emission(rgb: [f32; 3]) -> [u8; 3] {
30:     pack_rgb(rgb)
31: }
````

````rust
 3: use super::propagate_through_air::{AirPropagation, UNREACHABLE};
 4: use super::settings::VoxelLightingSettings;

 8: pub(crate) fn write_air_irradiance(

15:             return;
16:         }

18:         let mut irradiance = [0.0; 3];
19:         for emission in &propagated.emissions {
20:             let distance_steps = emission.distance_steps[index];
21:             if distance_steps != UNREACHABLE {
22:                 accumulate_attenuated(
23:                     &mut irradiance,
24:                     emission.profile,
25:                     distance_steps,
26:                     0.5,
27:                     settings,
28:                 );
29:             }
30:         }
31:         grid.set_light_rgb(coord.x, coord.y, coord.z, pack_rgb(irradiance));
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_one/mod.rs
````rust
 1: //! Level 1 — the Habitable Zone.
 2: //!
 3: //! A sprawling warehouse/parking structure honoring the Backrooms wiki canon:
 4: //! bare concrete walls and massive pillars, institutional tile floors,
 5: //! exposed ceiling pipes, low-hanging fog (the renderer's atmosphere, not
 6: //! voxels), and fluorescent fixtures dimmer and less reliable than Level 0's.
 7: //! No entities are generated at this stage.
 8: //!
 9: //! The level is carved into functional **sectors** on a fixed world lattice,
10: //! each with its own `StructuralSystem` flavor:
11: //!
12: //! * **Aquila** — bland parking-lot expanses: concrete slab, huge square
13: //!   pillars on a deep-span grid, sparse lighting.
14: //! * **Gild** — dense storage architecture: concrete room fabric packed with
15: //!   supply crates (almond water, food) behind doorway'd walls.
16: //! * **Gothic** — curved masonry: circular pillars joined by real arches
17: //!   under vaulted ceilings.
18: //! * **Construction** — perpetually unfinished: half-height walls, rebar
19: //!   clusters, dead ends, chaotic ceiling heights.
20: //!
21: //! Every column is a pure function of world-space coordinates and the seed,
22: //! so chunks tile seamlessly in any streaming order. Consumable supplies are
23: //! exported beside the geometry; whether one still exists is reality state
24: //! (`RealitySnapshot::supply_consumed`), never grid state.
25: 
26: pub(crate) mod generate;
27: #[cfg(test)]
28: mod tests;
29: 
30: /// Ceiling height budget shared with Level 0's grid allocation.
31: pub const GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS: f32 = 5.8;
32: 
33: /// Side of one sector cell, world units. Sector *type* changes per cell but
34: /// every structural lattice below is phased to world coordinates, so walls
35: /// and pillar grids run continuously across sector borders.
36: pub const SECTOR_CELL: f32 = 96.0;
37: 
38: /// Level 1 — one zero-sized generator, like its siblings.
39: pub struct HabitableLevel;
40: 
41: /// The functional sub-regions of Level 1.
42: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
43: pub enum Sector {
44:     Aquila,
45:     Gild,
46:     Gothic,
47:     Construction,
48: }
49: 
50: impl Sector {
51:     /// Deterministic sector of a world position (hash of its lattice cell).
52:     pub fn at(seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> Self {
53:         let cx = (wx / SECTOR_CELL).floor() as i64;
54:         let cz = (wz / SECTOR_CELL).floor() as i64;
55:         let roll = crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::hash(
56:             seed,
57:             0x1EE1_5EC7_0A00_0001,
58:             cx,
59:             cz,
60:         ) % 100;
61:         // The arrival cell is always Aquila: the wanderer steps out of the
62:         // door into readable parking-lot openness, exactly the first-report
63:         // canon of Level 1.
64:         if cx == 0 && cz == 0 {
65:             return Self::Aquila;
66:         }
67:         match roll {
68:             0..=34 => Self::Aquila,
69:             35..=62 => Self::Gild,
70:             63..=81 => Self::Gothic,
71:             _ => Self::Construction,
72:         }
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// HUD name of this sector.
76:     pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
77:         match self {
78:             Self::Aquila => "AQUILA SECTOR",
79:             Self::Gild => "GILD SECTOR",
80:             Self::Gothic => "GOTHIC SECTOR",
81:             Self::Construction => "CONSTRUCTION SECTOR",
82:         }
83:     }
84: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/assembly_sampler.rs
````rust
  1: //! Sampling one planned assembly: perimeter walls pierced by entrances,
  2: //! sparse interior partitions, structural bays (plus a renovator's
  3: //! contradictory grid), and fixtures on the room's ceiling modules.
  4: 
  5: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
  6:     AssemblyInstance, CeilingLanguage, StructuralSystem, StructuralSystemInstance,
  7: };
  8: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::LevelTuning;
  9: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
 10: 
 11: use super::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnPlan, DOOR_HEIGHT};
 12: 
 13: impl BackroomsLevel {
 14:     /// Is (wx, wz) on a structural column of this system?
 15:     pub(super) fn on_column(st: &StructuralSystemInstance, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> bool {
 16:         if st.system == StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell {
 17:             // Core-and-shell designers hide columns in walls; none inside.
 18:             return false;
 19:         }
 20:         let mut mx = (wx - st.phase.0).rem_euclid(st.bay_x);
 21:         let mz = (wz - st.phase.1).rem_euclid(st.bay_z);
 22:         if st.system == StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid {
 23:             let row = ((wz - st.phase.1) / st.bay_z).floor() as i64;
 24:             if row.rem_euclid(2) == 1 {
 25:                 mx = (wx - st.phase.0 + st.bay_x * 0.5).rem_euclid(st.bay_x);
 26:             }
 27:         }
 28:         mx < st.column_side && mz < st.column_side
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     /// Column plan for a point inside an assembly footprint or its
 32:     /// surrounding wall band (`inside == false`).
 33:     pub(super) fn assembly_column(
 34:         a: &AssemblyInstance,
 35:         inside: bool,
 36:         renovator: Option<&StructuralSystemInstance>,
 37:         tuning: &LevelTuning,
 38:         wx: f32,
 39:         wz: f32,
 40:     ) -> ColumnPlan {
 41:         let walls_on = tuning.walls > 0.0;
 42:         let zone = a.ceiling_zones.first();
 43:         let mut ceiling_units = zone.map_or(3.4, |c| c.height_units);
 44:         match zone.map(|c| c.language) {
 45:             // Coffered reads as a shading pattern now (see the splat
 46:             // shader), not stepped geometry.
 47:             Some(CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit) => ceiling_units -= 0.2,
 48:             _ => {}
 49:         }
 50:         let mut plan = ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units);
 51: 
 52:         // Entrances pierce the wall band (and win over everything solid).
 53:         for e in &a.entrances {
 54:             let (da, db) = if e.through_x_wall {
 55:                 ((wx - e.center.x).abs(), (wz - e.center.z).abs())
 56:             } else {
 57:                 ((wz - e.center.z).abs(), (wx - e.center.x).abs())
 58:             };
 59:             if da < e.width * 0.5 && db <= PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05 {
 60:                 plan.lintel_from_units = walls_on
 61:                     .then_some(e.lintel_units.unwrap_or(0.0))
 62:                     .filter(|u| *u > 0.0);
 63:                 return plan;
 64:             }
 65:         }
 66: 
 67:         if !inside {
 68:             // Perimeter wall band.
 69:             plan.solid = walls_on;
 70:             return plan;
 71:         }
 72: 
 73:         // Interior partitions: walls on space boundaries that are not the
 74:         // footprint perimeter, each with a centered doorway.
 75:         let fb = a.footprint.bounds();
 76:         if walls_on {
 77:             for s in &a.spaces {
 78:                 let sb = s.footprint.bounds();
 79:                 if wz >= sb.1 && wz <= sb.3 {
 80:                     for plane in [sb.0, sb.2] {
 81:                         if (plane - fb.0).abs() > 0.1
 82:                             && (plane - fb.2).abs() > 0.1
 83:                             && (wx - plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 84:                         {
 85:                             let door_c = (sb.1 + sb.3) * 0.5;
 86:                             if (wz - door_c).abs() < 0.6 {
 87:                                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(DOOR_HEIGHT);
 88:                             } else {
 89:                                 plan.solid = true;
 90:                             }
 91:                         }
 92:                     }
 93:                 }
 94:                 if wx >= sb.0 && wx <= sb.2 {
 95:                     for plane in [sb.1, sb.3] {
 96:                         if (plane - fb.1).abs() > 0.1
 97:                             && (plane - fb.3).abs() > 0.1
 98:                             && (wz - plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 99:                         {
100:                             let door_c = (sb.0 + sb.2) * 0.5;
101:                             if (wx - door_c).abs() < 0.6 {
102:                                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(DOOR_HEIGHT);
103:                             } else {
104:                                 plan.solid = true;
105:                             }
106:                         }
107:                     }
108:                 }
109:             }
110:         }
111: 
112:         // Structure: the original grid, plus the renovator's contradictory
113:         // grid where a renovation overlays the assembly.
114:         if tuning.pillars > 0.0 && !plan.solid {
115:             if Self::on_column(&a.structure, wx, wz) {
116:                 plan.solid = true;
117:             }
118:             if let Some(r) = renovator {
119:                 if a.corruption.renovation_overlay && Self::on_column(r, wx, wz) {
120:                     // Renovation columns intrude on the original bay rhythm;
121:                     // the contradiction itself is the corruption. They stay
122:                     // ordinary wall material — Level 0 has no red masonry.
123:                     plan.solid = true;
124:                 }
125:             }
126:         }
127: 
128:         // Fixtures, tied to the assembly's ceiling modules. In a red room
129:         // every fixture burns red: the anomaly is the room's light, applied
130:         // after all geometry decisions and on the same fixture spacing.
131:         if !plan.solid && tuning.lights > 0.0 {
132:             for f in &a.fixtures {
133:                 if f.lit && (wx - f.at.x).abs() <= f.half_x && (wz - f.at.z).abs() <= f.half_z {
134:                     plan.light = true;
135:                     plan.red_light = a.corruption.red_room;
136:                     break;
137:                 }
138:             }
139:         }
140:         plan
141:     }
142: }
````

````rust
 1: //! The shared column vocabulary every Level 0 sampler speaks.

 3: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_WALL};

 5: 
 6: /// What one (x, z) column of the level looks like.

 8: pub(crate) struct ColumnPlan {

10:     pub floor: bool,
11:     /// Raised solid floor above the base slab, world units (stair treads,
12:     /// landings, plinths). `0.0` is the ordinary one-voxel slab. Raised

17:     pub solid: bool,

20:     /// Ceiling light above this column.
21:     pub light: bool,
22:     /// The light above this column burns red (red-room corruption). Only
23:     /// ever true inside an assembly whose whole room is the anomaly.
24:     pub red_light: bool,
25:     /// Solid band hanging from the ceiling down to this height (door
26:     /// lintels). The space below stays walkable.
27:     pub lintel_from_units: Option<f32>,
28:     /// Material used for solid columns and lintels (a wall-treatment voxel
29:     /// from the shared
30:     /// [`crate::domain::entities::environment::EnvironmentProfile`] semantics).
31:     pub wall_material: u8,
32:     /// Material of the floor slab (carpet depth/condition/fluid semantics).
33:     pub floor_material: u8,
34:     /// Material of the fixture voxel when `light` is set (warm fluorescent,
35:     /// red pressure, or cool glimmer).
36:     pub light_material: u8,
37: }
38: 
39: impl ColumnPlan {
40:     /// An open ordinary-fabric column with the default Level 0 materials.
41:     pub(crate) fn open(ceiling_units: f32) -> Self {
42:         Self {
43:             floor: true,
44:             floor_units: 0.0,
45:             solid: false,
46:             ceiling_units,
47:             light: false,
48:             red_light: false,
49:             lintel_from_units: None,
50:             wall_material: VOXEL_WALL,
51:             floor_material: VOXEL_FLOOR,
52:             light_material: VOXEL_LIGHT,
53:         }
54:     }
55: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/planning.rs
````rust
  1: //! Assembly-derived Red Room encounter planning.
  2: //!
  3: //! A Red Room is not a macro-lattice shape. It inherits a real assembly's
  4: //! footprint and entrance, then adds stable semantic crossing planes.
  5: 
  6: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  7:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, Axis2, AxisDirection, OrientedFootprint, OrthoBasis, QuarterTurn,
  8:     TraversalGate, TraversalGateKind,
  9: };
 10: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::AssemblyInstance;
 11: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 12: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{SNAP, mix64, stable_id};
 13: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 14: 
 15: const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
 16: const THRESHOLD_DEPTH: f32 = 2.8;
 17: const LOOP_GATE_DEPTH: f32 = 6.0;
 18: 
 19: fn clamp_inward(desired: f32, far_inner_plane: f32, direction: AxisDirection) -> f32 {
 20:     match direction {
 21:         AxisDirection::Positive => desired.min(far_inner_plane),
 22:         AxisDirection::Negative => desired.max(far_inner_plane),
 23:     }
 24: }
 25: 
 26: fn red_room_instance(
 27:     seed: u32,
 28:     region_origin: Position,
 29:     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
 30: ) -> Option<AnomalyInstance> {
 31:     let entrance = *assembly.entrances.first()?;
 32:     let bounds = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 33:     let center = Position::new((bounds.0 + bounds.2) * 0.5, (bounds.1 + bounds.3) * 0.5);
 34:     let region_x = (region_origin.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 35:     let region_z = (region_origin.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 36:     let id = mix64(
 37:         stable_id(seed, AnomalyKind::RedRoom, region_x, region_z)
 38:             ^ (assembly.id as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9),
 39:     );
 40:     let footprint = OrientedFootprint {
 41:         center,
 42:         half_x: (bounds.2 - bounds.0) * 0.5,
 43:         half_z: (bounds.3 - bounds.1) * 0.5,
 44:         basis: OrthoBasis {
 45:             turn: QuarterTurn::Zero,
 46:         },
 47:     };
 48:     let axis = if entrance.through_x_wall {
 49:         Axis2::Z
 50:     } else {
 51:         Axis2::X
 52:     };
 53:     let (edge_coordinate, center_coordinate, half_depth) = match axis {
 54:         Axis2::X => (entrance.center.x, center.x, footprint.half_x),
 55:         Axis2::Z => (entrance.center.z, center.z, footprint.half_z),
 56:     };
 57:     let forward = if center_coordinate >= edge_coordinate {
 58:         AxisDirection::Positive
 59:     } else {
 60:         AxisDirection::Negative
 61:     };
 62: 
 63:     // Commitment happens inside the room, beyond the externally readable
 64:     // doorway. Entrance placement guarantees enough depth for this vestibule.
 65:     let threshold_plane = edge_coordinate + forward.sign() * THRESHOLD_DEPTH;
 66:     let (span_min, span_max) = if axis == Axis2::Z {
 67:         (
 68:             entrance.center.x - entrance.width * 0.5,
 69:             entrance.center.x + entrance.width * 0.5,
 70:         )
 71:     } else {
 72:         (
 73:             entrance.center.z - entrance.width * 0.5,
 74:             entrance.center.z + entrance.width * 0.5,
 75:         )
 76:     };
 77:     let affected_bounds = footprint.bounds();
 78:     let threshold_gate = TraversalGate {
 79:         id: mix64(id ^ 0x6A7E_0ED0),
 80:         instance_id: id,
 81:         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
 82:         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold,
 83:         axis,
 84:         plane: threshold_plane,
 85:         span_min,
 86:         span_max,
 87:         forward,
 88:         affected_bounds,
 89:     };
 90: 
 91:     // The loop checkpoint is six units beyond commitment when the room has
 92:     // that depth. Shallow rooms clamp it one plan voxel inside the far wall,
 93:     // keeping the semantic crossing on geometry owned by this encounter.
 94:     let far_inner_plane = center_coordinate + forward.sign() * (half_depth - SNAP).max(0.0);
 95:     let loop_plane = clamp_inward(
 96:         threshold_plane + forward.sign() * LOOP_GATE_DEPTH,
 97:         far_inner_plane,
 98:         forward,
 99:     );
100:     let loop_gate = TraversalGate {
101:         id: mix64(id ^ 0x9B4C_1A2F),
102:         instance_id: id,
103:         anomaly_kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
104:         kind: TraversalGateKind::RedLoop,
105:         axis,
106:         plane: loop_plane,
107:         span_min,
108:         span_max,
109:         // `forward` records the authored inward direction. Runtime state owns
110:         // the separate policy for which traversal directions advance a loop.
111:         forward,
112:         affected_bounds,
113:     };
114: 
115:     Some(AnomalyInstance {
116:         id,
117:         kind: AnomalyKind::RedRoom,
118:         footprint,
119:         basis: footprint.basis,
120:         macro_anchor: (region_x, region_z),
121:         pillar_lattice: None,
122:         pit_lattice: None,
123:         arch: None,
124:         gates: vec![threshold_gate, loop_gate],
125:         skeleton_half_width: 1.0,
126:         entry_band: THRESHOLD_DEPTH,
127:     })
128: }
129: 
130: pub(crate) fn plan_red_rooms(
131:     seed: u32,
132:     region_origin: Position,
133:     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
134:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
135: ) -> Vec<AnomalyInstance> {
136:     let forced = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
137:     let organic_enabled = config.anomalies.frequency > 0.0 && config.anomalies.red_rooms > 0.0;
138:     if !forced && !organic_enabled {
139:         return Vec::new();
140:     }
141: 
142:     assemblies
143:         .iter()
144:         .filter(|assembly| assembly.corruption.red_room)
145:         .filter_map(|assembly| red_room_instance(seed, region_origin, assembly))
146:         .collect()
147: }
148: 
149: #[cfg(test)]
150: mod tests {
151:     use super::*;
152:     use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
153:         CorruptionProfile, Opening, Polygon2, SpaceProgram, StructuralSystem,
154:         StructuralSystemInstance,
155:     };
156: 
157:     fn red_assembly(entrance_z: f32) -> AssemblyInstance {
158:         AssemblyInstance {
159:             id: 7,
160:             program: SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
161:             footprint: Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, 12.0, 8.0),
162:             entrances: vec![Opening {
163:                 center: Position::new(6.0, entrance_z),
164:                 width: 1.2,
165:                 through_x_wall: true,
166:                 lintel_units: Some(2.2),
167:             }],
168:             spaces: Vec::new(),
169:             structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
170:                 system: StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
171:                 bay_x: 4.0,
172:                 bay_z: 4.0,
173:                 phase: (0.0, 0.0),
174:                 column_side: 0.4,
175:             },
176:             ceiling_zones: Vec::new(),
177:             fixtures: Vec::new(),
178:             service_voids: Vec::new(),
179:             corruption: CorruptionProfile {
180:                 red_room: true,
181:                 ..CorruptionProfile::default()
182:             },
183:         }
184:     }
185: 
186:     #[test]
187:     fn forced_red_room_survives_zero_frequency_and_zero_family_weight() {
188:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
189:         config.anomalies.frequency = 0.0;
190:         config.anomalies.red_rooms = 0.0;
191:         config.anomalies.forced_kind = Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
192:         let rooms = plan_red_rooms(42, Position::new(0.0, 0.0), &[red_assembly(0.0)], &config);
193:         assert_eq!(rooms.len(), 1);
194:         assert_eq!(rooms[0].kind, AnomalyKind::RedRoom);
195:         assert_eq!(rooms[0].gates.len(), 2);
196:     }
197: 
198:     #[test]
199:     fn loop_gate_is_inside_both_entrance_orientations() {
200:         let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
201:         for entrance_z in [0.0, 8.0] {
202:             let room = plan_red_rooms(
203:                 42,
204:                 Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
205:                 &[red_assembly(entrance_z)],
206:                 &config,
207:             )
208:             .pop()
209:             .unwrap();
210:             let loop_gate = room
211:                 .gates
212:                 .iter()
213:                 .find(|gate| gate.kind == TraversalGateKind::RedLoop)
214:                 .unwrap();
215:             let bounds = room.footprint.bounds();
216:             assert!(loop_gate.plane >= bounds.min_z + SNAP - f32::EPSILON);
217:             assert!(loop_gate.plane <= bounds.max_z - SNAP + f32::EPSILON);
218:         }
219:     }
220: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/recursive_level.rs
````rust
  1: //! Addressing for the Level 0 world reached through a committed Red Room.
  2: //!
  3: //! A Red Room does not invent a second procedural grammar.  It addresses a
  4: //! distant, deterministic copy of Level 0 and changes its presentation.  The
  5: //! address must therefore be stable across chunk order and worker boundaries,
  6: //! while retaining all 64 bits of anomaly identity until hashing is complete.
  7: //! Converting an `AnomalyId` directly to `f32` loses most of those bits and can
  8: //! make distinct rooms share a world; this module derives integer region
  9: //! coordinates first and converts only the small final translation.
 10: 
 11: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
 12:     AnomalyId, AnomalyStateStamp, Axis2, PitHazard, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase, TraversalGate,
 13:     WorldBounds,
 14: };
 15: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 16: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 17: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 18: use crate::use_cases::infinite_level::InfiniteRegionWindow;
 19: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
 20: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 21: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 22: 
 23: const ADDRESS_DOMAIN: u64 = 0x5245_4452_4F4F_4D00; // "REDROOM\0"
 24: // Keep translated coordinates near enough to the origin that f32 retains
 25: // sub-centimetre detail for future fine voxel requests. Branch uniqueness is
 26: // carried by the derived seed, so the translation itself need not be huge.
 27: const MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS: i64 = 64;
 28: const TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN: u64 = 192;
 29: 
 30: /// Stable procedural address of the recursive Level 0 associated with one
 31: /// Red Room instance.
 32: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
 33: pub(crate) struct RecursiveLevelAddress {
 34:     instance_id: AnomalyId,
 35:     derived_seed: u32,
 36:     translation_regions: (i64, i64),
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// The finite planning window needed to render one request into a recursive
 40: /// Level 0 branch.  The branch remains infinite; this value is only its local
 41: /// query cache, just like an ordinary chunk's region window.
 42: pub(crate) struct RecursiveLevelWindow {
 43:     address: RecursiveLevelAddress,
 44:     seed: u32,
 45:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 46:     regions: InfiniteRegionWindow,
 47: }
 48: 
 49: impl RecursiveLevelWindow {
 50:     pub(crate) fn around_chunk(
 51:         source_origin: Position,
 52:         chunk_size: f32,
 53:         halo: f32,
 54:         world_seed: u32,
 55:         base_config: GeneratorConfig,
 56:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 57:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 58:     ) -> Option<Self> {
 59:         let (address, _) = RecursiveLevelAddress::from_reality(world_seed, reality)?;
 60:         let seed = address.derived_seed();
 61:         let config = address.recursive_config(base_config);
 62:         let recursive_origin = address.to_recursive_world(source_origin);
 63:         let regions = InfiniteRegionWindow::around_chunk(
 64:             recursive_origin,
 65:             chunk_size,
 66:             halo,
 67:             seed,
 68:             &config,
 69:             noise,
 70:         );
 71:         Some(Self {
 72:             address,
 73:             seed,
 74:             config,
 75:             regions,
 76:         })
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     pub(crate) fn seed(&self) -> u32 {
 80:         self.seed
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     pub(crate) fn instance_id(&self) -> AnomalyId {
 84:         self.address.instance_id
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     pub(crate) fn config(&self) -> &GeneratorConfig {
 88:         &self.config
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     /// Returns both the recursive coordinate and the plan that owns it.
 92:     /// Keeping them paired prevents the old failure where a recursive plan
 93:     /// was sampled with the base world's seed and coordinates.
 94:     pub(crate) fn plan_at(&self, source: Position) -> Option<(Position, &RegionPlan)> {
 95:         let recursive = self.address.to_recursive_world(source);
 96:         self.regions
 97:             .plan_at(recursive)
 98:             .map(|plan| (recursive, plan))
 99:     }
100: 
101:     pub(crate) fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = ((i64, i64), &RegionPlan)> {
102:         self.regions.iter()
103:     }
104: 
105:     /// Project a semantic gate authored in the recursive branch back into
106:     /// the player's visible coordinate frame.
107:     pub(crate) fn project_gate(&self, mut gate: TraversalGate) -> TraversalGate {
108:         let offset = self.address.translation_world();
109:         match gate.axis {
110:             Axis2::X => {
111:                 gate.plane -= offset.x;
112:                 gate.span_min -= offset.z;
113:                 gate.span_max -= offset.z;
114:             }
115:             Axis2::Z => {
116:                 gate.plane -= offset.z;
117:                 gate.span_min -= offset.x;
118:                 gate.span_max -= offset.x;
119:             }
120:         }
121:         gate.affected_bounds = self.project_bounds(gate.affected_bounds);
122:         gate
123:     }
124: 
125:     pub(crate) fn project_hazard(&self, mut hazard: PitHazard) -> PitHazard {
126:         hazard.center = self.address.to_source_world(hazard.center);
127:         hazard.recovery = self.address.to_source_world(hazard.recovery);
128:         hazard
129:     }
130: 
131:     pub(crate) fn project_position(&self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
132:         self.address.to_source_world(recursive)
133:     }
134: 
135:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> WorldBounds {
136:         let min = self
137:             .address
138:             .to_recursive_world(Position::new(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z));
139:         let max = self
140:             .address
141:             .to_recursive_world(Position::new(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z));
142:         WorldBounds::new(min.x, min.z, max.x, max.z)
143:     }
144: 
145:     fn project_bounds(&self, bounds: WorldBounds) -> WorldBounds {
146:         let min = self
147:             .address
148:             .to_source_world(Position::new(bounds.min_x, bounds.min_z));
149:         let max = self
150:             .address
151:             .to_source_world(Position::new(bounds.max_x, bounds.max_z));
152:         WorldBounds::new(min.x, min.z, max.x, max.z)
153:     }
154: }
155: 
156: impl RecursiveLevelAddress {
157:     /// Derives an address using integer avalanche hashes only.  Both halves of
158:     /// the 64-bit instance id participate in the seed and in each axis.
159:     pub(crate) fn derive(world_seed: u32, instance_id: AnomalyId) -> Self {
160:         let root = mix64(
161:             ADDRESS_DOMAIN ^ instance_id ^ (world_seed as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15),
162:         );
163:         let seed_hash = mix64(root ^ 0x5EED_5EED_A11C_0DE5);
164:         let derived_seed = (seed_hash as u32) ^ ((seed_hash >> 32) as u32);
165:         let translation_regions = (
166:             translation_component(root, 0x5841_5849_5300_0001),
167:             translation_component(root, 0x5A41_5849_5300_0002),
168:         );
169: 
170:         Self {
171:             instance_id,
172:             derived_seed,
173:             translation_regions,
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     /// Selects the committed Red Room represented by a canonical reality
178:     /// snapshot, then derives its recursive address.
179:     pub(crate) fn from_reality(
180:         world_seed: u32,
181:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
182:     ) -> Option<(Self, &AnomalyStateStamp)> {
183:         let state = active_red_room(reality)?;
184:         Some((Self::derive(world_seed, state.instance_id), state))
185:     }
186: 
187:     pub(crate) fn derived_seed(self) -> u32 {
188:         self.derived_seed
189:     }
190: 
191:     pub(crate) fn translation_regions(self) -> (i64, i64) {
192:         self.translation_regions
193:     }
194: 
195:     /// Exact transform for region keys.  Planning should prefer this form so
196:     /// large-world floating-point precision never participates in identity.
197:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_region(self, source_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
198:         (
199:             source_region.0.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.0),
200:             source_region.1.saturating_add(self.translation_regions.1),
201:         )
202:     }
203: 
204:     pub(crate) fn to_source_region(self, recursive_region: (i64, i64)) -> (i64, i64) {
205:         (
206:             recursive_region
207:                 .0
208:                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.0),
209:             recursive_region
210:                 .1
211:                 .saturating_sub(self.translation_regions.1),
212:         )
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// World-space form used by column sampling.  The translation is an exact
216:     /// multiple of the 80u region lattice, preserving portals and 0.4u plan
217:     /// geometry across every chunk and LOD.
218:     pub(crate) fn to_recursive_world(self, source: Position) -> Position {
219:         let (region, local) = split_world_position(source);
220:         let recursive = self.to_recursive_region(region);
221:         join_world_position(recursive, local)
222:     }
223: 
224:     pub(crate) fn to_source_world(self, recursive: Position) -> Position {
225:         let (region, local) = split_world_position(recursive);
226:         let source = self.to_source_region(region);
227:         join_world_position(source, local)
228:     }
229: 
230:     pub(crate) fn translation_world(self) -> Position {
231:         let translation = self.translation_regions();
232:         Position::new(
233:             translation.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
234:             translation.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
235:         )
236:     }
237: 
238:     /// Produces a Level 0 config for the addressed world.  Organic anomaly
239:     /// tuning is preserved, allowing recursive Level 0 to remain the complete
240:     /// generator; only the one-shot debug override is cleared so it cannot be
241:     /// cloned into every recursive address.
242:     pub(crate) fn recursive_config(self, mut base: GeneratorConfig) -> GeneratorConfig {
243:         base.level = LEVEL_BACKROOMS;
244:         base.anomalies.forced_kind = None;
245:         base
246:     }
247: }
248: 
249: /// Chooses one committed Red Room without depending on snapshot insertion
250: /// order.  Under the current state machine, only red thresholds can produce a
251: /// non-`Outside` phase.  Progress is compared explicitly because `epoch` is
252: /// the best available recency signal; stable identity is the final tie-break.
253: pub(crate) fn active_red_room(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> Option<&AnomalyStateStamp> {
254:     reality
255:         .stamps()
256:         .iter()
257:         .filter(|state| state.phase != RedRoomPhase::Outside)
258:         .max_by_key(|state| {
259:             (
260:                 state.epoch,
261:                 state.phase,
262:                 state.loop_count,
263:                 state.last_gate_id,
264:                 state.instance_id,
265:             )
266:         })
267: }
268: 
269: fn translation_component(root: u64, axis_domain: u64) -> i64 {
270:     let hash = mix64(root ^ axis_domain);
271:     let magnitude = MIN_TRANSLATION_REGIONS + (hash % TRANSLATION_REGION_SPAN) as i64;
272:     if hash & (1 << 63) == 0 {
273:         magnitude
274:     } else {
275:         -magnitude
276:     }
277: }
278: 
279: fn split_world_position(position: Position) -> ((i64, i64), (f32, f32)) {
280:     let region = (
281:         (position.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
282:         (position.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64,
283:     );
284:     let local = (
285:         position.x - region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
286:         position.z - region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
287:     );
288:     (region, local)
289: }
290: 
291: fn join_world_position(region: (i64, i64), local: (f32, f32)) -> Position {
292:     Position::new(
293:         region.0 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.0,
294:         region.1 as f32 * REGION_SIZE + local.1,
295:     )
296: }
297: 
298: fn mix64(mut value: u64) -> u64 {
299:     value ^= value >> 30;
300:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
301:     value ^= value >> 27;
302:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
303:     value ^ (value >> 31)
304: }
305:

307: mod tests {

336:         let source = (-91, 207);
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/circulation.rs
````rust
  1: //! Circulation routing: one dominant cross-region spine plus rare branches.
  2: //!
  3: //! The main spine always runs west portal -> east portal, so circulation
  4: //! chains across regions forever; branches are optional and never form a
  5: //! competing street grid.
  6: 
  7: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  8: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  9: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
 10: 
 11: use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, snap, snap_width, v_edge_portal_z};
 12: 
 13: /// Z coordinate of the main spine where it passes world x (assumes the spine
 14: /// is a west-to-east Manhattan path).
 15: fn spine_z_at(path: &[Position], x: f32) -> f32 {
 16:     for seg in path.windows(2) {
 17:         let (a, b) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
 18:         if a.z == b.z && (x >= a.x.min(b.x)) && (x <= a.x.max(b.x)) {
 19:             return a.z;
 20:         }
 21:     }
 22:     path[0].z
 23: }
 24: 
 25: pub(super) fn build_corridors(
 26:     seed: u32,
 27:     rx: i64,
 28:     rz: i64,
 29:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 30:     origin: Position,
 31:     size: f32,
 32: ) -> Vec<CirculationSpine> {
 33:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0 + k, rx, rz]);
 34:     let (x0, x1) = (origin.x, origin.x + size);
 35:     let (z0, z1) = (origin.z, origin.z + size);
 36:     let west_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx, rz);
 37:     let east_z = v_edge_portal_z(seed, rx + 1, rz);
 38:     // The primary route is deliberately too broad for an ordinary office
 39:     // corridor. It carries the infinite cross-region continuity; anything
 40:     // else is an optional branch, never a competing street grid.
 41:     let main_w = snap_width(4.8 + 2.4 * h(1));
 42:     let sec_w = snap_width(3.6 + 1.4 * hash01(seed, &[0xC1, rx, rz]));
 43: 
 44:     let mut spines = Vec::new();
 45:     let mut id = 0u32;
 46:     let mut push = |kind: SpaceProgram, path: Vec<Position>, width: f32, id: &mut u32| {
 47:         spines_push(&mut spines, kind, path, width, id);
 48:     };
 49: 
 50:     // Main spine: west portal -> east portal, always. Its Manhattan bend
 51:     // position is the designer's one free choice.
 52:     let bend_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.35 + 0.30 * h(2)));
 53:     let main_path: Vec<Position> = match genome.circulation {
 54:         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine => {
 55:             let mid_z = snap(z0 + size * (0.30 + 0.40 * h(3)));
 56:             let bend2_x = snap(x0 + size * (0.60 + 0.25 * h(4)));
 57:             vec![
 58:                 Position::new(x0, west_z),
 59:                 Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
 60:                 Position::new(bend_x, mid_z),
 61:                 Position::new(bend2_x, mid_z),
 62:                 Position::new(bend2_x, east_z),
 63:                 Position::new(x1, east_z),
 64:             ]
 65:         }
 66:         _ => vec![
 67:             Position::new(x0, west_z),
 68:             Position::new(bend_x, west_z),
 69:             Position::new(bend_x, east_z),
 70:             Position::new(x1, east_z),
 71:         ],
 72:     };
 73:     let main_z_at = main_path.clone();
 74:     push(SpaceProgram::MainCorridor, main_path, main_w, &mut id);
 75: 
 76:     // Secondary routes are branches, not a second regional grid: roughly a
 77:     // quarter of regions have none, most have one, and a few have two. The
 78:     // former ring and north/south through-route are intentionally absent.
 79:     let branch_count = match genome.circulation {
 80:         CirculationStyle::StraightSpine if h(11) < 0.45 => 0,
 81:         CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine if h(11) < 0.20 => 0,
 82:         _ if h(11) < 0.28 => 0,
 83:         _ if h(11) < 0.82 => 1,
 84:         _ => 2,
 85:     };
 86:     for k in 0..branch_count {
 87:         let sx = snap(x0 + size * (0.18 + 0.64 * h(12 + k)));
 88:         let sz = spine_z_at(&main_z_at, sx);
 89:         let len = snap(12.0 + 14.0 * h(22 + k));
 90:         let dir = if h(32 + k) < 0.5 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
 91:         let end = (sz + dir * len).clamp(z0 + EDGE_MARGIN, z1 - EDGE_MARGIN);
 92:         if (end - sz).abs() >= 8.0 {
 93:             push(
 94:                 SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall,
 95:                 vec![Position::new(sx, sz), Position::new(sx, snap(end))],
 96:                 sec_w,
 97:                 &mut id,
 98:             );
 99:         }
100:     }
101:     spines
102: }
103: 
104: fn spines_push(
105:     spines: &mut Vec<CirculationSpine>,
106:     kind: SpaceProgram,
107:     path: Vec<Position>,
108:     width: f32,
109:     id: &mut u32,
110: ) {
111:     spines.push(CirculationSpine {
112:         id: *id,
113:         spine_kind: kind,
114:         path,
115:         width,
116:     });
117:     *id += 1;
118: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Debug hook: ASCII plan view of one region.
 2: 
 3: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 4: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
 5: 
 6: /// ASCII plan view at `step` world units per character. Corridors `=`, macro
 7: /// anomalies `P/B/H` (pillar/blackout/pits), red loops `R`, assembly interiors
 8: /// by program initial, entrances `+`, empty fabric `.`.
 9: pub fn debug_region_ascii(plan: &RegionPlan, step: f32) -> String {
10:     let n = (plan.size_world / step) as usize;
11:     let mut out = String::with_capacity((n + 1) * n);
12:     for iz in 0..n {
13:         for ix in 0..n {
14:             let x = plan.origin_world.x + (ix as f32 + 0.5) * step;
15:             let z = plan.origin_world.z + (iz as f32 + 0.5) * step;
16:             let mut ch = '.';
17:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
18:                 if a.footprint.contains(x, z) {
19:                     ch = match a.program {
20:                         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => 'o',
21:                         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => 'p',
22:                         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 'c',
23:                         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => 'b',
24:                         SpaceProgram::Storage => 's',
25:                         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => 'v',
26:                         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => 'w',
27:                         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => 'x',
28:                         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 'A',
29:                         SpaceProgram::Stair => 'S',
30:                         _ => 'r',
31:                     };
32:                 }
33:             }
34:             for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
35:                 if anomaly.contains(x, z) {
36:                     ch = match anomaly.kind {
37:                         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => 'P',
38:                         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => 'B',
39:                         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => 'H',
40:                         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => 'R',
41:                         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => 'M',
42:                     };
43:                 }
44:             }
45:             for s in &plan.corridors {
46:                 if s.distance(x, z) <= s.width * 0.5 {
47:                     ch = '=';
48:                 }
49:             }
50:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
51:                 for e in &a.entrances {
52:                     if (x - e.center.x).abs() < e.width * 0.5 && (z - e.center.z).abs() < step {
53:                         ch = '+';
54:                     }
55:                 }
56:             }
57:             out.push(ch);
58:         }
59:         out.push('\n');
60:     }
61:     out
62: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/region_plan/mod.rs
````rust
  1: //! Region-scale architectural planning for Backrooms Level 0.
  2: //!
  3: //! The world is tiled by fixed 80 u square regions on a world-space lattice.
  4: //! [`generate_region_plan`] is a *pure* function of `(seed, region)`: it
  5: //! derives the region's designers ([`ArchitectGenome`]), routes a dominant
  6: //! circulation spine first (between edge portals shared with the neighboring
  7: //! regions), attaches incomplete program masses ([`AssemblyInstance`]) beside
  8: //! that circulation,
  9: //! gives them structure / ceilings / fixtures, and finally applies a
 10: //! Backrooms corruption pass (duplicated suites, abandoned expansions,
 11: //! renovation overlays).
 12: //!
 13: //! Cross-region continuity: a corridor leaves a region only at a *portal* on
 14: //! a shared edge, and the portal position is derived from the *edge's*
 15: //! lattice coordinate — both neighbors compute the identical portal, so
 16: //! corridors chain across regions forever (a main corridor that never ends
 17: //! is the first and cheapest corruption).
 18: //!
 19: //! All coordinates are snapped to a 0.4 u lattice — the coarsest voxel size —
 20: //! so plan geometry lands identically at every LOD.
 21: 
 22: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
 23: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 24: use crate::use_cases::anomaly_plan::plan_anomalies_for_region;
 25: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 26: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 27: 
 28: /// Side of a region, world units. A multiple of both chunk sizes (10/20).
 29: pub const REGION_SIZE: f32 = 80.0;
 30: /// Plan wall thickness: one coarse voxel, so walls survive every LOD.
 31: pub const PLAN_WALL_T: f32 = 0.4;
 32: /// Snap lattice for all plan geometry (= coarsest voxel size).
 33: const SNAP: f32 = 0.4;
 34: /// Keep-out margin from region edges for assembly footprints.
 35: const EDGE_MARGIN: f32 = 3.2;
 36: 
 37: /// Region lattice index of a world coordinate.
 38: pub fn region_index(w: f32) -> i64 {
 39:     (w / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64
 40: }
 41: 
 42: fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
 43:     (v / SNAP).round() * SNAP
 44: }
 45: 
 46: /// Corridor widths snap to 0.8 so *half*-widths stay on the 0.4 lattice and
 47: /// suite front walls land flush against corridor edges.
 48: fn snap_width(v: f32) -> f32 {
 49:     ((v / (2.0 * SNAP)).round() * 2.0 * SNAP).max(2.0 * SNAP)
 50: }
 51: 
 52: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 53: // Deterministic hashing and edge portals.
 54: //
 55: // All "randomness" flows through `world_topology::hash01`, and the portal a
 56: // corridor uses to cross a region border is the macro graph's portal — one
 57: // derivation shared by both neighbors of the edge and by the topology layer.
 58: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 59: 
 60: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::{hash01, primary_portal_z as v_edge_portal_z};
 61: 
 62: fn pick_index(h: f32, len: usize) -> usize {
 63:     ((h * len as f32) as usize).min(len - 1)
 64: }
 65: 
 66: /// World spawn: a point *on the main corridor centerline* of region (0, 0),
 67: /// a few units east of its west portal. The first thing the player sees is
 68: /// therefore the region's dominant circulation route — walls running away in
 69: /// both directions — rather than unplanned fabric. Both the generator core
 70: /// and the browser composition root derive spawn from this single function,
 71: /// so the player and the voxelizer can never disagree about where "here" is.
 72: pub fn spawn_point(seed: u32) -> Position {
 73:     // The main spine's west leg always runs from (0, west_z) to at least
 74:     // x = 0.35 * REGION_SIZE, so a few units in we are guaranteed to stand
 75:     // on a straight, readable stretch of corridor.
 76:     Position::new(6.0, v_edge_portal_z(seed, 0, 0))
 77: }
 78: 
 79: 
 80: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 81: // The planning stages, one intent per module.
 82: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 83: 
 84: mod circulation;
 85: mod corruption;
 86: mod debug;
 87: mod genome;
 88: mod suites;
 89: #[cfg(test)]
 90: mod tests;
 91: 
 92: pub use debug::debug_region_ascii;
 93: pub use genome::derive_genome;
 94: 
 95: use circulation::build_corridors;
 96: use corruption::corrupt;
 97: use suites::{SUITE_PROGRAMS, place_suite};
 98: 
 99: /// Pure, deterministic plan for the region whose lower-left corner is
100: /// `region_origin` (must lie on the region lattice).
101: pub fn generate_region_plan(
102:     seed: u32,
103:     region_origin: Position,
104:     region_size: f32,
105:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
106:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
107: ) -> RegionPlan {
108:     let rx = region_index(region_origin.x + 0.1);
109:     let rz = region_index(region_origin.z + 0.1);
110:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xA0 + k, rx, rz]);
111: 
112:     let dominant = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 0, noise);
113:     let renovator = derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 1, noise);
114:     let mut architects = vec![dominant.clone(), renovator];
115:     // A third designer intrudes where the style-blend field runs high: the
116:     // macro fields decide *where* cultures leak into each other; the hash
117:     // only decides whether this particular region exposes the seam.
118:     let fields = crate::use_cases::world_topology::sample_fields(
119:         noise,
120:         seed,
121:         (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
122:         (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE,
123:     );
124:     if h(0) < 0.10 + 0.55 * fields.style_blend {
125:         architects.push(derive_genome(seed, rx, rz, 2, noise));
126:     }
127: 
128:     let corridors = build_corridors(seed, rx, rz, &dominant, region_origin, region_size);
129: 
130:     // --- incomplete masses beside the dominant route -----------------------
131:     // Only the primary route receives masses. The secondary stubs remain
132:     // mostly exposed circulation, which prevents a region from resolving
133:     // into a tiled office floorplan.
134:     let mut assemblies: Vec<AssemblyInstance> = Vec::new();
135:     let mut taken: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = Vec::new();
136:     let mut id = 0u32;
137:     let legs: Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)> = corridors
138:         .iter()
139:         .filter(|s| s.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor)
140:         .flat_map(|s| {
141:             let w = s.width;
142:             s.path
143:                 .windows(2)
144:                 .filter(|seg| seg[0].z == seg[1].z)
145:                 .map(move |seg| (seg[0].x.min(seg[1].x), seg[0].x.max(seg[1].x), seg[0].z, w))
146:                 .collect::<Vec<_>>()
147:         })
148:         .filter(|(a, b, _, _)| b - a >= 14.0)
149:         .collect();
150: 
151:     for (li, &(lx0, lx1, lz, lw)) in legs.iter().enumerate() {
152:         let mut cursor = lx0 + 4.0;
153:         let mut side = if h(40 + li as i64) < 0.5 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
154:         while cursor < lx1 - 12.0 {
155:             let aseed = hash01(seed, &[0x5EA, rx, rz, id as i64]);
156:             let threshold_seed = hash01(seed, &[0x7A11, rx, rz, id as i64]);
157:             // Leave substantial pieces of the route exposed. When a mass is
158:             // placed, the next candidate begins 8--16 u beyond its end.
159:             if hash01(seed, &[0x5E8, rx, rz, id as i64]) < 0.62 {
160:                 let program = SUITE_PROGRAMS[pick_index(aseed, SUITE_PROGRAMS.len())];
161:                 if let Some(a) = place_suite(
162:                     id,
163:                     program,
164:                     &dominant,
165:                     aseed,
166:                     threshold_seed,
167:                     cursor,
168:                     lz,
169:                     lw * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T,
170:                     side,
171:                     region_origin,
172:                     region_size,
173:                     &taken,
174:                     &corridors,
175:                 ) {
176:                     let b = a.footprint.bounds();
177:                     cursor += (b.2 - b.0) + 8.0 + 8.0 * threshold_seed;
178:                     taken.push(b);
179:                     assemblies.push(a);
180:                 } else {
181:                     cursor += 8.0 + 8.0 * threshold_seed;
182:                 }
183:             } else {
184:                 cursor += 8.0 + 8.0 * threshold_seed;
185:             }
186:             side = -side;
187:             id += 1;
188:         }
189:     }
190: 
191:     // --- corruption pass ----------------------------------------------------
192:     corrupt(
193:         seed,
194:         rx,
195:         rz,
196:         &dominant,
197:         config,
198:         noise,
199:         &mut assemblies,
200:         &mut taken,
201:         &corridors,
202:     );
203: 
204:     // --- vertical circulation ------------------------------------------------
205:     // The macro graph may have reserved a stairwell here. Upward links are
206:     // realized as a Stair assembly beside the main spine; downward links
207:     // stay graph reservations until the engine streams below elevation 0.
208:     // Placed after corruption so no pass can duplicate, abandon, or redden
209:     // a stair core.
210:     if let Some(link) =
211:         crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, rx, rz)
212:         && crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::link_wants_geometry(&link)
213:         && let Some(stair) = crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::place_stairwell(
214:             id + 2000,
215:             &link,
216:             &legs,
217:             region_origin,
218:             region_size,
219:             EDGE_MARGIN,
220:             PLAN_WALL_T,
221:             &taken,
222:             |cx, cz, clearance| {
223:                 corridors
224:                     .iter()
225:                     .all(|s| s.distance(cx, cz) >= s.width * 0.5 + clearance)
226:             },
227:         )
228:     {
229:         taken.push(stair.footprint.bounds());
230:         assemblies.push(stair);
231:     }
232: 
233:     // Macro anomalies are derived after ordinary architecture so compact red
234:     // rooms can promote a real assembly, while region-spanning families keep
235:     // stable world-lattice identities independent of this region query.
236:     let anomalies = plan_anomalies_for_region(
237:         seed,
238:         region_origin,
239:         region_size,
240:         &assemblies,
241:         spawn_point(seed),
242:         config,
243:         noise,
244:     );
245: 
246:     RegionPlan {
247:         origin_world: region_origin,
248:         size_world: region_size,
249:         architects,
250:         assemblies,
251:         corridors,
252:         anomalies,
253:     }
254: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Program masses beside the dominant route: suite placement, structure,
  2: //! ceilings, fixtures, and sparse interior partitioning.
  3: 
  4: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  5: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  6: 
  7: use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, snap};
  8: 
  9: /// The suite program palette placed beside main corridors, roughly weighted.
 10: /// Large, unfinished open-office masses dominate. Small private rooms remain
 11: /// present only as occasional evidence that this once had an office program.
 12: pub(super) const SUITE_PROGRAMS: [SpaceProgram; 12] = [
 13:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 14:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 15:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 16:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 17:     SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
 18:     SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom,
 19:     SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom,
 20:     SpaceProgram::BreakRoom,
 21:     SpaceProgram::Storage,
 22:     SpaceProgram::ServerRoom,
 23:     SpaceProgram::WaitingArea,
 24:     SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
 25: ];
 26: 
 27: fn ceiling_height_for(program: SpaceProgram, aseed: f32) -> f32 {
 28:     match program {
 29:         SpaceProgram::Atrium => 4.8 + 0.6 * aseed,
 30:         // Compression is a deliberate contrast, never the default ceiling.
 31:         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom | SpaceProgram::Mechanical => 2.6 + 0.2 * aseed,
 32:         SpaceProgram::Storage | SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => 3.0 + 0.3 * aseed,
 33:         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => 3.5 + 0.7 * aseed,
 34:         _ => 3.2 + 0.5 * aseed,
 35:     }
 36: }
 37: 
 38: fn structure_for(genome: &ArchitectGenome, aseed: f32) -> StructuralSystemInstance {
 39:     let bay = snap(4.4 + 1.6 * aseed);
 40:     let (bay_x, bay_z) = match genome.structural_system {
 41:         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => (bay * 1.5, bay),
 42:         _ => (bay, bay),
 43:     };
 44:     // A designer with no tolerance for asymmetry (1) centers the column
 45:     // grid on the footprint instead of letting it fall wherever an offset
 46:     // phase lands; one with none of that tolerance (0) keeps today's
 47:     // freely offset grid.
 48:     let tol = genome.tolerance_for_symmetry.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 49:     let phase = (
 50:         snap(aseed * 4.0 * (1.0 - tol)),
 51:         snap(aseed * 8.0 % 4.0 * (1.0 - tol)),
 52:     );
 53:     StructuralSystemInstance {
 54:         system: genome.structural_system,
 55:         bay_x,
 56:         bay_z,
 57:         phase,
 58:         column_side: 0.4,
 59:     }
 60: }
 61: 
 62: /// Fixtures for a rectangular footprint in the genome's lighting language.
 63: fn fixtures_for(
 64:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
 65:     footprint: &Polygon2,
 66:     lit: bool,
 67:     aseed: f32,
 68: ) -> Vec<Fixture> {
 69:     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
 70:     let mut out = Vec::new();
 71:     match genome.lighting_language {
 72:         LightingLanguage::GridPanels => {
 73:             let step = 2.4;
 74:             let mut z = z0 + 1.2;
 75:             while z < z1 - 0.8 {
 76:                 let mut x = x0 + 1.2;
 77:                 while x < x1 - 0.8 {
 78:                     out.push(Fixture {
 79:                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(z)),
 80:                         half_x: 0.4,
 81:                         half_z: 0.4,
 82:                         lit,
 83:                     });
 84:                     x += step;
 85:                 }
 86:                 z += step;
 87:             }
 88:         }
 89:         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation => {
 90:             // Strips run down the room's long axis.
 91:             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
 92:             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
 93:             let step = 3.2;
 94:             if long_x {
 95:                 let mut x = x0 + 1.6;
 96:                 while x < x1 - 1.2 {
 97:                     out.push(Fixture {
 98:                         at: Position::new(snap(x), snap(cz)),
 99:                         half_x: 1.0,
100:                         half_z: 0.25,
101:                         lit,
102:                     });
103:                     x += step;
104:                 }
105:             } else {
106:                 let mut z = z0 + 1.6;
107:                 while z < z1 - 1.2 {
108:                     out.push(Fixture {
109:                         at: Position::new(snap(cx), snap(z)),
110:                         half_x: 0.25,
111:                         half_z: 1.0,
112:                         lit,
113:                     });
114:                     z += step;
115:                 }
116:             }
117:         }
118:         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants => {
119:             let n = 1 + (aseed * 2.0) as i32;
120:             // A designer with high tolerance for symmetry mirrors and
121:             // centers pendants along the room's long axis instead of
122:             // scattering them by golden-ratio jitter; `tol` blends between
123:             // the two rather than switching sharply between them.
124:             let tol = genome.tolerance_for_symmetry.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
125:             let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) * 0.5, (z0 + z1) * 0.5);
126:             let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
127:             for k in 0..n {
128:                 let jx = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.618 + aseed) % 1.0));
129:                 let jz = z0 + (z1 - z0) * (0.3 + 0.4 * ((k as f32 * 0.382 + aseed * 2.0) % 1.0));
130:                 let centered = if n > 1 {
131:                     k as f32 / (n - 1) as f32 - 0.5
132:                 } else {
133:                     0.0
134:                 };
135:                 let (sx, sz) = if long_x {
136:                     (cx + centered * (x1 - x0) * 0.6, cz)
137:                 } else {
138:                     (cx, cz + centered * (z1 - z0) * 0.6)
139:                 };
140:                 let fx = jx + (sx - jx) * tol;
141:                 let fz = jz + (sz - jz) * tol;
142:                 out.push(Fixture {
143:                     at: Position::new(snap(fx), snap(fz)),
144:                     half_x: 0.3,
145:                     half_z: 0.3,
146:                     lit,
147:                 });
148:             }
149:         }
150:     }
151:     out
152: }
153: 
154: /// Interior partitioning is deliberately sparse. A suite may split once or
155: /// twice, producing a few long interruptions rather than a cell grid. How
156: /// readily it splits at all is `furnishing_density`: 0 reads as a bare
157: /// shell that almost never partitions, 1 as a densely partitioned interior
158: /// that almost always does — the axis genome.rs derives but that, until
159: /// now, nothing consumed.
160: fn spaces_for(
161:     program: SpaceProgram,
162:     footprint: &Polygon2,
163:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
164:     aseed: f32,
165: ) -> Vec<Space> {
166:     if !matches!(
167:         program,
168:         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice | SpaceProgram::OpenOffice | SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom
169:     ) {
170:         return Vec::new();
171:     }
172:     let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
173:     let long_x = (x1 - x0) >= (z1 - z0);
174:     let span = if long_x { x1 - x0 } else { z1 - z0 };
175:     let want = genome.room_proportions.min_side.max(12.0);
176:     let n = ((span / want) as usize).clamp(1, 2);
177:     let split_threshold = (1.0 - genome.furnishing_density).clamp(0.05, 0.95);
178:     let n = if aseed > split_threshold { n } else { 1 };
179:     if n <= 1 {
180:         return Vec::new();
181:     }
182:     let mut out = Vec::new();
183:     for k in 0..n {
184:         let (a, b) = (
185:             snap(k as f32 / n as f32 * span),
186:             snap((k + 1) as f32 / n as f32 * span),
187:         );
188:         let rect = if long_x {
189:             Polygon2::rect(x0 + a, z0, b - a, z1 - z0)
190:         } else {
191:             Polygon2::rect(x0, z0 + a, x1 - x0, b - a)
192:         };
193:         out.push(Space {
194:             program,
195:             footprint: rect,
196:         });
197:     }
198:     out
199: }
200: 
201: pub(super) fn aabb_overlap(a: (f32, f32, f32, f32), b: (f32, f32, f32, f32), gap: f32) -> bool {
202:     a.0 < b.2 + gap && b.0 < a.2 + gap && a.1 < b.3 + gap && b.1 < a.3 + gap
203: }
204: 
205: /// Places one suite beside a horizontal corridor segment. Returns `None` if
206: /// the footprint would leave the region, collide with a prior assembly, or
207: /// cross another corridor.
208: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
209: pub(super) fn place_suite(
210:     id: u32,
211:     program: SpaceProgram,
212:     genome: &ArchitectGenome,
213:     aseed: f32,
214:     threshold_seed: f32,
215:     cursor_x: f32,
216:     corridor_z: f32,
217:     corridor_half: f32,
218:     side: f32, // +1 = suite on +Z side of corridor, -1 = -Z side
219:     origin: Position,
220:     size: f32,
221:     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
222:     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
223: ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
224:     let p = &genome.room_proportions;
225:     let w = snap((p.min_side + (p.max_side - p.min_side) * aseed).clamp(12.0, 24.0));
226:     let d = snap((w * (0.72 - 0.28 * p.elongation)).clamp(8.0, 18.0));
227: 
228:     let x0 = snap(cursor_x);
229:     let z_front = snap(if side > 0.0 {
230:         corridor_z + corridor_half
231:     } else {
232:         corridor_z - corridor_half - d
233:     });
234:     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, w, d);
235:     let b = footprint.bounds();
236: 
237:     // Stay inside the region with margin.
238:     if b.0 < origin.x + EDGE_MARGIN
239:         || b.1 < origin.z + EDGE_MARGIN
240:         || b.2 > origin.x + size - EDGE_MARGIN
241:         || b.3 > origin.z + size - EDGE_MARGIN
242:     {
243:         return None;
244:     }
245:     if taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, 0.8)) {
246:         return None;
247:     }
248:     // Don't let a suite swallow a *different* corridor (its front corridor
249:     // touching the footprint edge is fine and expected).
250:     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
251:     for s in spines {
252:         if s.distance(center.0, center.1) < s.width * 0.5 + d.min(w) * 0.25 {
253:             return None;
254:         }
255:     }
256: 
257:     // Entrance on the corridor-facing wall. The genome biases the language,
258:     // but a narrow framed door is only about 8--14% of thresholds globally.
259:     // Most fronts dissolve into a room through an unframed or broad portal.
260:     let threshold = match genome.threshold_language {
261:         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.14 => {
262:             ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel
263:         }
264:         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.08 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
265:         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
266:         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal if threshold_seed < 0.62 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
267:         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
268:         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel if threshold_seed < 0.50 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
269:         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
270:     };
271:     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
272:     let (width, lintel) = match threshold {
273:         ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel => (1.2, Some(2.2)),
274:         ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal => (4.8, None),
275:         ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal => (3.6, Some(3.0)),
276:     };
277:     let edge = width * 0.5 + 0.8;
278:     let door_x = snap((b.0 + w * (0.25 + 0.5 * threshold_seed)).clamp(b.0 + edge, b.2 - edge));
279:     let entrances = vec![Opening {
280:         center: Position::new(door_x, front_z),
281:         width,
282:         through_x_wall: true,
283:         lintel_units: lintel,
284:     }];
285: 
286:     let ceiling = CeilingZone {
287:         area: footprint.clone(),
288:         language: genome.ceiling_language,
289:         height_units: ceiling_height_for(program, aseed),
290:     };
291:     Some(AssemblyInstance {
292:         id,
293:         program,
294:         spaces: spaces_for(program, &footprint, genome, aseed),
295:         structure: structure_for(genome, aseed),
296:         ceiling_zones: vec![ceiling],
297:         fixtures: fixtures_for(genome, &footprint, true, aseed),
298:         service_voids: Vec::new(),
299:         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
300:         entrances,
301:         footprint,
302:     })
303: }
304: 
305: #[cfg(test)]
306: mod tests {
307:     use super::*;
308: 
309:     fn genome_with(furnishing_density: f32, tolerance_for_symmetry: f32) -> ArchitectGenome {
310:         ArchitectGenome {
311:             circulation: CirculationStyle::StraightSpine,
312:             structural_system: StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
313:             room_proportions: ProportionRules {
314:                 min_side: 12.0,
315:                 max_side: 18.0,
316:                 elongation: 0.5,
317:             },
318:             threshold_language: ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
319:             ceiling_language: CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
320:             lighting_language: LightingLanguage::SparsePendants,
321:             furnishing_density,
322:             renovation_history: RenovationStyle::Untouched,
323:             tolerance_for_symmetry,
324:         }
325:     }
326: 
327:     #[test]
328:     fn furnishing_density_scales_how_readily_a_suite_partitions() {
329:         // Wide enough (30u span, 12u min_side) that a split candidate exists
330:         // at all (n = 2 before the density gate).
331:         let footprint = Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, 30.0, 12.0);
332:         let bare_shell = genome_with(0.0, 0.5);
333:         let dense = genome_with(1.0, 0.5);
334:         assert!(
335:             spaces_for(SpaceProgram::OpenOffice, &footprint, &bare_shell, 0.5).is_empty(),
336:             "furnishing_density 0 should almost never partition"
337:         );
338:         assert_eq!(
339:             spaces_for(SpaceProgram::OpenOffice, &footprint, &dense, 0.5).len(),
340:             2,
341:             "furnishing_density 1 should almost always partition"
342:         );
343:     }
344: 
345:     #[test]
346:     fn interior_partitions_apply_beyond_private_office() {
347:         let footprint = Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, 30.0, 12.0);
348:         let dense = genome_with(1.0, 0.5);
349:         for program in [
350:             SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
351:             SpaceProgram::OpenOffice,
352:             SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom,
353:         ] {
354:             assert!(
355:                 !spaces_for(program, &footprint, &dense, 0.5).is_empty(),
356:                 "{program:?} should be eligible for interior partitioning"
357:             );
358:         }
359:         assert!(
360:             spaces_for(SpaceProgram::Storage, &footprint, &dense, 0.5).is_empty(),
361:             "programs outside the eligible set must stay bare shells"
362:         );
363:     }
364: 
365:     #[test]
366:     fn tolerance_for_symmetry_centers_the_structural_phase() {
367:         let aseed = 0.37;
368:         let free = structure_for(&genome_with(0.5, 0.0), aseed);
369:         assert_eq!(
370:             free.phase,
371:             (snap(aseed * 4.0), snap(aseed * 8.0 % 4.0)),
372:             "tolerance 0 must reproduce the original freely offset phase"
373:         );
374:         let centered = structure_for(&genome_with(0.5, 1.0), aseed);
375:         assert_eq!(
376:             centered.phase,
377:             (0.0, 0.0),
378:             "tolerance 1 must center the bay grid on the footprint"
379:         );
380:     }
381: 
382:     #[test]
383:     fn tolerance_for_symmetry_mirrors_and_centers_sparse_pendants() {
384:         let footprint = Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 10.0);
385:         let aseed = 0.6;
386:         let jittered = fixtures_for(&genome_with(0.5, 0.0), &footprint, true, aseed);
387:         let centered = fixtures_for(&genome_with(0.5, 1.0), &footprint, true, aseed);
388:         assert_eq!(jittered.len(), centered.len());
389:         assert!(
390:             jittered.iter().zip(&centered).any(|(j, c)| {
391:                 (j.at.x - c.at.x).abs() > 1e-3 || (j.at.z - c.at.z).abs() > 1e-3
392:             }),
393:             "full symmetry tolerance must move at least one pendant off its jittered spot"
394:         );
395:         // At full tolerance, an odd fixture count's middle pendant must land
396:         // exactly on the room's centerline (the mirrored layout's fixed
397:         // point), once snapped to the same lattice every position here uses.
398:         let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = footprint.bounds();
399:         let (cx, cz) = (snap((x0 + x1) * 0.5), snap((z0 + z1) * 0.5));
400:         if centered.len() % 2 == 1 {
401:             let mid = &centered[centered.len() / 2];
402:             assert!((mid.at.x - cx).abs() < 1e-4 && (mid.at.z - cz).abs() < 1e-4);
403:         }
404:     }
405: }
````
