## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/project_aabb_footprint.rs
````rust
  1: //! Exact conservative screen bounds for one axis-aligned voxel box.
  2: //!
  3: //! Projecting only the box center and multiplying its world half-size by a
  4: //! fudge factor under-covers oblique boxes.  Perspective projection is a
  5: //! linear-fractional map, so each screen-coordinate extremum over the AABB
  6: //! clipped to the near half-space occurs at a clipped-polyhedron vertex.
  7: //! Those vertices are the original corners in front of the near plane plus
  8: //! intersections of the twelve box edges with that plane. Projecting this
  9: //! small fixed set gives the exact axis-aligned screen rectangle used by
 10: //! culling, LOD selection, splitting, and splat writing.
 11: 
 12: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 13: 
 14: pub(super) const NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH: f32 = 0.01;
 15: 
 16: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 17: pub(super) struct ScreenFootprint {
 18:     pub(super) center: [f32; 2],
 19:     pub(super) half_extent: [f32; 2],
 20:     /// Nearest camera-space depth of any AABB corner.
 21:     pub(super) nearest_depth: f32,
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl ScreenFootprint {
 25:     /// Scalar radius used by the square-splat target and square HZ tiles.
 26:     /// It encloses the exact projected rectangle without an empirical pad.
 27:     pub(super) fn enclosing_radius(self) -> f32 {
 28:         self.half_extent[0].max(self.half_extent[1])
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     pub(super) fn outside_framebuffer(self, width: usize, height: usize) -> bool {
 32:         self.center[0] + self.half_extent[0] < 0.0
 33:             || self.center[0] - self.half_extent[0] >= width as f32
 34:             || self.center[1] + self.half_extent[1] < 0.0
 35:             || self.center[1] - self.half_extent[1] >= height as f32
 36:     }
 37: }
 38: 
 39: /// Exact camera-depth interval of an AABB.  This support-function form is
 40: /// equivalent to testing all corners but avoids eight dot products for the
 41: /// behind/near-plane decision.
 42: pub(super) fn aabb_camera_depth_interval(
 43:     camera: &Camera,
 44:     center_relative_to_camera: [f32; 3],
 45:     half_size: f32,
 46: ) -> [f32; 2] {
 47:     let center_depth = dot(center_relative_to_camera, camera.forward);
 48:     let depth_radius =
 49:         half_size * (camera.forward[0].abs() + camera.forward[1].abs() + camera.forward[2].abs());
 50:     [center_depth - depth_radius, center_depth + depth_radius]
 51: }
 52: 
 53: /// Projects the exact vertices of an AABB clipped against the near plane.
 54: /// Returns `None` for non-finite/malformed or wholly-behind geometry.
 55: pub(super) fn project_screen_footprint(
 56:     camera: &Camera,
 57:     min: [f32; 3],
 58:     size: f32,
 59:     nearest_depth: f32,
 60: ) -> Option<ScreenFootprint> {
 61:     if !size.is_finite()
 62:         || size <= 0.0
 63:         || !nearest_depth.is_finite()
 64:         || min.into_iter().any(|coordinate| !coordinate.is_finite())
 65:     {
 66:         return None;
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     let mut relative_corners = [[0.0; 3]; 8];
 70:     let mut depths = [0.0; 8];
 71:     for octant in 0..8usize {
 72:         let corner = [
 73:             min[0] + if octant & 1 != 0 { size } else { 0.0 },
 74:             min[1] + if octant & 2 != 0 { size } else { 0.0 },
 75:             min[2] + if octant & 4 != 0 { size } else { 0.0 },
 76:         ];
 77:         let relative = [
 78:             corner[0] - camera.pos[0],
 79:             corner[1] - camera.pos[1],
 80:             corner[2] - camera.pos[2],
 81:         ];
 82:         let depth = dot(relative, camera.forward);
 83:         if !depth.is_finite() || relative.into_iter().any(|component| !component.is_finite()) {
 84:             return None;
 85:         }
 86:         relative_corners[octant] = relative;
 87:         depths[octant] = depth;
 88:     }
 89: 
 90:     let mut screen_min = [f32::INFINITY; 2];
 91:     let mut screen_max = [f32::NEG_INFINITY; 2];
 92:     let mut include_projection = |relative: [f32; 3], depth: f32| -> Option<()> {
 93:         let inverse_depth = 1.0 / depth;
 94:         let screen = [
 95:             camera.half_w + dot(relative, camera.right) * inverse_depth * camera.focal_px,
 96:             camera.half_h - dot(relative, camera.up) * inverse_depth * camera.focal_px,
 97:         ];
 98:         if screen.into_iter().any(|coordinate| !coordinate.is_finite()) {
 99:             return None;
100:         }
101:         for axis in 0..2 {
102:             screen_min[axis] = screen_min[axis].min(screen[axis]);
103:             screen_max[axis] = screen_max[axis].max(screen[axis]);
104:         }
105:         Some(())
106:     };
107: 
108:     for octant in 0..8usize {
109:         if depths[octant] >= NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH {
110:             include_projection(relative_corners[octant], depths[octant])?;
111:         }
112:     }
113: 
114:     // Each undirected AABB edge appears once: its low endpoint has the
115:     // corresponding axis bit clear. Crossing edges add the vertices created
116:     // by clipping the box against camera-space z = near.
117:     for axis_bit in [1usize, 2, 4] {
118:         for low in 0..8usize {
119:             if low & axis_bit != 0 {
120:                 continue;
121:             }
122:             let high = low | axis_bit;
123:             let low_depth = depths[low];
124:             let high_depth = depths[high];
125:             let crosses = (low_depth < NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH && high_depth > NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH)
126:                 || (high_depth < NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH && low_depth > NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH);
127:             if !crosses {
128:                 continue;
129:             }
130:             let t = (NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH - low_depth) / (high_depth - low_depth);
131:             let intersection = [
132:                 relative_corners[low][0]
133:                     + (relative_corners[high][0] - relative_corners[low][0]) * t,
134:                 relative_corners[low][1]
135:                     + (relative_corners[high][1] - relative_corners[low][1]) * t,
136:                 relative_corners[low][2]
137:                     + (relative_corners[high][2] - relative_corners[low][2]) * t,
138:             ];
139:             include_projection(intersection, NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH)?;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:     if screen_min[0] == f32::INFINITY {
144:         return None;
145:     }
146: 
147:     let center = [
148:         (screen_min[0] + screen_max[0]) * 0.5,
149:         (screen_min[1] + screen_max[1]) * 0.5,
150:     ];
151:     let half_extent = [
152:         (screen_max[0] - screen_min[0]) * 0.5,
153:         (screen_max[1] - screen_min[1]) * 0.5,
154:     ];
155:     Some(ScreenFootprint {
156:         center,
157:         half_extent,
158:         nearest_depth: nearest_depth.max(NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH),
159:     })
160: }
161:
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/render_cpu_frame.rs
````rust
  1: //! Orchestrate one complete CPU-splat frame.
  2: //!
  3: //! The sequence is intentionally visible in [`SoftwareRasterizer::render_cpu_frame`]:
  4: //! capture atmosphere, clear reusable buffers, build the camera, choose chunk
  5: //! order, reject non-contributing chunks, traverse, then draw flare cores.
  6: //! Individual rendering algorithms live behind those named operations.
  7: 
  8: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams};
  9: 
 10: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 11: use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
 12: use super::frame_work_budget::FrameWorkBudget;
 13: use super::project_aabb_footprint::{
 14:     NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH, aabb_camera_depth_interval, project_screen_footprint,
 15: };
 16: use super::select_lights_for_chunk::select_lights_for_chunk;
 17: 
 18: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 19:     pub(super) fn render_cpu_frame(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
 20:         self.environment = frame.environment;
 21:         self.frame_work_budget =
 22:             FrameWorkBudget::for_target(&self.settings, self.width(), self.height());
 23:         self.clear();
 24:         self.reset_frame_telemetry();
 25:         if self.atlas.is_empty() {
 26:             return;
 27:         }
 28: 
 29:         let camera = Camera::new(frame, self.width(), self.height(), &self.settings);
 30:         let ordered_chunks = chunks_in_draw_order(
 31:             chunks,
 32:             frame.camera_pos,
 33:             self.settings.toggles.front_to_back,
 34:         );
 35:         // Reused across chunks: one world-fixture scan per chunk, no
 36:         // per-splat allocation and no truncation of overlapping lights.
 37:         let mut chunk_scene_lights = std::mem::take(&mut self.chunk_light_scratch);
 38:         let global_hero_id = frame.active_scene_lights().first().map(|light| light.id);
 39: 
 40:         for chunk in ordered_chunks {
 41:             // Do not keep scanning fixtures/chunks after an absolute work
 42:             // budget has ended traversal for this frame.
 43:             if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes)
 44:                 || self.frame_work_budget.nodes_exhausted(self.visited_nodes)
 45:             {
 46:                 self.budget_exhausted = true;
 47:                 break;
 48:             }
 49:             if self.settings.toggles.distance_cull
 50:                 && !chunk_can_contribute(
 51:                     chunk,
 52:                     &camera,
 53:                     self.width(),
 54:                     self.height(),
 55:                     self.settings.max_draw_distance,
 56:                 )
 57:             {
 58:                 continue;
 59:             }
 60:             select_lights_for_chunk(frame.active_scene_lights(), chunk, &mut chunk_scene_lights);
 61:             self.traverse_voxel_chunk(&camera, chunks, chunk, &chunk_scene_lights, global_hero_id);
 62:         }
 63: 
 64:         self.chunk_light_scratch = chunk_scene_lights;
 65:         self.draw_visible_flare_cores(frame, &camera);
 66:         self.hero_light_visibility.advance_frame();
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     fn reset_frame_telemetry(&mut self) {
 70:         self.visited_nodes = 0;
 71:         self.budget_exhausted = false;
 72:         self.max_virtual_depth_reached = 0;
 73:         self.splat_count = 0;
 74:         self.pixel_writes = 0;
 75:     }
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /// Front-to-back ordering is an optional performance policy; fine depth
 79: /// testing makes the original chunk order the output-equivalent reference.
 80: fn chunks_in_draw_order(
 81:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 82:     camera_position: [f32; 3],
 83:     front_to_back: bool,
 84: ) -> Vec<&ChunkDraw> {
 85:     let mut ordered: Vec<_> = chunks.iter().collect();
 86:     if front_to_back {
 87:         ordered.sort_by(|a, b| {
 88:             chunk_distance_sq(a, camera_position).total_cmp(&chunk_distance_sq(b, camera_position))
 89:         });
 90:     }
 91:     ordered
 92: }
 93: 
 94: /// Conservative chunk-level distance and screen-bounds rejection.
 95: fn chunk_can_contribute(
 96:     chunk: &ChunkDraw,
 97:     camera: &Camera,
 98:     width: usize,
 99:     height: usize,
100:     max_draw_distance: f32,
101: ) -> bool {
102:     let half_size = chunk.world_size * 0.5;
103:     let center = [
104:         chunk.origin[0] + half_size,
105:         chunk.origin[1] + half_size,
106:         chunk.origin[2] + half_size,
107:     ];
108:     let radius = chunk.world_size * 0.5 * 3.0_f32.sqrt();
109:     let relative_to_camera = [
110:         center[0] - camera.pos[0],
111:         center[1] - camera.pos[1],
112:         center[2] - camera.pos[2],
113:     ];
114: 
115:     if dot(relative_to_camera, relative_to_camera).sqrt() - radius > max_draw_distance {
116:         return false;
117:     }
118:     let depth_interval = aabb_camera_depth_interval(camera, relative_to_camera, half_size);
119:     if depth_interval[1] <= NEAR_PLANE_DEPTH {
120:         return false;
121:     }
122: 
123:     project_screen_footprint(camera, chunk.origin, chunk.world_size, depth_interval[0])
124:         .is_some_and(|footprint| !footprint.outside_framebuffer(width, height))
125: }
126: 
127: fn chunk_distance_sq(chunk: &ChunkDraw, position: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
128:     let half = chunk.world_size * 0.5;
129:     let dx = chunk.origin[0] + half - position[0];
130:     let dz = chunk.origin[2] + half - position[2];
131:     dx * dx + dz * dz
132: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/resolve_hero_light_visibility.rs
````rust
  1: //! Resolve the CPU renderer's optional hero-light visibility term.
  2: //!
  3: //! Hero rays are intentionally a policy layer around the exact SVO raycast:
  4: //! they are limited to nearby, non-emissive receivers, stopped when the frame
  5: //! is already expensive, and amortized through a position-hashed cache. The
  6: //! traversal only asks for a visibility factor; it does not know how that
  7: //! factor is budgeted or cached.
  8: 
  9: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightSource};
 10: 
 11: use super::super::camera::dot;
 12: use super::super::raycast::{ray_box_interval, svo_segment_is_occluded};
 13: use super::super::settings::CpuShadowMode;
 14: use super::super::shading::HeroLightVisibility;
 15: use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
 16: 
 17: const CACHE_ENTRIES: usize = 65_536;
 18: const RETRACE_PERIOD_FRAMES: usize = 4;
 19: const MAX_RECEIVER_DISTANCE: f32 = 24.0;
 20: const RECEIVER_EXIT_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 21: const EMITTER_ENDPOINT_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 22: /// Above this write level, hero shadow rays are no longer affordable.
 23: const SHADOW_PIXEL_BUDGET: usize = 1_500_000;
 24: 
 25: /// Persistent visibility samples and the staggered refresh clock.
 26: pub(super) struct HeroLightVisibilityCache {
 27:     samples: Vec<CachedVisibility>,
 28:     frame_index: usize,
 29: }
 30: 
 31: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Default)]
 32: struct CachedVisibility {
 33:     query_key: u64,
 34:     visibility: f32,
 35:     valid: bool,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: impl HeroLightVisibilityCache {
 39:     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
 40:         Self {
 41:             samples: vec![CachedVisibility::default(); CACHE_ENTRIES],
 42:             frame_index: 0,
 43:         }
 44:     }
 45: 
 46:     pub(super) fn advance_frame(&mut self) {
 47:         self.frame_index = self.frame_index.wrapping_add(1);
 48:     }
 49: }
 50: 
 51: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 52:     /// Returns no override for the reference/no-shadow path, otherwise an
 53:     /// id-matched binary SVO visibility sample for one real scene fixture.
 54:     pub(super) fn resolve_hero_light_visibility(
 55:         &mut self,
 56:         chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 57:         center: [f32; 3],
 58:         receiver_world_size: f32,
 59:         is_emissive: bool,
 60:         receiver_distance: f32,
 61:         hero: Option<&LightSource>,
 62:     ) -> Option<HeroLightVisibility> {
 63:         let hero = hero?;
 64:         let affordable =
 65:             receiver_distance <= MAX_RECEIVER_DISTANCE && self.pixel_writes < SHADOW_PIXEL_BUDGET;
 66:         if self.settings.shadows != CpuShadowMode::Hero || is_emissive || !affordable {
 67:             return None;
 68:         }
 69: 
 70:         let query_key = hash_receiver_and_light(center, receiver_world_size, hero.id);
 71:         let cache_index = query_key as usize % self.hero_light_visibility.samples.len();
 72:         let should_trace = (query_key as usize + self.hero_light_visibility.frame_index)
 73:             .is_multiple_of(RETRACE_PERIOD_FRAMES);
 74:         let cached = self.hero_light_visibility.samples[cache_index];
 75:         if !should_trace && cached.valid && cached.query_key == query_key {
 76:             return Some(HeroLightVisibility {
 77:                 light_id: hero.id,
 78:                 visibility: cached.visibility,
 79:             });
 80:         }
 81: 
 82:         let visibility = trace_hero_fixture(
 83:             &self.atlas,
 84:             chunks,
 85:             center,
 86:             receiver_world_size,
 87:             hero.position,
 88:         );
 89:         self.hero_light_visibility.samples[cache_index] = CachedVisibility {
 90:             query_key,
 91:             visibility,
 92:             valid: true,
 93:         };
 94:         Some(HeroLightVisibility {
 95:             light_id: hero.id,
 96:             visibility,
 97:         })
 98:     }
 99: }
100: 
101: fn hash_receiver_and_light(center: [f32; 3], world_size: f32, light_id: u64) -> u64 {
102:     let mut key = light_id ^ 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
103:     for value in [center[0], center[1], center[2], world_size] {
104:         let bits = if value == 0.0 { 0 } else { value.to_bits() };
105:         key ^= u64::from(bits);
106:         key = key.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
107:     }
108:     key ^= key >> 33;
109:     key = key.wrapping_mul(0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd);
110:     key ^ (key >> 33)
111: }
112: 
113: fn trace_hero_fixture(
114:     atlas: &[u32],
115:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
116:     center: [f32; 3],
117:     receiver_world_size: f32,
118:     light_position: [f32; 3],
119: ) -> f32 {
120:     let to_light = [
121:         light_position[0] - center[0],
122:         light_position[1] - center[1],
123:         light_position[2] - center[2],
124:     ];
125:     let distance_to_light = dot(to_light, to_light).sqrt();
126:     if distance_to_light <= 0.001 {
127:         return 1.0;
128:     }
129: 
130:     let inverse_distance = 1.0 / distance_to_light;
131:     let direction = to_light.map(|component| component * inverse_distance);
132:     let receiver_half = receiver_world_size * 0.5;
133:     let receiver_min = center.map(|coordinate| coordinate - receiver_half);
134:     let receiver_max = center.map(|coordinate| coordinate + receiver_half);
135:     let Some(receiver_interval) = ray_box_interval(center, direction, receiver_min, receiver_max)
136:     else {
137:         return 1.0;
138:     };
139:     let origin_offset = receiver_interval.exit.max(0.0) + RECEIVER_EXIT_BIAS;
140:     let trace_length = distance_to_light - origin_offset - EMITTER_ENDPOINT_BIAS;
141:     if trace_length <= 0.0 {
142:         return 1.0;
143:     }
144:     let origin = [
145:         center[0] + direction[0] * origin_offset,
146:         center[1] + direction[1] * origin_offset,
147:         center[2] + direction[2] * origin_offset,
148:     ];
149:     if svo_segment_is_occluded(atlas, chunks, origin, direction, trace_length) {
150:         0.0
151:     } else {
152:         1.0
153:     }
154: }
155: 
156: #[cfg(test)]
157: mod tests {
158:     use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
159: 
160:     use super::trace_hero_fixture;
161: 
162:     #[test]
163:     fn coarse_receiver_does_not_occlude_its_own_hero_ray() {
164:         // One solid root leaf fills the whole 4u chunk. A center-biased ray
165:         // would immediately hit it; exiting the represented receiver first
166:         // leaves no geometry between its top face and the fixture.
167:         let atlas = [1, 1, 0xFF_FF_FF, 15];
168:         let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
169:             origin: [0.0; 3],
170:             root_index: 0,
171:             world_size: 4.0,
172:             voxel_size: 4.0,
173:             svo_depth: 0,
174:         }];
175: 
176:         let visibility = trace_hero_fixture(&atlas, &chunks, [2.0, 2.0, 2.0], 4.0, [2.0, 8.0, 2.0]);
177: 
178:         assert_eq!(visibility, 1.0);
179:     }
180: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/rasterizer/select_lights_for_chunk.rs
````rust
  1: //! Build an exact finite-support fixture cluster for one voxel chunk.
  2: //!
  3: //! Traversal shades many splats from the same chunk. Scanning every world
  4: //! fixture for every splat would dominate the CPU path, so the frame scans
  5: //! the fixture list once per chunk. A light is rejected only when the minimum
  6: //! distance between its emitter geometry and the chunk AABB exceeds its
  7: //! authored finite range; this changes no radiometric result.
  8: 
  9: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightKind, LightSource};
 10: 
 11: pub(super) fn select_lights_for_chunk(
 12:     scene_lights: &[LightSource],
 13:     chunk: &ChunkDraw,
 14:     selected: &mut Vec<LightSource>,
 15: ) {
 16:     selected.clear();
 17:     selected.extend(
 18:         scene_lights
 19:             .iter()
 20:             .copied()
 21:             .filter(|light| light_can_reach_chunk(light, chunk)),
 22:     );
 23: }
 24: 
 25: fn light_can_reach_chunk(light: &LightSource, chunk: &ChunkDraw) -> bool {
 26:     if !light.enabled
 27:         || !light.radius.is_finite()
 28:         || light.radius <= 0.0
 29:         || light
 30:             .position
 31:             .iter()
 32:             .any(|coordinate| !coordinate.is_finite())
 33:     {
 34:         return false;
 35:     }
 36: 
 37:     let emitter_half_size = match light.kind {
 38:         LightKind::Point => [0.0, 0.0],
 39:         LightKind::CeilingPanel | LightKind::Strip | LightKind::Emergency => {
 40:             if light
 41:                 .half_size
 42:                 .iter()
 43:                 .any(|half| !half.is_finite() || *half <= 0.0)
 44:             {
 45:                 return false;
 46:             }
 47:             light.half_size
 48:         }
 49:     };
 50: 
 51:     let chunk_max = chunk.origin.map(|minimum| minimum + chunk.world_size);
 52:     let dx = interval_distance(
 53:         light.position[0] - emitter_half_size[0],
 54:         light.position[0] + emitter_half_size[0],
 55:         chunk.origin[0],
 56:         chunk_max[0],
 57:     );
 58:     let dy = point_interval_distance(light.position[1], chunk.origin[1], chunk_max[1]);
 59:     let dz = interval_distance(
 60:         light.position[2] - emitter_half_size[1],
 61:         light.position[2] + emitter_half_size[1],
 62:         chunk.origin[2],
 63:         chunk_max[2],
 64:     );
 65:     dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz <= light.radius * light.radius
 66: }
 67: 
 68: fn interval_distance(a_min: f32, a_max: f32, b_min: f32, b_max: f32) -> f32 {
 69:     if a_max < b_min {
 70:         b_min - a_max
 71:     } else if b_max < a_min {
 72:         a_min - b_max
 73:     } else {
 74:         0.0
 75:     }
 76: }
 77: 
 78: fn point_interval_distance(point: f32, minimum: f32, maximum: f32) -> f32 {
 79:     if point < minimum {
 80:         minimum - point
 81:     } else if point > maximum {
 82:         point - maximum
 83:     } else {
 84:         0.0
 85:     }
 86: }
 87:
````

````rust
  1: //! Validated configuration for the CPU splatter.
  2: //!
  3: //! The browser owns *selection* (preset or custom controls), while the
  4: //! renderer receives one immutable [`CpuRenderSettings`] snapshot per frame.
  5: //! No traversal or shading function reads DOM state or atomics directly.
  6: //!
  7: //! The neighboring files make the two policies explicit:
  8: //!
  9: //! * [`quality_preset`] is the small, typed product model shown in Settings.
 10: //! * [`validation`] is the only place that accepts untrusted browser values.

 20: /// Per-splat shadow tracing mode.
 21: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 22: pub enum CpuShadowMode {
 23:     /// No fixture shadow rays. Direct diffuse lighting still renders.
 24:     Off,
 25:     /// Trace the selected hero fixture for each affordable splat.
 26:     Hero,
 27:     /// Correctness reference: trace every contributing point-light endpoint
 28:     /// and every 2x2 rectangle quadrature endpoint through the SVO scene.
 29:     Full,
 30: }
 31: 
 32: /// Effective flashlight visibility policy. It is derived from the independent
 33: /// `rt_beam_occlusion` switch instead of being silently coupled to a preset.
 34: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 35: pub enum CpuFlashlightVisibility {
 36:     /// Fast diagnostic path: the cone is evaluated without scene visibility.
 37:     Unoccluded,
 38:     /// Correctness path: trace the scene between the light and receiver.
 39:     TraceScene,
 40: }
 41: 
 42: impl CpuShadowMode {
 43:     /// Stable browser-facing representation.
 44:     pub const fn from_id(id: u32) -> Self {
 45:         match id {
 46:             1 => Self::Hero,
 47:             2 => Self::Full,
 48:             _ => Self::Off,
 49:         }
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     pub const fn id(self) -> u32 {
 53:         match self {
 54:             Self::Off => 0,
 55:             Self::Hero => 1,
 56:             Self::Full => 2,
 57:         }
 58:     }
 59: }
 60: 
 61: /// Quality controls for the software rasterizer.
 62: ///
 63: /// Fields are public because native reference fixtures construct exact test
 64: /// configurations. Browser values must enter through [`Self::validated`].
 65: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 66: pub struct CpuRenderSettings {
 67:     /// Multiplier on the CPU renderer's quarter-viewport baseline.
 68:     /// `1.0` is 25% of the GPU backing dimensions; `2.0` is 50%.
 69:     pub internal_scale: f32,
 70:     /// Projected-radius threshold below which a subtree becomes one MIP
 71:     /// splat. Smaller values preserve finer distant geometry.
 72:     pub lod_cutoff_px: f32,
 73:     /// Largest allowed projected splat *radius*. Smaller values virtually
 74:     /// subdivide large leaves and reduce block artifacts.
 75:     pub max_splat_radius_px: f32,
 76:     /// Recursion cap for virtual subdivision of a solid leaf.
 77:     pub max_virtual_depth: u8,
 78:     /// World-space floor for virtual subdivision.
 79:     pub min_split_size: f32,
 80:     /// Chunk/node rejection distance in world units.
 81:     pub max_draw_distance: f32,
 82:     /// Minimum occupancy for one collapsed MIP splat.
 83:     pub min_mip_occupancy: f32,
 84:     /// Fixture-shadow quality. This is independent from flashlight
 85:     /// occlusion, which remains an individually diagnosable optimization.
 86:     pub shadows: CpuShadowMode,
 87:     /// `tan(vertical_fov / 2)`; supplied by the camera composition root.
 88:     pub fov_tan: f32,
 89:     /// Independent optimization switches shared with other renderers.

 91: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Named CPU quality profiles.
  2: //!
  3: //! Presets only choose scalar quality and workload budgets. They never hide

  7: use crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles;

 11: /// Stable IDs cross the WASM boundary; names remain presentation concerns.
 12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 13: #[repr(u32)]
 14: pub enum CpuQualityPreset {
 15:     Performance = 0,
 16:     Balanced = 1,
 17:     Quality = 2,
 18:     Maximum = 3,
 19: }
 20: 
 21: impl CpuQualityPreset {
 22:     pub const fn from_id(id: u32) -> Self {
 23:         match id {
 24:             0 => Self::Performance,
 25:             2 => Self::Quality,
 26:             3 => Self::Maximum,
 27:             _ => Self::Balanced,
 28:         }
 29:     }
 30: 
 31:     /// Complete renderer settings for this profile.
 32:     pub fn settings(self) -> CpuRenderSettings {
 33:         let (
 34:             internal_scale,
 35:             lod_cutoff_px,
 36:             max_splat_radius_px,
 37:             max_virtual_depth,
 38:             max_draw_distance,
 39:             min_mip_occupancy,
 40:             shadows,
 41:         ) = match self {
 42:             Self::Performance => (0.5, 1.5, 14.0, 4, 72.0, 0.35, CpuShadowMode::Off),
 43:             Self::Balanced => (1.0, 1.0, 8.0, 5, 96.0, 0.25, CpuShadowMode::Off),
 44:             Self::Quality => (1.5, 0.65, 4.0, 6, 128.0, 0.12, CpuShadowMode::Hero),
 45:             Self::Maximum => (2.0, 0.35, 2.0, 8, 160.0, 0.05, CpuShadowMode::Full),
 46:         };
 47: 
 48:         CpuRenderSettings {
 49:             internal_scale,
 50:             lod_cutoff_px,
 51:             max_splat_radius_px,
 52:             max_virtual_depth,
 53:             min_split_size: 0.005,
 54:             max_draw_distance,
 55:             min_mip_occupancy,
 56:             shadows,
 57:             fov_tan: 0.767,
 58:             toggles: RenderToggles::default(),
 59:         }
 60:     }
 61: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/evaluate_dynamic_irradiance.rs

````rust
 1: //! Runtime point-light irradiance (currently dropped flares).
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 4: 
 5: use super::super::camera::Camera;
 6: use super::evaluate_fixture_irradiance::point_light_irradiance;
 7: 
 8: pub(super) fn dynamic_irradiance(
 9:     cam: &Camera,
10:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
11:     normal: [f32; 3],
12: ) -> LinearRgb {
13:     let mut sum = [0.0; 3];
14:     for light in &cam.dynamic_lights[..cam.dynamic_light_count] {
15:         let contribution = point_light_irradiance(
16:             surface_position,
17:             normal,
18:             light.position,
19:             light.color,
20:             light.radius,
21:             light.intensity,
22:         );
23:         for channel in 0..3 {
24:             sum[channel] += contribution[channel];
25:         }
26:     }
27:     sum
28: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Emitted radiance for exposed fixture undersides.
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 4: 
 5: use super::SplatSurface;
 6: 
 7: pub(crate) fn emission_strength(base_color: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
 8:     let near = |reference: [f32; 3]| {
 9:         base_color
10:             .into_iter()
11:             .zip(reference)
12:             .all(|(actual, expected)| (actual - expected).abs() <= 0.5)
13:     };
14:     if near([255.0, 248.0, 214.0]) {
15:         10.0
16:     } else if near([255.0, 68.0, 51.0]) {
17:         8.0
18:     } else if near([159.0, 196.0, 232.0]) {
19:         0.9
20:     } else {
21:         1.0
22:     }
23: }
24: 
25: #[cfg(test)]
26: pub(super) fn emitted_radiance(
27:     surface: &SplatSurface,
28:     albedo: LinearRgb,
29:     normal: [f32; 3],
30: ) -> Option<LinearRgb> {
31:     emitted_radiance_with_strength(
32:         surface,
33:         albedo,
34:         normal,
35:         surface
36:             .is_emissive
37:             .then(|| emission_strength(surface.base_color)),
38:     )
39: }
40: 
41: /// Prepared-material variant used by production traversal. Its scalar comes
42: /// from the material id, so no encoded color has to travel through every
43: /// virtual-node visit merely to identify one of three fixture strengths.
44: pub(super) fn emitted_radiance_with_strength(
45:     surface: &SplatSurface,
46:     albedo: LinearRgb,
47:     normal: [f32; 3],
48:     strength: Option<f32>,
49: ) -> Option<LinearRgb> {
50:     if !surface.is_emissive || normal[1] >= -0.5 {
51:         return None;
52:     }
53:     Some(albedo.map(|channel| channel * strength.unwrap_or(1.0)))
54: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/evaluate_fixture_irradiance.rs
````rust
  1: //! Analytic static-fixture irradiance. Point emitters and finite rectangular
  2: //! ceiling emitters share one sanitized radiometric boundary.
  3: 
  4: use crate::application::ports::{LightKind, LightSource};
  5: use crate::application::rendering::{LinearRgb, finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation};
  6: 
  7: use super::super::camera::dot;
  8: use super::FrameLighting;
  9: use super::trace_direct_light_visibility::DirectLightVisibility;
 10: 
 11: const GAUSS_ABSCISSA: f32 = 0.577_350_26;
 12: const MINIMUM_LIGHT_DISTANCE: f32 = 0.2;
 13: 
 14: /// Exact zero test for the four quadrature samples. This is not a lighting
 15: /// approximation: it rejects work only when every sample is outside the
 16: /// finite support, behind the one-sided emitter, or behind the receiver.
 17: fn rectangle_can_contribute(
 18:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
 19:     normal: [f32; 3],
 20:     light: &LightSource,
 21: ) -> bool {
 22:     if !light.radius.is_finite() || light.radius <= 0.0 {
 23:         return false;
 24:     }
 25:     let center_delta = [
 26:         light.position[0] - surface_position[0],
 27:         light.position[1] - surface_position[1],
 28:         light.position[2] - surface_position[2],
 29:     ];
 30:     if center_delta
 31:         .into_iter()
 32:         .chain(normal)
 33:         .any(|component| !component.is_finite())
 34:     {
 35:         return false;
 36:     }
 37: 
 38:     // Every sample shares the emitter height. A horizontal panel emits only
 39:     // downward, so receivers level with or above it get exactly zero.
 40:     if center_delta[1] <= 0.0 {
 41:         return false;
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     let sample_extent_x = GAUSS_ABSCISSA * light.half_size[0];
 45:     let sample_extent_z = GAUSS_ABSCISSA * light.half_size[1];
 46:     let nearest_x = (center_delta[0].abs() - sample_extent_x).max(0.0);
 47:     let nearest_z = (center_delta[2].abs() - sample_extent_z).max(0.0);
 48:     let nearest_squared =
 49:         nearest_x * nearest_x + center_delta[1] * center_delta[1] + nearest_z * nearest_z;
 50:     if nearest_squared >= light.radius * light.radius {
 51:         return false;
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     // Dot products are affine over the sample rectangle, so this bound is
 55:     // the exact maximum receiver cosine numerator among its four corners.
 56:     let maximum_receiver_dot = dot(normal, center_delta)
 57:         + normal[0].abs() * sample_extent_x
 58:         + normal[2].abs() * sample_extent_z;
 59:     maximum_receiver_dot > 0.0
 60: }
 61: 
 62: fn sanitized_light_scale(color: LinearRgb, intensity: f32) -> LinearRgb {
 63:     if !intensity.is_finite() || intensity <= 0.0 {
 64:         return [0.0; 3];
 65:     }
 66:     color.map(|channel| {
 67:         if channel.is_finite() {
 68:             channel.max(0.0) * intensity
 69:         } else {
 70:             0.0
 71:         }
 72:     })
 73: }
 74: 
 75: fn normalized(vector: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
 76:     if vector.into_iter().any(|component| !component.is_finite()) {
 77:         return None;
 78:     }
 79:     let scale = vector
 80:         .into_iter()
 81:         .fold(0.0_f32, |largest, component| largest.max(component.abs()));
 82:     if scale == 0.0 {
 83:         return None;
 84:     }
 85:     let scaled = vector.map(|component| component / scale);
 86:     let length = dot(scaled, scaled).sqrt();
 87:     Some(scaled.map(|component| component / length))
 88: }
 89: 
 90: /// Reuses the one surface-to-light normalization for every geometric term.
 91: /// The generic rendering helpers normalize each argument independently;
 92: /// doing that twice per Gauss sample is mathematically redundant and was the
 93: /// dominant arithmetic cost in fixture-heavy CPU frames.
 94: pub(super) fn sample_geometry(
 95:     receiver_normal: [f32; 3],
 96:     surface_to_light: [f32; 3],
 97: ) -> Option<(f32, f32, f32)> {
 98:     let distance = dot(surface_to_light, surface_to_light).sqrt();
 99:     if !distance.is_finite() || distance <= 0.0 {
100:         return None;
101:     }
102:     let inverse_distance = 1.0 / distance;
103:     let direction = surface_to_light.map(|component| component * inverse_distance);
104:     let receiver_cosine = dot(receiver_normal, direction).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
105:     // Horizontal rectangular fixtures point down. For direction L from the
106:     // receiver to the light, dot(-Y, direction_light_to_receiver) == L.y.
107:     let downward_emitter_cosine = direction[1].clamp(0.0, 1.0);
108:     Some((distance, receiver_cosine, downward_emitter_cosine))
109: }
110: 
111: pub(super) fn point_light_irradiance(
112:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
113:     normal: [f32; 3],
114:     light_position: [f32; 3],
115:     color: LinearRgb,
116:     range: f32,
117:     intensity: f32,
118: ) -> LinearRgb {
119:     let delta = [
120:         light_position[0] - surface_position[0],
121:         light_position[1] - surface_position[1],
122:         light_position[2] - surface_position[2],
123:     ];
124:     let distance_squared = dot(delta, delta);
125:     if !range.is_finite()
126:         || range <= 0.0
127:         || !distance_squared.is_finite()
128:         || distance_squared >= range * range
129:     {
130:         return [0.0; 3];
131:     }
132:     let Some(normal) = normalized(normal) else {
133:         return [0.0; 3];
134:     };
135:     let Some((distance, geometry, _)) = sample_geometry(normal, delta) else {
136:         return [0.0; 3];
137:     };
138:     let attenuation =
139:         finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(distance, range, MINIMUM_LIGHT_DISTANCE);
140:     let scale = sanitized_light_scale(color, intensity);
141:     scale.map(|channel| channel * geometry * attenuation)
142: }
143: 
144: /// Deterministic 2x2 Gauss quadrature over a physical XZ rectangle.
145: #[cfg(test)]
146: pub(super) fn rectangle_light_irradiance(
147:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
148:     normal: [f32; 3],
149:     light: &LightSource,
150: ) -> LinearRgb {
151:     rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(
152:         surface_position,
153:         normal,
154:         light,
155:         DirectLightVisibility::unoccluded(),
156:     )
157: }
158: 
159: fn rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(
160:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
161:     normal: [f32; 3],
162:     light: &LightSource,
163:     visibility: DirectLightVisibility<'_>,
164: ) -> LinearRgb {
165:     let [half_x, half_z] = light.half_size;
166:     if !half_x.is_finite() || !half_z.is_finite() || half_x <= 0.0 || half_z <= 0.0 {
167:         return [0.0; 3];
168:     }
169:     if !rectangle_can_contribute(surface_position, normal, light) {
170:         return [0.0; 3];
171:     }
172:     let mut integral = 0.0;
173:     for x in [-GAUSS_ABSCISSA, GAUSS_ABSCISSA] {
174:         for z in [-GAUSS_ABSCISSA, GAUSS_ABSCISSA] {
175:             let sample = [
176:                 light.position[0] + x * half_x,
177:                 light.position[1],
178:                 light.position[2] + z * half_z,
179:             ];
180:             let surface_to_light = [
181:                 sample[0] - surface_position[0],
182:                 sample[1] - surface_position[1],
183:                 sample[2] - surface_position[2],
184:             ];
185:             let Some((distance, receiver_cosine, emitter_cosine)) =
186:                 sample_geometry(normal, surface_to_light)
187:             else {
188:                 continue;
189:             };
190:             if receiver_cosine <= 0.0
191:                 || emitter_cosine <= 0.0
192:                 || !visibility.sample_is_visible(surface_position, normal, sample)
193:             {
194:                 continue;
195:             }
196:             integral += receiver_cosine
197:                 * emitter_cosine
198:                 * finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(
199:                     distance,
200:                     light.radius,
201:                     MINIMUM_LIGHT_DISTANCE,
202:                 );
203:         }
204:     }
205:     let area = 4.0 * half_x * half_z;
206:     let scale = sanitized_light_scale(light.color, light.intensity);
207:     scale.map(|channel| channel * area * integral * 0.25)
208: }
209: 
210: fn scene_light_irradiance(
211:     light: &LightSource,
212:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
213:     normal: [f32; 3],
214:     visibility: DirectLightVisibility<'_>,
215: ) -> LinearRgb {
216:     if !light.enabled {
217:         return [0.0; 3];
218:     }
219:     match light.kind {
220:         LightKind::Point => {
221:             let contribution = point_light_irradiance(
222:                 surface_position,
223:                 normal,
224:                 light.position,
225:                 light.color,
226:                 light.radius,
227:                 light.intensity,
228:             );
229:             if contribution != [0.0; 3]
230:                 && !visibility.sample_is_visible(surface_position, normal, light.position)
231:             {
232:                 [0.0; 3]
233:             } else {
234:                 contribution
235:             }
236:         }
237:         LightKind::CeilingPanel | LightKind::Strip | LightKind::Emergency => {
238:             rectangle_light_irradiance_with_visibility(surface_position, normal, light, visibility)
239:         }
240:     }
241: }
242: 
243: #[cfg(test)]
244: pub(super) fn fixture_irradiance(
245:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
246:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
247:     normal: [f32; 3],
248: ) -> LinearRgb {
249:     fixture_irradiance_with_visibility(
250:         lighting,
251:         surface_position,
252:         normal,
253:         DirectLightVisibility::unoccluded(),
254:     )
255: }
256: 
257: pub(super) fn fixture_irradiance_with_visibility(
258:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
259:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
260:     normal: [f32; 3],
261:     direct_visibility: DirectLightVisibility<'_>,
262: ) -> LinearRgb {
263:     let mut sum = [0.0; 3];
264:     for light in lighting.scene_lights {
265:         let visibility = lighting
266:             .hero_visibility
267:             .filter(|hero| hero.light_id == light.id)
268:             .map_or(1.0, |hero| hero.visibility.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
269:         let contribution =
270:             scene_light_irradiance(light, surface_position, normal, direct_visibility);
271:         for channel in 0..3 {
272:             sum[channel] += contribution[channel] * visibility;
273:         }
274:     }
275:     sum
276: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Linear-radiance shading for one CPU splat.
 2: //!
 3: //! The file tree is the rendering sentence:
 4: //!
 5: //! 1. [`surface_reconstruction`] selects one physical receiver sample;
 6: //! 2. [`compose_environment_irradiance`], [`evaluate_fixture_irradiance`],
 7: //!    and [`evaluate_dynamic_irradiance`] build independent light terms;
 8: //! 3. [`evaluate_emission`] handles exposed luminous panel undersides;
 9: //! 4. [`shade_visible_splat`] composes reflection and flashlight energy;
10: //! 5. [`present_radiance`] applies atmosphere and display encoding once.
11: //!
12: //! Static fixtures in [`FrameLighting`] are authoritative. The quantized SVO
13: //! light level is an optional, restrained fill and cannot replace them.
14: 
15: mod compose_environment_irradiance;
16: mod evaluate_dynamic_irradiance;
17: mod evaluate_emission;
18: mod evaluate_fixture_irradiance;
19: mod present_radiance;
20: mod shade_visible_splat;
21: mod surface_reconstruction;
22: mod trace_direct_light_visibility;
23: 
24: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
25: 
26: use super::surface_geometry::SurfaceExposure;
27: 
28: #[cfg(test)]
29: pub(crate) use evaluate_emission::emission_strength;
30: pub(crate) use shade_visible_splat::shade_predecoded_with_frame_lighting;
31: pub use shade_visible_splat::shade_with_frame_lighting;
32: 
33: /// Everything the lighting model needs to know about one splat.
34: pub struct SplatSurface {
35:     /// World-space center of the shaded box.
36:     pub center: [f32; 3],
37:     /// World-space side length of the box.
38:     pub world_size: f32,
39:     /// Camera-space depth used by projection/depth testing. Fog recomputes
40:     /// the Euclidean path length from `center`; depth is not a path length.
41:     pub dist: f32,
42:     /// Authored sRGB albedo, 0..255 per channel.
43:     pub base_color: [f32; 3],
44:     /// Quantized colored cached diffuse-fill channels, 0..15. Analytic
45:     /// fixtures remain authoritative; this optional field is never promoted
46:     /// to direct light.
47:     pub baked_irradiance: [f32; 3],
48:     /// Authored voxel material. Thin architectural materials use this to
49:     /// preserve their physical orientation instead of behaving like cubes.
50:     pub voxel_type: u32,
51:     pub is_emissive: bool,
52:     /// Prepared physical surface area open to air. Shading may choose among
53:     /// these faces but must never invent a face outside this contract.
54:     pub exposure: SurfaceExposure,
55:     /// Number of occupied siblings in the parent octant (ambient AO proxy).
56:     pub crowded_siblings: u32,
57: }
58: 
59: /// Visibility of one specific analytic fixture at the current receiver.
60: /// Keeping the light id beside the factor prevents an assumed-grid shadow
61: /// from accidentally darkening ambient or a different fixture.
62: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
63: pub struct HeroLightVisibility {
64:     pub light_id: u64,
65:     pub visibility: f32,
66: }
67: 
68: /// Immutable per-frame fixture inputs plus the one per-receiver hero query.
69: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
70: pub struct FrameLighting<'a> {
71:     pub scene_lights: &'a [LightSource],
72:     pub hero_visibility: Option<HeroLightVisibility>,
73: }
74: 
75: impl<'a> FrameLighting<'a> {
76:     pub fn unshadowed(scene_lights: &'a [LightSource]) -> Self {
77:         Self {
78:             scene_lights,
79:             hero_visibility: None,
80:         }
81:     }
82: 
83:     pub fn with_hero_visibility(
84:         scene_lights: &'a [LightSource],
85:         light_id: u64,
86:         visibility: f32,
87:     ) -> Self {
88:         Self {
89:             scene_lights,
90:             hero_visibility: Some(HeroLightVisibility {
91:                 light_id,
92:                 visibility: visibility.clamp(0.0, 1.0),
93:             }),
94:         }
95:     }
96: }
97:

99: mod tests;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/present_radiance.rs
````rust
 1: //! Compose the level atmosphere in linear RGB, tone-map, and encode once.
 2: 
 3: use crate::application::ports::Environment;
 4: use crate::application::rendering::{
 5:     LinearRgb, compose_fog, encode_display_color, fog_transmittance,
 6: };
 7: 
 8: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 9: use super::SplatSurface;
10: 
11: pub(super) fn view_distance(
12:     cam: &Camera,
13:     surface: &SplatSurface,
14:     surface_position: [f32; 3],
15: ) -> f32 {
16:     let delta = [
17:         surface_position[0] - cam.pos[0],
18:         surface_position[1] - cam.pos[1],
19:         surface_position[2] - cam.pos[2],
20:     ];
21:     let distance = dot(delta, delta).sqrt();
22:     if distance.is_finite() {
23:         distance
24:     } else {
25:         surface.dist.max(0.0)
26:     }
27: }
28: 
29: pub(super) fn present_radiance(
30:     radiance: LinearRgb,
31:     distance: f32,
32:     environment: &Environment,
33: ) -> [u8; 3] {
34:     let transmittance = fog_transmittance(distance, environment.fog_start, environment.fog_density);
35:     let through_fog = compose_fog(radiance, environment.fog_color, transmittance);
36:     encode_display_color(through_fog)
37:         .map(|channel| (channel * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8)
38: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/surface_reconstruction.rs
````rust
 1: //! Reconstruct one representative point and normal from an axis-aligned
 2: //! splat, then decode its authored albedo into linear RGB.
 3: 
 4: pub(super) use super::super::decode_srgb_albedo::decode_albedo;
 5: #[cfg(test)]
 6: pub(super) use super::super::decode_srgb_albedo::srgb_channel_to_linear;
 7: pub(super) use super::super::surface_geometry::representative_surface_position;
 8: use super::super::surface_geometry::select_surface_normal;
 9: use super::SplatSurface;
10: 
11: /// Exact normal of the AABB face entered by the center-directed camera ray.
12: /// For a centered cube this is the dominant ray axis. Ties use X, then Y,
13: /// then Z, making edge/corner views deterministic without inventing a
14: /// diagonal receiver cosine.
15: #[cfg(test)]
16: pub(super) fn camera_facing_aabb_normal(camera_to_surface: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
17:     if camera_to_surface
18:         .into_iter()
19:         .any(|component| !component.is_finite())
20:     {
21:         return None;
22:     }
23:     let absolute = camera_to_surface.map(f32::abs);
24:     let axis = if absolute[0] >= absolute[1] && absolute[0] >= absolute[2] {
25:         0
26:     } else if absolute[1] >= absolute[2] {
27:         1
28:     } else {
29:         2
30:     };
31:     if absolute[axis] <= 1.0e-6 {
32:         return None;
33:     }
34:     let mut normal = [0.0; 3];
35:     normal[axis] = if camera_to_surface[axis] > 0.0 {
36:         -1.0
37:     } else {
38:         1.0
39:     };
40:     Some(normal)
41: }
42: 
43: /// Selects one actual exposed face, with authored orientation for floor,
44: /// ceiling, and emissive panel materials. Camera dominance is used only for
45: /// cube-like materials and only among faces present in the geometry contract.
46: pub(super) fn representative_normal(
47:     surface: &SplatSurface,
48:     camera_to_surface: [f32; 3],
49: ) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
50:     select_surface_normal(
51:         surface.voxel_type,
52:         surface.is_emissive,
53:         surface.exposure,
54:         camera_to_surface,
55:     )
56: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/trace_direct_light_visibility.rs
````rust
 1: //! Exact finite SVO visibility segments for analytic fixture samples.
 2: //!
 3: //! The expensive CPU `Full` shadow policy calls this once for a point light
 4: //! and once for each of a rectangle's four Gauss samples. Receiver and
 5: //! emitter biases mirror the strict GPU raymarch reference so neither the
 6: //! receiver voxel nor the luminous endpoint shadows itself.
 7: 
 8: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 9: 
10: use super::super::camera::dot;
11: use super::super::raycast::svo_segment_is_occluded;
12: 
13: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
14: pub(super) struct DirectLightVisibility<'a> {
15:     atlas: &'a [u32],
16:     chunks: &'a [ChunkDraw],
17:     receiver_world_size: f32,
18:     trace_scene: bool,
19: }
20: 
21: impl<'a> DirectLightVisibility<'a> {
22:     pub(super) fn unoccluded() -> Self {
23:         Self {
24:             atlas: &[],
25:             chunks: &[],
26:             receiver_world_size: 0.0,
27:             trace_scene: false,
28:         }
29:     }
30: 
31:     pub(super) fn trace_scene(
32:         atlas: &'a [u32],
33:         chunks: &'a [ChunkDraw],
34:         receiver_world_size: f32,
35:     ) -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             atlas,
38:             chunks,
39:             receiver_world_size,
40:             trace_scene: true,
41:         }
42:     }
43: 
44:     pub(super) fn sample_is_visible(
45:         self,
46:         surface_position: [f32; 3],
47:         surface_normal: [f32; 3],
48:         sample_position: [f32; 3],
49:     ) -> bool {
50:         if !self.trace_scene {
51:             return true;
52:         }
53: 
54:         let bias = (self.receiver_world_size.abs() * 1.0e-3).max(1.0e-5);
55:         let origin = [
56:             surface_position[0] + surface_normal[0] * bias,
57:             surface_position[1] + surface_normal[1] * bias,
58:             surface_position[2] + surface_normal[2] * bias,
59:         ];
60:         let segment = [
61:             sample_position[0] - origin[0],
62:             sample_position[1] - origin[1],
63:             sample_position[2] - origin[2],
64:         ];
65:         let segment_length = dot(segment, segment).sqrt();
66:         if !segment_length.is_finite() || segment_length <= bias * 2.0 {
67:             return true;
68:         }
69:         let inverse_length = 1.0 / segment_length;
70:         let direction = segment.map(|component| component * inverse_length);
71:         let blocker_limit = segment_length - bias * 2.0;
72:         !svo_segment_is_occluded(self.atlas, self.chunks, origin, direction, blocker_limit)
73:     }
74: }
75: 
76: #[cfg(test)]
77: mod tests {
78:     use super::DirectLightVisibility;
79:     use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
80: 
81:     #[test]
82:     fn finite_sample_segment_detects_only_blockers_before_the_endpoint() {
83:         let atlas = [1, 1, 0x00ff_ffff, 0];
84:         let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
85:             origin: [0.0; 3],
86:             root_index: 0,
87:             world_size: 1.0,
88:             voxel_size: 1.0,
89:             svo_depth: 0,
90:         }];
91:         let visibility = DirectLightVisibility::trace_scene(&atlas, &chunks, 0.5);
92: 
93:         assert!(!visibility.sample_is_visible([0.5, 0.5, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0], [0.5, 0.5, 2.0],));
94:         assert!(
95:             visibility.sample_is_visible([0.5, 0.5, -1.0], [0.0, 0.0, 1.0], [0.5, 0.5, -0.25],)
96:         );
97:     }
98: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/project_surface_depth.rs
````rust
  1: //! Project one selected box face into an exact per-pixel depth plane.
  2: //!
  3: //! A square splat covers more screen pixels than the projected voxel face.
  4: //! Giving that whole square the voxel-center depth makes adjacent coplanar
  5: //! voxels disagree about the depth of the same physical plane.  The error is
  6: //! especially visible when a ceiling voxel overlaps a luminous panel.
  7: //!
  8: //! For a pinhole camera, reciprocal camera depth on a world-space plane is
  9: //! affine in screen coordinates.  The three coefficients below therefore
 10: //! recover the exact ray/plane intersection depth at every pixel without a
 11: //! per-pixel world-space ray construction.
 12: 
 13: use super::super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 14: use super::{SurfaceExposure, select_surface_normal};
 15: 
 16: /// Camera-depth information for one selected physical box face.
 17: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 18: pub(crate) struct ProjectedSurfaceDepth {
 19:     representative_depth: f32,
 20:     /// `1 / depth = ax + by + c`, evaluated at pixel centers.
 21:     reciprocal_depth: [f32; 3],
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl ProjectedSurfaceDepth {
 25:     /// Constant-depth constructor retained for non-surface flare splats and
 26:     /// narrow renderer tests. Production voxel surfaces use [`project_surface_depth`].
 27:     pub(crate) fn constant(depth: f32) -> Self {
 28:         Self {
 29:             representative_depth: depth,
 30:             reciprocal_depth: [0.0, 0.0, depth.recip()],
 31:         }
 32:     }
 33: 
 34:     pub(crate) fn representative_depth(self) -> f32 {
 35:         self.representative_depth
 36:     }
 37: 
 38:     /// Exact positive reciprocal camera depth at a target-space sample.
 39:     /// Fine depth comparison consumes this directly, avoiding a division for
 40:     /// every candidate pixel.
 41:     pub(crate) fn reciprocal_at_pixel(self, pixel: [f32; 2]) -> Option<f32> {
 42:         let inverse_depth = self.reciprocal_depth[0].mul_add(
 43:             pixel[0],
 44:             self.reciprocal_depth[1].mul_add(pixel[1], self.reciprocal_depth[2]),
 45:         );
 46:         if !inverse_depth.is_finite() || inverse_depth <= 0.0 {
 47:             return None;
 48:         }
 49:         Some(inverse_depth)
 50:     }
 51: }
 52: 
 53: /// Selects one exposed face and projects its plane into target space.
 54: pub(crate) fn project_surface_depth(
 55:     camera: &Camera,
 56:     center: [f32; 3],
 57:     world_size: f32,
 58:     voxel_type: u32,
 59:     is_emissive: bool,
 60:     exposure: SurfaceExposure,
 61: ) -> Option<ProjectedSurfaceDepth> {
 62:     let camera_to_surface = [
 63:         center[0] - camera.pos[0],
 64:         center[1] - camera.pos[1],
 65:         center[2] - camera.pos[2],
 66:     ];
 67:     let normal = select_surface_normal(voxel_type, is_emissive, exposure, camera_to_surface)?;
 68:     let position = representative_surface_position(center, world_size, normal);
 69:     let position_from_camera = [
 70:         position[0] - camera.pos[0],
 71:         position[1] - camera.pos[1],
 72:         position[2] - camera.pos[2],
 73:     ];
 74:     let representative_depth = dot(position_from_camera, camera.forward);
 75:     let plane_offset = dot(normal, position_from_camera);
 76:     if !representative_depth.is_finite()
 77:         || representative_depth <= 0.0
 78:         || !plane_offset.is_finite()
 79:         || plane_offset.abs() <= 1.0e-8
 80:         || !camera.focal_px.is_finite()
 81:         || camera.focal_px <= 0.0
 82:     {
 83:         return None;
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     let normal_right = dot(normal, camera.right);
 87:     let normal_up = dot(normal, camera.up);
 88:     let reciprocal_scale = (camera.focal_px * plane_offset).recip();
 89:     let reciprocal_depth = [
 90:         normal_right * reciprocal_scale,
 91:         -normal_up * reciprocal_scale,
 92:         dot(normal, camera.forward) / plane_offset
 93:             + (-normal_right * camera.half_w + normal_up * camera.half_h) * reciprocal_scale,
 94:     ];
 95:     if reciprocal_depth
 96:         .into_iter()
 97:         .any(|coefficient| !coefficient.is_finite())
 98:     {
 99:         return None;
100:     }
101: 
102:     Some(ProjectedSurfaceDepth {
103:         representative_depth,
104:         reciprocal_depth,
105:     })
106: }
107: 
108: /// Intersects the normal ray from the box center with the AABB boundary.
109: /// Lighting and fine depth both use this same physical surface sample.
110: pub(crate) fn representative_surface_position(
111:     center: [f32; 3],
112:     world_size: f32,
113:     normal: [f32; 3],
114: ) -> [f32; 3] {
115:     let dominant = normal
116:         .into_iter()
117:         .fold(0.0_f32, |largest, component| largest.max(component.abs()));
118:     if !world_size.is_finite() || world_size <= 0.0 || dominant <= 1.0e-6 {
119:         return center;
120:     }
121:     let distance_to_boundary = world_size * 0.5 / dominant;
122:     [
123:         center[0] + normal[0] * distance_to_boundary,
124:         center[1] + normal[1] * distance_to_boundary,
125:         center[2] + normal[2] * distance_to_boundary,
126:     ]
127: }
128:
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/propagate_exposure_to_octant.rs
````rust
 1: //! Propagate exposed parent and sibling boundaries into one octant.
 2: 
 3: use super::{SurfaceExposure, SurfaceFace};
 4: 
 5: /// Surface area visible on one occupied child octant.
 6: ///
 7: /// A face on the parent's outside inherits that parent's prepared exposure.
 8: /// A face inside the parent is exposed only when the adjacent sibling is
 9: /// absent from the occupancy mask. Passing `0xff` for a virtually subdivided
10: /// solid leaf is important: artificial children then inherit the real box's
11: /// exterior, but their internal cut planes stay closed.
12: pub(crate) fn exposure_for_octant(
13:     parent: SurfaceExposure,
14:     occupied_siblings: u32,
15:     octant: u32,
16: ) -> SurfaceExposure {
17:     debug_assert!(octant < 8);
18:     let mut result = SurfaceExposure::NONE;
19: 
20:     for face in SurfaceFace::ALL {
21:         let bit = face.axis_bit();
22:         let child_on_positive_side = octant & bit != 0;
23:         let child_on_parent_face = child_on_positive_side == face.is_positive();
24:         let area = if child_on_parent_face {
25:             parent.area(face)
26:         } else {
27:             let adjacent_octant = octant ^ bit;
28:             if occupied_siblings & (1 << adjacent_octant) == 0 {
29:                 255
30:             } else {
31:                 0
32:             }
33:         };
34:         result.set_area(face, area);
35:     }
36: 
37:     result
38: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/select_surface_normal.rs
````rust
 1: //! Choose a lighting normal from prepared surface geometry.
 2: 
 3: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 4:     VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GRASS,
 5:     VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_WATER,
 6: };
 7: 
 8: use super::{SurfaceExposure, SurfaceFace};
 9: 
10: /// Material semantics orient thin architectural layers.
11: ///
12: /// Floors and carpets are authored walking surfaces, while ceiling voxels
13: /// are authored undersides. Cube-like walls deliberately return no hint and
14: /// use the most camera-visible exposed face instead.
15: fn material_face(voxel_type: u32, is_emissive: bool) -> Option<SurfaceFace> {
16:     if is_emissive {
17:         return Some(SurfaceFace::NegativeY);
18:     }
19:     let voxel_type = u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok()?;
20:     match voxel_type {
21:         VOXEL_FLOOR | VOXEL_DRY_CARPET | VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET | VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET | VOXEL_GRASS
22:         | VOXEL_WATER | VOXEL_FLUID => Some(SurfaceFace::PositiveY),
23:         VOXEL_CEILING => Some(SurfaceFace::NegativeY),
24:         _ => None,
25:     }
26: }
27: 
28: /// Select one exact axis normal that belongs to an exposed physical face.
29: ///
30: /// Thin-layer material orientation wins when that authored face is exposed;
31: /// this is why a floor in front of a mostly-horizontal camera remains a floor
32: /// and receives overhead Lambertian light. Generic cube materials choose the
33: /// exposed face with the largest positive surface-to-camera cosine. Area is
34: /// the deterministic tie-breaker and improves coarse MIP choices.
35: pub(crate) fn select_surface_normal(
36:     voxel_type: u32,
37:     is_emissive: bool,
38:     exposure: SurfaceExposure,
39:     camera_to_surface: [f32; 3],
40: ) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
41:     if exposure.is_empty()
42:         || camera_to_surface
43:             .into_iter()
44:             .any(|component| !component.is_finite())
45:     {
46:         return None;
47:     }
48: 
49:     if let Some(face) = material_face(voxel_type, is_emissive) {
50:         let normal = face.normal();
51:         let facing = -(normal[0] * camera_to_surface[0]
52:             + normal[1] * camera_to_surface[1]
53:             + normal[2] * camera_to_surface[2]);
54:         if exposure.contains(face) && facing > 1.0e-6 {
55:             return Some(face.normal());
56:         }
57:     }
58: 
59:     let mut best: Option<(f32, u8, SurfaceFace)> = None;
60:     for face in SurfaceFace::ALL {
61:         let area = exposure.area(face);
62:         if area == 0 {
63:             continue;
64:         }
65:         let normal = face.normal();
66:         let facing = -(normal[0] * camera_to_surface[0]
67:             + normal[1] * camera_to_surface[1]
68:             + normal[2] * camera_to_surface[2]);
69:         if facing <= 1.0e-6 {
70:             continue;
71:         }
72:         let candidate = (facing, area, face);
73:         let replace = best.is_none_or(|current| {
74:             candidate.0 > current.0 || (candidate.0 == current.0 && candidate.1 > current.1)
75:         });
76:         if replace {
77:             best = Some(candidate);
78:         }
79:     }
80:     best.map(|(_, _, face)| face.normal())
81: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/surface_geometry/surface_exposure.rs
````rust
  1: //! Compact directional surface-area data.
  2: 
  3: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  4:     FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z,
  5:     FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z,
  6: };
  7: 
  8: /// Stable direction order shared by traversal and MIP preparation.
  9: ///
 10: /// The discriminants index [`SurfaceExposure`]'s six bytes. Keeping the
 11: /// normal here makes it impossible for propagation and shading to disagree
 12: /// about bit/axis conventions.
 13: #[repr(u8)]
 14: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 15: pub enum SurfaceFace {
 16:     NegativeX = 0,
 17:     PositiveX = 1,
 18:     NegativeY = 2,
 19:     PositiveY = 3,
 20:     NegativeZ = 4,
 21:     PositiveZ = 5,
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl SurfaceFace {
 25:     pub const ALL: [Self; 6] = [
 26:         Self::NegativeX,
 27:         Self::PositiveX,
 28:         Self::NegativeY,
 29:         Self::PositiveY,
 30:         Self::NegativeZ,
 31:         Self::PositiveZ,
 32:     ];
 33: 
 34:     pub const fn normal(self) -> [f32; 3] {
 35:         match self {
 36:             Self::NegativeX => [-1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 37:             Self::PositiveX => [1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 38:             Self::NegativeY => [0.0, -1.0, 0.0],
 39:             Self::PositiveY => [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],
 40:             Self::NegativeZ => [0.0, 0.0, -1.0],
 41:             Self::PositiveZ => [0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
 42:         }
 43:     }
 44: 
 45:     pub const fn opposite(self) -> Self {
 46:         match self {
 47:             Self::NegativeX => Self::PositiveX,
 48:             Self::PositiveX => Self::NegativeX,
 49:             Self::NegativeY => Self::PositiveY,
 50:             Self::PositiveY => Self::NegativeY,
 51:             Self::NegativeZ => Self::PositiveZ,
 52:             Self::PositiveZ => Self::NegativeZ,
 53:         }
 54:     }
 55: 
 56:     pub(super) const fn axis_bit(self) -> u32 {
 57:         match self {
 58:             Self::NegativeX | Self::PositiveX => 1,
 59:             Self::NegativeY | Self::PositiveY => 2,
 60:             Self::NegativeZ | Self::PositiveZ => 4,
 61:         }
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     pub(super) const fn is_positive(self) -> bool {
 65:         matches!(self, Self::PositiveX | Self::PositiveY | Self::PositiveZ)
 66:     }
 67: }
 68: 
 69: /// Exposed area in each axis direction, normalized to one node face.
 70: ///
 71: /// `0` means no known surface in that direction and `255` means one complete
 72: /// node face. MIP preparation may use intermediate values or saturate above
 73: /// one node-face worth of internal surface. Six bytes per node are enough to
 74: /// preserve orientation without putting floats in the atlas-side cache.
 75: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
 76: pub struct SurfaceExposure {
 77:     area: [u8; 6],
 78: }
 79: 
 80: impl SurfaceExposure {
 81:     pub const NONE: Self = Self { area: [0; 6] };
 82:     pub const ALL_FACES: Self = Self { area: [255; 6] };
 83: 
 84:     pub const fn from_area(area: [u8; 6]) -> Self {
 85:         Self { area }
 86:     }
 87: 
 88:     /// Decodes the authoritative six neighbor bits carried by a real atlas
 89:     /// leaf. Clear occupancy means air, hence a fully exposed face.
 90:     pub const fn from_neighbor_occlusion(mask: u8) -> Self {
 91:         Self::from_area([
 92:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X),
 93:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_X),
 94:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Y),
 95:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y),
 96:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_Z),
 97:             exposed_area(mask, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Z),
 98:         ])
 99:     }
100: 
101:     pub fn area(self, face: SurfaceFace) -> u8 {
102:         self.area[face as usize]
103:     }
104: 
105:     pub fn contains(self, face: SurfaceFace) -> bool {
106:         self.area(face) != 0
107:     }
108: 
109:     pub(super) fn set_area(&mut self, face: SurfaceFace, area: u8) {
110:         self.area[face as usize] = area;
111:     }
112: 
113:     pub(crate) fn add_saturating(&mut self, other: Self) {
114:         for face in SurfaceFace::ALL {
115:             let index = face as usize;
116:             self.area[index] = self.area[index].saturating_add(other.area[index]);
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     pub(super) fn is_empty(self) -> bool {
121:         self.area == [0; 6]
122:     }
123: 
124:     /// Directional area of a child subtree expressed in parent-face units.
125:     /// One octant face has one quarter of its parent's face area.
126:     pub(crate) fn scaled_to_parent(self) -> Self {
127:         Self::from_area(self.area.map(|area| ((u16::from(area) + 2) / 4) as u8))
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: const fn exposed_area(mask: u8, neighbor_bit: u8) -> u8 {
132:     if mask & neighbor_bit == 0 { 255 } else { 0 }
133: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/decode_srgb_albedo.rs
````rust
 1: //! Decode authored 8-bit sRGB albedo at data-preparation boundaries.
 2: //!
 3: //! Production splats carry this linear value from the per-upload atlas/MIP
 4: //! pass, so the hot shading loop never evaluates three transfer-function
 5: //! powers. Reference callers that begin with an encoded color use the same
 6: //! functions and therefore retain exactly the same radiometric contract.
 7: 
 8: use crate::application::rendering::LinearRgb;
 9: 
10: pub(crate) fn srgb_channel_to_linear(byte: f32) -> f32 {
11:     let encoded = (byte / 255.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
12:     if encoded <= 0.040_45 {
13:         encoded / 12.92
14:     } else {
15:         ((encoded + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)
16:     }
17: }
18: 
19: pub(crate) fn decode_albedo(bytes: [f32; 3]) -> LinearRgb {
20:     bytes.map(srgb_channel_to_linear)
21: }
22: 
23: pub(crate) fn decode_packed_albedo(packed: u32) -> LinearRgb {
24:     decode_albedo([
25:         ((packed >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32,
26:         ((packed >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32,
27:         (packed & 0xFF) as f32,
28:     ])
29: }
30: 
31: #[cfg(test)]
32: mod tests {
33:     use super::{decode_albedo, decode_packed_albedo, srgb_channel_to_linear};
34: 
35:     #[test]
36:     fn packed_and_unpacked_authored_colors_share_one_decode() {
37:         assert_eq!(
38:             decode_packed_albedo(0x80_FF_00),
39:             decode_albedo([128.0, 255.0, 0.0])
40:         );
41:         assert!((srgb_channel_to_linear(128.0) - 0.215_86).abs() < 1.0e-4);
42:     }
43: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Validate and apply one independent pooled-atlas row update.
  2: //!
  3: //! Streaming supplies a complete row-aligned chunk slot whose child pointers
  4: //! were already rebased by [`crate::application::atlas::AtlasPool`]. This
  5: //! boundary validates that independence before mutating persistent renderer
  6: //! state, then rebuilds only the corresponding prepared MIP slice.
  7: 
  8: use std::ops::Range;
  9: 
 10: use crate::application::atlas::ROW_TEXELS;
 11: 
 12: use super::atlas::{MipNode, rebuild_mips_in_node_range};
 13: 
 14: const WORDS_PER_NODE: usize = 4;
 15: const WORDS_PER_ROW: usize = ROW_TEXELS * WORDS_PER_NODE;
 16: 
 17: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 18: struct ValidatedRowUpdate {
 19:     word_range: Range<usize>,
 20:     node_range: Range<usize>,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: /// Applies a complete independent slot update without reallocating the atlas.
 24: pub(super) fn update_prepared_atlas_rows(
 25:     atlas: &mut [u32],
 26:     mips: &mut [MipNode],
 27:     mip_visit_scratch: &mut Vec<bool>,
 28:     first_row: u32,
 29:     texels: &[u32],
 30: ) -> bool {
 31:     let Some(update) = validate_row_update(atlas, mips, first_row, texels) else {
 32:         return false;
 33:     };
 34: 
 35:     atlas[update.word_range].copy_from_slice(texels);
 36:     let rebuilt = rebuild_mips_in_node_range(atlas, mips, update.node_range, mip_visit_scratch);
 37:     debug_assert!(rebuilt, "validated row range must always rebuild");
 38:     rebuilt
 39: }
 40: 
 41: /// Validation is deliberately complete before the first persistent write.
 42: fn validate_row_update(
 43:     atlas: &[u32],
 44:     mips: &[MipNode],
 45:     first_row: u32,
 46:     texels: &[u32],
 47: ) -> Option<ValidatedRowUpdate> {
 48:     if atlas.is_empty()
 49:         || texels.is_empty()
 50:         || atlas.len() % WORDS_PER_ROW != 0
 51:         || texels.len() % WORDS_PER_ROW != 0
 52:         || mips.len().checked_mul(WORDS_PER_NODE)? != atlas.len()
 53:     {
 54:         return None;
 55:     }
 56: 
 57:     let first_row = usize::try_from(first_row).ok()?;
 58:     let word_start = first_row.checked_mul(WORDS_PER_ROW)?;
 59:     let word_end = word_start.checked_add(texels.len())?;
 60:     if word_end > atlas.len() {
 61:         return None;
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     let node_range = word_start / WORDS_PER_NODE..word_end / WORDS_PER_NODE;
 65:     validate_independent_node_block(texels, node_range.clone())?;
 66:     Some(ValidatedRowUpdate {
 67:         word_range: word_start..word_end,
 68:         node_range,
 69:     })
 70: }
 71: 
 72: /// Every internal node in a streamed slot must keep all eight child slots
 73: /// inside that same update. This rejects partial-slot rows and corrupted or
 74: /// unrebased pointers before they can invalidate an unrelated slot's MIPs.
 75: fn validate_independent_node_block(texels: &[u32], global_nodes: Range<usize>) -> Option<()> {
 76:     for node in texels.chunks_exact(WORDS_PER_NODE) {
 77:         match node[0] {
 78:             1 => {}
 79:             0 => {
 80:                 if node[2] & !0xff != 0 {
 81:                     return None;
 82:                 }
 83:                 let child_base = usize::try_from(node[1]).ok()?;
 84:                 let child_end = child_base.checked_add(8)?;
 85:                 if child_base < global_nodes.start || child_end > global_nodes.end {
 86:                     return None;
 87:                 }
 88:             }
 89:             _ => return None,
 90:         }
 91:     }
 92:     Some(())
 93: }
````
