## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/engine/noclip.rs
````rust
 1: //! Backrooms lore made mechanical: holding a walk into solid wall long
 2: //! enough occasionally phases the player through reality. A child module of
 3: //! `engine`; see `presenter.rs` for why that gives it access to `Engine`'s
 4: //! private fields.
 5: 
 6: use super::{
 7:     Engine, InputFrame, LEVEL_BACKROOMS, LEVEL_GRASSLAND, NOCLIP_CHANCE, NOCLIP_PUSH_SECONDS,
 8: };
 9: 
10: impl Engine {
11:     pub(super) fn rng_next01(&mut self) -> f32 {
12:         self.rng ^= self.rng << 13;
13:         self.rng ^= self.rng >> 7;
14:         self.rng ^= self.rng << 17;
15:         (self.rng >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
16:     }
17: 
18:     /// Backrooms lore made mechanical: holding a walk into solid wall long
19:     /// enough occasionally phases the player through reality.
20:     pub(super) fn update_noclip(&mut self, dt: f32, input: &InputFrame, old_pos: [f32; 3]) {
21:         self.noclip_cooldown = (self.noclip_cooldown - dt).max(0.0);
22: 
23:         let i = input.intent;
24:         let pushing = input.locked && (i.forward || i.backward || i.left || i.right);
25:         let dx = self.player.position[0] - old_pos[0];
26:         let dz = self.player.position[2] - old_pos[2];
27:         let pinned = pushing && (dx * dx + dz * dz) < 0.002 * 0.002;
28: 
29:         if !pinned {
30:             self.push_seconds = 0.0;
31:             return;
32:         }
33:         self.push_seconds += dt;
34:         if self.push_seconds < NOCLIP_PUSH_SECONDS || self.noclip_cooldown > 0.0 {
35:             return;
36:         }
37:         self.noclip_cooldown = 1.0;
38:         if self.rng_next01() < NOCLIP_CHANCE {
39:             self.noclip();
40:         }
41:     }
42: 
43:     /// Phase through reality by pushing into walls. From Level 0 the fall is
44:     /// into the grassland; from anywhere else — including Level 1, exactly
45:     /// as the wiki warns — a noclip drops the wanderer back into Level 0.
46:     fn noclip(&mut self) {
47:         let (target, arrival) = if self.level == LEVEL_BACKROOMS {
48:             // Into the grassland you phase in place.
49:             (LEVEL_GRASSLAND, None)
50:         } else {
51:             // The way back drops you at the spawn clearing so you can't
52:             // rematerialize inside a wall.
53:             (LEVEL_BACKROOMS, Some(self.config.spawn))
54:         };
55:         self.switch_level(target, arrival);
56:     }
57: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/engine/peripheral_shift.rs
````rust
  1: //! Peripheral Shift: "whenever not directly observed, the layout can warp,
  2: //! stretch, or rearrange itself" — the one non-Euclidean mechanic the game
  3: //! has today, and the template for any future level's own version of "the
  4: //! space doesn't stay put." A child module of `engine`; see `presenter.rs`
  5: //! for why that gives it access to `Engine`'s private fields.
  6: //!
  7: //! Structured as a small [`LevelShiftPolicy`] trait with exactly one
  8: //! concrete implementation ([`FabricDriftShift`], level 0's fabric drift).
  9: //! Deliberately not generalized further than that: `RealitySnapshot`'s
 10: //! epoch storage and the fixed 40u `FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL` lattice are still
 11: //! level-0-specific, and there is no second consumer yet to prove a more
 12: //! generic shape against. What this buys today is real: the level-0
 13: //! hardcoding becomes a registration instead of an inline guard, so
 14: //! `Engine::tick` no longer needs to know which levels reshape themselves.
 15: 
 16: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{
 17:     AnomalyKind, FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL, WorldBounds, fabric_drift_cell_of,
 18: };
 19: 
 20: use super::{BLACKOUT_HIDE_DISTANCE, BLACKOUT_SHIFT_PERIOD_S, ChunkKey, Engine, LEVEL_BACKROOMS, chunk_key};
 21: 
 22: /// A level's "the space doesn't stay put when unobserved" mechanic. A level
 23: /// with no registered policy simply has none — the space stays put, which
 24: /// is the correct default for every level but 0 today.
 25: pub(super) trait LevelShiftPolicy {
 26:     /// Which level this policy governs.
 27:     fn level(&self) -> u32;
 28:     /// Advance the mechanic by one tick. Has full access to `Engine`
 29:     /// because every existing implementation (and every plausible future
 30:     /// one — a level's own chunk store, player pose, and reality state)
 31:     /// needs it; the pluggability this buys is *which* mechanic runs per
 32:     /// level, not isolation from engine state.
 33:     fn update(&self, engine: &mut Engine, dt: f32);
 34: }
 35: 
 36: /// Level 0's fabric drift: the sole concrete `LevelShiftPolicy` today.
 37: pub(super) struct FabricDriftShift;
 38: 
 39: impl LevelShiftPolicy for FabricDriftShift {
 40:     fn level(&self) -> u32 {
 41:         LEVEL_BACKROOMS
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     fn update(&self, engine: &mut Engine, dt: f32) {
 45:         engine.run_fabric_drift_shift(dt);
 46:     }
 47: }
 48: 
 49: impl Engine {
 50:     /// The registered policy for `level`, if any. The only place level ids
 51:     /// map to shift mechanics — adding a second level's policy later means
 52:     /// adding one arm here, not touching `tick`.
 53:     fn shift_policy_for(level: u32) -> Option<&'static dyn LevelShiftPolicy> {
 54:         const FABRIC_DRIFT: FabricDriftShift = FabricDriftShift;
 55:         if level == FABRIC_DRIFT.level() {
 56:             Some(&FABRIC_DRIFT)
 57:         } else {
 58:             None
 59:         }
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     /// Runs the current level's shift mechanic, if it has one. Replaces
 63:     /// what used to be a hardcoded `if self.level != LEVEL_BACKROOMS` guard
 64:     /// at the call site — `tick` no longer needs to know which levels
 65:     /// reshape themselves, only that some might.
 66:     pub(super) fn update_peripheral_shift(&mut self, dt: f32) {
 67:         if let Some(policy) = Self::shift_policy_for(self.level) {
 68:             policy.update(self, dt);
 69:         }
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     /// Squared distance from a point to a drift cell's world rectangle
 73:     /// (0 inside the cell).
 74:     fn drift_cell_dist2(cell: (i64, i64), px: f32, pz: f32) -> f32 {
 75:         let x0 = cell.0 as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
 76:         let z0 = cell.1 as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
 77:         let dx = (x0 - px).max(px - (x0 + FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL)).max(0.0);
 78:         let dz = (z0 - pz).max(pz - (z0 + FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL)).max(0.0);
 79:         dx * dx + dz * dz
 80:     }
 81: 
 82:     /// A drift cell is hidden from the player once it's farther than any
 83:     /// light source could plausibly reveal detail at. Named and pulled out
 84:     /// on its own (rather than left as an inline expression) because it's
 85:     /// the one piece of tier 2 that's a genuine "can the player perceive
 86:     /// this" predicate, not blackout-specific geometry — the natural first
 87:     /// thing a second shift mechanic would want to reuse.
 88:     fn is_hidden_from_player(cell: (i64, i64), px: f32, pz: f32) -> bool {
 89:         Self::drift_cell_dist2(cell, px, pz) > BLACKOUT_HIDE_DISTANCE.powi(2)
 90:     }
 91: 
 92:     /// Every drift cell any resident chunk could touch counts as observed.
 93:     /// The far radius adds hysteresis of a couple of cells, so a cell only
 94:     /// drifts once the player has genuinely abandoned it.
 95:     fn drift_near_radius(&self) -> f32 {
 96:         (self.visual_policy.radius as f32 + 1.0) * self.config.chunk_size
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     fn drift_far_radius(&self) -> f32 {
100:         // A mismanaging wanderer loses the hysteresis: the fabric rearranges
101:         // almost the moment it leaves the streaming footprint.
102:         self.drift_near_radius()
103:             + 2.0 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL * (1.0 - 0.85 * self.survival.mismanagement())
104:     }
105: 
106:     /// Advances one drift cell's reality epoch and stops watching it. The
107:     /// single-cell primitive both tier 1 (a filtered subset of watched
108:     /// cells) and `abandon_all_watched_drift_cells` (every watched cell,
109:     /// unconditionally) are built from.
110:     fn abandon_drift_cell(&mut self, cell: (i64, i64)) {
111:         self.drift_near.remove(&cell);
112:         self.reality = self.reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cell.0, cell.1);
113:     }
114: 
115:     /// Leaving the level unobserves everything at once: every tracked drift
116:     /// cell rearranges, so phasing out and back never returns the wanderer
117:     /// to the hallways they left. Called from `switch_level` — previously
118:     /// that reimplemented this drain-and-advance loop inline instead of
119:     /// sharing it with tier 1's version below.
120:     pub(super) fn abandon_all_watched_drift_cells(&mut self) {
121:         let watched: Vec<(i64, i64)> = self.drift_near.drain().collect();
122:         for cell in watched {
123:             self.reality = self.reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cell.0, cell.1);
124:         }
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Tier 1 — abandoned territory. Cells the player walks near are marked;
128:     /// when one falls beyond the far radius every chunk of it has long been
129:     /// evicted, its drift epoch advances, and whatever streams back in later
130:     /// is a lawfully different warren (corridors, assemblies, and anomalies
131:     /// never move — navigation survives; hallway memory does not).
132:     ///
133:     /// Tier 2 — inside a blackout the shift stalks the player in real time:
134:     /// on a slow cadence, cells that lie entirely behind the player's facing,
135:     /// beyond what any light could reveal, and fully inside the blackout's
136:     /// bounds advance immediately and their resident chunks rebuild. The
137:     /// darkness hides the swap; turning around is never a way back.
138:     fn run_fabric_drift_shift(&mut self, dt: f32) {
139:         let (px, pz) = (self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]);
140: 
141:         // -- tier 1: mark near cells, drift abandoned ones -------------------
142:         let near = self.drift_near_radius();
143:         let min_cx = fabric_drift_cell_of(px - near);
144:         let max_cx = fabric_drift_cell_of(px + near);
145:         let min_cz = fabric_drift_cell_of(pz - near);
146:         let max_cz = fabric_drift_cell_of(pz + near);
147:         for cz in min_cz..=max_cz {
148:             for cx in min_cx..=max_cx {
149:                 if Self::drift_cell_dist2((cx, cz), px, pz) <= near * near {
150:                     self.drift_near.insert((cx, cz));
151:                 }
152:             }
153:         }
154:         let far2 = self.drift_far_radius() * self.drift_far_radius();
155:         let abandoned: Vec<(i64, i64)> = self
156:             .drift_near
157:             .iter()
158:             .copied()
159:             .filter(|&cell| Self::drift_cell_dist2(cell, px, pz) > far2)
160:             .collect();
161:         for cell in abandoned {
162:             self.abandon_drift_cell(cell);
163:         }
164: 
165:         // -- tier 2: the blackout rearranges behind the player ---------------
166:         self.blackout_shift_cooldown = (self.blackout_shift_cooldown - dt).max(0.0);
167:         let blackout_bounds = self
168:             .store
169:             .all_traversal_gates()
170:             .find(|gate| {
171:                 gate.anomaly_kind == AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse
172:                     && gate.affected_bounds.contains(px, pz)
173:             })
174:             .map(|gate| gate.affected_bounds);
175:         let Some(bounds) = blackout_bounds else {
176:             self.blackout_shift_debug.0 = false;
177:             return;
178:         };
179:         self.blackout_shift_debug.0 = true;
180:         if self.blackout_shift_cooldown > 0.0 {
181:             return;
182:         }
183:         let forward = self.player.forward();
184:         // The rear shift reaches past the streaming footprint on purpose:
185:         // cells it advances beyond residency simply rebuild on approach,
186:         // exactly like tier-1 drift.
187:         let reach = self.drift_near_radius().max(3.0 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL);
188:         let mut shifted = Vec::new();
189:         for cz in fabric_drift_cell_of(pz - reach)..=fabric_drift_cell_of(pz + reach) {
190:             for cx in fabric_drift_cell_of(px - reach)..=fabric_drift_cell_of(px + reach) {
191:                 let cx_w = (cx as f32 + 0.5) * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
192:                 let cz_w = (cz as f32 + 0.5) * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
193:                 // Center-based checks on purpose: a 40 u cell near the
194:                 // blackout's edge or the player's flank still shifts. The
195:                 // sliver a check this loose can expose sits in blackout
196:                 // darkness — and a half-glimpsed wall that wasn't there is
197:                 // the intended experience, not a bug.
198:                 let inside = bounds.contains(cx_w, cz_w);
199:                 let behind = (cx_w - px) * forward[0] + (cz_w - pz) * forward[2] < -4.0;
200:                 let hidden = Self::is_hidden_from_player((cx, cz), px, pz);
201:                 if inside && behind && hidden {
202:                     shifted.push((cx, cz));
203:                 }
204:             }
205:         }
206:         self.blackout_shift_debug = (true, shifted.len(), self.blackout_shift_debug.2);
207:         if shifted.is_empty() {
208:             return;
209:         }
210:         self.blackout_shift_debug.2 += shifted.len();
211:         // Mismanagement accelerates the stalking dark: at full strain the
212:         // rear shift fires three times as often.
213:         self.blackout_shift_cooldown =
214:             BLACKOUT_SHIFT_PERIOD_S / (1.0 + 2.0 * self.survival.mismanagement());
215:         for &(cx, cz) in &shifted {
216:             self.reality = self.reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cx, cz);
217:         }
218:         // Rebuild the resident chunks of the shifted cells in place. The
219:         // install path's player-overlap check keeps the swap safe, and the
220:         // request carries the advanced reality by construction.
221:         let cell_bounds: Vec<WorldBounds> = shifted
222:             .iter()
223:             .map(|&(cx, cz)| {
224:                 WorldBounds::new(
225:                     cx as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
226:                     cz as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
227:                     (cx + 1) as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
228:                     (cz + 1) as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
229:                 )
230:             })
231:             .collect();
232:         let cs = self.config.chunk_size;
233:         let targets: Vec<ChunkKey> = self
234:             .store
235:             .iter_ordered()
236:             .filter(|chunk| {
237:                 let rect = WorldBounds::new(
238:                     chunk.origin.0,
239:                     chunk.origin.1,
240:                     chunk.origin.0 + cs,
241:                     chunk.origin.1 + cs,
242:                 );
243:                 cell_bounds.iter().any(|cell| cell.intersects(rect))
244:             })
245:             .map(|chunk| chunk_key(chunk.origin.0, chunk.origin.1))
246:             .collect();
247:         for key in targets {
248:             self.force_rebuild(key);
249:         }
250:     }
251: }
252: 
253: #[cfg(test)]
254: mod tests {
255:     use super::*;
256:     use crate::application::engine::EngineConfig;
257:     use crate::application::ports::{ChunkPayload, ChunkSourcePort, FrameParams, RendererPort};
258: 
259:     /// A minimal renderer relying entirely on `RendererPort`'s defaults
260:     /// beyond the two required methods — this test never inspects a frame,
261:     /// it only needs `Engine::new` to accept something.
262:     struct NoopRenderer;
263:     impl RendererPort for NoopRenderer {
264:         fn upload_atlas(&mut self, _texels: &[u32]) {}
265:         fn draw(&mut self, _frame: &FrameParams, _chunks: &[super::super::ChunkDraw]) {}
266:     }
267: 
268:     /// Never actually called: this test drives the shift policy directly,
269:     /// not through `Engine::tick`, so no chunk load is ever requested.
270:     struct UnusedSource;
271:     impl ChunkSourcePort for UnusedSource {
272:         fn load(&self, _origin_x: f32, _origin_z: f32, _level: u32, _lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
273:             unreachable!("this test never streams chunks")
274:         }
275:     }
276: 
277:     fn test_engine() -> Engine {
278:         Engine::new(
279:             EngineConfig::default(),
280:             Box::new(NoopRenderer),
281:             Box::new(UnusedSource),
282:         )
283:     }
284: 
285:     /// A fake policy for a level that doesn't really have one, proving
286:     /// `update_peripheral_shift` actually dispatches through the registry
287:     /// instead of only ever running level 0's mechanic regardless of what's
288:     /// registered — the real claim "pluggable" makes.
289:     struct SpyShift {
290:         level: u32,
291:     }
292: 
293:     impl LevelShiftPolicy for SpyShift {
294:         fn level(&self) -> u32 {
295:             self.level
296:         }
297: 
298:         fn update(&self, engine: &mut Engine, _dt: f32) {
299:             // A visible, checkable side effect distinct from anything the
300:             // real fabric-drift mechanic would do on its own: relocate the
301:             // player to a fixed marker position.
302:             engine.player.position = [999.0, 999.0, 999.0];
303:         }
304:     }
305: 
306:     #[test]
307:     fn a_registered_policy_actually_runs() {
308:         let spy = SpyShift { level: 7 };
309:         assert_eq!(spy.level(), 7);
310:         let mut engine = test_engine();
311:         let before = engine.player.position;
312:         spy.update(&mut engine, 0.016);
313:         assert_ne!(engine.player.position, before);
314:         assert_eq!(engine.player.position, [999.0, 999.0, 999.0]);
315:     }
316: 
317:     #[test]
318:     fn level_zero_resolves_to_the_fabric_drift_policy() {
319:         let policy = Engine::shift_policy_for(LEVEL_BACKROOMS).expect("level 0 has a policy");
320:         assert_eq!(policy.level(), LEVEL_BACKROOMS);
321:     }
322: 
323:     #[test]
324:     fn an_unregistered_level_has_no_policy() {
325:         assert!(Engine::shift_policy_for(999).is_none());
326:     }
327: }
````

````rust
  1: //! HUD/diagnostic presentation over engine state: everything the debug
  2: //! overlay and the diagnostic aperture read, and the `HudStats` snapshot the
  3: //! ordinary HUD renders from. Pure formatting/aggregation — no simulation
  4: //! logic lives here, only reading and describing what `Engine::tick` already
  5: //! decided. A child module of `engine` (not a sibling): its private fields
  6: //! stay private to outside callers, but Rust visibility cascades to
  7: //! descendant modules, so these methods reach `self.player`, `self.store`,
  8: //! etc. exactly as if they were still defined in `engine.rs`.
  9: 
 10: use std::fmt::Write;
 11: 
 12: use crate::application::streaming::chunk_key;
 13: 
 14: use super::{AWARENESS_RANGE_M, Engine, HudStats};
 15: use crate::application::navigation::{relative_bearing_deg, select_anomaly_focus};
 16: 
 17: impl Engine {
 18:     /// Multi-line plain-text report of the live anomaly machinery, for the
 19:     /// debug overlay: reality-snapshot epochs, resident traversal gates and
 20:     /// pit hazards (nearest first), and the streaming pipeline counters.
 21:     /// Pure formatting over engine state — no browser types, natively
 22:     /// testable.
 23:     pub fn anomaly_debug_text(&self) -> String {
 24:         let p = self.player.position;
 25:         let mut out = String::with_capacity(1024);
 26:         let _ = writeln!(
 27:             out,
 28:             "pos ({:.1}, {:.1}, {:.1})  level {}  yaw {:.2}",
 29:             p[0], p[1], p[2], self.level, self.player.yaw
 30:         );
 31:         let _ = writeln!(
 32:             out,
 33:             "chunks {} resident ({} fine) | pending {} | backlog {} | forced reloads {}",
 34:             self.store.len(),
 35:             self.store.iter_ordered().filter(|c| c.lod == 0).count(),
 36:             self.pending.len(),
 37:             self.completed_backlog.len(),
 38:             self.forced_reloads.len(),
 39:         );
 40:         let _ = writeln!(
 41:             out,
 42:             "flares {} | push {:.2}s",
 43:             self.flares.len(),
 44:             self.push_seconds
 45:         );
 46: 
 47:         let stamps = self.reality.stamps();
 48:         let _ = writeln!(out, "reality: {} stamp(s)", stamps.len());
 49:         let _ = writeln!(
 50:             out,
 51:             "peripheral shift: {} drifted cell(s), {} watched",
 52:             self.reality.fabric_drifts().len(),
 53:             self.drift_near.len()
 54:         );
 55:         let (inside, eligible, total) = self.blackout_shift_debug;
 56:         let _ = writeln!(
 57:             out,
 58:             "blackout shift: inside={inside} eligible={eligible} \
 59:              shifted_total={total} cooldown={:.1}s",
 60:             self.blackout_shift_cooldown
 61:         );
 62:         for stamp in stamps {
 63:             let _ = writeln!(
 64:                 out,
 65:                 "  {:016x} epoch {}  plane {:.1} {:?} {:?}",
 66:                 stamp.instance_id,
 67:                 stamp.epoch,
 68:                 stamp.gate_plane(),
 69:                 stamp.gate_axis,
 70:                 stamp.travel_direction,
 71:             );
 72:         }
 73: 
 74:         let mut gates: Vec<_> = self.store.all_traversal_gates().copied().collect();
 75:         gates.sort_by_key(|g| g.id);
 76:         gates.dedup_by_key(|g| g.id);
 77:         gates.sort_by(|a, b| {
 78:             let d = |g: &vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGate| match g.axis {
 79:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::X => (g.plane - p[0]).abs(),
 80:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::Z => (g.plane - p[2]).abs(),
 81:             };
 82:             d(a).total_cmp(&d(b))
 83:         });
 84:         let _ = writeln!(out, "gates resident: {}", gates.len());
 85:         for gate in gates.iter().take(6) {
 86:             let dist = match gate.axis {
 87:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::X => (gate.plane - p[0]).abs(),
 88:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::Z => (gate.plane - p[2]).abs(),
 89:             };
 90:             let epoch = self.reality.lookup(gate.instance_id).map_or(0, |s| s.epoch);
 91:             let _ = writeln!(
 92:                 out,
 93:                 "  {:?}/{:?} of {:?} {:08x}  plane {:.1} on {:?}  d={:.1}  epoch {}",
 94:                 gate.kind,
 95:                 gate.forward,
 96:                 gate.anomaly_kind,
 97:                 (gate.instance_id & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32,
 98:                 gate.plane,
 99:                 gate.axis,
100:                 dist,
101:                 epoch,
102:             );
103:         }
104: 
105:         let mut pits: Vec<_> = self.store.all_pit_hazards().copied().collect();
106:         pits.sort_by_key(|h| h.id);
107:         pits.dedup_by_key(|h| h.id);
108:         pits.sort_by(|a, b| {
109:             let d = |h: &vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::PitHazard| {
110:                 let dx = h.center.x - p[0];
111:                 let dz = h.center.z - p[2];
112:                 dx * dx + dz * dz
113:             };
114:             d(a).total_cmp(&d(b))
115:         });
116:         let _ = writeln!(out, "pit hazards resident: {}", pits.len());
117:         for pit in pits.iter().take(4) {
118:             let dx = pit.center.x - p[0];
119:             let dz = pit.center.z - p[2];
120:             let _ = writeln!(
121:                 out,
122:                 "  {:08x} at ({:.1}, {:.1})  half {:.1}  d={:.1}  recovery ({:.1}, {:.1})",
123:                 (pit.id & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32,
124:                 pit.center.x,
125:                 pit.center.z,
126:                 pit.half_side,
127:                 (dx * dx + dz * dz).sqrt(),
128:                 pit.recovery.x,
129:                 pit.recovery.z,
130:             );
131:         }
132:         out
133:     }

208:             survival.vitals.hydration,

210:             survival.vitals.condition,
211:             survival.excess,
212:         );
213:         let _ = writeln!(
214:             out,
215:             "carried: water {}  rations {}  | assisted consumption {}  deaths {}",
216:             survival.almond_bottles,
217:             survival.rations,
218:             if survival.assisted_consumption {
219:                 "on"
220:             } else {
221:                 "off"
222:             },
223:             survival.deaths,
224:         );
225: 
226:         let _ = writeln!(out, "§ ROUTE");
227:         match (self.route_target, self.route_anchor()) {
228:             (Some(target), Some(anchor)) => {
229:                 let _ = writeln!(
230:                     out,
231:                     "door {:08x} -> level {}  at ({:.1}, {:.1})",
232:                     (target.exit_id & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32,
233:                     target.target_level,
234:                     target.position[0],
235:                     target.position[1],
236:                 );
237:                 let _ = writeln!(
238:                     out,
239:                     "range {:.1} m  bearing {:03}  [straight-line; no route graph exists]",
240:                     anchor.range_m, anchor.bearing_deg,
241:                 );
242:             }
243:             _ => {
244:                 let _ = writeln!(out, "unresolved: no door inside the streamed field");
245:             }
246:         }
247: 
248:         let _ = writeln!(out, "§ AWARENESS");
249:         let player = [self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]];
250:         let focus = select_anomaly_focus(
251:             self.store.all_traversal_gates(),
252:             self.store.all_pit_hazards(),
253:             player,
254:             AWARENESS_RANGE_M,
255:         );
256:         match focus {
257:             Some(focus) => {
258:                 let _ = writeln!(
259:                     out,
260:                     "{:?} {:08x}  range {:.1} m  bearing {:03}  priority {}",
261:                     focus.kind,
262:                     (focus.instance_id & 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32,
263:                     focus.range_m,
264:                     relative_bearing_deg(self.player.yaw, player, focus.position),
265:                     focus.priority,
266:                 );
267:                 let _ = writeln!(
268:                     out,
269:                     "(debug-only: no player-facing sensing mechanic exists yet)"
270:                 );
271:             }
272:             None => {
273:                 let _ = writeln!(
274:                     out,
275:                     "no anomaly signature resident within {AWARENESS_RANGE_M:.0} m"
276:                 );
277:             }
278:         }
279: 
280:         let _ = writeln!(out, "§ FIELD");
281:         out.push_str(&self.anomaly_debug_text());
282:         out
283:     }
284: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/engine/route.rs
````rust
 1: //! The navigation-objective mechanic: which resident level exit the HUD's
 2: //! route needle points at, reselected on a bounded cadence and invalidated
 3: //! on level/reality transitions. Thin — `navigation.rs` owns the actual
 4: //! selection/bearing math; this module is only the engine-state glue around
 5: //! it. A child module of `engine`; see `presenter.rs` for why that gives it
 6: //! access to `Engine`'s private fields.
 7: 
 8: use crate::application::navigation::{range_m, relative_bearing_deg, select_route_target};
 9: 
10: use super::{Engine, ROUTE_RECOMPUTE_PERIOD_S, RouteAnchor};
11: 
12: impl Engine {
13:     /// Drops the cached navigation objective; the next tick reselects from
14:     /// whatever the *current* level/reality has resident. Called on level
15:     /// switches, reality transitions, and death so telemetry never crosses
16:     /// a reality address.
17:     pub(super) fn invalidate_route(&mut self) {
18:         self.route_target = None;
19:         self.route_cooldown = 0.0;
20:     }
21: 
22:     /// Reselects the route objective on a bounded cadence from the resident
23:     /// level exits — authoritative generator output, never invented. No
24:     /// resident door means no route, truthfully.
25:     pub(super) fn update_route(&mut self, dt: f32) {
26:         self.route_cooldown -= dt;
27:         if self.route_cooldown > 0.0 {
28:             return;
29:         }
30:         self.route_cooldown = ROUTE_RECOMPUTE_PERIOD_S;
31:         let player = [self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]];
32:         let selected = select_route_target(self.store.all_level_exits(), player);
33:         self.route_target = selected;
34:     }
35: 
36:     /// The presenter-facing route anchor: bearing/range are derived fresh
37:     /// from the cached target and the live player pose (cheap trig), so the
38:     /// needle tracks head movement between reselections.
39:     pub(super) fn route_anchor(&self) -> Option<RouteAnchor> {
40:         let target = self.route_target?;
41:         let player = [self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]];
42:         Some(RouteAnchor {
43:             target_level: target.target_level,
44:             bearing_deg: relative_bearing_deg(self.player.yaw, player, target.position),
45:             range_m: range_m(player, target.position),
46:         })
47:     }
48: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/rendering/camera.rs
````rust
  1: //! Camera transforms shared by every presentation strategy.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module deliberately knows nothing about a graphics API.  Raster
  4: //! renderers consume the WebGPU projection matrix while ray renderers consume
  5: //! the orthonormal basis.  Keeping both products behind one function prevents
  6: //! switching renderer from subtly changing the camera.
  7: 
  8: use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;
  9: 
 10: /// `tan(vertical field of view / 2)` for the 75 degree default.
 11: pub const DEFAULT_FOV_TAN: f32 = 0.767_326_95;
 12: 
 13: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 14: pub struct CameraBasis {
 15:     pub right: [f32; 3],
 16:     pub up: [f32; 3],
 17:     pub forward: [f32; 3],
 18: }
 19: 
 20: /// Builds the canonical right/up/forward basis from engine yaw and pitch.
 21: pub fn camera_basis(yaw: f32, pitch: f32) -> CameraBasis {
 22:     let (sin_pitch, cos_pitch) = pitch.sin_cos();
 23:     let (sin_yaw, cos_yaw) = yaw.sin_cos();
 24:     CameraBasis {
 25:         right: [cos_yaw, 0.0, -sin_yaw],
 26:         up: [sin_pitch * sin_yaw, cos_pitch, sin_pitch * cos_yaw],
 27:         forward: [-cos_pitch * sin_yaw, sin_pitch, -cos_pitch * cos_yaw],
 28:     }
 29: }
 30: 
 31: /// Returns a column-major WebGPU view-projection matrix.
 32: ///
 33: /// WebGPU's clip-space depth is `0..1`, unlike the old OpenGL `-1..1`
 34: /// convention.  Naming the convention here makes the migration testable and
 35: /// keeps backend-specific correction matrices out of individual pipelines.
 36: pub fn webgpu_view_projection(
 37:     frame: &FrameParams,
 38:     width: u32,
 39:     height: u32,
 40:     far: f32,
 41:     fov_tan: f32,
 42: ) -> [f32; 16] {
 43:     let basis = camera_basis(frame.yaw, frame.pitch);
 44:     let p = frame.camera_pos;
 45:     let dot = |a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]| a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2];
 46:     let view = [
 47:         basis.right[0],
 48:         basis.up[0],
 49:         -basis.forward[0],
 50:         0.0,
 51:         basis.right[1],
 52:         basis.up[1],
 53:         -basis.forward[1],
 54:         0.0,
 55:         basis.right[2],
 56:         basis.up[2],
 57:         -basis.forward[2],
 58:         0.0,
 59:         -dot(basis.right, p),
 60:         -dot(basis.up, p),
 61:         dot(basis.forward, p),
 62:         1.0,
 63:     ];
 64: 
 65:     let near = 0.03;
 66:     let far = far.max(near + 0.01);
 67:     let f = 1.0 / fov_tan.clamp(0.05, 4.0);
 68:     let aspect = width.max(1) as f32 / height.max(1) as f32;
 69:     let projection = [
 70:         f / aspect,
 71:         0.0,
 72:         0.0,
 73:         0.0,
 74:         0.0,
 75:         f,
 76:         0.0,
 77:         0.0,
 78:         0.0,
 79:         0.0,
 80:         far / (near - far),
 81:         -1.0,
 82:         0.0,
 83:         0.0,
 84:         (far * near) / (near - far),
 85:         0.0,
 86:     ];
 87:     multiply_column_major(&projection, &view)
 88: }
 89: 
 90: pub fn multiply_column_major(a: &[f32; 16], b: &[f32; 16]) -> [f32; 16] {
 91:     let mut result = [0.0; 16];
 92:     for column in 0..4 {
 93:         for row in 0..4 {
 94:             result[column * 4 + row] = a[row] * b[column * 4]
 95:                 + a[4 + row] * b[column * 4 + 1]
 96:                 + a[8 + row] * b[column * 4 + 2]
 97:                 + a[12 + row] * b[column * 4 + 3];
 98:         }
 99:     }
100:     result
101: }
102: 
103: #[cfg(test)]
104: mod tests {
105:     use super::*;
106: 
107:     fn dot(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
108:         a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]
109:     }
110: 
111:     #[test]
112:     fn basis_is_orthonormal_for_oblique_camera() {
113:         let basis = camera_basis(-1.1, 0.37);
114:         for axis in [basis.right, basis.up, basis.forward] {
115:             assert!((dot(axis, axis) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-5);
116:         }
117:         assert!(dot(basis.right, basis.up).abs() < 1e-5);
118:         assert!(dot(basis.right, basis.forward).abs() < 1e-5);
119:         assert!(dot(basis.up, basis.forward).abs() < 1e-5);
120:     }
121: 
122:     #[test]
123:     fn webgpu_projection_maps_near_and_far_to_zero_and_one() {
124:         let frame = FrameParams::default();
125:         let matrix = webgpu_view_projection(&frame, 160, 90, 100.0, DEFAULT_FOV_TAN);
126:         // At yaw/pitch zero, forward is -Z and the view is identity.  Apply
127:         // just the depth rows to two points in front of the camera.
128:         let project_depth = |z: f32| {
129:             let clip_z = matrix[10] * z + matrix[14];
130:             let clip_w = matrix[11] * z + matrix[15];
131:             clip_z / clip_w
132:         };
133:         assert!(project_depth(-0.03).abs() < 1e-4);
134:         assert!((project_depth(-100.0) - 1.0).abs() < 1e-4);
135:     }
136: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/body.rs
````rust
  1: //! The wanderer's embodied telemetry: pedometer, exertion, fatigue, and the
  2: //! heart signal the interface listens to.
  3: //!
  4: //! Pure application math — no clocks, no DOM, no renderer knowledge. The
  5: //! engine feeds it the one collision-resolved horizontal movement delta per
  6: //! tick (relocations, teleports, and level transitions already excluded)
  7: //! plus the survival state it owns, and reads back plain presentation-safe
  8: //! numbers. Everything is finite, clamped, and deterministic: same inputs,
  9: //! same outputs, on every machine.
 10: //!
 11: //! Units are explicit throughout: seconds, meters, meters/second, beats per
 12: //! minute, and dimensionless normalized factors in `0..=1`.
 13: 
 14: /// World meters of resolved walking that count as one step. The pedometer
 15: /// keeps the raw distance in `f64`; only whole steps are presented.
 16: pub const STRIDE_LENGTH_M: f32 = 0.7;
 17: 
 18: /// Resting pulse of a healthy wanderer, beats per minute.
 19: const BASELINE_BPM: f32 = 58.0;
 20: /// Hard physiological ceiling; the target is clamped below this.
 21: const MAX_BPM: f32 = 185.0;
 22: /// Hard floor (bradycardia is not simulated).
 23: const MIN_BPM: f32 = 45.0;
 24: /// Seconds for the pulse to close ~63% of the gap while rising.
 25: const BPM_RISE_TAU_S: f32 = 4.0;
 26: /// Seconds for the pulse to recover while falling; dehydration and fatigue
 27: /// stretch this, which is what "delayed recovery" feels like.
 28: const BPM_FALL_TAU_S: f32 = 9.0;
 29: 
 30: /// Movement at terminal walk speed reaches this much of full intensity.
 31: /// (Terminal speed is `player::ACCELERATION / player::FRICTION` = 2.5 u/s;
 32: /// the model is tuned against it but only sees measured meters.)
 33: const FULL_INTENSITY_SPEED_MPS: f32 = 2.5;
 34: 
 35: /// Equilibrium exertion of a healthy wanderer walking flat out. Baseline
 36: /// exploration must stay cheap: 0.4 costs almost no capacity (see
 37: /// `exertion_capacity_multiplier`).
 38: const HEALTHY_WALK_EXERTION: f32 = 0.4;
 39: /// Seconds for exertion to close ~63% of the gap while rising.
 40: const EXERTION_RISE_TAU_S: f32 = 22.0;
 41: /// Seconds for exertion to recover at rest with full recovery quality.
 42: const EXERTION_FALL_TAU_S: f32 = 16.0;
 43: 
 44: /// Fatigue accrues only above this exertion level, so ordinary walking
 45: /// never wears the wanderer down permanently.
 46: const FATIGUE_EXERTION_THRESHOLD: f32 = 0.6;
 47: /// Fatigue per second at maximal exertion (~80 s of redline to exhaustion).
 48: const FATIGUE_RISE_PER_S: f32 = 0.0125;
 49: /// Seconds of deliberate stillness before fatigue starts to mend.
 50: const FATIGUE_REST_DELAY_S: f32 = 3.0;
 51: /// Fatigue recovered per second of rest (~2 min of standing still from
 52: /// fully exhausted). Rest is the loop; there is no sleep system yet — the
 53: /// extension point is `resting` below.
 54: const FATIGUE_RECOVERY_PER_S: f32 = 1.0 / 120.0;
 55: 
 56: /// Ambient °C above which heat begins to stress the body.
 57: const HEAT_STRESS_FLOOR_C: f32 = 27.0;
 58: /// °C span from first stress to full heat stress.
 59: const HEAT_STRESS_SPAN_C: f32 = 12.0;
 60: 
 61: /// The lowest combined movement multiplier before death: severe depletion
 62: /// is alarming and restrictive, never immobilizing.
 63: const MOVEMENT_FLOOR: f32 = 0.35;
 64: 
 65: /// Presentation-safe classification of the heart signal.
 66: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 67: pub enum PulseSignal {
 68:     /// Calm body: the HUD shows only a faint beat.
 69:     Quiet,
 70:     /// Working body: elevated pulse worth glancing at.
 71:     Active,
 72:     /// Something is wrong — heat, thirst, exhaustion, or injury.
 73:     Strained,
 74:     /// Imminent physiological danger.
 75:     Critical,
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /// Survival context the engine already owns, passed by value each tick.
 79: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 80: pub struct BodyContext {
 81:     /// Hydration reserve, 0..=1.
 82:     pub hydration: f32,
 83:     /// Satiety reserve, 0..=1.
 84:     pub satiety: f32,
 85:     /// Physical condition, 0..=1 (0 is death).
 86:     pub condition: f32,
 87:     /// Felt ambient temperature, °C.
 88:     pub ambient_c: f32,
 89: }
 90: 
 91: /// One tick's presentation-safe reading.
 92: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 93: pub struct BodyReadout {
 94:     /// Whole session steps.
 95:     pub steps: u64,
 96:     /// Current smoothed pulse, BPM.
 97:     pub bpm: f32,
 98:     /// Where the pulse is heading, BPM (debug only; never shown normally).
 99:     pub target_bpm: f32,
100:     /// Normalized beat prominence 0..=1 (amplitude of the visual pulse).
101:     pub beat_intensity: f32,
102:     /// Signal classification for sparse color/reveal decisions.
103:     pub signal: PulseSignal,
104:     /// Short-term exertion, 0 fresh ..= 1 spent.
105:     pub exertion: f32,
106:     /// Long-term fatigue, 0 rested ..= 1 exhausted.
107:     pub fatigue: f32,
108:     /// Combined bounded movement multiplier, `MOVEMENT_FLOOR..=1`.
109:     pub movement_factor: f32,
110: }
111: 
112: /// Debug-only decomposition of the movement multiplier and pulse target.
113: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
114: pub struct BodyDebug {
115:     pub exertion_capacity: f32,
116:     pub hydration_factor: f32,
117:     pub satiety_factor: f32,
118:     pub condition_factor: f32,
119:     pub fatigue_factor: f32,
120:     pub heat_stress: f32,
121:     pub recovery_quality: f32,
122: }
123: 
124: /// The wanderer's body. Advanced once per engine tick.
125: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
126: pub struct Body {
127:     /// Precise resolved walking distance, meters. Steps derive from this.
128:     walked_m: f64,
129:     exertion: f32,
130:     fatigue: f32,
131:     bpm: f32,
132:     target_bpm: f32,
133:     /// Beat phase 0..1; wraps once per beat.
134:     beat_phase: f32,
135:     /// True on the tick the phase wrapped (a beat event).
136:     beat_event: bool,
137:     /// Seconds of near-stillness, for the fatigue rest gate.
138:     still_seconds: f32,
139:     context: BodyContext,
140: }
141: 
142: impl Default for Body {
143:     fn default() -> Self {
144:         Self {
145:             walked_m: 0.0,
146:             exertion: 0.0,
147:             fatigue: 0.0,
148:             bpm: BASELINE_BPM,
149:             target_bpm: BASELINE_BPM,
150:             beat_phase: 0.0,
151:             beat_event: false,
152:             still_seconds: 0.0,
153:             context: BodyContext {
154:                 hydration: 1.0,
155:                 satiety: 1.0,
156:                 condition: 1.0,
157:                 ambient_c: 21.0,
158:             },
159:         }
160:     }
161: }
162: 
163: fn finite01(value: f32) -> f32 {
164:     if value.is_finite() {
165:         value.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
166:     } else {
167:         0.0
168:     }
169: }
170: 
171: /// Smoothstep over `edge0..edge1`, safe for any finite input.
172: fn smooth(edge0: f32, edge1: f32, x: f32) -> f32 {
173:     let t = ((x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
174:     t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
175: }
176: 
177: impl Body {
178:     /// Death/respawn: strain resets with the new body, but the session
179:     /// pedometer keeps counting — the record of ground covered survives.
180:     pub fn reset_strain(&mut self) {
181:         self.exertion = 0.0;
182:         self.fatigue = 0.0;
183:         self.bpm = BASELINE_BPM;
184:         self.target_bpm = BASELINE_BPM;
185:         self.still_seconds = 0.0;
186:     }
187: 
188:     /// Advances one tick.
189:     ///
190:     /// `moved_m` must be the collision-resolved horizontal movement of this
191:     /// tick only — the caller excludes relocations, teleports, pit recovery,
192:     /// respawns, and level transitions before calling. Non-finite or absurd
193:     /// inputs are clamped; dt is bounded so a background-tab hitch cannot
194:     /// spike the model.
195:     pub fn advance(&mut self, dt_seconds: f32, moved_m: f32, context: BodyContext) {
196:         let dt = if dt_seconds.is_finite() {
197:             dt_seconds.clamp(0.0, 0.25)
198:         } else {
199:             0.0
200:         };
201:         let moved = if moved_m.is_finite() {
202:             // One tick of walking can never legitimately exceed a few meters.
203:             moved_m.clamp(0.0, 2.0)
204:         } else {
205:             0.0
206:         };
207:         self.context = BodyContext {
208:             hydration: finite01(context.hydration),
209:             satiety: finite01(context.satiety),
210:             condition: finite01(context.condition),
211:             ambient_c: if context.ambient_c.is_finite() {
212:                 context.ambient_c.clamp(-50.0, 80.0)
213:             } else {
214:                 21.0
215:             },
216:         };
217:         if dt <= 0.0 {
218:             self.beat_event = false;
219:             return;
220:         }
221: 
222:         self.walked_m += moved as f64;
223: 
224:         // -- movement intensity ------------------------------------------------
225:         let speed = moved / dt;
226:         let intensity = (speed / FULL_INTENSITY_SPEED_MPS).clamp(0.0, 1.5).powf(1.3);
227: 
228:         // -- stress inputs -----------------------------------------------------
229:         let c = self.context;
230:         let heat_stress = smooth(
231:             HEAT_STRESS_FLOOR_C,
232:             HEAT_STRESS_FLOOR_C + HEAT_STRESS_SPAN_C,
233:             c.ambient_c,
234:         );
235:         let dehydration = smooth(0.5, 0.0, c.hydration); // 0 fine .. 1 parched
236:         let hunger = smooth(0.35, 0.0, c.satiety); // 0 fine .. 1 starving
237:         let injury = smooth(0.6, 0.0, c.condition); // 0 fine .. 1 broken
238: 
239:         // Exertion cost multiplier: adverse conditions make the same walk
240:         // more expensive. Bounded to keep equilibria inside 0..1.
241:         let cost = (1.0 + 0.9 * heat_stress + 0.9 * dehydration + 0.5 * hunger + 0.6 * injury)
242:             .clamp(1.0, 3.0);
243:         // Recovery quality: how well rest actually restores.
244:         let recovery_quality = (1.0
245:             - 0.45 * dehydration
246:             - 0.30 * hunger
247:             - 0.25 * self.fatigue
248:             - 0.25 * heat_stress)
249:             .clamp(0.25, 1.0);
250: 
251:         // -- exertion: approach a cost-scaled target ---------------------------
252:         let target_exertion = (intensity * HEALTHY_WALK_EXERTION * cost).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
253:         if target_exertion > self.exertion {
254:             let blend = (dt / EXERTION_RISE_TAU_S).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
255:             self.exertion += (target_exertion - self.exertion) * blend;
256:         } else {
257:             let blend = (dt * recovery_quality / EXERTION_FALL_TAU_S).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
258:             self.exertion += (target_exertion - self.exertion) * blend;
259:         }
260:         self.exertion = finite01(self.exertion);
261: 
262:         // -- fatigue: sustained redline wears; deliberate rest mends -----------
263:         let resting = intensity < 0.05;
264:         self.still_seconds = if resting {
265:             (self.still_seconds + dt).min(3600.0)
266:         } else {
267:             0.0
268:         };
269:         if self.exertion > FATIGUE_EXERTION_THRESHOLD {
270:             let over = (self.exertion - FATIGUE_EXERTION_THRESHOLD)
271:                 / (1.0 - FATIGUE_EXERTION_THRESHOLD);
272:             self.fatigue += over * FATIGUE_RISE_PER_S * dt;
273:         } else if resting && self.still_seconds >= FATIGUE_REST_DELAY_S {
274:             self.fatigue -= FATIGUE_RECOVERY_PER_S * recovery_quality * dt;
275:         }
276:         self.fatigue = finite01(self.fatigue);
277: 
278:         // -- pulse: target model with asymmetric smoothing ---------------------
279:         let deficit_stress = 0.5 * hunger + 0.5 * dehydration;
280:         let mut target = BASELINE_BPM
281:             + 78.0 * self.exertion
282:             + 26.0 * heat_stress.max(dehydration) // heat and thirst share a pathway
283:             + 10.0 * deficit_stress
284:             + 14.0 * self.fatigue
285:             + 24.0 * injury;
286:         target = target.clamp(MIN_BPM, MAX_BPM);
287:         self.target_bpm = target;
288:         let tau = if target > self.bpm {
289:             BPM_RISE_TAU_S
290:         } else {
291:             // Recovery slows when the body is depleted: stopping helps, but
292:             // the pulse settles reluctantly.
293:             BPM_FALL_TAU_S / recovery_quality
294:         };
295:         let blend = (dt / tau).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
296:         self.bpm += (target - self.bpm) * blend;
297:         self.bpm = self.bpm.clamp(MIN_BPM, MAX_BPM);
298: 
299:         // -- beat phase --------------------------------------------------------
300:         let next_phase = self.beat_phase + self.bpm / 60.0 * dt;
301:         self.beat_event = next_phase >= 1.0;
302:         self.beat_phase = next_phase.fract();
303:     }
304: 
305:     /// Whole steps walked this session.
306:     pub fn steps(&self) -> u64 {
307:         (self.walked_m / STRIDE_LENGTH_M as f64) as u64
308:     }
309: 
310:     /// Precise resolved walking distance, meters (debug/diagnostics).
311:     pub fn walked_m(&self) -> f64 {
312:         self.walked_m
313:     }
314: 
315:     /// True exactly on ticks where the beat phase wrapped.
316:     pub fn beat_event(&self) -> bool {
317:         self.beat_event
318:     }
319: 
320:     /// Beat phase, 0..1.
321:     pub fn beat_phase(&self) -> f32 {
322:         self.beat_phase
323:     }
324: 
325:     fn heat_stress(&self) -> f32 {
326:         smooth(
327:             HEAT_STRESS_FLOOR_C,
328:             HEAT_STRESS_FLOOR_C + HEAT_STRESS_SPAN_C,
329:             self.context.ambient_c,
330:         )
331:     }
332: 
333:     /// Debug decomposition of every factor feeding movement and pulse.
334:     pub fn debug(&self) -> BodyDebug {
335:         let c = self.context;
336:         let dehydration = smooth(0.5, 0.0, c.hydration);
337:         let hunger = smooth(0.35, 0.0, c.satiety);
338:         BodyDebug {
339:             exertion_capacity: self.exertion_capacity_multiplier(),
340:             hydration_factor: self.hydration_multiplier(),
341:             satiety_factor: self.satiety_multiplier(),
342:             condition_factor: self.condition_multiplier(),
343:             fatigue_factor: self.fatigue_multiplier(),
344:             heat_stress: self.heat_stress(),
345:             recovery_quality: (1.0
346:                 - 0.45 * dehydration
347:                 - 0.30 * hunger
348:                 - 0.25 * self.fatigue
349:                 - 0.25 * self.heat_stress())
350:             .clamp(0.25, 1.0),
351:         }
352:     }
353: 
354:     /// High exertion trims sustainable pace; quadratic so the healthy walk
355:     /// equilibrium (~0.4) costs almost nothing.
356:     fn exertion_capacity_multiplier(&self) -> f32 {
357:         1.0 - 0.35 * self.exertion * self.exertion
358:     }
359: 
360:     fn hydration_multiplier(&self) -> f32 {
361:         0.75 + 0.25 * smooth(0.0, 0.5, self.context.hydration)
362:     }
363: 
364:     fn satiety_multiplier(&self) -> f32 {
365:         0.85 + 0.15 * smooth(0.0, 0.35, self.context.satiety)
366:     }
367: 
368:     fn condition_multiplier(&self) -> f32 {
369:         0.6 + 0.4 * self.context.condition
370:     }
371: 
372:     fn fatigue_multiplier(&self) -> f32 {
373:         1.0 - 0.25 * self.fatigue
374:     }
375: 
376:     /// The single bounded multiplier the movement integrator applies:
377:     ///
378:     /// `effective = base * exertion_capacity * hydration * satiety *
379:     /// condition * fatigue`, floored at `MOVEMENT_FLOOR` so every nonfatal
380:     /// state keeps meaningful movement.
381:     pub fn movement_factor(&self) -> f32 {
382:         let product = self.exertion_capacity_multiplier()
383:             * self.hydration_multiplier()
384:             * self.satiety_multiplier()
385:             * self.condition_multiplier()
386:             * self.fatigue_multiplier();
387:         product.clamp(MOVEMENT_FLOOR, 1.0)
388:     }
389: 
390:     fn signal(&self) -> PulseSignal {
391:         let c = self.context;
392:         if c.condition < 0.25 || self.bpm > 160.0 {
393:             PulseSignal::Critical
394:         } else if self.bpm > 118.0 || c.hydration < 0.2 || self.fatigue > 0.7 || c.condition < 0.6
395:         {
396:             PulseSignal::Strained
397:         } else if self.bpm > 76.0 {
398:             PulseSignal::Active
399:         } else {
400:             PulseSignal::Quiet
401:         }
402:     }
403: 
404:     /// The presentation snapshot the HUD consumes.
405:     pub fn readout(&self) -> BodyReadout {
406:         let signal = self.signal();
407:         // Beat prominence follows how far the pulse sits above baseline.
408:         let beat_intensity = smooth(BASELINE_BPM + 4.0, 150.0, self.bpm).max(match signal {
409:             PulseSignal::Critical => 0.9,
410:             PulseSignal::Strained => 0.45,
411:             _ => 0.12,
412:         });
413:         BodyReadout {
414:             steps: self.steps(),
415:             bpm: self.bpm,
416:             target_bpm: self.target_bpm,
417:             beat_intensity,
418:             signal,
419:             exertion: self.exertion,
420:             fatigue: self.fatigue,
421:             movement_factor: self.movement_factor(),
422:         }
423:     }
424: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Dropped-flare lifecycle and per-frame light selection.
  2: //!
  3: //! Flares are transient world objects rather than chunk data. This module
  4: //! owns their age, insertion order, collision-aware placement, retirement,
  5: //! and clockless renderer payload. The engine only supplies player/world
  6: //! context and the shared simulation time.
  7: 
  8: use crate::application::collision::{Aabb, CollisionWorld};
  9: use crate::application::ports::{DynamicLight, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
 10: 
 11: /// Flare lifetime in seconds; intensity fades during the final tenth.
 12: const FLARE_LIFETIME_S: f32 = 90.0;
 13: /// Global active-flare cap. A new drop retires the oldest flare at the cap.
 14: const FLARE_CAP: usize = 12;
 15: /// Flares farther than this horizontal distance do not light the frame.
 16: const FLARE_CULL_DISTANCE: f32 = 40.0;
 17: /// Local warm glow radius of one flare.
 18: const FLARE_LIGHT_RADIUS: f32 = 9.0;
 19: /// Horizontal distance from the player at which a drop is attempted.
 20: const FLARE_DROP_DISTANCE: f32 = 0.9;
 21: /// Flare flame height above the floor slab.
 22: const FLARE_HEIGHT: f32 = 0.3;
 23: /// Height above the flame used to detect geometry remapped over a flare.
 24: const BURIED_PROBE_HEIGHT: f32 = 0.2;
 25: 
 26: /// One dropped flare: pure runtime world-space state. Never serialized into
 27: /// chunks, never part of the reality snapshot, and preserved untouched by
 28: /// ordinary chunk streaming.
 29: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 30: pub struct Flare {
 31:     pub position: [f32; 3],
 32:     pub age_seconds: f32,
 33:     /// Monotonic drop order; doubles as the deterministic flicker phase.
 34:     pub sequence: u64,
 35: }
 36: 
 37: impl Flare {
 38:     pub fn remaining_seconds(&self) -> f32 {
 39:         (FLARE_LIFETIME_S - self.age_seconds).max(0.0)
 40:     }
 41: }
 42: 
 43: /// Fixed renderer payload and the meaningful prefix length.
 44: pub(crate) struct FlareLightSet {
 45:     pub(crate) lights: [DynamicLight; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
 46:     pub(crate) count: u8,
 47: }
 48: 
 49: /// Active flare collection, kept oldest first.
 50: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 51: pub(crate) struct FlareField {
 52:     active: Vec<Flare>,
 53:     sequence: u64,
 54: }
 55: 
 56: impl FlareField {
 57:     /// Advances every flare and retires those whose lifetime has elapsed.
 58:     pub(crate) fn advance(&mut self, dt_seconds: f32) {
 59:         for flare in &mut self.active {
 60:             flare.age_seconds += dt_seconds;
 61:         }
 62:         self.active
 63:             .retain(|flare| flare.age_seconds < FLARE_LIFETIME_S);
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     /// Drops a flare slightly ahead of the player unless that placement
 67:     /// would collide, in which case the known-valid player position wins.
 68:     pub(crate) fn drop_from(
 69:         &mut self,
 70:         eye: [f32; 3],
 71:         forward: [f32; 3],
 72:         collision: &CollisionWorld,
 73:     ) {
 74:         let ahead = [
 75:             eye[0] + forward[0] * FLARE_DROP_DISTANCE,
 76:             eye[1],
 77:             eye[2] + forward[2] * FLARE_DROP_DISTANCE,
 78:         ];
 79:         let spot = if collision.collides(ahead) {
 80:             eye
 81:         } else {
 82:             ahead
 83:         };
 84: 
 85:         if self.active.len() >= FLARE_CAP {
 86:             self.active.remove(0);
 87:         }
 88:         self.sequence += 1;
 89:         self.active.push(Flare {
 90:             position: [spot[0], FLARE_HEIGHT, spot[2]],
 91:             age_seconds: 0.0,
 92:             sequence: self.sequence,
 93:         });
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     /// Extinguishes flares covered by newly installed collision geometry.
 97:     /// The inclusive point test intentionally matches the former engine
 98:     /// policy at box faces.
 99:     pub(crate) fn extinguish_buried(&mut self, boxes: &[Aabb]) {
100:         self.active.retain(|flare| {
101:             let probe = [
102:                 flare.position[0],
103:                 flare.position[1] + BURIED_PROBE_HEIGHT,
104:                 flare.position[2],
105:             ];
106:             !boxes.iter().any(|bounds| point_in_aabb(probe, bounds))
107:         });
108:     }
109: 
110:     /// Builds the nearest-light payload once. Selection, count, fade, and
111:     /// deterministic flicker therefore cannot disagree within a frame.
112:     pub(crate) fn lights(&self, camera: [f32; 3], time_seconds: f32) -> FlareLightSet {
113:         let nearest = self.nearest(camera);
114:         let count = nearest.len() as u8;
115:         let mut lights = [DynamicLight::default(); MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS];
116: 
117:         for (slot, flare) in nearest.into_iter().enumerate() {
118:             let fade = (flare.remaining_seconds() / (FLARE_LIFETIME_S * 0.1)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
119:             let phase = time_seconds * 13.0 + flare.sequence as f32 * 1.7;
120:             let flicker = 0.85 + 0.15 * phase.sin() * (phase * 0.37).cos();
121:             lights[slot] = DynamicLight {
122:                 position: flare.position,
123:                 color: [1.0, 0.45, 0.18],
124:                 radius: FLARE_LIGHT_RADIUS,
125:                 intensity: 1.6 * fade * flicker,
126:             };
127:         }
128: 
129:         FlareLightSet { lights, count }
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Removes active flares without rewinding their monotonic identity.
133:     pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
134:         self.active.clear();
135:     }
136: 
137:     pub(crate) fn active(&self) -> &[Flare] {
138:         &self.active
139:     }
140: 
141:     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
142:         self.active.len()
143:     }
144: 
145:     fn nearest(&self, camera: [f32; 3]) -> Vec<&Flare> {
146:         let cull_distance_squared = FLARE_CULL_DISTANCE * FLARE_CULL_DISTANCE;
147:         let distance_squared = |flare: &Flare| {
148:             let dx = flare.position[0] - camera[0];
149:             let dz = flare.position[2] - camera[2];
150:             dx * dx + dz * dz
151:         };
152:         let mut nearest: Vec<_> = self
153:             .active
154:             .iter()
155:             .filter(|flare| distance_squared(flare) < cull_distance_squared)
156:             .collect();
157:         nearest.sort_by(|a, b| {
158:             distance_squared(a)
159:                 .total_cmp(&distance_squared(b))
160:                 .then_with(|| a.sequence.cmp(&b.sequence))
161:         });
162:         nearest.truncate(MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS);
163:         nearest
164:     }
165: }
166: 
167: fn point_in_aabb(point: [f32; 3], bounds: &Aabb) -> bool {
168:     point[0] >= bounds.min[0]
169:         && point[0] <= bounds.max[0]
170:         && point[1] >= bounds.min[1]
171:         && point[1] <= bounds.max[1]
172:         && point[2] >= bounds.min[2]
173:         && point[2] <= bounds.max[2]
174: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Route and awareness telemetry: pure selection and bearing math over the
  2: //! authoritative world records the streamer already holds.
  3: //!
  4: //! Nothing here invents targets. A route exists only when a real
  5: //! [`LevelExit`] is resident; an anomaly focus exists only when a real
  6: //! traversal gate or pit hazard is resident. When the data is not streamed
  7: //! in, the truthful answer is `None` — the presenter says "beyond field"
  8: //! instead of pretending.
  9: //!
 10: //! Range is always the straight-line (Euclidean) walking-plane distance and
 11: //! is labelled RANGE by the presenter — there is no navigable route graph
 12: //! in the engine today, so a "path distance" would be a fabrication.
 13: 
 14: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyKind, PitHazard, TraversalGate};
 15: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::LevelExit;
 16: 
 17: /// A selected navigation objective (a real, resident level door).
 18: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 19: pub struct RouteTarget {
 20:     pub exit_id: u64,
 21:     /// Level on the far side of the door.
 22:     pub target_level: u32,
 23:     /// Door trigger center on the walking plane.
 24:     pub position: [f32; 2],
 25: }
 26: 
 27: /// Straight-line range on the walking plane, meters.
 28: pub fn range_m(from: [f32; 2], to: [f32; 2]) -> f32 {
 29:     let dx = to[0] - from[0];
 30:     let dz = to[1] - from[1];
 31:     (dx * dx + dz * dz).sqrt()
 32: }
 33: 
 34: /// Bearing of `to` relative to the player's facing, in whole degrees
 35: /// normalized to `0..=359`. 0° is dead ahead; 90° is to the player's right
 36: /// (clockwise positive, viewed from above).
 37: ///
 38: /// The facing convention matches [`crate::application::player::Player`]:
 39: /// forward is `[-sin(yaw), -cos(yaw)]` on the XZ plane.
 40: pub fn relative_bearing_deg(yaw: f32, from: [f32; 2], to: [f32; 2]) -> u16 {
 41:     let fwd = [-yaw.sin(), -yaw.cos()];
 42:     let dir = [to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1]];
 43:     if !dir[0].is_finite() || !dir[1].is_finite() || (dir[0] == 0.0 && dir[1] == 0.0) {
 44:         return 0;
 45:     }
 46:     // Clockwise-from-forward: right-hand cross on the ground plane, with +Y
 47:     // up, gives the signed turn toward the target.
 48:     let cross = fwd[0] * dir[1] - fwd[1] * dir[0];
 49:     let dot = fwd[0] * dir[0] + fwd[1] * dir[1];
 50:     let deg = cross.atan2(dot).to_degrees();
 51:     let wrapped = ((deg % 360.0) + 360.0) % 360.0;
 52:     (wrapped.round() as i64).rem_euclid(360) as u16
 53: }
 54: 
 55: /// Selects the navigation objective from the resident level exits: the
 56: /// nearest door, ties broken by id so the choice is deterministic even for
 57: /// coincident duplicates surfaced by chunk-halo overlap.
 58: pub fn select_route_target<'a>(
 59:     exits: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LevelExit>,
 60:     player: [f32; 2],
 61: ) -> Option<RouteTarget> {
 62:     exits
 63:         .map(|exit| {
 64:             let pos = [exit.center.x, exit.center.z];
 65:             (range_m(player, pos), exit.id, exit, pos)
 66:         })
 67:         .min_by(|a, b| a.0.total_cmp(&b.0).then(a.1.cmp(&b.1)))
 68:         .map(|(_, _, exit, pos)| RouteTarget {
 69:             exit_id: exit.id,
 70:             target_level: exit.target_level,
 71:             position: pos,
 72:         })
 73: }
 74: 
 75: /// Debug-only anomaly focus: the single most relevant resident anomaly
 76: /// record near the player. The normal HUD never shows this — the game has
 77: /// no player-facing anomaly-sensing mechanic yet, so surfacing it outside
 78: /// the diagnostic aperture would make the interface psychic. When such a
 79: /// mechanic exists, it can consume this same deterministic selection.
 80: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 81: pub struct AnomalyFocus {
 82:     pub kind: AnomalyKind,
 83:     pub instance_id: u64,
 84:     /// Nearest point distance is not derived; this is center/plane range, m.
 85:     pub range_m: f32,
 86:     /// Absolute position used for bearing math.
 87:     pub position: [f32; 2],
 88:     /// Larger is more urgent; used only for deterministic ranking.
 89:     pub priority: u8,
 90: }
 91: 
 92: fn kind_priority(kind: AnomalyKind) -> u8 {
 93:     // Ranked by immediate danger to the wanderer.
 94:     match kind {
 95:         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => 4,
 96:         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => 3,
 97:         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => 2,
 98:         _ => 1,
 99:     }
100: }
101: 
102: /// Deterministic single-focus selection over resident gates and pits within
103: /// `awareness_m`. Ordering: priority class first, then distance (quantized
104: /// to 0.1 m so float noise cannot flip the choice), then instance id.
105: pub fn select_anomaly_focus<'a>(
106:     gates: impl Iterator<Item = &'a TraversalGate>,
107:     pits: impl Iterator<Item = &'a PitHazard>,
108:     player: [f32; 2],
109:     awareness_m: f32,
110: ) -> Option<AnomalyFocus> {
111:     let gate_candidates = gates.map(|gate| {
112:         // The gate's reference point: the nearest point of its plane span.
113:         let (x, z) = match gate.axis {
114:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::X => {
115:                 (gate.plane, player[1].clamp(gate.span_min, gate.span_max))
116:             }
117:             vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::Axis2::Z => {
118:                 (player[0].clamp(gate.span_min, gate.span_max), gate.plane)
119:             }
120:         };
121:         AnomalyFocus {
122:             kind: gate.anomaly_kind,
123:             instance_id: gate.instance_id,
124:             range_m: range_m(player, [x, z]),
125:             position: [x, z],
126:             priority: kind_priority(gate.anomaly_kind),
127:         }
128:     });
129:     let pit_candidates = pits.map(|pit| AnomalyFocus {
130:         kind: AnomalyKind::PitLattice,
131:         instance_id: pit.instance_id,
132:         range_m: range_m(player, [pit.center.x, pit.center.z]),
133:         position: [pit.center.x, pit.center.z],
134:         priority: kind_priority(AnomalyKind::PitLattice),
135:     });
136:     gate_candidates
137:         .chain(pit_candidates)
138:         .filter(|focus| focus.range_m.is_finite() && focus.range_m <= awareness_m)
139:         .min_by(|a, b| {
140:             b.priority
141:                 .cmp(&a.priority)
142:                 .then(((a.range_m * 10.0) as i64).cmp(&((b.range_m * 10.0) as i64)))
143:                 .then(a.instance_id.cmp(&b.instance_id))
144:         })
145: }
146: 
147: #[cfg(test)]
148: mod tests {
149:     use super::*;
150:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{

152:     };

154: 
155:     fn exit(id: u64, x: f32, z: f32, target_level: u32) -> LevelExit {
156:         LevelExit {
157:             id,
158:             target_level,
159:             center: Position::new(x, z),
160:             half_extent: 0.7,
161:             arrival: Position::new(3.0, 3.0),
162:         }
163:     }
164: 
165:     #[test]
166:     fn bearing_covers_all_quadrants_and_wraps() {
167:         // yaw = 0: forward is -Z.
168:         let p = [0.0, 0.0];
169:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [0.0, -10.0]), 0, "ahead");
170:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [10.0, 0.0]), 90, "right");
171:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [0.0, 10.0]), 180, "behind");
172:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [-10.0, 0.0]), 270, "left");
173:         // Diagonals.
174:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [10.0, -10.0]), 45);
175:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [-10.0, -10.0]), 315);
176:         // A quarter-turn of yaw shifts every bearing by the same amount.
177:         let quarter = std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2; // now facing -X
178:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(quarter, p, [-10.0, 0.0]), 0);
179:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(quarter, p, [0.0, -10.0]), 90);
180:         // Degenerate/absurd input collapses to 0, never panics.
181:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, p), 0);
182:         assert_eq!(relative_bearing_deg(0.0, p, [f32::NAN, 1.0]), 0);
183:     }
184: 
185:     #[test]
186:     fn route_selection_is_nearest_and_deterministic() {
187:         let doors = [
188:             exit(9, 30.0, 0.0, 1),
189:             exit(2, 10.0, 0.0, 1),
190:             exit(1, 10.0, 0.0, 1), // coincident duplicate: lower id wins
191:         ];
192:         let chosen = select_route_target(doors.iter(), [0.0, 0.0]).unwrap();
193:         assert_eq!(chosen.exit_id, 1);
194:         assert_eq!(chosen.target_level, 1);
195:         assert!((range_m([0.0, 0.0], chosen.position) - 10.0).abs() < 1e-4);
196:         // No resident doors: truthfully nothing.
197:         assert_eq!(select_route_target([].iter(), [0.0, 0.0]), None);
198:     }
199: 
200:     #[test]

207:             axis: Axis2::X,
208:             plane,

214:         let pit = PitHazard {

217:             center: Position::new(6.0, 0.0),
218:             half_side: 2.0,
219:             depth: 3.0,

222:         // A red room farther away outranks a nearer blackout; the pit sits

229:             select_anomaly_focus(gates.iter(), [pit].iter(), [0.0, 0.0], 20.0).unwrap();
230:         assert_eq!(focus.instance_id, 11, "danger class outranks distance");
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/application/perf_governor.rs
````rust
  1: //! Adaptive internal-resolution policy, independent of renderer and browser.
  2: 
  3: /// Adaptive internal-resolution governor. Low-spec machines get fewer rays
  4: /// per frame by rendering at a reduced backing-store resolution; the driver
  5: /// applies the scale to the canvas. Hysteresis + cooldown prevent flapping.
  6: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  7: pub struct PerfGovernor {
  8:     ema_frame_ms: f32,
  9:     scale: f32,
 10:     cooldown_frames: u32,
 11:     /// Frames since the last scale-up attempt (saturating).
 12:     frames_since_raise: u32,
 13:     /// While positive, scale-ups are locked out because a recent raise
 14:     /// immediately overloaded the GPU and had to be reverted (anti-flap).
 15:     raise_lockout_frames: u32,
 16: }
 17: 
 18: impl PerfGovernor {
 19:     const SCALES: [f32; 4] = [0.5, 0.65, 0.8, 1.0];
 20:     /// A drop this soon after a raise counts as a failed raise.
 21:     const RAISE_PROBE_FRAMES: u32 = 600;
 22:     /// How long a failed raise blocks further raise attempts (~1 min).
 23:     const RAISE_LOCKOUT_FRAMES: u32 = 3600;
 24: 
 25:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 26:         Self {
 27:             ema_frame_ms: 16.0,
 28:             scale: 0.8,
 29:             cooldown_frames: 0,
 30:             frames_since_raise: u32::MAX,
 31:             raise_lockout_frames: 0,
 32:         }
 33:     }
 34: 
 35:     pub fn scale(&self) -> f32 {
 36:         self.scale
 37:     }
 38: 
 39:     pub fn update(&mut self, frame_ms: f32) {
 40:         self.ema_frame_ms = self.ema_frame_ms * 0.95 + frame_ms.clamp(0.0, 100.0) * 0.05;
 41:         self.frames_since_raise = self.frames_since_raise.saturating_add(1);
 42:         self.raise_lockout_frames = self.raise_lockout_frames.saturating_sub(1);
 43:         if self.cooldown_frames > 0 {
 44:             self.cooldown_frames -= 1;
 45:             return;
 46:         }
 47:         let idx = Self::SCALES
 48:             .iter()
 49:             .position(|&s| s == self.scale)
 50:             .unwrap_or(2);
 51:         if self.ema_frame_ms > 33.0 && idx > 0 {
 52:             // Sustained under ~30 fps: drop one resolution step. If this
 53:             // happens right after a raise, the raise failed — lock raises
 54:             // out for a while so the scale doesn't oscillate.
 55:             if self.frames_since_raise < Self::RAISE_PROBE_FRAMES {
 56:                 self.raise_lockout_frames = Self::RAISE_LOCKOUT_FRAMES;
 57:             }
 58:             self.scale = Self::SCALES[idx - 1];
 59:             self.cooldown_frames = 120;
 60:         } else if self.ema_frame_ms < 17.5
 61:             && idx + 1 < Self::SCALES.len()
 62:             && self.raise_lockout_frames == 0
 63:         {
 64:             // Holding 60Hz vsync (rAF EMA floors at ~16.7 ms, so a lower
 65:             // threshold would never fire): probe one resolution step up.
 66:             self.scale = Self::SCALES[idx + 1];
 67:             self.cooldown_frames = 240;
 68:             self.frames_since_raise = 0;
 69:         }
 70:     }
 71: }
 72: 
 73: #[cfg(test)]
 74: mod tests {
 75:     use super::*;
 76: 
 77:     #[test]
 78:     fn governor_drops_resolution_under_sustained_load() {
 79:         let mut governor = PerfGovernor::new();
 80:         for _ in 0..200 {
 81:             governor.update(50.0); // 20 fps
 82:         }
 83:         assert!(governor.scale() < 0.8);
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     #[test]
 87:     fn governor_raises_resolution_when_holding_60hz_vsync() {
 88:         let mut governor = PerfGovernor::new();
 89:         // rAF on a 60Hz display floors at ~16.7ms even with GPU headroom.
 90:         for _ in 0..600 {
 91:             governor.update(16.7);
 92:         }
 93:         assert_eq!(governor.scale(), 1.0, "must reach native res under vsync");
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     #[test]
 97:     fn governor_locks_out_raises_after_a_failed_probe() {
 98:         let mut governor = PerfGovernor::new();
 99:         for _ in 0..300 {
100:             governor.update(16.7); // raises to 1.0 almost immediately
101:         }
102:         assert_eq!(governor.scale(), 1.0);
103:         for _ in 0..600 {
104:             governor.update(40.0); // raise fails: overloaded at 1.0
105:         }
106:         assert!(governor.scale() < 1.0);
107:         let settled = governor.scale();
108:         for _ in 0..600 {
109:             governor.update(16.7); // healthy again, but inside the lockout
110:         }
111:         assert_eq!(governor.scale(), settled, "raise must stay locked out");
112:     }
113: }
````

````rust
 1: //! One quality decision shared by world generation and renderer profiles.
 2: //!
 3: //! The URL adapter parses `?spec=` into this application-owned value once.
 4: //! Generation and presentation then derive their independent concrete
 5: //! settings from the same decision, preventing case or fallback drift.
 6: 
 7: use std::{error::Error, fmt, str::FromStr};
 8: 
 9: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
10: pub enum QualityProfile {
11:     /// Standard workloads intended for integrated and mobile-class GPUs.
12:     #[default]
13:     Low,
14:     /// Finer generation and larger rendering workloads for high-end systems.
15:     High,
16: }
17: 
18: impl QualityProfile {
19:     pub const ALL: [Self; 2] = [Self::Low, Self::High];
20: 
21:     /// Parses the stable `low`/`high` vocabulary case-insensitively.
22:     pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Option<Self> {
23:         let value = value.trim();
24:         Self::ALL
25:             .into_iter()
26:             .find(|quality| value.eq_ignore_ascii_case(quality.query_value()))
27:     }
28: 
29:     pub const fn query_value(self) -> &'static str {
30:         match self {
31:             Self::Low => "low",
32:             Self::High => "high",
33:         }
34:     }
35: 
36:     pub const fn label(self) -> &'static str {
37:         match self {
38:             Self::Low => "Standard",
39:             Self::High => "High",
40:         }
41:     }
42: }
43: 
44: impl fmt::Display for QualityProfile {
45:     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
46:         formatter.write_str(self.query_value())
47:     }
48: }
49: 
50: impl FromStr for QualityProfile {
51:     type Err = ParseQualityProfileError;
52: 
53:     fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
54:         Self::parse(value).ok_or(ParseQualityProfileError)
55:     }
56: }
57: 
58: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
59: pub struct ParseQualityProfileError;
60: 
61: impl fmt::Display for ParseQualityProfileError {
62:     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
63:         formatter.write_str("expected quality profile `low` or `high`")
64:     }
65: }
66: 
67: impl Error for ParseQualityProfileError {}
68: 
69: #[cfg(test)]
70: mod tests {
71:     use super::*;
72: 
73:     #[test]
74:     fn stable_quality_vocabulary_is_case_insensitive() {
75:         for quality in QualityProfile::ALL {
76:             let value = quality.query_value();
77:             assert_eq!(QualityProfile::parse(value), Some(quality));
78:             assert_eq!(
79:                 QualityProfile::parse(&value.to_ascii_uppercase()),
80:                 Some(quality)
81:             );
82:             assert_eq!(value.parse(), Ok(quality));
83:         }
84:         assert_eq!(QualityProfile::parse("ultra"), None);
85:     }
86: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Survival state and carried-supply policy for one wanderer.
  2: //!
  3: //! The frame orchestrator measures the world (notably its instantaneous
  4: //! temperature) and passes those observations here. This object owns the
  5: //! resulting felt temperature, vitals, inventory, consumption decisions,
  6: //! overconsumption strain, and attrition bookkeeping. Keeping those rules
  7: //! together prevents presentation, streaming, and player relocation concerns
  8: //! from becoming another way to mutate survival state.
  9: 
 10: use vackrooms::domain::entities::player_vitals::{
 11:     ALMOND_WATER_HYDRATION, PlayerVitals, RATION_SATIETY,
 12: };
 13: use vackrooms::domain::entities::supplies::SupplyKind;
 14: 
 15: /// Carried supplies beyond immediate need, per kind.
 16: const CARRY_CAP: u32 = 3;
 17: /// Assisted consumption acts once the matching reserve falls below this.
 18: const AUTO_CONSUME_AT: f32 = 0.5;
 19: /// Share of restoration beyond a full reserve charged to excess strain.
 20: const EXCESS_PER_WASTE: f32 = 0.8;
 21: /// Frugal time drains the excess meter to zero in five minutes.
 22: const EXCESS_DECAY_PER_S: f32 = 1.0 / 300.0;
 23: /// Felt air closes roughly 63% of the gap to measured air in this many
 24: /// seconds. The bounded frame step makes the linear blend stable.
 25: const THERMAL_TAU_S: f32 = 8.0;
 26: 
 27: /// Edge-triggered choices made during one simulation step.
 28: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
 29: pub(crate) struct ConsumptionIntent {
 30:     pub drink: bool,
 31:     pub eat: bool,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: /// Immutable presenter/body view of the survival aggregate.
 35: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 36: pub(crate) struct SurvivalReadout {
 37:     pub vitals: PlayerVitals,
 38:     pub excess: f32,
 39:     pub almond_bottles: u32,
 40:     pub rations: u32,
 41:     pub assisted_consumption: bool,
 42:     pub ambient_c: f32,
 43:     pub deaths: u32,
 44: }
 45: 
 46: /// Cohesive survival aggregate. World mutation after a pickup or death stays
 47: /// with the engine; all survival-state mutation stays here.
 48: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
 49: pub(crate) struct SurvivalInventory {
 50:     vitals: PlayerVitals,
 51:     excess: f32,
 52:     almond_bottles: u32,
 53:     rations: u32,
 54:     assisted_consumption: bool,
 55:     ambient_c: f32,
 56:     deaths: u32,
 57: }
 58: 
 59: impl SurvivalInventory {
 60:     pub fn new(initial_ambient_c: f32) -> Self {
 61:         Self {

 92:     /// Smooths the measured air temperature, then advances physiological
 93:     /// depletion under that felt temperature.
 94:     pub fn advance_vitals(&mut self, dt: f32, instantaneous_c: f32) {
 95:         let blend = (dt / THERMAL_TAU_S).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 96:         self.ambient_c += (instantaneous_c - self.ambient_c) * blend;
 97:         self.vitals = self.vitals.advanced(dt, self.ambient_c);
 98:     }
````
