## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/shaders/surface.wgsl
````wgsl
 1: // Indexed greedy-surface strategy. Packed vertices are pulled from a storage
 2: // buffer and decoded on the GPU, avoiding a CPU-side expanded vertex copy.
 3: 
 4: struct SurfaceVertex {
 5:     @builtin(position) clip_position: vec4<f32>,
 6:     @location(0) world: vec3<f32>,
 7:     @location(1) normal: vec3<f32>,
 8:     @location(2) @interpolate(flat) visual: u32,
 9:     @location(3) @interpolate(flat) baked: f32,
10:     @location(4) @interpolate(flat) ao: f32,
11: };
12: 
13: @vertex
14: fn surface_vertex(@builtin(vertex_index) vertex_index: u32) -> SurfaceVertex {
15:     let packed = packed_vertices[vertex_index];
16:     let normal_axis = (packed.z_normal_material >> 16u) & 255u;
17:     let world = surface_world_position(packed);
18: 
19:     var output: SurfaceVertex;
20:     output.clip_position = frame.view_projection * vec4<f32>(world, 1.0);
21:     output.world = world;
22:     output.normal = normal_for_axis(normal_axis);
23:     output.visual = packed.visual;
24:     output.baked = f32(packed.light_ao & 255u) / 15.0;
25:     output.ao = 1.0 - f32((packed.light_ao >> 8u) & 255u) / 255.0;
26:     return output;
27: }
28: 
29: @fragment
30: fn surface_fragment(input: SurfaceVertex) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
31:     let albedo = packed_srgb_to_linear(input.visual);
32:     let emission = f32(input.visual >> 24u) / 25.5;
33:     let emits = emission > 0.0 && input.normal.y < -0.5;
34:     let radiance = select(
35:         raster_surface_radiance(
36:             input.world,
37:             input.normal,
38:             albedo,
39:             input.baked,
40:             input.ao,
41:             chunk.draw.x,
42:             chunk.draw.y
43:         ),
44:         albedo * emission,
45:         emits
46:     );
47:     return present_radiance(radiance, input.world, input.clip_position.xy);
48: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/config.rs
````rust
  1: //! Typed, target-independent configuration for every WebGPU strategy.
  2: //!
  3: //! The browser may obtain these values from query parameters and settings
  4: //! controls, but no DOM or `wgpu` type crosses this boundary. A profile owns
  5: //! quality and workload budgets. Capability switches cap the runtime toggle
  6: //! set, so profiles cannot claim paths the selected strategy does not own.
  7: 
  8: use std::{error::Error, fmt, str::FromStr};
  9: 
 10: pub use crate::application::ports::RenderArtifactNeeds;
 11: pub use crate::application::quality::{
 12:     ParseQualityProfileError as ParseGpuQualityProfileError, QualityProfile as GpuQualityProfile,
 13: };
 14: use crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles;
 15: 
 16: /// A production rendering strategy with WebGPU presentation.
 17: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
 18: pub enum RendererKind {
 19:     /// Indexed greedy meshes rendered with fixed-function depth testing.
 20:     #[default]
 21:     Surface,
 22:     /// Instanced rectangles reconstructed from compact surface-face records.
 23:     Splat,
 24:     /// Fullscreen primary rays traversing serialized sparse voxel octrees.
 25:     Raymarch,
 26:     /// Software SVO rasterization uploaded through a WebGPU presentation pass.
 27:     Cpu,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: impl RendererKind {
 31:     /// Stable iteration order for menus, diagnostics, and exhaustive tests.
 32:     pub const ALL: [Self; 4] = [Self::Surface, Self::Splat, Self::Raymarch, Self::Cpu];
 33: 
 34:     /// Parses a renderer query value. Surrounding whitespace and ASCII case
 35:     /// are ignored; aliases are deliberately rejected so URLs remain stable.
 36:     pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Option<Self> {
 37:         let value = value.trim();
 38:         Self::ALL
 39:             .into_iter()
 40:             .find(|kind| value.eq_ignore_ascii_case(kind.query_value()))
 41:     }
 42: 
 43:     /// Canonical value used by `?renderer=<value>` and persisted settings.
 44:     pub const fn query_value(self) -> &'static str {
 45:         match self {
 46:             Self::Surface => "surface",
 47:             Self::Splat => "splat",
 48:             Self::Raymarch => "raymarch",
 49:             Self::Cpu => "cpu",
 50:         }
 51:     }
 52: 
 53:     /// Human-readable name suitable for renderer menus and telemetry.
 54:     pub const fn label(self) -> &'static str {
 55:         match self {
 56:             Self::Surface => "WebGPU indexed surfaces",
 57:             Self::Splat => "WebGPU face splats",
 58:             Self::Raymarch => "WebGPU SVO raymarcher",
 59:             Self::Cpu => "CPU reference / WebGPU present",
 60:         }
 61:     }
 62: 
 63:     /// Generation artifacts that must remain available for this strategy.
 64:     pub const fn artifact_needs(self) -> RenderArtifactNeeds {
 65:         match self {
 66:             Self::Surface => RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE,
 67:             Self::Splat => RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT,
 68:             Self::Raymarch => RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH,
 69:             Self::Cpu => RenderArtifactNeeds::CPU,
 70:         }
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     /// Builds the selected strategy's complete profile at one quality tier.
 74:     pub const fn profile(self, quality: GpuQualityProfile) -> RendererProfile {
 75:         RendererProfile::for_renderer(self, quality)
 76:     }
 77: }
 78: 
 79: impl fmt::Display for RendererKind {
 80:     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
 81:         formatter.write_str(self.query_value())
 82:     }
 83: }
 84: 
 85: impl FromStr for RendererKind {
 86:     type Err = ParseRendererKindError;
 87: 
 88:     fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
 89:         Self::parse(value).ok_or(ParseRendererKindError)
 90:     }
 91: }
 92: 
 93: /// Returned when a renderer query value is not in [`RendererKind::ALL`].
 94: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 95: pub struct ParseRendererKindError;
 96: 
 97: impl fmt::Display for ParseRendererKindError {
 98:     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
 99:         formatter.write_str("expected renderer `surface`, `splat`, `raymarch`, or `cpu`")
100:     }
101: }
102: 
103: impl Error for ParseRendererKindError {}
104: 
105: /// Runtime capabilities shared by renderer strategies.
106: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
107: pub struct CommonOptimizationSettings {
108:     /// Permit a strategy's conservative chunk visibility rejection.
109:     pub cull_invisible_chunks: bool,
110:     /// Permit output dithering in WebGPU strategies that implement it.
111:     pub dither_output: bool,
112: }
113: 
114: impl CommonOptimizationSettings {
115:     pub const fn optimized() -> Self {
116:         Self {
117:             cull_invisible_chunks: true,
118:             dither_output: true,
119:         }
120:     }
121: 
122:     /// Deterministic baseline used by offscreen correctness tests.
123:     pub const fn reference() -> Self {
124:         Self {
125:             cull_invisible_chunks: false,
126:             dither_output: false,
127:         }
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: impl Default for CommonOptimizationSettings {
132:     fn default() -> Self {
133:         Self::optimized()
134:     }
135: }
136: 
137: /// Quality metadata shared by renderer profiles.
138: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
139: pub struct CommonGpuConfig {

277: /// Implemented CPU submission and shadow policies for the face-splat
278: /// renderer. Both visible and depth-only draws expand compact face records.
279: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
280: pub struct SplatOptimizationSettings {
281:     /// Sort resident chunks on the CPU before direct draw submission.
282:     pub cpu_front_to_back_submission: bool,

284:     pub cpu_cell_range_culling: bool,
285:     /// Stop submitting whole far chunks after the profile face budget.
286:     pub enforce_face_budget: bool,
287:     /// Permit the hero-fixture face-expanded shadow-map pass.
288:     pub hero_light_shadow_map: bool,
289:     /// Permit the optional compact baked-light scalar in splat shading.
290:     pub baked_surface_lighting: bool,
291: }

300:             baked_surface_lighting: true,
301:         }
302:     }

306:             cpu_front_to_back_submission: false,

359: /// Work-reduction capability policy for the SVO raymarcher.
360: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
361: pub struct RaymarchOptimizationSettings {
362:     /// Traverse intersected chunk intervals from nearest to farthest.
363:     pub front_to_back_chunk_order: bool,
364:     /// Advance across the complete empty SVO leaf containing a sample.
365:     pub empty_space_skipping: bool,
366:     /// Permit finite SVO visibility traces to analytic emitter samples.
367:     pub direct_light_visibility: bool,
368: }
369: 
370: impl RaymarchOptimizationSettings {
371:     pub const fn optimized() -> Self {
372:         Self {
373:             front_to_back_chunk_order: true,
374:             empty_space_skipping: true,
375:             direct_light_visibility: true,
376:         }
377:     }
378: 
379:     pub const fn reference() -> Self {
380:         Self {
381:             front_to_back_chunk_order: false,
382:             empty_space_skipping: false,
383:             // Visibility changes the image, so the reference retains it.
384:             direct_light_visibility: true,
385:         }
386:     }
387: }
388: 
389: impl Default for RaymarchOptimizationSettings {
390:     fn default() -> Self {
391:         Self::optimized()
392:     }
393: }

395: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
396: pub struct RaymarchProfile {
397:     pub common: CommonGpuConfig,
398:     /// Capacity of the camera-visible chunk table (3x3 or 5x5 profile).
399:     pub maximum_resident_chunks: u32,
400:     /// Hard bound for one primary-ray traversal. Empty-leaf skipping changes
401:     /// how much world one step covers without weakening this safety budget.
402:     pub maximum_trace_steps: u32,
403:     /// Analytic rectangle-light visibility samples (center or 2x2 Gauss).
404:     pub area_light_visibility_samples: u8,
405:     pub optimizations: RaymarchOptimizationSettings,
406: }
407: 
408: impl RaymarchProfile {
409:     pub const fn for_quality(quality: GpuQualityProfile) -> Self {
410:         let (maximum_resident_chunks, maximum_trace_steps, area_light_visibility_samples) =
411:             match quality {
412:                 GpuQualityProfile::Low => (9, 768, 1),
413:                 GpuQualityProfile::High => (25, 1_536, 4),
414:             };
415:         Self {
416:             common: CommonGpuConfig::for_quality(quality),
417:             maximum_resident_chunks,
418:             maximum_trace_steps,
419:             area_light_visibility_samples,
420:             optimizations: RaymarchOptimizationSettings::optimized(),
421:         }
422:     }
423: 
424:     pub const fn low() -> Self {
425:         Self::for_quality(GpuQualityProfile::Low)
426:     }
427: 
428:     pub const fn high() -> Self {
429:         Self::for_quality(GpuQualityProfile::High)
430:     }
431: }
432: 
433: impl Default for RaymarchProfile {
434:     fn default() -> Self {
435:         Self::low()
436:     }
437: }

452:     }

469: /// Complete, type-safe configuration for one selected strategy.
470: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
471: pub enum RendererProfile {
472:     Surface(SurfaceProfile),
473:     Splat(SplatProfile),
474:     Raymarch(RaymarchProfile),
475:     Cpu(CpuPresentationProfile),
476: }
477: 
478: impl RendererProfile {
479:     pub const fn for_renderer(renderer: RendererKind, quality: GpuQualityProfile) -> Self {
480:         match renderer {
481:             RendererKind::Surface => Self::Surface(SurfaceProfile::for_quality(quality)),
482:             RendererKind::Splat => Self::Splat(SplatProfile::for_quality(quality)),
483:             RendererKind::Raymarch => Self::Raymarch(RaymarchProfile::for_quality(quality)),
484:             RendererKind::Cpu => Self::Cpu(CpuPresentationProfile::for_quality(quality)),
485:         }
486:     }
487: 
488:     pub const fn renderer(self) -> RendererKind {
489:         match self {
490:             Self::Surface(_) => RendererKind::Surface,
491:             Self::Splat(_) => RendererKind::Splat,
492:             Self::Raymarch(_) => RendererKind::Raymarch,
493:             Self::Cpu(_) => RendererKind::Cpu,
494:         }
495:     }
496: 
497:     pub const fn common(&self) -> &CommonGpuConfig {
498:         match self {
499:             Self::Surface(profile) => &profile.common,
500:             Self::Splat(profile) => &profile.common,
501:             Self::Raymarch(profile) => &profile.common,
502:             Self::Cpu(profile) => &profile.common,
503:         }
504:     }
505: 
506:     pub const fn artifact_needs(self) -> RenderArtifactNeeds {
507:         self.renderer().artifact_needs()
508:     }
509: 
510:     /// GPU backing-store multiplier selected by this profile. CPU rendering
511:     /// returns `None` because its software-framebuffer scale is already a
512:     /// complete resolution policy and must not be multiplied a second time.
513:     pub const fn initial_gpu_render_scale(&self) -> Option<f32> {
514:         match self {
515:             Self::Surface(profile) => Some(profile.common.initial_render_scale),
516:             Self::Splat(profile) => Some(profile.common.initial_render_scale),
517:             Self::Raymarch(profile) => Some(profile.common.initial_render_scale),
518:             Self::Cpu(_) => None,
519:         }
520:     }
521: 
522:     /// Intersects the global runtime switchboard with this strategy's typed
523:     /// capability policy. The returned value contains no switches belonging
524:     /// exclusively to another strategy; retained shadow switches are the
525:     /// explicitly configured visibility capability for that strategy.
526:     pub fn apply_runtime_toggles(&self, requested: RenderToggles) -> RenderToggles {
527:         match self {
528:             Self::Surface(profile) => {
529:                 let mut applied = apply_common_gpu_toggles(&profile.common, requested);
530:                 applied.shadow_pass =
531:                     requested.shadow_pass && profile.optimizations.hero_light_shadow_map;
532:                 applied.baked_lighting =
533:                     requested.baked_lighting && profile.optimizations.baked_surface_lighting;
534:                 applied
535:             }
536:             Self::Splat(profile) => {
537:                 let mut applied = apply_common_gpu_toggles(&profile.common, requested);
538:                 applied.front_to_back =
539:                     requested.front_to_back && profile.optimizations.cpu_front_to_back_submission;
540:                 applied.cell_culling =
541:                     requested.cell_culling && profile.optimizations.cpu_cell_range_culling;
542:                 applied.face_budget =
543:                     requested.face_budget && profile.optimizations.enforce_face_budget;
544:                 applied.shadow_pass =
545:                     requested.shadow_pass && profile.optimizations.hero_light_shadow_map;
546:                 applied.baked_lighting =
547:                     requested.baked_lighting && profile.optimizations.baked_surface_lighting;
548:                 applied
549:             }
550:             Self::Raymarch(profile) => {
551:                 let mut applied = apply_common_gpu_toggles(&profile.common, requested);
552:                 applied.front_to_back =
553:                     requested.front_to_back && profile.optimizations.front_to_back_chunk_order;
554:                 applied.empty_space_skip =
555:                     requested.empty_space_skip && profile.optimizations.empty_space_skipping;
556:                 applied.shadow_pass =
557:                     requested.shadow_pass && profile.optimizations.direct_light_visibility;
558:                 applied
559:             }
560:             Self::Cpu(profile) => {
561:                 let mut applied = RenderToggles::disabled();
562:                 applied.hierarchical_z = requested.hierarchical_z;
563:                 applied.front_to_back = requested.front_to_back;
564:                 applied.mip_lod = requested.mip_lod;
565:                 applied.flashlight_occlusion = requested.flashlight_occlusion;
566:                 applied.deferred_shading = requested.deferred_shading;
567:                 applied.ambient_occlusion = requested.ambient_occlusion;
568:                 applied.baked_lighting = requested.baked_lighting;
569:                 applied.distance_cull =
570:                     requested.distance_cull && profile.common.optimizations.cull_invisible_chunks;
571:                 applied
572:             }
573:         }
574:     }
575: }
576: 
577: fn apply_common_gpu_toggles(common: &CommonGpuConfig, requested: RenderToggles) -> RenderToggles {
578:     let mut applied = RenderToggles::disabled();
579:     applied.distance_cull = requested.distance_cull && common.optimizations.cull_invisible_chunks;
580:     applied.dither = requested.dither && common.optimizations.dither_output;
581:     applied
582: }
583: 
584: impl Default for RendererProfile {
585:     fn default() -> Self {
586:         Self::Surface(SurfaceProfile::default())
587:     }
588: }

590: #[cfg(test)]
591: mod tests {
592:     use super::*;

594:     #[test]
595:     fn renderer_catalog_has_stable_unique_values_and_labels() {
596:         let expected = [
597:             (RendererKind::Surface, "surface", "WebGPU indexed surfaces"),
598:             (RendererKind::Splat, "splat", "WebGPU face splats"),
599:             (RendererKind::Raymarch, "raymarch", "WebGPU SVO raymarcher"),
600:             (RendererKind::Cpu, "cpu", "CPU reference / WebGPU present"),
601:         ];
602:         assert_eq!(RendererKind::ALL.len(), expected.len());
603:         for (index, (kind, query_value, label)) in expected.into_iter().enumerate() {
604:             assert_eq!(RendererKind::ALL[index], kind);
605:             assert_eq!(kind.query_value(), query_value);
606:             assert_eq!(kind.label(), label);
607:             assert_eq!(kind.to_string(), query_value);
608:             assert_eq!(query_value.parse(), Ok(kind));
609:             assert_eq!(query_value.to_ascii_uppercase().parse(), Ok(kind));
610:             assert_eq!(
611:                 RendererKind::parse(&format!("  {query_value}  ")),
612:                 Some(kind)
613:             );
614:         }
615:     }
616: 
617:     #[test]

619:         for invalid in ["", "gpu", "mesh", "software", "webgl", "surface-extra"] {
620:             assert_eq!(RendererKind::parse(invalid), None, "accepted {invalid:?}");
621:             assert_eq!(invalid.parse::<RendererKind>(), Err(ParseRendererKindError));
622:         }
623:         assert_eq!(RendererKind::default(), RendererKind::Surface);
624:     }

631:         ];
632:         assert_eq!(GpuQualityProfile::ALL.len(), expected.len());
633:         for (index, (quality, query_value, label)) in expected.into_iter().enumerate() {
634:             assert_eq!(GpuQualityProfile::ALL[index], quality);
635:             assert_eq!(quality.query_value(), query_value);
636:             assert_eq!(quality.label(), label);
637:             assert_eq!(quality.to_string(), query_value);
638:             assert_eq!(query_value.parse(), Ok(quality));

653:         assert_eq!(CommonGpuConfig::for_quality(GpuQualityProfile::High), high);

  1: //! Bind group zero: one immutable layout and two streaming buffers shared by
  2: //! every GPU strategy.
  3: 
  4: use std::num::NonZeroU64;
  5: 
  6: use bytemuck::Zeroable;
  7: use wgpu::util::DeviceExt;
  8: 
  9: use super::gpu_types::{GpuFrameUniforms, GpuLight};
 10: 
 11: pub struct FrameResources {
 12:     layout: wgpu::BindGroupLayout,
 13:     frame_buffer: wgpu::Buffer,
 14:     light_buffer: wgpu::Buffer,
 15:     bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
 16:     light_capacity: usize,
 17: }
 18: 
 19: impl FrameResources {
 20:     pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device) -> Self {
 21:         let layout = device.create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
 22:             label: Some("webgpu.frame-layout"),
 23:             entries: &[
 24:                 wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
 25:                     binding: 0,
 26:                     visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::VERTEX_FRAGMENT,
 27:                     ty: wgpu::BindingType::Buffer {
 28:                         ty: wgpu::BufferBindingType::Uniform,
 29:                         has_dynamic_offset: false,
 30:                         min_binding_size: NonZeroU64::new(size_of::<GpuFrameUniforms>() as u64),
 31:                     },
 32:                     count: None,
 33:                 },
 34:                 wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
 35:                     binding: 1,
 36:                     visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::VERTEX_FRAGMENT,
 37:                     ty: wgpu::BindingType::Buffer {
 38:                         ty: wgpu::BufferBindingType::Storage { read_only: true },
 39:                         has_dynamic_offset: false,
 40:                         min_binding_size: NonZeroU64::new(size_of::<GpuLight>() as u64),
 41:                     },
 42:                     count: None,
 43:                 },
 44:             ],
 45:         });
 46:         let frame_buffer = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
 47:             label: Some("webgpu.frame-uniforms"),
 48:             size: size_of::<GpuFrameUniforms>() as u64,
 49:             usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
 50:             mapped_at_creation: false,
 51:         });
 52:         let light_capacity = 1;
 53:         let light_buffer = create_light_buffer(device, light_capacity);
 54:         let bind_group = create_bind_group(device, &layout, &frame_buffer, &light_buffer);
 55:         Self {
 56:             layout,
 57:             frame_buffer,
 58:             light_buffer,
 59:             bind_group,
 60:             light_capacity,
 61:         }
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     pub fn layout(&self) -> &wgpu::BindGroupLayout {
 65:         &self.layout
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     pub fn bind_group(&self) -> &wgpu::BindGroup {
 69:         &self.bind_group
 70:     }
 71: 
 72:     pub fn write(
 73:         &mut self,
 74:         device: &wgpu::Device,
 75:         queue: &wgpu::Queue,
 76:         frame: &GpuFrameUniforms,
 77:         lights: &[GpuLight],
 78:     ) {
 79:         if lights.len().max(1) > self.light_capacity {
 80:             self.light_capacity = lights.len().max(1).next_power_of_two();
 81:             self.light_buffer = create_light_buffer(device, self.light_capacity);
 82:             self.bind_group =
 83:                 create_bind_group(device, &self.layout, &self.frame_buffer, &self.light_buffer);
 84:         }
 85:         queue.write_buffer(&self.frame_buffer, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(frame));
 86:         if lights.is_empty() {
 87:             queue.write_buffer(
 88:                 &self.light_buffer,
 89:                 0,
 90:                 bytemuck::bytes_of(&GpuLight::zeroed()),
 91:             );
 92:         } else {
 93:             queue.write_buffer(&self.light_buffer, 0, bytemuck::cast_slice(lights));
 94:         }
 95:     }
 96: }
 97: 
 98: fn create_light_buffer(device: &wgpu::Device, capacity: usize) -> wgpu::Buffer {
 99:     device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
100:         label: Some("webgpu.frame-lights"),
101:         contents: &vec![0; capacity * size_of::<GpuLight>()],
102:         usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::STORAGE | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
103:     })
104: }
105: 
106: fn create_bind_group(
107:     device: &wgpu::Device,
108:     layout: &wgpu::BindGroupLayout,
109:     frame: &wgpu::Buffer,
110:     lights: &wgpu::Buffer,
111: ) -> wgpu::BindGroup {
112:     device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
113:         label: Some("webgpu.frame-bind-group"),
114:         layout,
115:         entries: &[
116:             wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
117:                 binding: 0,
118:                 resource: frame.as_entire_binding(),
119:             },
120:             wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
121:                 binding: 1,
122:                 resource: lights.as_entire_binding(),
123:             },
124:         ],
125:     })
126: }

  1: //! Explicit CPU-to-GPU records.
  2: //!
  3: //! Every struct is 16-byte aligned where WGSL requires it. Compact mesh and
  4: //! face records use integer words and are decoded by vertex pulling, so the
  5: //! worker codec remains independent of wgpu and no compiler layout is relied
  6: //! upon.
  7: 
  8: use bytemuck::{Pod, Zeroable};
  9: 
 10: use crate::application::ports::{
 11:     DynamicLight, FrameParams, LightKind, LightSource, PackedFaceInstance, PackedVertex,
 12:     SupplySprite,
 13: };
 14: use crate::application::render_settings::RenderToggles;
 15: use crate::application::rendering::{camera_basis, webgpu_view_projection};
 16: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{MATERIAL_COLORS, material_emission_strength};
 17: 
 18: /// The high byte of a packed material visual stores authored emission over
 19: /// the current domain range of `0..=10`. The low 24 bits remain the canonical
 20: /// `0xRRGGBB` palette entry, so raster shaders never maintain a second palette.
 21: const PACKED_EMISSION_UNITS_PER_RADIANCE: f32 = u8::MAX as f32 / 10.0;
 22: 
 23: fn pack_material_visual(material: u8) -> u32 {
 24:     let color = MATERIAL_COLORS
 25:         .get(usize::from(material))
 26:         .copied()
 27:         .unwrap_or_default()
 28:         & 0x00ff_ffff;
 29:     let emission = material_emission_strength(material).unwrap_or_default();
 30:     let quantized_emission = (emission * PACKED_EMISSION_UNITS_PER_RADIANCE)
 31:         .round()
 32:         .clamp(0.0, f32::from(u8::MAX)) as u32;
 33:     color | (quantized_emission << 24)
 34: }

265: impl GpuRayScene {
266:     pub const fn from_policy(
267:         chunk_count: u32,
268:         empty_space_skip: bool,
269:         front_to_back: bool,
270:         direct_light_visibility: bool,
271:         area_light_visibility_samples: u8,
272:     ) -> Self {
273:         let mut policy_flags = 0;
274:         if empty_space_skip {
275:             policy_flags |= RAY_POLICY_EMPTY_SPACE_SKIP;
276:         }
277:         if front_to_back {
278:             policy_flags |= RAY_POLICY_FRONT_TO_BACK;
279:         }
280:         if direct_light_visibility {
281:             policy_flags |= RAY_POLICY_DIRECT_LIGHT_VISIBILITY;
282:         }
283:         Self {
284:             chunk_count,
285:             policy_flags,
286:             reserved: [
287:                 validated_area_light_visibility_samples(area_light_visibility_samples),
288:                 0,
289:             ],
290:         }
291:     }
292: }

  1: //! Literate WGSL composition.
  2: //!
  3: //! Each strategy file describes only its own data and pass. The shared file
  4: //! is prepended once so camera, lighting, fog, and display equations cannot
  5: //! drift between surface, splat, and raymarch pipelines.
  6: 
  7: use std::borrow::Cow;
  8: use std::fmt::Write;

 12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 13: pub enum ShaderProgram {
 14:     Surface,
 15:     SurfaceShadow,
 16:     Splat,
 17:     SplatShadow,
 18:     Raymarch,
 19:     CpuPresent,
 20:     SupplyLabels,
 21: }
 22: 
 23: impl ShaderProgram {
 24:     pub fn label(self) -> &'static str {
 25:         match self {
 26:             Self::Surface => "webgpu.surface",
 27:             Self::SurfaceShadow => "webgpu.surface-shadow",
 28:             Self::Splat => "webgpu.splat",
 29:             Self::SplatShadow => "webgpu.splat-shadow",
 30:             Self::Raymarch => "webgpu.raymarch",
 31:             Self::CpuPresent => "webgpu.cpu-present",
 32:             Self::SupplyLabels => "webgpu.supply-labels",
 33:         }
 34:     }
 35: 
 36:     pub fn source(self) -> Cow<'static, str> {
 37:         const COMMON: &str = include_str!("shaders/common.wgsl");
 38:         const HERO_SHADOW_CONTRACT: &str = include_str!("shaders/hero_shadow_contract.wgsl");
 39:         const RASTER_SHADOW: &str = include_str!("shaders/raster_shadow.wgsl");
 40:         const RASTER_CHUNK: &str = include_str!("shaders/raster_chunk_contract.wgsl");
 41:         const SHADOW_CASTER: &str = include_str!("shaders/shadow_caster.wgsl");
 42:         const SURFACE_GEOMETRY: &str = include_str!("shaders/surface_geometry.wgsl");
 43:         const SPLAT_GEOMETRY: &str = include_str!("shaders/splat_geometry.wgsl");
 44:         match self {
 45:             Self::Surface => Cow::Owned(
 46:                 [
 47:                     COMMON,
 48:                     HERO_SHADOW_CONTRACT,
 49:                     RASTER_SHADOW,
 50:                     RASTER_CHUNK,
 51:                     SURFACE_GEOMETRY,
 52:                     include_str!("shaders/surface.wgsl"),
 53:                 ]
 54:                 .concat(),
 55:             ),
 56:             Self::SurfaceShadow => Cow::Owned(
 57:                 [
 58:                     HERO_SHADOW_CONTRACT,
 59:                     SHADOW_CASTER,
 60:                     RASTER_CHUNK,
 61:                     SURFACE_GEOMETRY,
 62:                     include_str!("shaders/surface_shadow.wgsl"),
 63:                 ]
 64:                 .concat(),
 65:             ),
 66:             Self::Splat => Cow::Owned(
 67:                 [
 68:                     COMMON,
 69:                     HERO_SHADOW_CONTRACT,
 70:                     RASTER_SHADOW,
 71:                     RASTER_CHUNK,
 72:                     SPLAT_GEOMETRY,
 73:                     include_str!("shaders/splat.wgsl"),
 74:                 ]
 75:                 .concat(),
 76:             ),
 77:             Self::SplatShadow => Cow::Owned(
 78:                 [
 79:                     HERO_SHADOW_CONTRACT,
 80:                     SHADOW_CASTER,
 81:                     RASTER_CHUNK,
 82:                     SPLAT_GEOMETRY,
 83:                     include_str!("shaders/splat_shadow.wgsl"),
 84:                 ]
 85:                 .concat(),
 86:             ),
 87:             Self::Raymarch => {
 88:                 let mut source = String::from(COMMON);
 89:                 source.push_str(&material_emission_contract_wgsl());
 90:                 source.push_str(include_str!("shaders/raymarch.wgsl"));
 91:                 Cow::Owned(source)
 92:             }
 93:             Self::CpuPresent => Cow::Borrowed(include_str!("shaders/cpu_present.wgsl")),
 94:             Self::SupplyLabels => {
 95:                 Cow::Owned([COMMON, include_str!("shaders/supply_labels.wgsl")].concat())
 96:             }
 97:         }
 98:     }
 99: 
100:     pub fn create_module(self, device: &wgpu::Device) -> wgpu::ShaderModule {
101:         device.create_shader_module(wgpu::ShaderModuleDescriptor {
102:             label: Some(self.label()),
103:             source: wgpu::ShaderSource::Wgsl(self.source()),
104:         })
105:     }
106: }

108: /// Generates the ray-visible emission switch directly from the domain
109: /// contract. Raster uploads carry the same information in their compact
110: /// visual word; the SVO already carries color but still needs an exact
111: /// material-to-strength mapping at shader creation time.
112: fn material_emission_contract_wgsl() -> String {
113:     let mut source = String::from(
114:         "\n// Generated from voxel_grid::material_emission_strength.\n\
115:          fn authored_emission_strength(material: u32) -> f32 {\n\
116:              switch material {\n",
117:     );
118:     for material in 0..VOXEL_MATERIAL_COUNT {
119:         let material = material as u8;
120:         let Some(strength) = material_emission_strength(material) else {
121:             continue;
122:         };
123:         writeln!(
124:             source,
125:             "        case {material}u: {{ return {strength:.6}; }}"
126:         )
127:         .expect("writing WGSL to a String cannot fail");
128:     }
129:     source.push_str(
130:         "        default: { return 0.0; }\n\
131:              }\n\
132:          }\n",
133:     );
134:     source
135: }

 1: //! Browser implementation of the core's `TelemetryPort`:
 2: //! `performance.now()` for durations, `console.log` for output.
 3: 
 4: use vackrooms::use_cases::ports::TelemetryPort;
 5: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 6: 
 7: pub struct ConsoleTelemetry;
 8: 
 9: /// Shared instance handed to use cases as `&'static dyn TelemetryPort`.
10: pub static CONSOLE_TELEMETRY: ConsoleTelemetry = ConsoleTelemetry;
11: 
12: impl TelemetryPort for ConsoleTelemetry {
13:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64 {
14:         web_sys::window()
15:             .and_then(|w| w.performance())
16:             .map(|p| (p.now() * 1000.0) as u64)
17:             .unwrap_or(0)
18:     }
19: 
20:     fn log(&self, message: &str) {
21:         web_sys::console::log_1(&JsValue::from_str(message));
22:     }
23: }
````

15:     pub toggles: RenderToggles,
16:     pub cpu: CpuRenderSettings,
17: }
18: 
19: impl ReferenceRenderSettings {
20:     /// Apply the fixture camera's vertical field of view to the CPU settings
21:     /// shared by both reference renderers.
22:     pub fn effective_cpu_settings(&self) -> CpuRenderSettings {
23:         let mut cpu = self.cpu;
24:         if self.camera.fov_degrees.is_finite() && (1.0..179.0).contains(&self.camera.fov_degrees) {
25:             cpu.fov_tan = (self.camera.fov_degrees.to_radians() * 0.5).tan();
26:         }
27:         cpu.toggles = self.toggles;
28:         cpu
29:     }
30: 
31:     pub fn frame_params(&self, scene_lights: &[LightSource]) -> FrameParams {
32:         FrameParams {
33:             camera_pos: self.camera.position,
34:             yaw: self.camera.yaw,
35:             pitch: self.camera.pitch,
36:             scene_lights: scene_lights.to_vec(),
37:             environment: self.environment,
38:             ..FrameParams::default()
39:         }
40:     }
41: }
42:

44: pub struct RenderedImage {
45:     pub width: u32,
46:     pub height: u32,
47:     pub rgba: Vec<u8>,
48: }
49: 
50: pub trait ReferenceRendererPort {
51:     fn render(
52:         &mut self,
53:         scene: &RenderSceneSnapshot,
54:         settings: &ReferenceRenderSettings,
55:     ) -> RenderedImage;
56: }
57: 
58: pub fn render_reference(
59:     scene: &RenderSceneSnapshot,
60:     settings: &ReferenceRenderSettings,
61:     mut renderer: impl ReferenceRendererPort,
62: ) -> RenderedImage {
63:     renderer.render(scene, settings)
64: }

23: /// A platform-free dense scene description. Rendering metadata is deliberately
24: /// absent: [`crate::reference::scene::build_render_scene`] owns SVO
25: /// construction and atlas serialization.
26: pub struct RoomScene {
27:     voxels: VoxelGrid,
28:     voxel_size: f32,
29:     origin: [f32; 3],
30: }
31: 
32: impl RoomScene {
33:     /// One closed 4x4x4-world-unit room with a single 0.5-unit fluorescent
34:     /// ceiling panel. The panel replaces one ceiling voxel and its underside
35:     /// borders air; the entire floor remains ordinary non-emissive carpet.
36:     pub fn single_ceiling_fixture() -> Self {
37:         let mut voxels = VoxelGrid::new(ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS, ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS, ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS);
38:         fill_floor(&mut voxels);
39:         fill_boundary_walls(&mut voxels);
40:         fill_ceiling(&mut voxels);
41:         voxels.set(PANEL_X, ROOM_CEILING_Y, PANEL_Z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
42: 
43:         Self {
44:             voxels,
45:             voxel_size: REFERENCE_VOXEL_SIZE,
46:             origin: [0.0; 3],
47:         }
48:     }
49: 
50:     pub fn voxels(&self) -> &VoxelGrid {
51:         &self.voxels
52:     }
53: 
54:     pub fn voxel_size(&self) -> f32 {
55:         self.voxel_size
56:     }
57: 
58:     pub fn origin(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
59:         self.origin
60:     }
61: 
62:     pub(crate) fn into_parts(self) -> (VoxelGrid, f32, [f32; 3]) {
63:         (self.voxels, self.voxel_size, self.origin)
64:     }
65: }
66: 
67: fn fill_floor(voxels: &mut VoxelGrid) {
68:     for z in 0..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS {
69:         for x in 0..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS {
70:             voxels.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_FLOOR);
71:         }
72:     }
73: }
74: 
75: fn fill_boundary_walls(voxels: &mut VoxelGrid) {
76:     for y in 1..=ROOM_CEILING_Y {
77:         for edge in 0..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS {
78:             voxels.set(0, y, edge, VOXEL_WALL);
79:             voxels.set(ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS - 1, y, edge, VOXEL_WALL);
80:             voxels.set(edge, y, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
81:             voxels.set(edge, y, ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS - 1, VOXEL_WALL);
82:         }
83:     }
84: }
85: 
86: fn fill_ceiling(voxels: &mut VoxelGrid) {
87:     for z in 1..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS - 1 {
88:         for x in 1..ROOM_EDGE_VOXELS - 1 {
89:             voxels.set(x, ROOM_CEILING_Y, z, VOXEL_CEILING);
90:         }
91:     }
92: }
93: 
94: pub trait RoomFixture {
95:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str;
96:     fn build(&self) -> RoomScene;
97:     fn camera(&self) -> CameraSpec;
98:     fn environment(&self) -> Environment;
99: }

 1: //! Compile dense reference rooms into the serialized scene contract consumed
 2: //! by reference renderers.
 3: 
 4: use crate::adapters::collect_emissive_lights::collect_emissive_lights;
 5: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, LightSource};
 6: use crate::reference::room::RoomScene;
 7: use vackrooms::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
 8: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
 9: use vackrooms::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
10: use vackrooms::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::{VoxelLightingSettings, bake_voxel_lighting};
11: 
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
13: pub struct RenderSceneSnapshot {
14:     /// Row-padded SVO storage words (four `u32` values per node).
15:     pub atlas: Vec<u32>,
16:     pub chunks: Vec<ChunkDraw>,
17:     /// Analytic fixtures derived from the same emissive voxel surfaces as
18:     /// the atlas. Reference renderers must not silently fall back to the
19:     /// low-precision bake when production frames use physical lights.
20:     pub scene_lights: Vec<LightSource>,
21: }
22: 
23: pub fn build_render_scene(scene: RoomScene) -> RenderSceneSnapshot {
24:     let (mut voxels, voxel_size, origin) = scene.into_parts();
25:     let svo_depth = cube_depth(&voxels);
26:     let world_size = voxels.width() as f32 * voxel_size;
27:     let scene_lights = collect_emissive_lights(&voxels, voxel_size, origin, 0);
28: 
29:     let lighting = VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(voxel_size)
30:         .expect("RoomScene guarantees a positive finite voxel size");
31:     bake_voxel_lighting(&mut voxels, lighting);
32: 
33:     let svo = BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&voxels, svo_depth, world_size);
34:     let serialized = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
35:     RenderSceneSnapshot {
36:         atlas: serialized.texel_data,
37:         chunks: vec![ChunkDraw {
38:             origin,
39:             root_index: svo.root as i32,
40:             world_size,
41:             voxel_size,
42:             svo_depth: svo_depth as u8,
43:         }],
44:         scene_lights,
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: fn cube_depth(voxels: &VoxelGrid) -> u32 {
49:     let edge = voxels.width();
50:     assert!(
51:         edge.is_power_of_two(),
52:         "reference room edge must be a power of two"
53:     );
54:     assert_eq!(voxels.height(), edge, "reference room must be cubic");
55:     assert_eq!(voxels.depth(), edge, "reference room must be cubic");
56:     edge.ilog2()
57: }
58: 
59: #[cfg(test)]
60: mod tests {
61:     use super::*;
62:     use crate::application::ports::LightKind;
63: 
64:     #[test]
65:     fn reference_snapshot_keeps_the_analytic_ceiling_fixture() {
66:         let snapshot = build_render_scene(RoomScene::single_ceiling_fixture());

68:         assert_eq!(snapshot.scene_lights.len(), 1);
69:         let fixture = snapshot.scene_lights[0];

71:         assert_eq!(fixture.kind, LightKind::CeilingPanel);
72:         assert!(fixture.intensity > 0.0);

75: }

 1: //! Route-anchor telemetry against the real Level 0 generator: the anchor
 2: //! must find the guaranteed level door from authoritative streamed exits,
 3: //! never from invented data.
 4: 
 5: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 6: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 7: use wasm_frontend::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;

15:     fn draw(&mut self, _frame: &FrameParams, _chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {}
16: }
17: 
18: /// The world-tuning default guarantees a Level 0 door near (172, -116).
19: /// Standing a dozen meters away, the route anchor must resolve it with a
20: /// truthful straight-line range; far from any door it must stay empty.
21: #[test]
22: fn route_anchor_resolves_the_guaranteed_door_from_streamed_world_data() {
23:     let seed = 42;
24:     let config = EngineConfig {
25:         seed,
26:         chunk_size: 10.0,
27:         chunk_radius: 1,
28:         spawn: [172.0, 1.7, -104.0],
29:         spawn_yaw: 0.0,
30:         initial_level: 0,
31:         ..EngineConfig::default()
32:     };
33:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(
34:         SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
35:         seed,
36:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
37:     );
38:     let mut engine = Engine::new(config, Box::new(NullRenderer), Box::new(source));
39: 
40:     let input = InputFrame::default();
41:     // Stream the neighborhood in and let the route cadence fire.
42:     for _ in 0..120 {
43:         engine.tick(1.0 / 60.0, &input);
44:     }
45: 
46:     let route = engine
47:         .stats()
48:         .route
49:         .expect("the guaranteed door must be resident and selected");
50:     assert_eq!(route.target_level, 1, "Level 0's guaranteed door leads to 1");
51:     assert!(
52:         (5.0..40.0).contains(&route.range_m),
53:         "range must be the real straight-line distance, got {}",
54:         route.range_m
55:     );
56:     assert!(route.bearing_deg < 360);
57: }
58: 
59: #[test]
60: fn route_anchor_is_truthfully_absent_away_from_doors() {
61:     let seed = 42;
62:     let spawn_at = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(seed);
63:     let config = EngineConfig {
64:         seed,
65:         chunk_size: 10.0,
66:         chunk_radius: 1,
67:         spawn: [spawn_at.x, 1.7, spawn_at.z],
68:         spawn_yaw: 0.0,
69:         initial_level: 0,
70:         ..EngineConfig::default()
71:     };
72:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(
73:         SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
74:         seed,
75:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
76:     );
77:     let mut engine = Engine::new(config, Box::new(NullRenderer), Box::new(source));
78:     let input = InputFrame::default();
79:     for _ in 0..60 {
80:         engine.tick(1.0 / 60.0, &input);
81:     }
82:     // The spawn corridor is far from the guaranteed door; unless generation
83:     // happens to place one inside this 3x3 footprint, the anchor is empty.
84:     if let Some(route) = engine.stats().route {
85:         // If a door genuinely is resident, the range must at least be real.
86:         assert!(route.range_m.is_finite() && route.range_m < 100.0);

88: }

199: fn create_vulkan_context() -> VulkanContext {
200:     let mut descriptor = wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle();
201:     descriptor.backends = wgpu::Backends::VULKAN;
202:     descriptor.flags =
203:         wgpu::InstanceFlags::debugging() | wgpu::InstanceFlags::STRICT_WEBGPU_COMPLIANCE;
204:     let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(descriptor);
205:     let adapter = pollster::block_on(instance.request_adapter(&wgpu::RequestAdapterOptions {
206:         power_preference: wgpu::PowerPreference::None,
207:         force_fallback_adapter: false,
208:         compatible_surface: None,
209:         apply_limit_buckets: false,
210:     }))
211:     .unwrap_or_else(|error| {
212:         panic!(
213:             "Vulkan renderer tests require a Vulkan 1.2+ adapter; install Mesa Lavapipe or expose a Vulkan device: {error}"
214:         )
215:     });
216:     let info = adapter.get_info();
217:     assert_eq!(
218:         info.backend,
219:         wgpu::Backend::Vulkan,
220:         "test harness must never fall back from Vulkan; selected {info:?}"
221:     );
222:     eprintln!(
223:         "Vulkan test adapter: {} ({}, {})",
224:         info.name, info.driver, info.driver_info
225:     );
226: 
227:     let (device, queue) = pollster::block_on(adapter.request_device(&wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
228:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-device"),
229:         required_features: wgpu::Features::empty(),
230:         required_limits: wgpu::Limits::defaults(),
231:         ..Default::default()
232:     }))
233:     .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("failed to create the Vulkan test device: {error}"));
234: 
235:     VulkanContext {
236:         _instance: instance,
237:         device,
238:         queue,
239:     }
240: }

286: fn add_lateral_air_halo(source: &VoxelGrid) -> VoxelGrid {
287:     let mut halo = VoxelGrid::new(source.width() + 2, source.height(), source.depth() + 2);
288:     for z in 0..source.depth() {
289:         for y in 0..source.height() {
290:             for x in 0..source.width() {
291:                 halo.set(x + 1, y, z + 1, source.get(x, y, z));
292:                 halo.set_light_rgb(x + 1, y, z + 1, source.get_light_rgb(x, y, z));
293:             }
294:         }
295:     }
296:     halo
297: }

299: fn create_production_pipelines(gpu: &VulkanContext) -> ProductionPipelines {
300:     let validation = gpu.device.push_error_scope(wgpu::ErrorFilter::Validation);
301:     let frame = FrameResources::new(&gpu.device);
302:     let surface = SurfacePipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout(), 16.0);
303:     let splat = SplatPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout(), 16.0, 16_384);
304:     let mut raymarch = RaymarchPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout(), 1);
305:     raymarch.configure(RaymarchRuntimeOptions::new(16.0, true, 4));
306:     let cpu_present = CpuPresentPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, WIDTH, HEIGHT);
307:     let supply_labels = SupplyLabelPipeline::new(&gpu.device, TARGET_FORMAT, frame.layout());
308:     assert_validation_clean(&gpu.device, validation, "production pipeline creation");
309:     ProductionPipelines {
310:         frame,
311:         surface,
312:         splat,
313:         raymarch,
314:         cpu_present,
315:         supply_labels,
316:     }
317: }

321:     let lights = collect_frame_lights(&fixture.frame);
322:     let frame = GpuFrameUniforms::from_frame(
323:         &fixture.frame,
324:         WIDTH,
325:         HEIGHT,
326:         FOV_TAN,
327:         16.0,
328:         512,
329:         lights.len(),
330:         fixture.toggles,
331:     );
332:     pipelines
333:         .frame
334:         .write(&gpu.device, &gpu.queue, &frame, &lights);
335:     let surface_chunk = SurfaceChunk {
336:         key: (0, 0),
337:         origin: [0.0; 3],
338:         mesh: &fixture.surface_mesh,
339:     };
340:     let splat_chunk = SurfaceChunk {
341:         key: (0, 0),
342:         origin: [0.0; 3],
343:         mesh: &fixture.splat_mesh,

452: fn upload_raster_fixture(
453:     gpu: &VulkanContext,
454:     fixture: &Fixture,
455:     surface: &mut SurfacePipeline,
456:     splat: &mut SplatPipeline,
457: ) {
458:     surface.upload(
459:         &gpu.device,
460:         &[SurfaceChunk {
461:             key: (0, 0),
462:             origin: [0.0; 3],
463:             mesh: &fixture.surface_mesh,
464:         }],
465:     );
466:     splat.upload(
467:         &gpu.device,
468:         &[SurfaceChunk {

470:             origin: [0.0; 3],
471:             mesh: &fixture.splat_mesh,
472:         }],
473:     );

475: 
476: fn render_offscreen(
477:     gpu: &VulkanContext,
478:     label: &str,
479:     draw: impl FnOnce(&mut wgpu::CommandEncoder, &wgpu::TextureView, &wgpu::TextureView),
480: ) -> Vec<u8> {
481:     let validation = gpu.device.push_error_scope(wgpu::ErrorFilter::Validation);
482:     let extent = wgpu::Extent3d {
483:         width: WIDTH,
484:         height: HEIGHT,
485:         depth_or_array_layers: 1,
486:     };
487:     let color = gpu.device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
488:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-color"),
489:         size: extent,
490:         mip_level_count: 1,
491:         sample_count: 1,
492:         dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
493:         format: TARGET_FORMAT,
494:         usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_SRC,
495:         view_formats: &[],
496:     });
497:     let depth = gpu.device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
498:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-depth"),
499:         size: extent,
500:         mip_level_count: 1,
501:         sample_count: 1,
502:         dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
503:         format: wgpu::TextureFormat::Depth32Float,
504:         usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT,
505:         view_formats: &[],
506:     });
507:     let color_view = color.create_view(&Default::default());
508:     let depth_view = depth.create_view(&Default::default());
509:     let readback = gpu.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
510:         label: Some("vackrooms.vulkan-test-readback"),
511:         size: u64::from(COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW * HEIGHT),
512:         usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST | wgpu::BufferUsages::MAP_READ,
513:         mapped_at_creation: false,
514:     });
515:     let mut encoder = gpu
516:         .device
517:         .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor { label: Some(label) });
518:     draw(&mut encoder, &color_view, &depth_view);
519:     encoder.copy_texture_to_buffer(
520:         color.as_image_copy(),
521:         wgpu::TexelCopyBufferInfo {
522:             buffer: &readback,
523:             layout: wgpu::TexelCopyBufferLayout {
524:                 offset: 0,
525:                 bytes_per_row: Some(COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW),
526:                 rows_per_image: Some(HEIGHT),
527:             },
528:         },
529:         extent,
530:     );
531:     gpu.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);
532:     let validation_result = validation.pop();
533: 
534:     let (mapped_tx, mapped_rx) = mpsc::channel();
535:     readback
536:         .slice(..)
537:         .map_async(wgpu::MapMode::Read, move |result| {
538:             mapped_tx.send(result).expect("map receiver remains alive");
539:         });
540:     gpu.device
541:         .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
542:         .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: device polling failed: {error}"));
543:     mapped_rx
544:         .recv()
545:         .expect("Vulkan map callback must run")
546:         .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: readback mapping failed: {error}"));
547: 
548:     let pixels = {
549:         let padded = readback
550:             .slice(..)
551:             .get_mapped_range()
552:             .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: mapped range is unavailable: {error}"));
553:         let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity((RGBA_BYTES_PER_ROW * HEIGHT) as usize);
554:         for row in padded.chunks_exact(COPY_BYTES_PER_ROW as usize) {
555:             pixels.extend_from_slice(&row[..RGBA_BYTES_PER_ROW as usize]);
556:         }
557:         pixels
558:     };
559:     readback.unmap();
560:     if let Some(error) = pollster::block_on(validation_result) {
561:         panic!("{label}: WebGPU/Vulkan validation error: {error}");
562:     }
563:     pixels
564: }
565: 
566: fn assert_validation_clean(device: &wgpu::Device, validation: wgpu::ErrorScopeGuard, label: &str) {
567:     let result = validation.pop();
568:     device
569:         .poll(wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely())
570:         .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{label}: device polling failed: {error}"));
571:     if let Some(error) = pollster::block_on(result) {
572:         panic!("{label}: WebGPU/Vulkan validation error: {error}");
573:     }
574: }
575: 
576: fn assert_non_clear_variation(label: &str, rgba: &[u8]) {
577:     assert_eq!(rgba.len(), (WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4) as usize);
578:     let first = &rgba[..3];
579:     let mut different_from_clear = 0usize;
580:     let mut min_luminance = u16::MAX;
581:     let mut max_luminance = 0u16;
582:     for pixel in rgba.chunks_exact(4) {
583:         assert_eq!(pixel[3], 255, "{label} emitted non-opaque pixels");
584:         different_from_clear += usize::from(&pixel[..3] != first);
585:         let luminance = u16::from(pixel[0]) + u16::from(pixel[1]) + u16::from(pixel[2]);
586:         min_luminance = min_luminance.min(luminance);
587:         max_luminance = max_luminance.max(luminance);
588:     }
589:     assert!(
590:         different_from_clear > 8,
591:         "{label} remained at its clear color: first={first:?}, changed={different_from_clear}"
592:     );
593:     assert!(
594:         max_luminance.saturating_sub(min_luminance) > 6,
595:         "{label} produced no meaningful scene contrast: min={min_luminance}, max={max_luminance}"
596:     );
597: }
````

  8: 
  9: Most importantly, it correctly drops far **whole chunks** once the face budget is exhausted, rather than randomly thinning individual faces and creating holes; fog is intended to hide that cutoff.  11: ## Why it locks up
 12: 
 13: The lockup is **not primarily a GPU splat issue**. The game remains single-threaded WASM: when a new section is required, `LocalChunkSource::load()` synchronously performs the full pipeline—halo generation, crop, surface-mesh/face-instance extraction, SVO construction, GPU serialization, and collision-AABB extraction—before the browser can render the next frame.  14: 
 15: Your engine does limit the *number* of loads per tick, and it loads coarse chunks before later refinement, but each selected load is still an indivisible, blocking job. The codebase’s architecture notes explicitly identify that there is no background meshing thread in single-threaded WASM; the current answer is time slicing, while Web Worker/WASM-thread generation is listed as the future solution.  16: 
 17: The likely trigger when crossing into another chunk is therefore:
 18: 
 19: ```text
 20: Player crosses streaming boundary
 21: -> required resident set changes
 22: -> Engine calls synchronous ChunkSource::load()
 23: -> one whole chunk pipeline runs on the main WASM/UI thread
 24: -> rendering/input/event loop cannot run
 25: -> visible freeze
 26: ```
 27: 
 28: The initial load may feel acceptable because it happens behind the loading overlay. Later section generation happens while the player is moving, so the same cost becomes a lock-up.
 29: 
 30: ## Multithreading target
 31: 
 32: Move **only pure chunk construction** to workers first. Keep the game loop, WebGL, renderer resource ownership, player state, input, and chunk-store mutation on the main thread.
 33: 
 34: ```text
 35: Main thread
 36:   StreamingPolicy decides required chunk keys
 37:   -> enqueue (origin, LOD, seed, config, request generation)
 38:   -> continue rendering current resident set
 39:   <- receive completed ChunkPayload
 40:   -> validate request is still wanted
 41:   -> upload face/mesh/light GPU buffers
 42:   -> install collision + chunk payload
 43: 
 44: Worker pool
 45:   Generate architectural VoxelGrid with halo
 46:   -> BFS voxel lighting
 47:   -> build greedy surface mesh / face instances
 48:   -> build SVO + serialize atlas data
 49:   -> extract collision AABBs
 50:   -> post ChunkPayload back
 51: ```
 52: 
 53: This split is clean because `LocalChunkSource::load()` already encapsulates exactly those pure operations, and its output is a self-contained `ChunkPayload`.  55: ## Do this before threads
 56: 
 57: Before adding workers, add per-stage timing around `load()` so you know what actually freezes:
 58: 
 59: - Region/architectural generation
 60: - BFS light propagation
 61: - Surface mesh + face-instance extraction
 62: - SVO build
 63: - GPU serialization
 64: - Collision extraction
 65: - Main-thread GPU buffer upload
 66: 
 67: Your telemetry already has a port architecture, and the renderer already exposes GPU timing and splat counts, so adding per-chunk CPU stage timings will identify whether the main offender is generation, mesh extraction, SVO recursion, or WebGL upload.  68: 
 69: Also make the main thread reject stale work: if the player has moved away before a worker completes a chunk, discard its payload rather than uploading it. Worker results must be keyed by `(origin, lod, generation_epoch)` so an old fine result cannot overwrite a newer resident decision.
 70: 
 71: ## Worker constraints
 72: 
 73: WebAssembly threads with shared memory require cross-origin isolation in browsers, typically `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` plus `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. If you do not want to impose that immediately, use ordinary Web Workers with a second WASM instance and transfer completed typed-array payloads back; it will still remove the visible UI freeze, though payload transfer/allocation overhead must be measured.
 74: 
 75: Do **not** share a WebGL context with generation workers. WebGL buffer and texture creation should remain on the render thread; workers should output plain serialized chunk data.
 76: 
 77: ## The flashlight-grey bug
 78: 
 79: Your wall source color is still correct in the underlying world data: `VOXELWALL` maps to `0xddcc66`, which is the yellow-beige wall color you expect.  82: 
 83: The most likely failure modes are:
 84: 
 85: 1. **Direct flashlight light is added as neutral grey after albedo is lost**, such as writing `vec3(lightAmount)` instead of multiplying yellow wall albedo by illumination.
 86: 2. **The flashlight bypasses or overwrites the material palette**, especially if the shader branches into a generic “lit surface” color.
 87: 3. **The 3D light volume is treated as grayscale intensity instead of RGB indirect light**, removing the warm/yellow information under direct illumination.
 88: 4. **The flat vertex-stage light output uses a white direct term but fails to preserve `materialColor`**, then fog simply mixes the already-grey result.
 89: 5. **The face material mapping differs from the greedy shader mapping**, so wall instances resolve to a default grey material rather than `VOXELWALL`.
 90: 
 91: The evidence points away from missing material data: `PackedFaceInstance` explicitly uploads `material`, and wall color is defined in the core SVO builder. [ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws](https://ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/web/direct-files/attachments/6575456/ab41dcc8-f278-45ea-bf6f-5471d0de6e55/repomix-output.json?AWSAccessKeyId=ASIA2F3EMEYEUNKBDGCY&Signature=F%2FDYJSkuyq%2F7o9epLmsNDjRFXyQ%3D&x-amz-security-token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEPL%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2FwEaCXVzLWVhc3QtMSJGMEQCIBLo83%2BRB7u8wThue5C96yz28Sm1LtoJD9cbXhhWUtThAiB7Yfj0JmF4YAPykj5galiYafeTL6BujDFOWTtD2sQmEir8BAi7%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F8BEAEaDDY5OTc1MzMwOTcwNSIMVbIUrxiHU%2FAKYJ87KtAEZcM0pjXLz2Mkg7pl18xV%2FSYpnjZ5NXbFXxF7X5YnbhlIZVljbiApa4J0XFqb3WVStFYHwUhqm76dFL%2Flkq47gQdRdM%2F%2B7oA5ZuxGOiZv6EbJTXr2HCnUbMUK4zA8BYKZiavzkpjIUDfM3hmxJHfBPEXoHIxKbyPVkPxEN6P9NA9WqsuQIFxJ4hCMuQHIpKqKm5MDki38U0G4OKlwjEEN2UGQSY4ZT2TWeV%2BN0Z%2FKyf2OZ87FwQKq%2FovUMVnZLweb9mhzeb7nTCNJgCDT3aGIE67RnOQAOuKFQ48L%2B%2FNcK%2BNtz%2Flm7%2BHXpONNlgK2%2F0ulovyLBa%2FGlRMBKwkUrPR38yjD9EdOfNzc31CpiCIaH6q4Mzlqnxfq6XBwPfdhkKI2OlxmaVx3CZ4ybTSBYln1uKZOsTwaQWaYIAyFy9G0NLOEb4q%2F3B%2FLvpfpQHWDG4KDUezz%2BKjIwitmArnFsCpLfxppZfRMmLPV%2BLvE%2BU%2Bk7BFyMXc%2FymY8CrcLyIIu208NHKYsR0%2F22nqqfmneV1RTYVng%2BIlUgdIkvMHhIMdZoy%2FPFjCnuMv3DYCatMnlLg93t%2B2fbOFExP%2Fo0dzDoC7cx3SxyBJ%2BMl0%2B0t45LjpGTwzIHChQKrbuSRtgPmMXs%2FgSuWe06SWIrT5UOdYlr%2B3q%2BE%2FzOYxxcd9tyWMLVOQE5YwnOrcl5TrnrLcPoAoj9L88UQwVXF3qWPSuZQtRLnFSZlKo0LT55j%2Fhr6lfrUyqpVFy9yseh4s2rIkxEuN2kYdTYJUik7u1j1ESyX%2FnJyCwpzCt3sTSBjqZAZvHbt1emQDF054tPL%2F6z%2B0gwNXwe%2BYK8YoT2BbL0J%2FznQgBxYy%2Bf%2F6AfY%2Bgql6QoxtiXr0pLcxg0oAOnPBMqtsKILP1HJiaMofgZb0ndEIbfYJacko5EeBwKmVgnOA3vEPZuBVt7EmuTmu4kVNnwR%2F8xxsfVP7DgGtlhBAZiqMVRaje%2Fkf2njBCdm5cJBKZEmpN9E3Xs4nMeg%3D%3D&Expires=1783708928)
 92: 
 93: ## Correct lighting rule
 94: 
 95: Every non-emissive surface should follow this rule:
 96: 
 97: \[
 98: \text{final surface color} =
 99: \text{wall albedo} \times
100: (\text{indirect light} + \text{direct flashlight/light contribution})
101: \]
102: 
103: Not this:
104: 
105: \[
106: \text{final surface color} =
107: \text{indirectly colored wall} + \text{white flashlight replacement}
108: \]
109: 
110: In shader terms, make the material color the immutable base:
111: 
112: ```glsl
113: vec3 albedo = materialColor(aFaceMeta.w); // wall -> vec3(0.867, 0.800, 0.400)
114: 
115: vec3 indirect = sampleLightVolume(faceCenter) * aoTerm;
116: vec3 direct = flashlightTerm + selectedFixtureTerms;
117: vec3 lighting = max(indirect, vec3(0.04)) + direct;
118: 
119: // Preserve material hue under all direct illumination.
120: vec3 lit = albedo * lighting;
121: 
122: // Only emissive fixtures bypass ordinary albedo lighting.
123: if (isEmissive) {
124:     lit = max(lit, emissiveFixtureColor);
125: }
126: ```
127: 
128: The flashlight should make the walls become **brighter yellow**, perhaps slightly desaturated at extreme brightness after tone mapping, but never neutral grey.
129: 
130: ## Lighting restoration order
131: 
132: 1. Render `materialColor` only—no fog, lights, AO, or shadow—and verify walls are unmistakably `0xddcc66`.
133: 2. Add baked light-volume RGB multiplied by albedo; verify dark walls remain yellow-brown rather than grey.
134: 3. Add AO and face-direction bands.
135: 4. Add flashlight alone; verify it brightens yellow, not replaces it.
136: 5. Add fixture lights.
137: 6. Add hero shadow.
138: 7. Add fog last.
139: 
140: This isolates the exact pass that destroys the wall color instead of tuning all lighting at once.
141: 
142: ## Best next change
143: 
144: Do **not** begin with all the complexity of shared-memory WASM threads. First, profile and split `LocalChunkSource::load()` into measurable stages; then put that pure pipeline in a worker queue while the current renderer keeps drawing the previous resident set. In parallel, add the material-only shader debug mode and fix the flashlight equation before changing any more lighting aesthetics. [ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws](https://ppl-ai-file-upload.s3.amazonaws.com/web/direct-files/attachments/6575456/ab41dcc8-f278-45ea-bf6f-5471d0de6e55/repomix-output.json?AWSAccessKeyId=ASIA2F3EMEYEUNKBDGCY&Signature=F%2FDYJSkuyq%2F7o9epLmsNDjRFXyQ%3D&x-amz-security-token=IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEPL%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2FwEaCXVzLWVhc3QtMSJGMEQCIBLo83%2BRB7u8wThue5C96yz28Sm1LtoJD9cbXhhWUtThAiB7Yfj0JmF4YAPykj5galiYafeTL6BujDFOWTtD2sQmEir8BAi7%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F%2F8BEAEaDDY5OTc1MzMwOTcwNSIMVbIUrxiHU%2FAKYJ87KtAEZcM0pjXLz2Mkg7pl18xV%2FSYpnjZ5NXbFXxF7X5YnbhlIZVljbiApa4J0XFqb3WVStFYHwUhqm76dFL%2Flkq47gQdRdM%2F%2B7oA5ZuxGOiZv6EbJTXr2HCnUbMUK4zA8BYKZiavzkpjIUDfM3hmxJHfBPEXoHIxKbyPVkPxEN6P9NA9WqsuQIFxJ4hCMuQHIpKqKm5MDki38U0G4OKlwjEEN2UGQSY4ZT2TWeV%2BN0Z%2FKyf2OZ87FwQKq%2FovUMVnZLweb9mhzeb7nTCNJgCDT3aGIE67RnOQAOuKFQ48L%2B%2FNcK%2BNtz%2Flm7%2BHXpONNlgK2%2F0ulovyLBa%2FGlRMBKwkUrPR38yjD9EdOfNzc31CpiCIaH6q4Mzlqnxfq6XBwPfdhkKI2OlxmaVx3CZ4ybTSBYln1uKZOsTwaQWaYIAyFy9G0NLOEb4q%2F3B%2FLvpfpQHWDG4KDUezz%2BKjIwitmArnFsCpLfxppZfRMmLPV%2BLvE%2BU%2Bk7BFyMXc%2FymY8CrcLyIIu208NHKYsR0%2F22nqqfmneV1RTYVng%2BIlUgdIkvMHhIMdZoy%2FPFjCnuMv3DYCatMnlLg93t%2B2fbOFExP%2Fo0dzDoC7cx3SxyBJ%2BMl0%2B0t45LjpGTwzIHChQKrbuSRtgPmMXs%2FgSuWe06SWIrT5UOdYlr%2B3q%2BE%2FzOYxxcd9tyWMLVOQE5YwnOrcl5TrnrLcPoAoj9L88UQwVXF3qWPSuZQtRLnFSZlKo0LT55j%2Fhr6lfrUyqpVFy9yseh4s2rIkxEuN2kYdTYJUik7u1j1ESyX%2FnJyCwpzCt3sTSBjqZAZvHbt1emQDF054tPL%2F6z%2B0gwNXwe%2BYK8YoT2BbL0J%2FznQgBxYy%2Bf%2F6AfY%2Bgql6QoxtiXr0pLcxg0oAOnPBMqtsKILP1HJiaMofgZb0ndEIbfYJacko5EeBwKmVgnOA3vEPZuBVt7EmuTmu4kVNnwR%2F8xxsfVP7DgGtlhBAZiqMVRaje%2Fkf2njBCdm5cJBKZEmpN9E3Xs4nMeg%3D%3D&Expires=1783708928)

10:         self.rows = (height + cell_size - 1) // cell_size

16:         r0 = max(0, int(y0) // self.cell_size)
17:         c1 = min(self.cols - 1, int(x1) // self.cell_size)
18:         r1 = min(self.rows - 1, int(y1) // self.cell_size)

20:         for r in range(r0, r1 + 1):
21:             for c in range(c0, c1 + 1):
22:                 if z_near <= self.buffer[r * self.cols + c]:
23:                     return True
24:         return False

29:         # No, a coarse z-buffer stores the FARTHEST depth of any pixel in the cell.
