## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/column_field.rs
````rust
 1: //! A sampled Level 0 area plus the one-column halo needed for clean caps.
 2: 
 3: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 4: 
 5: /// Resolution-dependent samples of a resolution-independent world plan.
 6: ///
 7: /// The halo is part of this type's invariant.  Callers cannot accidentally
 8: /// voxelize a chunk without knowing its neighbours' ceiling heights, which is
 9: /// what keeps separately generated requests sealed at their shared edge.
10: pub(crate) struct ColumnField {
11:     width: usize,
12:     depth: usize,
13:     columns: Vec<ColumnPlan>,
14: }
15: 
16: impl ColumnField {
17:     pub(crate) fn sample(
18:         width: usize,
19:         depth: usize,
20:         mut plan_at: impl FnMut(i64, i64) -> ColumnPlan,
21:     ) -> Self {
22:         let mut columns = Vec::with_capacity((width + 2) * (depth + 2));
23:         for z in -1..=depth as i64 {
24:             for x in -1..=width as i64 {
25:                 columns.push(plan_at(x, z));
26:             }
27:         }
28:         Self {
29:             width,
30:             depth,
31:             columns,
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     pub(crate) fn width(&self) -> usize {
36:         self.width
37:     }
38: 
39:     pub(crate) fn depth(&self) -> usize {
40:         self.depth
41:     }
42: 
43:     /// Local coordinates include the halo, so `x` and `z` may be `-1` or
44:     /// exactly the corresponding output dimension.
45:     pub(crate) fn get(&self, x: i64, z: i64) -> &ColumnPlan {
46:         debug_assert!((-1..=self.width as i64).contains(&x));
47:         debug_assert!((-1..=self.depth as i64).contains(&z));
48:         &self.columns[((z + 1) as usize) * (self.width + 2) + (x + 1) as usize]
49:     }
50: }
51: 
52: #[cfg(test)]
53: mod tests {
54:     use super::*;
55: 
56:     #[test]
57:     fn sampler_owns_a_one_column_halo() {
58:         let field = ColumnField::sample(2, 3, |x, z| ColumnPlan::open((x + z + 10) as f32));
59:         assert_eq!(field.get(-1, -1).ceiling_units, 8.0);
60:         assert_eq!(field.get(2, 3).ceiling_units, 15.0);
61:     }
62: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/red_rooms/geometry.rs
````rust
  1: //! Red Room presentation layered over an authored Level 0 assembly.
  2: //!
  3: //! This sampler knows nothing about chunks or voxel indices.  It receives one
  4: //! world column and returns one architectural decision, leaving recursive
  5: //! world addressing and voxelization to their own stages.
  6: 
  7: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyInstance, Axis2, RealitySnapshot, RedRoomPhase};
  8: use crate::domain::entities::environment::EnvironmentProfile;
  9: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
 10: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 11: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 12: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
 13: 
 14: /// Applies avoidable warning cues and the committed encounter topology.
 15: pub(crate) fn sample_red_room(
 16:     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
 17:     mut column: ColumnPlan,
 18:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 19:     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 20:     world_x: f32,
 21:     world_z: f32,
 22: ) -> ColumnPlan {
 23:     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
 24:     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
 25:     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
 26:     let loop_width = 2.0f32.min(half_x * 0.35).min(half_z * 0.35).max(1.2);
 27:     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
 28: 
 29:     // Warning cues intensify toward the shell but never replace masonry with
 30:     // a special red wall.  The anomaly is read through carpet, compression,
 31:     // and light; collision remains ordinary Level 0 architecture.
 32:     let contamination = (1.0 - boundary / (loop_width * 2.0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 33:     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::red_room(contamination);
 34:     if boundary > PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05 {
 35:         if contamination > 0.15 {
 36:             column.floor_material = profile.floor_voxel();
 37:         }
 38:         if contamination > 0.33 {
 39:             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.2).max(2.6);
 40:         }
 41:         if contamination > 0.66 {
 42:             column.ceiling_units = (column.ceiling_units - 0.4).max(2.4);
 43:         }
 44:     }
 45:     column.red_light = true;
 46: 
 47:     let Some(state) = instance.state(reality) else {
 48:         return column;
 49:     };
 50:     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::Outside {
 51:         return column;
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     // Commitment closes the remembered entrance and reduces the authored
 55:     // room to one walkable perimeter loop around an opaque core.
 56:     let in_core = local_x.abs() < half_x - loop_width && local_z.abs() < half_z - loop_width;
 57:     column.solid = boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T || in_core;
 58:     column.lintel_from_units = None;
 59:     column.floor_material = VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET;
 60:     column.ceiling_units = column.ceiling_units.min(2.8);
 61:     if column.solid {
 62:         column.light = false;
 63:     }
 64: 
 65:     if state.phase == RedRoomPhase::EscapeOpen {
 66:         open_single_escape(
 67:             instance,
 68:             state.epoch,
 69:             config.anomalies.red_escape_bias,
 70:             local_x,
 71:             local_z,
 72:             &mut column,
 73:         );
 74:     }
 75:     column
 76: }
 77: 
 78: /// Opens one deterministic side of the loop.  The bias is an authored width
 79: /// control: zero keeps the encounter sealed; positive values widen a single
 80: /// breach without turning both symmetric walls into exits.
 81: fn open_single_escape(
 82:     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
 83:     epoch: u32,
 84:     bias: f32,
 85:     local_x: f32,
 86:     local_z: f32,
 87:     column: &mut ColumnPlan,
 88: ) {
 89:     let width = bias.clamp(0.0, 1.0) * 2.4;
 90:     if width <= 0.0 {
 91:         return;
 92:     }
 93:     let Some(threshold) = instance.gates.first() else {
 94:         return;
 95:     };
 96:     let side_sign = if stable_bit(instance.id, epoch) {
 97:         1.0
 98:     } else {
 99:         -1.0
100:     };
101:     let (side_coordinate, side_extent, along) = match threshold.axis {
102:         Axis2::Z => (local_x, instance.footprint.half_x, local_z),
103:         Axis2::X => (local_z, instance.footprint.half_z, local_x),
104:     };
105:     let on_selected_wall = (side_coordinate - side_sign * side_extent).abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T + 0.1;
106:     if on_selected_wall && along.abs() < width {
107:         column.solid = false;
108:     }
109: }
110: 
111: fn stable_bit(instance_id: u64, epoch: u32) -> bool {
112:     let mut value = instance_id ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(29) ^ 0xE5CA_9E5C_A9E5_CA9E;
113:     value ^= value >> 30;
114:     value = value.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
115:     value ^= value >> 27;
116:     value & 1 == 1
117: }
````

````rust
  1: //! The Backrooms corruption pass: the plan was sane; the building is not.
  2: //!
  3: //! Duplicated suites, abandoned expansions, renovation overlays, and the
  4: //! realization of macro-graph red-room events on eligible assemblies.
  5: 
  6: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
  7: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
  8: use crate::entities::models::Position;
  9: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 10: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 11: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
 12: 
 13: use super::suites::{aabb_overlap, place_suite};
 14: use super::{EDGE_MARGIN, PLAN_WALL_T, REGION_SIZE, pick_index, region_index, snap, spawn_point};
 15: 
 16: /// Backrooms corruption: the plan was sane; the building is not. Pure
 17: /// sequencing over four independent rules, each its own named function so
 18: /// any one of them is testable without the other three — previously all
 19: /// four were inlined together sharing one hash-key closure, which made it
 20: /// impossible to exercise, say, just the abandonment rule in isolation.
 21: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 22: pub(super) fn corrupt(
 23:     seed: u32,
 24:     rx: i64,
 25:     rz: i64,
 26:     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
 27:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 28:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 29:     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
 30:     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
 31:     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 32: ) {
 33:     if assemblies.is_empty() {
 34:         return;
 35:     }
 36:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0xC0DE + k, rx, rz]);
 37: 
 38:     if h(1) < 0.6 {
 39:         let src = pick_index(h(2), assemblies.len());
 40:         let shift = snap(12.0 + 12.0 * h(3));
 41:         if let Some(dup) = duplicate_suite_candidate(assemblies, taken, spines, rx, rz, src, shift)
 42:         {
 43:             taken.push(dup.footprint.bounds());
 44:             assemblies.push(dup);
 45:         }
 46:     }
 47: 
 48:     if h(6) < 0.6 {
 49:         let k = pick_index(h(7), assemblies.len());
 50:         abandon_assembly(&mut assemblies[k]);
 51:     }
 52: 
 53:     apply_renovation_history(dominant.renovation_history, assemblies, h(8), h(9));
 54: 
 55:     // Applied last so it respects whatever the earlier passes decided (an
 56:     // abandoned shell stays dark).
 57:     let sp = spawn_point(seed);
 58:     let forced_in_spawn_region = config.anomalies.forced_kind == Some(AnomalyKind::RedRoom)
 59:         && rx == region_index(sp.x)
 60:         && rz == region_index(sp.z);
 61:     let red_room_realized = forced_in_spawn_region
 62:         && force_red_room_in_spawn_region(dominant, rx, rz, assemblies, taken, spines);
 63:     if !red_room_realized {
 64:         let red_room_scale = config.anomalies.frequency * config.anomalies.red_rooms;
 65:         realize_red_room_event(seed, noise, rx, rz, red_room_scale, assemblies);
 66:     }
 67: }
 68: 
 69: /// Rule 1: a suite repeats itself further down the corridor, slightly wrong.
 70: /// Pure — reads the existing plan, returns the candidate duplicate (already
 71: /// translated, with its misalignment recorded) or `None` if it would fall
 72: /// outside the region, overlap something already placed, or seal itself
 73: /// away from every corridor. The caller decides whether to keep it.
 74: fn duplicate_suite_candidate(
 75:     assemblies: &[AssemblyInstance],
 76:     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 77:     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
 78:     rx: i64,
 79:     rz: i64,
 80:     src: usize,
 81:     shift: f32,
 82: ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
 83:     // Keep the copied threshold flush with its source corridor. The
 84:     // repetition is wrong in its longitudinal position, not sealed away
 85:     // behind an accidental strip of wall.
 86:     let skew = 0.0;
 87:     let mut dup = assemblies[src].clone();
 88:     let translate = |poly: &mut Polygon2| {
 89:         for v in &mut poly.vertices {
 90:             v.0 += shift;
 91:             v.1 += skew;
 92:         }
 93:     };
 94:     translate(&mut dup.footprint);
 95:     for s in &mut dup.spaces {
 96:         translate(&mut s.footprint);
 97:     }
 98:     for c in &mut dup.ceiling_zones {
 99:         translate(&mut c.area);
100:     }
101:     for f in &mut dup.fixtures {
102:         f.at.x += shift;
103:         f.at.z += skew;
104:     }
105:     for e in &mut dup.entrances {
106:         e.center.x += shift;
107:         e.center.z += skew;
108:     }
109:     dup.id = assemblies.len() as u32 + 1000;
110:     dup.corruption.misalignment = (shift, skew);
111: 
112:     let b = dup.footprint.bounds();
113:     let inside = b.0 > rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
114:         && b.2 < (rx + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN
115:         && b.1 > rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE + EDGE_MARGIN
116:         && b.3 < (rz + 1) as f32 * REGION_SIZE - EDGE_MARGIN;
117:     // The skewed entrance must still reach a corridor, or the copy would be
118:     // a sealed pocket.
119:     let reachable = dup.entrances.iter().any(|e| {
120:         spines
121:             .iter()
122:             .any(|s| s.distance(e.center.x, e.center.z) <= s.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05)
123:     });
124:     (inside && reachable && !taken.iter().any(|t| aabb_overlap(*t, b, 0.4))).then_some(dup)
125: }
126: 
127: /// Rule 2: one assembly was built and then never occupied — an empty shell,
128: /// nothing lit.
129: fn abandon_assembly(assembly: &mut AssemblyInstance) {
130:     assembly.program = SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion;
131:     assembly.corruption.abandoned = true;
132:     assembly.spaces.clear();
133:     for f in &mut assembly.fixtures {
134:         f.lit = false;
135:     }
136: }
137: 
138: /// Rule 3: renovation history overlays the original structural grid. A
139: /// partial refit contradicts one assembly; a fuller history of layered
140: /// refits leaves a second, distinct assembly contradicted too — otherwise
141: /// the two `RenovationStyle` variants would be indistinguishable once
142: /// generated, despite the type's own doc comment promising more.
143: fn apply_renovation_history(
144:     history: RenovationStyle,
145:     assemblies: &mut [AssemblyInstance],
146:     pick1: f32,
147:     pick2: f32,
148: ) {
149:     match history {
150:         RenovationStyle::Untouched => {}
151:         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit => {
152:             let k = pick_index(pick1, assemblies.len());
153:             overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k]);
154:         }
155:         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits => {
156:             let k1 = pick_index(pick1, assemblies.len());
157:             overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k1]);
158:             if assemblies.len() > 1 {
159:                 // Offset from k1 rather than re-rolling, so the second pick
160:                 // is guaranteed distinct instead of merely likely to be.
161:                 let k2 = (k1 + 1 + pick_index(pick2, assemblies.len() - 1)) % assemblies.len();
162:                 overlay_renovation(&mut assemblies[k2]);
163:             }
164:         }
165:     }
166: }
167: 
168: /// A renovation overlays the original structural grid on one assembly.
169: fn overlay_renovation(assembly: &mut AssemblyInstance) {
170:     assembly.corruption.renovation_overlay = true;
171: }
172: 
173: /// Rule 4a: the debug/authored path. `?force_anomaly=redroom` targets the
174: /// region the player actually spawns in, so this must succeed there even
175: /// when nothing qualifies yet — mark an existing occupied assembly if one
176: /// exists, otherwise place a brand new one against the main corridor.
177: /// Returns whether a red room was realized.
178: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
179: fn force_red_room_in_spawn_region(
180:     dominant: &ArchitectGenome,
181:     rx: i64,
182:     rz: i64,
183:     assemblies: &mut Vec<AssemblyInstance>,
184:     taken: &mut Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32)>,
185:     spines: &[CirculationSpine],
186: ) -> bool {
187:     if let Some(a) = assemblies
188:         .iter_mut()
189:         .find(|a| !a.entrances.is_empty() && !a.corruption.abandoned)
190:     {
191:         a.corruption.red_room = true;
192:         return true;
193:     }
194:     let Some(spine) = spines
195:         .iter()
196:         .find(|s| s.spine_kind == SpaceProgram::MainCorridor)
197:     else {
198:         return false;
199:     };
200:     let Some(seg) = spine.path.windows(2).find(|seg| seg[0].z == seg[1].z) else {
201:         return false;
202:     };
203:     let lx0 = seg[0].x.min(seg[1].x);
204:     let lz = seg[0].z;
205:     let origin = Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE);
206:     let Some(mut a) = place_suite(
207:         9999,
208:         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice,
209:         dominant,
210:         0.5,
211:         0.5,
212:         lx0 + 12.0,
213:         lz,
214:         spine.width * 0.5 + PLAN_WALL_T,
215:         1.0,
216:         origin,
217:         REGION_SIZE,
218:         taken,
219:         spines,
220:     ) else {
221:         return false;
222:     };
223:     a.corruption.red_room = true;
224:     taken.push(a.footprint.bounds());
225:     assemblies.push(a);
226:     true
227: }
228: 
229: /// Rule 4b: the ordinary path. Where a red room happens is a *graph event*,
230: /// not a per-region coin flip — the macro topology plans separated events on
231: /// its lattice (`world_topology::red_room_event_for_region`), and this rule
232: /// merely realizes an event that targets this region on one eligible
233: /// assembly, rotating from a stable start so the choice replays identically
234: /// for every query of this region. If no assembly qualifies the event stays
235: /// unrealized — a planned encounter never overwrites navigable circulation.
236: fn realize_red_room_event(
237:     seed: u32,
238:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
239:     rx: i64,
240:     rz: i64,
241:     red_room_scale: f32,
242:     assemblies: &mut [AssemblyInstance],
243: ) {
244:     let Some(event) = crate::use_cases::world_topology::red_room_event_for_region(
245:         seed,
246:         noise,
247:         rx,
248:         rz,
249:         red_room_scale.clamp(0.0, 4.0),
250:     ) else {
251:         return;
252:     };
253:     let count = assemblies.len();
254:     let start = (event.id % count as u64) as usize;
255:     for offset in 0..count {
256:         let a = &mut assemblies[(start + offset) % count];
257:         if !a.corruption.abandoned && !a.entrances.is_empty() {
258:             a.corruption.red_room = true;
259:             break;
260:         }
261:     }
262: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Architect genomes: the designers a region inherits.
  2: //!
  3: //! `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator, 2 = intruder. The circulation style
  4: //! comes from low-frequency noise so neighboring regions tend to share a
  5: //! culture; every other property is hash-derived, but *not independently*:
  6: //! a real designer's decisions form a chain, not a set of parallel dice
  7: //! rolls. `structural_system` and `renovation_history` are decided first;
  8: //! everything downstream of them (room proportions, ceiling language,
  9: //! threshold language, furnishing density, tolerance for symmetry) biases
 10: //! toward what that earlier choice implies, with its own hash key still
 11: //! supplying the roll *within* the biased range. A `CoreAndShell` designer
 12: //! who chose that system to achieve big clear-span rooms should get big
 13: //! rooms and a ceiling that doesn't pretend to hide beams it doesn't have;
 14: //! a `DeepSpansWithBeams` designer's ceiling should show the beams that
 15: //! justify the system's name.
 16: 
 17: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::*;
 18: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 19: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 20: use crate::use_cases::world_topology::hash01;
 21: 
 22: use super::{REGION_SIZE, pick_index};
 23: 
 24: /// Derive one designer for a region. `salt` 0 = dominant, 1 = renovator,
 25: /// 2 = intruder. The circulation style comes from low-frequency noise so
 26: /// neighboring regions tend to share a culture; everything else hashes.
 27: pub fn derive_genome(
 28:     seed: u32,
 29:     rx: i64,
 30:     rz: i64,
 31:     salt: i64,
 32:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 33: ) -> ArchitectGenome {
 34:     let h = |k: i64| hash01(seed, &[0x6E0 + salt, rx, rz, k]);
 35:     // ~130 u wavelength: cultures span a few regions.
 36:     let culture = noise.evaluate_2d(
 37:         seed ^ 0xA11C_0DE ^ (salt as u32),
 38:         Position::new(
 39:             (rx as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
 40:             (rz as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE * 0.15,
 41:         ),
 42:     );
 43:     let circulation = match ((culture * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999) * 4.0) as u32 {
 44:         0 => CirculationStyle::StraightSpine,
 45:         1 => CirculationStyle::MeanderingSpine,
 46:         2 => CirculationStyle::PairedBranches,
 47:         _ => CirculationStyle::TreeWithCulDeSacs,
 48:     };
 49:     // ---- site strategy: decided first, everything else answers to it ----
 50:     let structural_system = *[
 51:         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid,
 52:         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams,
 53:         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid,
 54:         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
 55:     ]
 56:     .get(pick_index(h(1), 4))
 57:     .unwrap();
 58:     let renovation_history = *[
 59:         RenovationStyle::Untouched,
 60:         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit,
 61:         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits,
 62:     ]
 63:     .get(pick_index(h(5), 3))
 64:     .unwrap();
 65: 
 66:     // ---- consequences of the structural system --------------------------
 67:     // CoreAndShell and DeepSpansWithBeams are chosen specifically to permit
 68:     // large clear-span rooms (see `suites::on_column`, which gives
 69:     // CoreAndShell zero interior columns); RegularGrid/OffsetGrid bound
 70:     // their rooms to a small structural module instead. Room size is a
 71:     // consequence of that choice, not a second independent roll.
 72:     let spans_wide = matches!(
 73:         structural_system,
 74:         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell | StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams
 75:     );
 76:     let (min_lo, min_span, max_lo, max_span) = if spans_wide {
 77:         (16.0, 6.0, 24.0, 10.0)
 78:     } else {
 79:         (12.0, 4.0, 18.0, 6.0)
 80:     };
 81: 
 82:     // A coffered or exposed-soffit ceiling is a description of what a deep
 83:     // beam grid looks like from underneath, not an unrelated stylistic
 84:     // choice — so it should follow from having beams to show. CoreAndShell
 85:     // has no beam grid to express at all; flat tiles are the honest default
 86:     // for it. RegularGrid/OffsetGrid are unbiased: either reads as fine for
 87:     // an ordinary column grid.
 88:     let ceiling_language = match structural_system {
 89:         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => match h(3) {
 90:             v if v < 0.55 => CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
 91:             v if v < 0.85 => CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
 92:             _ => CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
 93:         },
 94:         StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => match h(3) {
 95:             v if v < 0.70 => CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
 96:             v if v < 0.90 => CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
 97:             _ => CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
 98:         },
 99:         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid | StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid => *[
100:             CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles,
101:             CeilingLanguage::Coffered,
102:             CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
103:         ]
104:         .get(pick_index(h(3), 3))
105:         .unwrap(),
106:     };
107: 
108:     // A grid that never breaks its own module (Regular, CoreAndShell) reads
109:     // as more deliberately symmetric than one that already contradicts
110:     // itself every other row (OffsetGrid).
111:     let symmetry_bias = match structural_system {
112:         StructuralSystem::RegularGrid | StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => 0.25,
113:         StructuralSystem::OffsetGrid => -0.20,
114:         StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => 0.0,
115:     };
116: 
117:     // ---- consequences of the renovation history --------------------------
118:     // A framed office door is now an anomaly. The chosen language is only a
119:     // bias; each assembly still picks its own threshold so a whole region
120:     // never turns into a row of identical openings. A designer who left
121:     // layered refits behind also left wider, less consistent thresholds and
122:     // denser leftover furnishing than a plan nobody ever touched.
123:     let refit_bias = match renovation_history {
124:         RenovationStyle::Untouched => 0.0,
125:         RenovationStyle::PartialRefit => 0.12,
126:         RenovationStyle::LayeredRefits => 0.25,
127:     };
128:     let threshold_language = match (h(2) + refit_bias).min(0.999) {
129:         v if v < 0.10 => ThresholdLanguage::DoorWithLintel,
130:         v if v < 0.55 => ThresholdLanguage::OpenPortal,
131:         _ => ThresholdLanguage::WidePortal,
132:     };
133: 
134:     let lighting_language = *[
135:         LightingLanguage::GridPanels,
136:         LightingLanguage::GridPanels,
137:         LightingLanguage::StripsAlongCirculation,
138:         LightingLanguage::SparsePendants,
139:     ]
140:     .get(pick_index(h(4), 4))
141:     .unwrap();
142: 
143:     ArchitectGenome {
144:         circulation,
145:         structural_system,
146:         room_proportions: ProportionRules {
147:             // Level 0 reads as broken retail-backroom masses, not a cubicle
148:             // tiling. A suite frontage normally survives 12--24 u before a
149:             // meaningful interruption, wider still where the structure
150:             // permits it.
151:             min_side: min_lo + min_span * h(6),
152:             max_side: max_lo + max_span * h(7),
153:             elongation: h(8),
154:         },
155:         threshold_language,
156:         ceiling_language,
157:         lighting_language,
158:         furnishing_density: (0.3 + 0.7 * h(9) + refit_bias).min(1.0),
159:         renovation_history,
160:         tolerance_for_symmetry: (h(10) + symmetry_bias).clamp(0.0, 1.0),
161:     }
162: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/ports.rs
````rust
 1: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 2: 
 3: /// The Ports layer implements the Dependency Inversion Principle (SOLID).
 4: /// Instead of the Use Cases depending on a concrete external noise library or framework,
 5: /// the Use Cases define the interface (Port) they need, and the external layers
 6: /// (Adapters/Drivers) must implement this interface.
 7: 
 8: /// NoiseProvider is a pure interface for extracting deterministic continuous noise.
 9: /// We use this to evaluate the Macro Field (Drift, Density, Motif Selection).
10: pub trait NoiseProvider {
11:     /// Returns a noise value, ideally in the range [-1.0, 1.0].
12:     /// The function must be deterministic given the same seed and position.
13:     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32;
14: }
15: 
16: /// TelemetryPort abstracts wall-clock access and log emission so Use Cases
17: /// never touch `std::time` or stdout directly. Both are frameworks concerns,
18: /// and `SystemTime::now()` panics on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
19: pub trait TelemetryPort {
20:     /// Monotonic-ish timestamp in microseconds from an arbitrary epoch.
21:     /// Only ever used to compute durations, never absolute dates.
22:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64;
23:     /// Emits one log line to whatever sink the outer layer provides.
24:     fn log(&self, message: &str);
25: }
26: 
27: /// Silent TelemetryPort used by default and in tests.
28: pub struct NullTelemetry;
29: 
30: impl TelemetryPort for NullTelemetry {
31:     fn now_micros(&self) -> u64 {
32:         0
33:     }
34:     fn log(&self, _message: &str) {}
35: }
36: 
37: /// Shared instance so constructors can hand out `&'static dyn TelemetryPort`
38: /// without forcing callers to own a telemetry object.
39: pub static NULL_TELEMETRY: NullTelemetry = NullTelemetry;
````

````rust
  1: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_STAINED_CARPET, VOXEL_WALL};
  2: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
  3: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
  4: /// Collision Diagnostic Tests — TDD Phase 1
  5: ///
  6: /// WHY THESE TESTS EXIST:
  7: /// The player reported spawning inside a wall.  Before changing any logic
  8: /// we must prove (a) what coordinates the spawn point produces and (b) whether
  9: /// the floor voxel's collision box overlaps the player's AABB at spawn.
 10: ///
 11: /// Test-first order:
 12: ///   1. Prove the exact world-space coordinates the chunk generator places floor/wall
 13: ///      voxels at for the (0,0) hub chunk in low-spec mode.
 14: ///   2. Prove the spawn point (5.0, 1.7, 5.0) does NOT overlap any wall voxel.
 15: ///   3. Prove the floor voxel box does NOT block the player at spawn.
 16: ///   4. Prove terminal velocity is sane (<= 5 world-units/second).
 17: ///
 18: /// If test 2 or 3 fails, it proves the bug.  Then we add a fix and verify
 19: /// the test passes.
 20: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::{GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase, GeneratorConfig};
 21: 
 22: /// The JavaScript side extracts wall collision boxes from the SVO.
 23: /// This Rust analogue extracts the same information directly from the VoxelGrid
 24: /// so we can verify coordinates without the JS/SVO layer.
 25: fn grid_wall_boxes_at_spawn_x(chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 26:     // Returns (minX, maxX, minY, maxY, minZ, maxZ) for every solid wall voxel
 27:     // at approximately x=5 world-units inside the chunk.
 28:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 29:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 30:     let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 31:     let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 32: 
 33:     let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 34:     let mut boxes = vec![];
 35: 
 36:     for y in 0..grid.height() {
 37:         for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 38:             for x in 0..grid.width() {
 39:                 let vt = grid.get(x, y, z);
 40:                 if vt == VOXEL_WALL {
 41:                     let wx = chunk_x + x as f32 * scale;
 42:                     let wy = y as f32 * scale;
 43:                     let wz = chunk_z + z as f32 * scale;
 44:                     // The JS collision system gives walls a 1-voxel-size box
 45:                     boxes.push((wx, wx + scale, wy, wy + scale, wz, wz + scale));
 46:                 }
 47:             }
 48:         }
 49:     }
 50:     boxes
 51: }
 52: 
 53: fn floor_boxes(chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32)> {
 54:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 55:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 56:     let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
 57:     let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 58: 
 59:     let scale = config.voxel_scale;
 60:     let mut boxes = vec![];
 61: 
 62:     for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 63:         for x in 0..grid.width() {
 64:             let vt = grid.get(x, 0, z);
 65:             // Ordinary fabric floor now voxelizes as either the fresh or
 66:             // the institution-age-stained carpet material; both are the
 67:             // same walkable floor geometry this diagnostic cares about.
 68:             if vt == VOXEL_FLOOR || vt == VOXEL_STAINED_CARPET {
 69:                 let wx = chunk_x + x as f32 * scale;
 70:                 let wz = chunk_z + z as f32 * scale;
 71:                 // Floor voxel: y=0 to y=scale
 72:                 boxes.push((wx, wx + scale, 0.0_f32, scale, wz, wz + scale));
 73:             }
 74:         }
 75:     }
 76:     boxes
 77: }
 78: 
 79: /// Player AABB: eye-level at pos.y, feet at pos.y - 1.65, head at pos.y + 0.1
 80: fn player_overlaps(
 81:     pos: (f32, f32, f32),
 82:     radius: f32,
 83:     vbox: (f32, f32, f32, f32, f32, f32),
 84: ) -> bool {
 85:     let (px, py, pz) = pos;
 86:     let p_min_x = px - radius;
 87:     let p_max_x = px + radius;
 88:     let p_min_y = py - 1.65;
 89:     let p_max_y = py + 0.1;
 90:     let p_min_z = pz - radius;
 91:     let p_max_z = pz + radius;
 92:     let (v_min_x, v_max_x, v_min_y, v_max_y, v_min_z, v_max_z) = vbox;
 93: 
 94:     p_max_x > v_min_x
 95:         && p_min_x < v_max_x
 96:         && p_max_y > v_min_y
 97:         && p_min_y < v_max_y
 98:         && p_max_z > v_min_z
 99:         && p_min_z < v_max_z
100: }
101: 
102: // ============================================================
103: // TEST 1: Verify hub chunk (0,0) has walls only on boundary
104: // ============================================================
105: #[test]
106: fn test_hub_chunk_interior_is_wall_free() {

108:     // No wall voxels should exist at x≈5.0, z≈5.0 (centre of chunk).
109:     let walls = grid_wall_boxes_at_spawn_x(0.0, 0.0);

112:     let radius = 0.35_f32;

115:         .iter()
116:         .filter(|&&b| player_overlaps(spawn, radius, b))
117:         .collect();
118: 
119:     assert!(

134: // (extractSvoCollisions only passes WALL/RED_WALL to isColliding).
135: // This test is kept as living documentation of the bug's root cause.
136: // ============================================================
137: #[test]
138: #[should_panic(expected = "Floor voxels at spawn OVERLAP")]
139: fn test_floor_geometry_overlaps_player_proving_the_bug() {
140:     // Floor voxels are at y=0 to y=voxel_scale (0.2 for low-spec).

142:     // If pMinY(0.05) < vMaxY(0.2) AND pMaxY(1.8) > vMinY(0.0) → geometric overlap.
143:     // This test PROVES the overlap exists in the geometry.

145:     let floors = floor_boxes(0.0, 0.0);

157:          Count: {}\n\
158:          This causes the player to spawn 'stuck' and unable to move.\n\
159:          Fix: exclude FLOOR and CEILING voxels from collision extraction.\n\
160:          First overlapping floor box: {:?}",
161:         floor_at_spawn.len(),

163:     );

168: // ============================================================
169: #[test]
170: fn test_terminal_velocity_is_sane() {
171:     // JS formula: velocity.z -= direction.z * speed * delta
172:     //             velocity.z -= velocity.z * friction * delta   (drag)
173:     // Terminal velocity = speed / friction
174:     let speed: f32 = 4.0; // target walk speed (world units/sec)
175:     let friction: f32 = 10.0; // damping coefficient

177: 
178:     // The old code used speed=15.0 → terminal = 1.5 units/frame @60fps = 90 u/s
179:     assert!(

182:          This causes the 'too fast' movement bug.\n\

185:         friction * 5.0,

188: }
````

  1: //! Path-traced reference of randomly generated scenes, written as PNG.
  2: //!
  3: //! Ground truth for renderer testing: generates a random world with the
  4: //! production `LocalChunkSource`, then Monte-Carlo path traces the spawn
  5: //! neighborhood through the same serialized SVO and canonical `trace_svo`
  6: //! traversal the CPU renderer uses. Ceiling fixtures are the only emitters
  7: //! (their authored emission strengths), every other material is a diffuse
  8: //! reflector of its palette albedo — so global illumination, soft shadows,
  9: //! and color bleed in the output are physically plausible for the exact
 10: //! same scene data the real-time paths draw.
 11: //!
 12: //! ```sh
 13: //! cargo run -p wasm_frontend --example path_trace --release
 14: //! SEED=7 SPP=512 SIZE=960x540 cargo run -p wasm_frontend --example path_trace --release
 15: //! ```

 17: //! Env knobs: `SEED` (default random — a new scene every run), `RADIUS`
 18: //! (chunk rings around spawn: 1 → 3x3 chunks, 2 → 5x5, …; default 1),
 19: //! `SIZE` (`WxH`, default 640x360), `SPP` (samples per pixel, default 128),
 20: //! `BOUNCES` (default 6), `EXPOSURE` (default 1.4). Output lands in
 21: //! `target/path-traces/seed-<seed>.png`.

 47:         .and_then(|value| value.parse().ok())
 48:         .unwrap_or_else(random_seed);
 49:     let (width, height) = parse_size();
 50:     let radius: i32 = env_number("RADIUS", 1).clamp(0, 8) as i32;
 51:     let spp: u32 = env_number("SPP", 128);
 52:     let bounces: u32 = env_number("BOUNCES", 6);
 53:     let exposure: f32 = std::env::var("EXPOSURE")
 54:         .ok()
 55:         .and_then(|value| value.parse().ok())
 56:         .unwrap_or(1.4);
 57: 
 58:     let scene = load_scene(seed, radius);
 59:     eprintln!(
 60:         "scene: seed {seed}, {} chunks (radius {radius}), {} lights, {} atlas words | {width}x{height}, {spp} spp, {bounces} bounces",
 61:         scene.chunks.len(),
 62:         scene.lights.len(),
 63:         scene.atlas.len(),
 64:     );
 65: 
 66:     let start = Instant::now();
 67:     let camera = Camera::at_spawn(seed, width, height);
 68:     let mut pixels = vec![0u8; (width * height * 3) as usize];
 69:     let rows_done = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
 70:     let report_every = (height as usize / 50).max(1);
 71:     pixels
 72:         .par_chunks_mut((width * 3) as usize)
 73:         .enumerate()
 74:         .for_each(|(row, out)| {
 75:             for column in 0..width as usize {
 76:                 let mut accumulated = [0.0f32; 3];
 77:                 for sample in 0..spp {
 78:                     let mut rng =
 79:                         Pcg32::new(((row as u64) << 40) ^ ((column as u64) << 20) ^ sample as u64, seed as u64);
 80:                     let ray = camera.primary_ray(column as f32, row as f32, &mut rng);
 81:                     let radiance = trace_path(&scene, ray, bounces, &mut rng);
 82:                     for axis in 0..3 {
 83:                         accumulated[axis] += radiance[axis];
 84:                     }
 85:                 }
 86:                 for axis in 0..3 {
 87:                     let mean = accumulated[axis] / spp as f32;
 88:                     // Filmic-ish exposure curve, then gamma for the PNG.
 89:                     let mapped = 1.0 - (-mean * exposure).exp();
 90:                     out[column * 3 + axis] = (mapped.clamp(0.0, 1.0).powf(1.0 / 2.2) * 255.0) as u8;
 91:                 }
 92:             }
 93:             // Row-level progress on one rewritten terminal line: percent,
 94:             // rows, elapsed, and a remaining-time estimate.
 95:             let done = rows_done.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) + 1;
 96:             if done % report_every == 0 || done == height as usize {
 97:                 let elapsed = start.elapsed().as_secs_f32();
 98:                 let fraction = done as f32 / height as f32;
 99:                 let remaining = elapsed / fraction - elapsed;
100:                 eprint!(
101:                     "\rtracing {:>3.0}%  ({done}/{} rows, {elapsed:.0}s elapsed, ~{remaining:.0}s left)   ",
102:                     fraction * 100.0,
103:                     height,
104:                 );
105:             }
106:         });
107:     eprintln!("\ntraced in {:.1}s", start.elapsed().as_secs_f32());
108: 
109:     let out_dir = PathBuf::from("target/path-traces");
110:     fs::create_dir_all(&out_dir).expect("create output directory");
111:     let path = out_dir.join(format!("seed-{seed}.png"));
112:     image::RgbImage::from_raw(width, height, pixels)
113:         .expect("pixel buffer matches dimensions")
114:         .save(&path)
115:         .expect("write png");
116:     println!("{}", path.display());
117: }
118: 
119: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
120: // Scene: the production spawn neighborhood, atlas-assembled like streaming.
121: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
122: 
123: struct Scene {
124:     atlas: Vec<u32>,
125:     chunks: Vec<ChunkDraw>,
126:     /// Renderer-neutral analytic fixtures exported by generation; the
127:     /// next-event estimator samples their panel rectangles directly.
128:     lights: Vec<LightSource>,
129:     voxel_size: f32,
130: }
131: 
132: fn load_scene(seed: u32, radius: i32) -> Scene {
133:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
134:     let spawn = spawn_point(seed);
135:     let origin_x = (spawn.x / config.chunk_size).floor() * config.chunk_size;
136:     let origin_z = (spawn.z / config.chunk_size).floor() * config.chunk_size;
137:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
138: 
139:     let mut payloads = Vec::new();
140:     for dz in -radius..=radius {
141:         for dx in -radius..=radius {
142:             let x = origin_x + dx as f32 * config.chunk_size;
143:             let z = origin_z + dz as f32 * config.chunk_size;
144:             payloads.push((x, z, source.load(x, z, 0, 0)));
145:         }
146:     }
147:     let max_rows = payloads
148:         .iter()
149:         .map(|(_, _, payload)| payload_rows(payload))
150:         .max()
151:         .expect("spawn neighborhood is never empty");
152:     let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
153:     pool.ensure_layout(payloads.len(), max_rows);
154: 
155:     let mut atlas = Vec::new();
156:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
157:     let mut voxel_size = config.voxel_scale;
158:     let mut unique_lights = HashMap::new();
159:     for (x, z, payload) in &payloads {
160:         let slot = pool.assign(chunk_key(*x, *z)).expect("atlas sized for all");
161:         let offset = slot * pool.slot_nodes();
162:         atlas.extend(pool.rebased_block(slot, payload));
163:         voxel_size = payload.voxel_size;
164:         chunks.push(ChunkDraw {
165:             origin: [*x, 0.0, *z],
166:             root_index: (offset + payload.root as usize) as i32,
167:             world_size: payload.world_size,
168:             voxel_size: payload.voxel_size,
169:             svo_depth: payload.svo_depth,
170:         });
171:         for light in &payload.lights {
172:             if light.enabled {
173:                 unique_lights.entry(light.id).or_insert(*light);
174:             }
175:         }
176:     }
177:     Scene {
178:         atlas,
179:         chunks,
180:         lights: unique_lights.into_values().collect(),
181:         voxel_size,
182:     }
183: }
184: 
185: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
186: // Path tracing over the SVO.
187: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
188: 
189: struct Ray {
190:     origin: [f32; 3],
191:     direction: [f32; 3],
192: }
193: 
194: /// Full path-tracing estimator: at every diffuse vertex, next-event
195: /// estimation samples one fixture rectangle through a shadow ray; the
196: /// bounce ray then carries indirect light. Emitter hits contribute only on
197: /// camera rays (NEE already accounts for them at later vertices), which
198: /// keeps the split unbiased without double counting.
199: fn trace_path(scene: &Scene, mut ray: Ray, bounces: u32, rng: &mut Pcg32) -> [f32; 3] {
200:     let mut radiance = [0.0f32; 3];
201:     let mut throughput = [1.0f32; 3];
202:     for bounce in 0..bounces {
203:         let Some(hit) = trace_svo(
204:             &scene.atlas,
205:             &scene.chunks,
206:             ray.origin,
207:             ray.direction,
208:             MAX_TRACE_DISTANCE,
209:             true,
210:         ) else {
211:             break; // The Backrooms have no sky.
212:         };
213:         let voxel = hit.voxel_type;
214:         let color = material_color_f32(voxel as u8);
215:         if is_emissive(voxel) {
216:             if bounce == 0 {
217:                 let strength = emission_strength(voxel).unwrap_or(1.0);
218:                 for axis in 0..3 {
219:                     radiance[axis] += throughput[axis] * color[axis] * strength;
220:                 }
221:             }
222:             break; // Fixtures emit; they do not bounce.
223:         }
224: 
225:         let hit_point = [
226:             ray.origin[0] + ray.direction[0] * hit.t,
227:             ray.origin[1] + ray.direction[1] * hit.t,
228:             ray.origin[2] + ray.direction[2] * hit.t,
229:         ];
230:         let normal = face_normal(hit_point, ray.direction, scene.voxel_size);
231:         let epsilon = scene.voxel_size * 0.05;
232:         let surface_point = [
233:             hit_point[0] + normal[0] * epsilon,
234:             hit_point[1] + normal[1] * epsilon,
235:             hit_point[2] + normal[2] * epsilon,
236:         ];
237: 
238:         // Next-event estimation toward one sampled fixture.
239:         let direct = sample_direct_light(scene, surface_point, normal, rng);
240:         for axis in 0..3 {
241:             radiance[axis] += throughput[axis] * color[axis] * direct[axis];
242:         }
243: 
244:         for axis in 0..3 {
245:             throughput[axis] *= color[axis];
246:         }
247:         // Russian roulette once the throughput has earned it.
248:         if bounce >= 3 {
249:             let survive = throughput[0]
250:                 .max(throughput[1])
251:                 .max(throughput[2])
252:                 .clamp(0.05, 0.95);
253:             if rng.uniform() > survive {
254:                 break;
255:             }
256:             for axis in 0..3 {
257:                 throughput[axis] /= survive;
258:             }
259:         }
260:         ray = Ray {
261:             origin: surface_point,
262:             direction: cosine_hemisphere(normal, rng),
263:         };
264:     }
265:     radiance
266: }
267: 
268: /// Estimates direct irradiance (already divided by π for the Lambertian
269: /// BRDF) at a surface point by sampling one fixture rectangle uniformly.
270: /// Fixture panels hang from ceilings and emit downward (-Y).
271: fn sample_direct_light(
272:     scene: &Scene,
273:     surface_point: [f32; 3],
274:     normal: [f32; 3],
275:     rng: &mut Pcg32,
276: ) -> [f32; 3] {
277:     if scene.lights.is_empty() {
278:         return [0.0; 3];
279:     }
280:     let picked = (rng.uniform() * scene.lights.len() as f32) as usize;
281:     let light = &scene.lights[picked.min(scene.lights.len() - 1)];
282:     let half = [light.half_size[0].max(0.01), light.half_size[1].max(0.01)];
283:     let sample_point = [
284:         light.position[0] + (rng.uniform() * 2.0 - 1.0) * half[0],
285:         light.position[1],
286:         light.position[2] + (rng.uniform() * 2.0 - 1.0) * half[1],
287:     ];
288:     let to_light = [
289:         sample_point[0] - surface_point[0],
290:         sample_point[1] - surface_point[1],
291:         sample_point[2] - surface_point[2],
292:     ];
293:     let distance_sq = to_light[0] * to_light[0] + to_light[1] * to_light[1] + to_light[2] * to_light[2];
294:     let distance = distance_sq.sqrt().max(1e-4);
295:     let direction = [
296:         to_light[0] / distance,
297:         to_light[1] / distance,
298:         to_light[2] / distance,
299:     ];
300:     let cos_surface = direction[0] * normal[0] + direction[1] * normal[1] + direction[2] * normal[2];
301:     // Panels radiate downward; the receiver must also face the panel.
302:     let cos_light = direction[1].max(0.0);
303:     if cos_surface <= 0.0 || cos_light <= 0.0 {
304:         return [0.0; 3];
305:     }
306:     // Shadow ray. The panel's own emissive voxels sit at the endpoint, so a
307:     // near-endpoint emissive hit counts as arrival, not occlusion.
308:     if let Some(obstruction) = trace_svo(
309:         &scene.atlas,
310:         &scene.chunks,
311:         surface_point,
312:         direction,
313:         distance,
314:         true,
315:     ) {
316:         let reached_panel = is_emissive(obstruction.voxel_type)
317:             && obstruction.t > distance - scene.voxel_size * 4.0;
318:         if !reached_panel {
319:             return [0.0; 3];
320:         }
321:     }
322:     let area = 4.0 * half[0] * half[1];
323:     let pdf = 1.0 / (area * scene.lights.len() as f32);
324:     let geometry = cos_surface * cos_light / distance_sq;
325:     let scale = light.intensity * geometry / (std::f32::consts::PI * pdf);
326:     [
327:         light.color[0] * scale,
328:         light.color[1] * scale,
329:         light.color[2] * scale,
330:     ]
331: }
332: 
333: /// Which axis face of the voxel grid the hit crossed: the axis whose
334: /// coordinate sits nearest a voxel boundary. Exact for face hits; edges and
335: /// corners (measure zero) pick either adjacent face, which is harmless in
336: /// Monte-Carlo estimation.
337: fn face_normal(point: [f32; 3], direction: [f32; 3], voxel_size: f32) -> [f32; 3] {
338:     let mut best_axis = 0;
339:     let mut best_distance = f32::MAX;
340:     for axis in 0..3 {
341:         let cell = point[axis] / voxel_size;
342:         let fractional = cell - cell.floor();
343:         let distance = fractional.min(1.0 - fractional);
344:         if distance < best_distance {
345:             best_distance = distance;
346:             best_axis = axis;
347:         }
348:     }
349:     let mut normal = [0.0f32; 3];
350:     normal[best_axis] = -direction[best_axis].signum();
351:     normal
352: }
353: 
354: fn cosine_hemisphere(normal: [f32; 3], rng: &mut Pcg32) -> [f32; 3] {
355:     // Orthonormal basis around the normal (axis-aligned normals make this
356:     // trivial, but stay general for safety).
357:     let tangent = if normal[0].abs() < 0.9 {
358:         normalize(cross(normal, [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]))
359:     } else {
360:         normalize(cross(normal, [0.0, 1.0, 0.0]))
361:     };
362:     let bitangent = cross(normal, tangent);
363:     let u1 = rng.uniform();
364:     let u2 = rng.uniform();
365:     let r = u1.sqrt();
366:     let phi = std::f32::consts::TAU * u2;
367:     let (x, y) = (r * phi.cos(), r * phi.sin());
368:     let z = (1.0 - u1).max(0.0).sqrt();
369:     normalize([
370:         tangent[0] * x + bitangent[0] * y + normal[0] * z,
371:         tangent[1] * x + bitangent[1] * y + normal[1] * z,
372:         tangent[2] * x + bitangent[2] * y + normal[2] * z,
373:     ])
374: }
375: 
376: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
377: // Camera at the spawn corridor, matching the real-time boot view.
378: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
379: 
380: struct Camera {
381:     position: [f32; 3],
382:     right: [f32; 3],
383:     up: [f32; 3],
384:     forward: [f32; 3],
385:     width: f32,
386:     height: f32,
387:     aspect: f32,
388: }
389: 
390: impl Camera {
391:     fn at_spawn(seed: u32, width: u32, height: u32) -> Self {
392:         let spawn = spawn_point(seed);
393:         let yaw = -std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
394:         let forward = [yaw.sin(), 0.0, -yaw.cos()];
395:         let right = [-forward[2], 0.0, forward[0]];
396:         Self {
397:             position: [spawn.x, 1.7, spawn.z],
398:             right,
399:             up: [0.0, 1.0, 0.0],
400:             forward,
401:             width: width as f32,
402:             height: height as f32,
403:             aspect: width as f32 / height as f32,
404:         }
405:     }
406: 
407:     fn primary_ray(&self, column: f32, row: f32, rng: &mut Pcg32) -> Ray {
408:         let u = ((column + rng.uniform()) / self.width * 2.0 - 1.0) * FOV_TAN * self.aspect;
409:         let v = (1.0 - (row + rng.uniform()) / self.height * 2.0) * FOV_TAN;
410:         Ray {
411:             origin: self.position,
412:             direction: normalize([
413:                 self.right[0] * u + self.up[0] * v + self.forward[0],
414:                 self.right[1] * u + self.up[1] * v + self.forward[1],
415:                 self.right[2] * u + self.up[2] * v + self.forward[2],
416:             ]),
417:         }
418:     }
419: }
420: 
421: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
422: // Small numerics: PCG32 sampling and vector helpers.
423: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
424: 
425: /// Minimal PCG32 (O'Neill); deterministic per (pixel, sample, seed).
426: struct Pcg32 {
427:     state: u64,
428:     increment: u64,
429: }
430: 
431: impl Pcg32 {
432:     fn new(stream: u64, seed: u64) -> Self {
433:         let mut rng = Self {
434:             state: seed.wrapping_add(0x853c_49e6_748f_ea9b),
435:             increment: (stream << 1) | 1,
436:         };
437:         rng.next();
438:         rng.next();
439:         rng
440:     }
441: 
442:     fn next(&mut self) -> u32 {
443:         let old = self.state;
444:         self.state = old
445:             .wrapping_mul(6_364_136_223_846_793_005)
446:             .wrapping_add(self.increment);
447:         let xorshifted = (((old >> 18) ^ old) >> 27) as u32;
448:         let rotation = (old >> 59) as u32;
449:         xorshifted.rotate_right(rotation)
450:     }
451: 
452:     fn uniform(&mut self) -> f32 {
453:         (self.next() >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
454:     }
455: }
456: 
457: fn random_seed() -> u32 {
458:     use std::hash::{BuildHasher, Hasher};
459:     std::collections::hash_map::RandomState::new()
460:         .build_hasher()
461:         .finish() as u32
462: }
463: 
464: fn env_number(name: &str, fallback: u32) -> u32 {
465:     std::env::var(name)
466:         .ok()
467:         .and_then(|value| value.parse().ok())
468:         .unwrap_or(fallback)
469: }
470: 
471: fn parse_size() -> (u32, u32) {
472:     std::env::var("SIZE")
473:         .ok()
474:         .and_then(|value| {
475:             let (w, h) = value.split_once('x')?;
476:             Some((w.parse().ok()?, h.parse().ok()?))
477:         })
478:         .unwrap_or((640, 360))
479: }
480: 
481: fn cross(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
482:     [
483:         a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1],
484:         a[2] * b[0] - a[0] * b[2],
485:         a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0],
486:     ]
487: }
488: 
489: fn normalize(v: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
490:     let length = (v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1] + v[2] * v[2]).sqrt().max(1e-8);
491:     [v[0] / length, v[1] / length, v[2] / length]
492: }

````rust
  1: //! Boundary validation for CPU render settings.
  2: //!
  3: //! Sliders, saved JSON, and query strings are untrusted input. Keeping every
  4: //! numerical limit here prevents the UI, WASM exports, and renderer from
  5: //! developing slightly different interpretations of the same setting.
  6: 
  7: use super::CpuRenderSettings;
  8: 
  9: pub struct CpuSettingsLimits;
 10: 
 11: impl CpuSettingsLimits {
 12:     pub const INTERNAL_SCALE: (f32, f32) = (0.25, 2.0);
 13:     pub const LOD_CUTOFF_PX: (f32, f32) = (0.25, 2.0);
 14:     pub const MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_PX: (f32, f32) = (1.0, 16.0);
 15:     pub const MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH: (u8, u8) = (3, 8);
 16:     pub const MIN_SPLIT_SIZE: (f32, f32) = (0.005, 1.0);
 17:     pub const MAX_DRAW_DISTANCE: (f32, f32) = (16.0, 256.0);
 18:     pub const MIN_MIP_OCCUPANCY: (f32, f32) = (0.0, 0.5);
 19:     pub const FOV_TAN: (f32, f32) = (0.1, 4.0);
 20: }
 21: 
 22: fn finite_clamp(value: f32, fallback: f32, limits: (f32, f32)) -> f32 {
 23:     if value.is_finite() {
 24:         value.clamp(limits.0, limits.1)
 25:     } else {
 26:         fallback
 27:     }
 28: }
 29: 
 30: impl CpuRenderSettings {
 31:     /// Returns a finite, bounded snapshot safe for traversal and allocation.
 32:     pub fn validated(mut self) -> Self {
 33:         let fallback = Self::default();
 34:         self.internal_scale = finite_clamp(
 35:             self.internal_scale,
 36:             fallback.internal_scale,
 37:             CpuSettingsLimits::INTERNAL_SCALE,
 38:         );
 39:         self.lod_cutoff_px = finite_clamp(
 40:             self.lod_cutoff_px,
 41:             fallback.lod_cutoff_px,
 42:             CpuSettingsLimits::LOD_CUTOFF_PX,
 43:         );
 44:         self.max_splat_radius_px = finite_clamp(
 45:             self.max_splat_radius_px,
 46:             fallback.max_splat_radius_px,
 47:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_SPLAT_RADIUS_PX,
 48:         );
 49:         self.max_virtual_depth = self.max_virtual_depth.clamp(
 50:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.0,
 51:             CpuSettingsLimits::MAX_VIRTUAL_DEPTH.1,
 52:         );
 53:         self.min_split_size = finite_clamp(
 54:             self.min_split_size,
 55:             fallback.min_split_size,
 56:             CpuSettingsLimits::MIN_SPLIT_SIZE,
 57:         );
 58:         self.max_draw_distance = finite_clamp(
 59:             self.max_draw_distance,

 63:         self.min_mip_occupancy = finite_clamp(

 67:         );
 68:         self.fov_tan = finite_clamp(self.fov_tan, fallback.fov_tan, CpuSettingsLimits::FOV_TAN);
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/shading/compose_environment_irradiance.rs

````rust
 1: //! Ambient visibility and the optional cached diffuse-fill contribution.
 2: //! Neither term owns direct-light, flashlight, emission, or atmosphere math.
 3: 
 4: use crate::application::ports::Environment;
 5: use crate::application::rendering::{
 6:     CACHED_DIFFUSE_FILL_GAIN, INDOOR_AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE, LinearRgb, OUTDOOR_AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE,
 7: };
 8: 
 9: use super::super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
10: use super::SplatSurface;
11: 
12: pub(super) fn ambient_irradiance(environment: &Environment) -> LinearRgb {
13:     let base = if environment.outdoor {
14:         OUTDOOR_AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE
15:     } else {
16:         INDOOR_AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE
17:     };
18:     base.map(|channel| channel * environment.ambient_scale.max(0.0))
19: }
20: 
21: /// Crowding is only an ambient-visibility approximation. Analytic lights,
22: /// flashlight visibility, and emission are never multiplied by it.
23: pub(super) fn ambient_visibility(crowded_siblings: u32) -> f32 {
24:     let neighbors = crowded_siblings.saturating_sub(1).min(7) as f32;
25:     (1.0 - 0.055 * neighbors).clamp(0.62, 1.0)
26: }
27: 
28: pub(super) fn cached_fill_irradiance(
29:     surface: &SplatSurface,
30:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
31: ) -> LinearRgb {
32:     if !settings.toggles.baked_lighting {
33:         return [0.0; 3];
34:     }
35:     surface
36:         .baked_irradiance
37:         .map(|channel| (channel / 15.0).clamp(0.0, 1.0) * CACHED_DIFFUSE_FILL_GAIN)
38: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Facade for one complete visible-splat shading evaluation.
  2: 
  3: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, Environment};
  4: use crate::application::rendering::{DIFFUSE_REFLECTANCE_INV_PI, LinearRgb};
  5: 
  6: use super::super::camera::Camera;
  7: use super::super::flashlight;
  8: use super::super::settings::{CpuRenderSettings, CpuShadowMode};
  9: use super::compose_environment_irradiance::{
 10:     ambient_irradiance, ambient_visibility, cached_fill_irradiance,
 11: };
 12: use super::evaluate_dynamic_irradiance::dynamic_irradiance;
 13: use super::evaluate_emission::{emission_strength, emitted_radiance_with_strength};
 14: use super::evaluate_fixture_irradiance::fixture_irradiance_with_visibility;
 15: use super::present_radiance::{present_radiance, view_distance};
 16: use super::surface_reconstruction::{
 17:     decode_albedo, representative_normal, representative_surface_position,
 18: };
 19: use super::trace_direct_light_visibility::DirectLightVisibility;
 20: use super::{FrameLighting, SplatSurface};
 21: 
 22: /// Correctness path with the complete analytic fixture contract.
 23: pub fn shade_with_frame_lighting(
 24:     cam: &Camera,
 25:     environment: &Environment,
 26:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
 27:     atlas: &[u32],
 28:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 29:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
 30:     surface: &SplatSurface,
 31: ) -> [u8; 3] {
 32:     shade_predecoded_with_frame_lighting(
 33:         cam,
 34:         environment,
 35:         settings,
 36:         atlas,
 37:         chunks,
 38:         lighting,
 39:         surface,
 40:         decode_albedo(surface.base_color),
 41:         surface
 42:             .is_emissive
 43:             .then(|| emission_strength(surface.base_color)),
 44:     )
 45: }
 46: 
 47: /// Hot production path. Atlas upload already decoded authored sRGB and MIP
 48: /// filtering already averaged in linear space, so shading consumes the
 49: /// prepared albedo without repeating transfer-function powers per splat.
 50: pub(crate) fn shade_predecoded_with_frame_lighting(
 51:     cam: &Camera,
 52:     environment: &Environment,
 53:     settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
 54:     atlas: &[u32],
 55:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
 56:     lighting: FrameLighting<'_>,
 57:     surface: &SplatSurface,
 58:     albedo: LinearRgb,
 59:     emission_strength: Option<f32>,
 60: ) -> [u8; 3] {
 61:     let camera_to_surface = [
 62:         surface.center[0] - cam.pos[0],
 63:         surface.center[1] - cam.pos[1],
 64:         surface.center[2] - cam.pos[2],
 65:     ];
 66:     let reconstructed_normal = representative_normal(surface, camera_to_surface);
 67:     let normal = reconstructed_normal.unwrap_or([0.0, 1.0, 0.0]);
 68:     let surface_position =
 69:         representative_surface_position(surface.center, surface.world_size, normal);
 70:     let distance = view_distance(cam, surface, surface_position);
 71: 
 72:     if let Some(emission) =
 73:         emitted_radiance_with_strength(surface, albedo, normal, emission_strength)
 74:     {
 75:         return present_radiance(emission, distance, environment);
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     let ambient_visibility = if settings.toggles.ambient_occlusion {
 79:         ambient_visibility(surface.crowded_siblings)
 80:     } else {
 81:         1.0
 82:     };
 83:     let mut irradiance =
 84:         ambient_irradiance(environment).map(|channel| channel * ambient_visibility);
 85:     // AO approximates only open environment visibility. The cached field
 86:     // already represents transported diffuse fill and must not be darkened a
 87:     // second time.
 88:     let cached = cached_fill_irradiance(surface, settings);
 89:     let direct_visibility = if settings.shadows == CpuShadowMode::Full {
 90:         DirectLightVisibility::trace_scene(atlas, chunks, surface.world_size)
 91:     } else {
 92:         DirectLightVisibility::unoccluded()
 93:     };
 94:     let fixtures =
 95:         fixture_irradiance_with_visibility(lighting, surface_position, normal, direct_visibility);
 96:     let dynamics = dynamic_irradiance(cam, surface_position, normal);
 97:     let flashlight = if cam.flashlight && reconstructed_normal.is_some() {
 98:         flashlight::beam_contribution(
 99:             cam,
100:             atlas,
101:             chunks,
102:             flashlight::BeamReceiver::surface_sample(
103:                 surface.center,
104:                 surface.world_size,
105:                 surface_position,
106:                 normal,
107:             ),
108:             settings.flashlight_visibility(),
109:         )
110:     } else {
111:         [0.0; 3]
112:     };
113: 
114:     for channel in 0..3 {
115:         irradiance[channel] +=
116:             cached[channel] + fixtures[channel] + dynamics[channel] + flashlight[channel];
117:     }
118:     let reflected = [
119:         albedo[0] * irradiance[0] * DIFFUSE_REFLECTANCE_INV_PI,
120:         albedo[1] * irradiance[1] * DIFFUSE_REFLECTANCE_INV_PI,
121:         albedo[2] * irradiance[2] * DIFFUSE_REFLECTANCE_INV_PI,
122:     ];
123:     present_radiance(reflected, distance, environment)
124: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Persistent state and public facade for CPU voxel splatting.

 82: impl SoftwareRasterizer {
 83:     pub fn new(width: usize, height: usize) -> Self {
 84:         let settings = CpuRenderSettings::default();

100:             environment: Environment::default(),

102:     }

106:     }

119:     }

121:     pub fn telemetry(&self) -> SoftwareRasterizerTelemetry {
122:         let node_budget_limited = self.budget_exhausted
123:             && self
124:                 .frame_work_budget
125:                 .outside_focus_reserve(self.visited_nodes);
126:         let pixel_budget_limited =
127:             self.budget_exhausted && self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes);
128:         SoftwareRasterizerTelemetry {
129:             visited_nodes: self.visited_nodes,
130:             node_soft_limit: self.frame_work_budget.soft_node_visit_limit(),
131:             node_visit_limit: self.frame_work_budget.node_visit_limit(),
132:             node_budget_limited,
133:             budget_exhausted: self.budget_exhausted,
134:             max_virtual_depth: self.max_virtual_depth_reached,
135:             splat_count: self.splat_count,
136:             pixel_writes: self.pixel_writes,
137:             pixel_write_limit: self.frame_work_budget.pixel_write_limit(),
138:             pixel_budget_limited,
139:         }
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// Test seam and frame clear: atmosphere chooses the background; target
143:     /// storage owns color/depth/HZ reset mechanics.
144:     pub(super) fn clear(&mut self) {
145:         let background_radiance = if self.environment.outdoor {
146:             self.environment.sky_color
147:         } else {
148:             self.environment.fog_color
149:         };
150:         let background = encode_display_color(background_radiance)
151:             .map(|channel| (channel * 255.0).round().clamp(0.0, 255.0) as u8);
152:         self.target.clear(background);
153:     }
154: 
155:     /// Frame-policy wrapper around the pixel-only target operation. It keeps
156:     /// the exact in-loop write cap and renderer telemetry out of `target`.
157:     fn splat(&mut self, cx: f32, cy: f32, half: f32, z: f32, rgb: [u8; 3]) {
158:         self.write_splat_request(SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, z, rgb));
159:     }
160: 
161:     /// Writes a shaded voxel surface using its exact ray/plane depth. The
162:     /// emissive flag affects only exact coplanar reconstruction ties.
163:     fn surface_splat(
164:         &mut self,
165:         cx: f32,
166:         cy: f32,
167:         half: f32,
168:         depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth,
169:         rgb: [u8; 3],
170:         emissive: bool,
171:     ) {
172:         let mut splat = SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, depth.representative_depth(), rgb)
173:             .with_surface_depth(depth);
174:         if emissive {
175:             splat = splat.with_equal_depth_priority();
176:         }
177:         self.write_splat_request(splat);
178:     }
179: 
180:     fn write_splat_request(&mut self, splat: SquareSplat) {
181:         if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes) {
182:             self.budget_exhausted = true;
183:             return;
184:         }
185:         self.splat_count += 1;
186: 
187:         let result = self.target.write_splat(
188:             splat,
189:             self.frame_work_budget
190:                 .remaining_pixel_writes(self.pixel_writes),
191:             self.settings.toggles.hierarchical_z,
192:         );
193:         self.pixel_writes += result.pixel_writes;
194:         self.budget_exhausted |= result.budget_exhausted;
195:     }
196: 
197:     /// Exact pre-shading fine-depth rejection. This deliberately lives at the
198:     /// renderer boundary: traversal can avoid radiance and visibility work,
199:     /// while the pixel target remains the single owner of clipping/depth math.
200:     fn surface_splat_may_contribute(
201:         &self,
202:         cx: f32,
203:         cy: f32,
204:         half: f32,
205:         depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth,
206:         emissive: bool,
207:     ) -> bool {
208:         if self.frame_work_budget.writes_exhausted(self.pixel_writes) {
209:             return false;
210:         }
211:         let mut splat = SquareSplat::new(cx, cy, half, depth.representative_depth(), [0; 3])
212:             .with_surface_depth(depth);
213:         if emissive {
214:             splat = splat.with_equal_depth_priority();
215:         }
216:         self.target.surface_splat_may_contribute(&splat)
217:     }

365:         self.render_cpu_frame(frame, chunks);

369: #[cfg(test)]
370: mod atlas_row_upload_tests {
371:     use crate::application::atlas::ROW_TEXELS;
372:     use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, RendererPort};
373: 
374:     use super::SoftwareRasterizer;
375: 
376:     const WORDS_PER_NODE: usize = 4;
377:     const AIR: [u32; WORDS_PER_NODE] = [1, 0, 0, 0];
378: 
379:     fn air_rows(rows: usize) -> Vec<u32> {
380:         AIR.repeat(ROW_TEXELS * rows)
381:     }
382: 
383:     #[test]
384:     fn renderer_port_row_upload_matches_a_full_reference_upload() {
385:         let initial = air_rows(2);
386:         let mut changed_row = air_rows(1);
387:         changed_row[1] = 1;
388:         changed_row[2] = 0x66aa44;
389:         changed_row[3] = 9 | (9 << 16) | (7 << 20) | (5 << 24);
390: 
391:         let mut incremental = SoftwareRasterizer::new(8, 8);
392:         incremental.upload_atlas(&initial);
393:         assert!(incremental.upload_atlas_rows(1, &changed_row));
394: 
395:         let mut expected_atlas = initial;
396:         let second_row_start = ROW_TEXELS * WORDS_PER_NODE;
397:         expected_atlas[second_row_start..].copy_from_slice(&changed_row);
398:         let mut reference = SoftwareRasterizer::new(8, 8);
399:         reference.upload_atlas(&expected_atlas);
400: 
401:         assert_eq!(incremental.atlas, reference.atlas);
402:         assert_eq!(incremental.mips, reference.mips);
403:         assert_eq!(incremental.mip_update_scratch.len(), ROW_TEXELS);
404: 
405:         let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
406:             origin: [0.0; 3],
407:             root_index: ROW_TEXELS as i32,
408:             world_size: 1.0,
409:             voxel_size: 1.0,
410:             svo_depth: 0,
411:         }];
412:         let frame = FrameParams {
413:             camera_pos: [0.5, 0.5, -2.0],
414:             yaw: std::f32::consts::PI,
415:             ..FrameParams::default()
416:         };
417:         incremental.draw(&frame, &chunks);
418:         reference.draw(&frame, &chunks);
419:         assert_eq!(incremental.framebuffer(), reference.framebuffer());
420:     }
421: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Names the section of the world the player is standing in, for the HUD.
  2: //!
  3: //! The locator re-derives the deterministic region plan for the player's
  4: //! current region (cached per region key, so the plan is recomputed only on
  5: //! a region crossing) and classifies the position against, in priority
  6: //! order: anomaly footprints, assembly footprints, and circulation spines.
  7: //! Platform-agnostic — no browser types — so the classification is natively
  8: //! unit-testable.
  9: 
 10: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind;
 11: use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::{RegionPlan, SpaceProgram};
 12: use vackrooms::entities::models::Position;
 13: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
 14: use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 15: use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, generate_region_plan};
 16: 
 17: /// Backrooms level ids, mirroring the engine's.
 18: const LEVEL_HABITABLE: u32 = 1;
 19: const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
 20: 
 21: pub struct SectionLocator {
 22:     seed: u32,
 23:     config: GeneratorConfig,
 24:     noise: SimpleNoiseProvider,
 25:     cached_region: Option<(i64, i64)>,
 26:     plan: Option<RegionPlan>,
 27: }
 28: 
 29: impl SectionLocator {
 30:     pub fn new(seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> Self {
 31:         Self {
 32:             seed,
 33:             config,
 34:             noise: SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
 35:             cached_region: None,
 36:             plan: None,
 37:         }
 38:     }
 39: 
 40:     /// Human-readable "where am I" line for the HUD, e.g.
 41:     /// `LEVEL 0 · PILLAR EXPANSE · REGION (2, -1)`.
 42:     pub fn describe(&mut self, level: u32, x: f32, z: f32) -> String {
 43:         if level == LEVEL_GRASSLAND {
 44:             return "LEVEL 34 · THE GRASSLAND".to_string();
 45:         }
 46:         if level == LEVEL_HABITABLE {
 47:             // Level 1's sectors are a pure world-lattice function; no
 48:             // region plan exists (or is needed) on the Habitable Zone.
 49:             let sector =
 50:                 vackrooms::use_cases::level_one::Sector::at(self.seed, x, z).name();
 51:             return format!("LEVEL 1 · HABITABLE ZONE · {sector}");
 52:         }
 53:         let rx = (x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 54:         let rz = (z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
 55:         let zone = self.zone_name(rx, rz, x, z);
 56:         format!("LEVEL {level} · {zone} · REGION ({rx}, {rz})")
 57:     }
 58: 
 59:     fn zone_name(&mut self, rx: i64, rz: i64, x: f32, z: f32) -> &'static str {
 60:         if self.cached_region != Some((rx, rz)) {
 61:             self.plan = Some(generate_region_plan(
 62:                 self.seed,
 63:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 64:                 REGION_SIZE,
 65:                 &self.config,
 66:                 &self.noise,
 67:             ));
 68:             self.cached_region = Some((rx, rz));
 69:         }
 70:         let plan = self.plan.as_ref().expect("plan cached above");
 71: 
 72:         // Anomalies dominate: standing inside one matters more than which
 73:         // office footprint it swallowed.
 74:         for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
 75:             if anomaly.footprint.contains(x, z) {
 76:                 return match anomaly.kind {
 77:                     AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => "PILLAR EXPANSE",
 78:                     AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => "BLACKOUT EXPANSE",
 79:                     AnomalyKind::PitLattice => "PIT LATTICE",
 80:                     AnomalyKind::RedRoom => "RED LOOP",
 81:                     AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => "ARCHWAY ANCHOR",
 82:                 };
 83:             }
 84:         }
 85:         for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 86:             if assembly.footprint.contains(x, z) {
 87:                 return program_name(assembly.program);
 88:             }
 89:         }
 90:         for corridor in &plan.corridors {
 91:             if corridor.distance(x, z) <= corridor.width * 0.5 {
 92:                 return program_name(corridor.spine_kind);
 93:             }
 94:         }
 95:         "OPEN FABRIC"
 96:     }
 97: }
 98: 
 99: fn program_name(program: SpaceProgram) -> &'static str {
100:     match program {
101:         SpaceProgram::Arrival => "ARRIVAL",
102:         SpaceProgram::Reception => "RECEPTION",
103:         SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => "MAIN CORRIDOR",
104:         SpaceProgram::SecondaryHall => "SECONDARY HALL",
105:         SpaceProgram::OpenOffice => "OPEN OFFICE",
106:         SpaceProgram::PrivateOffice => "PRIVATE OFFICE",
107:         SpaceProgram::ConferenceRoom => "CONFERENCE ROOM",
108:         SpaceProgram::WaitingArea => "WAITING AREA",
109:         SpaceProgram::BreakRoom => "BREAK ROOM",
110:         SpaceProgram::Storage => "STORAGE",
111:         SpaceProgram::ServerRoom => "SERVER ROOM",
112:         SpaceProgram::RestroomCore => "RESTROOM CORE",
113:         SpaceProgram::Stair => "STAIRWELL",
114:         SpaceProgram::Mechanical => "MECHANICAL",
115:         SpaceProgram::Atrium => "ATRIUM",
116:         SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "ABANDONED EXPANSION",
117:     }
118: }
119: 
120: #[cfg(test)]
121: mod tests {
122:     use super::*;
123:     use vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point;
124: 
125:     #[test]
126:     fn grassland_never_computes_a_plan() {
127:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
128:         assert_eq!(
129:             locator.describe(34, 12345.0, -9876.0),
130:             "LEVEL 34 · THE GRASSLAND"
131:         );
132:         assert!(locator.plan.is_none(), "no region plan needed outdoors");
133:     }
134: 
135:     #[test]
136:     fn spawn_is_on_the_main_corridor() {
137:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
138:         let at = spawn_point(42);
139:         let text = locator.describe(0, at.x, at.z);
140:         assert!(
141:             text.contains("MAIN CORRIDOR") || text.contains("ARRIVAL"),
142:             "spawn should sit on readable circulation, got: {text}"
143:         );
144:         assert!(text.starts_with("LEVEL 0 · "), "{text}");
145:         assert!(text.contains("REGION (0, 0)"), "{text}");
146:     }
147: 
148:     #[test]
149:     fn region_plan_is_cached_until_a_region_crossing() {
150:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, GeneratorConfig::low_spec());
151:         locator.describe(0, 5.0, 5.0);
152:         let first = locator.cached_region;
153:         locator.describe(0, 6.0, 6.0);
154:         assert_eq!(locator.cached_region, first, "same region: no recompute");
155:         locator.describe(0, 5.0 + REGION_SIZE, 5.0);
156:         assert_ne!(locator.cached_region, first, "crossing must recompute");
157:     }
158: 
159:     #[test]
160:     fn forced_anomaly_is_reported_at_its_own_center() {
161:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
162:         config.anomalies.forced_kind =
163:             Some(vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
164:         let mut locator = SectionLocator::new(42, config);
165:         // Find the forced instance's center via the same plan the locator
166:         // uses; standing on its center must classify as the anomaly.
167:         let plan = generate_region_plan(
168:             42,
169:             Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
170:             REGION_SIZE,
171:             &config,
172:             &SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
173:         );
174:         let forced = plan
175:             .anomalies
176:             .iter()
177:             .find(|a| a.kind == vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse);
178:         if let Some(instance) = forced {
179:             let c = instance.footprint.center;
180:             let text = locator.describe(0, c.x, c.z);
181:             assert!(text.contains("PILLAR EXPANSE"), "{text}");
````
