````rust
52: /// Level 0 — the Backrooms proper. One zero-sized generator; every stage it
53: /// composes is a pure function of world-space coordinates and the immutable
54: /// reality snapshot, so chunks tile seamlessly in any streaming order.
55: pub struct BackroomsLevel;
````

````rust
  6: struct TestNoise;
  7: 
  8: impl TestNoise {
  9:     fn hash2d(seed: u32, x: i32, y: i32) -> f32 {
 10:         let mut h = seed
 11:             .wrapping_add(x as u32 ^ 0x9E3779B9)
 12:             .wrapping_add(y as u32 ^ 0x85EBCA6B);
 13:         h ^= h >> 16;
 14:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EBCA6B);
 15:         h ^= h >> 13;
 16:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2AE35);
 17:         h ^= h >> 16;
 18:         ((h as f32) / (std::u32::MAX as f32)) * 2.0 - 1.0
 19:     }
 20: 
 21:     fn lerp(a: f32, b: f32, t: f32) -> f32 {
 22:         a + t * (b - a)
 23:     }
 24: 
 25:     fn smoothstep(t: f32) -> f32 {
 26:         t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
 27:     }
 28: }
 29: 
 30: impl NoiseProvider for TestNoise {
 31:     fn evaluate_2d(&self, seed: u32, position: Position) -> f32 {
 32:         let freq = 0.05;
 33:         let x = position.x * freq;
 34:         let y = position.z * freq;
 35:         let x0 = x.floor() as i32;
 36:         let x1 = x0 + 1;
 37:         let y0 = y.floor() as i32;
 38:         let y1 = y0 + 1;
 39:         let tx = x - (x0 as f32);
 40:         let ty = y - (y0 as f32);
 41:         let u = Self::smoothstep(tx);
 42:         let v = Self::smoothstep(ty);
 43:         let v00 = Self::hash2d(seed, x0, y0);
 44:         let v10 = Self::hash2d(seed, x1, y0);
 45:         let v01 = Self::hash2d(seed, x0, y1);
 46:         let v11 = Self::hash2d(seed, x1, y1);
 47:         let nx0 = Self::lerp(v00, v10, u);
 48:         let nx1 = Self::lerp(v01, v11, u);
 49:         Self::lerp(nx0, nx1, v)
 50:     }
 51: }

325: /// `derive_genome`'s fields must not be independent rolls: a designer who
326: /// chose a deep-beam structural system (specifically to achieve a wide
327: /// clear span) should show that beam grid in the ceiling, and a designer
328: /// who chose core-and-shell (no interior columns at all, nothing to
329: /// coffer) should not. If the two conditional distributions of
330: /// `ceiling_language` were the same, `structural_system` would be
331: /// statistically irrelevant to it — exactly the independent-hash-roll bug
332: /// this phase removes.
333: #[test]
334: fn ceiling_language_is_not_independent_of_structural_system() {
335:     use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{CeilingLanguage, StructuralSystem};
336: 
337:     let noise = TestNoise;
338:     let mut deep_span_flat = 0u32;
339:     let mut deep_span_total = 0u32;
340:     let mut core_shell_flat = 0u32;
341:     let mut core_shell_total = 0u32;
342:     for rx in -40i64..40 {
343:         for rz in -40i64..40 {
344:             for salt in 0i64..3 {
345:                 let genome = derive_genome(42, rx, rz, salt, &noise);
346:                 match genome.structural_system {
347:                     StructuralSystem::DeepSpansWithBeams => {
348:                         deep_span_total += 1;
349:                         if genome.ceiling_language == CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles {
350:                             deep_span_flat += 1;
351:                         }
352:                     }
353:                     StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell => {
354:                         core_shell_total += 1;
355:                         if genome.ceiling_language == CeilingLanguage::FlatTiles {
356:                             core_shell_flat += 1;
357:                         }
358:                     }
359:                     _ => {}
360:                 }
361:             }
362:         }
363:     }
364:     assert!(
365:         deep_span_total > 100 && core_shell_total > 100,
366:         "sample too small: {deep_span_total} deep-span, {core_shell_total} core-and-shell genomes"
367:     );
368:     let deep_span_flat_rate = deep_span_flat as f32 / deep_span_total as f32;
369:     let core_shell_flat_rate = core_shell_flat as f32 / core_shell_total as f32;
370:     assert!(
371:         deep_span_flat_rate < 0.30,
372:         "a deep-beam designer chose flat tiles {deep_span_flat_rate:.2} of the time — \
373:          ceiling language is not tracking the structural system"
374:     );
375:     assert!(
376:         core_shell_flat_rate > 0.50,
377:         "a core-and-shell designer (no beams to show) chose flat tiles only \
378:          {core_shell_flat_rate:.2} of the time"
379:     );
380:     assert!(
381:         core_shell_flat_rate - deep_span_flat_rate > 0.30,
382:         "flat-tile rate barely differs between structural systems \
383:          ({deep_span_flat_rate:.2} vs {core_shell_flat_rate:.2}) — \
384:          this would not reject independence"
385:     );
386: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/grassland_level.rs
````rust
  1: //! Level 34-B — "The Grassland".
  2: //!
  3: //! A safe, flat, endless grass plane you can noclip into from Level 0:
  4: //! * grass ground everywhere, with smooth-noise **lakes** of shallow water,
  5: //! * scattered **trees** (solid trunk, leaf canopy) on a hashed world grid,
  6: //! * a glowing **sky layer** at the top of the grid plus dim ground glow
  7: //!   sources hidden inside the turf, so the plane reads as daylight even
  8: //!   though lighting is the same BFS flood used indoors.
  9: //!
 10: //! Like every [`LevelGenerator`], all placement is a pure function of
 11: //! world-space coordinates so chunks tile seamlessly.
 12: 
 13: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 14:     VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
 15: };
 16: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 17: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 18: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
 19: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 20: 
 21: /// Grid height in world units; the sky glow layer sits at the top.
 22: const GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS: f32 = 5.8;
 23: /// Trees sit on a world grid of this period (units); most cells are empty.
 24: const TREE_PERIOD: f32 = 9.0;
 25: /// Ground glow sources ("sun-lit turf") every N units.
 26: const GLOW_PERIOD: f32 = 3.2;
 27: 
 28: pub struct GrasslandLevel;
 29: 
 30: impl GrasslandLevel {
 31:     /// Uniform per-cell hash in [0, 1): samples the value noise exactly on
 32:     /// its lattice (provider frequency 0.05 → inputs that are multiples of
 33:     /// 20 hit lattice points, where the noise is a raw uniform hash).
 34:     fn hash(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, salt: u32, cx: i64, cz: i64) -> f32 {
 35:         let v = noise.evaluate_2d(
 36:             seed ^ salt,
 37:             Position::new(cx as f32 * 20.0, cz as f32 * 20.0),
 38:         );
 39:         (v * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 0.999)
 40:     }
 41: }
 42: 
 43: impl LevelGenerator for GrasslandLevel {
 44:     fn generate(
 45:         &self,
 46:         chunk_pos: Position,
 47:         seed: u32,
 48:         config: GeneratorConfig,
 49:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 50:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
 51:         let s = config.voxel_scale;
 52:         let width = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 53:         let depth = (config.chunk_size / s).round() as usize;
 54:         let height = (GRID_HEIGHT_UNITS / s) as usize;
 55:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
 56:         let sky_y = height - 1;
 57: 
 58:         for z in 0..depth {
 59:             for x in 0..width {
 60:                 let wx = chunk_pos.x + (x as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 61:                 let wz = chunk_pos.z + (z as f32 + 0.5) * s;
 62: 
 63:                 // Lakes: smooth blobs of the world-space noise field.
 64:                 let lake = noise.evaluate_2d(seed ^ 0x1A5E, Position::new(wx * 0.7, wz * 0.7));
 65:                 let ground = if lake > 0.62 {
 66:                     VOXEL_WATER
 67:                 } else {
 68:                     VOXEL_GRASS
 69:                 };
 70:                 grid.set(x, 0, z, ground);
 71: 
 72:                 // Sky glow: an unbroken luminous layer overhead.
 73:                 grid.set(x, sky_y, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 74: 
 75:                 // Ground glow grid keeps the turf bright at eye level (the
 76:                 // BFS light from the sky layer alone fades before the floor).
 77:                 let gx = wx.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
 78:                 let gz = wz.rem_euclid(GLOW_PERIOD);
 79:                 if ground == VOXEL_GRASS && gx < s && gz < s {
 80:                     grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
 81:                 }
 82: 
 83:                 // Trees: hashed world cells, never in water.
 84:                 let cell_x = (wx / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
 85:                 let cell_z = (wz / TREE_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
 86:                 if Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE5, cell_x, cell_z) > 0.6 && ground == VOXEL_GRASS {
 87:                     // Trunk position jittered inside the cell.
 88:                     let jx =
 89:                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE6, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
 90:                     let jz =
 91:                         Self::hash(noise, seed, 0x7EE7, cell_x, cell_z) * (TREE_PERIOD - 2.0) + 1.0;
 92:                     let tx = cell_x as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jx;
 93:                     let tz = cell_z as f32 * TREE_PERIOD + jz;
 94:                     let dx = wx - tx;
 95:                     let dz = wz - tz;
 96:                     let d2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 97: 
 98:                     let trunk_top = (2.2 / s) as usize;
 99:                     let canopy_top = (3.6 / s) as usize;
100:                     if d2 < (0.25f32).powi(2) {
101:                         for y in 1..trunk_top.min(height - 2) {
102:                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_TREE);
103:                         }
104:                     }
105:                     if d2 < (1.6f32).powi(2) {
106:                         for y in trunk_top..canopy_top.min(height - 2) {
107:                             grid.set(x, y, z, VOXEL_GRASS);
108:                         }
109:                     }
110:                 }
111:             }
112:         }
113: 
114:         grid
115:     }
116: }
117:
````

````rust
  1: //! Stairwells: the first physical layer of the vertical world graph.
  2: //!
  3: //! The macro topology ([`crate::use_cases::world_topology`]) reserves
  4: //! [`VerticalLink`]s — stair and shaft obligations anchored inside regions.
  5: //! This module realizes the *upward* links as concrete architecture:
  6: //!
  7: //! * [`place_stairwell`] gives the region planner a `SpaceProgram::Stair`
  8: //!   assembly beside its primary corridor, near the link's anchor.
  9: //! * [`apply_stair_profile`] shapes the interior per voxel column: a flat
 10: //!   vestibule, a flight of 0.2 u treads, and a landing. An
 11: //!   [`VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent`] flight never lands — it keeps
 12: //!   rising under a raised, unlit shaft ceiling until the far wall
 13: //!   swallows it in the dark.
 14: //!
 15: //! What this deliberately does **not** do yet: move the player between
 16: //! elevations. The engine's collision world is a fixed-eye-height slider,
 17: //! so a stair is currently a readable, colliding landmark and a topology
 18: //! contract. Downward links (`EndlessDescent`, `ServiceShaft`) stay
 19: //! reservation-only until chunks can stream below elevation 0; realizing
 20: //! them as fake geometry would spend the mystery without paying it off.
 21: //!
 22: //! Geometry invariants (tested in `region_plan` / here):
 23: //! * treads rise monotonically from the entrance, 0.2 u per 0.4 u of run;
 24: //! * headroom above every tread stays >= 2.2 u;
 25: //! * the entrance column itself is always flat and walkable;
 26: //! * the profile is a pure function of world position and the assembly.
 27: 
 28: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
 29:     AssemblyInstance, CeilingZone, CorruptionProfile, Fixture, Opening, Polygon2, SpaceProgram,
 30:     StructuralSystem, StructuralSystemInstance,
 31: };
 32: use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind};
 33: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 34: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnPlan;
 35: 
 36: /// Stairwell frontage along its corridor, world units.
 37: const STAIR_WIDTH: f32 = 4.8;
 38: /// Stairwell depth away from the corridor.
 39: const STAIR_DEPTH: f32 = 8.8;
 40: /// Flat entry vestibule before the first riser.
 41: const VESTIBULE_DEPTH: f32 = 2.0;
 42: /// One tread: rise per run, both on the 0.4/0.2 plan lattices.
 43: const TREAD_RUN: f32 = 0.4;
 44: const TREAD_RISE: f32 = 0.2;
 45: /// An ordinary flight lands here (half a story on the macro lattice).
 46: const LANDING_UNITS: f32 = 1.6;
 47: /// An endless ascent keeps climbing to this height before the dark takes it.
 48: const ASCENT_MAX_UNITS: f32 = 3.2;
 49: /// Clear space kept above every tread.
 50: const MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS: f32 = 2.2;
 51: /// Stairwell ceiling: high enough that the top of an endless flight still
 52: /// has headroom, low enough to fit the level's 5.8 u grid.
 53: const STAIR_CEILING_UNITS: f32 = 5.4;
 54: 
 55: fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
 56:     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
 57: }
 58: 
 59: /// Should this link become a stair assembly this iteration? Upward links
 60: /// voxelize; downward links remain graph reservations (see module docs).
 61: pub(crate) fn link_wants_geometry(link: &VerticalLink) -> bool {
 62:     matches!(
 63:         link.kind,
 64:         VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair | VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent
 65:     )
 66: }
 67: 
 68: /// Builds the stairwell assembly for one vertical link, beside a horizontal
 69: /// main-corridor leg. Mirrors the suite-placement contract: returns `None`
 70: /// if the footprint would escape the region, collide with a prior assembly,
 71: /// or swallow another corridor — the reservation then stays unrealized
 72: /// rather than corrupting the plan.
 73: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
 74: pub(crate) fn place_stairwell(
 75:     id: u32,
 76:     link: &VerticalLink,
 77:     legs: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 78:     origin: Position,
 79:     size: f32,
 80:     edge_margin: f32,
 81:     wall_t: f32,
 82:     taken: &[(f32, f32, f32, f32)],
 83:     corridor_clearance: impl Fn(f32, f32, f32) -> bool,
 84: ) -> Option<AssemblyInstance> {
 85:     // The leg whose axis passes closest to the anchor hosts the stair.
 86:     let (lx0, lx1, lz, lw) = legs.iter().copied().min_by(|a, b| {
 87:         let da = (link.anchor.z - a.2).abs();
 88:         let db = (link.anchor.z - b.2).abs();
 89:         da.total_cmp(&db)
 90:     })?;
 91:     if lx1 - lx0 < STAIR_WIDTH + 8.0 {
 92:         return None;
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     let side = if link.anchor.z >= lz { 1.0 } else { -1.0 };
 96:     let corridor_half = lw * 0.5 + wall_t;
 97:     let x0 = snap((link.anchor.x - STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5).clamp(lx0 + 4.0, lx1 - STAIR_WIDTH - 4.0));
 98:     let z_front = snap(if side > 0.0 {
 99:         lz + corridor_half
100:     } else {
101:         lz - corridor_half - STAIR_DEPTH
102:     });
103:     let footprint = Polygon2::rect(x0, z_front, STAIR_WIDTH, STAIR_DEPTH);
104:     let b = footprint.bounds();
105: 
106:     if b.0 < origin.x + edge_margin
107:         || b.1 < origin.z + edge_margin
108:         || b.2 > origin.x + size - edge_margin
109:         || b.3 > origin.z + size - edge_margin
110:     {
111:         return None;
112:     }
113:     if taken
114:         .iter()
115:         .any(|t| t.0 < b.2 + 0.8 && b.0 < t.2 + 0.8 && t.1 < b.3 + 0.8 && b.1 < t.3 + 0.8)
116:     {
117:         return None;
118:     }
119:     let center = ((b.0 + b.2) * 0.5, (b.1 + b.3) * 0.5);
120:     if !corridor_clearance(center.0, center.1, STAIR_DEPTH.min(STAIR_WIDTH) * 0.25) {
121:         return None;
122:     }
123: 
124:     // A broad, framed threshold: the stair announces itself as circulation.
125:     let front_z = if side > 0.0 { b.1 } else { b.3 };
126:     let entrances = vec![Opening {
127:         center: Position::new(snap(x0 + STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5), front_z),
128:         width: 2.4,
129:         through_x_wall: true,
130:         lintel_units: Some(2.6),
131:     }];
132: 
133:     // One warm fixture over the vestibule; the flight above stays unlit so
134:     // the climb visibly leaves the light.
135:     let vestibule_z = if side > 0.0 {
136:         b.1 + VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5
137:     } else {
138:         b.3 - VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5
139:     };
140:     let fixtures = vec![Fixture {
141:         at: Position::new(snap(x0 + STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5), snap(vestibule_z)),
142:         half_x: 0.4,
143:         half_z: 0.4,
144:         lit: true,
145:     }];
146: 
147:     Some(AssemblyInstance {
148:         id,
149:         program: SpaceProgram::Stair,
150:         spaces: Vec::new(),
151:         // Core-and-shell: the stair core carries itself; no interior columns
152:         // may interrupt a flight.
153:         structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
154:             system: StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
155:             bay_x: 4.8,
156:             bay_z: 4.8,
157:             phase: (0.0, 0.0),
158:             column_side: 0.4,
159:         },
160:         ceiling_zones: vec![CeilingZone {
161:             area: footprint.clone(),
162:             language: crate::domain::entities::architecture::CeilingLanguage::ExposedSoffit,
163:             height_units: STAIR_CEILING_UNITS,
164:         }],
165:         fixtures,
166:         service_voids: Vec::new(),
167:         corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
168:         entrances,
169:         footprint,
170:     })
171: }
172: 
173: /// Shapes one interior column of a stair assembly: vestibule, flight,
174: /// landing (or an endless climb). Pure in `(assembly, kind, wx, wz)`.
175: pub(crate) fn apply_stair_profile(
176:     assembly: &AssemblyInstance,
177:     kind: VerticalLinkKind,
178:     plan: &mut ColumnPlan,
179:     _wx: f32,
180:     wz: f32,
181: ) {
182:     let Some(entrance) = assembly.entrances.first() else {
183:         return;
184:     };
185:     let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
186:     // Walk axis runs perpendicular to the entrance wall; depth is measured
187:     // from the entrance side inward.
188:     let depth_in = if entrance.through_x_wall {
189:         if (entrance.center.z - b.1).abs() < (entrance.center.z - b.3).abs() {
190:             wz - b.1
191:         } else {
192:             b.3 - wz
193:         }
194:     } else {
195:         // Stairwells are placed with X-wall entrances today; a Z-wall stair
196:         // would measure along X the same way.
197:         return;
198:     };
199: 
200:     let target = match kind {
201:         VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent => ASCENT_MAX_UNITS,
202:         _ => LANDING_UNITS,
203:     };
204:     let treads = ((depth_in - VESTIBULE_DEPTH) / TREAD_RUN).floor().max(0.0);
205:     let raw = treads * TREAD_RISE;
206:     plan.floor_units = raw.min(target);
207:     // Headroom is a hard invariant: the ceiling zone is planned high enough,
208:     // but clamp anyway so no future ceiling tweak can pinch a flight.
209:     plan.floor_units = plan
210:         .floor_units
211:         .min(plan.ceiling_units - MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS)
212:         .max(0.0);
213: 
214:     // The climb leaves the light: no fixture survives above the first riser,
215:     // and an endless flight rises into an unlit shaft.
216:     if plan.floor_units > 0.0 {
217:         plan.light = false;
218:     }
219: }
220: 
221: #[cfg(test)]
222: mod tests {
223:     use super::*;
224: 
225:     fn stair_assembly() -> AssemblyInstance {
226:         AssemblyInstance {
227:             id: 1,
228:             program: SpaceProgram::Stair,
229:             footprint: Polygon2::rect(0.0, 0.0, STAIR_WIDTH, STAIR_DEPTH),
230:             entrances: vec![Opening {
231:                 center: Position::new(STAIR_WIDTH * 0.5, 0.0),
232:                 width: 2.4,
233:                 through_x_wall: true,
234:                 lintel_units: Some(2.6),
235:             }],
236:             spaces: Vec::new(),
237:             structure: StructuralSystemInstance {
238:                 system: StructuralSystem::CoreAndShell,
239:                 bay_x: 4.8,
240:                 bay_z: 4.8,
241:                 phase: (0.0, 0.0),
242:                 column_side: 0.4,
243:             },
244:             ceiling_zones: Vec::new(),
245:             fixtures: Vec::new(),
246:             service_voids: Vec::new(),
247:             corruption: CorruptionProfile::default(),
248:         }
249:     }
250: 
251:     fn profile_at(kind: VerticalLinkKind, wz: f32) -> ColumnPlan {
252:         let assembly = stair_assembly();
253:         let mut plan = ColumnPlan::open(STAIR_CEILING_UNITS);
254:         apply_stair_profile(&assembly, kind, &mut plan, 2.4, wz);
255:         plan
256:     }
257: 
258:     #[test]
259:     fn flight_rises_monotonically_and_lands() {
260:         let mut previous = -1.0f32;
261:         let mut landing_seen = false;
262:         let mut wz = 0.1;
263:         while wz < STAIR_DEPTH {
264:             let plan = profile_at(VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, wz);
265:             assert!(
266:                 plan.floor_units >= previous - 1e-6,
267:                 "flight descends at depth {wz}"
268:             );
269:             assert!(
270:                 plan.ceiling_units - plan.floor_units >= MIN_HEADROOM_UNITS - 1e-6,
271:                 "headroom pinched at depth {wz}"
272:             );
273:             landing_seen |= (plan.floor_units - LANDING_UNITS).abs() < 1e-6;
274:             previous = plan.floor_units;
275:             wz += 0.1;
276:         }
277:         assert!(landing_seen, "ordinary flight never reaches its landing");
278:     }
279: 
280:     #[test]
281:     fn vestibule_is_flat_and_endless_ascent_outclimbs_the_landing() {
282:         assert_eq!(
283:             profile_at(VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, VESTIBULE_DEPTH * 0.5).floor_units,
284:             0.0,
285:             "vestibule must stay walkable from the corridor"
286:         );
287:         let deep = profile_at(VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent, STAIR_DEPTH - 0.2);
288:         assert!(
289:             deep.floor_units > LANDING_UNITS,
290:             "endless ascent stops at an ordinary landing"
291:         );
292:         assert!(!deep.light, "the top of an endless flight must be unlit");
293:     }
294: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/world_topology.rs
````rust
  1: //! The pure macro-scale world planner: an infinite graph, one cell at a time.
  2: //!
  3: //! [`plan_macro_cell`] is a pure function of `(seed, cell id, red-room
  4: //! scale)` — the top of the planning hierarchy documented in
  5: //! [`crate::domain::entities::world_topology`]. It owns three jobs:
  6: //!
  7: //! 1. **Parameter fields.** [`sample_fields`] turns the noise port into
  8: //!    multi-octave `[0, 1]` fields (openness, vertical pressure, anomaly
  9: //!    pressure, ...). This is the *only* legitimate role of fractal math in
 10: //!    the world: it chooses where the building's rules change; it never
 11: //!    substitutes for an architectural decision.
 12: //! 2. **Graph events.** Red rooms are planned here as separated events on
 13: //!    the macro lattice (a deterministic tournament gives every event a
 14: //!    cooldown radius), and vertical links reserve stairwell footprints
 15: //!    where vertical pressure is high.
 16: //! 3. **Continuity contracts.** Primary-route portals are derived from the
 17: //!    *edge's* lattice coordinate, so both neighbors of an edge compute the
 18: //!    identical crossing — the invariant that lets circulation chain across
 19: //!    regions forever.
 20: //!
 21: //! Everything downstream (region planner, anomaly planner, voxelizer)
 22: //! consumes these obligations; nothing here writes a voxel or knows a chunk
 23: //! size. Determinism is testable: see the 5×5 snapshot test at the bottom.
 24: 
 25: use crate::domain::entities::world_topology::{
 26:     MACRO_CELL_SIZE, MacroCell, MacroCellId, MacroFields, PlaceKind, Portal,
 27:     REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL, RedRoomEvent, VerticalLink, VerticalLinkKind, WorldNode,
 28: };
 29: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 30: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
 31: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 32: 
 33: /// Side of a region, world units. Kept in lockstep with
 34: /// `region_plan::REGION_SIZE` by a compile-time-adjacent test below.
 35: const REGION_SIZE: f32 = MACRO_CELL_SIZE / REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL as f32;
 36: 
 37: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 38: // Shared 32-bit deterministic hashing.
 39: //
 40: // All architectural "randomness" in region planning flows through these two
 41: // functions. They live here — at the top of the planning hierarchy — and
 42: // `region_plan` imports them, so the macro graph and the regional plans can
 43: // never disagree about a shared derivation (portals, most importantly).
 44: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45: 
 46: pub(crate) fn mix(mut h: u32) -> u32 {
 47:     h ^= h >> 16;
 48:     h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EB_CA6B);
 49:     h ^= h >> 13;
 50:     h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2_AE35);
 51:     h ^= h >> 16;
 52:     h
 53: }
 54: 
 55: /// Hash of a seed plus any number of integer keys, uniform in [0, 1).
 56: pub(crate) fn hash01(seed: u32, keys: &[i64]) -> f32 {
 57:     let mut h = mix(seed ^ 0x9E37_79B9);
 58:     for &k in keys {
 59:         h = mix(h ^ (k as u32)).wrapping_add(mix((k >> 32) as u32));
 60:     }
 61:     (mix(h) >> 8) as f32 / (1u32 << 24) as f32
 62: }
 63: 
 64: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 65: // Portals: the cross-region continuity contract.
 66: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 67: 
 68: /// World Z of the primary-route portal on the vertical edge
 69: /// `x = edge_x * REGION_SIZE` of region row `row_z`. Both regions sharing the
 70: /// edge derive the same value — this function is the single source of truth
 71: /// (the region planner routes its main spine between two of these).
 72: pub fn primary_portal_z(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> f32 {
 73:     let f = 0.30 + 0.40 * hash01(seed, &[0x0E1, edge_x, row_z]);
 74:     snap((row_z as f32 + f) * REGION_SIZE)
 75: }
 76: 
 77: /// Snap to the 0.4 u plan lattice (one coarse voxel).
 78: fn snap(v: f32) -> f32 {
 79:     (v / 0.4).round() * 0.4
 80: }
 81: 
 82: fn portal(seed: u32, edge_x: i64, row_z: i64) -> Portal {
 83:     Portal {
 84:         id: hash(seed, 0x7047_A100, edge_x, row_z),
 85:         edge_x,
 86:         row_z,
 87:         at: Position::new(
 88:             edge_x as f32 * REGION_SIZE,
 89:             primary_portal_z(seed, edge_x, row_z),
 90:         ),
 91:     }
 92: }
 93: 
 94: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 95: // Parameter fields.
 96: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 97: 
 98: /// One multi-octave field in [0, 1]:
 99: /// `F(x,z) = Σ aᵢ · N(x/sᵢ, z/sᵢ)`, rescaled and clamped. The provider's
100: /// base wavelength is ~20 u, so `20 / wavelength` stretches each octave.
101: fn field(
102:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
103:     seed: u32,
104:     salt: u32,
105:     wx: f32,
106:     wz: f32,
107:     wavelengths: [f32; 3],
108:     weights: [f32; 3],
109: ) -> f32 {
110:     let mut sum = 0.0;
111:     let mut norm = 0.0;
112:     for (octave, (&wavelength, &weight)) in wavelengths.iter().zip(weights.iter()).enumerate() {
113:         let s = 20.0 / wavelength;
114:         sum += weight
115:             * noise.evaluate_2d(
116:                 seed ^ salt.wrapping_add((octave as u32).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9)),
117:                 Position::new(wx * s, wz * s),
118:             );
119:         norm += weight;
120:     }
121:     // Octave sums cluster toward zero; stretch before biasing to [0, 1] so
122:     // thresholds see a usable spread instead of everything at 0.5.
123:     ((sum / norm) * 0.8 + 0.5).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
124: }
125: 
126: /// The institution-age field alone — how long this stretch of the building
127: /// has been rotting. Split out of [`sample_fields`] (and used by it, so the
128: /// two can never disagree) because per-column callers need one field, not
129: /// six: old territory keeps fewer of its fluorescents alive.
130: pub fn institution_age_at(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> f32 {
131:     field(
132:         noise,
133:         seed,
134:         0xF1E1_0003,
135:         wx,
136:         wz,
137:         [260.0, 90.0, 30.0],
138:         [1.0, 0.5, 0.25],
139:     )
140: }
141: 
142: /// Sample every macro parameter field at one world point. Pure and
143: /// world-space: two callers asking about the same point always agree,
144: /// regardless of which cell, region, or chunk asked.
145: pub fn sample_fields(noise: &dyn NoiseProvider, seed: u32, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> MacroFields {
146:     MacroFields {
147:         openness: field(
148:             noise,
149:             seed,
150:             0xF1E1_0001,
151:             wx,
152:             wz,
153:             [350.0, 130.0, 45.0],
154:             [1.0, 0.5, 0.2],
155:         ),
156:         vertical_pressure: field(
157:             noise,
158:             seed,
159:             0xF1E1_0002,
160:             wx,
161:             wz,
162:             [520.0, 170.0, 60.0],
163:             [1.0, 0.4, 0.15],
164:         ),
165:         institution_age: institution_age_at(noise, seed, wx, wz),
166:         anomaly_pressure: field(
167:             noise,
168:             seed,
169:             0xF1E1_0004,
170:             wx,
171:             wz,
172:             [620.0, 210.0, 70.0],
173:             [1.0, 0.35, 0.1],
174:         ),
175:         redroom_pressure: field(
176:             noise,
177:             seed,
178:             0xF1E1_0005,
179:             wx,
180:             wz,
181:             [700.0, 230.0, 80.0],
182:             [1.0, 0.3, 0.1],
183:         ),
184:         style_blend: field(
185:             noise,
186:             seed,
187:             0xF1E1_0006,
188:             wx,
189:             wz,
190:             [420.0, 140.0, 50.0],
191:             [1.0, 0.45, 0.2],
192:         ),
193:     }
194: }
195: 
196: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
197: // Red rooms as separated graph events.
198: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
199: 
200: /// Cooldown radius in macro cells (Chebyshev). Two committed events are
201: /// always at least one full macro cell (160 u) apart, so red rooms read as
202: /// rare landmarks instead of a recurring biome.
203: const RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS: i64 = 1;
204: 
205: /// Base per-cell candidate chance at `red_room_scale == 1.0`.
206: const RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE: f32 = 0.32;
207: 
208: /// The candidate score of one macro cell: `Some(score)` if the cell wants a
209: /// red room this epoch, lower score = higher priority in the tournament.
210: fn red_room_candidate(
211:     seed: u32,
212:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
213:     cell: MacroCellId,
214:     red_room_scale: f32,
215: ) -> Option<f32> {
216:     if red_room_scale <= 0.0 {
217:         return None;
218:     }
219:     let center = cell.center();
220:     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z).redroom_pressure;
221:     let score = unit(hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0011, cell.x, cell.z));
222:     // Pressure clusters events without ever making them uniform or certain.
223:     let chance = (RED_ROOM_BASE_CHANCE * red_room_scale).min(0.85) * (0.35 + 0.65 * pressure);
224:     (score < chance).then_some(score)
225: }
226: 
227: /// The red-room event a macro cell *wins*, if any. A candidate cell fires
228: /// only when no candidate within the separation radius beats its score
229: /// (ties broken by lattice coordinate), so any two firing cells are more
230: /// than the separation radius apart — a deterministic Matérn-style
231: /// exclusion, computed locally without global state.
232: pub fn red_room_event_for_cell(
233:     seed: u32,
234:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
235:     cell: MacroCellId,
236:     red_room_scale: f32,
237: ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
238:     let mine = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale)?;
239:     for dz in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
240:         for dx in -RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS..=RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS {
241:             if dx == 0 && dz == 0 {
242:                 continue;
243:             }
244:             let rival_cell = MacroCellId::new(cell.x + dx, cell.z + dz);
245:             if let Some(rival) = red_room_candidate(seed, noise, rival_cell, red_room_scale) {
246:                 let rival_wins = (rival, rival_cell.x, rival_cell.z) < (mine, cell.x, cell.z);
247:                 if rival_wins {
248:                     return None;
249:                 }
250:             }
251:         }
252:     }
253:     // The event targets exactly one of the cell's 2×2 regions.
254:     let pick = hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0022, cell.x, cell.z);
255:     let region = (
256:         cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + (pick & 1) as i64,
257:         cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + ((pick >> 1) & 1) as i64,
258:     );
259:     Some(RedRoomEvent {
260:         id: hash(seed, 0x8ED8_0033, cell.x, cell.z),
261:         region,
262:         score: mine,
263:     })
264: }
265: 
266: /// Does a red-room event target this specific region? This is the query the
267: /// region planner asks; the answer is independent of which chunk, region, or
268: /// LOD triggered the plan.
269: pub fn red_room_event_for_region(
270:     seed: u32,
271:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
272:     region_x: i64,
273:     region_z: i64,
274:     red_room_scale: f32,
275: ) -> Option<RedRoomEvent> {
276:     red_room_event_for_cell(
277:         seed,
278:         noise,
279:         MacroCellId::of_region(region_x, region_z),
280:         red_room_scale,
281:     )
282:     .filter(|event| event.region == (region_x, region_z))
283: }
284: 
285: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
286: // Vertical links.
287: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
288: 
289: /// The vertical link reserved inside one region, if any. Stairwells are
290: /// planned per region so the region planner can honor the reservation while
291: /// laying out its assemblies; the *kind* mix leans ordinary, with the
292: /// endless variants appearing only under high vertical pressure.
293: pub fn vertical_link_for_region(
294:     seed: u32,
295:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
296:     region_x: i64,
297:     region_z: i64,
298: ) -> Option<VerticalLink> {
299:     let center_x = (region_x as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
300:     let center_z = (region_z as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
301:     let pressure = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z).vertical_pressure;
302:     let gate = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0001, region_x, region_z));
303:     if gate >= 0.06 + 0.30 * pressure * pressure {
304:         return None;
305:     }
306: 
307:     let kind_roll = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0002, region_x, region_z));
308:     let (kind, to_elevation) = if kind_roll < 0.55 {
309:         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
310:     } else if kind_roll < 0.75 && pressure > 0.55 {
311:         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessAscent, 1)
312:     } else if kind_roll < 0.90 && pressure > 0.55 {
313:         (VerticalLinkKind::EndlessDescent, -1)
314:     } else if kind_roll < 0.97 {
315:         (VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair, 1)
316:     } else {
317:         (VerticalLinkKind::ServiceShaft, -1)
318:     };
319: 
320:     // Anchor well inside the region so the stair mass never has to fight the
321:     // edge margin. The region planner snaps the actual footprint to its
322:     // corridor network; the anchor only says "near here".
323:     let ax = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0003, region_x, region_z));
324:     let az = unit(hash(seed, 0x57A1_0004, region_x, region_z));
325:     Some(VerticalLink {
326:         id: hash(seed, 0x57A1_0005, region_x, region_z),
327:         kind,
328:         region: (region_x, region_z),
329:         anchor: Position::new(
330:             snap((region_x as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * ax) * REGION_SIZE),
331:             snap((region_z as f32 + 0.3 + 0.4 * az) * REGION_SIZE),
332:         ),
333:         from_elevation: 0,
334:         to_elevation,
335:     })
336: }
337: 
338: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
339: // The cell planner.
340: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
341: 
342: fn classify_region(
343:     seed: u32,
344:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
345:     region: (i64, i64),
346:     red_room_event: Option<&RedRoomEvent>,
347:     vertical: Option<&VerticalLink>,
348: ) -> PlaceKind {
349:     if red_room_event.is_some_and(|event| event.region == region) {
350:         return PlaceKind::RedRoomEncounter;
351:     }
352:     if vertical.is_some() {
353:         return PlaceKind::Stairwell;
354:     }
355:     let center_x = (region.0 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
356:     let center_z = (region.1 as f32 + 0.5) * REGION_SIZE;
357:     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center_x, center_z);
358:     if fields.openness > 0.66 {
359:         if fields.vertical_pressure > 0.60 {
360:             PlaceKind::Atrium
361:         } else {
362:             PlaceKind::OpenPlate
363:         }
364:     } else {
365:         PlaceKind::Warren
366:     }
367: }
368: 
369: /// Plan one macro cell of the infinite world graph.
370: ///
371: /// Pure: the same `(seed, cell, red_room_scale)` always yields the same
372: /// graph, and shared contracts (portals, red-room tournaments) agree with
373: /// every neighboring cell's own computation. `red_room_scale` is the
374: /// world-wide `anomalies.frequency * anomalies.red_rooms` product; passing
375: /// different scales for different cells of one world is a caller bug.
376: pub fn plan_macro_cell(
377:     seed: u32,
378:     cell: MacroCellId,
379:     red_room_scale: f32,
380:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
381: ) -> MacroCell {
382:     let center = cell.center();
383:     let fields = sample_fields(noise, seed, center.x, center.z);
384:     let red_room_event = red_room_event_for_cell(seed, noise, cell, red_room_scale);
385: 
386:     let region_x0 = cell.x * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL;
387:     let region_z0 = cell.z * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL;
388: 
389:     let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity((REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL) as usize);
390:     let mut vertical_links = Vec::new();
391:     for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
392:         for dx in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
393:             let region = (region_x0 + dx, region_z0 + dz);
394:             let vertical = vertical_link_for_region(seed, noise, region.0, region.1);
395:             nodes.push(WorldNode {
396:                 id: hash(seed, 0x40DE_0001, region.0, region.1),
397:                 region,
398:                 kind: classify_region(
399:                     seed,
400:                     noise,
401:                     region,
402:                     red_room_event.as_ref(),
403:                     vertical.as_ref(),
404:                 ),
405:                 elevation: 0,
406:             });
407:             vertical_links.extend(vertical);
408:         }
409:     }
410: 
411:     // Every vertical edge the cell's regions touch: interior, west boundary,
412:     // and east boundary. Boundary portals are recomputed identically by the
413:     // neighboring cell (asserted by test below).
414:     let mut portals = Vec::new();
415:     for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
416:         for edge in 0..=REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {
417:             portals.push(portal(seed, region_x0 + edge, region_z0 + dz));
418:         }
419:     }
420: 
421:     MacroCell {
422:         id: cell,
423:         fields,
424:         nodes,
425:         portals,
426:         vertical_links,
427:         red_room_event,
428:     }
429: }
430:

502:     fn snapshot_5x5() -> String {
503:         let noise = noise();
504:         let mut out = String::new();
505:         for cz in -2i64..=2 {
506:             for cx in -2i64..=2 {
507:                 out.push_str(&describe(&plan_macro_cell(
508:                     SEED,

518:     fn digest(text: &str) -> u64 {
519:         let mut h = 0xCBF2_9CE4_8422_2325u64;
520:         for byte in text.bytes() {
521:             h = mix64(h ^ byte as u64);
522:         }
523:         h
524:     }
525: 
526:     /// The same seed, coordinates and scale must always produce the same
527:     /// graph — byte for byte. If this digest changes, the world changed for
528:     /// every player: update the constant only for an *intentional*
529:     /// generation change, and say so in the commit message.
530:     #[test]
531:     fn five_by_five_topology_snapshot_is_stable() {
532:         let text = snapshot_5x5();
533:         assert_eq!(text, snapshot_5x5(), "topology is not replayable");
534:         assert_eq!(
535:             digest(&text),
536:             SNAPSHOT_DIGEST,
537:             "macro topology for seed {SEED} changed; snapshot follows:\n{text}"
538:         );
539:     }

541:     const SNAPSHOT_DIGEST: u64 = 11827557378851379719;

543:     /// Both neighbors of a shared edge must derive the identical portal.
544:     #[test]
545:     fn shared_edge_portals_agree_between_neighbor_cells() {
546:         let noise = noise();
547:         for cz in -2i64..=2 {
548:             for cx in -2i64..=2 {
549:                 let west = plan_macro_cell(SEED, MacroCellId::new(cx, cz), 1.0, &noise);
550:                 let east = plan_macro_cell(SEED, MacroCellId::new(cx + 1, cz), 1.0, &noise);
551:                 for p in &west.portals {
552:                     for q in &east.portals {
553:                         if p.edge_x == q.edge_x && p.row_z == q.row_z {

555:                         }
556:                     }
557:                 }
558:             }

562:     /// Any two committed red-room events keep the cooldown distance: no two
563:     /// events within the separation radius over a large scan.
564:     #[test]
565:     fn red_room_events_respect_their_separation_radius() {
566:         let noise = noise();
567:         let mut events = Vec::new();
568:         for cz in -12i64..=12 {
569:             for cx in -12i64..=12 {
570:                 if let Some(event) =
571:                     red_room_event_for_cell(SEED, &noise, MacroCellId::new(cx, cz), 1.0)
572:                 {
573:                     events.push(((cx, cz), event));
574:                 }
575:             }
576:         }
577:         assert!(
578:             events.len() >= 5,
579:             "red rooms too rare to test separation ({} events in 625 cells)",
580:             events.len()
581:         );
582:         for (i, ((ax, az), _)) in events.iter().enumerate() {
583:             for ((bx, bz), _) in events.iter().skip(i + 1) {
584:                 let chebyshev = (ax - bx).abs().max((az - bz).abs());
585:                 assert!(
586:                     chebyshev > RED_ROOM_SEPARATION_CELLS,
587:                     "events at ({ax},{az}) and ({bx},{bz}) violate the cooldown"
588:                 );

591:     }

601:                 for dz in 0..REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL {

603:                         let region = (

605:                             cz * REGIONS_PER_MACRO_CELL + dz,
606:                         );
607:                         let hit = red_room_event_for_region(SEED, &noise, region.0, region.1, 1.0);
608:                         match (&event, hit) {
609:                             (Some(e), Some(h)) => {
610:                                 assert_eq!(e.region, region);
611:                                 assert_eq!(*e, h);
612:                             }
613:                             (Some(e), None) => assert_ne!(e.region, region),
614:                             (None, Some(_)) => panic!("region fired without its cell"),
615:                             (None, None) => {}
616:                         }
617:                     }
618:                 }
619:             }
620:         }
621:     }

645:                 assert_eq!(a, b);

655:                 }

681:                     let z0 = rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE;
682:                     assert!(link.anchor.x > x0 + 8.0 && link.anchor.x < x0 + REGION_SIZE - 8.0);
683:                     assert!(link.anchor.z > z0 + 8.0 && link.anchor.z < z0 + REGION_SIZE - 8.0);
684:                 }
````

````rust
  1: //! Write square splats into a reusable, depth-tested CPU framebuffer.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module knows only pixels. Traversal decides *what* to draw and owns
  4: //! frame policy; the target clips a square splat, performs fine depth tests,
  5: //! enforces the caller's remaining write budget exactly, and maintains the
  6: //! coarse occlusion summary when requested.
  7: 
  8: use super::super::surface_geometry::ProjectedSurfaceDepth;
  9: 
 10: /// Coarse hierarchical-Z tile edge in pixels.
 11: const COARSE_TILE: usize = 8;
 12: 
 13: /// One depth-tested square request in target coordinates.
 14: pub(super) struct SquareSplat {
 15:     center: [f32; 2],
 16:     half: f32,
 17:     depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth,
 18:     color: [u8; 3],
 19:     /// Overlapping square reconstruction kernels can cover the same physical
 20:     /// coplanar face. An emitter owns that exact material tie, regardless of
 21:     /// traversal order; ordinary and genuinely farther samples never do.
 22:     equal_depth_wins: bool,
 23: }
 24: 
 25: impl SquareSplat {
 26:     pub(super) fn new(cx: f32, cy: f32, half: f32, depth: f32, color: [u8; 3]) -> Self {
 27:         Self {
 28:             center: [cx, cy],
 29:             half,
 30:             depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth::constant(depth),
 31:             color,
 32:             equal_depth_wins: false,
 33:         }
 34:     }
 35: 
 36:     pub(super) fn with_surface_depth(mut self, depth: ProjectedSurfaceDepth) -> Self {
 37:         self.depth = depth;
 38:         self
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     pub(super) fn with_equal_depth_priority(mut self) -> Self {
 42:         self.equal_depth_wins = true;
 43:         self
 44:     }

 47: /// Result of one square-splat write.
 48: pub(super) struct SplatWrite {
 49:     /// Fine-depth-tested pixels whose color and depth changed.
 50:     pub(super) pixel_writes: usize,
 51:     /// A further depth-passing pixel existed after the write budget ran out.
 52:     pub(super) budget_exhausted: bool,
 53: }
 54: 
 55: /// Reusable CPU render target. Reciprocal depth is affine under perspective,
 56: /// so zero means uncovered and larger finite values are nearer. A zero coarse
 57: /// value likewise means that the tile is not yet fully covered.
 58: pub(super) struct DepthTestedSplatTarget {
 59:     width: usize,
 60:     height: usize,
 61:     rgba: Vec<u8>,
 62:     reciprocal_depth: Vec<f32>,
 63:     /// Smallest (farthest) reciprocal fine depth in each fully covered tile.
 64:     coarse_reciprocal_depth: Vec<f32>,
 65:     /// Number of pixels that have transitioned from uncovered to covered.
 66:     coarse_filled: Vec<usize>,
 67:     coarse_width: usize,
 68:     coarse_height: usize,
 69: }
 70: 
 71: impl DepthTestedSplatTarget {
 72:     pub(super) fn new(width: usize, height: usize) -> Self {
 73:         let mut target = Self {
 74:             width: 0,
 75:             height: 0,
 76:             rgba: Vec::new(),
 77:             reciprocal_depth: Vec::new(),
 78:             coarse_reciprocal_depth: Vec::new(),
 79:             coarse_filled: Vec::new(),
 80:             coarse_width: 0,
 81:             coarse_height: 0,
 82:         };
 83:         target.resize(width, height);
 84:         target
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     pub(super) fn resize(&mut self, width: usize, height: usize) {
 88:         self.width = width.max(1);
 89:         self.height = height.max(1);
 90:         self.rgba = vec![0; self.width * self.height * 4];
 91:         self.reciprocal_depth = vec![0.0; self.width * self.height];
 92:         self.coarse_width = self.width.div_ceil(COARSE_TILE);
 93:         self.coarse_height = self.height.div_ceil(COARSE_TILE);
 94:         self.coarse_reciprocal_depth = vec![0.0; self.coarse_width * self.coarse_height];
 95:         self.coarse_filled = vec![0; self.coarse_width * self.coarse_height];
 96:     }
 97: 
 98:     pub(super) fn width(&self) -> usize {
 99:         self.width
100:     }
101: 
102:     pub(super) fn height(&self) -> usize {
103:         self.height
104:     }
105: 
106:     pub(super) fn rgba(&self) -> &[u8] {
107:         &self.rgba
108:     }
109: 
110:     pub(super) fn clear(&mut self, background: [u8; 3]) {
111:         for pixel in self.rgba.chunks_exact_mut(4) {
112:             pixel[0] = background[0];
113:             pixel[1] = background[1];
114:             pixel[2] = background[2];
115:             pixel[3] = 255;
116:         }
117:         self.reciprocal_depth.fill(0.0);
118:         self.coarse_reciprocal_depth.fill(0.0);
119:         self.coarse_filled.fill(0);
120:     }
121: 
122:     /// Exact fine-depth query for an unshaded square splat.
123:     ///
124:     /// Traversal uses this immediately before fixture, hero, and flashlight
125:     /// evaluation. A `false` result proves that `write_splat` would reject
126:     /// every pixel, so skipping those radiance calculations cannot change the
127:     /// framebuffer. A likely-visible splat returns at its first passing pixel.
128:     #[cfg(test)]
129:     pub(super) fn splat_may_contribute(&self, center: [f32; 2], half: f32, depth: f32) -> bool {
130:         self.request_may_contribute(&SquareSplat::new(center[0], center[1], half, depth, [0; 3]))
131:     }
132: 
133:     /// Fine-depth query for a projected physical surface. The exact same
134:     /// per-pixel depth and tie policy is consumed by [`Self::write_splat`].
135:     pub(super) fn surface_splat_may_contribute(&self, splat: &SquareSplat) -> bool {
136:         self.request_may_contribute(splat)
137:     }
138: 
139:     fn request_may_contribute(&self, splat: &SquareSplat) -> bool {
140:         let [x0, x1, y0, y1] = self.clipped_square_bounds(splat.center, splat.half);
141:         for y in y0..y1 {
142:             let row = y * self.width;
143:             for x in x0..x1 {
144:                 let Some(reciprocal_depth) = splat
145:                     .depth
146:                     .reciprocal_at_pixel([x as f32 + 0.5, y as f32 + 0.5])
147:                 else {
148:                     continue;
149:                 };
150:                 let stored = self.reciprocal_depth[row + x];
151:                 if reciprocal_depth > stored
152:                     || (splat.equal_depth_wins && reciprocal_depth == stored)
153:                 {
154:                     return true;
155:                 }
156:             }
157:         }
158:         false
159:     }
160: 
161:     /// Fills a depth-tested square. `half` is its half-extent in pixels.
162:     ///
163:     /// The budget check lives inside the depth-passing branch: rejected
164:     /// pixels cost no writes, while the first additional visible pixel after
165:     /// the budget is exhausted stops the splat and reports exhaustion.
166:     pub(super) fn write_splat(
167:         &mut self,
168:         splat: SquareSplat,
169:         write_budget: usize,
170:         maintain_coarse: bool,
171:     ) -> SplatWrite {
172:         // Traversal normally subdivides large footprints. Camera-plane and
173:         // budget fallbacks remain legal here; clipping plus `write_budget`
174:         // bounds their work without changing their requested coverage.
175:         let [x0, x1, y0, y1] = self.clipped_square_bounds(splat.center, splat.half);
176: 
177:         let mut pixel_writes = 0;
178:         let mut budget_exhausted = false;
179:         'pixels: for y in y0..y1 {
180:             let row = y * self.width;
181:             for x in x0..x1 {
182:                 let idx = row + x;
183:                 let Some(reciprocal_depth) = splat
184:                     .depth
185:                     .reciprocal_at_pixel([x as f32 + 0.5, y as f32 + 0.5])
186:                 else {
187:                     continue;
188:                 };
189:                 let stored = self.reciprocal_depth[idx];
190:                 if reciprocal_depth > stored
191:                     || (splat.equal_depth_wins && reciprocal_depth == stored)
192:                 {
193:                     if pixel_writes >= write_budget {
194:                         budget_exhausted = true;
195:                         break 'pixels;
196:                     }
197:                     let was_uncovered = stored == 0.0;
198:                     self.reciprocal_depth[idx] = reciprocal_depth;
199:                     let rgba_index = idx * 4;
200:                     self.rgba[rgba_index] = splat.color[0];
201:                     self.rgba[rgba_index + 1] = splat.color[1];
202:                     self.rgba[rgba_index + 2] = splat.color[2];
203:                     pixel_writes += 1;
204:                     if maintain_coarse && was_uncovered {
205:                         self.record_first_coverage(x, y);
206:                     }
207:                 }
208:             }
209:         }
210: 
211:         SplatWrite {
212:             pixel_writes,
213:             budget_exhausted,
214:         }
215:     }
216: 
217:     fn clipped_square_bounds(&self, center: [f32; 2], half: f32) -> [usize; 4] {
218:         // Traversal normally subdivides to the configured maximum radius,
219:         // but camera-plane intersections and explicit budget fallbacks can
220:         // legitimately cover more than 32 pixels.  The framebuffer is
221:         // already a finite clip bound and the caller supplies an exact write
222:         // budget, so silently shrinking the requested footprint would only
223:         // create holes.  A malformed infinity conservatively covers the
224:         // finite target instead of entering float-to-integer edge cases.
225:         let half = if half.is_finite() {
226:             half.max(0.0)
227:         } else {
228:             self.width.max(self.height) as f32
229:         };
230:         [
231:             (center[0] - half).floor().max(0.0) as usize,
232:             ((center[0] + half).ceil() as usize).min(self.width),
233:             (center[1] - half).floor().max(0.0) as usize,
234:             ((center[1] + half).ceil() as usize).min(self.height),
235:         ]
236:     }
237: 
238:     /// True only when every coarse tile under the screen rect is fully
239:     /// covered and its farthest stored pixel is nearer than `z_near`.
240:     #[cfg(test)]
241:     pub(super) fn coarse_occludes(&self, px: f32, py: f32, proj_radius: f32, z_near: f32) -> bool {
242:         self.coarse_rect_occludes([px, py], [proj_radius, proj_radius], z_near)
243:     }
244: 
245:     /// Rectangular form used by the exact projected AABB footprint. Keeping
246:     /// X/Y extents separate avoids turning a wide wall or shallow floor into
247:     /// an unnecessarily large square HZ query.
248:     pub(super) fn coarse_rect_occludes(
249:         &self,
250:         center: [f32; 2],
251:         half_extent: [f32; 2],
252:         z_near: f32,
253:     ) -> bool {
254:         let lower_tile = |value: f32, tiles: usize| {
255:             ((value.max(0.0) as usize) / COARSE_TILE).min(tiles.saturating_sub(1))
256:         };
257:         // Upper bounds are exclusive after `ceil`, matching the fine
258:         // `x0..x1`/`y0..y1` loops. Dividing that exclusive coordinate
259:         // directly includes the next tile at every exact 8-pixel boundary.
260:         let upper_tile = |value: f32, tiles: usize| {
261:             ((value.ceil().max(0.0) as usize).saturating_sub(1) / COARSE_TILE)
262:                 .min(tiles.saturating_sub(1))
263:         };
264:         let x0 = lower_tile((center[0] - half_extent[0]).floor(), self.coarse_width);
265:         let x1 = upper_tile(center[0] + half_extent[0], self.coarse_width);
266:         let y0 = lower_tile((center[1] - half_extent[1]).floor(), self.coarse_height);
267:         let y1 = upper_tile(center[1] + half_extent[1], self.coarse_height);
268:         if !z_near.is_finite() || z_near <= 0.0 {
269:             return false;
270:         }
271:         let reciprocal_near = z_near.recip();
272: 
273:         for tile_y in y0..=y1 {
274:             for tile_x in x0..=x1 {
275:                 if reciprocal_near
276:                     >= self.coarse_reciprocal_depth[tile_y * self.coarse_width + tile_x]
277:                 {
278:                     return false;
279:                 }
280:             }
281:         }
282:         true
283:     }
284: 
285:     /// Records an infinity-to-finite transition. A tile is scanned exactly
286:     /// once, when its final uncovered pixel becomes covered. Later depth
287:     /// writes only decrease values, so the stored maximum becomes a stale
288:     /// upper bound: conservative for rejection and free to maintain.
289:     fn record_first_coverage(&mut self, x: usize, y: usize) {
290:         let tile_x = x / COARSE_TILE;
291:         let tile_y = y / COARSE_TILE;
292:         let tile_index = tile_y * self.coarse_width + tile_x;
293:         self.coarse_filled[tile_index] += 1;
294:         if self.coarse_filled[tile_index] == self.tile_pixel_count(tile_x, tile_y) {
295:             self.coarse_reciprocal_depth[tile_index] =
296:                 self.scan_tile_farthest_reciprocal_depth(tile_x, tile_y);
297:         }
298:     }
299: 
300:     fn tile_pixel_count(&self, tile_x: usize, tile_y: usize) -> usize {
301:         let width = ((tile_x + 1) * COARSE_TILE).min(self.width) - tile_x * COARSE_TILE;
302:         let height = ((tile_y + 1) * COARSE_TILE).min(self.height) - tile_y * COARSE_TILE;
303:         width * height
304:     }
305: 
306:     fn scan_tile_farthest_reciprocal_depth(&self, tile_x: usize, tile_y: usize) -> f32 {
307:         let x0 = tile_x * COARSE_TILE;
308:         let x1 = (x0 + COARSE_TILE).min(self.width);
309:         let y0 = tile_y * COARSE_TILE;
310:         let y1 = (y0 + COARSE_TILE).min(self.height);
311:         let mut farthest = f32::INFINITY;
312:         for y in y0..y1 {
313:             for x in x0..x1 {
314:                 farthest = farthest.min(self.reciprocal_depth[y * self.width + x]);
315:             }
316:         }
317:         farthest
318:     }
319: }
````

````rust
  1: //! SVO atlas decoding and MIP filtering.
  2: //!
  3: //! The atlas is the GPU-serialized octree shared with every other renderer:
  4: //! 4 `u32` per node (see the core's `OctreeGpuSerializer`). This module owns
  5: //! the two pieces of *data preparation* the splatter needs:
  6: //!
  7: //! * [`decode_node`] — one node's texels → leaf payload or child pointer.
  8: //! * [`build_mips`] — a per-node pyramid of filtered attributes (average
  9: //!   linear albedo, max light, occupancy), computed once per atlas upload so the
 10: //!   LOD path can draw a whole subtree as a single splat.
 11: 
 12: use std::ops::Range;
 13: 
 14: use super::decode_srgb_albedo::decode_packed_albedo;
 15: use super::surface_geometry::SurfaceExposure;
 16: 
 17: /// Voxel type constants shared with the core serializer.
 18: pub const VOXEL_AIR: u32 = 0;
 19: 
 20: /// Single CPU-renderer predicate mirroring the domain's emissive palette.
 21: /// Keeping this beside atlas decoding prevents traversal and shading from
 22: /// growing renderer-specific material lists.
 23: pub fn is_emissive(voxel_type: u32) -> bool {
 24:     u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok().is_some_and(|material| {
 25:         vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material)
 26:     })
 27: }
 28: 
 29: /// Authored emitted-radiance scale for one emissive material.
 30: ///
 31: /// This is material data, not a color heuristic. Keeping it next to the
 32: /// palette predicate lets traversal carry only the compact material id while
 33: /// the shading boundary receives the exact scalar used by fixture extraction.
 34: pub fn emission_strength(voxel_type: u32) -> Option<f32> {
 35:     vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::material_emission_strength(
 36:         u8::try_from(voxel_type).ok()?,
 37:     )
 38: }
 39: 
 40: /// A decoded atlas node. Exactly one of the two shapes is meaningful:
 41: /// leaves carry material/color/light, while interiors carry
 42: /// `child_base`/`child_mask`.
 43: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 44: pub struct DecodedNode {
 45:     pub is_leaf: bool,
 46:     pub child_base: usize,
 47:     pub child_mask: u32,
 48:     pub voxel_type: u32,
 49:     /// Leaf albedo in the renderer's 0..255 reference range. Production CPU
 50:     /// traversal uses the upload-prepared linear value instead; the encoded
 51:     /// form remains part of the shared decoder for diagnostic renderers.
 52:     pub color: [f32; 3],
 53:     /// Leaf scalar diffuse-fill level, 0..15.
 54:     pub light: f32,
 55:     /// Quantized colored diffuse-fill channels, 0..15.
 56:     pub baked_rgb: [u8; 3],
 57:     /// Exact authored faces open to air, decoded from the serialized neighbor
 58:     /// occlusion mask.
 59:     pub exposure: SurfaceExposure,
 60: }
 61: 
 62: /// Reads node `node_idx` out of the texel stream. Returns `None` when the
 63: /// index runs past the atlas (defensive: a truncated upload must degrade to
 64: /// missing geometry, not out-of-bounds panics).
 65: pub fn decode_node(atlas: &[u32], node_idx: usize) -> Option<DecodedNode> {
 66:     let t = node_idx * 4;
 67:     if t + 3 >= atlas.len() {
 68:         return None;
 69:     }
 70:     let is_leaf = atlas[t] == 1;
 71:     if is_leaf {
 72:         let packed_color = atlas[t + 2];
 73:         let packed_lighting = atlas[t + 3];
 74:         Some(DecodedNode {
 75:             is_leaf: true,
 76:             child_base: 0,
 77:             child_mask: 0,
 78:             voxel_type: atlas[t + 1],
 79:             color: [
 80:                 ((packed_color >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32,
 81:                 ((packed_color >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32,
 82:                 (packed_color & 0xFF) as f32,
 83:             ],
 84:             light: (packed_lighting & 0xFF) as f32,
 85:             baked_rgb: decode_baked_rgb(packed_lighting),
 86:             exposure: decode_surface_exposure(packed_lighting),
 87:         })
 88:     } else {
 89:         Some(DecodedNode {
 90:             is_leaf: false,
 91:             child_base: atlas[t + 1] as usize,
 92:             child_mask: atlas[t + 2],
 93:             voxel_type: 0,
 94:             color: [0.0; 3],
 95:             light: 0.0,
 96:             baked_rgb: [0; 3],
 97:             exposure: SurfaceExposure::NONE,
 98:         })
 99:     }
100: }
101: 
102: /// Per-node MIP-filtered attributes, rebuilt on every atlas upload.
103: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq)]
104: pub struct MipNode {
105:     /// Occupancy-weighted linear albedo of the subtree. Decoding before the
106:     /// average is both physically correct and removes sRGB powers per splat.
107:     pub linear_albedo: [f32; 3],
108:     /// Occupancy-weighted colored diffuse fill (0..15). A maximum would smear
109:     /// one bright receiver across the entire collapsed subtree.
110:     pub baked_rgb: [f32; 3],
111:     /// Fraction of the subtree volume that is solid, 0..1.
112:     pub occupancy: f32,
113:     /// Material owning the largest occupied fraction of this subtree.
114:     pub dominant_voxel_type: u32,
115:     /// Occupied fraction represented by `dominant_voxel_type`.
116:     dominant_coverage: f32,
117:     /// Fraction of the subtree occupied by emissive material.
118:     pub emissive_coverage: f32,
119:     /// Emitted radiance averaged over the whole subtree volume. Ordinary LOD
120:     /// refuses to collapse emissive subtrees; this keeps a bounded hard-cap
121:     /// fallback visible instead of silently deleting a panel.
122:     pub emitted_radiance_density: [f32; 3],
123:     /// Directional exposed surface area prepared from exact leaf masks.
124:     pub exposed_area: SurfaceExposure,
125: }
126: 
127: fn decode_baked_rgb(packed_lighting: u32) -> [u8; 3] {
128:     [
129:         ((packed_lighting >> 16) & 0xF) as u8,
130:         ((packed_lighting >> 20) & 0xF) as u8,
131:         ((packed_lighting >> 24) & 0xF) as u8,
132:     ]
133: }
134: 
135: fn decode_surface_exposure(packed_lighting: u32) -> SurfaceExposure {
136:     SurfaceExposure::from_neighbor_occlusion(((packed_lighting >> 8) & 0x3F) as u8)
137: }
138: 
139: /// Bottom-up MIP filtering over the whole atlas. Node order in the arena is
140: /// not guaranteed (`SparseVoxelOctree::set` appends children after parents,
141: /// `BuildOctreeUseCase` pushes the root last), so each subtree is resolved by
142: /// memoized recursion instead of a single directional sweep. Still O(n): every
143: /// node is computed exactly once.
144: pub fn build_mips(atlas: &[u32]) -> Vec<MipNode> {
145:     let node_count = atlas.len() / 4;
146:     let mut mips = vec![MipNode::default(); node_count];
147:     let mut done = vec![false; node_count];
148:     for i in 0..node_count {
149:         compute_mip(atlas, i, &mut mips, &mut done, 0);
150:     }
151:     mips
152: }
153: 
154: /// Rebuilds one independent pooled-slot range without touching other MIPs.
155: ///
156: /// `done_scratch` is owned by the renderer and reused between stream updates;
157: /// its size is proportional to the changed slot, never the complete atlas.
158: pub(crate) fn rebuild_mips_in_node_range(
159:     atlas: &[u32],
160:     mips: &mut [MipNode],
161:     node_range: Range<usize>,
162:     done_scratch: &mut Vec<bool>,
163: ) -> bool {
164:     let node_count = atlas.len() / 4;
165:     if atlas.len() % 4 != 0
166:         || mips.len() != node_count
167:         || node_range.is_empty()
168:         || node_range.end > node_count
169:     {
170:         return false;
171:     }
172: 
173:     mips[node_range.clone()].fill(MipNode::default());
174:     done_scratch.clear();
175:     done_scratch.resize(node_range.len(), false);
176:     for node_index in node_range.clone() {
177:         compute_mip(atlas, node_index, mips, done_scratch, node_range.start);
178:     }
179:     true
180: }
181: 
182: fn compute_mip(atlas: &[u32], i: usize, mips: &mut [MipNode], done: &mut [bool], done_base: usize) {
183:     let Some(done_index) = i.checked_sub(done_base).filter(|&index| index < done.len()) else {
184:         return;
185:     };
186:     if done[done_index] {
187:         return;
188:     }
189:     // Marked before descending: a malformed cycle degrades to a zero mip
190:     // instead of infinite recursion.
191:     done[done_index] = true;
192: 
193:     let t = i * 4;
194:     if atlas[t] == 1 {
195:         // Leaf.
196:         let voxel_type = atlas[t + 1];
197:         if voxel_type != VOXEL_AIR {
198:             let c = atlas[t + 2];
199:             let packed_lighting = atlas[t + 3];
200:             let linear_albedo = decode_packed_albedo(c);
201:             let strength = emission_strength(voxel_type);
202:             mips[i] = MipNode {
203:                 linear_albedo,
204:                 baked_rgb: decode_baked_rgb(packed_lighting).map(f32::from),
205:                 occupancy: 1.0,
206:                 dominant_voxel_type: voxel_type,
207:                 dominant_coverage: 1.0,
208:                 emissive_coverage: if strength.is_some() { 1.0 } else { 0.0 },
209:                 emitted_radiance_density: strength.map_or([0.0; 3], |scale| {
210:                     linear_albedo.map(|channel| channel * scale)
211:                 }),
212:                 exposed_area: decode_surface_exposure(packed_lighting),
213:             };
214:         }
215:     } else {
216:         let child_base = atlas[t + 1] as usize;
217:         let child_mask = atlas[t + 2];
218:         let mut acc = MipNode::default();
219:         for child in 0..8usize {
220:             if child_mask & (1 << child) == 0 {
221:                 continue;
222:             }
223:             let idx = child_base + child;
224:             if idx >= mips.len() {
225:                 continue;
226:             }
227:             compute_mip(atlas, idx, mips, done, done_base);
228:             let m = mips[idx];
229:             let w = m.occupancy / 8.0;
230:             acc.linear_albedo[0] += m.linear_albedo[0] * w;
231:             acc.linear_albedo[1] += m.linear_albedo[1] * w;
232:             acc.linear_albedo[2] += m.linear_albedo[2] * w;
233:             acc.baked_rgb[0] += m.baked_rgb[0] * w;
234:             acc.baked_rgb[1] += m.baked_rgb[1] * w;
235:             acc.baked_rgb[2] += m.baked_rgb[2] * w;
236:             acc.emissive_coverage += m.emissive_coverage / 8.0;
237:             acc.emitted_radiance_density[0] += m.emitted_radiance_density[0] / 8.0;
238:             acc.emitted_radiance_density[1] += m.emitted_radiance_density[1] / 8.0;
239:             acc.emitted_radiance_density[2] += m.emitted_radiance_density[2] / 8.0;
240:             acc.exposed_area
241:                 .add_saturating(m.exposed_area.scaled_to_parent());
242:             let dominant_coverage = m.dominant_coverage / 8.0;
243:             if dominant_coverage > acc.dominant_coverage {
244:                 acc.dominant_coverage = dominant_coverage;
245:                 acc.dominant_voxel_type = m.dominant_voxel_type;
246:             }
247:             acc.occupancy += w;
248:         }
249:         if acc.occupancy > 0.0 {
250:             let inv = 1.0 / acc.occupancy;
251:             acc.linear_albedo[0] *= inv;
252:             acc.linear_albedo[1] *= inv;
253:             acc.linear_albedo[2] *= inv;
254:             acc.baked_rgb[0] *= inv;
255:             acc.baked_rgb[1] *= inv;
256:             acc.baked_rgb[2] *= inv;
257:         }
258:         mips[i] = acc;
259:     }
260: }
261: 
262: #[cfg(test)]
263: mod tests {
264:     use super::{emission_strength, is_emissive};
265:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
266:         VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
267:     };
268: 
269:     #[test]
270:     fn emissive_palette_matches_the_domain() {
271:         assert!(is_emissive(VOXEL_LIGHT as u32));
272:         assert!(is_emissive(VOXEL_RED_LIGHT as u32));
273:         assert!(is_emissive(VOXEL_GLIMMER as u32));
274:         assert!(!is_emissive(VOXEL_AIR as u32));
275:         assert!(!is_emissive(u32::MAX));
276:         assert_eq!(emission_strength(VOXEL_LIGHT as u32), Some(10.0));
277:         assert_eq!(emission_strength(VOXEL_RED_LIGHT as u32), Some(8.0));
278:         assert_eq!(emission_strength(VOXEL_GLIMMER as u32), Some(0.9));
279:         assert_eq!(emission_strength(VOXEL_AIR as u32), None);
280:     }
281: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Pinhole camera for the splatter, matching the GPU shaders' yaw/pitch
 2: //! basis exactly (the same formulas feed the shared WebGPU frame uniforms),
 3: //! so switching renderers never changes the framing.
 4: 
 5: use crate::application::ports::{DynamicLight, FrameParams, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
 6: 
 7: use super::settings::CpuRenderSettings;
 8: 
 9: pub fn dot(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
10:     a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]
11: }
12: 
13: /// Camera basis + per-frame light state, derived once per frame.
14: pub struct Camera {
15:     pub pos: [f32; 3],
16:     pub right: [f32; 3],
17:     pub up: [f32; 3],
18:     pub forward: [f32; 3],
19:     /// Focal length in pixels: h / (2 * tan(fov/2)).
20:     pub focal_px: f32,
21:     pub half_w: f32,
22:     pub half_h: f32,
23:     pub flashlight: bool,
24:     /// Per-frame dynamic lights (flares), pre-flickered by the engine.
25:     pub dynamic_lights: [DynamicLight; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
26:     pub dynamic_light_count: usize,
27: }
28: 
29: impl Camera {
30:     pub fn new(
31:         frame: &FrameParams,
32:         width: usize,
33:         height: usize,
34:         settings: &CpuRenderSettings,
35:     ) -> Self {
36:         let (sy, cy) = frame.yaw.sin_cos();
37:         let (sp, cp) = frame.pitch.sin_cos();
38:         Self {
39:             pos: frame.camera_pos,
40:             right: [cy, 0.0, -sy],
41:             up: [sp * sy, cp, sp * cy],
42:             forward: [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy],
43:             focal_px: height as f32 / (2.0 * settings.fov_tan),
44:             half_w: width as f32 / 2.0,
45:             half_h: height as f32 / 2.0,
46:             flashlight: frame.flashlight,
47:             dynamic_lights: frame.dynamic_lights,
48:             dynamic_light_count: (frame.dynamic_light_count as usize).min(MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS),
49:         }
50:     }
51: }
52:
````
