## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/raycast.rs
````rust
  1: //! Stack-based SVO ray traversal — the CPU twin of the GLSL `raymarchSVO`.
  2: //!
  3: //! Primary visibility comes from splatting, not marching. This module offers
  4: //! two explicit query contracts: [`trace_svo`] returns the nearest hit for
  5: //! reference/debug callers, while [`svo_segment_is_occluded`] is the
  6: //! allocation-free early-out used by flashlight and hero visibility.
  7: //! Both share the same bounded single-chunk marcher. Its work budget is
  8: //! derived from the chunk's real voxel resolution, so selecting 0.05-unit
  9: //! voxels cannot silently inherit the old 160-step coarse-scene limit:
 10: //!
 11: //! 1. Slab-test every chunk AABB and optionally sort hits near-to-far
 12: //!    ([`trace_svo`], controlled by `rt_f2b`).
 13: //! 2. Inside a chunk, descend toward the octant containing the current
 14: //!    point; **empty-space skip** jumps a whole empty leaf/octant in one
 15: //!    step via its AABB exit plane instead of voxel-by-voxel DDA.
 16: //! 3. After a skip, pop every ancestor the point exited (a skip through a
 17: //!    shared plane can leave several boxes at once).
 18: 
 19: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 20: 
 21: use super::atlas::decode_node;
 22: 
 23: /// A solid-leaf intersection: ray parameter and the voxel's material type.
 24: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 25: pub struct RayHit {
 26:     pub t: f32,
 27:     pub voxel_type: u32,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// The parameter interval over which a ray lies inside an axis-aligned box.
 31: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 32: pub(super) struct RayInterval {
 33:     pub entry: f32,
 34:     pub exit: f32,
 35: }
 36: 
 37: /// Exact ray/AABB slab intersection shared by chunk traversal and flashlight
 38: /// receiver geometry.
 39: ///
 40: /// A zero direction component means that axis is parallel: the ray either
 41: /// remains inside that slab forever or can never enter it. Tiny *non-zero*
 42: /// components remain untouched. Replacing them with an epsilon changes the
 43: /// ray itself and made CPU flashlight shadows jump when yaw or pitch crossed
 44: /// a cardinal direction.
 45: pub(super) fn ray_box_interval(
 46:     origin: [f32; 3],
 47:     direction: [f32; 3],
 48:     bounds_min: [f32; 3],
 49:     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
 50: ) -> Option<RayInterval> {
 51:     let mut entry = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
 52:     let mut exit = f32::INFINITY;
 53:     let mut has_direction = false;
 54: 
 55:     for axis in 0..3 {
 56:         let origin_axis = origin[axis];
 57:         let direction_axis = direction[axis];
 58:         if !origin_axis.is_finite()
 59:             || !direction_axis.is_finite()
 60:             || !bounds_min[axis].is_finite()
 61:             || !bounds_max[axis].is_finite()
 62:         {
 63:             return None;
 64:         }
 65: 
 66:         if direction_axis == 0.0 {
 67:             if origin_axis < bounds_min[axis] || origin_axis > bounds_max[axis] {
 68:                 return None;
 69:             }
 70:             continue;
 71:         }
 72: 
 73:         has_direction = true;
 74:         let first = (bounds_min[axis] - origin_axis) / direction_axis;
 75:         let second = (bounds_max[axis] - origin_axis) / direction_axis;
 76:         entry = entry.max(first.min(second));
 77:         exit = exit.min(first.max(second));
 78: 
 79:         if entry > exit {
 80:             return None;
 81:         }
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     has_direction.then_some(RayInterval { entry, exit })
 85: }
 86: 
 87: /// One saved traversal level: the parent node and its bounds.
 88: #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
 89: struct TraversalFrame {
 90:     node_idx: usize,
 91:     b_min: [f32; 3],
 92:     b_max: [f32; 3],
 93: }
 94: 
 95: /// The mutable cursor of one chunk march: current node, its bounds, and the
 96: /// ancestor stack (an SVO chunk is at most 8 levels deep, +1 slack).
 97: struct TraversalCursor {
 98:     stack: [TraversalFrame; 9],
 99:     stack_ptr: usize,
100:     node: usize,
101:     b_min: [f32; 3],
102:     b_max: [f32; 3],
103: }
104: 
105: /// Result of marching one intersected chunk.
106: ///
107: /// `Indeterminate` is deliberately distinct from a clear segment. A corrupt
108: /// atlas or exhausted safety budget must not become a light leak: visibility
109: /// queries treat it as blocked, while the nearest-hit diagnostic API (which
110: /// cannot represent an unknown material) simply continues to another chunk.
111: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
112: enum ChunkMarch {
113:     Hit(RayHit),
114:     Clear,
115:     Indeterminate,
116: }
117: 
118: const MIN_TRAVERSAL_STEPS: usize = 160;
119: const MAX_TRAVERSAL_STEPS: usize = 32_768;
120: 
121: /// Conservative upper work bound for a valid octree traversal.
122: ///
123: /// A line crosses at most roughly three times the leaf count of a cubic grid.
124: /// In the pessimistic sparse-tree case each crossing can descend every SVO
125: /// level again. The absolute ceiling still protects a frame from malformed or
126: /// hostile metadata; reaching it produces [`ChunkMarch::Indeterminate`].
127: fn traversal_step_budget(world_size: f32, voxel_size: f32, svo_depth: u8) -> usize {
128:     let geometry_cells =
129:         if world_size.is_finite() && voxel_size.is_finite() && world_size > 0.0 && voxel_size > 0.0
130:         {
131:             (world_size / voxel_size).ceil().clamp(1.0, 1_048_576.0) as u64
132:         } else {
133:             1
134:         };
135:     let depth_cells = 1_u64
136:         .checked_shl(u32::from(svo_depth.min(20)))
137:         .unwrap_or(1_048_576);
138:     let cells_per_axis = geometry_cells.max(depth_cells);
139:     let levels = u64::from(svo_depth).saturating_add(1);
140:     let estimated = cells_per_axis
141:         .saturating_mul(3)
142:         .saturating_add(1)
143:         .saturating_mul(levels)
144:         .saturating_add(16);
145:     estimated.clamp(MIN_TRAVERSAL_STEPS as u64, MAX_TRAVERSAL_STEPS as u64) as usize
146: }
147: 
148: impl TraversalCursor {
149:     fn at_root(root: usize, world_size: f32) -> Self {
150:         Self {
151:             stack: [TraversalFrame {
152:                 node_idx: 0,
153:                 b_min: [0.0; 3],
154:                 b_max: [0.0; 3],
155:             }; 9],
156:             stack_ptr: 0,
157:             node: root,
158:             b_min: [0.0; 3],
159:             b_max: [world_size; 3],
160:         }
161:     }
162: 
163:     fn push(&mut self) {
164:         if self.stack_ptr < 8 {
165:             self.stack[self.stack_ptr] = TraversalFrame {
166:                 node_idx: self.node,
167:                 b_min: self.b_min,
168:                 b_max: self.b_max,
169:             };
170:             self.stack_ptr += 1;
171:         }
172:     }
173: 
174:     /// Pops EVERY level `p` exited: a skip through a plane shared by several
175:     /// ancestor boxes leaves `p` outside more than one of them, and
176:     /// descending from a box that no longer contains `p` corrupts the
177:     /// traversal (wall cracks). Returns `false` when `p` left the chunk.
178:     fn pop_exited(&mut self, p: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
179:         while p[0] < self.b_min[0]
180:             || p[0] > self.b_max[0]
181:             || p[1] < self.b_min[1]
182:             || p[1] > self.b_max[1]
183:             || p[2] < self.b_min[2]
184:             || p[2] > self.b_max[2]
185:         {
186:             if self.stack_ptr == 0 {
187:                 return false;
188:             }
189:             self.stack_ptr -= 1;
190:             let frame = self.stack[self.stack_ptr];
191:             self.node = frame.node_idx;
192:             self.b_min = frame.b_min;
193:             self.b_max = frame.b_max;
194:         }
195:         true
196:     }
197: }
198: 
199: /// Advances the ray to `bounds`' exit and nudges every tied axis by one
200: /// representable float just past its plane.
201: ///
202: /// This is scale independent. The old fixed `0.001` world-unit push could
203: /// jump over geometry when the user selected 0.05-unit voxels, while its
204: /// fixed tie epsilon merged unrelated planes on long rays.
205: fn skip_to_exit(
206:     ro: [f32; 3],
207:     rd: [f32; 3],
208:     b_min: [f32; 3],
209:     b_max: [f32; 3],
210: ) -> Option<(f32, [f32; 3])> {
211:     let exit_plane = |axis: usize| match rd[axis].total_cmp(&0.0) {
212:         std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => b_max[axis],
213:         std::cmp::Ordering::Less => b_min[axis],
214:         std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => ro[axis],
215:     };
216:     let axis_exit = |axis: usize| {
217:         if rd[axis] == 0.0 {
218:             f32::INFINITY
219:         } else {
220:             (exit_plane(axis) - ro[axis]) / rd[axis]
221:         }
222:     };
223:     let t_max_planes = [axis_exit(0), axis_exit(1), axis_exit(2)];
224:     let t_exit = t_max_planes[0].min(t_max_planes[1]).min(t_max_planes[2]);
225:     if !t_exit.is_finite() {
226:         return None;
227:     }
228:     let mut p = [
229:         ro[0] + t_exit * rd[0],
230:         ro[1] + t_exit * rd[1],
231:         ro[2] + t_exit * rd[2],
232:     ];
233:     for axis in 0..3 {
234:         let axis_t = t_max_planes[axis];
235:         if !axis_t.is_finite() {
236:             continue;
237:         }
238:         let tie_tolerance = f32::EPSILON * 4.0 * t_exit.abs().max(axis_t.abs()).max(1.0);
239:         if (t_exit - axis_t).abs() <= tie_tolerance {
240:             let plane = exit_plane(axis);
241:             p[axis] = if rd[axis] > 0.0 {
242:                 plane.next_up()
243:             } else {
244:                 plane.next_down()
245:             };
246:         }
247:     }
248:     Some((t_exit, p))
249: }
250: 
251: /// Marches one chunk's SVO from `t_entry`. `ro`/`rd` are chunk-local.
252: /// Distinguishes a proven-clear segment from an invalid or exhausted march.
253: fn raymarch_svo_single(
254:     atlas: &[u32],
255:     ro: [f32; 3],
256:     rd: [f32; 3],
257:     chunk_root_idx: usize,
258:     t_entry: f32,
259:     max_t: f32,
260:     world_size: f32,
261:     voxel_size: f32,
262:     svo_depth: u8,
263: ) -> ChunkMarch {
264:     let mut t = t_entry;
265:     let mut p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
266:     let mut cursor = TraversalCursor::at_root(chunk_root_idx, world_size);
267: 
268:     let max_steps = traversal_step_budget(world_size, voxel_size, svo_depth);
269:     for _ in 0..max_steps {
270:         // A finite visibility segment must not spend the rest of its step
271:         // budget walking geometry beyond the receiver. Equality remains a
272:         // valid endpoint hit, matching `trace_svo`'s public contract.
273:         if t > max_t {
274:             return ChunkMarch::Clear;
275:         }
276:         let Some(node) = decode_node(atlas, cursor.node) else {
277:             return ChunkMarch::Indeterminate;
278:         };
279: 
280:         if node.is_leaf {
281:             if node.voxel_type != 0 {
282:                 return ChunkMarch::Hit(RayHit {
283:                     t,
284:                     voxel_type: node.voxel_type,
285:                 });
286:             }
287:             // TRAVERSAL: empty-space skip — one step to this empty
288:             // leaf's exit plane instead of voxel-by-voxel stepping.
289:             let Some(next) = skip_to_exit(ro, rd, cursor.b_min, cursor.b_max) else {
290:                 return ChunkMarch::Indeterminate;
291:             };
292:             (t, p) = next;
293:             if !cursor.pop_exited(p) {
294:                 return ChunkMarch::Clear;
295:             }
296:             continue;
297:         }
298: 
299:         let center = [
300:             (cursor.b_min[0] + cursor.b_max[0]) * 0.5,
301:             (cursor.b_min[1] + cursor.b_max[1]) * 0.5,
302:             (cursor.b_min[2] + cursor.b_max[2]) * 0.5,
303:         ];
304:         let ox = (p[0] >= center[0]) as usize;
305:         let oy = (p[1] >= center[1]) as usize;
306:         let oz = (p[2] >= center[2]) as usize;
307:         let child_idx = (oz << 2) | (oy << 1) | ox;
308: 
309:         // The octant's own bounds, picked axis-by-axis from the parent box
310:         // and its center plane.
311:         //
312:         // BUG FIX (cone light): `oct_min[1]` used to read `center[1]` in
313:         // both branches. Every secondary ray crossing an empty lower-Y
314:         // octant computed a too-near exit plane, stalled until the step
315:         // budget ran out, and reported "no hit" — so the flashlight beam
316:         // shone through floors and hero-shadow rays never found occluders.
317:         let oct_min = [
318:             if ox == 1 { center[0] } else { cursor.b_min[0] },
319:             if oy == 1 { center[1] } else { cursor.b_min[1] },
320:             if oz == 1 { center[2] } else { cursor.b_min[2] },
321:         ];
322:         let oct_max = [
323:             if ox == 1 { cursor.b_max[0] } else { center[0] },
324:             if oy == 1 { cursor.b_max[1] } else { center[1] },
325:             if oz == 1 { cursor.b_max[2] } else { center[2] },
326:         ];
327: 
328:         if (node.child_mask & (1 << child_idx)) != 0 {
329:             // Descend into the occupied octant.
330:             cursor.push();
331:             cursor.b_min = oct_min;
332:             cursor.b_max = oct_max;
333:             cursor.node = node.child_base + child_idx;
334:         } else {
335:             // TRAVERSAL: masked-out (air) octant skipped in one step.
336:             let Some(next) = skip_to_exit(ro, rd, oct_min, oct_max) else {
337:                 return ChunkMarch::Indeterminate;
338:             };
339:             (t, p) = next;
340:             if !cursor.pop_exited(p) {
341:                 return ChunkMarch::Clear;
342:             }
343:         }
344:     }
345:     ChunkMarch::Indeterminate
346: }
347: 
348: /// Traces a world-space ray through every resident chunk. Returns the first
349: /// solid hit within `max_t`.
350: pub fn trace_svo(
351:     atlas: &[u32],
352:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
353:     origin: [f32; 3],
354:     direction: [f32; 3],
355:     max_t: f32,
356:     front_to_back: bool,
357: ) -> Option<RayHit> {
358:     struct ChunkHit {
359:         idx: usize,
360:         t_min: f32,
361:     }
362: 
363:     let mut hits = Vec::with_capacity(chunks.len());
364: 
365:     for (i, chunk) in chunks.iter().enumerate() {
366:         let local_ro = [
367:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
368:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
369:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
370:         ];
371: 
372:         let Some(interval) = ray_box_interval(local_ro, direction, [0.0; 3], [chunk.world_size; 3])
373:         else {
374:             continue;
375:         };
376: 
377:         if interval.entry < interval.exit && interval.exit > 0.0 && interval.entry < max_t {
378:             hits.push(ChunkHit {
379:                 idx: i,
380:                 t_min: interval.entry.max(0.0),
381:             });
382:         }
383:     }
384: 
385:     // OPTIMIZATION (rt_f2b): nearest chunk first permits the first valid hit
386:     // to return immediately. The disabled reference path visits input order
387:     // and explicitly retains the nearest hit, producing the same answer.
388:     if front_to_back {
389:         hits.sort_by(|a, b| a.t_min.total_cmp(&b.t_min));
390:     }
391: 
392:     let mut closest = None;
393:     for hit in hits {
394:         // OPTIMIZATION (rt_f2b): sorting permits a safe early exit once the
395:         // next chunk does not begin before the closest solid already found.
396:         // Returning after the first intersected chunk is not equivalent:
397:         // padded chunk AABBs overlap, so a nearer box entry can contain a
398:         // farther solid than the following box.
399:         if front_to_back && closest.is_some_and(|current: RayHit| current.t <= hit.t_min) {
400:             break;
401:         }
402: 
403:         let chunk = &chunks[hit.idx];
404:         let local_ro = [
405:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
406:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
407:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
408:         ];
409: 
410:         if let ChunkMarch::Hit(ray_hit) = raymarch_svo_single(
411:             atlas,
412:             local_ro,
413:             direction,
414:             chunk.root_index as usize,
415:             hit.t_min,
416:             max_t,
417:             chunk.world_size,
418:             chunk.voxel_size,
419:             chunk.svo_depth,
420:         ) {
421:             // BUG FIX (cone light): the old code ignored `max_t` once inside
422:             // a chunk, so a wall *behind* the lit surface could "occlude"
423:             // the flashlight ray and randomly black out beam splats.
424:             if ray_hit.t <= max_t {
425:                 if closest.is_none_or(|current: RayHit| ray_hit.t < current.t) {
426:                     closest = Some(ray_hit);
427:                 }
428:             }
429:         }
430:     }
431: 
432:     closest
433: }
434: 
435: /// Returns `true` as soon as any solid voxel intersects the finite ray
436: /// segment `[origin, origin + direction * max_t]`.
437: ///
438: /// Visibility queries do not need the nearest material hit. Keeping that
439: /// contract separate from [`trace_svo`] avoids its per-query chunk-hit
440: /// allocation and sort: each resident chunk is slab-tested in place and the
441: /// first solid hit inside the segment terminates the scan. The SVO march is
442: /// still resolution-bounded and absolutely capped, so malformed atlas data
443: /// cannot hang a flashlight or fixture-shadow query.
444: pub fn svo_segment_is_occluded(
445:     atlas: &[u32],
446:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
447:     origin: [f32; 3],
448:     direction: [f32; 3],
449:     max_t: f32,
450: ) -> bool {
451:     if !max_t.is_finite() || max_t <= 0.0 {
452:         return false;
453:     }
454: 
455:     for chunk in chunks {
456:         let local_origin = [
457:             origin[0] - chunk.origin[0],
458:             origin[1] - chunk.origin[1],
459:             origin[2] - chunk.origin[2],
460:         ];
461:         let Some(interval) =
462:             ray_box_interval(local_origin, direction, [0.0; 3], [chunk.world_size; 3])
463:         else {
464:             continue;
465:         };
466:         if interval.entry >= interval.exit || interval.exit <= 0.0 || interval.entry >= max_t {
467:             continue;
468:         }
469: 
470:         let entry = interval.entry.max(0.0);
471:         match raymarch_svo_single(
472:             atlas,
473:             local_origin,
474:             direction,
475:             chunk.root_index as usize,
476:             entry,
477:             max_t,
478:             chunk.world_size,
479:             chunk.voxel_size,
480:             chunk.svo_depth,
481:         ) {
482:             ChunkMarch::Hit(hit) if hit.t <= max_t => return true,
483:             // Unknown traversal is conservatively shadowed. Treating it as
484:             // clear created bright leaks exactly where fine-voxel scenes
485:             // exceeded the former fixed step budget.
486:             ChunkMarch::Indeterminate => return true,
487:             ChunkMarch::Hit(_) | ChunkMarch::Clear => {}
488:         }
489:     }
490: 
491:     false
492: }
````

  1: //! Renderer-independent reference equations.
  2: //!
  3: //! This module defines the small, platform-free mathematical contract that
  4: //! presentation drivers can implement. Values are linear (never gamma
  5: //! encoded), distances are in world units, and all cosine terms are
  6: //! dimensionless.

  8: mod camera;

 14: /// Linear RGB radiance or radiance-like intensity.
 15: pub type LinearRgb = [f32; 3];
 16: 
 17: /// Canonical diffuse environment irradiance shared by every renderer.
 18: pub const INDOOR_AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE: LinearRgb = [0.045, 0.040, 0.024];
 19: pub const OUTDOOR_AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE: LinearRgb = [0.32, 0.38, 0.48];

 22: /// Lambertian BRDF scale applied once after all reflected irradiance terms.

 25: /// One authoritative unoccluded hand-lamp contract.
 26: ///
 27: /// Visibility is intentionally absent: CPU ray queries and future GPU
 28: /// visibility passes may attenuate this same irradiance without changing its
 29: /// origin, cone, transport, or spectrum.
 30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 31: pub struct FlashlightSpec {

 53: /// Converts linear HDR radiance to the canvas' ordinary sRGB encoding.
 54: ///
 55: /// The same monotone Reinhard curve and IEC sRGB transfer function are used
 56: /// by both new GPU shaders. Keeping a CPU form here prevents clear colors and
 57: /// test probes from accidentally treating linear atmosphere values as display
 58: /// values (which made unloaded outdoor space much too dark).
 59: pub fn encode_display_color(radiance: LinearRgb) -> LinearRgb {
 60:     radiance.map(|channel| {
 61:         let linear = nonnegative_radiance(channel);
 62:         let mapped = if linear == f32::INFINITY {
 63:             1.0
 64:         } else {
 65:             linear / (1.0 + linear)
 66:         };
 67:         if mapped <= 0.003_130_8 {
 68:             mapped * 12.92
 69:         } else {
 70:             1.055 * mapped.powf(1.0 / 2.4) - 0.055
 71:         }
 72:     })
 73: }
 74: 
 75: /// Beer-Lambert transmittance through a homogeneous medium.
 76: ///
 77: /// ```text
 78: /// T(d) = exp(-sigma_t * d)
 79: /// ```
 80: ///
 81: /// `distance` is a path length in world units and `extinction` is the total
 82: /// extinction coefficient `sigma_t` in inverse world units. Negative lengths
 83: /// and coefficients are treated as zero. A `NaN` input produces full
 84: /// transmittance rather than contaminating the frame with `NaN` values.
 85: pub fn beer_lambert_transmittance(distance: f32, extinction: f32) -> f32 {
 86:     let Some(distance) = nonnegative(distance) else {
 87:         return 1.0;
 88:     };
 89:     let Some(extinction) = nonnegative(extinction) else {
 90:         return 1.0;
 91:     };
 92: 
 93:     if distance == 0.0 || extinction == 0.0 {
 94:         return 1.0;
 95:     }
 96: 
 97:     (-extinction * distance).exp()
 98: }
 99: 
100: /// Beer-Lambert transmittance with a clear near field.
101: ///
102: /// Fog occupies only the portion of the view ray beyond `fog_start`:
103: ///
104: /// ```text
105: /// d_fog = max(view_distance - fog_start, 0)
106: /// T     = exp(-sigma_t * d_fog)
107: /// ```
108: ///
109: /// All distances use world units. Negative distances and starts are clamped
110: /// to zero. Invalid (`NaN`) values fail open with full transmittance.
111: pub fn fog_transmittance(view_distance: f32, fog_start: f32, extinction: f32) -> f32 {
112:     let (Some(view_distance), Some(fog_start)) =
113:         (nonnegative(view_distance), nonnegative(fog_start))
114:     else {
115:         return 1.0;
116:     };
117: 
118:     let fog_distance = if view_distance <= fog_start {
119:         0.0
120:     } else {
121:         view_distance - fog_start
122:     };
123:     beer_lambert_transmittance(fog_distance, extinction)
124: }
125: 
126: /// Composes surface radiance with homogeneous fog in linear RGB.
127: ///
128: /// ```text
129: /// L = T * L_surface + (1 - T) * L_fog
130: /// ```
131: ///
132: /// Both RGB inputs must use the same linear radiometric units. Negative and
133: /// `NaN` channels are treated as zero. `transmittance` is clamped to `[0, 1]`;
134: /// `NaN` fails open (`T = 1`). Endpoint branches avoid `0 * infinity`.
135: pub fn compose_fog(
136:     surface_radiance: LinearRgb,
137:     fog_radiance: LinearRgb,
138:     transmittance: f32,
139: ) -> LinearRgb {
140:     let surface = surface_radiance.map(nonnegative_radiance);
141:     let fog = fog_radiance.map(nonnegative_radiance);
142:     let transmittance = unit_interval_or_one(transmittance);
143: 
144:     if transmittance == 1.0 {
145:         return surface;
146:     }
147:     if transmittance == 0.0 {
148:         return fog;
149:     }
150: 
151:     let scattered = 1.0 - transmittance;
152:     [
153:         surface[0] * transmittance + fog[0] * scattered,
154:         surface[1] * transmittance + fog[1] * scattered,
155:         surface[2] * transmittance + fog[2] * scattered,
156:     ]
157: }
158: 
159: /// Smooth compact-support window for a finite-range light.
160: ///
161: /// For distance `d` and range `R` (both world lengths), the window is
162: ///
163: /// ```text
164: /// w(d, R) = (1 - (d / R)^4)^2,  0 <= d < R
165: ///           0,                    d >= R
166: /// ```
167: ///
168: /// The value and first derivative are zero at `R`, avoiding a hard lighting
169: /// seam. A non-positive, `NaN`, or otherwise invalid range disables the light.
170: pub fn compact_support_window(distance: f32, range: f32) -> f32 {
171:     let Some(distance) = nonnegative(distance) else {
172:         return 0.0;
173:     };
174:     let Some(range) = positive(range) else {
175:         return 0.0;
176:     };
177: 
178:     if distance >= range || distance == f32::INFINITY {
179:         return 0.0;
180:     }
181:     if range == f32::INFINITY {
182:         return 1.0;
183:     }
184: 
185:     let ratio_squared = (distance / range).powi(2);
186:     let one_minus_fourth = 1.0 - ratio_squared * ratio_squared;
187:     one_minus_fourth * one_minus_fourth
188: }
189: 
190: /// Finite-range inverse-square attenuation.
191: ///
192: /// ```text
193: /// A(d) = w(d, R) / max(d, d_min)^2
194: /// ```
195: ///
196: /// `distance`, `range`, and `minimum_distance` are world lengths, so the
197: /// result has units of inverse world-units squared. `minimum_distance` is the
198: /// finite emitter-size clamp that removes the point-light singularity. A
199: /// non-positive or `NaN` range/clamp disables the term; `NaN` distance also
200: /// returns zero.
201: pub fn finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(
202:     distance: f32,
203:     range: f32,
204:     minimum_distance: f32,
205: ) -> f32 {
206:     let Some(distance) = nonnegative(distance) else {
207:         return 0.0;
208:     };
209:     let Some(minimum_distance) = positive(minimum_distance) else {
210:         return 0.0;
211:     };
212: 
213:     let window = compact_support_window(distance, range);
214:     if window == 0.0 {
215:         return 0.0;
216:     }
217: 
218:     let denominator = distance.max(minimum_distance).powi(2);
219:     if denominator == f32::INFINITY {
220:         0.0
221:     } else {
222:         window / denominator
223:     }
224: }
225: 
226: /// Lambertian receiver cosine.
227: ///
228: /// ```text
229: /// cos_receiver = max(dot(n_receiver, omega_to_light), 0)
230: /// ```
231: ///
232: /// Vectors are normalized internally, so callers may use any finite non-zero
233: /// magnitude. Zero-length or non-finite vectors return zero.
234: pub fn lambertian_receiver_cosine(receiver_normal: [f32; 3], direction_to_light: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
235:     positive_cosine(receiver_normal, direction_to_light)
236: }
237: 
238: /// One-sided emission cosine for a horizontal rectangular ceiling panel.
239: ///
240: /// The panel's emitting normal is `(0, -1, 0)`. For a direction from a point
241: /// on the emitter toward the receiver,
242: ///
243: /// ```text
244: /// cos_emitter = max(dot((0, -1, 0), omega_to_receiver), 0)
245: /// ```
246: ///
247: /// Rectangle area belongs to the later irradiance integral; this function is
248: /// only its dimensionless directional factor. Zero-length or non-finite
249: /// directions return zero.
250: pub fn downward_rectangular_emitter_cosine(direction_to_receiver: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
251:     positive_cosine([0.0, -1.0, 0.0], direction_to_receiver)
252: }
253: 
254: fn positive_cosine(a: [f32; 3], b: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
255:     let (Some(a), Some(b)) = (normalize(a), normalize(b)) else {
256:         return 0.0;
257:     };
258:     (a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
259: }
260: 
261: /// Normalizes without overflowing when a finite component is near `f32::MAX`.
262: fn normalize(vector: [f32; 3]) -> Option<[f32; 3]> {
263:     if vector.iter().any(|component| !component.is_finite()) {
264:         return None;
265:     }
266: 
267:     let scale = vector
268:         .iter()
269:         .fold(0.0_f32, |largest, component| largest.max(component.abs()));
270:     if scale == 0.0 {
271:         return None;
272:     }
273: 
274:     let scaled = vector.map(|component| component / scale);
275:     let length = (scaled[0] * scaled[0] + scaled[1] * scaled[1] + scaled[2] * scaled[2]).sqrt();
276:     Some(scaled.map(|component| component / length))
277: }
278: 
279: fn nonnegative(value: f32) -> Option<f32> {
280:     if value.is_nan() {
281:         None
282:     } else {
283:         Some(value.max(0.0))
284:     }
285: }
286: 
287: fn positive(value: f32) -> Option<f32> {
288:     if value.is_nan() || value <= 0.0 {
289:         None
290:     } else {
291:         Some(value)
292:     }
293: }
294: 
295: fn nonnegative_radiance(value: f32) -> f32 {
296:     if value.is_nan() || value < 0.0 {
297:         0.0
298:     } else {
299:         value
300:     }
301: }
302: 
303: fn unit_interval_or_one(value: f32) -> f32 {
304:     if value.is_nan() {
305:         1.0
306:     } else {
307:         value.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
308:     }
309: }

````rust
  1: //! Conservative finite-range fixture clustering for a world-space AABB.
  2: //!
  3: //! Both rewritten GPU paths use this exact predicate. It removes work, not
  4: //! light: a fixture is omitted only when no point on its rectangle can be
  5: //! within its compact-support range of any receiver in the bounds.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
  8: 
  9: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 10: pub struct LightRange {
 11:     pub first: i32,
 12:     pub count: i32,
 13: }
 14: 
 15: pub fn append_lights_reaching_bounds(
 16:     lights: &[LightSource],
 17:     bounds_min: [f32; 3],
 18:     bounds_max: [f32; 3],
 19:     clustered: &mut Vec<LightSource>,
 20: ) -> LightRange {
 21:     let first = clustered.len();
 22:     clustered.extend(
 23:         lights
 24:             .iter()
 25:             .copied()
 26:             .filter(|light| reaches_bounds(light, bounds_min, bounds_max)),
 27:     );
 28:     LightRange {
 29:         first: first.min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
 30:         count: clustered.len().saturating_sub(first).min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
 31:     }
 32: }
 33: 
 34: fn reaches_bounds(light: &LightSource, bounds_min: [f32; 3], bounds_max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
 35:     // Expanding X/Z by the emitter half-size converts rectangle-to-box
 36:     // distance into point-to-box distance (the Minkowski-sum construction).
 37:     let expanded_min = [
 38:         bounds_min[0] - light.half_size[0],
 39:         bounds_min[1],
 40:         bounds_min[2] - light.half_size[1],
 41:     ];
 42:     let expanded_max = [
 43:         bounds_max[0] + light.half_size[0],
 44:         bounds_max[1],
 45:         bounds_max[2] + light.half_size[1],
 46:     ];
 47:     let mut distance_squared = 0.0;
 48:     for axis in 0..3 {
 49:         let delta = if light.position[axis] < expanded_min[axis] {
 50:             expanded_min[axis] - light.position[axis]
 51:         } else if light.position[axis] > expanded_max[axis] {
 52:             light.position[axis] - expanded_max[axis]
 53:         } else {
 54:             0.0
 55:         };
 56:         distance_squared += delta * delta;
 57:     }
 58:     distance_squared <= light.radius * light.radius
 59: }
 60: 
 61: /// Persistent cache for per-chunk top-K light selection with hysteresis.
 62: ///
 63: /// # Rationale & Design Pattern (Observer & Strategy Pattern)
 64: /// Prevents light popping across chunk seams when camera movement or floating point sorting
 65: /// slight changes candidate light order. A candidate replaces an existing selected light only
 66: /// if its calculated importance score exceeds the existing light's score by at least 20%.
 67: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
 68: pub struct LightSelectionCache {
 69:     entries: std::collections::HashMap<crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey, Vec<u64>>,
 70: }
 71: 
 72: impl LightSelectionCache {
 73:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 74:         Self {
 75:             entries: std::collections::HashMap::new(),
 76:         }
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     /// Ranks lights reaching bounds and applies a hysteresis filter against previous frame selection.
 80:     pub fn select_lights_with_hysteresis(
 81:         &mut self,
 82:         key: crate::application::ports::SurfaceChunkKey,
 83:         candidate_lights: &[LightSource],
 84:         bounds_min: [f32; 3],
 85:         bounds_max: [f32; 3],
 86:         top_k: usize,
 87:     ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
 88:         let center = [
 89:             (bounds_min[0] + bounds_max[0]) * 0.5,
 90:             (bounds_min[1] + bounds_max[1]) * 0.5,
 91:             (bounds_min[2] + bounds_max[2]) * 0.5,
 92:         ];
 93: 
 94:         // Rank candidates by estimated irradiance score = intensity / (distance_sq + 1.0)
 95:         let mut scored: Vec<(f32, &LightSource)> = candidate_lights
 96:             .iter()
 97:             .map(|light| {
 98:                 let dx = light.position[0] - center[0];
 99:                 let dy = light.position[1] - center[1];
100:                 let dz = light.position[2] - center[2];
101:                 let dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
102:                 let score = light.intensity / (dist_sq + 1.0);
103:                 (score, light)
104:             })
105:             .collect();
106:         scored.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
107: 
108:         let previous_ids = self.entries.get(&key);
109:         let mut selected = Vec::with_capacity(top_k.min(scored.len()));
110: 
111:         for (score, light) in scored {
112:             if selected.len() >= top_k {
113:                 break;
114:             }
115:             let is_previously_selected = previous_ids.map_or(false, |ids| ids.contains(&light.id));
116:             let effective_score = if is_previously_selected {
117:                 score * 1.20 // 20% hysteresis boost to retain current lights and prevent seam popping
118:             } else {
119:                 score
120:             };
121:             selected.push((effective_score, light));
122:         }
123: 
124:         selected.sort_by(|a, b| b.0.partial_cmp(&a.0).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
125:         let result: Vec<LightSource> = selected.into_iter().take(top_k).map(|(_, l)| *l).collect();
126:         self.entries.insert(key, result.iter().map(|l| l.id).collect());
127:         result
128:     }
129: }
````

````rust
 1: //! Baked 3D light-volume upload, shared by the surface and splat drivers.
 2: //!
 3: //! The WebGPU migration removed baked volumes from generation (`rt_bake`
 4: //! always defaulted off), but the GLSL programs still declare and bind the
 5: //! sampler. Until the bake path returns, every chunk shares one black 1³
 6: //! texel so the shaders stay valid and the toggle simply has no effect.
 7: 
 8: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 9: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
10: 
11: use crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload;
12: 
13: /// Uploads a chunk's 3D irradiance probe volume texture (or 1x1x1 black fallback).
14: ///
15: /// Texture sampling uses `LINEAR` minification and magnification filters, with `CLAMP_TO_EDGE`
16: /// wrapping so boundary probe samples interpolate smoothly across adjacent chunk borders.
17: pub fn upload_light_volume(gl: &Gl, mesh: &SurfaceMeshPayload) -> Result<WebGlTexture, JsValue> {
18:     let texture = gl
19:         .create_texture()
20:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create light texture"))?;
21:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Some(&texture));
22:     gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 1);
23: 
24:     let fallback = [0u8, 0u8, 0u8];
25:     let (width, height, depth, bytes) = if !mesh.light_volume_bytes.is_empty()

27:         && mesh.light_volume_dims[1] > 0

48:         Gl::RGB,

53:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_3D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::LINEAR as i32);
````

````rust
 1: //! Depth-only render target for the hero-light shadow map.
 2: 
 3: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 4: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlFramebuffer, WebGlTexture};
 5: 
 6: pub struct ShadowTarget {
 7:     pub fbo: WebGlFramebuffer,
 8:     pub texture: WebGlTexture,
 9:     pub size: i32,
10: }
11: 
12: /// Creates a `size`² DEPTH_COMPONENT16 texture bound to a framebuffer's
13: /// depth attachment. NEAREST filtering: the shaders do their own PCF.
14: pub fn create_shadow_target(gl: &Gl, size: i32) -> Result<ShadowTarget, JsValue> {
15:     let texture = gl
16:         .create_texture()
17:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create shadow texture"))?;
18:     gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
19:     gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_u8_array(
20:         Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
21:         0,
22:         Gl::DEPTH_COMPONENT16 as i32,
23:         size,
24:         size,
25:         0,
26:         Gl::DEPTH_COMPONENT,
27:         Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT,
28:         None,
29:     )?;
30:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
31:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
32:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
33:     gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
34: 
35:     let fbo = gl
36:         .create_framebuffer()
37:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("create shadow FBO"))?;
38:     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, Some(&fbo));
39:     gl.framebuffer_texture_2d(
40:         Gl::FRAMEBUFFER,
41:         Gl::DEPTH_ATTACHMENT,
42:         Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
43:         Some(&texture),
44:         0,
45:     );
46: 
47:     // A depth-only WebGL2 target has no color attachment. Explicitly route
48:     // both drawing and reading to NONE; leaving the defaults at
49:     // COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 makes strict mobile drivers report an incomplete
50:     // framebuffer and silently discard the shadow pass.
51:     let draw_buffers = js_sys::Array::new();
52:     draw_buffers.push(&wasm_bindgen::JsValue::from_f64(Gl::NONE as f64));
53:     gl.draw_buffers(draw_buffers.as_ref());
54:     gl.read_buffer(Gl::NONE);
55: 
56:     let status = gl.check_framebuffer_status(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER);
57:     if status != Gl::FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE {
58:         gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
59:         gl.delete_framebuffer(Some(&fbo));
60:         gl.delete_texture(Some(&texture));
61:         return Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!(
62:             "shadow framebuffer is incomplete (status 0x{status:04x})"
63:         )));
64:     }
65:     gl.bind_framebuffer(Gl::FRAMEBUFFER, None);
66: 
67:     Ok(ShadowTarget { fbo, texture, size })
68: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/timer.rs
````rust
 1: //! Asynchronous GPU frame timing via `EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2`.
 2: //!
 3: //! One query is in flight at a time; results are polled (never blocked on)
 4: //! at the top of the next frames, so the HUD's GPU number lags a frame or
 5: //! two but the pipeline never stalls. Toggleable (`RenderToggles::gpu_timer`)
 6: //! because some drivers serialize on timer queries.
 7: 
 8: use js_sys::Object;
 9: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlQuery};
10: 
11: /// Extension constants absent from WebGL2 core.
12: const TIME_ELAPSED_EXT: u32 = 0x88BF;
13: const GPU_DISJOINT_EXT: u32 = 0x8FBB;
14: 
15: pub struct GpuFrameTimer {
16:     extension: Option<Object>,
17:     pending: Option<WebGlQuery>,
18:     last_ms: Option<f32>,
19: }
20: 
21: impl GpuFrameTimer {
22:     /// Probes for the extension; a `None` extension makes every method a
23:     /// no-op so callers never branch on support.
24:     pub fn new(gl: &Gl) -> Self {
25:         Self {
26:             extension: gl
27:                 .get_extension("EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2")
28:                 .ok()
29:                 .flatten(),
30:             pending: None,
31:             last_ms: None,
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     pub fn last_ms(&self) -> Option<f32> {
36:         self.last_ms
37:     }
38: 
39:     /// Collects a finished query, if any. Disjoint intervals (GPU clock
40:     /// disturbance) discard the sample.
41:     pub fn poll(&mut self, gl: &Gl) {
42:         let Some(query) = self.pending.as_ref() else {
43:             return;
44:         };
45:         let available = gl
46:             .get_query_parameter(query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE)
47:             .as_bool()
48:             .unwrap_or(false);
49:         let disjoint = self.extension.is_some()
50:             && gl
51:                 .get_parameter(GPU_DISJOINT_EXT)
52:                 .ok()
53:                 .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
54:                 .unwrap_or(false);
55:         if !available && !disjoint {
56:             return;
57:         }
58:         let query = self.pending.take().expect("pending timer exists");
59:         if available && !disjoint {
60:             self.last_ms = gl
61:                 .get_query_parameter(&query, Gl::QUERY_RESULT)
62:                 .as_f64()
63:                 .map(|nanos| (nanos as f32) * 1.0e-6);
64:         }
65:         gl.delete_query(Some(&query));
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// Starts timing this frame. Returns whether a query was issued (pass
69:     /// it to [`Self::end`]). `enabled` comes from the toggle switchboard.
70:     pub fn begin(&mut self, gl: &Gl, enabled: bool) -> bool {
71:         if !enabled {
72:             // The HUD must not present an old sample as current after timing
73:             // has been switched off. An in-flight query is still collected
74:             // by `poll` and then discarded from view on this frame.
75:             self.last_ms = None;
76:             return false;
77:         }
78:         if self.extension.is_none() || self.pending.is_some() {
79:             return false;
80:         }
81:         let Some(query) = gl.create_query() else {
82:             return false;
83:         };
84:         gl.begin_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT, &query);
85:         self.pending = Some(query);
86:         true
87:     }
88: 
89:     pub fn end(&self, gl: &Gl, started: bool) {
90:         if started {
91:             gl.end_query(TIME_ELAPSED_EXT);
92:         }
93:     }
94: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/upload_scene_lights.rs
````rust
  1: //! Complete analytic-fixture upload shared by the surface and raymarch paths.
  2: //!
  3: //! A texture is used instead of fragment-uniform arrays for two reasons: the
  4: //! physical scene is not silently truncated to a camera-ranked slot budget,
  5: //! and the large raymarch chunk table no longer competes with lights for the
  6: //! WebGL minimum uniform-vector allowance. Each light occupies three RGBA32F
  7: //! texels in the layout decoded by `shaders/sample_scene_lights.rs`.
  8: 
  9: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 10: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
 11: 
 12: use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
 13: 
 14: const PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS: i32 = 1024;
 15: const TEXELS_PER_LIGHT: usize = 3;
 16: 
 17: pub struct SceneLightTexture {
 18:     texture: WebGlTexture,
 19:     width: i32,
 20:     maximum_size: i32,
 21:     staging: Vec<f32>,
 22:     last_lights: Vec<LightSource>,
 23:     uploaded: bool,
 24: }
 25: 
 26: impl SceneLightTexture {
 27:     pub fn create(gl: &Gl) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 28:         let texture = gl
 29:             .create_texture()
 30:             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("failed to create scene-light texture"))?;
 31:         let maximum_size = gl
 32:             .get_parameter(Gl::MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE)?
 33:             .as_f64()
 34:             .unwrap_or(0.0) as i32;
 35:         if maximum_size < 1 {
 36:             return Err(JsValue::from_str("WebGL reported no 2-D texture capacity"));
 37:         }
 38:         let width = PREFERRED_ROW_TEXELS.min(maximum_size);
 39:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
 40:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 41:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 42:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 43:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 44:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 45:         Ok(Self {
 46:             texture,
 47:             width,
 48:             maximum_size,
 49:             staging: Vec::new(),
 50:             last_lights: Vec::new(),
 51:             uploaded: false,
 52:         })
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     /// Replaces the immutable frame snapshot and returns its exact light count.
 56:     pub fn upload(&mut self, gl: &Gl, lights: &[LightSource]) -> Result<i32, JsValue> {
 57:         if self.uploaded && self.last_lights == lights {
 58:             return Ok(lights.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32);
 59:         }
 60:         let texel_count = lights.len().max(1) * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT;
 61:         let rows = (texel_count as i32 + self.width - 1) / self.width;
 62:         if rows > self.maximum_size || lights.len() > i32::MAX as usize {
 63:             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
 64:                 "resident fixture list exceeds the WebGL scene-light texture",
 65:             ));
 66:         }
 67: 
 68:         self.staging.clear();
 69:         self.staging
 70:             .resize(self.width as usize * rows as usize * 4, 0.0);
 71:         for (index, light) in lights.iter().enumerate() {
 72:             let offset = index * TEXELS_PER_LIGHT * 4;
 73:             self.staging[offset..offset + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
 74:             self.staging[offset + 3] = light.kind as u8 as f32;
 75:             self.staging[offset + 4..offset + 7].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
 76:             self.staging[offset + 7] = light.intensity;
 77:             self.staging[offset + 8] = light.radius;
 78:             self.staging[offset + 9] = light.half_size[0];
 79:             self.staging[offset + 10] = light.half_size[1];
 80:         }
 81: 
 82:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
 83:         gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
 84:         let view = js_sys::Float32Array::from(self.staging.as_slice());
 85:         gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
 86:             Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
 87:             0,
 88:             Gl::RGBA32F as i32,
 89:             self.width,
 90:             rows,
 91:             0,
 92:             Gl::RGBA,
 93:             Gl::FLOAT,
 94:             Some(&view),
 95:         )?;
 96:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 97:         self.last_lights.clear();
 98:         self.last_lights.extend_from_slice(lights);
 99:         self.uploaded = true;
100:         Ok(lights.len() as i32)
101:     }
102: 
103:     pub fn bind(&self, gl: &Gl) {
104:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&self.texture));
105:     }
106: 
107:     pub fn width(&self) -> i32 {
108:         self.width
109:     }
110: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/render_world_surfaces/compose_surface_lighting.rs
````rust
 1: //! Compose emission, ambient fill, cached fill, fixtures, and flashlight.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: vec3 ambientIrradiance() {
 5:     if (uOutdoor == 1) return vec3(0.32, 0.38, 0.48) * uAmbientScale;
 6:     return vec3(0.045, 0.040, 0.024) * uAmbientScale;
 7: }
 8: 
 9: vec3 composeSurfaceLighting(vec3 normal, vec3 albedo) {
10:     if (isEmissiveMaterial(vMaterial) && isDownwardEmittingFace(normal)) {
11:         return emittedRadiance(vMaterial, albedo, normal);
12:     }
13: 
14:     float ambientOcclusion = mix(1.0, 0.62, clamp(vAo, 0.0, 1.0));
15:     vec3 ambient = ambientIrradiance();
16:     // The voxel field is deliberately a restrained diffuse-fill term.
17:     // It never substitutes for the analytic fixtures below.
18:     vec3 cachedStatic = sampleStaticIrradiance(vWorldPosition, normal) * 0.12;
19:     vec3 analyticDirect = vec3(0.0);
20: 
21:     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < uLightCount; ++lightIndex) {
22:         SceneLight light = readSceneLight(uLightFirst + lightIndex);
23:         vec3 delta = light.position - vWorldPosition;
24:         vec3 surfaceToLight = normalize(delta);
25:         float visibility = lightIndex == uShadowedLightIndex
26:             ? shadowVisibility(vWorldPosition, normal, surfaceToLight)
27:             : 1.0;
28:         analyticDirect += evaluateSceneLight(
29:             vWorldPosition,
30:             normal,
31:             light.position,
32:             light.halfSize,
33:             light.color,
34:             light.range,
35:             light.intensity,
36:             light.kind
37:         ) * visibility;
38:     }
39:     for (int lightIndex = 0; lightIndex < 4; ++lightIndex) {
40:         if (lightIndex >= uDynamicLightCount) break;
41:         analyticDirect += evaluatePointLight(
42:             vWorldPosition,
43:             normal,
44:             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].xyz,
45:             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].rgb,
46:             uDynamicPosRadius[lightIndex].w,
47:             uDynamicColorIntensity[lightIndex].a
48:         );
49:     }
50: 
51:     // Screen-space/voxel AO is only a model of indirect sky/room
52:     // visibility. Applying it to analytic or already-occluded cached
53:     // fixture light darkens corners twice and violates the light model.
54:     vec3 radiance = albedo * (
55:         ambient * ambientOcclusion + cachedStatic + analyticDirect
56:     ) * (1.0 / PI);
57:     if (uFlashlightEnabled == 1) {
58:         radiance += albedo * spotBeam(
59:             uCameraPosition, uCamForward, vWorldPosition, normal
60:         );
61:     }
62:     return radiance;
63: }
64: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/render_world_surfaces/hero_shadow_visibility.rs
````rust
 1: //! Sample the optional hero-light shadow map for one visible surface point.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: float shadowVisibility(vec3 worldPosition, vec3 normal, vec3 surfaceToLight) {
 5:     vec4 clip = uLightViewProjection * vec4(worldPosition + normal * 0.02, 1.0);
 6:     vec3 projected = clip.xyz / max(abs(clip.w), 1e-8);
 7:     vec2 uv = projected.xy * 0.5 + 0.5;
 8:     float receiverDepth = projected.z * 0.5 + 0.5;
 9:     if (any(lessThan(uv, vec2(0.0))) || any(greaterThan(uv, vec2(1.0)))
10:         || receiverDepth <= 0.0 || receiverDepth >= 1.0) {
11:         return 1.0;
12:     }
13: 
14:     vec2 texel = 1.0 / vec2(textureSize(uShadowMap, 0));
15:     float bias = max(0.0015 * (1.0 - dot(normal, surfaceToLight)), 0.0005);
16:     float visible = 0.0;
17:     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
18:         vec2(-0.5, -0.5), vec2(0.5, -0.5),
19:         vec2(-0.5, 0.5), vec2(0.5, 0.5)
20:     );
21:     for (int tap = 0; tap < 4; ++tap) {
22:         float storedDepth = texture(uShadowMap, uv + offsets[tap] * texel).r;
23:         visible += receiverDepth - bias <= storedDepth ? 1.0 : 0.0;
24:     }
25:     return visible * 0.25;
26: }
27: "#;
````

````rust
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: void main() {
 5:     vec3 normal = normalize(vNormal);

14:     // at its own along-ray distance rather than fogging it as if it were on
15:     // the receiver surface.

18:     );

21:     if (uDitherEnabled == 1) {
22:         displayColor += (ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) - 0.5) * (1.0 / 255.0);
23:     }
24:     fragColor = vec4(clamp(displayColor, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0);
````

````rust
 1: //! Reconstruct chunk-local packed vertices as world-space surfaces.
 2: 
 3: pub const VERTEX_SHADER: &str = r#"#version 300 es
 4: precision highp float;
 5: 
 6: layout(location = 0) in vec3 aPosition;
 7: in float aNormalAxis;
 8: in float aMaterial;
 9: in float aStaticIndirect;
10: in float aAo;
11: 
12: uniform mat4 uProjection;
13: uniform mat4 uView;
14: uniform vec3 uChunkOrigin;
15: 
16: out vec3 vWorldPosition;
17: out vec3 vNormal;
18: flat out float vMaterial;
19: flat out float vStaticIndirect;
20: flat out float vAo;
21: 
22: vec3 normalForAxis(float axis) {
23:     if (axis < 0.5) return vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0);
24:     if (axis < 1.5) return vec3(0.0, -1.0, 0.0);
25:     if (axis < 2.5) return vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0);
26:     if (axis < 3.5) return vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0);
27:     if (axis < 4.5) return vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
28:     return vec3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
29: }
30: 
31: void main() {
32:     vec3 worldPosition = uChunkOrigin + aPosition * (1.0 / 1024.0);
33:     vWorldPosition = worldPosition;
34:     vNormal = normalForAxis(aNormalAxis);
35:     vMaterial = aMaterial;
36:     vStaticIndirect = aStaticIndirect;
37:     vAo = aAo;
38:     gl_Position = uProjection * uView * vec4(worldPosition, 1.0);
````

````rust
 1: //! Define which visible material faces emit and their linear radiance.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: bool isEmissiveMaterial(float material) {
 5:     return abs(material - 4.0) < 0.1
 6:         || abs(material - 9.0) < 0.1
 7:         || abs(material - 16.0) < 0.1;
 8: }
 9: 
10: bool isDownwardEmittingFace(vec3 normal) {
11:     return normal.y < -0.5;
12: }
13: 
14: vec3 emittedRadiance(float material, vec3 albedo, vec3 normal) {
15:     if (!isDownwardEmittingFace(normal)) return vec3(0.0);
16:     if (abs(material - 4.0) < 0.1) return albedo * 10.0;
17:     if (abs(material - 9.0) < 0.1) return albedo * 8.0;
18:     if (abs(material - 16.0) < 0.1) return albedo * 0.9;
19:     return vec3(0.0);
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/collect_ordered_chunk_intervals.rs
````rust
 1: //! Intersect the camera ray with resident chunks and optionally order entries.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: int collectOrderedChunkIntervals(
 5:     vec3 rayDirection,
 6:     out ChunkInterval intervals[25]
 7: ) {
 8:     int intervalCount = 0;
 9:     for (int chunkIndex = 0; chunkIndex < uNumChunks; ++chunkIndex) {
10:         vec3 localOrigin = uCameraPosition - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
11:         RayBoxHit box = intersectBox(
12:             localOrigin,
13:             rayDirection,
14:             vec3(0.0),
15:             vec3(uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex])
16:         );
17:         if (!box.hit) continue;
18: 
19:         int insertion = intervalCount;
20:         if (uFrontToBackEnabled == 1) {
21:             while (insertion > 0 && intervals[insertion - 1].entry > box.entry) {
22:                 intervals[insertion] = intervals[insertion - 1];
23:                 insertion--;
24:             }
25:         }
26:         intervals[insertion] = ChunkInterval(
27:             chunkIndex, box.entry, box.exit, box.entryNormal
28:         );
29:         intervalCount++;
30:     }
31:     return intervalCount;
32: }
33: "#;
````

````rust
 1: //! Stateless point lookup in the packed SVO atlas.
 2: //!
 3: //! Restarting at the root for each step costs a few integer fetches but
 4: //! removes the fragile mutable stack/pop state that caused cracks and phantom
 5: //! boxes. A masked-out child returns its exact empty octant bounds without a
 6: //! texture fetch; the optimization can then jump over that whole region.
 7: 
 8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 9: struct AtlasNode {
10:     bool leaf;
11:     uint payload;
12:     uint colorOrMask;
13:     uint lightWord;
14: };
15: 
16: struct VoxelLeaf {
17:     uint material;
18:     uint color;
19:     uint lightWord;
20:     vec3 boundsMin;
21:     vec3 boundsMax;
22: };
23: 
24: AtlasNode readAtlasNode(int nodeIndex) {
25:     ivec2 texel = ivec2(nodeIndex % 1024, nodeIndex / 1024);
26:     uvec4 packed = texelFetch(uNodeTexture, texel, 0);
27:     return AtlasNode(packed.x == 1u, packed.y, packed.z, packed.w);
28: }
29: 
30: VoxelLeaf lookupVoxelLeaf(
31:     vec3 point,
32:     int rootIndex,
33:     float worldSize,
34:     int svoDepth
35: ) {
36:     int nodeIndex = rootIndex;
37:     vec3 boundsMin = vec3(0.0);
38:     vec3 boundsMax = vec3(worldSize);
39: 
40:     // Generator validation bounds depth; the runtime value only shortens
41:     // this statically bounded loop for ordinary 6/8-level chunks.
42:     for (int level = 0; level <= 10; ++level) {
43:         AtlasNode node = readAtlasNode(nodeIndex);
44:         if (node.leaf || level >= svoDepth) {
45:             return VoxelLeaf(node.payload, node.colorOrMask, node.lightWord, boundsMin, boundsMax);
46:         }
47: 
48:         vec3 center = (boundsMin + boundsMax) * 0.5;
49:         int childX = point.x >= center.x ? 1 : 0;
50:         int childY = point.y >= center.y ? 1 : 0;
51:         int childZ = point.z >= center.z ? 1 : 0;
52:         int child = (childZ << 2) | (childY << 1) | childX;
53: 
54:         vec3 childMin = vec3(
55:             childX == 1 ? center.x : boundsMin.x,
56:             childY == 1 ? center.y : boundsMin.y,
57:             childZ == 1 ? center.z : boundsMin.z
58:         );
59:         vec3 childMax = vec3(
60:             childX == 1 ? boundsMax.x : center.x,
61:             childY == 1 ? boundsMax.y : center.y,
62:             childZ == 1 ? boundsMax.z : center.z
63:         );
64: 
65:         if ((node.colorOrMask & (1u << uint(child))) == 0u) {
66:             return VoxelLeaf(0u, 0u, 0u, childMin, childMax);
67:         }
68:         nodeIndex = int(node.payload) + child;
69:         boundsMin = childMin;
70:         boundsMax = childMax;
71:     }
72:     return VoxelLeaf(0u, 0u, 0u, boundsMin, boundsMax);
73: }
74: "#;
````

````rust
 1: //! Resolve a miss or carry a shaded voxel through fog into display space.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: void main() {
 5:     vec3 rayDirection = constructCameraRay();
 6: 
 7:     ChunkInterval intervals[25];
 8:     int intervalCount = collectOrderedChunkIntervals(rayDirection, intervals);
 9: 
10:     int closestChunkIndex;
11:     VoxelHit closest = selectNearestVoxelHit(
12:         rayDirection, intervals, intervalCount, closestChunkIndex
13:     );
14: 
15:     if (!closest.hit) {
16:         vec3 missRadiance = uOutdoor == 1 ? uSkyColor : uFogColor;
17:         fragColor = vec4(encodeDisplayColor(missRadiance), 1.0);
18:         return;
19:     }
20: 
21:     vec3 worldPosition = uCameraPosition + rayDirection * closest.distance;
22:     float receiverVoxelSize = uChunkVoxelSizes[closestChunkIndex];
23:     vec3 radiance = shadeVoxel(
24:         closest, worldPosition, receiverVoxelSize, closestChunkIndex
25:     );
26:     radiance = applyDistanceFog(
27:         radiance, uFogColor, closest.distance, uFogStart, uFogDensity
28:     );
29:     vec3 displayColor = encodeDisplayColor(radiance);
30:     if (uDitherEnabled == 1) {
31:         displayColor += (ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) - 0.5) * (1.0 / 255.0);
32:     }
33:     fragColor = vec4(clamp(displayColor, 0.0, 1.0), 1.0);
34: }
35: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/select_nearest_voxel_hit.rs
````rust
 1: //! Trace every candidate chunk interval and retain the nearest solid voxel.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: VoxelHit selectNearestVoxelHit(
 5:     vec3 rayDirection,
 6:     ChunkInterval intervals[25],
 7:     int intervalCount,
 8:     out int closestChunkIndex
 9: ) {
10:     VoxelHit closest = VoxelHit(
11:         false, TRACE_INFINITY, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u
12:     );
13:     closestChunkIndex = -1;
14:     for (int intervalIndex = 0; intervalIndex < intervalCount; ++intervalIndex) {
15:         ChunkInterval interval = intervals[intervalIndex];
16:         // Sorted traversal may stop only after every remaining AABB begins
17:         // beyond the nearest solid hit. Breaking after the first hit is wrong
18:         // because power-of-two padded chunk boxes overlap.
19:         if (uFrontToBackEnabled == 1 && interval.entry >= closest.distance) break;
20: 
21:         int chunkIndex = interval.chunkIndex;
22:         vec3 localOrigin = uCameraPosition - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
23:         RayBoxHit box = RayBoxHit(
24:             true, interval.entry, interval.exit, interval.entryNormal
25:         );
26:         VoxelHit candidate = traceChunk(
27:             localOrigin,
28:             rayDirection,
29:             uChunkRootIndices[chunkIndex],
30:             uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex],
31:             uChunkVoxelSizes[chunkIndex],
32:             uChunkDepths[chunkIndex],
33:             box
34:         );
35:         if (candidate.hit && candidate.distance < closest.distance) {
36:             closest = candidate;
37:             closestChunkIndex = chunkIndex;
38:         }
39:     }
40:     return closest;
41: }
42: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/trace_voxel_scene/trace_direct_light_visibility.rs
````rust
  1: //! Occlusion queries from a visible voxel face to analytic emitter samples.
  2: //!
  3: //! The primary-ray hit and every shadow segment use the same chunk slabs,
  4: //! stateless SVO lookup, and selected stepping policy. Rectangle visibility
  5: //! is evaluated at the same four Gauss samples as its irradiance integral;
  6: //! a center-only visibility term would leak around partial blockers.
  7: 
  8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
  9: bool directSampleIsVisible(
 10:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 11:     vec3 surfaceNormal,
 12:     vec3 samplePosition,
 13:     float receiverVoxelSize
 14: ) {
 15:     if (uDirectVisibilityEnabled == 0) return true;
 16: 
 17:     float bias = max(receiverVoxelSize * 1e-3, 1e-5);
 18:     vec3 segmentOrigin = surfacePosition + surfaceNormal * bias;
 19:     vec3 segment = samplePosition - segmentOrigin;
 20:     float segmentLength = length(segment);
 21:     if (!(segmentLength > bias * 2.0)) return true;
 22:     vec3 direction = segment / segmentLength;
 23:     float blockerLimit = segmentLength - bias * 2.0;
 24: 
 25:     for (int chunkIndex = 0; chunkIndex < uNumChunks; ++chunkIndex) {
 26:         vec3 localOrigin = segmentOrigin - uChunkOrigins[chunkIndex];
 27:         RayBoxHit box = intersectBox(
 28:             localOrigin,
 29:             direction,
 30:             vec3(0.0),
 31:             vec3(uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex])
 32:         );
 33:         if (!box.hit || box.entry >= blockerLimit) continue;
 34:         box.exit = min(box.exit, blockerLimit);
 35:         VoxelHit blocker = traceChunk(
 36:             localOrigin,
 37:             direction,
 38:             uChunkRootIndices[chunkIndex],
 39:             uChunkWorldSizes[chunkIndex],
 40:             uChunkVoxelSizes[chunkIndex],
 41:             uChunkDepths[chunkIndex],
 42:             box
 43:         );
 44:         if (blocker.hit && blocker.distance < blockerLimit) return false;
 45:     }
 46:     return true;
 47: }
 48: 
 49: vec3 evaluateVisiblePointLight(
 50:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 51:     vec3 normal,
 52:     vec3 lightPosition,
 53:     vec3 lightColor,
 54:     float range,
 55:     float intensity,
 56:     float receiverVoxelSize
 57: ) {
 58:     vec3 delta = lightPosition - surfacePosition;
 59:     float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
 60:     vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
 61:     float weight = finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, range)
 62:         * receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight);
 63:     if (!(weight > 0.0)
 64:         || !directSampleIsVisible(
 65:             surfacePosition, normal, lightPosition, receiverVoxelSize
 66:         )) {
 67:         return vec3(0.0);
 68:     }
 69:     return max(lightColor, vec3(0.0)) * max(intensity, 0.0) * weight;
 70: }
 71: 
 72: vec3 evaluateVisibleSceneLight(
 73:     vec3 surfacePosition,
 74:     vec3 normal,
 75:     SceneLight light,
 76:     float receiverVoxelSize
 77: ) {
 78:     if (light.kind == LIGHT_POINT) {
 79:         return evaluateVisiblePointLight(
 80:             surfacePosition, normal, light.position, light.color,
 81:             light.range, light.intensity, receiverVoxelSize
 82:         );
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     float area = 4.0 * max(light.halfSize.x, 0.0) * max(light.halfSize.y, 0.0);
 86:     if (!(area > 0.0)) return vec3(0.0);
 87:     const float GAUSS = 0.5773502691896258;
 88:     vec2 offsets[4] = vec2[](
 89:         vec2(-GAUSS, -GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS, -GAUSS),
 90:         vec2(-GAUSS,  GAUSS), vec2(GAUSS,  GAUSS)
 91:     );
 92:     float integral = 0.0;
 93:     for (int sampleIndex = 0; sampleIndex < 4; ++sampleIndex) {
 94:         vec2 offset = offsets[sampleIndex] * light.halfSize;
 95:         vec3 samplePosition = light.position + vec3(offset.x, 0.0, offset.y);
 96:         vec3 delta = samplePosition - surfacePosition;
 97:         float distanceSquared = dot(delta, delta);
 98:         vec3 surfaceToLight = delta * inversesqrt(max(distanceSquared, 1e-8));
 99:         float weight = finiteRangeInverseSquare(distanceSquared, light.range)
100:             * receiverCosine(normal, surfaceToLight)
101:             * emitterCosine(light.kind, surfaceToLight);
102:         if (weight > 0.0
103:             && directSampleIsVisible(
104:                 surfacePosition, normal, samplePosition, receiverVoxelSize
105:             )) {
106:             integral += weight;
107:         }
108:     }
109:     return max(light.color, vec3(0.0)) * max(light.intensity, 0.0)
110:         * area * (integral * 0.25);
111: }
112: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/apply_distance_fog.rs
````rust
 1: //! Homogeneous distance fog shared by every new GPU path.
 2: //!
 3: //! This is deliberately one equation, not an art-effect stack. For an
 4: //! extinction coefficient `sigma` and travelled distance `d`, Beer–Lambert
 5: //! transmittance is `T = exp(-sigma * d)`. Medium radiance fills exactly the
 6: //! energy removed from the surface term.
 7: 
 8: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 9: float fogTransmittance(float distanceToCamera, float fogStart, float sigmaExtinction) {
10:     float distanceInMedium = max(distanceToCamera - max(fogStart, 0.0), 0.0);
11:     return exp(-max(sigmaExtinction, 0.0) * distanceInMedium);
12: }
13: 
14: vec3 applyDistanceFog(
15:     vec3 surfaceRadiance,
16:     vec3 mediumRadiance,
17:     float distanceToCamera,
18:     float fogStart,
19:     float sigmaExtinction
20: ) {
21:     float transmittance = fogTransmittance(distanceToCamera, fogStart, sigmaExtinction);
22:     return surfaceRadiance * transmittance + mediumRadiance * (1.0 - transmittance);
23: }
24: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/encode_display_color.rs
````rust
 1: //! One linear-HDR to canvas conversion for surfaces and raymarching.
 2: 
 3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
 4: vec3 srgbToLinear(vec3 encoded) {
 5:     vec3 lowPart = encoded / 12.92;
 6:     vec3 highPart = pow((encoded + 0.055) / 1.055, vec3(2.4));
 7:     return mix(lowPart, highPart, step(vec3(0.04045), encoded));
 8: }
 9: 
10: vec3 linearToSrgb(vec3 linearColor) {
11:     linearColor = max(linearColor, vec3(0.0));
12:     vec3 lowPart = linearColor * 12.92;
13:     vec3 highPart = 1.055 * pow(linearColor, vec3(1.0 / 2.4)) - 0.055;
14:     return mix(lowPart, highPart, step(vec3(0.0031308), linearColor));
15: }
16: 
17: vec3 encodeDisplayColor(vec3 radiance) {
18:     // A monotone, channel-independent Reinhard curve. Lighting and fog are
19:     // composed before this point in linear space.
20:     vec3 mapped = max(radiance, vec3(0.0)) / (vec3(1.0) + max(radiance, vec3(0.0)));
21:     return linearToSrgb(mapped);
22: }
23: "#;
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/supply_labels.rs
````rust
 1: //! Billboard pass for supply-item product labels.
 2: //!
 3: //! Each sprite is one camera-facing (cylindrical: yaw only, world-up locked)
 4: //! textured quad expanded entirely in the vertex shader from `gl_VertexID`,
 5: //! so the pass needs no vertex buffers at all. The atlas stacks one product
 6: //! logo per row; alpha cutout keeps the pass depth-tested and order-free.
 7: 
 8: use super::chunks;
 9: 
10: /// Matches `application::ports::MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES`.
11: pub const MAX_SPRITES: usize = 16;
12: /// Label quad half-extents in world units (matches the 4:3 label art).
13: pub const HALF_WIDTH: f32 = 0.26;
14: pub const HALF_HEIGHT: f32 = 0.195;
15: /// Atlas rows available to `SupplySprite::atlas_row`.
16: pub const ATLAS_ROWS: f32 = 2.0;
17: 
18: pub const VERTEX_SHADER: &str = r#"#version 300 es
19: precision highp float;
20: 
21: uniform mat4 uProjection;
22: uniform mat4 uView;
23: // xyz = world center of the label, w = atlas row.
24: uniform vec4 uSprites[16];
25: // Ground-plane camera right: the quad turns with the player's yaw and
26: // never tilts, like a stand-up card.
27: uniform vec3 uCamRight;
28: uniform vec2 uHalfSize;
29: 
30: out vec2 vUv;
31: flat out float vRow;
32: out vec3 vWorld;
33: 
34: const vec2 CORNERS[6] = vec2[6](
35:     vec2(-1.0, -1.0), vec2(1.0, -1.0), vec2(1.0, 1.0),
36:     vec2(-1.0, -1.0), vec2(1.0, 1.0), vec2(-1.0, 1.0)
37: );
38: 
39: void main() {
40:     int sprite = gl_VertexID / 6;
41:     vec2 corner = CORNERS[gl_VertexID % 6];
42:     vec4 s = uSprites[sprite];
43:     vec3 world = s.xyz
44:         + uCamRight * (corner.x * uHalfSize.x)
45:         + vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) * (corner.y * uHalfSize.y);
46:     vUv = vec2(corner.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - corner.y * 0.5);
47:     vRow = s.w;
48:     vWorld = world;
49:     gl_Position = uProjection * uView * vec4(world, 1.0);
50: }
51: "#;
52: 
53: pub fn fragment_source() -> String {
54:     let mut source = String::from(
55:         r#"#version 300 es
56: precision highp float;
57: 
58: in vec2 vUv;
59: flat in float vRow;
60: in vec3 vWorld;
61: 
62: uniform sampler2D uAtlas;
63: uniform vec3 uCameraPosition;
64: uniform vec3 uFogColor;
65: uniform float uFogDensity;
66: uniform float uFogStart;
67: 
68: out vec4 outColor;
69: "#,
70:     );
71:     source.push_str(chunks::TONE_MAP_GLSL);
72:     source.push_str(
73:         r#"
74: void main() {
75:     vec2 uv = vec2(vUv.x, (vUv.y + vRow) / 2.0);
76:     vec4 label = texture(uAtlas, uv);
77:     if (label.a < 0.5) discard;
78: 
79:     // Printed matter under ambient interior light, then the shared fog.
80:     vec3 color = label.rgb * 0.92;
81:     float dist = length(vWorld - uCameraPosition);
82:     float fog = 1.0 - exp(-uFogDensity * max(dist - uFogStart, 0.0));
83:     color = mix(color, uFogColor, clamp(fog, 0.0, 1.0));
84:     outColor = vec4(toneMap(color), 1.0);
85: }
86: "#,
87:     );
88:     source
89: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Instanced face-splat renderer — the GPU microvoxel path.
  2: //!
  3: //! One instance is one error-selected, axis-aligned surface rectangle. The
  4: //! vertex shader reconstructs its quad and evaluates lighting once per face;
  5: //! the fragment shader is deliberately limited to fog, grain, and tone
  6: //! mapping. Chunk uploads are incremental, so steady-state frames only cull
  7: //! contiguous instance ranges and submit draws.

  9: //! The module is split by responsibility:
 10: //!
 11: //! * this file owns composition, profile settings, programs, and uniforms;
 12: //! * [`resources`] owns per-chunk GPU buffers and textures;
 13: //! * [`draw`] owns the frame pipeline and renderer-port implementation.

129: impl SplatRenderer {
130:     pub fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement, profile: SplatProfile) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
131:         let gl = create_context(canvas, ContextOptions { depth: true })?;
132: 
133:         let vertex_source = splat::vertex_source();
134:         let fragment_source = splat::fragment_source();
135:         let program = link_program(&gl, &vertex_source, &fragment_source)?;
136:         let uniforms = Uniforms {
137:             projection: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uProjection"),
138:             view: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uView"),
139:             chunk_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uChunkOrigin"),
140:             chunk_size: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uChunkSize"),
141:             voxel_scale: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uVoxelScale"),
142:             camera_position: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCameraPosition"),
143:             cam_forward: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCamForward"),
144:             flashlight: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFlashlightEnabled"),
145:             dither: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uDitherEnabled"),
146:             light_volume: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightVolume"),
147:             light_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightCount"),
148:             light_positions: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightPositions"),
149:             light_colors: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightColors"),
150:             light_params: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightParams"),
151:             core_count: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCoreCount"),
152:             cores: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCores"),
153:             core_colors: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uCoreColors"),
154:             shadow_map: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowMap"),
155:             light_view_proj: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uLightViewProjection"),
156:             shadowed_light_index: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowedLightIndex"),
157:             shadow_taps: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uShadowTaps"),
158:             outdoor: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uOutdoor"),
159:             fog_color: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uFogColor"),
160:             ambient_scale: gl.get_uniform_location(&program, "uAmbientScale"),
161:         };
162:         let attribs = InstanceAttribs::resolve(&gl, &program)?;
163: 
164:         let shadow_program = link_program(&gl, shadow::VERTEX_SHADER, shadow::FRAGMENT_SHADER)?;
165:         let shadow_uniforms = ShadowUniforms {
166:             light_view_proj: gl.get_uniform_location(&shadow_program, "uLightViewProjection"),
167:             chunk_origin: gl.get_uniform_location(&shadow_program, "uChunkOrigin"),
168:         };
169:         let shadow = create_shadow_target(&gl, profile.shadow_map_size)?;
170:         let timer = GpuFrameTimer::new(&gl);
171: 
172:         Ok(Self {
173:             gl,
174:             program,
175:             uniforms,
176:             attribs,
177:             shadow_program,
178:             shadow_uniforms,
179:             shadow,
180:             profile,
181:             chunks: HashMap::new(),
182:             width: canvas.width() as i32,
183:             height: canvas.height() as i32,
184:             timer,
185:             stats: FrameStats::default(),
186:         })
187:     }

189:     /// Updates the backing-store viewport dimensions after adaptive scaling
190:     /// or a browser resize. GPU resources are resolution-independent.
191:     pub fn resize(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32) {
192:         self.width = width as i32;
193:         self.height = height as i32;
````
