````rust
  1: //! Per-chunk GPU resources for the face-splat renderer.
  2: //!
  3: //! A chunk owns two representations derived from the same surface payload:
  4: //!
  5: //! * one packed instance page for the visible splat pass;
  6: //! * one retained greedy mesh used only as the hero-light shadow caster.
  7: //!
  8: //! WebGL2 has no `baseInstance`, so a cell-range draw re-points the four
  9: //! instance attributes at that range's byte offset before submission.
 10: 
 11: use js_sys::{Uint8Array, Uint32Array};
 12: use wasm_bindgen::JsValue;
 13: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlBuffer, WebGlProgram, WebGlVertexArrayObject};
 14: 
 15: use crate::application::ports::{FaceCellRange, SurfaceChunk};
 16: use crate::drivers::gl::light_volume::upload_light_volume;
 17: 
 18: use super::SplatRenderer;
 19: 
 20: /// Bytes per packed face instance uploaded to WebGL.
 21: pub(crate) const INSTANCE_STRIDE: i32 = 16;
 22: const SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE: i32 = 10;
 23: 
 24: /// Attribute locations are resolved once because every chunk uses the same
 25: /// packed instance layout.
 26: pub(crate) struct InstanceAttribs {
 27:     pos: u32,
 28:     extents: u32,
 29:     meta: u32,
 30:     flags: u32,
 31: }
 32: 
 33: impl InstanceAttribs {
 34:     pub(crate) fn resolve(gl: &Gl, program: &WebGlProgram) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 35:         let lookup = |name: &str| -> Result<u32, JsValue> {
 36:             let location = gl.get_attrib_location(program, name);
 37:             if location < 0 {
 38:                 return Err(JsValue::from_str(&format!("splat shader lost {name}")));
 39:             }
 40:             Ok(location as u32)
 41:         };
 42: 
 43:         Ok(Self {
 44:             pos: lookup("aFacePos")?,
 45:             extents: lookup("aFaceExtents")?,
 46:             meta: lookup("aFaceMeta")?,
 47:             flags: lookup("aFaceFlags")?,
 48:         })
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     fn enable(&self, gl: &Gl) {
 52:         for location in [self.pos, self.extents, self.meta, self.flags] {
 53:             gl.enable_vertex_attrib_array(location);
 54:             gl.vertex_attrib_divisor(location, 1);
 55:         }
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     /// Records attribute pointers for a range beginning at `first_instance`.
 59:     /// The caller must have the chunk VAO and its instance buffer bound.
 60:     pub(crate) fn point_at(&self, gl: &Gl, first_instance: u32) {
 61:         let base = first_instance as i32 * INSTANCE_STRIDE;
 62:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 63:             self.pos,
 64:             3,
 65:             Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT,
 66:             false,
 67:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 68:             base,
 69:         );
 70:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 71:             self.extents,
 72:             2,
 73:             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
 74:             false,
 75:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 76:             base + 6,
 77:         );
 78:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 79:             self.meta,
 80:             4,
 81:             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
 82:             false,
 83:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 84:             base + 8,
 85:         );
 86:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(
 87:             self.flags,
 88:             1,
 89:             Gl::UNSIGNED_BYTE,
 90:             false,
 91:             INSTANCE_STRIDE,
 92:             base + 12,
 93:         );
 94:     }
 95: }
 96: 
 97: /// All GPU and frame-selection data owned by one resident chunk.
 98: pub(crate) struct SplatChunk {
 99:     pub instance_vao: WebGlVertexArrayObject,
100:     pub instance_buffer: WebGlBuffer,
101:     pub instance_count: i32,
102:     pub cells: Vec<FaceCellRange>,
103:     pub cell_size: f32,
104:     pub voxel_scale: f32,
105:     pub shadow_vao: WebGlVertexArrayObject,
106:     pub shadow_vertex_buffer: WebGlBuffer,
107:     pub shadow_index_buffer: WebGlBuffer,
108:     pub shadow_index_count: i32,
109:     pub origin: [f32; 3],
110:     pub bounds_max: [f32; 3],
111:     pub light_texture: web_sys::WebGlTexture,
112: }
113: 
114: impl SplatRenderer {
115:     pub(crate) fn destroy_chunk(&self, chunk: SplatChunk) {
116:         let gl = &self.gl;
117:         gl.delete_vertex_array(Some(&chunk.instance_vao));
118:         gl.delete_buffer(Some(&chunk.instance_buffer));
119:         gl.delete_vertex_array(Some(&chunk.shadow_vao));
120:         gl.delete_buffer(Some(&chunk.shadow_vertex_buffer));
121:         gl.delete_buffer(Some(&chunk.shadow_index_buffer));
122:         gl.delete_texture(Some(&chunk.light_texture));
123:     }
124: 
125:     pub(crate) fn upload_surface(&mut self, chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>) {
126:         if let Some(old) = self.chunks.remove(&chunk.key) {
127:             self.destroy_chunk(old);
128:         }
129:         if chunk.mesh.faces.instances.is_empty() {
130:             return;
131:         }
132: 
133:         let (instance_vao, instance_buffer) = self.upload_instance_page(chunk);
134:         let (shadow_vao, shadow_vertex_buffer, shadow_index_buffer) =
135:             self.upload_shadow_mesh(chunk);
136:         let light_texture =
137:             upload_light_volume(&self.gl, chunk.mesh).expect("upload splat light volume");
138: 
139:         self.chunks.insert(
140:             chunk.key,
141:             SplatChunk {
142:                 instance_vao,
143:                 instance_buffer,
144:                 instance_count: chunk.mesh.faces.instances.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
145:                 cells: chunk.mesh.faces.cells.clone(),
146:                 cell_size: chunk.mesh.faces.cell_size,
147:                 voxel_scale: chunk.mesh.voxel_scale,
148:                 shadow_vao,
149:                 shadow_vertex_buffer,
150:                 shadow_index_buffer,
151:                 shadow_index_count: chunk.mesh.indices.len().min(i32::MAX as usize) as i32,
152:                 origin: chunk.origin,
153:                 bounds_max: chunk.mesh.bounds.max,
154:                 light_texture,
155: 
156:             },
157:         );
158:     }
159: 
160:     fn upload_instance_page(
161:         &self,
162:         chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>,
163:     ) -> (WebGlVertexArrayObject, WebGlBuffer) {
164:         let gl = &self.gl;
165:         let vao = gl.create_vertex_array().expect("create splat VAO");
166:         let buffer = gl.create_buffer().expect("create splat instance buffer");
167:         let packed = pack_instances(chunk);
168: 
169:         gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&vao));
170:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, Some(&buffer));
171:         let bytes = Uint8Array::from(packed.as_slice());
172:         gl.buffer_data_with_array_buffer_view(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, &bytes, Gl::STATIC_DRAW);
173:         self.attribs.enable(gl);
174:         self.attribs.point_at(gl, 0);
175:         gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
176:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, None);
177: 
178:         (vao, buffer)
179:     }
180: 
181:     fn upload_shadow_mesh(
182:         &self,
183:         chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>,
184:     ) -> (WebGlVertexArrayObject, WebGlBuffer, WebGlBuffer) {
185:         let gl = &self.gl;
186:         let vao = gl.create_vertex_array().expect("create splat shadow VAO");
187:         let vertex_buffer = gl
188:             .create_buffer()
189:             .expect("create splat shadow vertex buffer");
190:         let index_buffer = gl
191:             .create_buffer()
192:             .expect("create splat shadow index buffer");
193:         let packed_vertices = pack_shadow_vertices(chunk);
194: 
195:         gl.bind_vertex_array(Some(&vao));
196:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, Some(&vertex_buffer));
197:         let vertices = Uint8Array::from(packed_vertices.as_slice());
198:         gl.buffer_data_with_array_buffer_view(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, &vertices, Gl::STATIC_DRAW);
199: 
200:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, Some(&index_buffer));
201:         let indices = Uint32Array::from(chunk.mesh.indices.as_slice());
202:         gl.buffer_data_with_array_buffer_view(Gl::ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, &indices, Gl::STATIC_DRAW);
203: 
204:         // The shared shadow shader declares `aPosition` at location zero.
205:         gl.enable_vertex_attrib_array(0);
206:         gl.vertex_attrib_pointer_with_i32(0, 3, Gl::UNSIGNED_SHORT, false, SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE, 0);
207:         gl.bind_vertex_array(None);
208:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ARRAY_BUFFER, None);
209:         gl.bind_buffer(Gl::ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, None);
210: 
211:         (vao, vertex_buffer, index_buffer)
212:     }
213: }
214: 
215: /// Serializes `PackedFaceInstance` explicitly so the GPU layout is stable
216: /// across Rust compiler versions and host alignment rules.
217: fn pack_instances(chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>) -> Vec<u8> {
218:     let instances = &chunk.mesh.faces.instances;
219:     let mut packed = Vec::with_capacity(instances.len() * INSTANCE_STRIDE as usize);
220:     for instance in instances {
221:         packed.extend_from_slice(&instance.position[0].to_le_bytes());
222:         packed.extend_from_slice(&instance.position[1].to_le_bytes());
223:         packed.extend_from_slice(&instance.position[2].to_le_bytes());
224:         packed.push(instance.extent_u);
225:         packed.push(instance.extent_v);
226:         packed.push(instance.normal_axis);
227:         packed.push(instance.material);
228:         packed.push(instance.baked_light);
229:         packed.push(instance.ao);
230:         packed.push(instance.flags);
231:         packed.extend_from_slice(&[0, 0, 0]);
232:     }
233:     packed
234: }
235: 
236: /// Serializes the retained 10-byte greedy-mesh vertices. Only position is
237: /// consumed in the shadow pass, but retaining the canonical stride keeps the
238: /// caster byte-for-byte aligned with the visible surface representation.
239: fn pack_shadow_vertices(chunk: SurfaceChunk<'_>) -> Vec<u8> {
240:     let mut packed = Vec::with_capacity(chunk.mesh.vertices.len() * SHADOW_VERTEX_STRIDE as usize);
241:     for vertex in &chunk.mesh.vertices {
242:         packed.extend_from_slice(&vertex.position[0].to_le_bytes());
243:         packed.extend_from_slice(&vertex.position[1].to_le_bytes());
244:         packed.extend_from_slice(&vertex.position[2].to_le_bytes());
245:         packed.extend_from_slice(&[
246:             vertex.normal_axis,
247:             vertex.material,
248:             vertex.static_indirect,
249:             vertex.ao,
250:         ]);
251:     }
252:     packed
253: }
````

````rust
  1: //! RGBA32UI SVO node-atlas lifecycle.
  2: //!
  3: //! The serializer pads every atlas row to [`ATLAS_WIDTH`], which makes both a
  4: //! full replacement and an incremental row overwrite exact typed-array copies.
  5: 
  6: use web_sys::{WebGl2RenderingContext as Gl, WebGlTexture};
  7: 
  8: /// Must match the raymarch shader's node-index decoder and the core
  9: /// `OctreeGpuSerializer` row padding.
 10: const ATLAS_WIDTH: i32 = 1024;
 11: 
 12: pub(super) struct AtlasTexture {
 13:     texture: Option<WebGlTexture>,
 14:     /// Allocated atlas height, used to reject out-of-bounds row patches.
 15:     rows: i32,
 16: }
 17: 
 18: impl AtlasTexture {
 19:     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
 20:         Self {
 21:             texture: None,
 22:             rows: 0,
 23:         }
 24:     }
 25: 
 26:     /// Replaces the whole atlas. An empty stream intentionally releases the
 27:     /// previous texture so level transitions cannot sample stale nodes.
 28:     pub(super) fn replace(&mut self, gl: &Gl, texels: &[u32]) {
 29:         if let Some(old) = self.texture.take() {
 30:             gl.delete_texture(Some(&old));
 31:         }
 32:         self.rows = 0;
 33:         if texels.is_empty() {
 34:             return;
 35:         }
 36: 
 37:         debug_assert_eq!(texels.len() % 4, 0, "atlas texels are RGBA u32 values");
 38:         let texel_count = (texels.len() / 4) as i32;
 39:         let rows = (texel_count + ATLAS_WIDTH - 1) / ATLAS_WIDTH;
 40:         let texture = gl.create_texture().expect("create SVO atlas texture");
 41: 
 42:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Some(&texture));
 43:         gl.pixel_storei(Gl::UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
 44:         let view = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(texels);
 45:         gl.tex_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_i32_and_format_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
 46:             Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
 47:             0,
 48:             Gl::RGBA32UI as i32,
 49:             ATLAS_WIDTH,
 50:             rows,
 51:             0,
 52:             Gl::RGBA_INTEGER,
 53:             Gl::UNSIGNED_INT,
 54:             Some(&view),
 55:         )
 56:         .expect("SVO atlas texture upload failed");
 57:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 58:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, Gl::NEAREST as i32);
 59:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_S, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 60:         gl.tex_parameteri(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, Gl::TEXTURE_WRAP_T, Gl::CLAMP_TO_EDGE as i32);
 61:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 62: 
 63:         self.texture = Some(texture);
 64:         self.rows = rows;
 65:     }
 66: 
 67:     /// Patches complete atlas rows without reallocating the texture.
 68:     pub(super) fn update_rows(&mut self, gl: &Gl, first_row: u32, texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
 69:         let row_stride = 4 * ATLAS_WIDTH as usize;
 70:         let patch_rows = texels.len() / row_stride;
 71:         if self.texture.is_none()
 72:             || patch_rows == 0
 73:             || texels.len() % row_stride != 0
 74:             || first_row as i32 + patch_rows as i32 > self.rows
 75:         {
 76:             return false;
 77:         }
 78: 
 79:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, self.texture.as_ref());
 80:         let view = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(texels);
 81:         let uploaded = gl
 82:             .tex_sub_image_2d_with_i32_and_i32_and_u32_and_type_and_opt_array_buffer_view(
 83:                 Gl::TEXTURE_2D,
 84:                 0,
 85:                 0,
 86:                 first_row as i32,
 87:                 ATLAS_WIDTH,
 88:                 patch_rows as i32,
 89:                 Gl::RGBA_INTEGER,
 90:                 Gl::UNSIGNED_INT,
 91:                 Some(&view),
 92:             )
 93:             .is_ok();
 94:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, None);
 95:         uploaded
 96:     }
 97: 
 98:     pub(super) fn bind(&self, gl: &Gl) {
 99:         gl.bind_texture(Gl::TEXTURE_2D, self.texture.as_ref());
100:     }
101: }
````

````rust
 1: use crate::application::ports::{POSITION_FIXED_SCALE, SurfaceChunk};
 2: use crate::reference::artifact_sink::ArtifactSinkPort;
 3: use crate::reference::renderer::RenderedImage;
 4: use std::fs;
 5: use std::io::Write;
 6: use std::path::Path;
 7: 
 8: pub struct FsArtifactSink;
 9: 
10: impl ArtifactSinkPort for FsArtifactSink {
11:     fn write_png(&self, path: &Path, image: &RenderedImage) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {
12:         // Encode raw RGBA bytes into a PNG file.
13:         image::save_buffer(
14:             path,
15:             &image.rgba,
16:             image.width,
17:             image.height,
18:             image::ExtendedColorType::Rgba8,
19:         )
20:         .map_err(|error| std::io::Error::other(error.to_string()))
21:     }
22: 
23:     fn write_obj(&self, path: &Path, chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {
24:         let mut file = fs::File::create(path)?;
25: 
26:         writeln!(file, "o backrooms_scene")?;
27: 
28:         let mut vertex_offset = 1; // OBJ indices are 1-based
29: 
30:         for chunk in chunks {
31:             writeln!(file, "g chunk_{}_{}", chunk.key.0, chunk.key.1)?;
32: 
33:             for v in &chunk.mesh.vertices {
34:                 let px = (v.position[0] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[0];
35:                 let py = (v.position[1] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[1];
36:                 let pz = (v.position[2] as f32 / POSITION_FIXED_SCALE) + chunk.origin[2];
37:                 writeln!(file, "v {:.6} {:.6} {:.6}", px, py, pz)?;
38:             }
39: 
40:             let mut i = 0;
41:             while i + 2 < chunk.mesh.indices.len() {
42:                 let i1 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i] as usize) + vertex_offset;
43:                 let i2 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i + 1] as usize) + vertex_offset;
44:                 let i3 = (chunk.mesh.indices[i + 2] as usize) + vertex_offset;
45:                 writeln!(file, "f {} {} {}", i1, i2, i3)?;
46:                 i += 3;
47:             }
48: 
49:             vertex_offset += chunk.mesh.vertices.len();
50:         }
51: 
52:         Ok(())
53:     }
54: }
````

````toml
 3: #                     plus the native dev server binary (Frameworks & Drivers).
 4: #                     The library is platform-agnostic and also compiles to wasm32.

 6: #                     shell; the same pipelines run headlessly on Vulkan/

15: edition = "2024"

19: # every RNG in the engine is deterministically seeded (StdRng::seed_from_u64),
````

````rust
 35:             color: 0,
 36:             light_rgb: [0; 3],
 37:             face_occlusion: 0,
 38:         };
 39:         Self {
 40:             root: 0,
 41:             nodes: vec![root_node],
 42:             depth,
 43:             world_size,
 44:         }
 45:     }
 46: 
 47:     /// Checks if the SVO is entirely empty (air).
 48:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 49:         match self.nodes[self.root] {
 50:             SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => voxel_type == 0,
 51:             SvoNode::Internal { child_mask, .. } => child_mask == 0,
 52:         }
 53:     }
 54: 
 55:     /// Queries the SVO for voxel attributes at integer coordinates `(x, y, z)`.
 56:     pub fn get(&self, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> Option<(u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8)> {
 57:         let max_coord = 1 << self.depth;
 58:         if x >= max_coord || y >= max_coord || z >= max_coord {
 59:             return None;
 60:         }
 61:         self.get_recursive(self.root, x, y, z, self.depth)
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     fn get_recursive(
 65:         &self,
 66:         node_idx: usize,
 67:         x: u32,
 68:         y: u32,
 69:         z: u32,
 70:         depth: u32,
 71:     ) -> Option<(u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8)> {
 72:         if node_idx >= self.nodes.len() {
 73:             return None;
 74:         }
 75: 
 76:         match self.nodes[node_idx] {
 77:             SvoNode::Leaf {
 78:                 voxel_type,
 79:                 color,
 80:                 light_rgb,
 81:                 face_occlusion,
 82:             } => Some((voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion)),
 83:             SvoNode::Internal {
 84:                 child_base_index,
 85:                 child_mask,
 86:             } => {
 87:                 if depth == 0 {
 88:                     return None;
 89:                 }
 90: 
 91:                 let bit = depth - 1;
 92:                 let octant_x = (x >> bit) & 1;
 93:                 let octant_y = (y >> bit) & 1;
 94:                 let octant_z = (z >> bit) & 1;
 95:                 let octant_idx = (octant_z << 2) | (octant_y << 1) | octant_x;
 96: 
 97:                 // Check if the octant is active in the child mask
 98:                 if (child_mask & (1 << octant_idx)) == 0 {
 99:                     return Some((0, 0, [0; 3], 0)); // Empty air
100:                 }
101: 
102:                 let child_node_idx = child_base_index as usize + octant_idx as usize;
103:                 let mask = (1 << bit) - 1;
104:                 self.get_recursive(child_node_idx, x & mask, y & mask, z & mask, depth - 1)
105:             }
106:         }
107:     }
108: 
109:     /// Sets voxel attributes at coordinate `(x, y, z)`. Splits nodes and collapses uniform subtrees recursively.
110:     pub fn set(
111:         &mut self,
112:         x: u32,
113:         y: u32,
114:         z: u32,
115:         voxel_type: u8,
116:         color: u32,
117:         light_rgb: [u8; 3],
118:         face_occlusion: u8,
119:     ) {
120:         let max_coord = 1 << self.depth;
121:         if x >= max_coord || y >= max_coord || z >= max_coord {
122:             return;
123:         }
124:         self.set_recursive(
125:             self.root,
126:             x,
127:             y,
128:             z,
129:             self.depth,
130:             voxel_type,
131:             color,
132:             light_rgb,
133:             face_occlusion,
134:         );
135:     }
136: 
137:     fn set_recursive(
138:         &mut self,
139:         node_idx: usize,
140:         x: u32,
141:         y: u32,
142:         z: u32,
143:         depth: u32,
144:         v_type: u8,
145:         col: u32,
146:         ll: [u8; 3],
147:         fo: u8,
148:     ) {
149:         match self.nodes[node_idx] {
150:             SvoNode::Leaf {
151:                 voxel_type,
152:                 color,
153:                 light_rgb,
154:                 face_occlusion,
155:             } => {
156:                 if voxel_type == v_type && color == col && light_rgb == ll && face_occlusion == fo {
157:                     return;
158:                 }
159: 
160:                 if depth == 0 {
161:                     self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Leaf {
162:                         voxel_type: v_type,
163:                         color: col,
164:                         light_rgb: ll,
165:                         face_occlusion: fo,
166:                     };
167:                     return;
168:                 }
169: 
170:                 // Split leaf node
171:                 let child_base_index = self.nodes.len() as u32;
172:                 let child_mask = if voxel_type == 0 { 0 } else { 0xFF };
173: 
174:                 for _ in 0..8 {
175:                     self.nodes.push(SvoNode::Leaf {
176:                         voxel_type,
177:                         color,
178:                         light_rgb,
179:                         face_occlusion,
180:                     });
181:                 }
182: 
183:                 self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Internal {
184:                     child_base_index,
185:                     child_mask,
186:                 };
187: 
188:                 self.set_recursive(node_idx, x, y, z, depth, v_type, col, ll, fo);
189:             }
190:             SvoNode::Internal {
191:                 child_base_index,
192:                 mut child_mask,
193:             } => {
194:                 let bit = depth - 1;
195:                 let octant_x = (x >> bit) & 1;
196:                 let octant_y = (y >> bit) & 1;
197:                 let octant_z = (z >> bit) & 1;
198:                 let octant_idx = (octant_z << 2) | (octant_y << 1) | octant_x;
199: 
200:                 let child_node_idx = child_base_index as usize + octant_idx as usize;
201: 
202:                 if v_type != 0 {
203:                     child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
204:                 }
205: 
206:                 self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Internal {
207:                     child_base_index,
208:                     child_mask,
209:                 };
210: 
211:                 let mask = (1 << bit) - 1;
212:                 self.set_recursive(
213:                     child_node_idx,
214:                     x & mask,
215:                     y & mask,
216:                     z & mask,
217:                     depth - 1,
218:                     v_type,
219:                     col,
220:                     ll,
221:                     fo,
222:                 );
223: 
224:                 // Try to collapse
225:                 self.collapse_if_uniform(node_idx);
226:             }
227:         }
228:     }
229: 
230:     fn collapse_if_uniform(&mut self, node_idx: usize) {
231:         if let SvoNode::Internal {
232:             child_base_index, ..
233:         } = self.nodes[node_idx]
234:         {
235:             let first_child_idx = child_base_index as usize;
236:             let mut uniform = true;
237:             let mut first_val = None;
238: 
239:             for i in 0..8 {
240:                 match self.nodes[first_child_idx + i] {
241:                     SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
242:                         uniform = false;
243:                         break;
244:                     }
245:                     SvoNode::Leaf {
246:                         voxel_type,
247:                         color,
248:                         light_rgb,
249:                         face_occlusion,
250:                     } => {
251:                         if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
252:                             if vt != voxel_type
253:                                 || col != color
254:                                 || ll != light_rgb
255:                                 || fo != face_occlusion
256:                             {
257:                                 uniform = false;
258:                                 break;
259:                             }
260:                         } else {
261:                             first_val = Some((voxel_type, color, light_rgb, face_occlusion));
262:                         }
263:                     }
264:                 }
265:             }
266: 
267:             if uniform {
268:                 if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
269:                     self.nodes[node_idx] = SvoNode::Leaf {
270:                         voxel_type: vt,
271:                         color: col,
272:                         light_rgb: ll,
273:                         face_occlusion: fo,
274:                     };
275:                 }
276:             }
277:         }
278:     }
279: }
````

````rust
 37: #[test]

 51: #[test]
 52: fn every_sector_keeps_the_ground_plane_walkable() {
 53:     // Flood-fill reachability over a 96u sector-sized window: from the
 54:     // arrival plaza, most open floor must be mutually reachable. Openings
 55:     // are >= 1 unit by construction (doorways 1.4u, lanes, bays).
 56:     let seed = 42;
 57:     let window = 96.0f32;
 58:     let cells = (window / SCAN_STEP) as usize;
 59:     let open = |ix: usize, iz: usize| -> bool {
 60:         let wx = ix as f32 * SCAN_STEP - window * 0.5;
 61:         let wz = iz as f32 * SCAN_STEP - window * 0.5;
 62:         let c = HabitableLevel::plan_column(seed, wx, wz);
 63:         !c.solid && c.floor_units < 0.5
 64:     };
 65:     let mut visited = vec![false; cells * cells];
 66:     let start = (cells / 2, cells / 2);
 67:     assert!(open(start.0, start.1), "arrival plaza must be open");
 68:     let mut stack = vec![start];
 69:     visited[start.1 * cells + start.0] = true;
 70:     let mut reached = 0usize;
 71:     while let Some((x, z)) = stack.pop() {
 72:         reached += 1;
 73:         let neighbors = [
 74:             (x.wrapping_sub(1), z),
 75:             (x + 1, z),
 76:             (x, z.wrapping_sub(1)),
 77:             (x, z + 1),
 78:         ];
 79:         for (nx, nz) in neighbors {
 80:             if nx < cells && nz < cells && !visited[nz * cells + nx] && open(nx, nz) {
 81:                 visited[nz * cells + nx] = true;
 82:                 stack.push((nx, nz));
 83:             }
 84:         }
 85:     }
 86:     let total_open = (0..cells * cells)
 87:         .filter(|i| open(i % cells, i / cells))
 88:         .count();
 89:     assert!(
 90:         reached * 100 >= total_open * 85,
 91:         "{reached} of {total_open} open columns reachable from the plaza"
 92:     );
 93: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Column composition: the one priority order in which Level 0's systems
  2: //! claim a world column. Circulation beats anomalies beats assemblies beats
  3: //! fabric — and archway anchors freeze every mutable family around them.
  4: 
  5: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyKind, RealitySnapshot};
  6: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::{
  7:     CirculationSpine, RegionPlan, SpaceProgram, StructuralSystemInstance,
  8: };
  9: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::geometry::sample_anomaly;
 10: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 11: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 12: use crate::use_cases::red_rooms::geometry::sample_red_room;
 13: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{PLAN_WALL_T, region_index, spawn_point};
 14: 
 15: use super::circulation_sampler::SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS;
 16: use super::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnPlan};
 17: 
 18: #[cfg(test)]
 19: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::LevelTuning;
 20: 
 21: impl BackroomsLevel {
 22: 
 23:     /// The architectural column plan: corridor beats assembly beats fabric.
 24:     #[cfg(test)]
 25:     pub(crate) fn plan_column(
 26:         plan: &RegionPlan,
 27:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 28:         seed: u32,
 29:         tuning: &LevelTuning,
 30:         wx: f32,
 31:         wz: f32,
 32:     ) -> ColumnPlan {
 33:         Self::plan_column_in_reality(
 34:             plan,
 35:             noise,
 36:             seed,
 37:             &GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_tuning(*tuning),
 38:             &RealitySnapshot::empty(),
 39:             wx,
 40:             wz,
 41:         )
 42:     }
 43: 
 44:     pub(crate) fn plan_column_in_reality(
 45:         plan: &RegionPlan,
 46:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 47:         seed: u32,
 48:         config: &GeneratorConfig,
 49:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 50:         wx: f32,
 51:         wz: f32,
 52:     ) -> ColumnPlan {
 53:         let tuning = &config.tuning;
 54:         // -- circulation ----------------------------------------------------
 55:         let mut in_corridor = false;
 56:         let mut corridor_ceiling = 0.0f32;
 57:         let mut corridor_light = false;
 58:         let mut corridor_wall = false;
 59:         // Edge-gap decisions are deferred: they read the Peripheral Shift,
 60:         // and whether this column's fabric is frozen (spawn radius, arch
 61:         // anchors) is only known further down.
 62:         let mut gap_probes: Vec<(&CirculationSpine, f32, bool)> = Vec::new();
 63:         for s in &plan.corridors {
 64:             let (d, along, is_horizontal) = s.nearest(wx, wz);
 65:             let half = s.width * 0.5;
 66:             if d <= half {
 67:                 in_corridor = true;
 68:                 corridor_ceiling =
 69:                     corridor_ceiling.max(Self::corridor_ceiling(s, noise, seed, wx, wz));
 70:                 // Light strip modules follow the corridor in world space.
 71:                 if d < 0.45 && along.rem_euclid(4.0) < 1.0 {
 72:                     corridor_light = true;
 73:                 }
 74:             } else if d <= half + PLAN_WALL_T {
 75:                 corridor_wall = true;
 76:                 corridor_ceiling =
 77:                     corridor_ceiling.max(Self::corridor_ceiling(s, noise, seed, wx, wz));
 78:                 gap_probes.push((s, along, is_horizontal));
 79:             }
 80:         }
 81:         if in_corridor {
 82:             let mut column = ColumnPlan {
 83:                 light: corridor_light && tuning.lights > 0.0,
 84:                 ..ColumnPlan::open(corridor_ceiling)
 85:             };
 86:             // Geometry priority and presentation priority are different
 87:             // things: the corridor owns passability — its route through a
 88:             // blackout stays carved open — but a blackout owns the *dark*.
 89:             // Past the approach band the corridor's light strips die like
 90:             // every other fixture, thinning through the same gradient, so
 91:             // circulation never reads as a lit tunnel through the anomaly.
 92:             if let Some(blackout) = plan
 93:                 .anomalies
 94:                 .iter()
 95:                 .find(|a| a.kind == AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse && a.contains(wx, wz))
 96:             {
 97:                 let depth = blackout.normalized_depth(wx, wz);
 98:                 if depth > 0.22 {
 99:                     column.light = false;
100:                 } else if depth > 0.0 && column.light {
101:                     let module = (wx.floor() as i64) ^ ((wz.floor() as i64) << 17);
102:                     let hash = {
103:                         let mut h = (blackout.id ^ module as u64)
104:                             .wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
105:                         h ^= h >> 33;
106:                         (h >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
107:                     };
108:                     column.light = hash < 1.0 - depth / 0.22;
109:                 }
110:             }
111:             return column;
112:         }
113: 
114:         // Archway anchors take precedence over every hostile family, and any
115:         // hostile column within an anchor's margin generates as if no epoch
116:         // had ever advanced: arch rooms and their surroundings are immune to
117:         // non-Euclidean transformation by construction, not by policy.
118:         if let Some(anchor) = plan
119:             .anomalies
120:             .iter()
121:             .find(|a| a.kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom && a.contains(wx, wz))
122:         {
123:             return sample_anomaly(anchor, noise, seed, config, reality, wx, wz);
124:         }
125:         let near_anchor = plan.anomalies.iter().any(|a| {
126:             a.kind == AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom
127:                 && a.footprint.bounds().expanded(3.2).contains(wx, wz)
128:         });
129: 
130:         if let Some(instance) = plan
131:             .anomalies
132:             .iter()
133:             .filter(|a| {
134:                 a.kind != AnomalyKind::RedRoom
135:                     && a.kind != AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom
136:                     && a.contains(wx, wz)
137:             })
138:             .max_by(|a, b| {
139:                 a.normalized_depth(wx, wz)
140:                     .total_cmp(&b.normalized_depth(wx, wz))
141:             })
142:         {
143:             let frozen = RealitySnapshot::empty();
144:             let effective_reality = if near_anchor { &frozen } else { reality };
145:             return sample_anomaly(instance, noise, seed, config, effective_reality, wx, wz);
146:         }
147: 
148:         // -- assemblies -------------------------------------------------------
149:         {
150:             let renovator_structure = plan.architects.get(1).map(|g| StructuralSystemInstance {
151:                 system: g.structural_system,
152:                 bay_x: 3.6,
153:                 bay_z: 4.4,
154:                 phase: (1.6, 2.4),
155:                 column_side: 0.4,
156:             });
157:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
158:                 let b = a.footprint.bounds();
159:                 let t = PLAN_WALL_T;
160:                 if wx < b.0 - t || wx > b.2 + t || wz < b.1 - t || wz > b.3 + t {
161:                     continue;
162:                 }
163:                 let inside = a.footprint.contains(wx, wz);
164:                 let mut base =
165:                     Self::assembly_column(a, inside, renovator_structure.as_ref(), tuning, wx, wz);
166:                 // A stair assembly shapes its interior as a flight: the
167:                 // vertical link that reserved it decides whether the flight
168:                 // lands or climbs endlessly. Stairs are architecture, so a
169:                 // walls=0 debug world flattens them along with everything.
170:                 if a.program == SpaceProgram::Stair && inside && !base.solid && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
171:                     let rx = region_index(plan.origin_world.x + 0.1);
172:                     let rz = region_index(plan.origin_world.z + 0.1);
173:                     let kind = crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region(
174:                         seed, noise, rx, rz,
175:                     )
176:                     .map(|link| link.kind)
177:                     .unwrap_or(
178:                         crate::domain::entities::world_topology::VerticalLinkKind::OrdinaryStair,
179:                     );
180:                     crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::apply_stair_profile(
181:                         a, kind, &mut base, wx, wz,
182:                     );
183:                 }
184:                 if a.corruption.red_room
185:                     && let Some(red) = plan.anomalies.iter().find(|r| {
186:                         r.kind == AnomalyKind::RedRoom
187:                             && r.footprint
188:                                 .bounds()
189:                                 .expanded(PLAN_WALL_T + 0.05)
190:                                 .contains(wx, wz)
191:                     })
192:                 {
193:                     return sample_red_room(red, base, config, reality, wx, wz);
194:                 }
195:                 return base;
196:             }
197:         }
198: 
199:         // -- the endless unplanned office fabric -------------------------------
200:         // Ordinary fabric is the Peripheral Shift's territory — with two
201:         // sanctuaries. Arch-anchor surroundings are immune by construction
202:         // (the same guarantee their hostile-family freeze gives above), and
203:         // the spawn opening sequence never rearranges: the first hallways a
204:         // wanderer learns are the last ones the level may take away.
205:         let sp = spawn_point(seed);
206:         let near_spawn = (wx - sp.x) * (wx - sp.x) + (wz - sp.z) * (wz - sp.z)
207:             < SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS * SPAWN_READABLE_RADIUS;
208:         let still_fabric = RealitySnapshot::empty();
209:         let fabric_reality = if near_anchor || near_spawn {
210:             &still_fabric
211:         } else {
212:             reality
213:         };
214: 
215:         // -- corridor edge walls through fabric -------------------------------
216:         // The mouths onto circulation drift and seal with the same reality
217:         // as the fabric they open into (frozen in the sanctuaries above).
218:         if corridor_wall && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
219:             let corridor_gap = gap_probes.iter().any(|&(s, along, is_horizontal)| {
220:                 Self::corridor_edge_opens(
221:                     s,
222:                     noise,
223:                     seed,
224:                     fabric_reality,
225:                     along,
226:                     is_horizontal,
227:                     wx,
228:                     wz,
229:                 )
230:             });
231:             if !corridor_gap {
232:                 return ColumnPlan {
233:                     solid: true,
234:                     ..ColumnPlan::open(corridor_ceiling.max(3.2))
235:                 };
236:             }
237:         }
238:         Self::column_plan_in_reality(noise, seed, tuning, fabric_reality, wx, wz)
239:     }
240: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/provisions.rs
````rust
  1: //! Level 0 provisions: scattered almond water and the rare physical door.
  2: //!
  3: //! Both are a deterministic post-pass over the already-voxelized chunk,
  4: //! derived purely from (seed, world lattice, reality). Supplies follow the
  5: //! 40u fabric-drift lattice; doors follow the 80u region lattice plus one
  6: //! authored door near spawn, so a fresh wanderer can always find Level 1.
  7: //! Red-room interiors and pit lattices never receive provisions: a sealed
  8: //! loop must stay barren, and nothing may hover over a pit.
  9: 
 10: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{AnomalyKind, LevelExit, RealitySnapshot};
 11: use crate::domain::entities::architecture::RegionPlan;
 12: use crate::domain::entities::supplies::{SupplyItem, SupplyKind};
 13: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_AIR, VOXEL_WALL, VoxelGrid};
 14: use crate::entities::models::Position;
 15: use crate::use_cases::anomalies::determinism::{hash, unit};
 16: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 17: use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_HABITABLE;
 18: use crate::use_cases::level_one::generate::{
 19:     ARRIVAL_POINT, DOOR_TRIGGER_HALF, stamp_level_door, stamp_supply_marker,
 20: };
 21: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 22: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::{REGION_SIZE, region_index};
 23: 
 24: use super::BackroomsLevel;
 25: 
 26: /// Supply lattice: one candidate per fabric-drift-sized cell.
 27: const SUPPLY_CELL: f32 = 40.0;
 28: /// Fraction of supply cells that roll a candidate spot. Each cell gets one
 29: /// deterministic spot (never a probe sequence, which would make placement
 30: /// depend on which chunk evaluates it); spots landing on solid columns are
 31: /// simply lost, so this is tuned above the desired field density.
 32: const ALMOND_CHANCE: f32 = 0.72;
 33: /// Of the successful cells, this fraction holds food instead of water.
 34: const RATION_SHARE: f32 = 0.25;
 35: 
 36: /// Fraction of 80u regions holding an organic door to Level 1 (at the
 37: /// default `level_doors` tuning of 1.0).
 38: const DOOR_CHANCE: f32 = 0.08;
 39: /// How far past its bounds a chunk stamps door geometry. Must stay within
 40: /// the region-plan window margin (1.0) and cover the frame plus clearing.
 41: const DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN: f32 = 1.0;
 42: /// The authored always-present door: guaranteed to exist, but a real hike
 43: /// from spawn — finding it should feel earned, not scripted. Debug runs
 44: /// raise `level_doors` (or walk straight here).
 45: const SPAWN_DOOR: (f32, f32) = (172.0, -116.0);
 46: 
 47: pub(crate) struct ProvisionContext<'a> {
 48:     pub seed: u32,
 49:     pub config: &'a GeneratorConfig,
 50:     pub reality: &'a RealitySnapshot,
 51:     pub noise: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
 52:     pub plans: &'a [((i64, i64), RegionPlan)],
 53: }
 54: 
 55: impl ProvisionContext<'_> {
 56:     fn plan_of(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> Option<&RegionPlan> {
 57:         let key = (region_index(wx), region_index(wz));
 58:         self.plans
 59:             .iter()
 60:             .find(|(k, _)| *k == key)
 61:             .map(|(_, plan)| plan)
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     /// True when the walking plane at a world point is ordinary open fabric:
 65:     /// not solid, not raised, and not inside a barren anomaly family.
 66:     fn is_open_floor(&self, wx: f32, wz: f32) -> bool {
 67:         let Some(plan) = self.plan_of(wx, wz) else {
 68:             return false;
 69:         };
 70:         let forbidden = plan.anomalies.iter().any(|anomaly| {
 71:             matches!(anomaly.kind, AnomalyKind::RedRoom | AnomalyKind::PitLattice)
 72:                 && anomaly.contains(wx, wz)
 73:         });
 74:         if forbidden {
 75:             return false;
 76:         }
 77:         let column = BackroomsLevel::plan_column_in_reality(
 78:             plan,
 79:             self.noise,
 80:             self.seed,
 81:             self.config,
 82:             self.reality,
 83:             wx,
 84:             wz,
 85:         );
 86:         column.floor && !column.solid && column.floor_units < 0.05
 87:     }
 88: }
 89: 
 90: /// Decides which almond-water/ration supply items exist within stamping
 91: /// range of this chunk, without touching the grid: one deterministic
 92: /// candidate per 40u supply-lattice cell, accepted only on open floor and
 93: /// only where the strain-scaled density and consumption history allow it.
 94: /// Pure — same hash-roll/position logic `stamp_level_zero_provisions` used
 95: /// inline, split out so it (and its rejection reasons) are testable without
 96: /// a `VoxelGrid`. Chunks that cannot even stamp a candidate (outside the
 97: /// 0.5u marker margin) skip without evaluating it further, so no decision
 98: /// ever depends on which chunk happens to be asking.
 99: fn decide_supply_items(chunk_pos: Position, ctx: &ProvisionContext<'_>) -> Vec<SupplyItem> {
100:     let water = ctx.config.tuning.almond_water.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
101:     let food = ctx.config.tuning.rations.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
102:     if water <= 0.0 && food <= 0.0 {
103:         return Vec::new();
104:     }
105:     let max_x = chunk_pos.x + ctx.config.chunk_size;
106:     let max_z = chunk_pos.z + ctx.config.chunk_size;
107:     let near_chunk = |x: f32, z: f32, m: f32| {
108:         x >= chunk_pos.x - m && x < max_x + m && z >= chunk_pos.z - m && z < max_z + m
109:     };
110: 
111:     let c0x = ((chunk_pos.x - 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
112:     let c1x = ((max_x + 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
113:     let c0z = ((chunk_pos.z - 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
114:     let c1z = ((max_z + 1.0) / SUPPLY_CELL).floor() as i64;
115:     let mut items = Vec::new();
116:     for cz in c0z..=c1z {
117:         for cx in c0x..=c1x {
118:             let roll = hash(ctx.seed, 0x0A1A_09D0_57A7_0000, cx, cz);
119:             // Water and food frequencies scale their halves of the density
120:             // independently; the kind roll then splits proportionally, so
121:             // e.g. rations=0 yields a pure-water world at water's density.
122:             let water_weight = (1.0 - RATION_SHARE) * water;
123:             let food_weight = RATION_SHARE * food;
124:             // A mismanaged wanderer finds a stingier level: each strain tier
125:             // withholds a share of the supply cells (same hash, lower
126:             // threshold, so rising strain removes bottles rather than
127:             // shuffling them). Tier 0 is the unstrained field.
128:             let strain_keep = 1.0 - 0.15 * ctx.reality.delirium() as f32;
129:             let cell_chance = ALMOND_CHANCE * (water_weight + food_weight) * strain_keep;
130:             if unit(roll) > cell_chance {
131:                 continue;
132:             }
133:             let id = roll | 1;
134:             if ctx.reality.supply_consumed(id) {
135:                 continue;
136:             }
137:             // One deterministic spot per cell.
138:             let probe = hash(ctx.seed, 0x0A1A_09D0_0000_0000, cx, cz);
139:             let px = (cx as f32 + 0.06 + 0.88 * unit(probe)) * SUPPLY_CELL;
140:             let pz = (cz as f32 + 0.06 + 0.88 * unit(probe.rotate_left(23))) * SUPPLY_CELL;
141:             if !near_chunk(px, pz, 0.5) || !ctx.is_open_floor(px, pz) {
142:                 continue;
143:             }
144:             let kind = if unit(roll.rotate_left(11)) * (water_weight + food_weight) < food_weight
145:             {
146:                 SupplyKind::Ration
147:             } else {
148:                 SupplyKind::AlmondWater
149:             };
150:             items.push(SupplyItem {
151:                 id,
152:                 kind,
153:                 position: Position::new(px, pz),
154:                 rest_y: 0.0,
155:             });
156:         }
157:     }
158:     items
159: }
160: 
161: /// Stamps supplies and doors into one Level 0 chunk and exports their
162: /// semantic records. Never called for recursive (red-room-interior) chunks.
163: pub(crate) fn stamp_level_zero_provisions(
164:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
165:     chunk_pos: Position,
166:     ctx: &ProvisionContext<'_>,
167: ) {
168:     let doors = ctx.config.tuning.level_doors.clamp(0.0, 4.0);
169:     let has_supplies =
170:         ctx.config.tuning.almond_water > 0.0 || ctx.config.tuning.rations > 0.0;
171:     if !has_supplies && doors <= 0.0 {
172:         return;
173:     }
174:     let s = ctx.config.voxel_scale;
175:     let max_x = chunk_pos.x + ctx.config.chunk_size;
176:     let max_z = chunk_pos.z + ctx.config.chunk_size;
177:     let in_chunk = |x: f32, z: f32| x >= chunk_pos.x && x < max_x && z >= chunk_pos.z && z < max_z;
178:     // Markers span a few voxels, so an item just outside this grid must
179:     // still stamp its overlapping voxels here or seams (and the halo crop)
180:     // would disagree with the neighbor that owns it. Stamping quantizes in
181:     // world space, making the overlap exact; the semantic export stays with
182:     // every grid whose bounds contain the item (halo overlaps are deduped by
183:     // id on the consuming side).
184:     let near_chunk = |x: f32, z: f32, m: f32| {
185:         x >= chunk_pos.x - m && x < max_x + m && z >= chunk_pos.z - m && z < max_z + m
186:     };
187: 
188:     for item in decide_supply_items(chunk_pos, ctx) {
189:         stamp_supply_marker(grid, chunk_pos, s, &item);
190:         if in_chunk(item.position.x, item.position.z) {
191:             grid.supply_items.push(item);
192:         }
193:     }
194: 
195:     // -- doors to Level 1 on the 80u region lattice ---------------------------
196:     let r0x = (chunk_pos.x / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
197:     let r1x = ((max_x - 0.01) / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
198:     let r0z = (chunk_pos.z / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
199:     let r1z = ((max_z - 0.01) / REGION_SIZE).floor() as i64;
200:     // The whole door footprint (frame + clearing) fits inside the region
201:     // plan window's 1.0u margin, so every chunk that must stamp part of a
202:     // door can also evaluate its acceptance identically.
203:     if doors <= 0.0 {
204:         return;
205:     }
206:     for rz in r0z..=r1z {
207:         for rx in r0x..=r1x {
208:             let spawn_door_region =
209:                 rx == region_index(SPAWN_DOOR.0) && rz == region_index(SPAWN_DOOR.1);
210:             let (dx, dz) = if spawn_door_region {
211:                 // The authored guaranteed door carves its own clearing; no
212:                 // floor check, so it exists in every reality.
213:                 SPAWN_DOOR
214:             } else {
215:                 let roll = hash(ctx.seed, 0xD00E_0000_5EED_0000, rx, rz);
216:                 if unit(roll) > DOOR_CHANCE * doors {
217:                     continue;
218:                 }
219:                 // One deterministic spot per region; a spot on solid or
220:                 // anomalous ground simply means this region has no door.
221:                 let probe = hash(ctx.seed, 0xD00E_0000_0000_0000, rx, rz);
222:                 let px = (rx as f32 + 0.15 + 0.7 * unit(probe)) * REGION_SIZE;
223:                 let pz = (rz as f32 + 0.15 + 0.7 * unit(probe.rotate_left(19))) * REGION_SIZE;
224:                 if !near_chunk(px, pz, DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN) || !ctx.is_open_floor(px, pz) {
225:                     continue;
226:                 }
227:                 (px, pz)
228:             };
229:             if !near_chunk(dx, dz, DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN) {
230:                 continue;
231:             }
232: 
233:             carve_door_clearing(grid, chunk_pos, s, dx, dz);
234:             stamp_level_door(grid, chunk_pos, s, dx, dz, VOXEL_WALL);
235:             if in_chunk(dx, dz) {
236:                 grid.level_exits.push(LevelExit {
237:                     id: hash(ctx.seed, 0xD00E_0000_0000_1D00, rx, rz),
238:                     target_level: LEVEL_HABITABLE,
239:                     center: Position::new(dx, dz),
240:                     half_extent: DOOR_TRIGGER_HALF,
241:                     arrival: Position::new(ARRIVAL_POINT.0, ARRIVAL_POINT.1),
242:                 });
243:             }
244:         }
245:     }
246: }
247: 
248: /// Guarantees approach space on both sides of a door: air to 2.6u within a
249: /// small square, with the floor slab restored underneath. The radius stays
250: /// under `DOOR_STAMP_MARGIN` so the carve never outruns what neighboring
251: /// chunks can reproduce.
252: fn carve_door_clearing(
253:     grid: &mut VoxelGrid,
254:     chunk_pos: Position,
255:     voxel_size: f32,
256:     cx: f32,
257:     cz: f32,
258: ) {
259:     let radius = 0.95;
260:     let height_v = (2.6 / voxel_size).round() as i64;
261:     let x0 = ((cx - radius - chunk_pos.x) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
262:     let x1 = ((cx + radius - chunk_pos.x) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
263:     let z0 = ((cz - radius - chunk_pos.z) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
264:     let z1 = ((cz + radius - chunk_pos.z) / voxel_size).floor() as i64;
265:     for z in z0.max(0)..=z1.max(-1) {
266:         for x in x0.max(0)..=x1.max(-1) {
267:             let (xu, zu) = (x as usize, z as usize);
268:             if xu >= grid.width() || zu >= grid.depth() {
269:                 continue;
270:             }
271:             for y in 1..=height_v {
272:                 grid.set(xu, y as usize, zu, VOXEL_AIR);
273:             }
274:             if grid.get(xu, 0, zu) == VOXEL_AIR {
275:                 grid.set(
276:                     xu,
277:                     0,
278:                     zu,
279:                     crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_FLOOR,
280:                 );
281:             }
282:         }
283:     }
284: }
285: 
286: #[cfg(test)]
287: mod tests {
288:     use super::*;
289:     use crate::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
290: 
291:     /// `decide_supply_items` is exercised directly, no `VoxelGrid` involved:
292:     /// confirms it's deterministic (same chunk always decides the same
293:     /// items) and that every accepted item actually lands on open floor —
294:     /// the property `is_open_floor` exists to guarantee.
295:     #[test]
296:     fn supply_items_are_deterministic_and_on_open_floor() {
297:         let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
298:         let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
299:         let reality = RealitySnapshot::empty();
300:         let mut any_items = false;
301: 
302:         for chunk in 0..40i64 {
303:             let chunk_pos = Position::new(chunk as f32 * config.chunk_size, 0.0);
304:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
305:                 chunk_pos,
306:                 config.chunk_size,
307:                 42,
308:                 &config,
309:                 &noise,
310:             );
311:             let ctx = ProvisionContext {
312:                 seed: 42,
313:                 config: &config,
314:                 reality: &reality,
315:                 noise: &noise,
316:                 plans: &plans,
317:             };
318: 
319:             let items_a = decide_supply_items(chunk_pos, &ctx);
320:             let items_b = decide_supply_items(chunk_pos, &ctx);
321:             assert_eq!(
322:                 items_a.len(),
323:                 items_b.len(),
324:                 "supply decision is not deterministic for chunk {chunk}"
325:             );
326:             for item in &items_a {
327:                 assert!(
328:                     ctx.is_open_floor(item.position.x, item.position.z),
329:                     "accepted supply item at {:?} is not on open floor",
330:                     item.position
331:                 );
332:             }
333:             any_items |= !items_a.is_empty();
334:         }
335:         assert!(any_items, "no supply items found across 40 sampled chunks");
336:     }
337: 
338:     /// `almond_water == 0 && rations == 0` must skip the lattice sweep
339:     /// entirely rather than decide items nobody wanted, matching the early
340:     /// return `stamp_level_zero_provisions` takes for the same setting.
341:     #[test]
342:     fn zero_tuning_decides_no_supply_items() {
343:         let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
344:         let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
345:         config.tuning.almond_water = 0.0;
346:         config.tuning.rations = 0.0;
347:         let reality = RealitySnapshot::empty();
348:         let chunk_pos = Position::new(0.0, 0.0);
349:         let plans =
350:             BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(chunk_pos, config.chunk_size, 42, &config, &noise);
351:         let ctx = ProvisionContext {
352:             seed: 42,
353:             config: &config,
354:             reality: &reality,
355:             noise: &noise,
356:             plans: &plans,
357:         };
358:         assert!(decide_supply_items(chunk_pos, &ctx).is_empty());
359:     }
360: }
````

## File: src/use_cases/level_zero/voxelize.rs
````rust
  1: //! Materialize sampled Level 0 columns at the requested voxel size.
  2: 
  3: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VoxelGrid};
  4: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::ColumnField;
  5: 
  6: /// Writes geometry and fixture voxels without knowing seeds, regions,
  7: /// anomalies, chunks, or recursive branches.  Those are planning concerns;
  8: /// this stage only quantizes an already sampled physical area.
  9: pub(crate) fn voxelize_columns(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, field: &ColumnField, voxel_size: f32) {
 10:     let max_y = grid.height().saturating_sub(1);
 11:     let to_voxel = |units: f32| ((units / voxel_size) as usize).clamp(2, max_y);
 12: 
 13:     for z in 0..field.depth() {
 14:         for x in 0..field.width() {
 15:             let plan = *field.get(x as i64, z as i64);
 16:             let ceiling_y = to_voxel(plan.ceiling_units);
 17: 
 18:             if plan.floor {
 19:                 grid.set(x, 0, z, plan.floor_material);
 20:                 // Raised floor (stair treads, landings) is solid mass in
 21:                 // wall material: collision derives from solid voxels, so a
 22:                 // tread must block like architecture, not paint like carpet.
 23:                 let raised = (plan.floor_units / voxel_size).round() as usize;
 24:                 for y in 1..=raised.min(max_y) {
 25:                     grid.set(x, y, z, plan.wall_material);
 26:                 }
 27:             }
 28: 
 29:             if plan.solid {
 30:                 for y in 1..ceiling_y {
 31:                     grid.set(x, y, z, plan.wall_material);
 32:                 }
 33:             } else if let Some(lintel_height) = plan.lintel_from_units {
 34:                 for y in to_voxel(lintel_height)..ceiling_y {
 35:                     grid.set(x, y, z, plan.wall_material);
 36:                 }
 37:             }
 38: 
 39:             // A ceiling-height step can only ever be voxelized where a wall
 40:             // or door header already reaches up to carry it: fabric_ceiling_
 41:             // height snaps to the same FABRIC_CELL lattice the wall/lintel
 42:             // decision reads, so a step is only possible exactly at a
 43:             // boundary this column's own `solid`/`lintel_from_units` already
 44:             // has an opinion about. Walls and headers legitimately grow to
 45:             // whichever neighbour is taller — that is just a wall being tall
 46:             // enough. An ordinary open column caps at its own height only:
 47:             // that is a real step in the ceiling plane at a doorway or
 48:             // opening, not a gap, and inventing a floating patch to hide it
 49:             // would be unsupported geometry with nothing holding it up.
 50:             let has_wall_support = plan.solid || plan.lintel_from_units.is_some();
 51:             let cap_top = if has_wall_support {
 52:                 let neighbour_ceiling = [
 53:                     field.get(x as i64 - 1, z as i64),
 54:                     field.get(x as i64 + 1, z as i64),
 55:                     field.get(x as i64, z as i64 - 1),
 56:                     field.get(x as i64, z as i64 + 1),
 57:                 ]
 58:                 .iter()
 59:                 .map(|neighbour| to_voxel(neighbour.ceiling_units))
 60:                 .max()
 61:                 .unwrap_or(ceiling_y);
 62:                 neighbour_ceiling.max(ceiling_y)
 63:             } else {
 64:                 ceiling_y
 65:             };
 66:             let cap_material = if has_wall_support {
 67:                 plan.wall_material
 68:             } else {
 69:                 VOXEL_CEILING
 70:             };
 71:             for y in ceiling_y..=cap_top {
 72:                 grid.set(x, y, z, cap_material);
 73:             }
 74: 
 75:             if plan.light && !plan.solid {
 76:                 let material = if plan.red_light {
 77:                     VOXEL_RED_LIGHT
 78:                 } else {
 79:                     plan.light_material
 80:                 };
 81:                 grid.set(x, ceiling_y, z, material);
 82:             }
 83:         }
 84:     }
 85: }

 87: #[cfg(test)]
 88: mod tests {
 89:     use super::*;
 90:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{

 94: 
 95:     /// Level 0 currently has one authored emitter contract: fixtures are
 96:     /// exposed panels in open ceiling columns. A fixture request on a solid
 97:     /// column must therefore remain ordinary architecture, never a buried
 98:     /// emissive voxel or a second light on the floor.
 99:     #[test]
100:     fn solid_columns_cannot_voxelize_fake_emitters() {
101:         let mut column = ColumnPlan::open(4.0);
102:         column.solid = true;
103:         column.light = true;
104:         column.red_light = true;
105:         column.light_material = VOXEL_RED_LIGHT;
106: 
107:         let field = ColumnField::sample(1, 1, |_, _| column);
108:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(1, 6, 1);
109:         voxelize_columns(&mut grid, &field, 1.0);
110: 
111:         assert_eq!(grid.get(0, 0, 0), VOXEL_FLOOR);
112:         for y in 0..grid.height() {
113:             let material = grid.get(0, y, 0);
114:             assert!(
115:                 !EMISSIVE_MATERIALS.contains(&material),
116:                 "solid column contains buried emitter {material} at y={y}"
117:             );
118:         }
119:         for y in 1..=4 {
120:             let material = grid.get(0, y, 0);
121:             assert_eq!(material, VOXEL_WALL);
122:         }
123:     }
124: 
125:     /// The bug this guards: two adjacent open (non-solid, no lintel)
126:     /// columns at different ceiling heights used to grow a `VOXEL_CEILING`
127:     /// skirt on the shorter column, bridging up to the taller neighbour's
128:     /// height with nothing underneath it — a ceiling patch floating over
129:     /// open, walkable floor. An open column must cap at its own height
130:     /// only; a real step in the ceiling plane at the boundary, not an
131:     /// unsupported patch.
132:     #[test]
133:     fn open_columns_never_grow_an_unsupported_ceiling_skirt() {
134:         let short = ColumnPlan::open(4.0);
135:         let tall = ColumnPlan::open(7.0);
136:         let field = ColumnField::sample(2, 1, |x, _z| if x == 0 { short } else { tall });
137:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(2, 8, 1);
138:         voxelize_columns(&mut grid, &field, 1.0);
139: 
140:         // Column 0's own ceiling cap sits at y=4; nothing above it.
141:         assert_eq!(grid.get(0, 4, 0), VOXEL_CEILING);
142:         for y in 5..grid.height() {
143:             assert_eq!(
144:                 grid.get(0, y, 0),
145:                 VOXEL_AIR,
146:                 "unsupported ceiling patch found at y={y} above an open column"
147:             );
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151:     /// The support-preserving counterpart: a *solid* boundary column
152:     /// between two different ceiling heights must still reach the taller
153:     /// neighbour — that is an ordinary wall being tall enough to actually
154:     /// separate the two rooms, not the bug above.
155:     #[test]
156:     fn solid_boundary_columns_still_reach_the_taller_neighbour() {
157:         let mut wall = ColumnPlan::open(4.0);
158:         wall.solid = true;
159:         let tall = ColumnPlan::open(7.0);
160:         let field = ColumnField::sample(2, 1, |x, _z| if x == 0 { wall } else { tall });
161:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(2, 8, 1);
162:         voxelize_columns(&mut grid, &field, 1.0);
163: 
164:         for y in 1..=7 {
165:             assert_eq!(
166:                 grid.get(0, y, 0),
167:                 VOXEL_WALL,
168:                 "wall should reach the taller neighbour's ceiling at y={y}"
169:             );
170:         }
171:     }
````

````rust
 1: //! The pluggable level-generator port: each Backrooms "level" (Level 0
 2: //! offices, Level 34-B grassland, ...) is one implementation.
 3: //!
 4: //! Contract for implementors:
 5: //! * **Seamless tiling** — derive ALL geometry from *world-space* coordinates
 6: //!   (chunk origin + local voxel index), never from chunk-local positions, so
 7: //!   independently generated chunks line up at their borders.
 8: //! * **Walkability** — the ground plane must stay connected: never fully
 9: //!   enclose a region the player could be in. Doorways/gaps must be at least
10: //!   ~1 world unit wide.
11: //! * **Determinism** — same (chunk_pos, seed, config) must always produce the
12: //!   same grid; only the injected [`NoiseProvider`] may be used for variety.
13: //! * Lighting is NOT the generator's job: place `VOXEL_LIGHT` sources and the
14: //!   orchestrating use case runs the exposed-face lighting bake afterwards.
15: 
16: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
17: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
18: use crate::entities::models::Position;
19: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
20: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;

23: pub const LEVEL_BACKROOMS: u32 = 0;
24: /// Level 1, the Habitable Zone: concrete warehouse/parking structure.
25: pub const LEVEL_HABITABLE: u32 = 1;
26: pub const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
27: /// The pre-canon office blueprint, kept reachable for tests and archaeology.
28: /// It vacated id 1 when the canonical Level 1 landed.
29: pub const LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES: u32 = 90;
30: 
31: pub trait LevelGenerator {
32:     /// Fills one chunk. `chunk_pos` is the chunk origin in world units.
33:     fn generate(
34:         &self,
35:         chunk_pos: Position,
36:         seed: u32,
37:         config: GeneratorConfig,
38:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
39:     ) -> VoxelGrid;
40: 
41:     /// Fills one chunk under a deterministic encounter-state snapshot.
42:     ///
43:     /// Most levels are entirely immutable and inherit this implementation.
44:     /// Level 0 overrides it so anomaly infill/topology can be a pure function
45:     /// of the same snapshot that keyed the chunk request. Keeping the legacy
46:     /// `generate` entry point makes stateless tools and tests explicit users
47:     /// of epoch zero.
48:     fn generate_with_reality(
49:         &self,
50:         chunk_pos: Position,
51:         seed: u32,
52:         config: GeneratorConfig,
53:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
54:         _reality: &RealitySnapshot,
55:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
56:         self.generate(chunk_pos, seed, config, noise)
57:     }
58: }
````

````rust
 12: /// Presentation Layer & Driver:
 13: /// A minimalist, zero-dependency HTTP server that connects our
 14: /// Clean Architecture engine to the Browser Voxel Renderer.
 15: fn main() {
 16:     let port = 3000;
 17:     let listener = TcpListener::bind(format!("0.0.0.0:{}", port)).unwrap();
 18:     println!("--- Backrooms Engine Running ---");
 19:     println!("Server listening on http://localhost:{}", port);
 20:     println!("Open the above URL in your browser to view the Voxel Rendering.");
 21: 
 22:     for stream in listener.incoming() {
 23:         match stream {
 24:             Ok(stream) => {
 25:                 thread::spawn(move || {
 26:                     handle_client(stream);
 27:                 });
 28:             }
 29:             Err(e) => {
 30:                 eprintln!("Failed to accept connection: {}", e);
 31:             }
 32:         }
 33:     }

 36: fn handle_client(mut stream: TcpStream) {
 37:     let mut buffer = [0; 1024];
 38:     if let Ok(bytes_read) = stream.read(&mut buffer) {
 39:         if bytes_read == 0 {
 40:             return;
 41:         }
 42: 
 43:         let request = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer[..bytes_read]);
 44:         let request_line = request.lines().next().unwrap_or("");
 45: 
 46:         if request_line.starts_with("GET /maze") {
 47:             // Serve the Procedural Voxel Data with support for coordinate query parameters
 48:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
 49:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/maze");
 50: 
 51:             let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
 52:             let mut chunk_z = 0.0;
 53:             let mut spec = "high";
 54: 
 55:             if let Some(query_idx) = url.find('?') {
 56:                 let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
 57:                 for param in query.split('&') {
 58:                     let key_val: Vec<&str> = param.split('=').collect();
 59:                     if key_val.len() == 2 {
 60:                         match key_val[0] {
 61:                             "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
 62:                             "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
 63:                             "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
 64:                             _ => {}
 65:                         }
 66:                     }
 67:                 }
 68:             }
 69: 
 70:             let config = if spec == "low" {
 71:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
 72:             } else {
 73:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
 74:             };
 75: 
 76:             let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 77:             let telemetry = StdTelemetry;
 78:             let generator =

 80: 
 81:             let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
 82: 
 83:             // Adapt to Web Format (greedy meshed faces)
 84:             let json = WebRendererAdapter::to_json(&chunk, config.chunk_size);
 85: 
 86:             let response = format!(
 87:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n{}",
 88:                 json.len(),
 89:                 json
 90:             );
 91:             let _ = stream.write_all(response.as_bytes());
 92:         } else if request_line.starts_with("GET /octree") {
 93:             // Serve the SVO Packed Data
 94:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
 95:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/octree");
 96: 
 97:             let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
 98:             let mut chunk_z = 0.0;
 99:             let mut spec = "high";
100: 
101:             if let Some(query_idx) = url.find('?') {
102:                 let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
103:                 for param in query.split('&') {

105:                     if key_val.len() == 2 {
106:                         match key_val[0] {
107:                             "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
108:                             "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
109:                             "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
110:                             _ => {}
111:                         }
112:                     }
113:                 }
114:             }
115: 
116:             let config = if spec == "low" {
117:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
118:             } else {
119:                 vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
120:             };
121: 
122:             let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
123:             let telemetry = StdTelemetry;
124:             let generator =
125:                 GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&noise_provider, &telemetry);
126: 
127:             // Generate chunk at position with GeneratorConfig
128:             let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);
129: 
130:             // Adapt to Web Format using SVO representation
131:             let depth = config.svo_depth();
132:             let world_size = config.svo_world_size();
133:             let binary = WebRendererAdapter::to_octree_binary(
134:                 &chunk,
135:                 depth,
136:                 world_size,
137:                 config.voxel_scale,
138:                 config.chunk_size,
139:             );
140: 
141:             let header = format!(
142:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
143:                 binary.len()
144:             );
145:             let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + binary.len());
146:             response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
147:             response.extend_from_slice(&binary);
148:             let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
149:         } else if request_line.starts_with("GET ") {
150:             // Static file service for the WebGPU front end.
151:             let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
152:             let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/");
153:             let path = url.split('?').next().unwrap_or("/");
154:             serve_static(&mut stream, path);
155:         } else {
156:             let error = "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\n";
157:             let _ = stream.write_all(error.as_bytes());
158:         }
159:     }
160: }
161: 
162: /// Maps a URL path to a file under `static/` and serves it with the correct
163: /// MIME type. `application/wasm` matters: browsers refuse to instantiate
164: /// wasm streams served under the wrong content type.
165: fn serve_static(stream: &mut TcpStream, url_path: &str) {
166:     let relative = match url_path {
167:         "/" | "/index.html" => "index.html",
168:         other => other.trim_start_matches('/'),
169:     };
170: 
171:     // Path traversal guard: reject anything trying to escape `static/`.
172:     if relative.split('/').any(|seg| seg == "..") || relative.contains('\\') {
173:         let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n\r\n");
174:         return;
175:     }
176: 
177:     let file_path = format!("static/{}", relative);
178:     match fs::read(&file_path) {
179:         Ok(body) => {
180:             let mime = match file_path.rsplit('.').next() {
181:                 Some("html") => "text/html; charset=utf-8",
182:                 Some("js") | Some("mjs") => "text/javascript",
183:                 Some("wasm") => "application/wasm",
184:                 Some("css") => "text/css",
185:                 Some("json") => "application/json",
186:                 Some("png") => "image/png",
187:                 _ => "application/octet-stream",
188:             };
189:             let header = format!(
190:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
191:                 mime,
192:                 body.len()
193:             );
194:             let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + body.len());
195:             response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
196:             response.extend_from_slice(&body);
197:             let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
198:         }
199:         Err(_) => {
200:             let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\nFile not found.");
201:         }
202:     }
203: }
````

## File: static/worker.js
````javascript
  1: // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, producing
  2: // renderer-selected chunk artifacts off the main thread. The handler is
  3: // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
  4: // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
  5: // promise chain.
  6: //
  7: // Protocol (main -> worker):
  8: //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
  9: //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality }
 10: //                   one chunk order; artifacts is a u8 bitfield and reality
 11: //                   is Uint32Array
 12: // (worker -> main):
 13: //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, ms, buf }
 14: //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
 15: //   { type: "failed", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, message }
 16: //                                   one request failed and may be retried
 17: //   { type: "fatal", message }      worker initialization failed
 18: import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";
 19: 
 20: let wasmReady = null;
 21: function ensureWasm() {
 22:   if (!wasmReady) wasmReady = init();
 23:   return wasmReady;
 24: }
 25: 
 26: let queue = Promise.resolve();
 27: 
 28: function errorMessage(error) {
 29:   if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
 30:   return String(error);
 31: }
 32: 
 33: function reportFailure(message, error) {
 34:   const description = errorMessage(error);
 35:   console.error("[WORKER] generation failure:", description);
 36:   try {
 37:     if (message?.type === "gen") {
 38:       postMessage({
 39:         type: "failed",
 40:         requestId: message.requestId,
 41:         ox: message.ox,
 42:         oz: message.oz,
 43:         level: message.level,
 44:         lod: message.lod,
 45:         artifacts: message.artifacts,
 46:         reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality),
 47:         message: description,
 48:       });
 49:     } else {
 50:       postMessage({ type: "fatal", message: description });
 51:     }
 52:   } catch (reportError) {
 53:     // The browser's Worker error event is the final recovery path when even
 54:     // the structured failure message cannot be cloned or delivered.
 55:     console.error("[WORKER] could not report generation failure:", reportError);
 56:   }
 57: }
 58: 
 59: async function processMessage(message) {
 60:   await ensureWasm();
 61:   if (message.type === "init") {
 62:     worker_init(message.query, message.seed >>> 0);
 63:     return;
 64:   }
 65:   if (message.type !== "gen") return;
 66: 
 67:   const t0 = performance.now();
 68:   const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);
 69:   const bytes = worker_generate(
 70:     message.requestId >>> 0,
 71:     message.ox,
 72:     message.oz,
 73:     message.level,
 74:     message.lod,
 75:     message.artifacts >>> 0,
 76:     reality
 77:   );
 78:   const ms = performance.now() - t0;
 79:   console.debug(
 80:     `[WORKER] chunk (${message.ox}, ${message.oz}) lod ${message.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
 81:   );
 82:   postMessage(
 83:     {
 84:       type: "done",
 85:       requestId: message.requestId,
 86:       ox: message.ox,
 87:       oz: message.oz,
 88:       level: message.level,
 89:       lod: message.lod,
 90:       artifacts: message.artifacts,
 91:       reality,
 92:       ms,
 93:       buf: bytes.buffer,
 94:     },
 95:     [bytes.buffer]
 96:   );
 97: }
 98: 
 99: onmessage = (event) => {
100:   const message = event.data;
101:   // Catch each queue item independently. A failed request must not leave the
102:   // promise chain rejected, which would silently skip every later request.
103:   queue = queue
104:     .then(() => processMessage(message))
105:     .catch((error) => reportFailure(message, error));
106: };
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/mod.rs
