182: /// Generates one legacy blueprint chunk. Pure in `(chunk_pos, seed, config)`
183: /// given a deterministic noise provider; telemetry is observation only.
184: pub(crate) fn generate_legacy_blueprint(
185:     noise_provider: &dyn NoiseProvider,
186:     telemetry: &dyn TelemetryPort,
187:     chunk_pos: Position,
188:     seed: u32,
189:     config: GeneratorConfig,
190: ) -> VoxelGrid {
191:     let start_micros = telemetry.now_micros();
192: 
193:     let width = (config.chunk_size / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
194:     let depth = (config.chunk_size / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
195: 
196:     // Cell voxel borders derive from world space (cells are 5.0 units) so
197:     // every LOD of a chunk puts its walls on the same world planes.
198:     // Truncating a fixed voxels-per-cell instead compresses the maze at
199:     // scales where 5.0/voxel_scale is fractional.
200:     let cell_border = |c: usize| (c as f32 * 5.0 / config.voxel_scale).round() as usize;
201:     let cell_w = ((config.chunk_size / 5.0).round() as usize).max(1);
202:     let cell_d = cell_w;
203: 
204:     let mut abstract_grid = Grid::new(cell_w, cell_d);
205: 
206:     // --- ZONE ASSIGNMENT PASS ---
207:     let mut max_chunk_height_units = 3.0_f32;
208:     for cz in 0..cell_d {
209:         for cx in 0..cell_w {
210:             let wx = chunk_pos.x * config.chunk_size + (cx as f32) * 5.0;
211:             let wz = chunk_pos.z * config.chunk_size + (cz as f32) * 5.0;
212: 
213:             // Low frequency noise for zone clustering
214:             let n = noise_provider.evaluate_2d(
215:                 seed ^ 0x2b8f_a43c,
216:                 crate::entities::models::Position::new(wx * 0.05, wz * 0.05),
217:             ); // n is in [-1, 1]
218: 
219:             use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
220:             let mut zone = MicrobiomeZone::Standard;
221: 
222:             if n < -0.7 {
223:                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Blackout;
224:             } else if n < -0.4 {
225:                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Holes;
226:             } else if n > 0.85 - (config.tuning.atria as f32 * 0.1) {
227:                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Atrium;
228:             } else if n > 0.6 {
229:                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::PillarField;
230:             } else if n > 0.4 {
231:                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::Arch;
232:             } else if n > 0.2 && n < 0.25 {
233:                 zone = MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom;
234:             }
235: 
236:             if let Some(cell) = abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, cz) {
237:                 cell.zone = zone;
238:             }
239: 
240:             let cell_h = match zone {
241:                 MicrobiomeZone::Atrium => 12.0,  // 4.0 * 3.0x
242:                 MicrobiomeZone::Blackout => 3.2, // 4.0 * 0.8x
243:                 _ => 4.0,
244:             };
245:             if cell_h > max_chunk_height_units {
246:                 max_chunk_height_units = cell_h;
247:             }
248:         }
249:     }
250: 
251:     let height = (max_chunk_height_units / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize + 2; // +2 for floor and ceiling bounds
252: 
253:     telemetry.log(&format!(
254:             "[INFO] Entering GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::execute. Args: chunk_pos={:?}, seed={}, chunk_size={} (Voxel dimensions: {}x{}x{})",
255:             chunk_pos, seed, config.chunk_size, width, height, depth
256:         ));
257: 
258:     let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(width, height, depth);
259: 
260:     // STARTING HUB OVERRIDE: Chunk (0,0) is a massive open plaza that feeds seamlessly into the maze
261:     if chunk_pos.x.abs() < 1.0 && chunk_pos.z.abs() < 1.0 {
262:         for z in 0..depth {
263:             for x in 0..width {
264:                 grid.set(x, 0, z, VOXEL_FLOOR);
265:                 grid.set(x, height - 1, z, VOXEL_CEILING);
266: 
267:                 // Scatter ceiling panels without replacing walkable floor material.
268:                 if x > 0 && z > 0 && x % 20 == 0 && z % 20 == 0 {
269:                     grid.set(x, height - 1, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
270:                 }
271:             }
272:         }
273:         let lighting =
274:             crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
275:                 config.voxel_scale,
276:             )
277:             .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
278:         crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
279:         return grid;
280:     }
281: 
282:     // ==========================================
283:     // DYNAMIC GENERATION (Growing Tree & BSP)
284:     // ==========================================
285:     let mut rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(
286:         (seed as u64) ^ (chunk_pos.x.to_bits() as u64) ^ (chunk_pos.z.to_bits() as u64),
287:     );
288:     // Per-voxel cosmetic noise (floor holes, dotted pillars) draws from
289:     // its own stream: the number of those draws depends on voxel
290:     // resolution, and letting them share the structural RNG would
291:     // desynchronize wall/door placement between LODs of the same chunk.
292:     let mut detail_rng = StdRng::seed_from_u64(
293:         (seed as u64)
294:             ^ (chunk_pos.x.to_bits() as u64)
295:             ^ (chunk_pos.z.to_bits() as u64)
296:             ^ 0xD57A_11ED,
297:     );
298: 
299:     let maze_gen = GrowingTreeGenerator {
300:         junction_density: config.tuning.junction_density,
301:     };
302:     maze_gen.generate(&mut abstract_grid, &mut rng);
303: 
304:     // Organic room segmentation
305:     let mut rooms = Vec::new();
306:     let mut room_grid = vec![None; cell_w * cell_d];
307: 
308:     // Tunable parameters
309:     let num_room_attempts = 15;
310:     for _ in 0..num_room_attempts {
311:         let cx = rng.random_range(0..cell_w);
312:         let cz = rng.random_range(0..cell_d);
313:         let rw = rng.random_range(1..=3);
314:         let rd = rng.random_range(1..=3);
315: 
316:         if cx + rw <= cell_w && cz + rd <= cell_d {
317:             let mut overlap = false;
318:             for i in 0..rw {
319:                 for j in 0..rd {
320:                     if room_grid[(cz + j) * cell_w + cx + i].is_some() {
321:                         overlap = true;
322:                     }
323:                 }
324:             }
325:             if !overlap {
326:                 let room_id = rooms.len();
327:                 for i in 0..rw {
328:                     for j in 0..rd {
329:                         room_grid[(cz + j) * cell_w + cx + i] = Some(room_id);
330:                         if let Some(cell) = abstract_grid.get_mut(cx + i, cz + j) {
331:                             if j > 0 {
332:                                 cell.walls[0] = false;
333:                             }
334:                             if i < rw - 1 {
335:                                 cell.walls[1] = false;
336:                             }
337:                             if j < rd - 1 {
338:                                 cell.walls[2] = false;
339:                             }
340:                             if i > 0 {
341:                                 cell.walls[3] = false;
342:                             }
343:                         }
344:                     }
345:                 }
346:                 rooms.push(Room {
347:                     name: "Organic",
348:                     x0: cell_border(cx),
349:                     x1: cell_border(cx + rw) - 1,
350:                     z0: cell_border(cz),
351:                     z1: cell_border(cz + rd) - 1,
352:                 });
353:             }
354:         }
355:     }
356: 
357:     // Hallway reservation (Part 1)
358:     let mut non_room_indices = Vec::new();
359:     for i in 0..(cell_w * cell_d) {
360:         if room_grid[i].is_none() {
361:             non_room_indices.push(i);
362:         }
363:     }
364: 
365:     let target_corridors = (non_room_indices.len() as f32 * 0.20) as usize;
366:     let mut corridor_count = 0;
367: 
368:     use rand::seq::SliceRandom;
369:     non_room_indices.shuffle(&mut rng);
370: 
371:     for &idx in &non_room_indices {
372:         if corridor_count >= target_corridors {
373:             break;
374:         }
375:         let cx = idx % cell_w;
376:         let cz = idx / cell_w;
377:         if abstract_grid.get(cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor {
378:             continue;
379:         }
380: 
381:         abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
382:         corridor_count += 1;
383: 
384:         // Extend North
385:         let mut current_cz = cz;
386:         while current_cz > 0 && !abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().walls[0] {
387:             current_cz -= 1;
388:             if room_grid[current_cz * cell_w + cx].is_some()
389:                 || abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor
390:             {
391:                 break;
392:             }
393:             abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
394:             corridor_count += 1;
395:         }
396:         // Extend South
397:         let mut current_cz = cz;
398:         while current_cz < cell_d - 1 && !abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().walls[2] {
399:             current_cz += 1;
400:             if room_grid[current_cz * cell_w + cx].is_some()
401:                 || abstract_grid.get(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor
402:             {
403:                 break;
404:             }
405:             abstract_grid.get_mut(cx, current_cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
406:             corridor_count += 1;
407:         }
408:         // Extend West
409:         let mut current_cx = cx;
410:         while current_cx > 0 && !abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().walls[3] {
411:             current_cx -= 1;
412:             if room_grid[cz * cell_w + current_cx].is_some()
413:                 || abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor
414:             {
415:                 break;
416:             }
417:             abstract_grid.get_mut(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
418:             corridor_count += 1;
419:         }
420:         // Extend East
421:         let mut current_cx = cx;
422:         while current_cx < cell_w - 1 && !abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().walls[1] {
423:             current_cx += 1;
424:             if room_grid[cz * cell_w + current_cx].is_some()
425:                 || abstract_grid.get(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor
426:             {
427:                 break;
428:             }
429:             abstract_grid.get_mut(current_cx, cz).unwrap().is_corridor = true;
430:             corridor_count += 1;
431:         }
432:     }
433: 
434:     // Draw abstract grid to VoxelGrid
435:     for cz in 0..cell_d {
436:         for cx in 0..cell_w {
437:             let cell = abstract_grid.get(cx, cz).unwrap();
438:             let v_x0 = cell_border(cx);
439:             let v_z0 = cell_border(cz);
440:             let v_x1 = (cell_border(cx + 1) - 1).min(width - 1);
441:             let v_z1 = (cell_border(cz + 1) - 1).min(depth - 1);
442: 
443:             use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
444:             let cell_h_units = match cell.zone {
445:                 MicrobiomeZone::Atrium => 12.0,
446:                 MicrobiomeZone::Blackout => 3.2,
447:                 _ => 4.0,
448:             };
449:             let wall_max_y = (cell_h_units / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize;
450:             let door_max_y = (2.5 / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize; // Doorways are 2.5 units tall
451: 
452:             let wall_type = VOXEL_WALL;
453: 
454:             // Floors and Ceilings
455:             for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
456:                 for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
457:                     grid.set(vx, 0, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
458: 
459:                     if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Holes {
460:                         if vx > v_x0 + 5 && vx < v_x1 - 5 && vz > v_z0 + 5 && vz < v_z1 - 5 {
461:                             if detail_rng.random_bool(0.05) {
462:                                 grid.set(vx, 0, vz, VOXEL_AIR);
463:                             }
464:                         }
465:                     }
466: 
467:                     if cell.zone != MicrobiomeZone::Atrium {
468:                         // Normal ceilings with hanging light
469:                         grid.set(vx, wall_max_y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING); // Always close the ceiling
470:                         if cell.zone != MicrobiomeZone::Blackout && (vx % 10 == 0 && vz % 10 == 0) {
471:                             if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom {
472:                                 grid.set(
473:                                     vx,
474:                                     wall_max_y - 1,
475:                                     vz,
476:                                     crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
477:                                 );
478:                             } else {
479:                                 grid.set(vx, wall_max_y - 1, vz, VOXEL_LIGHT);
480:                             }
481:                         }
482:                         for y in (wall_max_y + 1)..height {
483:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING);
484:                         }
485:                     } else {
486:                         // Atrium ceiling and bright hanging light
487:                         grid.set(vx, wall_max_y, vz, VOXEL_CEILING);
488:                         if vx % 10 == 0 && vz % 10 == 0 {
489:                             grid.set(vx, wall_max_y - 1, vz, VOXEL_LIGHT);
490:                         }
491:                     }
492:                 }
493:             }
494: 
495:             if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::PillarField {
496:                 for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
497:                     grid.set(v_x0, y, v_z0, wall_type);
498:                     grid.set(v_x1, y, v_z0, wall_type);
499:                     grid.set(v_x0, y, v_z1, wall_type);
500:                     grid.set(v_x1, y, v_z1, wall_type);
501:                     if detail_rng.random_bool(0.3) {
502:                         grid.set((v_x0 + v_x1 + 1) / 2, y, (v_z0 + v_z1 + 1) / 2, wall_type);
503:                     }
504:                 }
505:                 continue;
506:             }
507: 
508:             // South Wall (z1)
509:             if cz < cell_d - 1 {
510:                 let same_room = room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx] == room_grid[(cz + 1) * cell_w + cx]
511:                     && room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx].is_some();
512: 
513:                 if !same_room {
514:                     let width_choice = rng.random_range(0..100);
515:                     let hole_units = if width_choice < 15 {
516:                         1.2
517:                     } else if width_choice < 85 {
518:                         2.0
519:                     } else {
520:                         3.5
521:                     };
522:                     let hole_w = (hole_units / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
523:                     // Drawn in centimetres of the 5.0-unit cell span, not
524:                     // voxels, so every LOD picks the same door position.
525:                     let hole_cm = (hole_units * 100.0) as u32;
526:                     let max_offset_cm = 500u32.saturating_sub(hole_cm + 50);
527:                     let offset_cm = if max_offset_cm > 50 {
528:                         rng.random_range(50..max_offset_cm)
529:                     } else {
530:                         50
531:                     };
532:                     let offset = (offset_cm as f32 / 100.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
533:                     let hole_x0 = v_x0 + offset;
534:                     let hole_x1 = hole_x0 + hole_w;
535: 
536:                     for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
537:                         let in_hole = vx >= hole_x0 && vx < hole_x1;
538:                         if cell.walls[2] || !in_hole {
539:                             for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
540:                                 grid.set(vx, y, v_z1, wall_type);
541:                             }
542:                         } else if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Arch {
543:                             let dx = (vx as isize - (hole_x0 + hole_w / 2) as isize).abs() as usize;
544:                             let arch_top = door_max_y;
545:                             let block_y = arch_top.saturating_sub(dx);
546:                             for y in block_y..=wall_max_y {
547:                                 grid.set(vx, y, v_z1, wall_type);
548:                             }
549:                         } else {
550:                             for y in door_max_y..=wall_max_y {
551:                                 grid.set(vx, y, v_z1, wall_type);
552:                             }
553:                         }
554:                     }
555:                 }
556:             } else if cz == cell_d - 1 {
557:                 // Chunk boundary (force holes for connectivity)
558:                 let hole_w = (2.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
559:                 let hole_x0 = (v_x0 + v_x1 + 1) / 2 - hole_w / 2;
560:                 for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
561:                     let is_hole = vx >= hole_x0 && vx < hole_x0 + hole_w;
562:                     if !is_hole {
563:                         for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
564:                             grid.set(vx, y, v_z1, wall_type);
565:                         }
566:                     } else if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Arch {
567:                         let dx = (vx as isize - (hole_x0 + hole_w / 2) as isize).abs() as usize;
568:                         let arch_top = door_max_y;
569:                         let block_y = arch_top.saturating_sub(dx);
570:                         for y in block_y..=wall_max_y {
571:                             grid.set(vx, y, v_z1, wall_type);
572:                         }
573:                     } else {
574:                         for y in door_max_y..=wall_max_y {
575:                             grid.set(vx, y, v_z1, wall_type);
576:                         }
577:                     }
578:                 }
579:             }
580: 
581:             // East Wall (x1)
582:             if cx < cell_w - 1 {
583:                 let same_room = room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx] == room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx + 1]
584:                     && room_grid[cz * cell_w + cx].is_some();
585: 
586:                 if !same_room {
587:                     let width_choice = rng.random_range(0..100);
588:                     let hole_units = if width_choice < 15 {
589:                         1.2
590:                     } else if width_choice < 85 {
591:                         2.0
592:                     } else {
593:                         3.5
594:                     };
595:                     let hole_w = (hole_units / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
596:                     // Centimetre draw, same reasoning as the south wall.
597:                     let hole_cm = (hole_units * 100.0) as u32;
598:                     let max_offset_cm = 500u32.saturating_sub(hole_cm + 50);
599:                     let offset_cm = if max_offset_cm > 50 {
600:                         rng.random_range(50..max_offset_cm)
601:                     } else {
602:                         50
603:                     };
604:                     let offset = (offset_cm as f32 / 100.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
605:                     let hole_z0 = v_z0 + offset;
606:                     let hole_z1 = hole_z0 + hole_w;
607: 
608:                     for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
609:                         let in_hole = vz >= hole_z0 && vz < hole_z1;
610:                         if cell.walls[1] || !in_hole {
611:                             for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
612:                                 grid.set(v_x1, y, vz, wall_type);
613:                             }
614:                         } else if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Arch {
615:                             let dz = (vz as isize - (hole_z0 + hole_w / 2) as isize).abs() as usize;
616:                             let arch_top = door_max_y;
617:                             let block_y = arch_top.saturating_sub(dz);
618:                             for y in block_y..=wall_max_y {
619:                                 grid.set(v_x1, y, vz, wall_type);
620:                             }
621:                         } else {
622:                             for y in door_max_y..=wall_max_y {
623:                                 grid.set(v_x1, y, vz, wall_type);
624:                             }
625:                         }
626:                     }
627:                 }
628:             } else if cx == cell_w - 1 {
629:                 let hole_w = (2.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
630:                 let hole_z0 = (v_z0 + v_z1 + 1) / 2 - hole_w / 2;
631:                 for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
632:                     let is_hole = vz >= hole_z0 && vz < hole_z0 + hole_w;
633:                     if !is_hole {
634:                         for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
635:                             grid.set(v_x1, y, vz, wall_type);
636:                         }
637:                     } else if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Arch {
638:                         let dz = (vz as isize - (hole_z0 + hole_w / 2) as isize).abs() as usize;
639:                         let arch_top = door_max_y;
640:                         let block_y = arch_top.saturating_sub(dz);
641:                         for y in block_y..=wall_max_y {
642:                             grid.set(v_x1, y, vz, wall_type);
643:                         }
644:                     } else {
645:                         for y in door_max_y..=wall_max_y {
646:                             grid.set(v_x1, y, vz, wall_type);
647:                         }
648:                     }
649:                 }
650:             }
651: 
652:             // Draw narrower corridors for 2+ consecutive runs
653:             let mut is_ns_hall = false;
654:             let mut is_ew_hall = false;
655:             if cell.is_corridor {
656:                 let mut ns_run = 1;
657:                 if !cell.walls[0] && cz > 0 && abstract_grid.get(cx, cz - 1).unwrap().is_corridor {
658:                     ns_run += 1;
659:                 }
660:                 if !cell.walls[2]
661:                     && cz < cell_d - 1
662:                     && abstract_grid.get(cx, cz + 1).unwrap().is_corridor
663:                 {
664:                     ns_run += 1;
665:                 }
666: 
667:                 let mut ew_run = 1;
668:                 if !cell.walls[1]
669:                     && cx < cell_w - 1
670:                     && abstract_grid.get(cx + 1, cz).unwrap().is_corridor
671:                 {
672:                     ew_run += 1;
673:                 }
674:                 if !cell.walls[3] && cx > 0 && abstract_grid.get(cx - 1, cz).unwrap().is_corridor {
675:                     ew_run += 1;
676:                 }
677: 
678:                 if ns_run >= 2 {
679:                     is_ns_hall = true;
680:                 }
681:                 if ew_run >= 2 {
682:                     is_ew_hall = true;
683:                 }
684:             }
685: 
686:             if is_ns_hall && !is_ew_hall {
687:                 let inset_x = ((v_x1 - v_x0 + 1).saturating_sub(26)) / 2;
688:                 for vx in v_x0..=(v_x0 + inset_x) {
689:                     for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
690:                         for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
691:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
692:                         }
693:                     }
694:                 }
695:                 for vx in (v_x1 - inset_x)..=v_x1 {
696:                     for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
697:                         for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
698:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
699:                         }
700:                     }
701:                 }
702:             } else if is_ew_hall && !is_ns_hall {
703:                 let inset_z = ((v_z1 - v_z0 + 1).saturating_sub(26)) / 2;
704:                 for vz in v_z0..=(v_z0 + inset_z) {
705:                     for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
706:                         for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
707:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
708:                         }
709:                     }
710:                 }
711:                 for vz in (v_z1 - inset_z)..=v_z1 {
712:                     for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
713:                         for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
714:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
715:                         }
716:                     }
717:                 }
718:             } else if is_ns_hall && is_ew_hall {
719:                 let inset_x = ((v_x1 - v_x0 + 1).saturating_sub(26)) / 2;
720:                 let inset_z = ((v_z1 - v_z0 + 1).saturating_sub(26)) / 2;
721:                 for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
722:                     for vx in v_x0..=(v_x0 + inset_x) {
723:                         for vz in v_z0..=(v_z0 + inset_z) {
724:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
725:                         }
726:                     }
727:                     for vx in (v_x1 - inset_x)..=v_x1 {
728:                         for vz in v_z0..=(v_z0 + inset_z) {
729:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
730:                         }
731:                     }
732:                     for vx in v_x0..=(v_x0 + inset_x) {
733:                         for vz in (v_z1 - inset_z)..=v_z1 {
734:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
735:                         }
736:                     }
737:                     for vx in (v_x1 - inset_x)..=v_x1 {
738:                         for vz in (v_z1 - inset_z)..=v_z1 {
739:                             grid.set(vx, y, vz, wall_type);
740:                         }
741:                     }
742:                 }
743:             }
744:         }
745:     }
746: 
747:     // Chunk Boundaries (North and West)
748:     for cz in 0..cell_d {
749:         let cell = abstract_grid.get(0, cz).unwrap();
750:         use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
751:         let cell_h_units = match cell.zone {
752:             MicrobiomeZone::Atrium => 12.0,
753:             MicrobiomeZone::Blackout => 3.2,
754:             _ => 4.0,
755:         };
756:         let wall_max_y = (cell_h_units / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize;
757:         let door_max_y = (2.5 / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize;
758:         let wall_type = if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom {
759:             VOXEL_RED_WALL
760:         } else {
761:             VOXEL_WALL
762:         };
763: 
764:         if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::PillarField {
765:             continue;
766:         }
767: 
768:         let v_z0 = cell_border(cz);
769:         let v_z1 = (cell_border(cz + 1) - 1).min(depth - 1);
770:         let hole_w = (2.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
771:         let hole_z0 = (v_z0 + v_z1 + 1) / 2 - hole_w / 2;
772:         for vz in v_z0..=v_z1 {
773:             let is_hole = vz >= hole_z0 && vz < hole_z0 + hole_w;
774:             if !is_hole {
775:                 for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
776:                     grid.set(0, y, vz, wall_type);
777:                 }
778:             } else if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Arch {
779:                 let dz = (vz as isize - (hole_z0 + hole_w / 2) as isize).abs() as usize;
780:                 let arch_top = door_max_y;
781:                 let block_y = arch_top.saturating_sub(dz);
782:                 for y in block_y..=wall_max_y {
783:                     grid.set(0, y, vz, wall_type);
784:                 }
785:             } else {
786:                 for y in door_max_y..=wall_max_y {
787:                     grid.set(0, y, vz, wall_type);
788:                 }
789:             }
790:         }
791:     }
792:     for cx in 0..cell_w {
793:         let cell = abstract_grid.get(cx, 0).unwrap();
794:         use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
795:         let cell_h_units = match cell.zone {
796:             MicrobiomeZone::Atrium => 12.0,
797:             MicrobiomeZone::Blackout => 3.2,
798:             _ => 4.0,
799:         };
800:         let wall_max_y = (cell_h_units / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize;
801:         let door_max_y = (2.5 / config.voxel_scale).ceil() as usize;
802:         let wall_type = if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom {
803:             VOXEL_RED_WALL
804:         } else {
805:             VOXEL_WALL
806:         };
807: 
808:         if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::PillarField {
809:             continue;
810:         }
811: 
812:         let v_x0 = cell_border(cx);
813:         let v_x1 = (cell_border(cx + 1) - 1).min(width - 1);
814:         let hole_w = (2.0 / config.voxel_scale) as usize;
815:         let hole_x0 = (v_x0 + v_x1 + 1) / 2 - hole_w / 2;
816:         for vx in v_x0..=v_x1 {
817:             let is_hole = vx >= hole_x0 && vx < hole_x0 + hole_w;
818:             if !is_hole {
819:                 for y in 1..=wall_max_y {
820:                     grid.set(vx, y, 0, wall_type);
821:                 }
822:             } else if cell.zone == MicrobiomeZone::Arch {
823:                 let dx = (vx as isize - (hole_x0 + hole_w / 2) as isize).abs() as usize;
824:                 let arch_top = door_max_y;
825:                 let block_y = arch_top.saturating_sub(dx);
826:                 for y in block_y..=wall_max_y {
827:                     grid.set(vx, y, 0, wall_type);
828:                 }
829:             } else {
830:                 for y in door_max_y..=wall_max_y {
831:                     grid.set(vx, y, 0, wall_type);
832:                 }
833:             }
834:         }
835:     }
836: 
837:     // Apply Room Stamps to generated rooms
838:     let stamps = vec![
839:         RoomStamp::cubicles(),
840:         RoomStamp::showroom(),
841:         RoomStamp::waiting(),
842:         RoomStamp::storage(),
843:         RoomStamp::lounge(),
844:         RoomStamp::server_room(),
845:         RoomStamp::cafeteria(),
846:         RoomStamp::maintenance(),
847:     ];
848: 
849:     for room in &rooms {
850:         let mut possible_stamps = Vec::new();
851:         for stamp in &stamps {
852:             let max_stamps_w = (room.x1 - room.x0) / stamp.width.max(1);
853:             let max_stamps_d = (room.z1 - room.z0) / stamp.depth.max(1);
854:             if max_stamps_w > 0 && max_stamps_d > 0 {
855:                 possible_stamps.push(stamp);
856:             }
857:         }
858:         // Both rolls happen whether or not a stamp fits: which stamps fit
859:         // depends on voxel resolution, and skipping draws would
860:         // desynchronize the structural RNG between LODs of the chunk.
861:         let stamp_roll = rng.random_range(0..usize::MAX);
862:         let stairs_roll = rng.random_bool(0.15 * (config.tuning.stairs_density as f64));
863:         if !possible_stamps.is_empty() {
864:             let mut stamp = possible_stamps[stamp_roll % possible_stamps.len()];
865: 
866:             // Low-frequency stairs chance override
867:             let stairway = RoomStamp::stairway();
868:             if stairs_roll {
869:                 stamp = &stairway;
870:             }
871: 
872:             let spacing = (6.0 * (config.voxel_scale / 0.1)) as usize;
873:             let mut start_x = room.x0 + spacing;
874:             while start_x + stamp.width <= room.x1.saturating_sub(spacing) {
875:                 let mut start_z = room.z0 + spacing;
876:                 while start_z + stamp.depth <= room.z1.saturating_sub(spacing) {
877:                     if validate_stamp_placement(&grid, room, stamp, start_x, start_z) {
878:                         place_stamp(&mut grid, stamp, start_x, start_z);
879:                     }
880:                     start_z += stamp.depth + spacing;
881:                 }
882:                 start_x += stamp.width + spacing;
883:             }
884:         }
885: 
886:         // Basic room lighting
887:         let cx = (room.x0 + room.x1) / 2;
888:         let is_strip = rng.random_bool(0.3); // 30% chance for strip lights
889:         let mut z = room.z0 + 8;
890: 
891:         while z <= room.z1.saturating_sub(8) {
892:             if is_strip {
893:                 for offset in 0..4 {
894:                     if z + offset <= room.z1 {
895:                         grid.set(cx, height - 1, z + offset, VOXEL_LIGHT);
896:                     }
897:                 }
898:             } else {
899:                 grid.set(cx, height - 1, z, VOXEL_LIGHT);
900:             }
901:             z += 12;
902:         }
903:     }
904: 
905:     // Basic corridor lighting
906:     for cz in (8..depth).step_by(16) {
907:         for cx in (8..width).step_by(16) {
908:             if grid.get(cx, height - 1, cz) == VOXEL_CEILING && grid.get(cx, 1, cz) == VOXEL_AIR {
909:                 grid.set(cx, height - 1, cz, VOXEL_LIGHT);
910:             }
911:         }
912:     }
913: 
914:     // ==========================================
915:     // PHYSICAL VOXEL LIGHTING BAKE
916:     // ==========================================
917:     let lighting =
918:         crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
919:             config.voxel_scale,
920:         )
921:         .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
922:     crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
923: 
924:     let elapsed_micros = telemetry.now_micros().saturating_sub(start_micros);
925:     telemetry.log(&format!(
926:         "[TELEMETRY] execute completed. Duration={}us, OutputVoxelGridSize={}x{}x{}",
927:         elapsed_micros,
928:         grid.width(),
929:         grid.height(),
930:         grid.depth()
931:     ));
932: 
933:     grid
934: }
935: 
936: fn validate_stamp_placement(
937:     grid: &VoxelGrid,
938:     room: &Room,
939:     stamp: &RoomStamp,
940:     start_x: usize,
941:     start_z: usize,
942: ) -> bool {
943:     if start_x < room.x0
944:         || start_x + stamp.width > room.x1
945:         || start_z < room.z0
946:         || start_z + stamp.depth > room.z1
947:     {
948:         return false;
949:     }
950: 
951:     for lz in 0..stamp.depth {
952:         for lx in 0..stamp.width {
953:             let vx = start_x + lx;
954:             let vz = start_z + lz;
955:             if stamp.data[lz * stamp.width + lx] > 0 {
956:                 if grid.get(vx, 1, vz) != VOXEL_AIR && grid.get(vx, 1, vz) != VOXEL_FLOOR {
957:                     return false;
958:                 }
959:             }
960:         }
961:     }
962: 
963:     true
964: }
965: 
966: fn place_stamp(grid: &mut VoxelGrid, stamp: &RoomStamp, start_x: usize, start_z: usize) {
967:     let max_y = grid.height() - 2;
968:     for sz in 0..stamp.depth {
969:         for sx in 0..stamp.width {
970:             let val = stamp.data[sz * stamp.width + sx];
971:             let vx = start_x + sx;
972:             let vz = start_z + sz;
973:             if val == 1 {
974:                 for y in 1..=3 {
975:                     grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_WALL);
976:                 }
977:             } else if val == 2 {
978:                 for y in 1..=max_y {
979:                     grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_WALL);
980:                 }
981:             } else if val == 3 {
982:                 for y in 1..=1 {
983:                     grid.set(vx, y, vz, VOXEL_WALL);
984:                 }
985:             } else if val == 4 {
986:                 // Raised floor
987:                 grid.set(vx, 1, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
988:                 grid.set(vx, 2, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
989:             } else if val == 5 {
990:                 // Step 1
991:                 grid.set(vx, 1, vz, VOXEL_FLOOR);
992:             } else if val == 6 { // Step 2
993:                 // Just floor, already set
994:             }
995:         }
996:     }
997: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs
````rust
  1: //! A finite, one-sided spotlight used by the CPU splatter.
  2: //!
  3: //! The module keeps the four independent responsibilities visible:
  4: //!
  5: //! 1. [`cone_falloff`] describes the lamp's angular intensity profile;
  6: //! 2. inverse-square attenuation describes transport through distance;
  7: //! 3. a Lambert cosine describes how the receiver faces the lamp;
  8: //! 4. [`segment_is_occluded`] optionally tests geometric visibility.
  9: //!
 10: //! Occlusion is deliberately not folded into the light equation. Disabling
 11: //! `rt_beam_occlusion` removes only the visibility query; it cannot change
 12: //! the cone, range, color, or receiver response.
 13: 
 14: use crate::application::ports::ChunkDraw;
 15: #[cfg(test)]
 16: use crate::application::rendering::compact_support_window;
 17: use crate::application::rendering::{
 18:     FLASHLIGHT_SPEC, finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation, lambertian_receiver_cosine,
 19: };
 20: 
 21: use super::camera::{Camera, dot};
 22: use super::raycast::{ray_box_interval, svo_segment_is_occluded};
 23: use super::settings::CpuFlashlightVisibility;
 24: 
 25: /// Full-strength core and soft outer edge of the angular profile.
 26: pub const INNER_DEG: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.inner_degrees;
 27: pub const OUTER_DEG: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.outer_degrees;
 28: /// Finite support of the lamp in world units.
 29: pub const RANGE_END: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.range;
 30: /// Radiometric scale before inverse-square transport. It is intentionally a
 31: /// named calibration constant rather than a hidden post-lighting boost.
 32: pub const INTENSITY: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.intensity;
 33: /// Finite source-radius clamp, preventing a singularity against the lamp.
 34: pub const MINIMUM_DISTANCE: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.minimum_distance;
 35: /// Lamp offset from the eye: a small hand-held parallax, not an eye glow.
 36: pub const LAMP_FORWARD: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.forward_offset;
 37: pub const LAMP_DOWN: f32 = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.downward_offset;
 38: /// Warm-white spectral tint in linear RGB.
 39: pub const TINT: [f32; 3] = FLASHLIGHT_SPEC.tint;
 40: 
 41: /// Fixed world-space endpoint tolerances for the visibility segment.
 42: const OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 43: const OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS: f32 = 0.02;
 44: 
 45: fn smoothstep01(t: f32) -> f32 {
 46:     let t = t.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 47:     t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
 48: }
 49: 
 50: /// Angular intensity: one in the core, zero outside the outer cone, and a
 51: /// smooth transition between them. `alignment` is `cos(theta)`.
 52: pub fn cone_falloff(alignment: f32) -> f32 {
 53:     let inner_cos = INNER_DEG.to_radians().cos();
 54:     let outer_cos = OUTER_DEG.to_radians().cos();
 55:     if !alignment.is_finite() || alignment <= outer_cos {
 56:         return 0.0;
 57:     }
 58:     smoothstep01((alignment - outer_cos) / (inner_cos - outer_cos))
 59: }
 60: 
 61: /// Compact-support window used by the inverse-square term. Exposing it
 62: /// separately makes range behavior easy to inspect in diagnostics/tests.
 63: #[cfg(test)]
 64: pub fn range_falloff(distance: f32) -> f32 {
 65:     compact_support_window(distance, RANGE_END)
 66: }
 67: 
 68: fn lamp_position(cam: &Camera) -> [f32; 3] {
 69:     [
 70:         cam.pos[0] + cam.forward[0] * LAMP_FORWARD,
 71:         cam.pos[1] + cam.forward[1] * LAMP_FORWARD - LAMP_DOWN,
 72:         cam.pos[2] + cam.forward[2] * LAMP_FORWARD,
 73:     ]
 74: }
 75: 
 76: fn normalized_direction(from: [f32; 3], to: [f32; 3]) -> Option<([f32; 3], f32)> {
 77:     let delta = [to[0] - from[0], to[1] - from[1], to[2] - from[2]];
 78:     let distance = dot(delta, delta).sqrt();
 79:     if !distance.is_finite() || distance <= 1.0e-4 {
 80:         return None;
 81:     }
 82:     Some((delta.map(|component| component / distance), distance))
 83: }
 84: 
 85: /// The splatter shades an axis-aligned cube at one representative surface
 86: /// point and normal. Full bounds stop the visibility ray at the physical
 87: /// near face; transport is evaluated at `sample_position`.
 88: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 89: pub struct BeamReceiver {
 90:     center: [f32; 3],
 91:     sample_position: [f32; 3],
 92:     half_extent: f32,
 93:     normal: [f32; 3],
 94: }
 95: 
 96: impl BeamReceiver {
 97:     #[cfg(test)]
 98:     pub fn cube(center: [f32; 3], world_size: f32, normal: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 99:         Self {
100:             center,
101:             sample_position: center,
102:             half_extent: (world_size * 0.5).max(0.0),
103:             normal,
104:         }
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Uses an explicit representative point on the cube's visible surface
108:     /// while retaining the full bounds for the occlusion endpoint.
109:     pub fn surface_sample(
110:         center: [f32; 3],
111:         world_size: f32,
112:         sample_position: [f32; 3],
113:         normal: [f32; 3],
114:     ) -> Self {
115:         Self {
116:             center,
117:             sample_position,
118:             half_extent: (world_size * 0.5).max(0.0),
119:             normal,
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     fn bounds(self) -> ([f32; 3], [f32; 3]) {
124:         (
125:             self.center.map(|value| value - self.half_extent),
126:             self.center.map(|value| value + self.half_extent),
127:         )
128:     }
129: }
130: 
131: /// Pure unoccluded spotlight irradiance at one representative receiver.
132: ///
133: /// ```text
134: /// E = tint * I * cone(theta) * window(d, R) / max(d, d_min)^2
135: ///          * max(dot(n, omega_to_lamp), 0)
136: /// ```
137: pub fn unoccluded_irradiance(cam: &Camera, receiver: BeamReceiver) -> [f32; 3] {
138:     let lamp = lamp_position(cam);
139:     let Some((lamp_to_receiver, distance)) = normalized_direction(lamp, receiver.sample_position)
140:     else {
141:         return [0.0; 3];
142:     };
143: 
144:     let cone = cone_falloff(dot(lamp_to_receiver, cam.forward));
145:     let facing = lambertian_receiver_cosine(receiver.normal, lamp_to_receiver.map(|v| -v));
146:     let attenuation =
147:         finite_range_inverse_square_attenuation(distance, RANGE_END, MINIMUM_DISTANCE);
148:     let scalar = INTENSITY * cone * facing * attenuation;
149:     TINT.map(|channel| channel * scalar)
150: }
151: 
152: fn occlusion_trace_length(lamp_to_receiver_face: f32) -> Option<f32> {
153:     let length = lamp_to_receiver_face - OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS - OCCLUSION_RECEIVER_BIAS;
154:     (length > 0.0).then_some(length)
155: }
156: 
157: /// Tests only visibility of the finite lamp-to-receiver segment.
158: fn segment_is_occluded(
159:     cam: &Camera,
160:     atlas: &[u32],
161:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
162:     receiver: BeamReceiver,
163: ) -> bool {
164:     let lamp = lamp_position(cam);
165:     let Some((direction, _)) = normalized_direction(lamp, receiver.sample_position) else {
166:         return false;
167:     };
168:     let (bounds_min, bounds_max) = receiver.bounds();
169:     let Some(interval) = ray_box_interval(lamp, direction, bounds_min, bounds_max) else {
170:         return false;
171:     };
172:     let receiver_face = interval.entry.max(0.0);
173:     let Some(max_trace) = occlusion_trace_length(receiver_face) else {
174:         return false;
175:     };
176:     let origin = [
177:         lamp[0] + direction[0] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
178:         lamp[1] + direction[1] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
179:         lamp[2] + direction[2] * OCCLUSION_ORIGIN_BIAS,
180:     ];
181:     svo_segment_is_occluded(atlas, chunks, origin, direction, max_trace)
182: }
183: 
184: /// Spotlight irradiance with optional SVO visibility. The toggle is an
185: /// independent cost/quality switch: off is exactly the pure unoccluded term.
186: pub fn beam_contribution(
187:     cam: &Camera,
188:     atlas: &[u32],
189:     chunks: &[ChunkDraw],
190:     receiver: BeamReceiver,
191:     visibility: CpuFlashlightVisibility,
192: ) -> [f32; 3] {
193:     let irradiance = unoccluded_irradiance(cam, receiver);
194:     if irradiance == [0.0; 3] {
195:         return irradiance;
196:     }
197:     if visibility == CpuFlashlightVisibility::TraceScene
198:         && segment_is_occluded(cam, atlas, chunks, receiver)
199:     {
200:         [0.0; 3]
201:     } else {
202:         irradiance
203:     }
204: }
205: 
206: #[cfg(test)]
207: mod tests {

209:     use crate::application::ports::FrameParams;

  1: //! Native unit tests for the CPU splatter. Everything here runs with plain
  2: //! `cargo test` — no GPU, no browser.
  3: 
  4: use super::atlas::build_mips;
  5: use super::camera::Camera;
  6: use super::raycast::trace_svo;
  7: use super::settings::{CpuRenderSettings, CpuShadowMode};
  8: use super::shading::FrameLighting;
  9: use super::*;
 10: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, LightKind, LightSource, RendererPort};
 11: use vackrooms::adapters::octree_gpu_serializer::OctreeGpuSerializer;
 12: use vackrooms::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::SparseVoxelOctree;
 13: 
 14: /// depth-2 SVO (4^3) with one solid voxel, serialized like production.
 15: fn one_voxel_atlas(color: u32, light: u8) -> (Vec<u32>, u32) {
 16:     let mut svo = SparseVoxelOctree::new(2, 4.0);
 17:     svo.set(1, 1, 1, 1, color, [light; 3], 0);
 18:     let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
 19:     (gpu.texel_data, svo.root as u32)
 20: }
 21: 
 22: fn frame_at(pos: [f32; 3], yaw: f32) -> FrameParams {
 23:     FrameParams {
 24:         camera_pos: pos,
 25:         yaw,
 26:         pitch: 0.0,
 27:         flashlight: false,
 28:         ..FrameParams::default()
 29:     }
 30: }
 31: 
 32: fn center_pixel(r: &SoftwareRasterizer) -> [u8; 4] {
 33:     let idx = (r.height() / 2 * r.width() + r.width() / 2) * 4;
 34:     let fb = r.framebuffer();
 35:     [fb[idx], fb[idx + 1], fb[idx + 2], fb[idx + 3]]
 36: }
 37: 
 38: #[test]
 39: fn voxel_in_front_of_camera_covers_center_pixel() {
 40:     let (atlas, root) = one_voxel_atlas(0xFF8040, 15);
 41:     let mut r = SoftwareRasterizer::new(64, 64);
 42:     r.upload_atlas(&atlas);
 43: 
 44:     // Voxel spans (1..2)^3; look at its center from -z (yaw = PI faces +z).
 45:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
 46:         origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 47:         root_index: root as i32,
 48:         world_size: 4.0,
 49:         voxel_size: 1.0,
 50:         svo_depth: 2,
 51:     }];
 52:     r.draw(&frame_at([1.5, 1.5, -2.0], std::f32::consts::PI), &chunks);
 53: 
 54:     let px = center_pixel(&r);
 55:     assert!(px[0] > 0, "ambient-visible red channel, got {:?}", px);
 56:     assert!(px[0] > px[2], "red voxel must stay reddish, got {:?}", px);
 57: 
 58:     // A corner pixel remains the indoor fog background rather than inheriting
 59:     // the voxel's shaded color.
 60:     let fb = r.framebuffer();
 61:     assert_ne!(&fb[0..3], &px[0..3]);
 62: }

292: #[test]
293: fn mip_aggregation_works_for_root_last_node_order() {
294:     // BuildOctreeUseCase (the production chunk pipeline) pushes children
295:     // BEFORE their parent, so the root is the LAST node — the opposite
296:     // order of SparseVoxelOctree::set. build_mips must handle both.
297:     use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_WALL, VoxelGrid};
298:     use vackrooms::domain::use_cases::build_octree::BuildOctreeUseCase;
299: 
300:     let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 4, 4);
301:     grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
302:     grid.set(3, 3, 3, VOXEL_WALL);
303:     let svo = BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, 2, 4.0);
304:     let gpu = OctreeGpuSerializer::serialize_to_gpu_data(&svo);
305:     let mips = build_mips(&gpu.texel_data);
306: 
307:     let root = &mips[svo.root];
308:     assert!(
309:         root.occupancy > 0.0,
310:         "root mip must see its solid descendants, got occupancy 0"
311:     );

395: #[test]
396: fn exact_entry_face_changes_the_lambert_response_at_an_axis_boundary() {
397:     let mut r = SoftwareRasterizer::new(16, 16);
398:     let center = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
399: 
400:     // Case A: Camera Y is 1.01 (above the center, Y-dominant)
401:     let frame_a = FrameParams {
402:         camera_pos: [-1.0, 1.01, -0.1],
403:         yaw: 0.0,
404:         pitch: 0.0,
405:         flashlight: false,
406:         ..FrameParams::default()
407:     };
408:     let cam_a = Camera::new(&frame_a, 16, 16, &CpuRenderSettings::default());
409: 
410:     // Case B: Camera Y is 0.99 (below Case A, X-dominant)
411:     let frame_b = FrameParams {
412:         camera_pos: [-1.0, 0.99, -0.1],
413:         yaw: 0.0,
414:         pitch: 0.0,
415:         flashlight: false,
416:         ..FrameParams::default()
417:     };
418:     let cam_b = Camera::new(&frame_b, 16, 16, &CpuRenderSettings::default());
419: 
420:     r.clear();
421:     let fixture = [LightSource {
422:         id: 1,
423:         position: [0.0, 5.0, 0.0],
424:         half_size: [2.0, 2.0],
425:         color: [1.0, 0.9, 0.7],
426:         radius: 20.0,
427:         intensity: 10.0,
428:         kind: LightKind::CeilingPanel,
429:         flicker_mode: 0,
430:         enabled: true,
431:     }];
432: 
433:     r.shade_and_splat_with_frame_lighting(
434:         &cam_a,
435:         &[],
436:         FrameLighting::unshadowed(&fixture),
437:         center,
438:         8.0,                   // world_size
439:         8.0,                   // px — the center pixel both cases read
440:         8.0,                   // py
441:         1.0,                   // half_px
442:         1.0,                   // dist
443:         [100.0, 100.0, 100.0], // base color
444:         15.0,                  // light level
445:         false,                 // is_emissive
446:         1,                     // crowded siblings
447:     );
448:     let color_a = center_pixel(&r);
449: 
450:     r.clear();
451:     r.shade_and_splat_with_frame_lighting(
452:         &cam_b,
453:         &[],
454:         FrameLighting::unshadowed(&fixture),
455:         center,
456:         8.0,
457:         8.0,
458:         8.0,
459:         1.0,
460:         1.0,
461:         [100.0, 100.0, 100.0],
462:         15.0,
463:         false,
464:         1,
465:     );
466:     let color_b = center_pixel(&r);
467: 
468:     // The Y entry face sees the overhead panel. The neighboring X entry face
469:     // does not: this discontinuity is the exact AABB/Lambert result, not a
470:     // soft diagonal normal invented to hide a face boundary.
471:     assert!(
472:         color_a[0] > color_b[0] + 10,
473:         "expected exact face response: y-face={color_a:?}, x-face={color_b:?}"
474:     );
475: }

572: #[test]
573: fn camera_inside_large_solid_leaf_terminates_under_budget() {
574:     const VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP: u8 = 3;
575: 
576:     let mut atlas = vec![0u32; 4];
577:     atlas[0] = 1; // Leaf
578:     atlas[1] = 1; // Solid voxel type
579:     atlas[2] = 0xFFFFFF; // White color
580:     atlas[3] = 15; // quantized diffuse fill
581: 
582:     let mut r = SoftwareRasterizer::new(64, 64);
583:     // A camera-plane box must subdivide for exact clipped coverage. Use the
584:     // minimum supported cap so even a completely visible eight-way walk has
585:     // a small, deterministic upper bound independent of culling details.
586:     r.settings.max_virtual_depth = VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP;
587:     r.upload_atlas(&atlas);
588: 
589:     let chunks = [ChunkDraw {
590:         origin: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
591:         root_index: 0,
592:         world_size: 16.0, // Very large leaf
593:         voxel_size: 16.0,
594:         svo_depth: 0,
595:     }];
596: 
597:     // Camera inside the bounding sphere of the root chunk.
598:     r.draw(&frame_at([8.0, 8.0, 8.0], 0.0), &chunks);
599: 
600:     let stats = r.telemetry();
601:     let complete_tree_visit_bound = (8usize.pow(u32::from(VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP) + 1) - 1) / (8 - 1);
602: 
603:     assert_eq!(
604:         stats.max_virtual_depth,
605:         usize::from(VIRTUAL_DEPTH_CAP),
606:         "camera-plane coverage should refine to the explicit virtual-depth cap"
607:     );
608:     assert!(
609:         complete_tree_visit_bound < stats.node_soft_limit,
610:         "test fixture's complete tree must fit below the soft work budget"
611:     );
612:     assert!(
613:         stats.visited_nodes <= complete_tree_visit_bound,

707: fn trace_through_empty_lower_octant_still_finds_the_wall() {

852:     // camera looking down the column. The near wall face is lit; if we

868:     // the near voxel: an occlusion trace stopping short of the far surface
869:     // must report the near wall.

871:         &gpu.texel_data,

  1: //! First-person player controller: mouse look, WASD movement with friction,
  2: //! and axis-separated sliding collision against the [`CollisionWorld`].
  3: //!
  4: //! The tuning constants are carried over 1:1 from the original JS client so
  5: //! the wasm port feels identical.
  6: 
  7: use crate::application::collision::CollisionWorld;
  8: 
  9: /// Acceleration applied while a movement key is held (units/s^2 toward the
 10: /// wish direction). Terminal speed = ACCELERATION / FRICTION = 2.5 u/s (increased from 0.5 u/s).
 11: const ACCELERATION: f32 = 20.0;
 12: /// Exponential velocity damping factor (1/s).
 13: const FRICTION: f32 = 8.0;
 14: /// Radians of yaw/pitch per pixel of mouse movement.
 15: const MOUSE_SENSITIVITY: f32 = 0.002;
 16: /// Pitch is clamped just short of straight up/down to avoid gimbal flip.
 17: const PITCH_LIMIT: f32 = std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2 - 0.05;
 18: 
 19: /// Which movement keys are currently held.
 20: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
 21: pub struct MoveIntent {
 22:     pub forward: bool,
 23:     pub backward: bool,
 24:     pub left: bool,
 25:     pub right: bool,
 26:     pub turn_left: bool,
 27:     pub turn_right: bool,
 28: }
 29: 
 30: /// Player state. Position is the *eye* position in world space.
 31: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 32: pub struct Player {
 33:     pub position: [f32; 3],
 34:     pub yaw: f32,
 35:     pub pitch: f32,
 36:     /// Velocity in camera-local space: x = strafe, z = forward.
 37:     vel_strafe: f32,
 38:     vel_forward: f32,
 39: }
 40: 
 41: impl Player {
 42:     pub fn new(position: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
 43:         Self {
 44:             position,
 45:             yaw: 0.0,
 46:             pitch: 0.0,
 47:             vel_strafe: 0.0,
 48:             vel_forward: 0.0,
 49:         }
 50:     }
 51: 
 52:     /// Moves the player to an authored recovery point and clears momentum.
 53:     /// Pit relocation uses this instead of assigning `position` directly so
 54:     /// the velocity that carried the player over the edge cannot immediately
 55:     /// push them back into the same hazard.
 56:     pub fn relocate(&mut self, position: [f32; 3]) {
 57:         self.position = position;
 58:         self.vel_strafe = 0.0;
 59:         self.vel_forward = 0.0;
 60:     }
 61: 
 62:     /// Applies a mouse movement delta (in pixels) to yaw/pitch.
 63:     pub fn apply_look(&mut self, dx: f32, dy: f32) {
 64:         self.yaw -= dx * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY;
 65:         self.pitch = (self.pitch - dy * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY).clamp(-PITCH_LIMIT, PITCH_LIMIT);
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     /// World-space unit forward vector projected on the ground plane.
 69:     pub fn forward(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 70:         [-self.yaw.sin(), 0.0, -self.yaw.cos()]
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     /// World-space unit right vector on the ground plane.
 74:     pub fn right(&self) -> [f32; 3] {
 75:         [self.yaw.cos(), 0.0, -self.yaw.sin()]
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     /// Integrates one physics step and resolves collision by sliding:
 79:     /// the X and Z axes are moved and tested independently, so hitting a
 80:     /// wall diagonally slides the player along it instead of stopping dead.
 81:     pub fn step(&mut self, dt: f32, intent: &MoveIntent, world: &CollisionWorld) {
 82:         self.step_with_effort(dt, intent, world, 1.0);
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     /// [`Player::step`] with a bounded effort multiplier from the embodied
 86:     /// exertion model. Effort scales the wish acceleration, so both terminal
 87:     /// speed (`ACCELERATION * effort / FRICTION`) and responsiveness degrade
 88:     /// together, smoothly — friction and collision behavior are untouched.
 89:     pub fn step_with_effort(
 90:         &mut self,
 91:         dt: f32,
 92:         intent: &MoveIntent,
 93:         world: &CollisionWorld,
 94:         effort: f32,
 95:     ) {
 96:         let effort = if effort.is_finite() {
 97:             effort.clamp(0.05, 1.0)
 98:         } else {
 99:             1.0
100:         };
101:         // Friction: exponential-style decay, matching `v -= v * 8 * dt`.
102:         self.vel_strafe -= self.vel_strafe * FRICTION * dt;
103:         self.vel_forward -= self.vel_forward * FRICTION * dt;
104: 
105:         // Turn via keyboard (Doom controls)
106:         let turn_speed = 3.0; // radians per second
107:         if intent.turn_left {
108:             self.yaw += turn_speed * dt;
109:         }
110:         if intent.turn_right {
111:             self.yaw -= turn_speed * dt;
112:         }
113: 
114:         let mut wish_forward = (intent.forward as i32 - intent.backward as i32) as f32;
115:         let mut wish_strafe = (intent.right as i32 - intent.left as i32) as f32;
116:         let len = (wish_forward * wish_forward + wish_strafe * wish_strafe).sqrt();
117:         if len > 0.0 {
118:             wish_forward /= len;
119:             wish_strafe /= len;
120:         }
121: 
122:         self.vel_forward += wish_forward * ACCELERATION * effort * dt;
123:         self.vel_strafe += wish_strafe * ACCELERATION * effort * dt;
124: 
125:         let fwd = self.forward();
126:         let rgt = self.right();
127:         let step_x = (fwd[0] * self.vel_forward + rgt[0] * self.vel_strafe) * dt;
128:         let step_z = (fwd[2] * self.vel_forward + rgt[2] * self.vel_strafe) * dt;
129: 
130:         let old = self.position;
131: 
132:         self.position[0] = old[0] + step_x;
133:         if world.collides(self.position) {
134:             self.position[0] = old[0];
135:         }
136: 
137:         self.position[2] = old[2] + step_z;
138:         if world.collides(self.position) {
139:             self.position[2] = old[2];
140:         }
141:     }
142: }

````rust
  1: //! Renderer optimization toggles — one switch per labeled optimization.
  2: //!
  3: //! Every renderer in the engine (GPU surfaces, GPU face splats, the SVO
  4: //! raymarcher, and the CPU splatter) is written as a *correct, simple
  5: //! reference path* plus a set of clearly labeled optimizations layered on
  6: //! top. Each optimization can be disabled at runtime, which serves three
  7: //! purposes:
  8: //!
  9: //! 1. **Debugging** — when a frame looks wrong, binary-search the toggles to
 10: //!    find which optimization broke it.
 11: //! 2. **Benchmarking** — measure exactly what each optimization buys on a
 12: //!    given machine (the HUD shows frame times).
 13: //! 3. **Documentation** — the toggle list *is* the catalog of every shortcut
 14: //!    the pipeline takes.
 15: //!
 16: //! The struct is plain data with no browser dependencies, so it is natively
 17: //! unit-tested. It crosses the wasm boundary as a bitfield (one `AtomicU32`
 18: //! in `lib.rs`). Each browser driver snapshots it once at the frame boundary;
 19: //! platform-free render code receives the snapshot by value.
 20: //!
 21: //! URL controls: `?rt_hiz=0&rt_shadows=0` … (`rt_<name>=0|1`). The settings
 22: //! menu calls the `set_render_toggle(name, enabled)` wasm export with the
 23: //! same names.
 24: 
 25: /// One on/off switch per optimization, across all render paths.
 26: ///
 27: /// Correctness-preserving switches default on. The approximate diffuse-fill
 28: /// bake defaults off: first boot uses the strict analytic-light image, while
 29: /// `rt_bake=1` opts into the quantized field explicitly.
 30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 31: pub struct RenderToggles {
 32:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 33:     // CPU splatter (SoftwareRasterizer)
 34:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 35:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): 8x8-tile coarse hierarchical z-buffer. Rejects a
 36:     /// whole octree subtree with a handful of tile reads when something
 37:     /// nearer already covers its screen bounds. Off = every node is tested
 38:     /// per-pixel by the fine z-buffer only.
 39:     pub hierarchical_z: bool,
 40:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + splat + raymarch): near-to-far traversal,
 41:     /// submission, or resident-chunk selection. Maximizes early exits and
 42:     /// z-rejection. Off retains each strategy's deterministic reference order.
 43:     pub front_to_back: bool,
 44:     /// OPTIMIZATION (raymarch): jump across the complete empty SVO leaf
 45:     /// containing the current sample. Off = diagnostic finest-voxel DDA;
 46:     /// both paths use the same exact point lookup and must report the same
 47:     /// nearest hit/material/normal.
 48:     pub empty_space_skip: bool,
 49:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): coarse-to-fine LOD — a subtree whose projection
 50:     /// fits in ~a pixel is drawn as one MIP-filtered splat instead of being
 51:     /// descended. Off = full descent to leaves regardless of distance, except
 52:     /// for the renderer's non-optional malformed/workload safety cap.
 53:     pub mip_lod: bool,
 54:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): the flashlight's occlusion ray (one SVO trace per
 55:     /// shaded splat while the flashlight is on). This is a *quality*
 56:     /// optimization: off means the beam shines through walls but shading
 57:     /// gets cheaper.
 58:     pub flashlight_occlusion: bool,
 59:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): query the fine depth buffer before evaluating
 60:     /// fixture, hero, and flashlight radiance. Off = shade every projected
 61:     /// splat and let the ordinary write-time depth test reject it. The image
 62:     /// is identical; only hidden-splat shading work changes.
 63:     pub deferred_shading: bool,
 64:     /// APPROXIMATION (CPU): sibling-count ambient occlusion. Off is the
 65:     /// material/lighting reference with unit ambient visibility.
 66:     pub ambient_occlusion: bool,
 67:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 68:     // GPU paths (surface / splat / raymarch)
 69:     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
 70:     /// Direct-light visibility. Raster strategies use a hero-fixture depth
 71:     /// map; raymarch traces finite SVO segments to analytic emitter samples.
 72:     /// Off keeps otherwise-identical unoccluded direct lighting.
 73:     pub shadow_pass: bool,
 74:     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): per-cell instance-range culling. Face instances
 75:     /// are grouped into spatial cells; invisible cells are skipped and
 76:     /// visible neighbors coalesce into one instanced draw. Off = every
 77:     /// resident face is drawn every frame.
 78:     pub cell_culling: bool,
 79:     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): stop submitting whole far chunks after the
 80:     /// profile's face budget is exhausted. Off = draw every visible face;
 81:     /// useful as the correctness/reference path when diagnosing pop-out.
 82:     pub face_budget: bool,
 83:     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + GPU): range rejection for every strategy, plus
 84:     /// conservative camera visibility for raster paths. Raymarch filters
 85:     /// complete chunk bounds before its resident-set cap. Off keeps all
 86:     /// resident chunks eligible.
 87:     pub distance_cull: bool,
 88:     /// Dither/grain/banding-noise post effects (GPU). A visual feature more
 89:     /// than a speedup; toggle to isolate its contribution to the image.
 90:     pub dither: bool,
 91:     /// Optional quantized diffuse fill in the CPU, indexed-surface, and splat
 92:     /// strategies. Analytic fixtures remain authoritative; raymarch stays on
 93:     /// analytic lighting because its stored bake is face-independent.
 94:     pub baked_lighting: bool,
 95: }
 96: 
 97: impl Default for RenderToggles {
 98:     fn default() -> Self {
 99:         Self {
100:             hierarchical_z: true,
101:             front_to_back: true,
102:             empty_space_skip: true,
103:             mip_lod: true,
104:             flashlight_occlusion: true,
105:             deferred_shading: true,
106:             ambient_occlusion: true,
107:             shadow_pass: true,
108:             cell_culling: true,
109:             face_budget: true,
110:             distance_cull: true,
111:             dither: true,
112:             baked_lighting: false,
113:         }
114:     }
115: }
116: 
117: impl RenderToggles {
118:     /// Baseline used when a renderer profile admits only a named subset of
119:     /// the global switchboard.
120:     pub const fn disabled() -> Self {
121:         Self {
122:             hierarchical_z: false,
123:             front_to_back: false,
124:             empty_space_skip: false,
125:             mip_lod: false,
126:             flashlight_occlusion: false,
127:             deferred_shading: false,
128:             ambient_occlusion: false,
129:             shadow_pass: false,
130:             cell_culling: false,
131:             face_budget: false,
132:             distance_cull: false,
133:             dither: false,
134:             baked_lighting: false,
135:         }
136:     }
137: }
138: 
139: /// Canonical query-name/bit ordering used by parsing and bitfield round trips.
140: const TOGGLE_BITS: [(&str, u32); 13] = [
141:     ("hiz", 1 << 0),
142:     ("f2b", 1 << 1),
143:     ("mips", 1 << 2),
144:     ("beam_occlusion", 1 << 3),
145:     ("shadows", 1 << 4),
146:     ("cells", 1 << 5),
147:     ("budget", 1 << 6),
148:     ("cull", 1 << 7),
149:     ("dither", 1 << 8),
150:     ("skip", 1 << 9),
151:     ("bake", 1 << 10),
152:     ("deferred", 1 << 11),
153:     ("ao", 1 << 12),
154: ];
155: 
156: impl RenderToggles {
157:     fn field_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<&mut bool> {
158:         Some(match name {
159:             "hiz" => &mut self.hierarchical_z,
160:             "f2b" => &mut self.front_to_back,
161:             "skip" => &mut self.empty_space_skip,
162:             "mips" => &mut self.mip_lod,
163:             "beam_occlusion" => &mut self.flashlight_occlusion,
164:             "deferred" => &mut self.deferred_shading,
165:             "ao" => &mut self.ambient_occlusion,
166:             "shadows" => &mut self.shadow_pass,
167:             "cells" => &mut self.cell_culling,
168:             "budget" => &mut self.face_budget,
169:             "cull" => &mut self.distance_cull,
170:             "dither" => &mut self.dither,
171:             "bake" => &mut self.baked_lighting,
172:             _ => return None,
173:         })
174:     }
175: 
176:     fn field(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
177:         let mut copy = *self;
178:         copy.field_mut(name).map(|b| *b)
179:     }
180: 
181:     /// Sets one toggle by its short name. Unknown names are ignored (the
182:     /// settings menu and old URLs must never crash the engine).
183:     pub fn set(&mut self, name: &str, enabled: bool) {
184:         if let Some(field) = self.field_mut(name) {
185:             *field = enabled;
186:         }
187:     }
188: 
189:     /// Reads one toggle by its short name. Returning `None` for unknown
190:     /// names keeps diagnostics and browser tests on the same catalog as the
191:     /// parser and setter.
192:     pub fn enabled(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
193:         self.field(name)
194:     }
195: 
196:     /// Packs the toggles into a bitfield for the atomic global in `lib.rs`.
197:     pub fn to_bits(self) -> u32 {
198:         let mut bits = 0;
199:         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
200:             if self.field(name).expect("table names match fields") {
201:                 bits |= bit;
202:             }
203:         }
204:         bits
205:     }
206: 
207:     /// Inverse of [`Self::to_bits`].
208:     pub fn from_bits(bits: u32) -> Self {
209:         let mut toggles = Self::default();
210:         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
211:             toggles.set(name, bits & bit != 0);
212:         }
213:         toggles
214:     }
215: }
216: 
217: /// Applies `rt_<name>=0|1` pairs from a URL query (with or without the
218: /// leading `?`) on top of the defaults. Unknown keys and malformed values
219: /// are ignored, matching the generation-knob parser's tolerance.
220: pub fn parse_render_toggles(query: &str) -> RenderToggles {
221:     let mut toggles = RenderToggles::default();
222:     for pair in query.trim_start_matches('?').split('&') {
223:         let Some((key, value)) = pair.split_once('=') else {
224:             continue;
225:         };
226:         let Some(name) = key.strip_prefix("rt_") else {
227:             continue;
228:         };
229:         match value {
230:             "0" | "false" | "off" => toggles.set(name, false),
231:             "1" | "true" | "on" => toggles.set(name, true),
232:             _ => {}
233:         }
234:     }
235:     toggles
236: }
237: 
238: #[cfg(test)]
239: mod tests {
240:     use super::*;
241: 
242:     #[test]
243:     fn defaults_use_analytic_static_lighting() {
244:         let t = RenderToggles::default();
245:         assert!(t.hierarchical_z && t.front_to_back && t.empty_space_skip && t.mip_lod);
246:         assert!(t.flashlight_occlusion && t.deferred_shading && t.ambient_occlusion);
247:         assert!(t.shadow_pass && t.cell_culling && t.face_budget);
248:         assert!(t.distance_cull && t.dither);
249:         assert!(!t.baked_lighting);
250:         assert_eq!(RenderToggles::disabled().to_bits(), 0);
251:     }
252: 
253:     #[test]
254:     fn bits_round_trip_every_combination_of_low_bits() {
255:         for bits in 0..(1u32 << TOGGLE_BITS.len()) {
256:             assert_eq!(RenderToggles::from_bits(bits).to_bits(), bits);
257:         }
258:     }
259: 
260:     #[test]
261:     fn query_disables_named_toggles_only() {
262:         let t = parse_render_toggles("?seed=7&rt_hiz=0&rt_shadows=off&rt_bogus=0");
263:         assert!(!t.hierarchical_z);
264:         assert!(!t.shadow_pass);
265:         assert!(t.front_to_back, "unrelated toggles stay on");
266:     }
267: 
268:     #[test]
269:     fn set_ignores_unknown_names() {
270:         let mut t = RenderToggles::default();
271:         t.set("not_a_toggle", false);
272:         assert_eq!(t, RenderToggles::default());
273:     }
274: 
275:     #[test]
276:     fn enabled_uses_the_same_name_catalog_as_set() {
277:         let mut t = RenderToggles::default();
278:         t.set("budget", false);
279:         assert_eq!(t.enabled("budget"), Some(false));
280:         assert_eq!(t.enabled("not_a_toggle"), None);
281:     }
282: }

  1: //! Per-frame light selection — one implementation for the surface and
  2: //! splat renderers, which previously carried diverging copies.
  3: //!
  4: //! Inputs: fixture lights from every visible chunk (deduplicated by id —
  5: //! a fixture near a chunk border is listed by several chunks) plus the
  6: //! frame's dynamic lights (dropped flares). The most important lights fill
  7: //! the bounded shader slots; the most important *fixture* light also
  8: //! wins the hero shadow map (a flare at ankle height would collapse the
  9: //! top-down shadow frustum, so dynamic lights never own it).
 10: //!
 11: //! Importance = radius * sqrt(intensity) / (distance² + 0.1): bigger and
 12: //! brighter lights reach farther, nearby lights dominate.
 13: 
 14: use crate::application::ports::{FrameParams, LightSource, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
 15: 
 16: /// Maximum shader light slots (matches the GLSL uniform arrays).
 17: pub const MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS: usize = crate::application::ports::MAX_SCENE_LIGHTS;
 18: 
 19: /// The frame's selected lights, packed for `uniform[1i|3fv|4fv]` upload.
 20: pub struct SelectedLights {
 21:     pub count: usize,
 22:     pub positions: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 23:     pub colors: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 24:     /// Per light: radius, intensity, half_size.x, half_size.y.
 25:     pub params: [f32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
 26:     pub kinds: [i32; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
 27:     /// Slot index of the shadow-casting hero light, or -1.
 28:     pub hero_slot: i32,
 29:     /// Hero light's position/radius (meaningful when `hero_slot >= 0`).
 30:     pub hero_position: [f32; 3],
 31:     pub hero_radius: f32,
 32: }
 33: 
 34: /// Wraps the frame's dynamic lights as fixture-shaped sources with sentinel
 35: /// ids in the top range, so one selection pass handles both kinds.
 36: pub fn dynamic_light_sources(frame: &FrameParams) -> Vec<LightSource> {
 37:     frame
 38:         .active_dynamic_lights()
 39:         .iter()
 40:         .enumerate()
 41:         .map(|(i, d)| LightSource {
 42:             id: u64::MAX - i as u64,
 43:             position: d.position,
 44:             half_size: [0.25, 0.25],
 45:             color: d.color,
 46:             radius: d.radius,
 47:             intensity: d.intensity,
 48:             kind: crate::application::ports::LightKind::Point,
 49:             flicker_mode: 0,
 50:             enabled: true,
 51:         })
 52:         .collect()
 53: }
 54: 
 55: fn is_dynamic(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
 56:     light.id > u64::MAX - 16
 57: }
 58: 
 59: /// Selects and packs the frame's lights. `fixtures` should already be
 60: /// deduplicated by id (pass a `HashMap`'s values); `dynamic` comes from
 61: /// [`dynamic_light_sources`].
 62: pub fn select_lights<'a>(
 63:     fixtures: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
 64:     dynamic: &'a [LightSource],
 65:     frame: &FrameParams,
 66: ) -> SelectedLights {
 67:     let mut ranked: Vec<(&LightSource, f32)> = fixtures
 68:         .chain(dynamic.iter())
 69:         .map(|light| {
 70:             let dx = light.position[0] - frame.camera_pos[0];
 71:             let dy = light.position[1] - frame.camera_pos[1];
 72:             let dz = light.position[2] - frame.camera_pos[2];
 73:             let dist2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
 74:             (light, light.radius * light.intensity.sqrt() / (dist2 + 0.1))
 75:         })
 76:         .collect();
 77:     ranked.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
 78: 
 79:     let count = ranked.len().min(MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS);
 80:     let mut selected = SelectedLights {
 81:         count,
 82:         positions: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 83:         colors: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 3],
 84:         params: [0.0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS * 4],
 85:         kinds: [0; MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS],
 86:         hero_slot: -1,
 87:         hero_position: [0.0; 3],
 88:         hero_radius: 0.0,
 89:     };
 90:     for (i, (light, _)) in ranked[..count].iter().enumerate() {
 91:         selected.positions[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.position);
 92:         selected.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&light.color);
 93:         selected.params[i * 4] = light.radius;
 94:         selected.params[i * 4 + 1] = light.intensity;
 95:         selected.params[i * 4 + 2] = light.half_size[0];
 96:         selected.params[i * 4 + 3] = light.half_size[1];
 97:         selected.kinds[i] = light.kind as i32;
 98:     }
 99: 
100:     // Hero shadow: the strongest *fixture* light in the selected slots.
101:     if let Some(slot) = ranked[..count].iter().position(|(l, _)| !is_dynamic(l)) {
102:         selected.hero_slot = slot as i32;
103:         selected.hero_position = ranked[slot].0.position;
104:         selected.hero_radius = ranked[slot].0.radius;
105:     }
106:     selected
107: }
108: 
109: /// Flare-core uniforms (`uCoreCount`/`uCores`/`uCoreColors`), independent of
110: /// the merged light slots so a flare culled from the four shading lights
111: /// still shows its ember.
112: pub struct FlareCores {
113:     pub count: i32,
114:     /// xyz = position, w = pre-flickered intensity.
115:     pub pos_intensity: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
116:     pub colors: [f32; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
117: }
118: 
119: pub fn flare_cores(frame: &FrameParams) -> FlareCores {
120:     let cores = frame.active_dynamic_lights();
121:     let mut packed = FlareCores {
122:         count: cores.len() as i32,
123:         pos_intensity: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 4],
124:         colors: [0.0; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS * 3],
125:     };
126:     for (i, c) in cores.iter().enumerate() {
127:         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4..i * 4 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.position);
128:         packed.pos_intensity[i * 4 + 3] = c.intensity;
129:         packed.colors[i * 3..i * 3 + 3].copy_from_slice(&c.color);
130:     }
131:     packed
132: }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/gl/math.rs
