## File: src/domain/use_cases/build_octree.rs
````rust
  1: use crate::domain::entities::sparse_voxel_octree::{SparseVoxelOctree, SvoNode};
  2: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{MATERIAL_COLORS, VOXEL_AIR, VoxelGrid};
  3: 
  4: const AIR_LEAF: SvoNode = SvoNode::Leaf {
  5:     voxel_type: VOXEL_AIR,
  6:     color: 0,
  7:     light_rgb: [0; 3],
  8:     face_occlusion: 0,
  9: };
 10: 
 11: /// Use Case to convert a dense VoxelGrid into a collapsed Sparse Voxel Octree.
 12: pub struct BuildOctreeUseCase;
 13: 
 14: impl BuildOctreeUseCase {
 15:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 16:         Self
 17:     }
 18: 
 19:     /// Converts a dense VoxelGrid into an SVO of the specified depth.
 20:     pub fn execute(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, depth: u32, world_size: f32) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
 21:         self.execute_internal::<true>(grid, depth, world_size)
 22:     }
 23: 
 24:     /// Shared implementation kept generic over the pruning policy so tests can
 25:     /// compare the optimized traversal with the former exhaustive traversal.
 26:     fn execute_internal<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
 27:         &self,
 28:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
 29:         depth: u32,
 30:         world_size: f32,
 31:     ) -> SparseVoxelOctree {
 32:         let mut nodes = Vec::new();
 33:         let size = 1 << depth;
 34: 
 35:         // Recursive build from root
 36:         let root_node =
 37:             self.build_recursive::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(grid, &mut nodes, 0, 0, 0, size, depth);
 38: 
 39:         // Push the root node to the end of the nodes array
 40:         let root_idx = nodes.len();
 41:         nodes.push(root_node);
 42: 
 43:         SparseVoxelOctree {
 44:             root: root_idx,
 45:             nodes,
 46:             depth,
 47:             world_size,
 48:         }
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     fn build_recursive<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
 52:         &self,
 53:         grid: &VoxelGrid,
 54:         nodes: &mut Vec<SvoNode>,
 55:         x: u32,
 56:         y: u32,
 57:         z: u32,
 58:         size: u32,
 59:         depth: u32,
 60:     ) -> SvoNode {
 61:         // Every coordinate sampled outside the dense grid is canonical air.
 62:         // Recursive cubes only extend in the positive direction, so when the
 63:         // cube's minimum lies past any grid dimension the former exhaustive
 64:         // traversal could only collapse back to this same leaf. It also could
 65:         // not append arena nodes, which makes this short-circuit byte-for-byte
 66:         // equivalent while avoiding all descendant calls.
 67:         if PRUNE_OUTSIDE && self.region_is_outside_grid(grid, x, y, z) {
 68:             return AIR_LEAF;
 69:         }
 70: 
 71:         if depth == 0 {
 72:             let (v_type, color, ll, fo) = self.get_voxel_attrs(grid, x, y, z);
 73:             return SvoNode::Leaf {
 74:                 voxel_type: v_type,
 75:                 color,
 76:                 light_rgb: ll,
 77:                 face_occlusion: fo,
 78:             };
 79:         }
 80: 
 81:         let child_size = size / 2;
 82:         let mut children = [AIR_LEAF; 8];
 83: 
 84:         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
 85:             let dx = (octant_idx & 1) * child_size;
 86:             let dy = ((octant_idx >> 1) & 1) * child_size;
 87:             let dz = ((octant_idx >> 2) & 1) * child_size;
 88: 
 89:             children[octant_idx as usize] = self.build_recursive::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(
 90:                 grid,
 91:                 nodes,
 92:                 x + dx,
 93:                 y + dy,
 94:                 z + dz,
 95:                 child_size,
 96:                 depth - 1,
 97:             );
 98:         }
 99: 
100:         // Check if all 8 children are uniform leaves
101:         let mut uniform = true;
102:         let mut first_val = None;
103:         for child in &children {
104:             match child {
105:                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
106:                     uniform = false;
107:                     break;
108:                 }
109:                 SvoNode::Leaf {
110:                     voxel_type,
111:                     color,
112:                     light_rgb,
113:                     face_occlusion,
114:                 } => {
115:                     if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
116:                         if vt != *voxel_type
117:                             || col != *color
118:                             || ll != *light_rgb
119:                             || fo != *face_occlusion
120:                         {
121:                             uniform = false;
122:                             break;
123:                         }
124:                     } else {
125:                         first_val = Some((*voxel_type, *color, *light_rgb, *face_occlusion));
126:                     }
127:                 }
128:             }
129:         }
130: 
131:         if uniform {
132:             if let Some((vt, col, ll, fo)) = first_val {
133:                 return SvoNode::Leaf {
134:                     voxel_type: vt,
135:                     color: col,
136:                     light_rgb: ll,
137:                     face_occlusion: fo,
138:                 };
139:             }
140:         }
141: 
142:         // Push 8 children contiguously to arena
143:         let child_base_index = nodes.len() as u32;
144:         let mut child_mask = 0;
145: 
146:         for octant_idx in 0..8 {
147:             let child = children[octant_idx as usize];
148:             match child {
149:                 SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => {
150:                     if voxel_type != 0 {
151:                         child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
152:                     }
153:                 }
154:                 SvoNode::Internal { .. } => {
155:                     child_mask |= 1 << octant_idx;
156:                 }
157:             }
158:             nodes.push(child);
159:         }
160: 
161:         SvoNode::Internal {
162:             child_base_index,
163:             child_mask,
164:         }
165:     }
166: 
167:     fn region_is_outside_grid(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> bool {
168:         x as usize >= grid.width() || y as usize >= grid.height() || z as usize >= grid.depth()
169:     }
170: 
171:     fn get_voxel_attrs(&self, grid: &VoxelGrid, x: u32, y: u32, z: u32) -> (u8, u32, [u8; 3], u8) {
172:         if x >= grid.width() as u32 || y >= grid.height() as u32 || z >= grid.depth() as u32 {
173:             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0); // Out of bounds is air
174:         }
175: 
176:         let v_id = grid.get(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
177:         if v_id == VOXEL_AIR {
178:             return (0, 0, [0; 3], 0);
179:         }
180: 
181:         let ll = grid.get_light_rgb(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
182:         let fo = grid.get_face_occlusion(x as usize, y as usize, z as usize);
183:         let base_color = MATERIAL_COLORS
184:             .get(v_id as usize)
185:             .copied()
186:             .unwrap_or(0x000000);
187: 
188:         (v_id, base_color, ll, fo)
189:     }
190: }
191: 
192: #[cfg(test)]
193: mod tests {
194:     use super::*;
195:     use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
196:         FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y, VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_RED_WALL,
197:         VOXEL_WALL,
198:     };
199: 
200:     fn traversal_call_count<const PRUNE_OUTSIDE: bool>(
201:         dimensions: [u32; 3],
202:         origin: [u32; 3],
203:         depth: u32,
204:     ) -> usize {
205:         if PRUNE_OUTSIDE
206:             && (origin[0] >= dimensions[0]
207:                 || origin[1] >= dimensions[1]
208:                 || origin[2] >= dimensions[2])
209:         {
210:             return 1;
211:         }
212:         if depth == 0 {
213:             return 1;
214:         }
215: 
216:         let child_size = 1 << (depth - 1);
217:         let mut calls = 1;
218:         for octant in 0..8u32 {
219:             calls += traversal_call_count::<PRUNE_OUTSIDE>(
220:                 dimensions,
221:                 [
222:                     origin[0] + (octant & 1) * child_size,
223:                     origin[1] + ((octant >> 1) & 1) * child_size,
224:                     origin[2] + ((octant >> 2) & 1) * child_size,
225:                 ],
226:                 depth - 1,
227:             );
228:         }
229:         calls
230:     }
231: 
232:     #[test]
233:     fn test_empty_grid_collapses_to_single_root_leaf() {
234:         let grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 4, 4);
235:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
236:         let svo = builder.execute(&grid, 2, 4.0);
237: 
238:         // An entirely empty grid should collapse into a single root node (Leaf containing air)
239:         assert_eq!(svo.nodes.len(), 1);
240:         match svo.nodes[svo.root] {
241:             SvoNode::Leaf { voxel_type, .. } => assert_eq!(voxel_type, 0),
242:             _ => panic!("Expected root to be a collapsed leaf node"),
243:         }
244:     }
245: 
246:     #[test]
247:     fn test_single_voxel_splits_octree() {
248:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(4, 4, 4);
249:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL); // Set wall at origin
250: 
251:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
252:         let svo = builder.execute(&grid, 2, 4.0); // depth 2
253: 
254:         // Since there is a single wall voxel, the tree must split and cannot be collapsed completely
255:         assert!(svo.nodes.len() > 1);
256: 
257:         // The root should be an internal node
258:         match svo.nodes[svo.root] {
259:             SvoNode::Internal { child_mask, .. } => {
260:                 assert!(child_mask > 0);
261:             }
262:             _ => panic!("Expected root to be an internal parent node"),
263:         }
264: 
265:         // Let's verify we can query the wall voxel at (0,0,0)
266:         let val = svo.get(0, 0, 0);
267:         assert!(val.is_some());
268:         let (v_type, color, _, _) = val.unwrap();
269:         assert_eq!(v_type, VOXEL_WALL);
270:         assert_eq!(color, 0xddcc66);
271:     }
272: 
273:     #[test]
274:     fn outside_pruning_preserves_non_power_of_two_tree_and_lookups() {
275:         let mut grid = VoxelGrid::new(5, 3, 6);
276:         grid.set(0, 0, 0, VOXEL_WALL);
277:         grid.set_light_rgb(0, 0, 0, [7, 5, 3]);
278:         grid.set_face_occlusion(0, 0, 0, FACE_OCCLUDED_POSITIVE_Y);
279:         grid.set(3, 1, 4, VOXEL_CEILING);
280:         grid.set_light_rgb(3, 1, 4, [2, 4, 6]);
281:         grid.set(4, 2, 5, VOXEL_RED_WALL);
282:         grid.set_face_occlusion(4, 2, 5, FACE_OCCLUDED_NEGATIVE_X);
283: 
284:         let builder = BuildOctreeUseCase::new();
285:         let optimized = builder.execute_internal::<true>(&grid, 3, 8.0);
286:         let exhaustive = builder.execute_internal::<false>(&grid, 3, 8.0);
287: 
288:         assert_eq!(
289:             optimized, exhaustive,
290:             "pruning must not renumber or alter nodes"
291:         );
292:         for z in 0..8 {
293:             for y in 0..8 {
294:                 for x in 0..8 {
295:                     assert_eq!(optimized.get(x, y, z), exhaustive.get(x, y, z));
296:                 }
297:             }
298:         }
299: 
300:         let dimensions = [
301:             grid.width() as u32,
302:             grid.height() as u32,
303:             grid.depth() as u32,
304:         ];
305:         let optimized_calls = traversal_call_count::<true>(dimensions, [0; 3], 3);
306:         let exhaustive_calls = traversal_call_count::<false>(dimensions, [0; 3], 3);
307:         assert_eq!(optimized_calls, 185);
308:         assert_eq!(exhaustive_calls, 585);
309:         assert!(
310:             optimized_calls * 3 <= exhaustive_calls,
311:             "expected at least a 3x traversal reduction, got {optimized_calls} optimized calls vs {exhaustive_calls} exhaustive calls"
312:         );
313:     }
````

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders/chunks.rs
````rust
  1: //! Shared GLSL chunks — snippets spliced into more than one shader so the
  2: //! engine has exactly one definition of each cross-cutting effect.
  3: //!
  4: //! Shader sources are assembled at startup by `format!` concatenation (a
  5: //! few string copies once per program link — nothing per frame). Each chunk
  6: //! is a self-contained set of GLSL functions/consts with no `uniform`
  7: //! declarations, so any stage can include it.
  8: 
  9: /// The flashlight spotlight cone — **GLSL mirror of the single spec in
 10: /// `adapters::cpu_splatter::flashlight`** (inner/outer angle, finite-range
 11: /// inverse-square transport, lamp offset, and tint). A tuning change there
 12: /// must be mirrored here.
 13: ///
 14: /// Shape: smoothstep between an inner cone (full strength, 11°) and an
 15: /// outer cone (zero, 24°) around the camera forward axis. Transport uses a
 16: /// compact-support inverse-square law and a strict Lambert receiver cosine.
 17: pub const SPOT_CONE_GLSL: &str = r#"
 18: // --- flashlight cone (spec: adapters/cpu_splatter/flashlight.rs) ---
 19: const float SPOT_INNER_COS = 0.9816272; // cos(11 deg)
 20: const float SPOT_OUTER_COS = 0.9135455; // cos(24 deg)
 21: const float SPOT_RANGE_END = 14.0;
 22: const float SPOT_INTENSITY = 32.0;
 23: const float SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE = 0.25;
 24: const float SPOT_INV_PI = 0.3183098861837907;
 25: const vec3  SPOT_TINT = vec3(1.0, 0.91, 0.72);
 26: 
 27: // The hand-held lamp sits slightly forward of and below the eye.
 28: vec3 spotLampPos(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward) {
 29:     return camPos + camForward * 0.18 - vec3(0.0, 0.10, 0.0);
 30: }
 31: 
 32: // Angular falloff: 1 inside the inner cone, 0 outside the outer.
 33: float spotCone(vec3 beam, vec3 camForward) {
 34:     return smoothstep(SPOT_OUTER_COS, SPOT_INNER_COS, dot(beam, camForward));
 35: }
 36: 
 37: // Finite-range inverse-square transport. The compact window and its first
 38: // derivative both reach zero at RANGE_END, so the beam has no hard rim.
 39: float spotAttenuation(float dist) {
 40:     if (!(dist >= 0.0) || dist >= SPOT_RANGE_END) return 0.0;
 41:     float normalizedSquared = (dist * dist) / (SPOT_RANGE_END * SPOT_RANGE_END);
 42:     float window = max(1.0 - normalizedSquared * normalizedSquared, 0.0);
 43:     float minimumSquared = SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE * SPOT_MIN_DISTANCE;
 44:     return (window * window) / max(dist * dist, minimumSquared);
 45: }
 46: 
 47: // Lambertian reflected-radiance factor at a surface point with normal N.
 48: // The CPU contract evaluates irradiance first and multiplies albedo / PI;
 49: // folding 1/PI here preserves that exact composition at GPU call sites.
 50: vec3 spotBeam(vec3 camPos, vec3 camForward, vec3 surfacePos, vec3 N) {
 51:     vec3 lamp = spotLampPos(camPos, camForward);
 52:     vec3 toSurf = surfacePos - lamp;
 53:     float dist = length(toSurf);
 54:     vec3 beam = toSurf / max(dist, 1e-4);
 55:     float cone = spotCone(beam, camForward);
 56:     float attenuation = spotAttenuation(dist);
 57:     float facing = max(-dot(beam, N), 0.0);
 58:     return SPOT_TINT * (SPOT_INTENSITY * SPOT_INV_PI * cone * attenuation * facing);
 59: }
 60: "#;
 61: 
 62: /// Material palette lookup, shared by the surface and splat paths so both
 63: /// rasterizers color a wall identically.
 64: pub const MATERIAL_COLOR_GLSL: &str = r#"
 65: vec3 materialColor(float material) {
 66:     // Exact bytes from domain::voxel_grid::MATERIAL_COLORS. Keeping the
 67:     // integer numerators visible makes palette drift reviewable.
 68:     if (material < 1.5) return vec3(221.0, 204.0, 102.0) / 255.0;
 69:     if (material < 2.5) return vec3(153.0, 136.0,  17.0) / 255.0;
 70:     if (material < 3.5) return vec3(204.0, 204.0, 204.0) / 255.0;
 71:     if (material < 4.5) return vec3(255.0, 248.0, 214.0) / 255.0;
 72:     if (material < 5.5) return vec3(136.0,   0.0,   0.0) / 255.0;
 73:     if (material < 6.5) return vec3( 79.0, 154.0,  61.0) / 255.0;
 74:     if (material < 7.5) return vec3( 58.0, 111.0, 184.0) / 255.0;
 75:     if (material < 8.5) return vec3(107.0,  74.0,  47.0) / 255.0;
 76:     if (material < 9.5) return vec3(255.0,  68.0,  51.0) / 255.0;
 77:     if (material < 10.5) return vec3(216.0, 210.0, 192.0) / 255.0;
 78:     if (material < 11.5) return vec3(138.0, 127.0,  92.0) / 255.0;
 79:     if (material < 12.5) return vec3(194.0, 183.0, 107.0) / 255.0;
 80:     if (material < 13.5) return vec3(107.0,  94.0,  34.0) / 255.0;
 81:     if (material < 14.5) return vec3(122.0,  74.0,  38.0) / 255.0;
 82:     if (material < 15.5) return vec3( 46.0,  42.0,  34.0) / 255.0;

 94: "#;
 95: 
 96: /// World-hash and interleaved-gradient-noise helpers.
 97: ///
 98: /// OPTIMIZATION: IGN is two `fract`s and a `dot` — far cheaper than a
 99: /// sin-hash — and is used to break up 8-bit banding in fog gradients,
100: /// which is especially visible at reduced internal resolutions.
101: pub const NOISE_GLSL: &str = r#"
102: float hash3D(vec3 p) {
103:     return fract(sin(dot(p, vec3(12.9898, 78.233, 45.164))) * 43758.5453);
104: }
105: 
106: float ign(vec2 p) {
107:     vec3 magic = vec3(0.06711056, 0.00583715, 52.9829189);
108:     return fract(magic.z * fract(dot(p, magic.xy)));
109: }
110: "#;
111: 
112: /// Reinhard tone map + gamma, shared by the surface and splat fragments.
113: pub const TONE_MAP_GLSL: &str = r#"
114: vec3 toneMap(vec3 color) {
115:     color = color / (color + vec3(1.0));
116:     return pow(color, vec3(1.0 / 2.2));
117: }
118: "#;
119: 
120: /// Flare-core glow sprites: additive embers occluded by any surface nearer
121: /// than the flare along the fragment's view ray — no x-ray dots. Shared by
122: /// the surface and splat fragments; requires the `uCoreCount` / `uCores` /
123: /// `uCoreColors` uniforms to be declared before this chunk is spliced in
124: /// (both programs declare them identically).
125: pub const FLARE_CORES_GLSL: &str = r#"
126: vec3 flareCoresThroughMedium(
127:     vec3 worldPos,
128:     vec3 camPos,
129:     float fogStart,
130:     float sigmaExtinction
131: ) {
132:     vec3 toFrag = worldPos - camPos;
133:     float fragDist = length(toFrag);
134:     vec3 rd = toFrag / max(fragDist, 1e-4);
135:     vec3 sum = vec3(0.0);
136:     for (int i = 0; i < uCoreCount; i++) {
137:         vec3 toLight = uCores[i].xyz - camPos;
138:         float along = dot(toLight, rd);
139:         if (along <= 0.05 || along >= fragDist) continue;
140:         float perp = length(toLight - rd * along);
141:         float coreSize = 0.06 + along * 0.004;
142:         float core = 1.0 - smoothstep(coreSize * 0.4, coreSize, perp);
143:         float mediumDistance = max(along - max(fogStart, 0.0), 0.0);
144:         float transmittance = exp(-max(sigmaExtinction, 0.0) * mediumDistance);
145:         sum += uCoreColors[i] * uCores[i].w * core * 1.4 * transmittance;
146:     }
147:     return sum;
148: }
149: 
150: vec3 flareCores(vec3 worldPos, vec3 camPos) {
151:     return flareCoresThroughMedium(worldPos, camPos, 0.0, 0.0);
152: }
153: "#;
````

````rust
  1: //! Web Worker chunk source — the multithreaded [`ChunkSourcePort`].
  2: //!
  3: //! Each worker (`static/worker.js`) is a second instance of this same wasm
  4: //! module running on its own OS thread. The main thread posts small
  5: //! `{gen, requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality}` messages
  6: //! round-robin. Workers always generate, bake, build the collision SVO, and
  7: //! extract collision; the artifact bitfield requests only the active
  8: //! renderer's mesh, face, or serialized-node products. One encoded byte
  9: //! buffer returns through `adapters::chunk_codec`; GPU resources remain owned
 10: //! by the main-thread render driver. Healthy pools keep generation off the
 11: //! frame loop. If every worker fatally fails, the driver uses its same-thread
 12: //! source as a correctness fallback instead of leaving the world pending.
 13: //!
 14: //! Stale-result rejection lives in the engine (`install_completed`), keyed
 15: //! by the echoed request. This driver owns transport failure detection and
 16: //! reports exact failed requests through the same application port.
 17: 
 18: use std::cell::RefCell;
 19: use std::rc::Rc;
 20: 
 21: use js_sys::{ArrayBuffer, Reflect, Uint8Array};
 22: use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;

 25: use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::decode_chunk_payload;
 26: use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
 27: use crate::application::generation_worker_policy::MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS;
 28: use crate::application::ports::{
 29:     ChunkPayload, ChunkRequest, ChunkSourcePort, CompletedChunk, RenderArtifactNeeds,
 30: };
 31: use crate::drivers::generation_worker_requests::GenerationWorkerRequests;
 32: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 33: use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;

 35: pub struct WorkerChunkSource {
 36:     workers: Vec<Worker>,
 37:     next_worker: usize,
 38:     completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>>,
 39:     failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>>,
 40:     requests: Rc<RefCell<GenerationWorkerRequests>>,
 41:     /// Keeps browser callbacks alive for the workers' lifetime.
 42:     _message_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>>,
 43:     _error_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>>,
 44:     /// Same-thread source for the synchronous [`ChunkSourcePort::load`]
 45:     /// contract and as a last-resort recovery if every worker has failed.
 46:     fallback: LocalChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>,
 47:     reported_emergency_fallback: bool,
 48: }
 49: 
 50: impl WorkerChunkSource {
 51:     /// Spawns the pool and hands every worker the URL query, so main thread
 52:     /// and workers derive the identical generator configuration.
 53:     pub fn new(query: &str, default_seed: u32, pool_size: usize) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 54:         if !(1..=usize::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)).contains(&pool_size) {
 55:             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
 56:                 "generation worker pool size must be 1..=4",
 57:             ));
 58:         }
 59: 
 60:         let completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
 61:         let failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
 62:         let requests = Rc::new(RefCell::new(GenerationWorkerRequests::new(pool_size)));
 63:         // The single-file bundle (scripts/build-single-file.mjs) has no
 64:         // sibling worker.js on disk; it publishes a blob: URL for the inlined
 65:         // worker script on the global scope instead.
 66:         let script_url = Reflect::get(&js_sys::global(), &"__VACKROOMS_WORKER_URL__".into())
 67:             .ok()
 68:             .and_then(|value| value.as_string())
 69:             .unwrap_or_else(|| "worker.js".to_string());
 70:         let mut workers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 71:         let mut message_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 72:         let mut error_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
 73:         for worker_index in 0..pool_size {
 74:             let options = WorkerOptions::new();
 75:             options.set_type(WorkerType::Module);
 76:             // Relative (not `/worker.js`): resolved against the document's
 77:             // URL, so this still finds the sibling file when the site is
 78:             // served from a subpath (e.g. a GitHub Pages project page at
 79:             // `<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) instead of the domain root.
 80:             let worker = Worker::new_with_options(&script_url, &options)?;
 81: 
 82:             let completed_sink = completed.clone();
 83:             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
 84:             let message_requests = requests.clone();
 85:             let worker_for_fatal_reply = worker.clone();
 86:             let handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>::new(move |event: MessageEvent| {
 87:                 match parse_worker_reply(&event) {
 88:                     WorkerReply::Completed(done) => {
 89:                         if message_requests
 90:                             .borrow_mut()
 91:                             .finish_exact(worker_index, &done.request)
 92:                         {
 93:                             completed_sink.borrow_mut().push(done);
 94:                         }
 95:                     }
 96:                     WorkerReply::Failed(echoed) => {
 97:                         if let Some(failed_request) = message_requests
 98:                             .borrow_mut()
 99:                             .fail_exact(worker_index, &echoed)
100:                         {
101:                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
102:                         }
103:                     }
104:                     WorkerReply::Fatal => {
105:                         let abandoned = message_requests
106:                             .borrow_mut()
107:                             .disable_and_drain(worker_index);
108:                         failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
109:                         worker_for_fatal_reply.terminate();
110:                     }
111:                     WorkerReply::Malformed => {
112:                         if let Some(failed_request) =
113:                             message_requests.borrow_mut().fail_oldest(worker_index)
114:                         {
115:                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
116:                         }
117:                     }
118:                 }
119:             });
120:             worker.set_onmessage(Some(handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
121: 
122:             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
123:             let error_requests = requests.clone();
124:             let worker_for_error = worker.clone();
125:             let error_handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |_event| {
126:                 let abandoned = error_requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
127:                 failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
128:                 worker_for_error.terminate();
129:             });
130:             worker.set_onerror(Some(error_handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
131: 
132:             let init = js_sys::Object::new();
133:             Reflect::set(&init, &"type".into(), &"init".into())?;
134:             Reflect::set(&init, &"query".into(), &query.into())?;
135:             Reflect::set(&init, &"seed".into(), &(default_seed as f64).into())?;
136:             worker.post_message(&init)?;
137: 
138:             workers.push(worker);
139:             message_handlers.push(handler);
140:             error_handlers.push(error_handler);
141:         }
142: 
143:         let (seed, config) =
144:             crate::adapters::query_config::generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
145:         Ok(Self {
146:             workers,
147:             next_worker: 0,
148:             completed,
149:             failed,
150:             requests,
151:             _message_handlers: message_handlers,
152:             _error_handlers: error_handlers,
153:             fallback: LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config),
154:             reported_emergency_fallback: false,
155:         })
156:     }
157: 
158:     pub fn pool_size(&self) -> usize {
159:         self.workers.len()
160:     }
161: }

163: impl ChunkSourcePort for WorkerChunkSource {
164:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
165:         self.fallback.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
166:     }
167: 
168:     fn load_with_reality(
169:         &self,
170:         origin_x: f32,
171:         origin_z: f32,
172:         level: u32,
173:         lod: u8,
174:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
175:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
176:         self.fallback
177:             .load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
178:     }
179: 
180:     fn load_with_artifacts(
181:         &self,
182:         origin_x: f32,
183:         origin_z: f32,
184:         level: u32,
185:         lod: u8,
186:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
187:         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
188:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
189:         self.fallback
190:             .load_with_artifacts(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality, artifacts)
191:     }
192: 
193:     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
194:         true
195:     }
196: 
197:     fn request(&mut self, request: ChunkRequest) {
198:         let worker_index = self.requests.borrow().next_accepting(self.next_worker);
199:         let Some(worker_index) = worker_index else {
200:             // Fatal worker startup/runtime failures must not strand streaming.
201:             // This path is deliberately exceptional: the healthy path always
202:             // generates off-thread, while an exhausted pool favors a complete
203:             // world over a permanently pending chunk.
204:             if !self.reported_emergency_fallback {
205:                 web_sys::console::warn_1(
206:                     &"generation worker pool failed; using same-thread recovery".into(),
207:                 );
208:                 self.reported_emergency_fallback = true;
209:             }
210:             let payload = self.fallback.load_with_artifacts(
211:                 request.origin_x,
212:                 request.origin_z,
213:                 request.level,
214:                 request.lod,
215:                 &request.reality,
216:                 request.artifacts,
217:             );
218:             self.completed
219:                 .borrow_mut()
220:                 .push(CompletedChunk { request, payload });
221:             return;
222:         };
223: 
224:         let message = js_sys::Object::new();
225:         let set = |k: &str, v: JsValue| {
226:             let _ = Reflect::set(&message, &k.into(), &v);
227:         };
228:         set("type", "gen".into());
229:         set("requestId", (request.request_id as f64).into());
230:         set("ox", (request.origin_x as f64).into());
231:         set("oz", (request.origin_z as f64).into());
232:         set("level", (request.level as f64).into());
233:         set("lod", (request.lod as f64).into());
234:         set("artifacts", (request.artifacts.bits() as f64).into());
235:         let reality_words = request.reality.to_words();
236:         let reality = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(reality_words.as_slice());
237:         set("reality", reality.into());
238:         let worker = &self.workers[worker_index];
239:         self.next_worker = (worker_index + 1) % self.workers.len();
240:         self.requests
241:             .borrow_mut()
242:             .assign(worker_index, request.clone());
243:         if let Err(error) = worker.post_message(&message) {
244:             // A synchronous send failure means this worker can no longer be
245:             // trusted with its already queued requests. Retire all of them;
246:             // the engine will validate their ids and retry on healthy slots.
247:             let abandoned = self.requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
248:             self.failed.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
249:             worker.terminate();
250:             web_sys::console::warn_2(
251:                 &"generation worker postMessage failed; disabling worker:".into(),
252:                 &error,
253:             );
254:         }
255:     }
256: 
257:     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
258:         std::mem::take(&mut *self.completed.borrow_mut())
259:     }
260: 
261:     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
262:         std::mem::take(&mut *self.failed.borrow_mut())
263:     }
264: }
265: 
266: enum WorkerReply {
267:     Completed(CompletedChunk),
268:     Failed(ChunkRequest),
269:     Fatal,
270:     Malformed,
271: }
272: 
273: /// Decodes the deliberately small worker protocol. Malformed replies are a
274: /// first-class outcome: the worker queue is serial, so the caller can fail its
275: /// oldest assigned request instead of leaving that chunk pending forever.
276: fn parse_worker_reply(event: &MessageEvent) -> WorkerReply {
277:     let data = event.data();
278:     let message_type = Reflect::get(&data, &"type".into())
279:         .ok()
280:         .and_then(|value| value.as_string());
281:     match message_type.as_deref() {
282:         Some("done") => parse_request(&data)
283:             .and_then(|request| {
284:                 parse_payload(&data).map(|payload| CompletedChunk { request, payload })
285:             })
286:             .map(WorkerReply::Completed)
287:             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
288:         Some("failed") => parse_request(&data)
289:             .map(WorkerReply::Failed)
290:             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
291:         Some("fatal") => WorkerReply::Fatal,
292:         _ => WorkerReply::Malformed,
293:     }
294: }
295: 
296: fn parse_request(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
297:     let field = |name: &str| Reflect::get(data, &name.into()).ok();
298:     Some(ChunkRequest {
299:         request_id: exact_u32(field("requestId")?)?,
300:         origin_x: finite_f32(field("ox")?)?,
301:         origin_z: finite_f32(field("oz")?)?,
302:         level: exact_u32(field("level")?)?,
303:         lod: u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("lod")?)?).ok()?,
304:         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(
305:             u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("artifacts")?)?).ok()?,
306:         )?,
307:         reality: {
308:             let encoded = field("reality")?;
309:             let words = encoded.dyn_into::<js_sys::Uint32Array>().ok()?.to_vec();
310:             RealitySnapshot::from_words(&words).ok()?
311:         },
312:     })
313: }
314: 
315: fn parse_payload(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkPayload> {
316:     let buffer: ArrayBuffer = Reflect::get(data, &"buf".into()).ok()?.dyn_into().ok()?;
317:     let bytes = Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec();
318:     decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)
319: }
320: 
321: fn exact_u32(value: JsValue) -> Option<u32> {
322:     let number = value.as_f64()?;
323:     (number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && (0.0..=f64::from(u32::MAX)).contains(&number))
324:         .then_some(number as u32)
325: }
326: 
327: fn finite_f32(value: JsValue) -> Option<f32> {
328:     let number = value.as_f64()?;
329:     let narrowed = number as f32;
330:     (number.is_finite() && narrowed.is_finite()).then_some(narrowed)
331: }
````

````rust
  2: //! ray-marcher (`shaders.rs::raymarchSVO`), marched through a real merged

 25: /// Merges chunks through the engine's pooled atlas, exactly like

 27: fn build_atlas(chunks: &[LoadedChunk]) -> AtlasBuild {

 29:     let rows = chunks
 30:         .iter()
 31:         .map(|c| payload_rows(&c.payload))
 32:         .max()
 33:         .unwrap_or(1)
 34:         .max(1);

 36: 
 37:     let mut draws = Vec::new();

 42:         draws.push(ChunkDraw {
 43:             origin: [c.origin.0, 0.0, c.origin.1],

 45:             world_size: c.payload.world_size,
 46:             voxel_size: c.payload.voxel_size,
 47:             svo_depth: c.payload.svo_depth,
 48:         });
 49:     }
 50:     let texels = pool.full_texels(|k| {
 51:         chunks
 52:             .iter()
 53:             .find(|c| chunk_key(c.origin.0, c.origin.1) == k)
 54:             .map(|c| &c.payload)
 55:     });

 59: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 60: #[allow(dead_code)] // `t`/`voxel_type` exist for the Debug dump on failure

 70: /// 1:1 Rust port of the GLSL `raymarchSVO` (same constants, same epsilons).
 71: fn raymarch_svo(
 72:     atlas: &[u32],
 73:     ro: [f32; 3],
 74:     rd: [f32; 3],
 75:     chunk_root_idx: usize,
 76:     t_entry: f32,
 77:     world_size: f32,
 78: ) -> Option<(f32, [f32; 3], [f32; 3], u32)> {
 79:     let mut t = t_entry;
 80:     let mut p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
 81: 
 82:     let mut stack: Vec<(usize, [f32; 3], [f32; 3])> = Vec::new();
 83:     let mut current_node = chunk_root_idx;
 84:     let mut cmin = [0.0f32; 3];
 85:     let mut cmax = [world_size; 3];
 86: 
 87:     for _ in 0..160 {
 88:         let tx = current_node * 4;
 89:         let (is_leaf, a, b) = (atlas[tx] == 1, atlas[tx + 1], atlas[tx + 2]);
 90: 
 91:         if is_leaf {
 92:             if a != 0 {
 93:                 return Some((t, cmin, cmax, a));
 94:             }
 95:             // Empty-space skip to this leaf's exit plane.
 96:             let exit = |lo: f32, hi: f32, o: f32, d: f32| (if d > 0.0 { hi } else { lo } - o) / d;
 97:             let tx = exit(cmin[0], cmax[0], ro[0], rd[0]);
 98:             let ty = exit(cmin[1], cmax[1], ro[1], rd[1]);
 99:             let tz = exit(cmin[2], cmax[2], ro[2], rd[2]);
100:             let t_exit = tx.min(ty).min(tz);
101:             t = t_exit;
102:             p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
103:             // Snap every tied axis past its exit plane (a ray exactly
104:             // through a corner advances diagonally; leaving an axis ON its
105:             // plane stalls the march instead).
106:             if (t_exit - tx).abs() < 1e-4 {
107:                 p[0] = (if rd[0] > 0.0 { cmax[0] } else { cmin[0] })
108:                     + (if rd[0] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
109:             }
110:             if (t_exit - ty).abs() < 1e-4 {
111:                 p[1] = (if rd[1] > 0.0 { cmax[1] } else { cmin[1] })
112:                     + (if rd[1] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
113:             }
114:             if (t_exit - tz).abs() < 1e-4 {
115:                 p[2] = (if rd[2] > 0.0 { cmax[2] } else { cmin[2] })
116:                     + (if rd[2] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
117:             }
118:             // Multi-level pop, mirroring the shader: the skip may cross
119:             // boundaries shared by several ancestor boxes at once.
120:             while outside(p, cmin, cmax) {
121:                 let Some(f) = stack.pop() else { return None };
122:                 current_node = f.0;
123:                 cmin = f.1;
124:                 cmax = f.2;
125:             }
126:         } else {
127:             let center = [
128:                 (cmin[0] + cmax[0]) * 0.5,
129:                 (cmin[1] + cmax[1]) * 0.5,
130:                 (cmin[2] + cmax[2]) * 0.5,
131:             ];
132:             let ox = (p[0] >= center[0]) as usize;
133:             let oy = (p[1] >= center[1]) as usize;
134:             let oz = (p[2] >= center[2]) as usize;
135:             let child_idx = (oz << 2) | (oy << 1) | ox;
136: 
137:             if b & (1 << child_idx) != 0 {
138:                 if stack.len() < 8 {
139:                     stack.push((current_node, cmin, cmax));
140:                 }
141:                 if ox == 1 {
142:                     cmin[0] = center[0]
143:                 } else {
144:                     cmax[0] = center[0]
145:                 }
146:                 if oy == 1 {
147:                     cmin[1] = center[1]
148:                 } else {
149:                     cmax[1] = center[1]
150:                 }
151:                 if oz == 1 {
152:                     cmin[2] = center[2]
153:                 } else {
154:                     cmax[2] = center[2]
155:                 }
156:                 current_node = a as usize + child_idx;
157:             } else {
158:                 let omin = [
159:                     if ox == 1 { center[0] } else { cmin[0] },
160:                     if oy == 1 { center[1] } else { cmin[1] },
161:                     if oz == 1 { center[2] } else { cmin[2] },
162:                 ];
163:                 let omax = [
164:                     if ox == 1 { cmax[0] } else { center[0] },
165:                     if oy == 1 { cmax[1] } else { center[1] },
166:                     if oz == 1 { cmax[2] } else { center[2] },
167:                 ];
168:                 let exit =
169:                     |lo: f32, hi: f32, o: f32, d: f32| (if d > 0.0 { hi } else { lo } - o) / d;
170:                 let tx = exit(omin[0], omax[0], ro[0], rd[0]);
171:                 let ty = exit(omin[1], omax[1], ro[1], rd[1]);
172:                 let tz = exit(omin[2], omax[2], ro[2], rd[2]);
173:                 let t_exit = tx.min(ty).min(tz);
174:                 t = t_exit;
175:                 p = [ro[0] + t * rd[0], ro[1] + t * rd[1], ro[2] + t * rd[2]];
176:                 if (t_exit - tx).abs() < 1e-4 {
177:                     p[0] = (if rd[0] > 0.0 { omax[0] } else { omin[0] })
178:                         + (if rd[0] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
179:                 }
180:                 if (t_exit - ty).abs() < 1e-4 {
181:                     p[1] = (if rd[1] > 0.0 { omax[1] } else { omin[1] })
182:                         + (if rd[1] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
183:                 }
184:                 if (t_exit - tz).abs() < 1e-4 {
185:                     p[2] = (if rd[2] > 0.0 { omax[2] } else { omin[2] })
186:                         + (if rd[2] > 0.0 { 0.001 } else { -0.001 });
187:                 }
188:                 while outside(p, cmin, cmax) {
189:                     let Some(f) = stack.pop() else { return None };
190:                     current_node = f.0;
191:                     cmin = f.1;
192:                     cmax = f.2;
193:                 }
194:             }
195:         }
196:     }
197:     None
198: }
199: 
200: fn outside(p: [f32; 3], min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
201:     p[0] < min[0]
202:         || p[0] > max[0]
203:         || p[1] < min[1]
204:         || p[1] > max[1]
205:         || p[2] < min[2]
206:         || p[2] > max[2]
207: }
208: 
209: /// Mirrors the shader's `main()`: slab-test all chunks, sort by entry, march
210: /// nearest first, return the first hit.
211: fn march_scene(
212:     atlas: &[u32],
213:     draws: &[wasm_frontend::application::ports::ChunkDraw],
214:     ro: [f32; 3],
215:     rd: [f32; 3],
216: ) -> Option<Hit> {
217:     let safe = |v: f32| {
218:         if v.abs() < 1e-4 {
219:             1e-4f32.copysign(v)
220:         } else {
221:             v
222:         }
223:     };
224:     // The shader passes safe_rd (not raw rd) into raymarchSVO too.
225:     let rd = [safe(rd[0]), safe(rd[1]), safe(rd[2])];
226:     let inv = [1.0 / rd[0], 1.0 / rd[1], 1.0 / rd[2]];
227: 
228:     let mut hits: Vec<(usize, f32)> = Vec::new();
229:     for (i, d) in draws.iter().enumerate() {
230:         let lro = [
231:             ro[0] - d.origin[0],
232:             ro[1] - d.origin[1],
233:             ro[2] - d.origin[2],
234:         ];
235:         let mut t_entry = f32::MIN;
236:         let mut t_exit = f32::MAX;
237:         for a in 0..3 {
238:             let t1 = (0.0 - lro[a]) * inv[a];
239:             let t2 = (d.world_size - lro[a]) * inv[a];
240:             t_entry = t_entry.max(t1.min(t2));
241:             t_exit = t_exit.min(t1.max(t2));
242:         }
243:         if t_entry < t_exit && t_exit > 0.0 {
244:             hits.push((i, t_entry.max(0.0)));
245:         }
246:     }
247:     hits.sort_by(|a, b| a.1.total_cmp(&b.1));
248: 
249:     for (i, t_min) in hits {
250:         let d = &draws[i];
251:         let lro = [
252:             ro[0] - d.origin[0],
253:             ro[1] - d.origin[1],
254:             ro[2] - d.origin[2],
255:         ];
256:         if let Some((t, bmin, bmax, vt)) =
257:             raymarch_svo(atlas, lro, rd, d.root_index as usize, t_min, d.world_size)
258:         {
259:             return Some(Hit {
260:                 chunk: i,
261:                 t,
262:                 box_min: bmin,
263:                 box_max: bmax,
264:                 voxel_type: vt,
265:             });
266:         }
267:     }
268:     None
269: }
270: 
271: /// Every hit the reference ray-marcher reports must be a genuinely solid
272: /// region of the source octree — otherwise the renderer shows phantom boxes.
273: #[test]
274: fn multi_chunk_raymarch_reports_no_phantom_geometry() {
275:     let seed = 42;
276:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
277:     let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
278:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
279: 
280:     // 3x3 resident set around spawn, same as the engine with radius 1.
281:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
282:     // Level 0 now has vaulted regions up to 5.4 u, so a steep ray starting
283:     // near the edge of the spawn chunk can travel farther laterally before
284:     // reaching its ceiling. Keep enough loaded world around the sweep to
285:     // test traversal, not an artificial streaming boundary.
286:     for dz in -2..=2 {
287:         for dx in -2..=2 {
288:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
289:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
290:                 (ox, oz),
291:                 0,
292:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
293:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
294:             ));
295:         }
296:     }
297:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
298: 
299:     // Ground truth: rebuild each chunk's SVO exactly like LocalChunkSource.
300:     let svos: Vec<_> = chunks
301:         .iter()
302:         .map(|c| {
303:             let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
304:             let grid = generator.execute(Position::new(c.origin.0, c.origin.1), seed, config);
305:             BuildOctreeUseCase::new().execute(&grid, config.svo_depth(), config.svo_world_size())
306:         })
307:         .collect();
308: 
309:     let ro = [5.0f32, 1.7, 5.0]; // spawn eye position
310:     let mut phantoms = Vec::new();
311:     let mut hit_count = 0usize;
312: 
313:     // Dense direction sweep: 64 yaw steps x 17 pitch steps.
314:     for yi in 0..64 {
315:         for pi in -8..=8i32 {
316:             let yaw = yi as f32 / 64.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
317:             let pitch = pi as f32 / 8.0 * 1.2;
318:             let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
319:             let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
320:             let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
321: 
322:             let Some(hit) = march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd) else {
323:                 continue;
324:             };
325:             hit_count += 1;
326: 
327:             // The leaf box center, in voxel coordinates of the owning chunk.
328:             let scale = config.voxel_scale;
329:             let c = [
330:                 (hit.box_min[0] + hit.box_max[0]) * 0.5,
331:                 (hit.box_min[1] + hit.box_max[1]) * 0.5,
332:                 (hit.box_min[2] + hit.box_max[2]) * 0.5,
333:             ];
334:             let (vx, vy, vz) = (
335:                 (c[0] / scale) as u32,
336:                 (c[1] / scale) as u32,
337:                 (c[2] / scale) as u32,
338:             );
339:             let truth = svos[hit.chunk].get(vx, vy, vz);
340:             let solid = truth.map(|(vt, _, _, _)| vt != 0).unwrap_or(false);
341:             if !solid {
342:                 phantoms.push((yaw, pitch, hit));
343:             }
344:         }
345:     }
346: 
347:     assert!(
348:         hit_count > 200,
349:         "sanity: the sweep must actually hit walls, got {hit_count}"
350:     );
351:     assert!(
352:         phantoms.is_empty(),
353:         "{} phantom hits out of {}; first 5: {:#?}",
354:         phantoms.len(),
355:         hit_count,
356:         &phantoms[..phantoms.len().min(5)]
357:     );
358: }
359: 
360: /// The world is a closed slab (floor everywhere at y=0, ceiling at the top),
361: /// so every ray with meaningful up/down pitch MUST hit something. A miss is
362: /// a traversal crack — the "black bars in walls" artifact caused by popping
363: /// only one stack level when a skip crosses several octree levels at once.
364: #[test]
365: fn pitched_rays_never_escape_through_cracks() {
366:     let seed = 42;
367:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
368:     let source = LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config);
369: 
370:     let mut chunks = Vec::new();
371:     for dz in -1..=1 {
372:         for dx in -1..=1 {
373:             let (ox, oz) = (dx as f32 * 10.0, dz as f32 * 10.0);
374:             chunks.push(LoadedChunk::new(
375:                 (ox, oz),
376:                 0,
377:                 vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot::empty(),
378:                 source.load(ox, oz, 0, 0),
379:             ));
380:         }
381:     }
382:     let build = build_atlas(&chunks);
383: 
384:     let mut misses = 0usize;
385:     let mut total = 0usize;
386:     for px in 0..8 {
387:         for pz in 0..8 {
388:             let ro = [1.0137 + px as f32 * 1.11, 1.7, 0.9713 + pz as f32 * 1.19];
389:             for yi in 0..128 {
390:                 for pi in [-40i32, -25, 25, 40] {
391:                     let yaw = (yi as f32 + 0.173) / 128.0 * std::f32::consts::TAU;
392:                     let pitch = pi as f32 / 60.0 * 1.2;
393:                     let (sy, cy) = yaw.sin_cos();
394:                     let (sp, cp) = pitch.sin_cos();
395:                     let rd = [-cp * sy, sp, -cp * cy];
396:                     total += 1;
397:                     if march_scene(&build.texels, &build.draws, ro, rd).is_none() {
398:                         misses += 1;
399:                     }
400:                 }
401:             }
402:         }
403:     }
404:     assert_eq!(
405:         misses, 0,
406:         "{misses} of {total} pitched rays escaped through cracks"
407:     );
408: }
````

````rust
  1: //! Column geometry for immutable, non-Red-Room anomaly families.
  2: //!
  3: //! The region planner decides *where* an anomaly exists. This module decides
  4: //! what one world-space column inside that immutable plan looks like. Red Rooms
  5: //! remain a separate encounter feature because their geometry is coupled to a
  6: //! dedicated phase machine and recursive Level 0 destination.
  7: 
  8: use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  9:     AnomalyInstance, AnomalyKind, ArchBehavior, ArchLayout, RealitySnapshot,
 10: };
 11: use crate::domain::entities::environment::{EnvironmentProfile, FloorState};
 12: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_LIGHT};
 13: use crate::use_cases::level_zero::{BackroomsLevel, ColumnPlan};
 14: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
 15: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
 16: use crate::use_cases::region_plan::PLAN_WALL_T;
 17: 
 18: const LIGHT_PERIOD: f32 = 2.8;
 19: 
 20: /// Mutable anomaly infill uses a stable content tile for its seam guard. The
 21: /// tile is a world-generation constant, never the size of an output request.
 22: const GENERATION_TILE_UNITS: f32 = 10.0;
 23: 
 24: struct SampleContext<'a> {
 25:     instance: &'a AnomalyInstance,
 26:     noise: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
 27:     seed: u32,
 28:     config: &'a GeneratorConfig,
 29:     reality: &'a RealitySnapshot,
 30:     world_x: f32,
 31:     world_z: f32,
 32:     local_x: f32,
 33:     local_z: f32,
 34:     boundary: f32,
 35:     perimeter: bool,
 36:     skeleton: bool,
 37:     away_from_seam: bool,
 38: }
 39: 
 40: /// Sample one immutable macro anomaly or stable archway anchor.
 41: ///
 42: /// Corridors have already won composition priority before this function is
 43: /// called, so every family may assume its protected bearing route is the only
 44: /// remaining cross-cutting circulation concern. Blackout expanses delegate
 45: /// their substrate to the ordinary Level 0 fabric sampler before applying the
 46: /// anomaly profile.
 47: pub(crate) fn sample_anomaly(
 48:     instance: &AnomalyInstance,
 49:     noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
 50:     seed: u32,
 51:     config: &GeneratorConfig,
 52:     reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 53:     world_x: f32,
 54:     world_z: f32,
 55: ) -> ColumnPlan {
 56:     let (local_x, local_z) = instance.local_coords(world_x, world_z);
 57:     let boundary = instance.boundary_distance(world_x, world_z);
 58:     let seam_x = world_x.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
 59:     let seam_z = world_z.rem_euclid(GENERATION_TILE_UNITS);
 60:     let context = SampleContext {
 61:         instance,
 62:         noise,
 63:         seed,
 64:         config,
 65:         reality,
 66:         world_x,
 67:         world_z,
 68:         local_x,
 69:         local_z,
 70:         boundary,
 71:         perimeter: boundary <= PLAN_WALL_T,
 72:         skeleton: local_z.abs() <= instance.skeleton_half_width,
 73:         away_from_seam: seam_x > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
 74:             && seam_x < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
 75:             && seam_z > PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0
 76:             && seam_z < GENERATION_TILE_UNITS - PLAN_WALL_T * 2.0,
 77:     };
 78: 
 79:     match instance.kind {
 80:         AnomalyKind::PillarExpanse => sample_pillar_expanse(&context),
 81:         AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse => sample_blackout_expanse(&context),
 82:         AnomalyKind::PitLattice => sample_pit_lattice(&context),
 83:         AnomalyKind::ArchwayRoom => sample_archway_anchor(&context),
 84:         AnomalyKind::RedRoom => unreachable!("red rooms have a dedicated geometry sampler"),
 85:     }
 86: }
 87: 
 88: /// Dehydration multiplies mutable-infill probability: tier 3 nearly
 89: /// doubles how much anomalous mass a re-dealt space grows.
 90: fn delirium_gain(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> f32 {
 91:     1.0 + 0.3 * reality.delirium() as f32
 92: }
 93: 
 94: fn anomaly_hash(instance: &AnomalyInstance, epoch: u32, salt: u64, x: i64, z: i64) -> f32 {
 95:     let mut hash = instance.id
 96:         ^ salt
 97:         ^ (epoch as u64).rotate_left(19)
 98:         ^ (x as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
 99:         ^ (z as u64).rotate_left(37);
100:     hash ^= hash >> 30;
101:     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
102:     hash ^= hash >> 27;
103:     hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB);
104:     hash ^= hash >> 31;
105:     (hash >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
106: }
107: 
108: fn remap_epoch(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> Option<u32> {
109:     let state = context.instance.state(context.reality)?;
110:     (state.epoch > 0
111:         && context.boundary > context.instance.entry_band
112:         && state.point_is_in_wake(
113:             context.world_x,
114:             context.world_z,
115:             context.config.anomalies.remap_distance,
116:         ))
117:     .then_some(state.epoch)
118: }

120: fn sample_pillar_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
121:     let instance = context.instance;
122:     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
123:     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
124:     let lattice = instance.pillar_lattice.expect("pillar instance lattice");
125:     let cell_x = ((local_x - lattice.phase_x) / lattice.bay_x).floor() as i64;
126:     let cell_z = ((local_z - lattice.phase_z) / lattice.bay_z).floor() as i64;
127:     let mut within_x = (local_x - lattice.phase_x).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_x);
128:     let within_z = (local_z - lattice.phase_z).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_z);
129:     let mut side = instance.pillar_size(cell_x, cell_z).unwrap_or(1.2);
130: 
131:     // Distortion grows only after the entry has taught the player a regular
132:     // grid. The route and entry band therefore remain a reliable baseline.
133:     let budget = ((context.boundary - instance.entry_band) / (instance.entry_band.max(8.0) * 2.5))
134:         .clamp(0.0, 1.0);
135:     let immutable_zone = context.skeleton || budget <= 0.0;
136:     let mut dropped = false;
137:     if !immutable_zone {
138:         dropped = anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D0, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.10 * budget;
139:         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D1, cell_z, 0) < 0.30 * budget {
140:             within_x = (within_x + lattice.bay_x * 0.5).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_x);
141:         }
142:         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D2, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.08 * budget {
143:             side += 0.4;
144:         }
145:     }
146: 
147:     // A committed wake may change relationships between bays, but never at a
148:     // stable content-tile seam where resident reality cohorts meet.
149:     let wake_epoch = (!immutable_zone && context.away_from_seam)
150:         .then(|| remap_epoch(context))
151:         .flatten();
152:     if let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
153:         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F4, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.25 {
154:             side += 0.4;
155:         }
156:         if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F5, cell_z, cell_x) < 0.35 {
157:             within_x = (within_x + 0.4).rem_euclid(lattice.bay_x);
158:         }
159:     }
160: 
161:     let dx = within_x.min(lattice.bay_x - within_x);
162:     let dz = within_z.min(lattice.bay_z - within_z);
163:     let mut solid = context.perimeter || (!dropped && dx < side * 0.5 && dz < side * 0.5);
164:     if !solid && let Some(epoch) = wake_epoch {
165:         let edge_x = within_x < PLAN_WALL_T || lattice.bay_x - within_x < PLAN_WALL_T;
166:         let edge_z = within_z < PLAN_WALL_T || lattice.bay_z - within_z < PLAN_WALL_T;
167:         let threshold = (0.12
168:             * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity
169:             * delirium_gain(context.reality))
170:         .clamp(0.0, 0.48);
171:         solid = (edge_x && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F1, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold)
172:             || (edge_z && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0x11F2, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold);
173:     }
174:     if context.skeleton {
175:         solid = false;
176:     }
177: 
178:     let lane_light =
179:         local_z.abs() < 0.45 && (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9 && tuning.lights > 0.0;
180:     let field_light = (local_x - 2.4 + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
181:         && (local_z + 0.45).rem_euclid(4.8) < 0.9
182:         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11A7, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.62 * tuning.lights;
183:     let ceiling_units = if !immutable_zone
184:         && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0x11D3, cell_x / 2, cell_z / 2) < 0.35 * budget
185:     {
186:         4.0
187:     } else {
188:         4.2
189:     };
190:     ColumnPlan {
191:         light: !solid && (lane_light || field_light),
192:         solid,
193:         ceiling_units,
194:         floor_material: EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel(),
195:         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
196:     }
197: }

199: fn sample_blackout_expanse(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
200:     let instance = context.instance;
201:     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
202:     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
203:     // The blackout substrate is ordinary fabric under the profile — and it
204:     // drifts under the same Peripheral Shift stamps as ordinary fabric. In
205:     // here the engine also advances drift *behind the player in real time*
206:     // (the darkness hides the swap), so a blackout rearranges more cruelly
207:     // than the level outside it: turning around is never a way back.
208:     let mut plan = BackroomsLevel::column_plan_in_reality(
209:         context.noise,
210:         context.seed ^ instance.id as u32,
211:         tuning,
212:         context.reality,
213:         context.world_x,
214:         context.world_z,
215:     );
216:     let depth = instance.normalized_depth(context.world_x, context.world_z);
217:     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::blackout(depth);
218:     plan.wall_material = profile.wall_voxel();
219:     plan.light_material = profile.light_voxel();
220: 
221:     // Ordinary fixtures thin through the approach instead of cutting directly
222:     // to black, so the darkness is spatially earned.
223:     if depth <= 0.22 {
224:         let cell_x = (context.world_x / LIGHT_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
225:         let cell_z = (context.world_z / LIGHT_PERIOD).floor() as i64;
226:         let keep = 1.0 - depth / 0.22;
227:         plan.light = plan.light && anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0xFADE, cell_x, cell_z) < keep;
228:         plan.light_material = VOXEL_LIGHT;
229:     } else {
230:         plan.light = false;
231:     }
232:     plan.red_light = false;
233:     plan.ceiling_units = if depth > 0.68 {
234:         2.6
235:     } else if depth > 0.35 {
236:         3.0
237:     } else {
238:         3.4
239:     };
240: 
241:     if profile.floor == FloorState::RecessedFluid && !plan.solid && !context.skeleton {
242:         let cell = 7.2;
243:         let basin_x = (local_x / cell).floor() as i64;
244:         let basin_z = (local_z / cell).floor() as i64;
245:         if anomaly_hash(instance, 0, 0xF10D, basin_x, basin_z) < 0.22
246:             && local_x.rem_euclid(cell) > 1.2
247:             && local_z.rem_euclid(cell) > 1.2
248:         {
249:             plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
250:         }
251:     }
252: 
253:     plan.solid |= context.perimeter;
254:     if context.skeleton {
255:         plan.solid = false;
256:         plan.light = local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45 && tuning.lights > 0.0;
257:         plan.light_material = VOXEL_GLIMMER;
258:         return plan;
259:     }
260: 
261:     // Deception is nearly unbounded on purpose: blackouts are meant to be
262:     // almost impossible to walk out of, so decoy glimmers may heavily
263:     // outnumber the honest skeleton — and a delirious wanderer sees more
264:     // liars still.
265:     let decoys = (context.config.anomalies.blackout_decoys
266:         + 0.03 * context.reality.delirium() as f32)
267:         .clamp(0.0, 0.95);
268:     let off_lane = (local_z.abs() - (instance.skeleton_half_width + 7.2)).abs() < 0.45;
269:     if off_lane
270:         && depth > 0.3
271:         && local_x.rem_euclid(28.0) < 0.45
272:         && tuning.lights > 0.0
273:         && anomaly_hash(
274:             instance,
275:             0,
276:             0xDEC0,
277:             (local_x / 28.0).floor() as i64,
278:             local_z.is_sign_negative() as i64,
279:         ) < decoys
280:     {
281:         plan.light = true;
282:         plan.light_material = VOXEL_GLIMMER;
283:     }
284: 
285:     if context.away_from_seam
286:         && let Some(epoch) = remap_epoch(context)
287:     {
288:         let cell = 7.2;
289:         let cell_x = (local_x / cell).floor() as i64;
290:         let cell_z = (local_z / cell).floor() as i64;
291:         let within_x = local_x.rem_euclid(cell);
292:         let within_z = local_z.rem_euclid(cell);
293:         let edge = within_x < PLAN_WALL_T || within_z < PLAN_WALL_T;
294:         let threshold = (0.20
295:             * context.config.anomalies.remap_intensity
296:             * delirium_gain(context.reality))
297:         .clamp(0.0, 0.65);
298:         if edge && anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, 0xB1AC, cell_x, cell_z) < threshold {
299:             plan.solid = true;
300:             plan.light = false;
301:         }
302:     }
303: 
304:     // The dark owns a structural layer the Peripheral Shift re-deals: past
305:     // the approach band, room-scale partitions stand on the instance's own
306:     // lattice. Their epoch comes from the fabric drift stamps, so the
307:     // engine's rear shift does not merely nudge 0.4 u fabric bands — it
308:     // rearranges *rooms* behind the player. Every drawn partition is
309:     // pierced by its own doorway, so no shift can seal space it creates,
310:     // and the recovery skeleton stays exempt below.
311:     if depth > 0.25 && !context.skeleton && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
312:         const PARTITION_CELL: f32 = 9.6;
313:         let cell_x = (local_x / PARTITION_CELL).floor() as i64;
314:         let cell_z = (local_z / PARTITION_CELL).floor() as i64;
315:         let anchor = instance.world_coords(
316:             (cell_x as f32 + 0.5) * PARTITION_CELL,
317:             (cell_z as f32 + 0.5) * PARTITION_CELL,
318:         );
319:         let epoch = context.reality.fabric_drift_epoch(anchor.x, anchor.z);
320:         let within_x = local_x.rem_euclid(PARTITION_CELL);
321:         let within_z = local_z.rem_euclid(PARTITION_CELL);
322:         for (in_band, along, wall_salt, door_salt) in [
323:             (within_x < PLAN_WALL_T, within_z, 0xB1D0u64, 0xB1D1u64),
324:             (within_z < PLAN_WALL_T, within_x, 0xB1D2u64, 0xB1D3u64),
325:         ] {
326:             if !in_band {
327:                 continue;
328:             }
329:             if anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, wall_salt, cell_x, cell_z) < 0.5 {
330:                 let gap = anomaly_hash(instance, epoch, door_salt, cell_x, cell_z);
331:                 let gap_pos = 0.8 + (PARTITION_CELL - 3.2) * gap;
332:                 if along < gap_pos || along >= gap_pos + 1.6 {
333:                     plan.solid = true;
334:                     plan.light = false;
335:                 }
336:             }
337:         }
338:     }
339:     plan
340: }
341: 
342: fn sample_pit_lattice(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
343:     let lattice = context.instance.pit_lattice.expect("pit instance lattice");
344:     let within_x = (context.local_x - lattice.phase_x).rem_euclid(lattice.spacing_x);
345:     let within_z = (context.local_z - lattice.phase_z).rem_euclid(lattice.spacing_z);
346:     let dx = within_x.min(lattice.spacing_x - within_x);
347:     let dz = within_z.min(lattice.spacing_z - within_z);
348:     let pit = !context.skeleton
349:         && context.boundary > lattice.side
350:         && dx < lattice.side * 0.5
351:         && dz < lattice.side * 0.5;
352:     ColumnPlan {
353:         floor: !pit,
354:         solid: context.perimeter,
355:         light: !context.perimeter
356:             && context.local_x.rem_euclid(3.2) < 0.45
357:             && context.local_z.rem_euclid(3.2) < 0.45
358:             && context.config.tuning.lights > 0.0,
359:         ..ColumnPlan::open(3.8)
360:     }
361: }
362: 
363: /// Stable pale arch rooms never inspect `RealitySnapshot`, which keeps them a
364: /// fixed landmark against every mutable anomaly family.
365: ///
366: /// A `Transition` room is a *graph connector*: its `ArchBehavior` decides
367: /// what its far half (local `z > 0`) belongs to. The seam is expressed only
368: /// through legal architectural vocabulary — ceiling regime, floor finish,
369: /// lintel height, fixture rhythm — never through impossible collision or a
370: /// repainted wall, so the crossing is felt before it is understood.
371: fn sample_archway_anchor(context: &SampleContext<'_>) -> ColumnPlan {
372:     let instance = context.instance;
373:     let tuning = &context.config.tuning;
374:     let (local_x, local_z) = (context.local_x, context.local_z);
375:     let arch = instance.arch.expect("arch instance profile");
376:     let profile = EnvironmentProfile::archway_room();
377:     let half_x = instance.footprint.half_x;
378:     let half_z = instance.footprint.half_z;
379: 
380:     // The far half of a seam room disagrees with the near half.
381:     let far_side = local_z > 0.0;
382:     let (ceiling_units, floor_material) = match arch.behavior {
383:         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => {
384:             (3.0, EnvironmentProfile::pillar_expanse().floor_voxel())
385:         }
386:         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => (4.4, profile.floor_voxel()),
387:         _ => (3.6, profile.floor_voxel()),
388:     };
389:     let mut plan = ColumnPlan {
390:         wall_material: profile.wall_voxel(),
391:         floor_material,
392:         ..ColumnPlan::open(ceiling_units)
393:     };
394: 
395:     let bay_index = ((local_x + half_x) / arch.bay).floor() as i64;
396:     let along = (local_x + half_x).rem_euclid(arch.bay);
397:     // The far arcade of a scale breach broadens its openings; a culture
398:     // seam presses its lintels lower. Both stay on the shared bay rhythm so
399:     // the two walls visibly disagree about the same structure.
400:     let effective_opening = match arch.behavior {
401:         ArchBehavior::ScaleBreach if far_side => arch.opening * 1.5,
402:         _ => arch.opening,
403:     };
404:     let head_drop = match arch.behavior {
405:         ArchBehavior::CultureSeam if far_side => 0.4,
406:         _ => 0.0,
407:     };
408:     let across_opening = (along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() < effective_opening * 0.5;
409:     let blind = bay_index.rem_euclid(arch.blind_every as i64) == arch.blind_every as i64 - 1;
410:     let arch_head = {
411:         let t = ((along - arch.bay * 0.5).abs() / (effective_opening * 0.5)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
412:         (((arch.spring_units - head_drop) + 0.6 * (1.0 - t)) / 0.2).round() * 0.2
413:     };
414: 
415:     if context.perimeter {
416:         plan.solid = tuning.walls > 0.0;
417:         let on_long_wall = half_z - local_z.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T;
418:         match arch.layout {
419:             ArchLayout::Transition => {
420:                 if on_long_wall && across_opening && !blind {
421:                     plan.solid = false;
422:                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(arch_head);
423:                 }
424:             }
425:             ArchLayout::DeadEnd => {
426:                 let on_entrance_wall = half_x - local_x.abs() <= PLAN_WALL_T && local_x < 0.0;
427:                 if on_entrance_wall && local_z.abs() < 1.0 {
428:                     plan.solid = false;
429:                     plan.lintel_from_units = (tuning.walls > 0.0).then_some(
430:                         ((arch.spring_units + 0.6 * (1.0 - local_z.abs())) / 0.2).round() * 0.2,
431:                     );
432:                 }
433:             }
434:         }
435:         return plan;
436:     }
437: 
438:     if arch.layout == ArchLayout::DeadEnd {
439:         let arcade_plane = half_z - 1.2 - PLAN_WALL_T;
440:         let in_arcade = (local_z.abs() - arcade_plane).abs() < PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5;
441:         let in_alcove = local_z.abs() > arcade_plane;
442:         if in_arcade && tuning.walls > 0.0 {
443:             if across_opening && !blind {
444:                 plan.lintel_from_units = Some(arch_head);
445:             } else {
446:                 plan.solid = true;
447:             }
448:         } else if in_alcove {
449:             plan.ceiling_units = 3.0;
450:             if ((local_x * 2.5).sin() * (local_z * 1.7).cos()).abs() < 0.3 {
451:                 plan.floor_material = VOXEL_FLUID;
452:             }
453:         }
454:     }
455: 
456:     plan.light = local_z.abs() < 0.45
457:         && (local_x + half_x - arch.bay * 0.5).rem_euclid(arch.bay * 2.0) < 0.45
458:         && tuning.lights > 0.0;
459:     let _ = context.boundary;
460:     plan
461: }
462:
````

````rust
  1: //! Converts the core greedy-quad output into the browser renderer's compact
  2: //! indexed mesh payload. Geometry stays chunk-local and fixed-point so GPU
  3: //! uploads are small and camera precision does not degrade far from origin.
  4: 
  5: use vackrooms::adapters::voxel_mapper::{FaceDirection, MergedQuad, VoxelMapper, VoxelType};
  6: use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
  7:     VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER, VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_CONCRETE_FLOOR, VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL, VOXEL_CRATE,
  8:     VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR, VOXEL_FLUID,
  9:     VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_METAL_DOOR, VOXEL_PALE_WALL, VOXEL_PIPE,
 10:     VOXEL_RED_LIGHT, VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WALL,
 11:     VOXEL_WATER, VoxelGrid,
 12: };
 13: 
 14: use vackrooms::domain::entities::probe_grid::{
 15:     DEFAULT_PROBE_DEPTH, DEFAULT_PROBE_HEIGHT, DEFAULT_PROBE_WIDTH, ProbeGrid,
 16: };
 17: 
 18: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 19: use crate::application::ports::{
 20:     POSITION_FIXED_SCALE, PackedVertex, RenderArtifactNeeds, SurfaceMeshPayload,
 21: };
 22: 
 23: /// Builds a seam-safe surface payload from a grid that includes a one-voxel
 24: /// X/Z halo. The mapper consults that halo before emitting boundary faces.
 25: pub fn build_surface_mesh(
 26:     halo_grid: &VoxelGrid,
 27:     voxel_scale: f32,
 28:     lod: u8,
 29:     lateral_padding: usize,
 30: ) -> SurfaceMeshPayload {
 31:     build_surface_artifacts(
 32:         halo_grid,
 33:         voxel_scale,
 34:         lod,
 35:         lateral_padding,
 36:         RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE,
 37:     )
 38: }
 39: 
 40: /// Builds only the raster representation selected by the renderer. Greedy
 41: /// quads are shared by both outputs, but indexed vertices and face instances
 42: /// are materialized independently so neither strategy pays for the other.
 43: pub fn build_surface_artifacts(
 44:     halo_grid: &VoxelGrid,
 45:     voxel_scale: f32,
 46:     lod: u8,
 47:     lateral_padding: usize,
 48:     artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
 49: ) -> SurfaceMeshPayload {
 50:     let mapper = VoxelMapper::new(voxel_scale);
 51:     let quads = mapper.map_voxel_grid_with_padding(halo_grid, lateral_padding);
 52:     let width = halo_grid.width() - lateral_padding * 2;
 53:     let depth = halo_grid.depth() - lateral_padding * 2;
 54:     let bounds = Aabb::new(
 55:         [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
 56:         [
 57:             width as f32 * voxel_scale,
 58:             halo_grid.height() as f32 * voxel_scale,
 59:             depth as f32 * voxel_scale,
 60:         ],
 61:     );
 62:     let probe_grid = ProbeGrid::from_voxel_grid(
 63:         halo_grid,
 64:         DEFAULT_PROBE_WIDTH,
 65:         DEFAULT_PROBE_HEIGHT,
 66:         DEFAULT_PROBE_DEPTH,
 67:     );
 68:     let (pw, ph, pd) = probe_grid.dimensions();
 69:     let mut mesh = SurfaceMeshPayload {
 70:         vertices: Vec::with_capacity(if artifacts.indexed_surface_mesh() {
 71:             quads.len() * 4
 72:         } else {
 73:             0
 74:         }),
 75:         indices: Vec::with_capacity(if artifacts.indexed_surface_mesh() {
 76:             quads.len() * 6
 77:         } else {
 78:             0
 79:         }),
 80:         bounds,
 81:         lod,
 82:         faces: if artifacts.face_splats() {
 83:             crate::adapters::face_instances::build_face_instances(&quads, voxel_scale)
 84:         } else {
 85:             crate::application::ports::FaceInstanceSet::empty()
 86:         },
 87:         voxel_scale,
 88:         light_volume_bytes: probe_grid.as_bytes().to_vec(),
 89:         light_volume_dims: [pw as u32, ph as u32, pd as u32],
 90:     };
 91:     if artifacts.indexed_surface_mesh() {
 92:         for quad in &quads {
 93:             append_quad(&mut mesh, quad, voxel_scale);
 94:         }
 95:     }
 96:     mesh
 97: }
 98: 
 99: fn append_quad(mesh: &mut SurfaceMeshPayload, quad: &MergedQuad, voxel_scale: f32) {
100:     let x0 = quad.x;
101:     let x1 = quad.x + quad.w;
102:     let y0 = quad.y;
103:     let y1 = quad.y + quad.h;
104:     let z0 = quad.z;
105:     let z1_horizontal = quad.z + quad.h;
106:     let z1_x_face = quad.z + quad.w;
107: 
108:     // `w` and `h` span different local axes per face. Move the positive
109:     // faces to the far voxel plane so the indexed mesh is a closed shell.
110:     let points = match quad.dir {
111:         FaceDirection::Up => {
112:             let y = quad.y + voxel_scale;
113:             [
114:                 [x0, y, z0],
115:                 [x0, y, z1_horizontal],
116:                 [x1, y, z1_horizontal],
117:                 [x1, y, z0],
118:             ]
119:         }
120:         FaceDirection::Down => [
121:             [x0, y0, z0],
122:             [x1, y0, z0],
123:             [x1, y0, z1_horizontal],
124:             [x0, y0, z1_horizontal],
125:         ],
126:         FaceDirection::North => [
127:             [x0, y0, quad.z],
128:             [x0, y1, quad.z],
129:             [x1, y1, quad.z],
130:             [x1, y0, quad.z],
131:         ],
132:         FaceDirection::South => {
133:             let z = quad.z + voxel_scale;
134:             [[x0, y0, z], [x1, y0, z], [x1, y1, z], [x0, y1, z]]
135:         }
136:         FaceDirection::East => {
137:             let x = quad.x + voxel_scale;
138:             [
139:                 [x, y0, z0],
140:                 [x, y1, z0],
141:                 [x, y1, z1_x_face],
142:                 [x, y0, z1_x_face],
143:             ]
144:         }
145:         FaceDirection::West => [
146:             [quad.x, y0, z0],
147:             [quad.x, y0, z1_x_face],
148:             [quad.x, y1, z1_x_face],
149:             [quad.x, y1, z0],
150:         ],
151:     };
152: 
153:     let base = mesh.vertices.len() as u32;
154:     let normal_axis = normal_axis(quad.dir);
155:     let material = material_id(quad.v_type);
156:     for position in points {
157:         mesh.vertices.push(PackedVertex {
158:             position: position.map(pack_position),
159:             normal_axis,
160:             material,
161:             static_indirect: quad.light,
162:             ao: quad.ao,
163:         });
164:     }
165:     mesh.indices
166:         .extend_from_slice(&[base, base + 1, base + 2, base, base + 2, base + 3]);
167: }
168: 
169: fn pack_position(value: f32) -> u16 {
170:     (value * POSITION_FIXED_SCALE)
171:         .round()
172:         .clamp(0.0, u16::MAX as f32) as u16
173: }
174: 
175: fn normal_axis(dir: FaceDirection) -> u8 {
176:     match dir {
177:         FaceDirection::Up => 0,
178:         FaceDirection::Down => 1,
179:         FaceDirection::North => 2,
180:         FaceDirection::South => 3,
181:         FaceDirection::East => 4,
182:         FaceDirection::West => 5,
183:     }
184: }
185: 
186: pub(crate) fn material_id(v_type: VoxelType) -> u8 {
187:     match v_type {
188:         VoxelType::Wall => VOXEL_WALL,
189:         VoxelType::Floor => VOXEL_FLOOR,
190:         VoxelType::Ceiling => VOXEL_CEILING,
191:         VoxelType::Light => VOXEL_LIGHT,
192:         VoxelType::RedWall => VOXEL_RED_WALL,
193:         VoxelType::Grass => VOXEL_GRASS,
194:         VoxelType::Water => VOXEL_WATER,
195:         VoxelType::Tree => VOXEL_TREE,
196:         VoxelType::RedLight => VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
197:         VoxelType::PaleWall => VOXEL_PALE_WALL,
198:         VoxelType::DamagedWall => VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL,
199:         VoxelType::DryCarpet => VOXEL_DRY_CARPET,
200:         VoxelType::DeepCarpet => VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET,
201:         VoxelType::StickyCarpet => VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET,
202:         VoxelType::Fluid => VOXEL_FLUID,
203:         VoxelType::Glimmer => VOXEL_GLIMMER,
204:         VoxelType::ConcreteWall => VOXEL_CONCRETE_WALL,
205:         VoxelType::TileFloor => VOXEL_TILE_FLOOR,
206:         VoxelType::ConcreteFloor => VOXEL_CONCRETE_FLOOR,
207:         VoxelType::Crate => VOXEL_CRATE,
208:         VoxelType::Pipe => VOXEL_PIPE,
209:         VoxelType::MetalDoor => VOXEL_METAL_DOOR,
210:         VoxelType::AlmondWater => VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER,
211:     }
212: }

218:     #[test]
219:     fn isolated_voxel_becomes_indexed_closed_surface() {

236:         assert!(!artifacts.faces.instances.is_empty());
````
