  1: //! Exact ray/box math, diagnostic DDA, and optional empty-leaf stepping.
  2: 
  3: pub const GLSL: &str = r#"
  4: const float TRACE_INFINITY = 1e30;
  5: const float TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON = 1e-7;
  6: 
  7: struct RayBoxHit {
  8:     bool hit;
  9:     float entry;
 10:     float exit;
 11:     vec3 entryNormal;
 12: };
 13: 
 14: struct ChunkInterval {
 15:     int chunkIndex;
 16:     float entry;
 17:     float exit;
 18:     vec3 entryNormal;
 19: };
 20: 
 21: struct VoxelHit {
 22:     bool hit;
 23:     float distance;
 24:     vec3 normal;
 25:     uint material;
 26:     uint color;
 27:     uint lightWord;
 28: };
 29: 
 30: float inverseDirection(float direction) {
 31:     if (abs(direction) < 1e-20) {
 32:         return direction < 0.0 ? -TRACE_INFINITY : TRACE_INFINITY;
 33:     }
 34:     return 1.0 / direction;
 35: }
 36: 
 37: float distanceTieTolerance(float distance) {
 38:     return max(abs(distance) * 1e-6, TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON);
 39: }
 40: 
 41: float traversalSampleBias(float voxelSize) {
 42:     // This moves classification points off an exactly shared plane; it must
 43:     // remain smaller than nearby, genuinely distinct boundary crossings.
 44:     // At the 0.2 m reference grid, 1e-4 skipped a 13 micrometre
 45:     // interval between a wall and ceiling and changed the reported face.
 46:     return max(voxelSize * 1e-5, TRACE_MIN_TIE_EPSILON);
 47: }
 48: 
 49: RayBoxHit intersectBox(vec3 rayOrigin, vec3 rayDirection, vec3 boundsMin, vec3 boundsMax) {
 50:     // Parallel axes are handled explicitly so a boundary value never forms
 51:     // the undefined product 0 * infinity.
 52:     if ((abs(rayDirection.x) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.x < boundsMin.x || rayOrigin.x > boundsMax.x))
 53:         || (abs(rayDirection.y) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.y < boundsMin.y || rayOrigin.y > boundsMax.y))
 54:         || (abs(rayDirection.z) < 1e-20 && (rayOrigin.z < boundsMin.z || rayOrigin.z > boundsMax.z))) {
 55:         return RayBoxHit(false, 0.0, 0.0, vec3(0.0));
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     vec3 inverseRay = vec3(
 59:         inverseDirection(rayDirection.x),
 60:         inverseDirection(rayDirection.y),
 61:         inverseDirection(rayDirection.z)
 62:     );
 63:     vec3 first = (boundsMin - rayOrigin) * inverseRay;
 64:     vec3 second = (boundsMax - rayOrigin) * inverseRay;
 65:     vec3 nearTimes = min(first, second);
 66:     vec3 farTimes = max(first, second);
 67:     if (abs(rayDirection.x) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.x = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.x = TRACE_INFINITY; }
 68:     if (abs(rayDirection.y) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.y = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.y = TRACE_INFINITY; }
 69:     if (abs(rayDirection.z) < 1e-20) { nearTimes.z = -TRACE_INFINITY; farTimes.z = TRACE_INFINITY; }
 70: 
 71:     float entry = max(nearTimes.x, max(nearTimes.y, nearTimes.z));
 72:     float exit = min(farTimes.x, min(farTimes.y, farTimes.z));
 73:     if (entry > exit || exit < 0.0) {
 74:         return RayBoxHit(false, entry, exit, vec3(0.0));
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     vec3 normal;
 78:     if (entry <= 0.0) {
 79:         vec3 absoluteRay = abs(rayDirection);
 80:         if (absoluteRay.x >= absoluteRay.y && absoluteRay.x >= absoluteRay.z) normal = vec3(-sign(rayDirection.x), 0.0, 0.0);
 81:         else if (absoluteRay.y >= absoluteRay.z) normal = vec3(0.0, -sign(rayDirection.y), 0.0);
 82:         else normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -sign(rayDirection.z));
 83:     } else if (nearTimes.x >= nearTimes.y && nearTimes.x >= nearTimes.z) {
 84:         normal = vec3(rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
 85:     } else if (nearTimes.y >= nearTimes.z) {
 86:         normal = vec3(0.0, rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0);
 87:     } else {
 88:         normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0);
 89:     }
 90:     return RayBoxHit(true, max(entry, 0.0), exit, normal);
 91: }
 92: 
 93: float exitDistanceFromBox(
 94:     vec3 rayOrigin,
 95:     vec3 rayDirection,
 96:     vec3 boundsMin,
 97:     vec3 boundsMax,
 98:     out vec3 nextNormal
 99: ) {
100:     vec3 exitTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);
101:     if (abs(rayDirection.x) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.x = ((rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? boundsMax.x : boundsMin.x) - rayOrigin.x) / rayDirection.x;
102:     if (abs(rayDirection.y) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.y = ((rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? boundsMax.y : boundsMin.y) - rayOrigin.y) / rayDirection.y;
103:     if (abs(rayDirection.z) >= 1e-20) exitTimes.z = ((rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? boundsMax.z : boundsMin.z) - rayOrigin.z) / rayDirection.z;
104: 
105:     float nearest = min(exitTimes.x, min(exitTimes.y, exitTimes.z));
106:     // Traversal bias and tie tolerance solve different problems. The former
107:     // moves a sample into the next cell; using that comparatively large value
108:     // here incorrectly merges distinct, very close wall/ceiling crossings.
109:     float tolerance = distanceTieTolerance(nearest);
110:     // Use the same tolerant X/Y/Z precedence as finest-cell DDA. Without
111:     // this, a mathematically tied edge ray can acquire a different face
112:     // normal solely because one path jumped across a larger empty leaf.
113:     if (abs(exitTimes.x - nearest) <= tolerance) {
114:         nextNormal = vec3(rayDirection.x > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0, 0.0);
115:         return nearest;
116:     }
117:     if (abs(exitTimes.y - nearest) <= tolerance) {
118:         nextNormal = vec3(0.0, rayDirection.y > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0, 0.0);
119:         return nearest;
120:     }
121:     nextNormal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, rayDirection.z > 0.0 ? -1.0 : 1.0);
122:     return nearest;
123: }
124: 
125: VoxelHit traceChunkDda(
126:     vec3 rayOrigin,
127:     vec3 rayDirection,
128:     int rootIndex,
129:     float worldSize,
130:     float voxelSize,
131:     int svoDepth,
132:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
133: );
134: 
135: VoxelHit traceChunkSkippingEmptyLeaves(
136:     vec3 rayOrigin,
137:     vec3 rayDirection,
138:     int rootIndex,
139:     float worldSize,
140:     float voxelSize,
141:     int svoDepth,
142:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
143: ) {
144:     float distance = chunkBox.entry;
145:     vec3 normal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
146:     float sampleBias = traversalSampleBias(voxelSize);
147:     float refinementEntry = chunkBox.entry;
148:     vec3 refinementEntryNormal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
149: 
150:     for (int stepIndex = 0; stepIndex < 768; ++stepIndex) {
151:         if (distance > chunkBox.exit) break;
152:         vec3 samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
153:         VoxelLeaf leaf = lookupVoxelLeaf(samplePoint, rootIndex, worldSize, svoDepth);
154:         if (leaf.material != 0u) {
155:             // The coarse walk proves emptiness only. Resolve the final
156:             // voxel-scale crossing with the diagnostic algorithm so both
157:             // policies produce one canonical distance, material, and normal.
158:             RayBoxHit refinementBox = RayBoxHit(
159:                 true, refinementEntry, chunkBox.exit, refinementEntryNormal
160:             );
161:             return traceChunkDda(
162:                 rayOrigin,
163:                 rayDirection,
164:                 rootIndex,
165:                 worldSize,
166:                 voxelSize,
167:                 svoDepth,
168:                 refinementBox
169:             );
170:         }
171: 
172:         vec3 crossedNormal;
173:         float nextDistance = exitDistanceFromBox(
174:             rayOrigin, rayDirection, leaf.boundsMin, leaf.boundsMax, crossedNormal
175:         );
176:         if (nextDistance <= distance + sampleBias * 0.25) {
177:             nextDistance = distance + sampleBias;
178:         }
179:         // A normalized ray moves at most one voxel per axis over this short
180:         // interval. Retaining it lets the exact resolver reconstruct every
181:         // potentially competing face without replaying the skipped octant.
182:         refinementEntry = max(distance, nextDistance - voxelSize);
183:         refinementEntryNormal = normal;
184:         distance = nextDistance;
185:         normal = crossedNormal;
186:     }
187:     return VoxelHit(false, 0.0, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u);
188: }
189: 
190: VoxelHit traceChunkDda(
191:     vec3 rayOrigin,
192:     vec3 rayDirection,
193:     int rootIndex,
194:     float worldSize,
195:     float voxelSize,
196:     int svoDepth,
197:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
198: ) {
199:     float sampleBias = traversalSampleBias(voxelSize);
200:     float distance = chunkBox.entry;
201:     vec3 samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
202:     vec3 cell = floor(samplePoint / voxelSize);
203:     vec3 directionStep = sign(rayDirection);
204:     vec3 normal = chunkBox.entryNormal;
205: 
206:     for (int stepIndex = 0; stepIndex < 768; ++stepIndex) {
207:         if (distance > chunkBox.exit) break;
208:         samplePoint = rayOrigin + rayDirection * min(distance + sampleBias, chunkBox.exit);
209:         VoxelLeaf leaf = lookupVoxelLeaf(samplePoint, rootIndex, worldSize, svoDepth);
210:         if (leaf.material != 0u) {
211:             return VoxelHit(true, distance, normal, leaf.material, leaf.color, leaf.lightWord);
212:         }
213: 
214:         // Recompute boundary times from the canonical integer cell each step.
215:         // Repeated `nextTime += deltaTime` accumulates enough rounding error
216:         // to reverse two distinct wall/ceiling crossings near a long ray.
217:         vec3 nextBoundary = (cell + max(directionStep, vec3(0.0))) * voxelSize;
218:         vec3 nextTimes = vec3(TRACE_INFINITY);
219:         if (abs(rayDirection.x) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.x = (nextBoundary.x - rayOrigin.x) / rayDirection.x;
220:         if (abs(rayDirection.y) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.y = (nextBoundary.y - rayOrigin.y) / rayDirection.y;
221:         if (abs(rayDirection.z) >= 1e-20) nextTimes.z = (nextBoundary.z - rayOrigin.z) / rayDirection.z;
222: 
223:         float nextDistance = min(nextTimes.x, min(nextTimes.y, nextTimes.z));
224:         if (nextDistance > chunkBox.exit) break;
225:         // Step every tied axis so a ray through an edge/corner cannot stall.
226:         // This is a floating-point equality tolerance, not the sampling bias.
227:         // Keeping them separate preserves the mathematically nearer face when
228:         // two boundaries are close but not actually coincident.
229:         float tieEpsilon = distanceTieTolerance(nextDistance);
230:         bool crossX = abs(nextTimes.x - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
231:         bool crossY = abs(nextTimes.y - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
232:         bool crossZ = abs(nextTimes.z - nextDistance) <= tieEpsilon;
233:         if (crossX) cell.x += directionStep.x;
234:         if (crossY) cell.y += directionStep.y;
235:         if (crossZ) cell.z += directionStep.z;
236:         if (crossX) normal = vec3(-directionStep.x, 0.0, 0.0);
237:         else if (crossY) normal = vec3(0.0, -directionStep.y, 0.0);
238:         else normal = vec3(0.0, 0.0, -directionStep.z);
239:         distance = nextDistance;
240:     }
241:     return VoxelHit(false, 0.0, vec3(0.0), 0u, 0u, 0u);
242: }
243: 
244: VoxelHit traceChunk(
245:     vec3 rayOrigin,
246:     vec3 rayDirection,
247:     int rootIndex,
248:     float worldSize,
249:     float voxelSize,
250:     int svoDepth,
251:     RayBoxHit chunkBox
252: ) {
253:     if (uEmptySpaceSkipEnabled == 1) {
254:         return traceChunkSkippingEmptyLeaves(
255:             rayOrigin, rayDirection, rootIndex, worldSize, voxelSize, svoDepth, chunkBox
256:         );
257:     }
258:     return traceChunkDda(
259:         rayOrigin, rayDirection, rootIndex, worldSize, voxelSize, svoDepth, chunkBox
260:     );
261: }

## File: wasm_frontend/src/drivers/cpu_canvas.rs
````rust
  1: //! Canvas-2D blit driver for the CPU splatting renderer.
  2: //!
  3: //! All rendering logic lives in the platform-free
  4: //! `adapters::cpu_splatter::SoftwareRasterizer`; this wrapper's only job is
  5: //! to copy the finished RGBA framebuffer into the canvas via `ImageData` —
  6: //! no WebGL context is created at all.
  7: 
  8: use wasm_bindgen::{Clamped, JsCast, JsValue};
  9: use web_sys::{CanvasRenderingContext2d, HtmlCanvasElement, ImageData};
 10: 
 11: use crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::SoftwareRasterizer;
 12: use crate::application::ports::{ChunkDraw, FrameParams, RendererPort};
 13: 
 14: pub struct CpuCanvasRenderer {
 15:     rasterizer: SoftwareRasterizer,
 16:     ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2d,
 17:     settings: crate::adapters::cpu_splatter::CpuRenderSettings,
 18:     /// Most recent synchronous CPU stages, measured independently so the
 19:     /// HUD can distinguish renderer cost from Canvas-2D presentation cost.
 20:     rasterizer_ms: f64,
 21:     blit_ms: f64,
 22: }
 23: 
 24: impl CpuCanvasRenderer {
 25:     pub fn new(canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
 26:         let ctx = canvas
 27:             .get_context("2d")?
 28:             .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no 2d context available"))?
 29:             .dyn_into::<CanvasRenderingContext2d>()?;
 30:         let settings = crate::get_cpu_settings();
 31:         Ok(Self {
 32:             rasterizer: SoftwareRasterizer::new(canvas.width() as usize, canvas.height() as usize),
 33:             ctx,
 34:             settings,
 35:             rasterizer_ms: 0.0,
 36:             blit_ms: 0.0,
 37:         })
 38:     }
 39: 
 40:     pub fn resize(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32) {
 41:         // The browser composition root already applies the validated CPU
 42:         // resolution factor to the canvas. Matching it exactly is essential:
 43:         // `put_image_data` does not scale a smaller image and would otherwise
 44:         // leave most of the canvas stale or black.
 45:         self.rasterizer
 46:             .resize(width.max(1) as usize, height.max(1) as usize);
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     pub fn telemetry_string(&self) -> String {
 50:         let stats = self.rasterizer.telemetry();
 51:         format!(
 52:             "CPU:{:.1}+{:.1}ms V:{}/{}{} (D:{})/S:{}/P:{}K/{}K{}{}",
 53:             self.rasterizer_ms,
 54:             self.blit_ms,
 55:             stats.visited_nodes,
 56:             stats.node_visit_limit,
 57:             if stats.node_budget_limited { "N!" } else { "" },
 58:             stats.max_virtual_depth,
 59:             stats.splat_count,
 60:             stats.pixel_writes / 1000,
 61:             stats.pixel_write_limit / 1000,
 62:             if stats.pixel_budget_limited { "P!" } else { "" },
 63:             if stats.budget_exhausted { "!" } else { "" }
 64:         )
 65:     }
 66: }
 67: 
 68: impl RendererPort for CpuCanvasRenderer {
 69:     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
 70:         self.rasterizer.upload_atlas(texels);
 71:     }
 72: 
 73:     fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
 74:         self.rasterizer.upload_atlas_rows(first_row, texels)
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     fn cpu_telemetry_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
 78:         Some(self.telemetry_string())
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
 82:         self.settings = crate::get_cpu_settings();
 83:         self.settings.fov_tan = crate::drivers::webgl::fov_tan();
 84:         // The optimization switchboard is sampled once per frame here; the
 85:         // platform-free rasterizer itself never reads globals.
 86:         self.settings.toggles = crate::get_render_toggles();
 87:         self.rasterizer.settings = self.settings;
 88: 
 89:         let render_start = browser_now_ms();
 90:         self.rasterizer.draw(frame, chunks);
 91:         let render_end = browser_now_ms();
 92:         let width = self.rasterizer.width() as u32;
 93:         let height = self.rasterizer.height() as u32;
 94:         let fb = self.rasterizer.framebuffer();
 95: 
 96:         if let Ok(image) = ImageData::new_with_u8_clamped_array_and_sh(Clamped(fb), width, height) {
 97:             let _ = self.ctx.put_image_data(&image, 0.0, 0.0);
 98:         }
 99:         let blit_end = browser_now_ms();
100:         self.rasterizer_ms = render_end - render_start;
101:         self.blit_ms = blit_end - render_end;
102:     }
103: }
104: 
105: fn browser_now_ms() -> f64 {
106:     web_sys::window()
107:         .and_then(|window| window.performance())
108:         .map_or(0.0, |performance| performance.now())
109: }
````

  1: /// Represents a dense 3D grid of voxels.

  3: pub struct VoxelGrid {
  4:     width: usize,
  5:     height: usize,

  7:     data: Vec<u8>,

 17:     pub traversal_gates: Vec<crate::domain::entities::anomaly::TraversalGate>,

 88: pub const VOXEL_ALMOND_WATER: u8 = 23;
 89: /// Duller, browner ordinary Level 0 wallpaper: `institution_age` past
 90: /// threshold. Solid like WALL, same material class, just older.
 91: pub const VOXEL_AGED_WALLPAPER: u8 = 24;
 92: /// Duller, blotchier ordinary Level 0 carpet, paired with

 99: /// The one authoritative material palette, `0xRRGGBB` per voxel id. Every
100: /// consumer — octree bake, greedy-mesh debug colors, CPU splatter, and the
101: /// generated GLSL tables — derives from this table so a new material can
102: /// never render differently across paths.
103: pub const MATERIAL_COLORS: [u32; VOXEL_MATERIAL_COUNT] = [
104:     0x000000, // 0 air (never drawn)
105:     0xDDCC66, // 1 yellow wallpaper wall
106:     0x998811, // 2 office carpet floor
107:     0xCCCCCC, // 3 dropped ceiling
108:     0xFFF8D6, // 4 fluorescent panel
109:     0x880000, // 5 crimson / peeled red wall
110:     0x4F9A3D, // 6 grass
111:     0x3A6FB8, // 7 water
112:     0x6B4A2F, // 8 tree / dark pillar
113:     0xFF4433, // 9 red light
114:     0xD8D2C0, // 10 pale arch wall
115:     0x8A7F5C, // 11 rough damaged wall
116:     0xC2B76B, // 12 dry shallow carpet
117:     0x6B5E22, // 13 deep wet carpet
118:     0x7A4A26, // 14 sticky red-room carpet
119:     0x2E2A22, // 15 dark pooled fluid
120:     0x9FC4E8, // 16 cool emergency glimmer
121:     0x8F8D88, // 17 bare structural concrete
122:     0xBDBBB0, // 18 institutional tile floor
123:     0x6E6C66, // 19 poured concrete slab
124:     0x9C7B4A, // 20 wooden supply crate
125:     0x3E4348, // 21 exposed pipe / rebar
126:     0x4A5A6A, // 22 metal fire-exit door
127:     0xEDE6D0, // 23 almond water bottle
128:     0xA69456, // 24 aged/stained yellow wallpaper

132: /// Palette lookup as normalized linear-ish RGB for shader tables.
133: pub fn material_color_f32(voxel: u8) -> [f32; 3] {
134:     let c = MATERIAL_COLORS
135:         .get(voxel as usize)
136:         .copied()
137:         .unwrap_or(0x000000);
138:     [
139:         ((c >> 16) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
140:         ((c >> 8) & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
141:         (c & 0xFF) as f32 / 255.0,
142:     ]
143: }

145: /// Materials that block the player and produce collision boxes. Everything
146: /// else is walkable or decorative.

  1: //! Pooled SVO node atlas: stable, fixed-size chunk slots inside one shared
  2: //! four-word-per-node storage stream.
  3: //!
  4: //! This is the raymarcher's analog of "vertex pooling" in mesh-based voxel
  5: //! engines. The naive approach (concatenate every resident chunk's node
  6: //! array and re-upload the whole GPU buffer on any change) makes every chunk
  7: //! load cost O(world) in CPU copies and transfer bandwidth. The pool instead
  8: //! gives each chunk a fixed row-aligned slot: loading a chunk rebases and
  9: //! uploads *only that slot's rows*, and evicting a chunk is free (its slot is
 10: //! simply reused later; stale nodes are never referenced by the draw table).
 11: //!
 12: //! Every chunk's node array is padded to whole 1024-node rows by the
 13: //! core `OctreeGpuSerializer`, so slots stay row-aligned by construction.
 14: 
 15: use crate::application::ports::ChunkPayload;
 16: use crate::application::streaming::ChunkKey;
 17: 
 18: /// The raymarch pass's fixed per-frame chunk-table capacity.
 19: pub const MAX_CHUNKS: usize = 25;
 20: 
 21: /// SVO nodes per atlas row. Must match the raymarch upload offset and the
 22: /// core serializer's row padding.
 23: pub const ROW_TEXELS: usize = 1024;
 24: 
 25: /// One air-leaf texel (type flag 1, voxel type 0): what free space decodes to.
 26: const AIR_LEAF: [u32; 4] = [1, 0, 0, 0];
 27: 
 28: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 29: pub struct AtlasPool {
 30:     /// Rows per slot. Grows (forcing a relayout) when a chunk won't fit.
 31:     slot_rows: usize,
 32:     /// Slot occupancy; index is the slot number.
 33:     slots: Vec<Option<ChunkKey>>,
 34: }
 35: 
 36: impl AtlasPool {
 37:     pub fn new() -> Self {
 38:         Self::default()
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     /// Nodes (texels) per slot.
 42:     pub fn slot_nodes(&self) -> usize {
 43:         self.slot_rows * ROW_TEXELS
 44:     }
 45: 
 46:     /// Total rows in the pooled texture.
 47:     pub fn total_rows(&self) -> usize {
 48:         self.slot_rows * self.slots.len()
 49:     }
 50: 
 51:     /// Ensures the pool holds at least `num_slots` slots of at least `rows`
 52:     /// rows each. Returns `true` when the layout changed — every slot
 53:     /// assignment is then dropped and the caller must reassign all resident
 54:     /// chunks and re-upload the whole pool.
 55:     pub fn ensure_layout(&mut self, num_slots: usize, rows: usize) -> bool {
 56:         let changed = rows > self.slot_rows || num_slots > self.slots.len();
 57:         if changed {
 58:             self.slot_rows = self.slot_rows.max(rows);
 59:             let len = self.slots.len().max(num_slots);
 60:             self.slots.clear();
 61:             self.slots.resize(len, None);
 62:         }
 63:         changed
 64:     }
 65: 
 66:     /// Assigns (or finds) the slot for `key`. Returns `None` when the pool
 67:     /// is full — the caller sized it for the streaming radius, so that is a
 68:     /// logic error handled by falling back to a full relayout.
 69:     pub fn assign(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 70:         if let Some(i) = self.slots.iter().position(|s| *s == Some(key)) {
 71:             return Some(i);
 72:         }
 73:         let free = self.slots.iter().position(|s| s.is_none())?;
 74:         self.slots[free] = Some(key);
 75:         Some(free)
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     pub fn release(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) {
 79:         for slot in &mut self.slots {
 80:             if *slot == Some(key) {
 81:                 *slot = None;
 82:             }
 83:         }
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     /// First texture row of a slot.
 87:     pub fn slot_first_row(&self, slot: usize) -> usize {
 88:         slot * self.slot_rows
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     /// Node offset of `key`'s slot within the pooled atlas.
 92:     pub fn node_offset_of(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 93:         self.slots
 94:             .iter()
 95:             .position(|s| *s == Some(key))
 96:             .map(|i| i * self.slot_nodes())
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     /// Whether `payload` fits in the current slot size.
100:     pub fn fits(&self, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> bool {
101:         payload.nodes.len() / 4 <= self.slot_nodes()
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// The slot-sized texel block for one chunk: child pointers rebased to
105:     /// the slot's node offset, tail padded with air leaves.
106:     pub fn rebased_block(&self, slot: usize, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> Vec<u32> {
107:         let node_offset = (slot * self.slot_nodes()) as u32;
108:         let mut block = Vec::with_capacity(self.slot_nodes() * 4);
109:         block.extend_from_slice(&payload.nodes);
110:         // Internal nodes (type flag 0) store child indices local to the
111:         // chunk; shift them into pool space.
112:         for i in 0..(payload.nodes.len() / 4) {
113:             if block[i * 4] == 0 {
114:                 block[i * 4 + 1] += node_offset;
115:             }
116:         }
117:         while block.len() < self.slot_nodes() * 4 {
118:             block.extend_from_slice(&AIR_LEAF);
119:         }
120:         block
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// The whole pool as one texel stream (initial upload, relayouts, and
124:     /// back ends without partial-update support). `lookup` resolves a slot's
125:     /// chunk key to its payload.
126:     pub fn full_texels<'a>(
127:         &self,
128:         lookup: impl Fn(ChunkKey) -> Option<&'a ChunkPayload>,
129:     ) -> Vec<u32> {
130:         let mut texels = Vec::with_capacity(self.total_rows() * ROW_TEXELS * 4);
131:         for (slot, occupant) in self.slots.iter().enumerate() {
132:             match occupant.and_then(&lookup) {
133:                 Some(payload) => texels.extend_from_slice(&self.rebased_block(slot, payload)),
134:                 None => {
135:                     for _ in 0..self.slot_nodes() {
136:                         texels.extend_from_slice(&AIR_LEAF);
137:                     }
138:                 }
139:             }
140:         }
141:         texels
142:     }
143: }
144: 
145: /// Rows needed to hold a payload's node array.
146: pub fn payload_rows(payload: &ChunkPayload) -> usize {
147:     (payload.nodes.len() / 4).div_ceil(ROW_TEXELS)
148: }
149: 
150: #[cfg(test)]
151: mod tests {
152:     use super::*;
153:     use crate::application::streaming::chunk_key;
154: 
155:     fn payload(root: u32, node_count: usize) -> ChunkPayload {
156:         ChunkPayload {
157:             root,
158:             nodes: vec![0; node_count * 4],
159:             world_size: 12.8,
160:             voxel_size: 0.2,
161:             svo_depth: 6,
162:             surface: crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload::empty(0),
163:             lights: vec![],
164:             collision: vec![],
165:             traversal_gates: vec![],
166:             pit_hazards: vec![],
167:             supply_items: vec![],
168:             level_exits: vec![],
169:         }
170:     }
171: 
172:     #[test]
173:     fn slots_are_stable_across_unrelated_evictions() {
174:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
175:         pool.ensure_layout(4, 2);
176:         let (a, b, c) = (
177:             chunk_key(0.0, 0.0),
178:             chunk_key(10.0, 0.0),
179:             chunk_key(20.0, 0.0),
180:         );
181:         let slot_a = pool.assign(a).unwrap();
182:         let slot_b = pool.assign(b).unwrap();
183:         pool.release(a);
184:         let slot_c = pool.assign(c).unwrap();
185:         // b never moved; c reused a's freed slot.
186:         assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(b), Some(slot_b * pool.slot_nodes()));
187:         assert_eq!(slot_c, slot_a);
188:     }
189: 
190:     #[test]
191:     fn rebased_block_shifts_internal_child_pointers_only() {
192:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
193:         pool.ensure_layout(2, 1);
194: 
195:         let mut p = payload(0, 2);
196:         // node 0: internal, child_base 8; node 1: leaf, voxel_type 42.
197:         p.nodes[0] = 0;
198:         p.nodes[1] = 8;
199:         p.nodes[4] = 1;
200:         p.nodes[5] = 42;
201: 
202:         let block = pool.rebased_block(1, &p);
203:         assert_eq!(block.len(), pool.slot_nodes() * 4);
204:         assert_eq!(block[1], 8 + pool.slot_nodes() as u32);
205:         assert_eq!(block[4], 1, "leaf type flag untouched");
206:         assert_eq!(block[5], 42, "leaf payload untouched");
207:         // Padding decodes as air leaves.
208:         assert_eq!(&block[8..12], &AIR_LEAF);
209:     }
210: 
211:     #[test]
212:     fn growing_the_layout_invalidates_assignments() {
213:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
214:         assert!(pool.ensure_layout(2, 1));
215:         let key = chunk_key(0.0, 0.0);
216:         pool.assign(key).unwrap();
217:         assert!(!pool.ensure_layout(2, 1), "same layout is a no-op");
218:         assert!(pool.ensure_layout(2, 3), "bigger slots relayout");
219:         assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(key), None);
220:     }
221: 
222:     #[test]
223:     fn full_texels_covers_every_slot() {
224:         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
225:         pool.ensure_layout(3, 1);
226:         let key = chunk_key(0.0, 0.0);
227:         let slot = pool.assign(key).unwrap();
228:         let p = payload(0, 4);
229:         let texels = pool.full_texels(|k| (k == key).then_some(&p));
230:         assert_eq!(texels.len(), 3 * pool.slot_nodes() * 4);
231:         // Unassigned slots are air.
232:         let other_slot = (slot + 1) % 3;
233:         let base = other_slot * pool.slot_nodes() * 4;
234:         assert_eq!(&texels[base..base + 4], &AIR_LEAF);
235:     }
236: }

  1: //! Chunk streaming policy and the in-memory chunk store.
  2: //!
  3: //! The world is an infinite plane of square chunks. Each frame the policy
  4: //! computes the set of chunk origins that should be resident around the
  5: //! player; the engine loads missing ones (budgeted, to avoid frame hitches —
  6: //! wasm has no threads, so time-slicing replaces the background meshing
  7: //! thread a native engine would use) and evicts the rest.
  8: 
  9: use std::collections::HashMap;
 10: 
 11: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 12: use crate::application::ports::ChunkPayload;
 13: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
 14: use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{LevelExit, PitHazard, TraversalGate};
 15: use vackrooms::domain::entities::supplies::SupplyItem;
 16: 
 17: /// Integer key for a chunk, quantized from its world origin.
 18: /// Origins are always integer multiples of `chunk_size`, so rounding to
 19: /// millimetres gives a stable, hashable key.
 20: pub type ChunkKey = (i64, i64);
 21: 
 22: pub fn chunk_key(origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32) -> ChunkKey {
 23:     (
 24:         (origin_x * 1000.0).round() as i64,
 25:         (origin_z * 1000.0).round() as i64,
 26:     )
 27: }
 28: 
 29: /// Decides which chunks should be resident for a given player position.
 30: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 31: pub struct StreamingPolicy {
 32:     /// World-space side length of a chunk.
 33:     pub chunk_size: f32,
 34:     /// Chebyshev radius in chunks: 1 -> 3x3 resident set, 2 -> 5x5.
 35:     pub radius: i32,
 36: }
 37: 
 38: impl StreamingPolicy {
 39:     /// Returns the desired chunk origins, sorted nearest-first so the load
 40:     /// budget is always spent on the most urgent chunk.
 41:     pub fn desired_origins(&self, player_x: f32, player_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32)> {
 42:         let px = if player_x.is_finite() { player_x } else { 0.0 };
 43:         let pz = if player_z.is_finite() { player_z } else { 0.0 };
 44:         let base_x = (px / self.chunk_size).floor() * self.chunk_size;
 45:         let base_z = (pz / self.chunk_size).floor() * self.chunk_size;
 46: 
 47:         let mut origins = Vec::with_capacity(((2 * self.radius + 1).pow(2)) as usize);
 48:         for dz in -self.radius..=self.radius {
 49:             for dx in -self.radius..=self.radius {
 50:                 origins.push((
 51:                     base_x + dx as f32 * self.chunk_size,
 52:                     base_z + dz as f32 * self.chunk_size,
 53:                 ));
 54:             }
 55:         }
 56:         origins.sort_by(|a, b| {
 57:             let da = (a.0 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px).powi(2)
 58:                 + (a.1 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz).powi(2);
 59:             let db = (b.0 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px).powi(2)
 60:                 + (b.1 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz).powi(2);
 61:             da.total_cmp(&db)
 62:         });
 63:         origins
 64:     }
 65: }
 66: 
 67: /// A resident chunk: payload plus its world origin and current level of
 68: /// detail (0 = full resolution; higher = coarser, see `ChunkSourcePort`).
 69: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 70: pub struct LoadedChunk {
 71:     pub origin: (f32, f32),
 72:     pub lod: u8,
 73:     /// Exact immutable encounter state from which every payload view
 74:     /// (collision, SVO, mesh and lighting) was derived.
 75:     pub reality: RealitySnapshot,
 76:     /// Cached identity for diagnostics and fast rejection paths. Exact
 77:     /// equality still uses `reality`, so a hash collision cannot mix worlds.
 78:     pub reality_fingerprint: u64,
 79:     pub payload: ChunkPayload,
 80: }
 81: 
 82: impl LoadedChunk {
 83:     pub fn new(
 84:         origin: (f32, f32),
 85:         lod: u8,
 86:         reality: RealitySnapshot,
 87:         payload: ChunkPayload,
 88:     ) -> Self {
 89:         let reality_fingerprint = reality.fingerprint();
 90:         Self {
 91:             origin,
 92:             lod,
 93:             reality,
 94:             reality_fingerprint,
 95:             payload,
 96:         }
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     pub fn is_in_reality(&self, reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> bool {
100:         self.reality_fingerprint == reality.fingerprint() && &self.reality == reality
101:     }
102: }
103: 
104: /// Keyed store of resident chunks. Iteration order is the insertion order of
105: /// keys (tracked separately) so atlas offsets stay deterministic.
106: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
107: pub struct ChunkStore {
108:     chunks: HashMap<ChunkKey, LoadedChunk>,
109:     order: Vec<ChunkKey>,
110: }
111: 
112: impl ChunkStore {
113:     pub fn new() -> Self {
114:         Self {
115:             chunks: HashMap::new(),
116:             order: Vec::new(),
117:         }
118:     }
119: 
120:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
121:         self.order.len()
122:     }
123: 
124:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
125:         self.order.is_empty()
126:     }
127: 
128:     pub fn contains(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> bool {
129:         self.chunks.contains_key(&key)
130:     }
131: 
132:     pub fn get(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<&LoadedChunk> {
133:         self.chunks.get(&key)
134:     }
135: 
136:     pub fn insert(&mut self, key: ChunkKey, chunk: LoadedChunk) {
137:         if self.chunks.insert(key, chunk).is_none() {
138:             self.order.push(key);
139:         }
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// Removes every chunk whose key is not in `keep`, returning whether
143:     /// anything changed.
144:     pub fn retain_keys(&mut self, keep: &[ChunkKey]) -> bool {
145:         let before = self.order.len();
146:         self.order.retain(|k| keep.contains(k));
147:         self.chunks.retain(|k, _| keep.contains(k));
148:         before != self.order.len()
149:     }
150: 
151:     /// Chunks in deterministic (insertion) order.
152:     pub fn iter_ordered(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LoadedChunk> {
153:         self.order.iter().filter_map(|k| self.chunks.get(k))
154:     }
155: 
156:     /// All collision boxes of all resident chunks.
157:     pub fn all_collision_boxes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Aabb> {
158:         self.iter_ordered().flat_map(|c| c.payload.collision.iter())
159:     }
160: 
161:     pub fn all_traversal_gates(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &TraversalGate> {
162:         self.iter_ordered()
163:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.traversal_gates.iter())
164:     }
165: 
166:     pub fn all_supply_items(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &SupplyItem> {
167:         self.iter_ordered()
168:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.supply_items.iter())
169:     }
170: 
171:     pub fn all_level_exits(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LevelExit> {
172:         self.iter_ordered()
173:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.level_exits.iter())
174:     }
175: 
176:     pub fn all_pit_hazards(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &PitHazard> {
177:         self.iter_ordered()
178:             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.pit_hazards.iter())
179:     }
180: }
181: 
182: #[cfg(test)]
183: mod tests {
184:     use super::*;
185: 
186:     #[test]
187:     fn desired_origins_covers_square_around_player() {
188:         let policy = StreamingPolicy {
189:             chunk_size: 10.0,
190:             radius: 1,
191:         };
192:         let origins = policy.desired_origins(5.0, 5.0);
193:         assert_eq!(origins.len(), 9);
194:         // Nearest-first: the chunk containing the player comes first.
195:         assert_eq!(origins[0], (0.0, 0.0));
196:         assert!(origins.contains(&(-10.0, -10.0)));
197:         assert!(origins.contains(&(10.0, 10.0)));
198:     }
199: 
200:     #[test]
201:     fn desired_origins_handles_negative_coordinates() {
202:         let policy = StreamingPolicy {
203:             chunk_size: 10.0,
204:             radius: 1,
205:         };
206:         let origins = policy.desired_origins(-0.1, -0.1);
207:         assert_eq!(origins[0], (-10.0, -10.0));
208:     }
209: 
210:     #[test]
211:     fn store_eviction_reports_change() {
212:         let mut store = ChunkStore::new();
213:         let payload = ChunkPayload {
214:             root: 0,
215:             nodes: vec![],
216:             world_size: 10.0,
217:             voxel_size: 0.2,
218:             svo_depth: 6,
219:             surface: crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload::empty(0),
220:             lights: vec![],
221:             collision: vec![],
222:             traversal_gates: vec![],
223:             pit_hazards: vec![],
224:             supply_items: vec![],
225:             level_exits: vec![],
226:         };
227:         store.insert(
228:             chunk_key(0.0, 0.0),
229:             LoadedChunk::new((0.0, 0.0), 0, RealitySnapshot::default(), payload.clone()),
230:         );
231:         store.insert(
232:             chunk_key(10.0, 0.0),
233:             LoadedChunk::new((10.0, 0.0), 0, RealitySnapshot::default(), payload),
234:         );
235:         assert_eq!(store.len(), 2);
236:         assert!(store.retain_keys(&[chunk_key(0.0, 0.0)]));
237:         assert_eq!(store.len(), 1);
238:         assert!(!store.retain_keys(&[chunk_key(0.0, 0.0)]));
239:     }
240: }

## File: README.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only engine in Rust, organized with Clean Architecture and compiled
  4: to WebAssembly. Procedural world planning, finite-range voxel irradiance,
  5: sparse voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk streaming, and sliding player
  6: collision remain deterministic CPU work. One WebGPU facade presents four
  7: runtime-selectable strategies: indexed surfaces, compact face splats, SVO
  8: raymarching, and a CPU reference image uploaded through WebGPU.
  9: 
 10: See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full design (layer map, ports,
 11: data flow, SVO node encoding, streaming, and rendering pipelines).
 12: 
 13: ## How it works
 14: 
 15: Each chunk starts with the same authoritative pipeline, on the main thread or
 16: in a generation worker. The selected renderer controls which derived upload
 17: artifacts are retained:
 18: 
 19: 1. **Procedural generation** (`src/use_cases/generate_chunk.rs` +
 20:    `*_level.rs`) — a `LevelGenerator` fills a `VoxelGrid` deterministically
 21:    from `(chunk position, seed, config)`. Level 0 is the office backrooms;
 22:    level 34 is an open grassland. Both tile seamlessly because geometry is
 23:    derived from world-space coordinates, never chunk-local ones.
 24: 2. **Lighting preparation** — exposed emissive faces seed an air-only,
 25:    finite-range RGB diffuse field; solids receive it but never propagate it.
 26:    Runtime panels are separately derived from exposed emissive undersides and
 27:    remain analytic area lights in every renderer strategy.
 28: 3. **SVO build + optional serialization** — the lit grid is packed into a
 29:    sparse voxel octree for collision and traversal. Recursive cubes wholly
 30:    beyond a non-power-of-two grid are pruned directly to the canonical air
 31:    leaf. Raymarch and CPU strategies serialize nodes as a row-padded,
 32:    four-`u32` stream; raymarch uploads it to GPU storage while the CPU
 33:    reference decodes the same words (`src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`).
 34: 4. **Streaming** (`wasm_frontend/src/application/streaming.rs`) — chunks
 35:    around the player are requested, LOD'd by distance, and evicted as the
 36:    player moves; a coarse-first pass keeps distant chunks cheap.
 37: 5. **Collision** — player movement is axis-separated (X and Z tested and
 38:    moved independently against a `CollisionWorld`), so hitting a wall
 39:    diagonally slides along it instead of stopping dead.
 40: 6. **Render** — one `WebGpuRenderer` port adapter delegates resident chunks to
 41:    one of four composable strategies (see below).
 42: 
 43: Generation is deliberately CPU-authoritative: architectural graph decisions,
 44: reality epochs, and seeded noise must produce the same chunk regardless of
 45: GPU or worker scheduling. The GPU instead performs renderer-derived work that
 46: does not redefine the world: vertex pulling, face-to-quad expansion,
 47: depth-tested supply-label billboard expansion, and per-pixel SVO traversal.
 48: 
 49: A standing gameplay quirk: leaning into a wall for a few seconds has a
 50: chance to "noclip" the player between level 0 (backrooms) and level 34
 51: (grassland) — see `update_noclip` in
 52: `wasm_frontend/src/application/engine.rs`.
 53: 
 54: ### Renderer backends
 55: 
 56: Chosen with `?renderer=` (see [Usage](#usage)):
 57: 
 58: | Value | WebGPU strategy | Notes |
 59: |---|---|---|
 60: | `surface` *(default)* | indexed surfaces | Greedy-mesh indices plus compact vertices. WGSL pulls and decodes vertices from a storage buffer; hardware depth resolves visibility. |
 61: | `splat` | face splats | Compact face records live in a storage buffer. The vertex stage expands each record into four corners; CPU draw submission applies the configured cell and face budgets. |
 62: | `raymarch` | SVO raymarcher | A fullscreen triangle drives fragment-stage traversal of the merged SVO storage-buffer atlas. |
 63: | `cpu` | CPU reference / WebGPU present | The deterministic software SVO rasterizer writes RGBA8; WebGPU uploads that framebuffer to a texture and presents it. |
 64: 
 65: All four choices require WebGPU for presentation. Adapter or device creation
 66: failure is reported in the loading HUD; the engine does not silently switch
 67: rendering algorithms.
 68: 
 69: ## Build & run
 70: 
 71: Prerequisites: Rust (with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target) and
 72: [`wasm-pack`](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/).
 73: The page imports wasm-bindgen's native ES-module output directly; there is no
 74: webpack build stage in this repository.
 75: 
 76: ```sh
 77: # 1. Build the wasm front end into static/pkg/
 78: npm run build:wasm
 79: 
 80: # 2. Run the dev server
 81: cargo run
 82: 
 83: # 3. Open http://localhost:3000
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: ## Usage
 87: 
 88: Click to capture the mouse; WASD to move, ESC to release.
 89: 
 90: - `http://localhost:3000/` — wasm engine (low-spec profile: 3×3 chunk
 91:   streaming, 0.2 u voxels, adaptive resolution)
 92: - `http://localhost:3000/?spec=high` — high-spec profile (5×5 chunks,
 93:   0.1 u voxels)
 94: 
 95: The former `/legacy` Three.js client and route have been retired. The native
 96: server still exposes `/maze` and `/octree` as diagnostic data endpoints; the
 97: wasm client does not depend on them.
 98: 
 99: Worlds are shareable by URL — every query parameter below is optional and
100: combinable:
101: 
102: | Parameter | Values | Effect |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | `spec` | `low`, `high` | Shared generation/rendering quality decision (case-insensitive). Default is low. |
105: | `voxel_size` | `0.4`, `0.2`, `0.1`, `0.05` | Overrides scene voxel size after seam, progressive-LOD, SVO-depth, and dense-memory validation. `0.4` is high-profile-only; `0.05` is standard-profile-only. |
106: | `seed` | number or text | World seed. Non-numeric text is hashed (FNV-1a) so words work too. |
107: | `pillars` | `0`–`4` | Structural column density multiplier (`0` = none). Default `1`. |
108: | `walls` | `0`–`4` | Office wall density multiplier (`0` = open plan). Default `1`. |
109: | `atria` | `0`–`4` | How much of the world vaults into tall atria. Default `1`. |
110: | `lights` | `0`–`4` | Ceiling light panel density. Default `1`. |
111: | `renderer` | `surface`, `splat`, `raymarch`, `cpu` | Selects one of the four WebGPU strategies (see above). |
112: | `cpu_preset` | `performance`, `balanced`, `quality`, `maximum`, `custom` | Typed CPU workload profile. Presets render at 12.5%–50% backing resolution per axis and present the complete image over the full page; `balanced` is the default. |
113: | `cpu_scale` | `0.25`–`2` | Custom CPU backing scale relative to the 25%-viewport baseline; CSS presentation always remains full-page. |
114: | `cpu_lod_px` | `0.25`–`2` | Custom projected-radius MIP cutoff; lower preserves finer distant geometry. |
115: | `cpu_splat_radius_px` | `1`–`16` | Custom maximum splat radius; lower values virtually split large leaves for finer surfaces. |
116: | `cpu_virtual_depth` | `3`–`8` | Custom cap on virtual solid-leaf subdivision. |
117: | `cpu_mip_occupancy` | `0`–`0.5` | Custom sparse-LOD rejection threshold; lower retains sparser distant detail. |
118: | `cpu_range` | `16`–`256` | CPU draw distance in world units. |
119: | `cpu_shadows` | `off`, `hero`, `full` | CPU fixture visibility: unshadowed, one cached hero-fixture approximation, or the expensive reference that traces every point/Gauss-sample endpoint. |
120: | `workers` | `auto`, `0`, `1`–`4` | Chunk-generation/streaming concurrency. `auto` reserves the main thread and uses at most four workers; explicit counts clamp to reported hardware. `0` uses the synchronous main-thread fallback. This does not parallelize rendering. |
121: | `level` | `0`, `34` | Debug: boots straight into a level (34 = the grassland) instead of waiting on a noclip roll. |
122: | `force_anomaly` | `pillars`, `blackout`, `pits`, `archway`, `redroom` | Debug: guarantees one anomaly of that family near spawn, bypassing organic frequency and the spawn keep-out. |
123: | `rt_hiz` | `0`, `1` | CPU hierarchical-Z rejection. |
124: | `rt_f2b` | `0`, `1` | CPU traversal plus splat/raymarch near-to-far chunk selection. Off preserves each strategy's deterministic reference order. |
125: | `rt_skip` | `0`, `1` | Raymarch empty-SVO-leaf skipping; `0` selects finest-cell diagnostic DDA. |
126: | `rt_mips` | `0`, `1` | CPU projected-size MIP/LOD collapse. |
127: | `rt_beam_occlusion` | `0`, `1` | CPU cone-light occlusion rays. |
128: | `rt_deferred` | `0`, `1` | CPU exact fine-depth rejection before hidden-splat shading. Off shades first and depth-tests later; pixels are identical. |
129: | `rt_ao` | `0`, `1` | CPU sibling-count ambient-occlusion approximation. Off selects unit ambient visibility for the reference path. |
130: | `rt_shadows` | `0`, `1` | Direct-light visibility. Surface/Splat use a hero-fixture depth map (128² hard comparison on low, 256² four-tap PCF on high); raymarch traces finite SVO segments to each point-light endpoint and one/four rectangle samples. |
131: | `rt_cells` | `0`, `1` | CPU-side splat cell-range rejection before direct draw submission. |
132: | `rt_budget` | `0`, `1` | Splat far-chunk face budget. |
133: | `rt_cull` | `0`, `1` | CPU and all WebGPU strategies reject chunks beyond the configured range; raster strategies also apply conservative camera visibility. Raymarch filters complete chunk bounds before its resident-set cap. |
134: | `rt_dither` | `0`, `1` | Shared WebGPU output dither. |
135: | `rt_bake` | `0`, `1` | Optional quantized diffuse fill for CPU, surface, and splat; raymarch remains analytic. |
136: 
137: The top-right HUD names the section you are in (level, zone, region), and
138: **F3** (or Settings → Debug) toggles the anomaly debug overlay: reality
139: epochs, resident traversal gates and pit hazards, and streaming counters.
140: 
141: The in-page settings menu (gear icon) also exposes mouse sensitivity, invert
142: Y, render scale, FOV, control scheme, typed CPU quality presets/custom detail,
143: and every renderer optimization switch. CPU quality scalars do not silently
144: change optimization switches: hierarchical Z, MIP collapse, traversal order,
145: chunk culling, hidden-splat rejection, ambient occlusion, and flashlight scene-visibility rays remain independently
146: diagnosable. Older `cpuScale`, `cpuSplatPx`, `cpuRange`, and `cpuShadows` links
147: are still accepted; the formerly ambiguous `cpuSplatPx` is interpreted as a
148: radius.
149: Live preferences are saved to `localStorage`; Apply & Reload writes disabled
150: optimizations into the URL so a regression setup can be shared exactly.
151: 
152: ## GitHub Pages
153: 
154: `.github/workflows/pages.yml` builds `wasm_frontend` in release mode and
155: deploys `static/` on every push to `master` (or via manual dispatch). The
156: main engine (`/`, low- and high-spec profiles) generates chunks entirely in
157: the browser, so it needs nothing but static files and runs unmodified from a
158: Pages project URL (`https://<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) — the worker pool
159: resolves `worker.js` relative to the page, not from the domain root.
160: 
161: The optional `/maze` and `/octree` diagnostics belong to `src/main.rs` and
162: are absent on Pages; the wasm engine needs neither endpoint.
163: 
164: One-time setup: in the repo's Settings → Pages, set Source to "GitHub
165: Actions".
166: 
167: ## Tests
168: 
169: ```sh
170: cargo test --workspace
171: cargo check -p wasm_frontend --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
172: npm run check:wasm
173: 
174: # Linux: deterministic headless GPU contracts through Vulkan/Lavapipe.
175: VK_DRIVER_FILES="$(find /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d -name 'lvp_icd*.json' -print -quit)" \
176:   WGPU_VALIDATION=1 \
177:   cargo test -p wasm_frontend --features vulkan-tests \
178:     --test vulkan_renderers -- --test-threads=1
179: ```
180: 
181: The application layers are browser-free by construction, so player physics,
182: collision, streaming, atlas assembly and input mapping are all covered by
183: native unit tests. The Vulkan suite uses a surface-free render target, forces
184: the Vulkan backend, and fails if no Vulkan adapter is available; CI pins it to
185: Mesa's deterministic Lavapipe software driver and enables Vulkan validation
186: layers. The exact Lavapipe ICD filename varies by distribution; CI discovers
187: it under `/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/` before running the suite.
188: 
189: `npm run build:wasm` also writes a source fingerprint into `static/pkg/`.
190: `npm run check:wasm` verifies that the checked-in wasm-bindgen glue matches
191: the current Rust and worker ABI, catching stale worker-call signatures without
192: bringing a browser automation dependency back into the project.
193: 
194: ## Workspace layout
195: 
196: | Path | What it is |
197: |---|---|
198: | `src/` | `vackrooms` core: entities, use cases, adapters + native dev server |
199: | `wasm_frontend/` | Portable application/adapters/WebGPU pipelines plus the wasm browser shell |
200: | `static/` | Thin HTML shell and wasm bundle output (`pkg/`) |
201: | `wasm_raycaster/` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (reference only) |
202: 
203: ## Modifying the engine
204: 
205: Ports (traits) sit at the boundary of each layer; implement the trait rather
206: than reaching into a concrete type:
207: 
208: - **New procedural level** — implement `LevelGenerator`
209:   (`src/use_cases/level_generator.rs`) alongside `backrooms_level.rs` /
210:   `grassland_level.rs`, register a level id, and give it a native unit test
211:   (generation must be deterministic and seamless at chunk borders — see the
212:   contract documented on the trait).
213: - **New renderer strategy** — add a focused pipeline under
214:   `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/pipelines/`, give it typed configuration
215:   and artifact requirements in `webgpu/config.rs`, then compose it inside the
216:   single `WebGpuRenderer` port adapter. Browser surface ownership stays out of
217:   the pipeline.
218: - **New chunk source** (e.g. a different streaming/caching strategy) —
219:   implement `ChunkSourcePort` (`wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs`); see
220:   `LocalChunkSource` and `WorkerChunkSource` for the synchronous and
221:   worker-pool implementations.
222: - **Player/physics tuning** — `wasm_frontend/src/application/player.rs` and
223:   `engine.rs`; both are plain Rust, unit-tested natively without a browser.
224: 
225: After changing anything under `src/` or `wasm_frontend/src/`, run
226: `cargo test --workspace` (native, browser-free) before rebuilding the wasm
227: bundle with the command in [Build & run](#build--run). See
228: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full layer map and data flow.
````

  21: impl TestNoise {
  22:     fn hash2d(seed: u32, x: i32, y: i32) -> f32 {
  23:         let mut h = seed
  24:             .wrapping_add(x as u32 ^ 0x9E3779B9)
  25:             .wrapping_add(y as u32 ^ 0x85EBCA6B);
  26:         h ^= h >> 16;
  27:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0x85EBCA6B);
  28:         h ^= h >> 13;
  29:         h = h.wrapping_mul(0xC2B2AE35);
  30:         h ^= h >> 16;
  31:         ((h as f32) / (std::u32::MAX as f32)) * 2.0 - 1.0
  32:     }

  35:         a + t * (b - a)
  36:     }

  40:     }

  47:         let y = position.z * freq;

  63:     }

  90: 
  91:     let open: Vec<(usize, usize)> = (margin..w - margin)
  92:         .flat_map(|x| (margin..d - margin).map(move |z| (x, z)))
  93:         .filter(|&(x, z)| is_open(&grid, x, z))
  94:         .collect();
  95:     assert!(
  96:         open.len() > (w - 2 * margin) * (d - 2 * margin) / 2,
  97:         "backrooms must be mostly open space"
  98:     );
  99: 
 100:     // BFS from the first open interior voxel.
 101:     let &(sx, sz) = open.first().expect("some open floor exists");
 102:     let mut visited = vec![false; w * d];
 103:     let mut queue = std::collections::VecDeque::from([(sx, sz)]);
 104:     visited[sx * d + sz] = true;
 105:     let mut reached = 0usize;
 106:     while let Some((x, z)) = queue.pop_front() {
 107:         reached += 1;
 108:         for (dx, dz) in [(1i64, 0i64), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)] {
 109:             let (nx, nz) = (x as i64 + dx, z as i64 + dz);
 110:             if nx < margin as i64
 111:                 || nz < margin as i64
 112:                 || nx >= (w - margin) as i64
 113:                 || nz >= (d - margin) as i64
 114:             {
 115:                 continue;
 116:             }
 117:             let (nx, nz) = (nx as usize, nz as usize);
 118:             if !visited[nx * d + nz] && is_open(&grid, nx, nz) {
 119:                 visited[nx * d + nz] = true;
 120:                 queue.push_back((nx, nz));
 121:             }
 122:         }
 123:     }
 124:     let ratio = reached as f32 / open.len() as f32;
 125:     assert!(
 126:         ratio > 0.95,
 127:         "only {:.0}% of open floor is reachable from spawn",
 128:         ratio * 100.0
 129:     );
 130: }

 132: /// Adjacent chunks must agree at their shared border: the column at
 133: /// world position g is the same whether it came from chunk A's last
 134: /// column or chunk B's first.
 135: #[test]
 136: fn chunks_tile_seamlessly() {
 137:     let noise = TestNoise;
 138:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 139:     let a = generate(0.0, 0.0);
 140:     let b = generate(10.0, 0.0);
 141:     let w = a.width();
 142: 
 143:     let plans =
 144:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 20.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 145:     for z in 0..a.depth() {
 146:         for (grid, lx, gx) in [(&a, w - 1, w - 1), (&b, 0usize, w)] {
 147:             let wx = (gx as f32 + 0.5) * config.voxel_scale;
 148:             let wz = (z as f32 + 0.5) * config.voxel_scale;
 149:             let key = (
 150:                 crate::use_cases::region_plan::region_index(wx),
 151:                 crate::use_cases::region_plan::region_index(wz),
 152:             );
 153:             let plan = plans
 154:                 .iter()
 155:                 .find(|(k, _)| *k == key)
 156:                 .map(|(_, p)| p)
 157:                 .unwrap();
 158:             let expect =
 159:                 BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &LevelTuning::default(), wx, wz);
 160:             let got_solid = grid.get(lx, 1, z) == VOXEL_WALL;
 161:             // Raised floor (stair treads) also writes wall material at
 162:             // the walkable layer, so it counts as expected solid here.
 163:             let expect_solid =
 164:                 expect.solid || (expect.floor_units / config.voxel_scale).round() >= 1.0;
 165:             assert_eq!(
 166:                 got_solid, expect_solid,
 167:                 "column mismatch at world x={gx} z={z}"
 168:             );
 169:         }
 170:     }
 171: }

 173: #[test]
 174: fn recursive_level_zero_is_independent_of_output_partition() {
 175:     use crate::domain::entities::anomaly::{
 176:         AnomalyStateStamp, Axis2, AxisDirection, RedRoomPhase,
 177:     };
 178: 
 179:     // A committed encounter selects a deterministic recursive Level 0
 180:     // address.  The ID is intentionally wider than f32 can represent so
 181:     // this also protects the integer-first branch derivation.
 182:     let reality = RealitySnapshot::new(vec![AnomalyStateStamp::new(
 183:         0xDEAD_BEEF_1234_5678,
 184:         1,
 185:         4.8,
 186:         Axis2::X,
 187:         AxisDirection::Positive,
 188:         RedRoomPhase::Sealed,
 189:         0,
 190:         0xCAFE,
 191:     )]);
 192:     let noise = TestNoise;
 193:     let small_config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 194:     let mut large_config = small_config;
 195:     large_config.chunk_size = 20.0;
 196: 
 197:     let large = BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 198:         Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
 199:         42,
 200:         large_config,
 201:         &noise,
 202:         &reality,
 203:     );
 204:     let chunks = [
 205:         BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 206:             Position::new(0.0, 0.0),
 207:             42,
 208:             small_config,
 209:             &noise,
 210:             &reality,
 211:         ),
 212:         BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 213:             Position::new(10.0, 0.0),
 214:             42,
 215:             small_config,
 216:             &noise,
 217:             &reality,
 218:         ),
 219:         BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 220:             Position::new(0.0, 10.0),
 221:             42,
 222:             small_config,
 223:             &noise,
 224:             &reality,
 225:         ),
 226:         BackroomsLevel.generate_with_reality(
 227:             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 228:             42,
 229:             small_config,
 230:             &noise,
 231:             &reality,
 232:         ),
 233:     ];
 234: 
 235:     let tile = chunks[0].width();
 236:     assert_eq!(large.width(), tile * 2);
 237:     assert_eq!(large.depth(), tile * 2);
 238:     for z in 0..large.depth() {
 239:         for x in 0..large.width() {
 240:             let tile_index = usize::from(x >= tile) + 2 * usize::from(z >= tile);
 241:             let local_x = x % tile;
 242:             let local_z = z % tile;
 243:             for y in 0..large.height() {
 244:                 assert_eq!(
 245:                     large.get(x, y, z),
 246:                     chunks[tile_index].get(local_x, y, local_z),
 247:                     "recursive Level 0 changed at ({x}, {y}, {z}) when the output was tiled"
 248:                 );
 249:             }
 250:         }
 251:     }
 252: }

 254: /// The plan is authoritative: corridor centerlines must be carved open
 255: /// in the voxelized chunks they cross.
 256: #[test]
 257: fn corridors_from_the_plan_are_carved_open() {
 258:     let noise = TestNoise;
 259:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 260:     let plans =
 261:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 80.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 262:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
 263:     let spine = &plan.corridors[0];
 264: 
 265:     let mut checked = 0;
 266:     for seg in spine.path.windows(2) {
 267:         let (p0, p1) = (seg[0], seg[1]);
 268:         let steps = 8;
 269:         for k in 1..steps {
 270:             let t = k as f32 / steps as f32;
 271:             let (wx, wz) = (p0.x + (p1.x - p0.x) * t, p0.z + (p1.z - p0.z) * t);
 272:             // Stay inside region (0,0) and off chunk edges.
 273:             if !(1.0..79.0).contains(&wx) || !(1.0..79.0).contains(&wz) {
 274:                 continue;
 275:             }
 276:             let (cx, cz) = ((wx / 10.0).floor() * 10.0, (wz / 10.0).floor() * 10.0);
 277:             let grid = generate(cx, cz);
 278:             let (lx, lz) = (
 279:                 ((wx - cx) / config.voxel_scale) as usize,
 280:                 ((wz - cz) / config.voxel_scale) as usize,
 281:             );
 282:             assert!(
 283:                 is_open(&grid, lx.min(grid.width() - 1), lz.min(grid.depth() - 1)),
 284:                 "main corridor blocked at world ({wx:.1}, {wz:.1})"
 285:             );
 286:             checked += 1;
 287:         }
 288:     }
 289:     assert!(checked > 5, "spine barely sampled ({checked} points)");
 290: }

 341: /// Assemblies voxelize as walled rooms whose planned entrance is open
 342: /// (with a lintel when the designer's threshold language wants one).
 343: #[test]
 344: fn assemblies_have_walls_and_open_entrances() {
 345:     let noise = TestNoise;
 346:     let mut config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 347:     config.anomalies.frequency = 0.0;
 348:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 349:     let plans =
 350:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 80.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 351:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
 352:     assert!(!plan.assemblies.is_empty());
 353: 
 354:     for a in &plan.assemblies {
 355:         let e = &a.entrances[0];
 356:         // The entrance column itself: open (possibly under a lintel).
 357:         let door =
 358:             BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, e.center.x, e.center.z);
 359:         assert!(!door.solid, "assembly {} door is walled shut", a.id);
 360:         // Somewhere along the same front wall, clear of the door span,
 361:         // there must be solid wall. Probe the middle of the wall band
 362:         // (the entrance center sits exactly on the footprint boundary,
 363:         // where containment is ambiguous).
 364:         let b = a.footprint.bounds();
 365:         let band = |c: f32, lo: f32, hi: f32| {
 366:             if (c - lo).abs() < (c - hi).abs() {
 367:                 lo - PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 368:             } else {
 369:                 hi + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5
 370:             }
 371:         };
 372:         let (lo, hi, door_along) = if e.through_x_wall {
 373:             (b.0, b.2, e.center.x)
 374:         } else {
 375:             (b.1, b.3, e.center.z)
 376:         };
 377:         let mut solid_found = false;
 378:         let mut along = lo + 0.3;
 379:         while along < hi - 0.2 {
 380:             if (along - door_along).abs() > e.width * 0.5 + 0.4 {
 381:                 let (wx, wz) = if e.through_x_wall {
 382:                     (along, band(e.center.z, b.1, b.3))
 383:                 } else {
 384:                     (band(e.center.x, b.0, b.2), along)
 385:                 };
 386:                 if BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz).solid {
 387:                     solid_found = true;
 388:                     break;
 389:                 }
 390:             }
 391:             along += 0.2;
 392:         }
 393:         assert!(
 394:             solid_found,
 395:             "assembly {} has no solid front wall anywhere",
 396:             a.id
 397:         );
 398:     }
 399: }

 401: /// An abandoned expansion is a dark shell: it keeps its walls but none of
 402: /// its fixtures are lit.
 403: #[test]
 404: fn abandoned_expansions_are_unlit() {
 405:     let noise = TestNoise;
 406:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 407:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 408:     let mut found = false;
 409:     for rx in -3i64..3 {
 410:         for rz in -3i64..3 {
 411:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 412:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * 80.0, rz as f32 * 80.0),
 413:                 1.0,
 414:                 42,
 415:                 &config,
 416:                 &noise,
 417:             );
 418:             let plan = &plans[0].1;
 419:             for a in &plan.assemblies {
 420:                 if !a.corruption.abandoned {
 421:                     continue;
 422:                 }
 423:                 found = true;
 424:                 let (x0, z0, x1, z1) = a.footprint.bounds();
 425:                 // No interior column may carry a lit fixture.
 426:                 let mut probe_z = z0 + 0.6;
 427:                 while probe_z < z1 - 0.4 {
 428:                     let mut probe_x = x0 + 0.6;
 429:                     while probe_x < x1 - 0.4 {
 430:                         // A corridor clipping the footprint may still run
 431:                         // its own lit strip through the shell — that is
 432:                         // canon ("unreachable but still lit"). Only the
 433:                         // room's fixtures must be dark.
 434:                         let in_corridor = plan
 435:                             .corridors
 436:                             .iter()
 437:                             .any(|s| s.distance(probe_x, probe_z) <= s.width * 0.5);
 438:                         if !in_corridor {
 439:                             let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(
 440:                                 plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, probe_x, probe_z,
 441:                             );
 442:                             assert!(!c.light, "abandoned assembly {} is lit", a.id);
 443:                         }
 444:                         probe_x += 0.8;
 445:                     }
 446:                     probe_z += 0.8;
 447:                 }
 448:             }
 449:         }
 450:     }
 451:     assert!(found, "no abandoned expansion within 36 regions");
 452: }

 454: /// A planned stairwell samples through the full column pipeline as a
 455: /// walkable flight: flat at the door, rising monotonically along the
 456: /// walk axis, reaching its landing with headroom intact.
 457: #[test]
 458: fn stairwells_sample_as_rising_flights() {
 459:     use crate::use_cases::vertical_circulation::link_wants_geometry;
 460:     use crate::use_cases::world_topology::vertical_link_for_region;
 461:     let noise = TestNoise;
 462:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 463:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 464: 
 465:     let mut checked = 0usize;
 466:     for rz in -8i64..=8 {
 467:         for rx in -8i64..=8 {
 468:             let Some(link) = vertical_link_for_region(42, &noise, rx, rz) else {
 469:                 continue;
 470:             };
 471:             if !link_wants_geometry(&link) {
 472:                 continue;
 473:             }
 474:             let plans = BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(
 475:                 Position::new(rx as f32 * REGION_SIZE, rz as f32 * REGION_SIZE),
 476:                 1.0,
 477:                 42,
 478:                 &config,
 479:                 &noise,
 480:             );
 481:             let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (rx, rz)).unwrap().1;
 482:             let Some(stair) = plan
 483:                 .assemblies
 484:                 .iter()
 485:                 .find(|a| a.program == SpaceProgram::Stair)
 486:             else {
 487:                 continue;
 488:             };
 489:             let door = stair.entrances[0].center;
 490:             let b = stair.footprint.bounds();
 491:             let inward = if (door.z - b.1).abs() < (door.z - b.3).abs() {
 492:                 1.0
 493:             } else {
 494:                 -1.0
 495:             };
 496: 
 497:             let at_door =
 498:                 BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, door.x, door.z);
 499:             assert!(!at_door.solid, "stair door is walled shut");
 500:             assert_eq!(at_door.floor_units, 0.0, "stair door is not flat");
 501: 
 502:             let mut previous = 0.0f32;
 503:             let mut peak = 0.0f32;
 504:             let mut depth = 0.7;
 505:             while depth < (b.3 - b.1) - 0.6 {
 506:                 let wz = door.z + inward * depth;
 507:                 let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, door.x, wz);
 508:                 if !c.solid {
 509:                     assert!(
 510:                         c.floor_units >= previous - 1e-6,
 511:                         "flight descends inside stair at region ({rx},{rz})"
 512:                     );
 513:                     assert!(
 514:                         c.ceiling_units - c.floor_units >= 2.2 - 1e-6,
 515:                         "flight headroom pinched at region ({rx},{rz})"
 516:                     );
 517:                     previous = c.floor_units;
 518:                     peak = peak.max(c.floor_units);
 519:                 }
 520:                 depth += 0.2;
 521:             }
 522:             assert!(
 523:                 peak >= 1.6 - 1e-6,
 524:                 "flight in ({rx},{rz}) peaked at {peak} u"
 525:             );
 526:             checked += 1;
 527:         }
 528:     }
 529:     assert!(checked >= 3, "only {checked} stairwells sampled");
 530: }

 532: /// The baseline is broad regular dropped ceiling, with enough expansive
 533: /// and vaulted territory to prevent Level 0 from reading as a low maze.
 534: #[test]
 535: fn ceilings_are_vast_and_varied() {
 536:     let noise = TestNoise;
 537:     let mut counts = [0usize; 4];
 538:     let mut lowest = f32::MAX;
 539:     let mut tallest = 0.0f32;
 540:     for z in (-600..=600).step_by(8) {
 541:         for x in (-600..=600).step_by(8) {
 542:             let (wx, wz) = (x as f32 + 0.5, z as f32 + 0.5);
 543:             let band = BackroomsLevel::fabric_ceiling_band(&noise, 42, wx, wz);
 544:             let ceiling = BackroomsLevel::fabric_ceiling_height(&noise, 42, wx, wz, band);
 545:             let index = match band {
 546:                 FabricCeilingBand::Compression => 0,
 547:                 FabricCeilingBand::Regular => 1,
 548:                 FabricCeilingBand::Expanse => 2,
 549:                 FabricCeilingBand::Vault => 3,
 550:             };
 551:             counts[index] += 1;
 552:             lowest = lowest.min(ceiling);
 553:             tallest = tallest.max(ceiling);
 554:         }
 555:     }
 556:     let total = counts.iter().sum::<usize>() as f32;
 557:     let ratio = |index| counts[index] as f32 / total;
 558:     // The labyrinth fabric is the default; open volumes punctuate it.
 559:     assert!(
 560:         (0.60..=0.85).contains(&ratio(1)),
 561:         "ceiling territories: compression {:.1}%, regular {:.1}%, expanse {:.1}%, vault {:.1}%",
 562:         ratio(0) * 100.0,
 563:         ratio(1) * 100.0,
 564:         ratio(2) * 100.0,
 565:         ratio(3) * 100.0
 566:     );
 567:     assert!(
 568:         (0.10..=0.28).contains(&ratio(2)),
 569:         "open expanse territory was {:.1}%",
 570:         ratio(2) * 100.0
 571:     );
 572:     assert!(
 573:         (0.03..=0.15).contains(&ratio(3)),
 574:         "vault territory was {:.1}%",
 575:         ratio(3) * 100.0
 576:     );
 577:     assert!(
 578:         (0.01..=0.10).contains(&ratio(0)),
 579:         "compression territory was {:.1}%",
 580:         ratio(0) * 100.0
 581:     );
 582:     assert!(
 583:         lowest <= 2.8 && tallest >= 4.5,
 584:         "ceiling range was only {lowest:.1}--{tallest:.1} u"
 585:     );
 586: }

 627: /// The generation knobs actually steer the output: zeroing pillars and
 628: /// walls empties the world of solids; cranking them fills it back up.
 629: #[test]
 630: fn tuning_knobs_control_density() {
 631:     let noise = TestNoise;
 632:     // Aggregate over chunks in different fabric regimes (walled rooms
 633:     // and open expanses) so both knobs have something to steer.
 634:     let count_solids = |tuning: LevelTuning| -> usize {
 635:         let mut n = 0;
 636:         for (ox, oz) in [(10.0, 10.0), (30.0, 10.0), (50.0, 30.0), (10.0, 50.0)] {
 637:             let grid = BackroomsLevel.generate(
 638:                 Position::new(ox, oz),
 639:                 42,
 640:                 GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_tuning(tuning),
 641:                 &noise,
 642:             );
 643:             for z in 0..grid.depth() {
 644:                 for x in 0..grid.width() {
 645:                     if grid.get(x, 1, z) != VOXEL_AIR {
 646:                         n += 1;
 647:                     }
 648:                 }
 649:             }
 650:         }
 651:         n
 652:     };
 653: 
 654:     // Provisions (bottles, doors) are content, not architecture: zero them
 655:     // so the knob comparison sees only pillar/wall mass.
 656:     let no_provisions = LevelTuning {
 657:         almond_water: 0.0,
 658:         rations: 0.0,
 659:         level_doors: 0.0,
 660:         ..Default::default()
 661:     };
 662:     let none = count_solids(LevelTuning {
 663:         pillars: 0.0,
 664:         walls: 0.0,
 665:         ..no_provisions
 666:     });
 667:     let sparse = count_solids(LevelTuning {
 668:         pillars: 0.3,
 669:         walls: 0.3,
 670:         ..no_provisions
 671:     });
 672:     let default = count_solids(no_provisions);
 673:     let dense = count_solids(LevelTuning {
 674:         pillars: 2.0,
 675:         walls: 2.0,
 676:         ..no_provisions
 677:     });
 678: 
 679:     assert_eq!(none, 0, "pillars=0 walls=0 must produce an empty plane");
 680:     assert!(
 681:         sparse < default,
 682:         "sparse ({sparse}) must be < default ({default})"
 683:     );
 684:     assert!(
 685:         default < dense,
 686:         "default ({default}) must be < dense ({dense})"
 687:     );
 688: }

 717: /// Every LOD of a chunk must voxelize the same plan: coarse walls stay
 718: /// within one fine voxel of fine walls (the streaming engine swaps LODs
 719: /// of a chunk in place, so they must be faithful proxies).
 720: #[test]
 721: fn lods_of_the_same_chunk_correspond() {
 722:     let noise = TestNoise;
 723:     let fine = BackroomsLevel.generate(
 724:         Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 725:         42,
 726:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
 727:         &noise,
 728:     );
 729:     let coarse = BackroomsLevel.generate(
 730:         Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
 731:         42,
 732:         GeneratorConfig::low_spec().at_lod(1),
 733:         &noise,
 734:     );
 735:     // Ordinary fabric walls now voxelize as either the fresh or the aged
 736:     // wallpaper material depending on `institution_age`, both equally solid.
 737:     let solid = |g: &VoxelGrid, x: usize, z: usize| {
 738:         matches!(g.get(x, 1, z), VOXEL_WALL | VOXEL_AGED_WALLPAPER)
 739:     };
 740:     let (mut matches, mut total) = (0usize, 0usize);
 741:     for z in 0..coarse.depth() {
 742:         for x in 0..coarse.width() {
 743:             if !solid(&coarse, x, z) {
 744:                 continue;
 745:             }
 746:             total += 1;
 747:             let mut near = false;
 748:             for dz in -1i32..=2 {
 749:                 for dx in -1i32..=2 {
 750:                     let (fx, fz) = (x as i32 * 2 + dx, z as i32 * 2 + dz);
 751:                     if fx >= 0
 752:                         && fz >= 0
 753:                         && (fx as usize) < fine.width()
 754:                         && (fz as usize) < fine.depth()
 755:                         && solid(&fine, fx as usize, fz as usize)
 756:                     {
 757:                         near = true;
 758:                     }
 759:                 }
 760:             }
 761:             if near {
 762:                 matches += 1;
 763:             }
 764:         }
 765:     }
 766:     assert!(total > 0, "coarse chunk has no walls at all");
 767:     assert!(
 768:         matches * 10 >= total * 9,
 769:         "coarse walls stray from fine walls: {matches}/{total}"
 770:     );
 771: }

 773: /// The player spawns *on the main corridor*: open floor along the
 774: /// centerline, a lit fixture within a light-strip period, and — for the
 775: /// readable opening sequence — solid edge walls on both sides.
 776: #[test]
 777: fn spawn_is_a_readable_walled_corridor() {
 778:     let noise = TestNoise;
 779:     let config = GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 780:     let tuning = LevelTuning::default();
 781:     let sp = crate::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(42);
 782: 
 783:     let plans =
 784:         BackroomsLevel::region_plans_for(Position::new(0.0, 0.0), 80.0, 42, &config, &noise);
 785:     let plan = &plans.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == (0, 0)).unwrap().1;
 786:     let spine = &plan.corridors[0];
 787:     assert!(
 788:         spine.distance(sp.x, sp.z) < 0.3,
 789:         "spawn ({}, {}) is not on the main corridor centerline",
 790:         sp.x,
 791:         sp.z
 792:     );
 793: 
 794:     // The corridor around spawn is open along the centerline, lit, and
 795:     // predominantly walled on both sides. Framed entrances and branch
 796:     // tees may pierce the run, but the edge must *read* as a wall — no
 797:     // dissolution into open fabric inside the readable radius.
 798:     let half = spine.width * 0.5;
 799:     let mut lit = false;
 800:     let mut solid_edges = [0usize; 2];
 801:     const STEPS: usize = 16;
 802:     for step in 0..STEPS {
 803:         let wx = sp.x + step as f32;
 804:         let c = BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, sp.z);
 805:         assert!(!c.solid, "main corridor blocked at ({wx}, {})", sp.z);
 806:         lit |= c.light;
 807:         for (i, side) in [-1.0, 1.0f32].iter().enumerate() {
 808:             let wz = sp.z + side * (half + PLAN_WALL_T * 0.5);
 809:             if BackroomsLevel::plan_column(plan, &noise, 42, &tuning, wx, wz).solid {
 810:                 solid_edges[i] += 1;
 811:             }
 812:         }
 813:     }
 814:     assert!(lit, "no lit fixture along the first {STEPS} u of corridor");
 815:     for (i, solid) in solid_edges.iter().enumerate() {
 816:         assert!(
 817:             solid * 10 >= STEPS * 6,
 818:             "start corridor side {i} is mostly open ({solid}/{STEPS}): \
 819:              the opening sequence must read as a walled corridor"
 820:         );
 821:     }
 822: }
