300: /// A camera-facing label floating over a supply pickup. The atlas row
301: /// selects which product logo the quad shows.
302: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
303: pub struct SupplySprite {
304:     /// World-space center of the label quad.
305:     pub position: [f32; 3],
306:     /// Atlas row: 0 = almond water, 1 = rations.
307:     pub atlas_row: u8,
308: }
309: 
310: /// Most label sprites a single frame will draw.
311: pub const MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES: usize = 16;
312: 
313: /// Camera state for one frame, in world space.
314: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
315: pub struct FrameParams {
316:     pub camera_pos: [f32; 3],
317:     pub yaw: f32,
318:     pub pitch: f32,
319:     pub flashlight: bool,
320:     /// Nearest active flares, distance-culled; only the first
321:     /// `dynamic_light_count` entries are meaningful.
322:     pub dynamic_lights: [DynamicLight; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
323:     pub dynamic_light_count: u8,
324:     /// Every finite, enabled, deduplicated world fixture. Correctness-first
325:     /// renderers must not discard a light merely because it is far from the
326:     /// camera: it can still be local to a visible distant receiver.
327:     pub scene_lights: Vec<LightSource>,
328:     /// Level atmosphere (sky, fog, ambient scale).
329:     pub environment: Environment,
330:     /// Nearby supply labels, nearest first, at most [`MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES`].
331:     pub supply_sprites: Vec<SupplySprite>,
332: }
333: 
334: impl FrameParams {
335:     pub fn active_dynamic_lights(&self) -> &[DynamicLight] {
336:         let count = (self.dynamic_light_count as usize).min(self.dynamic_lights.len());
337:         &self.dynamic_lights[..count]
338:     }
339: 
340:     pub fn active_scene_lights(&self) -> &[LightSource] {
341:         &self.scene_lights
342:     }
343: }
344: 
345: impl Default for FrameParams {
346:     fn default() -> Self {
347:         Self {
348:             camera_pos: [0.0; 3],
349:             yaw: 0.0,
350:             pitch: 0.0,
351:             flashlight: false,
352:             dynamic_lights: [DynamicLight::default(); MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
353:             dynamic_light_count: 0,
354:             scene_lights: Vec::new(),
355:             environment: Environment::default(),
356:             supply_sprites: Vec::new(),
357:         }
358:     }
359: }
360: 
361: /// Renderer-selected chunk artifacts, encoded as a stable compact bitfield.
362: ///
363: /// Collision and semantic data are application requirements and are always
364: /// generated. These bits describe only optional presentation products, so a
365: /// raymarcher never pays to build greedy faces and a rasterizer never pays to
366: /// serialize GPU SVO nodes.
367: #[repr(transparent)]
368: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
369: pub struct RenderArtifactNeeds(u8);
370: 
371: impl RenderArtifactNeeds {
372:     const INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT: u8 = 1 << 0;
373:     const FACE_SPLATS_BIT: u8 = 1 << 1;
374:     const SVO_NODES_BIT: u8 = 1 << 2;
375:     const KNOWN_BITS: u8 =
376:         Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT | Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT | Self::SVO_NODES_BIT;
377: 
378:     pub const NONE: Self = Self(0);
379:     pub const SURFACE: Self = Self(Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT);
380:     pub const SPLAT: Self = Self(Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT);
381:     pub const RAYMARCH: Self = Self(Self::SVO_NODES_BIT);
382:     pub const CPU: Self = Self(Self::SVO_NODES_BIT);
383:     pub const ALL: Self = Self(Self::KNOWN_BITS);
384: 
385:     pub const fn from_bits(bits: u8) -> Option<Self> {
386:         if bits & !Self::KNOWN_BITS == 0 {
387:             Some(Self(bits))
388:         } else {
389:             None
390:         }
391:     }
392: 
393:     pub const fn bits(self) -> u8 {
394:         self.0
395:     }
396: 
397:     pub const fn indexed_surface_mesh(self) -> bool {
398:         self.0 & Self::INDEXED_SURFACE_MESH_BIT != 0
399:     }
400: 
401:     pub const fn face_splats(self) -> bool {
402:         self.0 & Self::FACE_SPLATS_BIT != 0
403:     }
404: 
405:     pub const fn svo_nodes(self) -> bool {
406:         self.0 & Self::SVO_NODES_BIT != 0
407:     }
408: 
409:     pub const fn union(self, other: Self) -> Self {
410:         Self(self.0 | other.0)
411:     }
412: 
413:     pub const fn needs_surface_extraction(self) -> bool {
414:         self.indexed_surface_mesh() || self.face_splats()
415:     }
416: }
417: 
418: /// Abstraction over the actual renderer back end.
419: /// Implemented by `drivers::webgpu::renderer::WebGpuRenderer` in the browser
420: /// and by recording test doubles in native unit tests.
421: pub trait RendererPort {
422:     /// Optional presentation products consumed by this renderer. The default
423:     /// preserves older test doubles while concrete renderers report the exact
424:     /// representation they own.
425:     fn artifact_needs(&self) -> RenderArtifactNeeds {
426:         if self.uses_surface_meshes() {
427:             RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE
428:         } else {
429:             RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH
430:         }
431:     }
432: 
433:     /// Compatibility query for older callers and test doubles. New code uses
434:     /// [`Self::artifact_needs`]; true means some surface-derived representation
435:     /// is required, not necessarily an indexed mesh.
436:     fn uses_surface_meshes(&self) -> bool {
437:         false
438:     }
439: 
440:     /// Incrementally uploads newly loaded or refined chunk meshes.
441:     fn upload_surfaces(&mut self, _chunks: &[SurfaceChunk<'_>]) {}
442: 
443:     /// Releases meshes for chunks that left the streaming footprint.
444:     fn remove_surfaces(&mut self, _keys: &[SurfaceChunkKey]) {}
445: 
446:     /// Drops all resident meshes (used when noclipping to another level).
447:     fn clear_surfaces(&mut self) {}
448: 
449:     /// Telemetry data from the CPU reference strategy, if applicable.
450:     fn cpu_telemetry_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
451:         None
452:     }
453: 
454:     /// Uploads the merged SVO node atlas (four `u32` words per node, padded
455:     /// in 1024-node rows; see `OctreeGpuSerializer` in the core).
456:     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]);
457: 
458:     /// Overwrites whole atlas rows starting at `first_row` (1024 nodes per
459:     /// row) without reallocating or re-uploading the rest of the atlas.
460:     /// Returns `false` if the back end can't do partial updates (or has no
461:     /// atlas yet), in which case the caller must fall back to `upload_atlas`.
462:     fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, _first_row: u32, _texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
463:         false
464:     }
465: 
466:     /// Receives the decoded RGBA label atlas (stacked product logos). Ships
467:     /// once at boot; renderers without a sprite path simply ignore it.
468:     fn upload_label_atlas(&mut self, _rgba: &[u8], _width: u32, _height: u32) {}
469: 
470:     /// Draws one frame: fullscreen raymarch of every chunk in `chunks`.
471:     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]);
472: }
473: 
474: /// A fully prepared chunk as the application consumes it.
475: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
476: pub struct ChunkPayload {
477:     /// Root node index local to this chunk's `nodes` array.
478:     pub root: u32,
479:     /// GPU-serialized SVO nodes (row-padded, 4 u32 per node).
480:     pub nodes: Vec<u32>,
481:     /// Side length of the SVO cube in world units.
482:     pub world_size: f32,
483:     /// Exact leaf size/depth used to build `nodes`.
484:     pub voxel_size: f32,
485:     pub svo_depth: u8,
486:     /// Renderer-selected raster artifacts. Unrequested representations are
487:     /// empty while bounds/LOD metadata stays valid for the selected path.
488:     pub surface: SurfaceMeshPayload,
489:     /// Renderer-neutral analytic emitters used by rendering and thermal
490:     /// simulation even when no surface artifact was requested.
491:     pub lights: Vec<LightSource>,
492:     /// Solid-voxel bounding boxes in world space, for player collision.
493:     pub collision: Vec<Aabb>,
494:     /// Semantic threshold planes derived by the same generation snapshot as
495:     /// the voxel grid. The engine folds crossings into the next reality.
496:     pub traversal_gates: Vec<TraversalGate>,
497:     /// Authored floor openings with deterministic recovery destinations.
498:     pub pit_hazards: Vec<PitHazard>,
499:     /// Consumable pickups exported beside the geometry.
500:     pub supply_items: Vec<SupplyItem>,
501:     /// Physical doorways to other Backrooms levels.
502:     pub level_exits: Vec<LevelExit>,
503: }
504: 
505: /// One background chunk-load order, echoed back verbatim with its result so
506: /// the engine can reject stale work (wrong level, chunk no longer desired,
507: /// or already refined past this LOD).
508: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
509: pub struct ChunkRequest {
510:     /// Monotonic identity assigned by the engine. A completion may only
511:     /// clear the pending entry carrying this exact id; this prevents a late
512:     /// result from an evicted/re-requested chunk from cancelling newer work.
513:     pub request_id: u32,
514:     pub origin_x: f32,
515:     pub origin_z: f32,
516:     pub level: u32,
517:     pub lod: u8,
518:     /// Compact renderer-owned presentation request, echoed by workers as part
519:     /// of exact asynchronous request identity.
520:     pub artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
521:     /// Immutable encounter state used to generate this chunk. It is part of
522:     /// request identity, not ambient worker state.
523:     pub reality: RealitySnapshot,
524: }
525: 
526: impl ChunkRequest {
527:     /// Exact identity check for asynchronous completion validation. Origins
528:     /// compare by bits so this remains an identity operation rather than an
529:     /// approximate spatial comparison.
530:     pub fn is_same_request(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
531:         self.request_id == other.request_id
532:             && self.origin_x.to_bits() == other.origin_x.to_bits()
533:             && self.origin_z.to_bits() == other.origin_z.to_bits()
534:             && self.level == other.level
535:             && self.lod == other.lod
536:             && self.artifacts == other.artifacts
537:             && self.reality == other.reality
538:     }
539: }
540: 
541: /// A finished background load.
542: #[derive(Debug)]
543: pub struct CompletedChunk {
544:     pub request: ChunkRequest,
545:     pub payload: ChunkPayload,
546: }
547: 
548: /// Abstraction over where chunks come from. The browser build implements
549: /// this with in-wasm procedural generation (`adapters::local_chunk_source`)
550: /// or a Web Worker pool (`drivers::worker_source`); a networked build could
551: /// implement it with HTTP fetches instead.
552: pub trait ChunkSourcePort {
553:     /// Loads the chunk at `origin` for the given Backrooms level
554:     /// (0 = backrooms, 34 = grassland; see the core's `level_generator`).
555:     ///
556:     /// `lod` selects the level of detail: 0 is full resolution and each
557:     /// step doubles the voxel size, costing ~1/8 as much to produce. Any
558:     /// LOD of a chunk covers the same world cube (`world_size` invariant),
559:     /// so payloads are interchangeable to the renderer.
560:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32, lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload;
561: 
562:     /// Loads against an explicit immutable reality snapshot. Stateless
563:     /// sources retain source compatibility through the default implementation;
564:     /// procedural sources override this and route the snapshot into generation.
565:     fn load_with_reality(
566:         &self,
567:         origin_x: f32,
568:         origin_z: f32,
569:         level: u32,
570:         lod: u8,
571:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
572:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
573:         let _ = reality;
574:         self.load(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod)
575:     }
576: 
577:     /// Loads against an explicit reality while requesting only the optional
578:     /// presentation products consumed by the active renderer. Sources that
579:     /// do not specialize artifact production remain compatible by generating
580:     /// their ordinary complete payload.
581:     fn load_with_artifacts(
582:         &self,
583:         origin_x: f32,
584:         origin_z: f32,
585:         level: u32,
586:         lod: u8,
587:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
588:         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
589:     ) -> ChunkPayload {
590:         let _ = artifacts;
591:         self.load_with_reality(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality)
592:     }
593: 
594:     /// True when the source generates in the background. The engine then
595:     /// drives it with [`Self::request`]/[`Self::poll_completed`] instead of
596:     /// the blocking [`Self::load`], keeping the frame loop responsive.
597:     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
598:         false
599:     }
600: 
601:     /// Queues a background load. Deduplication is the caller's concern.
602:     fn request(&mut self, _request: ChunkRequest) {}
603: 
604:     /// Takes every finished background load. Results may arrive in any
605:     /// order and may be stale; the caller validates against its own state.
606:     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
607:         Vec::new()
608:     }
609: 
610:     /// Takes requests which the asynchronous transport definitively could
611:     /// not complete. The engine validates the full request identity before
612:     /// clearing pending state, then issues a fresh request on the same tick.
613:     /// Synchronous sources and infallible test doubles need not override it.
614:     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
615:         Vec::new()
616:     }
617: }
618: 
619: #[cfg(test)]
620: mod artifact_tests {
621:     use super::RenderArtifactNeeds;
622: 
623:     #[test]
624:     fn artifact_bitfield_round_trips_every_valid_combination() {
625:         for bits in 0..=RenderArtifactNeeds::ALL.bits() {
626:             let needs = RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(bits).expect("known bit combination");
627:             assert_eq!(needs.bits(), bits);
628:             assert_eq!(needs.indexed_surface_mesh(), bits & 1 != 0);
629:             assert_eq!(needs.face_splats(), bits & 2 != 0);
630:             assert_eq!(needs.svo_nodes(), bits & 4 != 0);
631:         }
632:         assert_eq!(RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(1 << 7), None);
633:     }
634: 
635:     #[test]
636:     fn renderer_artifact_sets_are_minimal_and_composable() {
637:         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.indexed_surface_mesh());
638:         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.face_splats());
639:         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE.svo_nodes());
640: 
641:         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.indexed_surface_mesh());
642:         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.face_splats());
643:         assert!(!RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT.svo_nodes());
644: 
645:         assert_eq!(RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH, RenderArtifactNeeds::CPU);
646:         assert!(RenderArtifactNeeds::CPU.svo_nodes());
647:         assert_eq!(
648:             RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE
649:                 .union(RenderArtifactNeeds::SPLAT)
650:                 .union(RenderArtifactNeeds::RAYMARCH),
651:             RenderArtifactNeeds::ALL,
652:         );
653:     }
654: }
````

## File: ARCHITECTURE.md
````markdown
  1: # Vackrooms — Architecture
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only rendering engine built on **Clean Architecture**, targeting
  4: low-spec hardware. The whole engine — procedural generation, lighting, sparse
  5: voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk streaming, player physics, and
  6: rendering — compiles to a single WebAssembly module. The browser
  7: runs it; a zero-dependency native HTTP server merely serves the files (or, on
  8: GitHub Pages, static files alone — the wasm engine generates chunks entirely
  9: client-side and needs no server).
 10: 
 11: ## Rendering family
 12: 
 13: The engine targets **WebGL2** as its primary production rendering API, prioritizing reliable hardware compatibility, static probe volume lighting, and selective dynamic shadows.
 14: 
 15: | Strategy | Role & Purpose | Target Profile |
 16: |---|---|---|
 17: | `surface` *(default)* | **Primary High-Quality Renderer** | Packed greedy meshes, per-chunk analytic light ranges, hero-light PCF shadows, dynamic dithered fog, and 3D probe volume sampling (`L_baked`). |
 18: | `splat` | **Low-Spec / Dense Geometry** | Instanced face splats with quad expansion; preserves flat retro voxel aesthetic and reads shared 3D probe volume. |
 19: | `raymarch` | **Diagnostic & Reference** | Fullscreen SVO raymarcher for volumetric inspection, special effects, and reference comparison. |
 20: | `cpu` | **Deterministic Fallback** | Software SVO rasterizer fallback for low-spec environments without rich global illumination. |
 21: 
 22: Initialization failures are reported to the loading HUD gracefully without silent algorithm fallback.
 23: 
 24: ### Renderer module boundaries
 25: 
 26: | Module | Responsibility |
 27: |---|---|
 28: | `drivers/browser.rs` | async composition root, HUD/settings projection, and rAF orchestration |
 29: | `drivers/browser/input_bindings.rs` | DOM listener lifetimes and translation into the platform-free input adapter |
 30: | `drivers/webgpu/browser_context.rs` | browser adapter/device/surface acquisition and resize/present lifecycle |
 31: | `drivers/webgpu/renderer.rs` | `RendererPort` adapter and strategy composition |
 32: | `drivers/webgpu/config.rs` | target-independent renderer kinds, quality profiles, budgets, optimization switches, and artifact requirements |
 33: | `drivers/webgpu/frame_resources.rs` | shared frame uniforms and light storage |
 34: | `drivers/webgpu/gpu_types.rs` | explicit, aligned CPU-to-WGSL records |
 35: | `drivers/webgpu/pipelines/` | one focused cache/pass implementation per strategy plus shared visibility and `raster_shadow` resource/math contracts |
 36: | `drivers/webgpu/shaders/` | small WGSL programs selected by `shader.rs` |
 37: | `adapters/cpu_splatter/` | browser-free reference rasterizer, traversal, shading, and typed CPU settings |
 38: 
 39: This split keeps DOM lifetime, GPU resource lifetime, pass encoding, and
 40: renderer policy out of a single god object. Adding a strategy means adding a
 41: pipeline and typed profile, then composing it behind the existing port.
 42: 
 43: ### Work ownership
 44: 
 45: Procedural generation is CPU-authoritative. World graphs, reality snapshots,
 46: seeded noise, lighting, collision, and SVO construction must not vary with GPU
 47: model, driver, or scheduling order. Workers may parallelize independent chunk
 48: requests, but the same request always produces the same artifact bytes.
 49: 
 50: The GPU owns renderer-derived work that cannot change world semantics:
 51: 
 52: - surface vertices are decoded by vertex pulling, avoiding an expanded CPU
 53:   vertex copy;
 54: - splat faces become quad corners in the vertex shader, avoiding CPU-generated
 55:   presentation vertices;
 56: - the raster hero shadow reuses Surface indices or expands the Splat face
 57:   buffer directly, so visibility does not broaden either artifact request;
 58: - each compact supply-label point becomes a six-vertex, camera-facing
 59:   billboard in WGSL and shares the raster strategies' depth target;
 60: - raymarch fragments traverse the compressed SVO directly, avoiding a dense
 61:   persistent voxel field;
 62: - the CPU reference path still uses the same WebGPU presentation lifecycle.
 63: 
 64: `BuildOctreeUseCase` also prunes any recursive cube whose minimum is already
 65: outside a source-grid dimension. Such cubes can only collapse to the canonical
 66: air leaf, so this skips work without changing arena indices or serialized
 67: bytes. A non-power-of-two fixture compares the exact pruned and exhaustive
 68: node arenas and every addressable lookup.
 69: 
 70: ### Configurable optimizations
 71: 
 72: `RendererProfile` separates bounded low/high quality budgets from
 73: `RenderToggles`. The browser snapshots toggles once per frame; inner passes do
 74: not read DOM globals. Each strategy consumes only switches it implements:
 75: 
 76: | Strategy | Explicit work controls |
 77: |---|---|
 78: | surface | chunk-sphere rejection, optional baked diffuse fill, profile-sized hero shadow map (128²/256² with one/four taps), and adaptive backing resolution |
 79: | splat | chunk/cell rejection, near-to-far submission, optional baked diffuse fill, far-face budget, and the same profile-sized hero map using face-expanded casters |
 80: | raymarch | stable versus near-to-far chunk selection, complete-AABB distance rejection before the resident cap, reference traversal versus empty-leaf skipping, one/four-sample finite-SVO direct-light visibility, maximum trace steps, and resident-chunk budget |
 81: | CPU | hierarchical Z, near-to-far order, projected-size MIPs, deferred hidden-splat shading, ambient occlusion, range, and hard work caps |
 82: 
 83: Compact storage records, GPU vertex pulling/face expansion, fixed-function
 84: depth, and the fullscreen-triangle passes are architectural choices rather
 85: than hidden toggles. Output dithering remains configurable. GPU timestamp
 86: collection is not implemented and is therefore not advertised as a switch.
 87: 
 88: ## The dependency rule
 89: 
 90: Source dependencies point inward only. No inner layer names a browser, GPU,
 91: socket, or clock.
 92: 
 93: ```
 94: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 95: │ FRAMEWORKS & DRIVERS                                               │
 96: │   wasm_frontend/drivers   WebGPU, DOM events, rAF, HUD, console    │
 97: │   src/main.rs             native HTTP server (std::net only)      │
 98: │   src/frameworks_drivers  SimpleNoiseProvider, StdTelemetry        │
 99: │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
100: │  │ INTERFACE ADAPTERS                                           │  │
101: │  │   src/adapters            OctreeGpuSerializer, VoxelMapper,  │  │
102: │  │                           JsonPresenter                      │  │
103: │  │   src/interface_adapters  WebRendererAdapter (presenters)    │  │
104: │  │   wasm_frontend/adapters  InputCollector, LocalChunkSource   │  │
105: │  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
106: │  │  │ USE CASES (application business rules)                 │  │  │
107: │  │  │   src/use_cases           GenerateChunk + ports        │  │  │
108: │  │  │   src/domain/use_cases    BuildOctree, lighting, maze  │  │  │
109: │  │  │   wasm_frontend/application  Engine (frame loop),      │  │  │
110: │  │  │      Player, CollisionWorld, StreamingPolicy, atlas    │  │  │
111: │  │  │      + ports (RendererPort, ChunkSourcePort)           │  │  │
112: │  │  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │  │
113: │  │  │  │ ENTITIES (enterprise business rules)             │  │  │  │
114: │  │  │  │   VoxelGrid, SparseVoxelOctree, Position, Grid   │  │  │  │
115: │  │  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │  │
116: │  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │
117: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
118: └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
119: ```
120: 
121: ### Crates
122: 
123: | Crate | Role | Targets |
124: |---|---|---|
125: | `vackrooms` (root) | Entities + use cases + adapters; native dev-server binary | native **and** wasm32 |
126: | `wasm_frontend` | Portable application/adapters/WebGPU pipelines plus the wasm browser shell | wasm32 and native headless Vulkan tests |
127: | `wasm_raycaster` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment | kept for reference |
128: 
129: The platform boundary inside `wasm_frontend` is enforced mechanically. `web-sys`,
130: `js-sys`, and `wasm-bindgen` are wasm-only dependencies; browser context,
131: events, and rAF are `cfg(wasm32)`. Target-independent WebGPU configuration,
132: record layouts, shader assembly, and pipelines compile on the host so native
133: tests exercise the same code through Vulkan without admitting DOM types.
134: 
135: ### Ports (dependency inversion boundaries)
136: 
137: | Port | Defined in (inner) | Implemented by (outer) |
138: |---|---|---|
139: | `NoiseProvider` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `SimpleNoiseProvider` |
140: | `TelemetryPort` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `StdTelemetry` (native stdout), `ConsoleTelemetry` (browser console), `NullTelemetry` (tests) |
141: | `RendererPort` | `wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs` | `WebGpuRenderer` with surface/splat/raymarch/CPU strategies; recording fakes in application tests |
142: | `ChunkSourcePort` | `wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs` | `LocalChunkSource` (synchronous, in-wasm generation), `WorkerChunkSource` (pooled Web Worker generation, default); an HTTP-fetching implementation would slot in without touching the engine |
143: 
144: ## Data flow: from noise to pixel
145: 
146: The request and world state are authoritative inputs. `RenderArtifactNeeds`
147: describes which expensive presentation products a selected strategy consumes;
148: collision remains an application requirement, not a renderer preference.
149: 
150: ```
151: SimpleNoiseProvider (driver)
152:       │ NoiseProvider port
153:       ▼
154: GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase ──► haloed VoxelGrid
155:       │                                  │
156:       │                         bake_voxel_lighting
157:       ▼                                  ▼
158: crop authoritative grid ─────────► BuildOctreeUseCase (outside-grid pruning)
159:       │                                  │
160:       ├─ greedy mesh ────────────────────┼─► surface storage + index buffers
161:       ├─ compact face records ───────────┼─► splat storage buffer
162:       │                                  ├─► collision AABBs
163:       │                                  ▼
164:       │                         OctreeGpuSerializer
165:       │                                  │ four-u32 nodes, 1024-node rows
166:       │                                  ▼
167:       │                         merged/rebased SVO atlas
168:       │                                  ├─► raymarch storage buffer
169:       │                                  └─► CPU reference rasterizer
170:       ▼
171: analytic light records ────────────────► shared WebGPU frame storage
172: ```
173: 
174: Collision geometry is derived from the same SVO built from the rendered voxel
175: source. Uniform solid subtrees become larger collision boxes without a second
176: geometry generator.
177: 
178: ### SVO node encoding (four `u32` words per node)
179: 
180: | Lane | Internal node (`x == 0`) | Leaf node (`x == 1`) |
181: |---|---|---|
182: | x | 0 | 1 |
183: | y | `child_base_index` (children contiguous at +0..+7) | `voxel_type` |
184: | z | `child_mask` (bit *i* set = child *i* non-empty) | 24-bit `0xRRGGBB` color |
185: | w | 0 | scalar light 0–15, face-occlusion bits, and RGB light 0–15/channel |
186: 
187: Rows remain padded to 1024 nodes so atlas slots and partial row updates are
188: stable. The source of truth is `src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`; the
189: WebGPU decoder is
190: `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/webgpu/shaders/raymarch.wgsl`.
191: 
192: ## Level 0: architecture first
193: 
194: Level 0 is a **world-planning system**, not a random room generator. Math
195: selects architectural *intentions*; it never substitutes for them. Planning
196: descends a strict scale hierarchy, each level constraining the next:
197: 
198: ```
199: world seed
200:   -> MacroFields         multi-octave parameter fields (world_topology)
201:     -> MacroCell graph   160 u cells: nodes, portals, red-room events,
202:                          vertical links (use_cases/world_topology.rs)
203:       -> RegionPlan      80 u architectural plan (use_cases/region_plan/)
204:         -> ColumnPlan    one voxel column (use_cases/level_zero/)
205:           -> VoxelGrid   resolution-dependent output (level_zero/voxelize.rs)
206: ```
207: 
208: **Fractal math's one job.** `world_topology::sample_fields` sums three
209: noise octaves per parameter (`F(x,z) = Σ aᵢ·N(x/sᵢ, z/sᵢ)`) into `[0, 1]`
210: fields — `openness`, `vertical_pressure`, `institution_age`,
211: `anomaly_pressure`, `redroom_pressure`, `style_blend`. Fields only bias
212: probabilities and style choices (where the building's rules change); a
213: planner still decides every corridor, room, stair, and threshold. This is
214: what makes billions of areas *differ* without ever placing a wall by noise.
215: 
216: **The macro graph.** `plan_macro_cell(seed, cell, red_room_scale, noise)`
217: is a pure function returning one 160 u `MacroCell`: a `WorldNode` per
218: region (classified `Warren` / `OpenPlate` / `Atrium` / `Stairwell` /
219: `RedRoomEncounter`), shared-edge `Portal`s (both neighbors of an edge
220: derive the identical crossing — the infinite-corridor contract),
221: `VerticalLink` stair reservations, and at most one `RedRoomEvent`. A 5×5
222: graph snapshot test pins the exact topology of seed 42: an unintentional
223: world change fails the build.
224: 
225: **Red rooms are graph events, not a biome.** Events are planned on the
226: macro lattice by a deterministic local tournament: a candidate cell fires
227: only if no candidate within the separation radius beats its score, so any
228: two encounters keep a cooldown distance (≥ 3 regions), clustered where
229: `redroom_pressure` runs high. The region planner merely *realizes* an event
230: that targets its region by promoting one occupied, reachable assembly.
231: 
232: **Vertical circulation.** `vertical_link_for_region` reserves stairwells
233: where `vertical_pressure` is high: `OrdinaryStair` and `EndlessAscent`
234: links are realized by `use_cases/vertical_circulation.rs` as compact Stair
235: assemblies beside the main spine — a lit vestibule, a monotonic flight of
236: 0.2 u treads (raised floor voxelizes as solid, so it collides), and either
237: a landing or an endless climb into an unlit 5.4 u shaft. Elevation is an
238: integer story index on `WorldNode`; `EndlessDescent` / `ServiceShaft`
239: links stay graph reservations until the engine can stream below elevation
240: 0 and the player gains vertical physics (see roadmap).
241: 
242: **Archways are topological connectors.** A `Transition` arch room carries
243: an `ArchBehavior`: most are plain `Anchor`s, but a `CultureSeam`'s far
244: half changes ceiling regime, floor grammar, and lintel height, and a
245: `ScaleBreach`'s far half repeats the same grammar larger. The seam is
246: expressed only through legal architectural vocabulary — never impossible
247: collision or repainted walls.
248: 
249: Both stages are split by intent, one module per planning concern:
250: `use_cases/region_plan/` (genome, circulation, suites, corruption, debug)
251: and `use_cases/level_zero/` (fabric, circulation_sampler, assembly_sampler,
252: compose_column, generate, column_field, voxelize). Within one region, the
253: planner works as follows:
254: 
255: 1. **Region plans.** The world tiles into fixed 80 u regions. A pure function
256:    of `(seed, region)` derives 1–3 `ArchitectGenome`s (circulation style,
257:    structural system, proportions, threshold/ceiling/lighting languages,
258:    renovation history), routes one dominant 4.8–7.2 u primary spine between
259:    shared edge portals (so it chains across regions forever), then adds at
260:    most two 3.6–5.0 u interior branches. It attaches incomplete, 12–24 u
261:    `AssemblyInstance` masses beside that circulation rather than tiling the
262:    region with rooms. Thresholds are selected per assembly: narrow lintelled
263:    doors are rare; most fronts use a broad or unframed portal.
264: 2. **Corruption.** A final pass makes the sane plan Backrooms: suites repeat
265:    with misaligned copies, one assembly becomes an unlit
266:    `AbandonedExpansion` shell, renovations overlay contradictory column
267:    grids.
268: 3. **Voxelization.** `BackroomsLevel` samples the plan per voxel column with
269:    priority *corridor → assembly → fabric*: corridors carve open under
270:    3.4–4.2 u (primary) or 3.0–3.6 u (secondary) ceilings; assemblies retain
271:    long perimeter runs and sparse partitions; everything between is a sparse
272:    18 u wall fabric that dissolves into open space. A broad ceiling field
273:    holds the visual baseline at 3.2–3.6 u, with 3.8–4.4 u expanses, 4.5–5.4 u
274:    vaults, and rare 2.5–2.8 u compression zones. This keeps cheap office
275:    finishes at an implausible scale instead of producing a low office maze.
276: 
277: **The Peripheral Shift.** "Whenever not directly observed, the layout can
278: warp, stretch, or rearrange itself." `RealitySnapshot` (RTY v5) carries one
279: drift epoch per 40 u fabric cell plus the mismanagement *strain* tier
280: (delirium 0–3). The epoch re-salts the fabric's decisions — wall dropout,
281: doorway direction/position/framing, dead lights — and re-deals each
282: corridor section's edge mouths, read at each deciding lattice cell's own
283: anchor, so walls rebuild whole. At tier 0 the binary-tree doorway rule
284: (hence global connectivity) holds at any epoch mix. Under strain the
285: guarantee erodes *by design*: warren cells brick over their guaranteed
286: doorway (~10 % per tier) into dead-end pockets, second doorways thin,
287: corridor mouths narrow and (tier ≥ 2) seal whole sections, supply cells
288: withhold a 15 % share per tier, and rare 0.8 u secret slips open in
289: otherwise doorless walls (tier ≥ 2) — the punished labyrinth grows secrets
290: alongside its dead ends. Corridor interiors, portals, assemblies, anomaly
291: identities, arch-anchor surroundings, and the spawn opening sequence never
292: drift or strain: the spine survives; hallway memory — and, mismanaged,
293: hallway mercy — does not.
294: The engine advances epochs two ways: territory abandoned beyond the
295: streaming footprint (plus hysteresis) drifts on departure, and *inside a
296: blackout* the shift runs in real time — cells wholly behind the player's
297: facing, beyond any light's reach, and fully inside the blackout advance on
298: a slow cadence and force-rebuild in place, hidden by the dark. Strain is
299: fed from both ends of resource mismanagement — dehydration bands
300: (underconsumption) and the excess meter of wasted supply value, i.e.
301: drinking or eating past a full reserve (overconsumption) — and the max of
302: the two also shrinks drift hysteresis and speeds the blackout's rear-shift
303: cadence.
304: 
305: **Fixture decay and flicker.** The `institution_age` field steers the
306: fabric's dead-light ratio (young wings ~1.15x survival, ancient wings
307: ~0.6x). A deterministic share of warm panels carries a `flicker_mode`
308: authored at light collection (tired-ballast shimmer, dying tubes); the
309: engine pre-flickers intensity CPU-side once per frame, like flares, so all
310: renderers agree and no shader needs a clock.
311: 
312: All plan geometry snaps to a 0.4 u lattice (one coarse voxel) so every LOD
313: of a chunk voxelizes the same architecture. Debug hook:
314: `cargo run --example dump_plan` prints region plans as ASCII;
315: `debug_region_ascii` renders any plan.
316: 
317: ### Infinite generation and anomalies
318: 
319: The generation code is organized by the language of Level 0, rather than by
320: delivery mechanism:
321: 
322: ```
323: world_topology (macro fields, graph events, portals, vertical links)
324:         │
325: InfiniteRegionWindow ──► RegionPlan(s) ──► architectural ColumnPlan
326:                                                 │
327: anomalies/{planning,geometry} ──────────────────┤
328: red_rooms/{planning,geometry,recursive_level} ──┤
329: vertical_circulation (stair profiles) ──────────┘
330:                                                 │
331:                                       ColumnField (1-column halo)
332:                                                 │
333:                                       voxelize_columns ──► VoxelGrid
334: ```
335: 
336: - `domain/entities/anomaly/` contains only domain language: rectilinear
337:   geometry, immutable anomaly instances, traversal semantics, and canonical
338:   reality snapshots. The public `anomaly` namespace remains stable.
339:   `domain/entities/world_topology.rs` holds the macro-graph language
340:   (`MacroCell`, `WorldNode`, `Portal`, `VerticalLink`, `MacroFields`).
341: - `use_cases/anomalies/` plans and samples macro anomaly families on the
342:   same 160 u lattice as the world graph; per-anchor chance is weighted by
343:   the `anomaly_pressure` field, so anomalies arrive in loose
344:   constellations, never a uniform sprinkle.
345:   `use_cases/red_rooms/` owns the assembly-derived encounter and its recursive
346:   Level 0 address. The old `anomaly_plan` module is only a compatibility
347:   facade. The pre-planning `?level=1` generator lives untouched in
348:   `use_cases/legacy_blueprint.rs`, consulted by nothing in Level 0.
349: - `InfiniteRegionWindow` is the finite query cache for an infinite region
350:   lattice. A missing plan is an error instead of silently falling back to an
351:   unrelated region.
352: - A committed Red Room derives its branch seed and region-aligned translation
353:   with integer hashes over the full 64-bit anomaly id. Planning and sampling
354:   use that same address, so worker order, chunk boundaries, and floating-point
355:   id precision cannot select different worlds.
356: - `ColumnField` and `voxelize_columns` are resolution-dependent output stages.
357:   World planning never reads the requested output extent; generating one 20 u
358:   area or four 10 u areas produces the same voxels at matching coordinates.
359: 
360: Reality is part of chunk identity. Entering a Red Room changes the active
361: infinite Level 0 address, so all resident chunks are atomically scheduled for
362: replacement; partially repainting only the vestibule would splice two worlds
363: at a streaming boundary.
364: 
365: ### Generation invariants (enforced by tests)
366: 
367: Massive procedural worlds only work when randomness is constrained. These
368: contracts are non-negotiable and each is asserted natively:
369: 
370: - The same seed, coordinates, LOD, and reality always produce identical
371:   geometry; the 5×5 macro-graph snapshot digest pins seed 42's topology.
372: - Neighboring regions independently compute the same shared portals, and
373:   the primary route crosses every region boundary (corridors chain forever).
374: - Every assembly entrance opens onto a corridor; sealed masses are
375:   intentional (`AbandonedExpansion`), never accidents.
376: - Stair flights rise monotonically from a flat entrance, keep ≥ 2.2 u of
377:   headroom over every tread, and reach their declared landing.
378: - Red-room events keep a minimum separation radius; a red room never
379:   produces red masonry — only red light over ordinary architecture.
380: - World planning never reads the requested output extent: one 20 u query
381:   and four 10 u queries produce the same voxels at matching coordinates.
382: 
383: ## Chunk streaming
384: 
385: Chunk generation runs on a pool of Web Workers (`WorkerChunkSource`,
386: `static/worker.js` — each a second instance of the same wasm module). The
387: pure `GenerationWorkerPreference` policy accepts `?workers=auto|0|1..4`:
388: `auto` reserves one reported hardware thread and caps the pool at four,
389: explicit counts are clamped to reported hardware and the four-worker product
390: cap, while `0` selects the synchronous in-thread `LocalChunkSource`. That
391: local source is also the automatic fallback if worker startup fails. These workers parallelize chunk
392: generation, lighting, meshes, SVO serialization, and collision extraction;
393: they do **not** parallelize any renderer, including the CPU splatter. Either
394: way, the resident set
395: itself is **time-sliced** and **progressive**: `StreamingPolicy` produces the
396: desired resident set (nearest-first) each frame, and the `Engine` spends a
397: per-tick cost budget on it in two phases:
398: 
399: 1. **Availability** — every missing chunk first loads at a *coarse LOD*
400:    (voxels 2× the size, ~1/8 the generation/lighting/SVO cost, ~1 budget
401:    unit), so the whole footprint renders after roughly one tick instead of
402:    trickling in chunk by chunk.
403: 2. **Refinement** — leftover budget reloads the nearest coarse chunk *within
404:    `fine_distance`* at full resolution, replacing it in place (same atlas
405:    slot, partial row upload). Chunks beyond `fine_distance` stay coarse: at
406:    that range a coarse voxel projects to about the same pixels as a fine one
407:    — a screen-space-error LOD. Refinement is monotonic while resident, so
408:    the LOD choice never flaps.
409: 
410: Every LOD of a chunk covers the same world cube (`GeneratorConfig::at_lod`
411: halves the SVO depth as it doubles `voxel_scale`), and cell borders/door
412: positions derive from world space, so a coarse chunk is a faithful low-res
413: proxy of its fine version and payloads are interchangeable to the renderer.
414: The SVO atlas and collision world are rebuilt only on a resident-set
415: change — steady-state frames upload nothing (asserted by
416: `steady_state_does_not_reupload_atlas`).
417: 
418: Profiles (selected by URL, `?spec=high`):
419: 
420: | | chunk size | radius | voxels (fine/coarse) | SVO depth | fine ring |
421: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
422: | low (default) | 10 u | 1 (3×3) | 0.2 / 0.4 u | 6 / 5 | 15 u (all 9) |
423: | high | 20 u | 2 (5×5) | 0.1 / 0.2 u | 8 / 7 | 25 u (~9 of 25) |
424: 
425: `?voxel_size=` overrides the fine voxel edge independently of the streaming
426: profile. `GeneratorConfig::try_with_voxel_size` is the single validator used
427: by the browser and every worker: the value must be finite and positive, tile
428: the chunk edge at both fine and progressive half-resolution LOD, fit the
429: depth-eight SVO payload contract, and remain
430: inside the measured dense-grid budget including the lateral halo. The UI
431: offers 0.4, 0.2, 0.1, and 0.05 u. The 10 u profile rejects 0.4 u because its
432: 25-cell axis cannot be halved exactly; the 20 u profile rejects 0.05 u because
433: it would require depth nine. Every chunk payload transports its exact voxel size
434: and depth, so no strategy reverse-engineers them from padded bounds.
435: 
436: The raymarch storage table is bounded at 25 chunks — exactly the 5×5 high-spec
437: worst case (`application::atlas::MAX_CHUNKS`).
438: 
439: ## Player simulation
440: 
441: `application::player` ports the original client's tuning 1:1: exponential
442: friction (8 s⁻¹), acceleration 4 u/s² (terminal 0.5 u/s), mouse sensitivity
443: 0.002 rad/px, pitch clamped short of ±90°. Collision is **axis-separated
444: sliding**: X and Z are moved and tested independently against the
445: `CollisionWorld`, so hitting a wall diagonally slides along it. `dt` is
446: clamped to 100 ms so a background-tab hitch cannot teleport the player
447: through a wall.
448: 
449: `application::body` is the embodied-telemetry layer on top: a pure,
450: deterministic model of session steps (stride 0.7 m over collision-resolved
451: walking only), short-term exertion, long-term fatigue with a rest loop, and
452: a target-BPM pulse with asymmetric smoothing. Its bounded movement factor
453: (≥ 0.35 before death) feeds back into `Player::step_with_effort`, scaling
454: acceleration — and therefore terminal speed — without touching collision.
455: `application::navigation` supplies pure route/bearing selection over the
456: resident `LevelExit`/gate/pit records: nearest-door prioritization, 0–359°
457: relative bearings, and deterministic anomaly focus for the diagnostic
458: aperture. Neither module invents targets — no resident record, no reading.
459: The browser driver stays a passive presenter of `HudStats`.
460: 
461: ## Testing strategy
462: 
463: Ports make the world and application rules natively testable without a
464: browser or GPU:
465: 
466: - `cargo test --workspace` covers entities, generation (including the
467:   macro-graph snapshot, red-room separation, stair-flight, and arch-seam
468:   invariants), lighting equations and bake invariants, octree build/serialize,
469:   plus the front end's player physics, sliding collision, streaming policy,
470:   atlas rebasing, input mapping, and the resolution governor.
471: - Renderer/chunk-source **test doubles** verify the engine's contract with
472:   its ports (upload counts, draw-table sizes) rather than pixels.
473: - The `vulkan_renderers` integration suite creates surface-free targets with
474:   the production pipeline modules. CI forces wgpu's Vulkan backend through
475:   Mesa Lavapipe, enables validation layers, and fails rather than silently
476:   skipping when no Vulkan adapter is present. This covers pipeline creation,
477:   storage layouts, draw encoding, readback, and deterministic renderer
478:   contracts without browser screenshots.
479: 
480: ## Native dev server
481: 
482: `src/main.rs` is a zero-dependency HTTP server used for local development. It
483: serves static files with correct MIME types (`application/wasm` is mandatory
484: for streaming instantiation) and retains `/maze` and `/octree` as diagnostic
485: JSON/binary endpoints. The wasm client needs no data endpoint. The former
486: Three.js client, its static asset, and the `/legacy` route are retired.
487: 
488: ## Roadmap (documented non-goals of this iteration)
489: 
490: - **Vertical streaming**: chunks keyed by `(x, z, elevation)` so
491:   `EndlessDescent` / `ServiceShaft` links can voxelize real destinations;
492:   player step-up and Y physics so planned flights become climbable. The
493:   topology contracts (`VerticalLink`, integer `elevation`) already exist —
494:   the endless variants should re-address the world at each landing, never
495:   mesh a literal infinite staircase.
496: - Arch seams as *portal transforms*: a `CultureSeam` crossing re-seeding
497:   the architect genome on the far side, `LoopBreach` returning near the
498:   origin under a shifted reality epoch (gate machinery exists; the arch
499:   kinds need their own `TraversalGate` semantics).
500: - Red-room progression: foreshadowing (warming/flickering fixtures across
501:   the one or two assemblies adjacent to a planned event, driven by the
502:   existing event lookup).
503: - Temporal reprojection / checkerboarding to complement adaptive resolution.
504: - Per-chunk AABB proxy draws with fragment-depth output to replace the
505:   fullscreen raymarch pass if resident chunk counts grow beyond 25.
506: - LOD: shallower SVO mip levels for distant chunks.
````

 16: /// The streaming engine always requests one half-resolution proxy before a
 17: /// fine chunk. A valid user resolution must therefore divide the chunk at
 18: /// both LOD 0 and LOD 1; otherwise the proxy silently grows past the shared
 19: /// chunk seam after rounding.
 20: const PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR: u32 = 2;
 21: 
 22: /// Maximum number of dense X/Z voxel columns generated for one chunk.
 23: ///
 24: /// The finest supported logical chunk is 200 x 200 cells. Browser generation
 25: /// retains one seam/light-sampling cell on every lateral side, so the actual
 26: /// measured allocation is 202 x 202 = 40,804 columns.
 27: pub const MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS: u64 = 40_804;
 28: 
 29: /// Tallest authored interior in the current generator catalog. Two boundary
 30: /// layers are added below when estimating the dense grid allocation.
 31: const MAX_GENERATED_HEIGHT_WORLD_UNITS: f64 = 12.0;
 32: 
 33: /// Maximum dense voxel samples allocated before SVO compression.
 34: ///
 35: /// This admits the standard 10u profile at 0.05u resolution, its one-cell
 36: /// lateral halo, and the tallest modeled interior: 202 x 202 x 242.
 37: pub const MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS: u64 = 9_874_568;
 38: 
 39: /// Why a requested scene voxel size cannot be used by a generator profile.
 40: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 41: pub enum VoxelSizeError {
 42:     NotFinite,
 43:     NotPositive,
 44:     /// The chunk edge must contain a whole number of voxels. Otherwise
 45:     /// independently generated neighbors disagree at their shared seam.
 46:     DoesNotTileChunk {
 47:         chunk_size: f32,
 48:         voxel_size: f32,
 49:     },
 50:     DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
 51:         fine_axis_voxels: u32,
 52:         divisor: u32,
 53:     },
 54:     SvoDepthExceedsLimit {
 55:         required: u32,
 56:         maximum: u32,
 57:     },
 58:     DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
 59:         required_columns: u64,
 60:         maximum_columns: u64,
 61:     },
 62:     DenseVoxelBudgetExceeded {
 63:         required_voxels: u64,
 64:         maximum_voxels: u64,
 65:     },
 66: }
 67: 
 68: impl std::fmt::Display for VoxelSizeError {
 69:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
 70:         match self {
 71:             Self::NotFinite => write!(f, "voxel size must be finite"),
 72:             Self::NotPositive => write!(f, "voxel size must be greater than zero"),
 73:             Self::DoesNotTileChunk {
 74:                 chunk_size,
 75:                 voxel_size,
 76:             } => write!(
 77:                 f,
 78:                 "voxel size {voxel_size} does not divide chunk size {chunk_size} into whole cells"
 79:             ),
 80:             Self::DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
 81:                 fine_axis_voxels,
 82:                 divisor,
 83:             } => write!(
 84:                 f,
 85:                 "fine axis has {fine_axis_voxels} cells, which cannot be divided by the required {divisor}x progressive LOD"
 86:             ),
 87:             Self::SvoDepthExceedsLimit { required, maximum } => write!(
 88:                 f,
 89:                 "voxel size requires SVO depth {required}, but the supported maximum is {maximum}"
 90:             ),
 91:             Self::DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
 92:                 required_columns,
 93:                 maximum_columns,
 94:             } => write!(
 95:                 f,
 96:                 "voxel size requires {required_columns} dense chunk columns, above the {maximum_columns}-column budget"
 97:             ),
 98:             Self::DenseVoxelBudgetExceeded {
 99:                 required_voxels,
100:                 maximum_voxels,
101:             } => write!(
102:                 f,
103:                 "voxel size requires up to {required_voxels} dense voxels, above the {maximum_voxels}-voxel memory budget"
104:             ),
105:         }
106:     }
107: }
108: 
109: impl std::error::Error for VoxelSizeError {}
110: 
111: /// User-tunable knobs for the level generators. All values are multipliers
112: /// around the defaults (1.0); 0 disables the feature, ~2 saturates it.
113: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
114: pub struct LevelTuning {
115:     /// Structural column / pillar density.
116:     pub pillars: f32,
117:     /// Office wall segment density.
118:     pub walls: f32,
119:     /// How much of the world vaults into tall atria.
120:     pub atria: f32,
121:     /// Ceiling light panel density.
122:     pub lights: f32,
123:     /// Dead-end and junction frequency (Growing Tree loop breaking).
124:     pub junction_density: f32,
125:     /// Frequency of stairs / vertical traversal generation.
126:     pub stairs_density: f32,
127:     /// Almond water pickup frequency. 0 removes every bottle.
128:     pub almond_water: f32,
129:     /// Ration pickup frequency. 0 removes all food.
130:     pub rations: f32,
131:     /// Level-door frequency. 0 removes every door, including the authored
132:     /// one near spawn.
133:     pub level_doors: f32,
134: }
135: 
136: impl Default for LevelTuning {
137:     fn default() -> Self {
138:         Self {
139:             pillars: 1.0,
140:             walls: 1.0,
141:             atria: 1.0,
142:             lights: 1.0,
143:             junction_density: 1.0,
144:             stairs_density: 1.0,
145:             almond_water: 1.0,
146:             rations: 1.0,
147:             level_doors: 1.0,
148:         }
149:     }
150: }

152: /// Dynamic config configuration profile to scale SVO dimensions and voxel grid.
153: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
154: pub struct GeneratorConfig {
155:     pub chunk_size: f32,
156:     pub voxel_scale: f32,
157:     /// Which level generator fills the chunks (see `level_generator`):
158:     /// 0 = Backrooms (default), 1 = legacy office blueprint, 34 = grassland.
159:     pub level: u32,
160:     /// User-facing generation knobs (URL query params in the browser).
161:     pub tuning: LevelTuning,
162:     /// Stateful Level 0 phenomena. Outdoor/legacy levels ignore this group.
163:     pub anomalies: AnomalyTuning,
164: }
165: 
166: impl GeneratorConfig {
167:     pub fn high_spec() -> Self {
168:         Self {
169:             chunk_size: 20.0,
170:             voxel_scale: 0.1,
171:             level: 0,
172:             tuning: LevelTuning::default(),
173:             anomalies: AnomalyTuning::default(),
174:         }
175:     }
176: 
177:     pub fn low_spec() -> Self {
178:         Self {
179:             chunk_size: 10.0,
180:             voxel_scale: 0.2,
181:             level: 0,
182:             tuning: LevelTuning::default(),
183:             anomalies: AnomalyTuning::default(),
184:         }
185:     }
186: 
187:     pub fn with_level(mut self, level: u32) -> Self {
188:         self.level = level;
189:         self
190:     }
191: 
192:     pub fn with_tuning(mut self, tuning: LevelTuning) -> Self {
193:         self.tuning = tuning;
194:         self
195:     }
196: 
197:     pub fn with_anomalies(mut self, anomalies: AnomalyTuning) -> Self {
198:         self.anomalies = anomalies;
199:         self
200:     }
201: 
202:     /// Applies a user-selected scene voxel size after checking every
203:     /// invariant relied upon by chunk generation and GPU traversal.
204:     ///
205:     /// The override must be finite, positive, tile this profile's chunk edge
206:     /// with a whole number of cells, fit the renderer's SVO-depth limit, and
207:     /// stay inside the dense pre-compression memory budget. Callers should
208:     /// keep the original profile when this returns an error.
209:     pub fn try_with_voxel_size(mut self, voxel_size: f32) -> Result<Self, VoxelSizeError> {
210:         if !voxel_size.is_finite() {
211:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotFinite);
212:         }
213:         if voxel_size <= 0.0 {
214:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::NotPositive);
215:         }
216: 
217:         let ratio = f64::from(self.chunk_size) / f64::from(voxel_size);
218:         let axis_voxels = ratio.round();
219:         let reconstructed_chunk = axis_voxels * f64::from(voxel_size);
220:         let seam_tolerance = f64::from(self.chunk_size).abs().mul_add(1.0e-6, 1.0e-6);
221:         if axis_voxels < 1.0
222:             || !ratio.is_finite()
223:             || (reconstructed_chunk - f64::from(self.chunk_size)).abs() > seam_tolerance
224:         {
225:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileChunk {
226:                 chunk_size: self.chunk_size,
227:                 voxel_size,
228:             });
229:         }
230: 
231:         let axis_voxels = axis_voxels as u32;
232:         if axis_voxels % PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR != 0 {
233:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DoesNotTileProgressiveLod {
234:                 fine_axis_voxels: axis_voxels,
235:                 divisor: PROGRESSIVE_LOD_DIVISOR,
236:             });
237:         }
238:         let required_depth = axis_voxels
239:             .checked_next_power_of_two()
240:             .map(u32::trailing_zeros)
241:             .unwrap_or(u32::BITS);
242:         if required_depth > MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH {
243:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::SvoDepthExceedsLimit {
244:                 required: required_depth,
245:                 maximum: MAX_SUPPORTED_SVO_DEPTH,
246:             });
247:         }
248: 
249:         // LocalChunkSource generates one lateral cell on each side for seam
250:         // visibility and boundary light-volume samples. Validate the real
251:         // dense allocation rather than only the cropped payload.
252:         let allocated_axis = u64::from(axis_voxels) + 2;
253:         let required_columns = allocated_axis * allocated_axis;
254:         if required_columns > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS {
255:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseChunkBudgetExceeded {
256:                 required_columns,
257:                 maximum_columns: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_COLUMNS,
258:             });
259:         }
260: 
261:         let height_voxels =
262:             (MAX_GENERATED_HEIGHT_WORLD_UNITS / f64::from(voxel_size)).ceil() as u64 + 2;
263:         let required_voxels = required_columns
264:             .checked_mul(height_voxels)
265:             .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
266:         if required_voxels > MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS {
267:             return Err(VoxelSizeError::DenseVoxelBudgetExceeded {
268:                 required_voxels,
269:                 maximum_voxels: MAX_DENSE_CHUNK_VOXELS,
270:             });
271:         }
272: 
273:         self.voxel_scale = voxel_size;
274:         Ok(self)
275:     }
276: 
277:     /// The same chunk at a coarser level of detail: voxels double per LOD
278:     /// step, so lod 1 costs ~1/8 of lod 0 to generate, light, and serialize.
279:     /// `svo_world_size()` is invariant across LODs (half the voxels at twice
280:     /// the scale), so payloads of any LOD are interchangeable to the renderer.
281:     pub fn at_lod(mut self, lod: u8) -> Self {
282:         self.voxel_scale *= (1u32 << lod.min(4)) as f32;
283:         self
284:     }
285: 
286:     pub fn svo_depth(&self) -> u32 {
287:         let voxels = (self.chunk_size / self.voxel_scale).round().max(1.0) as u32;
288:         voxels.next_power_of_two().trailing_zeros()
289:     }
290: 
291:     pub fn svo_world_size(&self) -> f32 {
292:         let size = 1 << self.svo_depth();
293:         size as f32 * self.voxel_scale
294:     }
295: }
296: 
297: pub struct GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
298:     noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
299:     telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
300: }
301: 
302: impl<'a> GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase<'a> {
303:     /// Constructs the use case with silent telemetry (tests, wasm default).
304:     pub fn new(noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider) -> Self {
305:         Self {
306:             noise_provider,
307:             telemetry: &NULL_TELEMETRY,
308:         }
309:     }
310: 
311:     /// Constructs the use case with an injected telemetry sink (native server,
312:     /// browser console, ...). Keeps the Dependency Rule intact: the use case
313:     /// only knows the TelemetryPort trait.
314:     pub fn with_telemetry(
315:         noise_provider: &'a dyn NoiseProvider,
316:         telemetry: &'a dyn TelemetryPort,
317:     ) -> Self {
318:         Self {
319:             noise_provider,
320:             telemetry,
321:         }
322:     }
323: 
324:     pub fn execute(&self, chunk_pos: Position, seed: u32, config: GeneratorConfig) -> VoxelGrid {
325:         self.execute_with_reality(chunk_pos, seed, config, &RealitySnapshot::default())
326:     }
327: 
328:     /// Generates a chunk against an immutable encounter-state snapshot.
329:     /// The snapshot is part of the request identity in the browser pipeline;
330:     /// generation itself remains pure and replayable.
331:     pub fn execute_with_reality(
332:         &self,
333:         chunk_pos: Position,
334:         seed: u32,
335:         config: GeneratorConfig,
336:         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
337:     ) -> VoxelGrid {
338:         // Pluggable levels: everything except the legacy office blueprint
339:         // (level 90, kept inline below) goes through the LevelGenerator port.
340:         // Level 0 is the architecturally *planned* Backrooms: region plans
341:         // (circulation -> assemblies -> corruption) drive the voxelization.
342:         if config.level == 0 || config.level == 1 || config.level == 34 {
343:             use crate::use_cases::grassland_level::GrasslandLevel;
344:             use crate::use_cases::level_generator::LevelGenerator;
345:             use crate::use_cases::level_one::HabitableLevel;
346:             use crate::use_cases::level_zero::BackroomsLevel;
347: 
348:             let start_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros();
349:             let generator: &dyn LevelGenerator = match config.level {
350:                 0 => &BackroomsLevel,
351:                 1 => &HabitableLevel,
352:                 _ => &GrasslandLevel,
353:             };
354:             let mut grid = generator.generate_with_reality(
355:                 chunk_pos,
356:                 seed,
357:                 config,
358:                 self.noise_provider,
359:                 reality,
360:             );
361:             let lighting =
362:                 crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::VoxelLightingSettings::with_default_range(
363:                     config.voxel_scale,
364:                 )
365:                 .expect("GeneratorConfig voxel_scale must be finite and greater than zero");
366:             crate::use_cases::bake_voxel_lighting::bake_voxel_lighting(&mut grid, lighting);
367: 
368:             let elapsed_micros = self.telemetry.now_micros().saturating_sub(start_micros);
369:             self.telemetry.log(&format!(
370:                 "[TELEMETRY] level {} chunk generated. Duration={}us, Grid={}x{}x{}",
371:                 config.level,
372:                 elapsed_micros,
373:                 grid.width(),
374:                 grid.height(),
375:                 grid.depth()
376:             ));
377:             return grid;
378:         }
379: 
380:         legacy_blueprint::generate_legacy_blueprint(
381:             self.noise_provider,
382:             self.telemetry,
383:             chunk_pos,
384:             seed,
385:             config,
386:         )
387:     }
388: }

516:     #[test]
517:     fn coarse_chunk_generates_the_same_layout_smaller() {
518:         let noise = MockNoiseProvider { value: 0.0 };
519:         let generator = GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::new(&noise);
520:         let fine = generator.execute(
521:             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
522:             42,
523:             GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES),
524:         );
525:         let coarse = generator.execute(
526:             Position::new(10.0, 10.0),
527:             42,
528:             GeneratorConfig::low_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES).at_lod(1),
529:         );
530:         assert_eq!(coarse.width() * 2, fine.width());
531:         assert_eq!(coarse.depth() * 2, fine.depth());
532:         // Same maze at half resolution. Cell sizes truncate differently per
533:         // scale (5.0/0.4 = 12 voxels vs 25 at fine), so wall planes may land
534:         // one fine voxel off; an LOD proxy only needs walls to line up to
535:         // within that tolerance.
536:         let wall = crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VOXEL_WALL;
537:         let mut wall_match = 0usize;
538:         let mut wall_total = 0usize;
539:         for z in 0..coarse.depth() {
540:             for x in 0..coarse.width() {
541:                 if coarse.get(x, 1, z) != wall {
542:                     continue;
543:                 }
544:                 wall_total += 1;
545:                 let (fx, fz) = (x * 2, z * 2);
546:                 let mut near = false;
547:                 for dz in -1i32..=2 {
548:                     for dx in -1i32..=2 {
549:                         let (sx, sz) = (fx as i32 + dx, fz as i32 + dz);
550:                         if sx >= 0
551:                             && sz >= 0
552:                             && (sx as usize) < fine.width()
553:                             && (sz as usize) < fine.depth()
554:                             && fine.get(sx as usize, 1, sz as usize) == wall
555:                         {
556:                             near = true;
557:                         }
558:                     }
559:                 }
560:                 if near {
561:                     wall_match += 1;
562:                 }
563:             }
564:         }
565:         assert!(wall_total > 0, "coarse chunk must still contain walls");
566:         assert!(
567:             wall_match * 10 >= wall_total * 9,
568:             "coarse walls should lie within one fine voxel of fine walls: {wall_match}/{wall_total}"
569:         );
570:     }

709:     #[test]
710:     fn test_microbiome_zones_generation_and_contiguous() {
711:         use crate::domain::entities::cell::MicrobiomeZone;
712:         use crate::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
713: 
714:         let noise = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
715:         let config = GeneratorConfig::high_spec().with_level(crate::use_cases::level_generator::LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES);
716:         let chunk_size = config.chunk_size;
717:         let mut zones = std::collections::HashSet::new();
718: 
719:         let seed = 42;
720:         let mut grid_zones = vec![MicrobiomeZone::Standard; 100];
721: 
722:         for cz in 0..10 {
723:             for cx in 0..10 {
724:                 let wx = 10.0 * chunk_size + (cx as f32) * 5.0;
725:                 let wz = 10.0 * chunk_size + (cz as f32) * 5.0;
726:                 let n = noise.evaluate_2d(
727:                     seed ^ 0x2b8f_a43c,
728:                     crate::entities::models::Position::new(wx * 0.05, wz * 0.05),
729:                 );
730: 
731:                 let zone = if n < -0.7 {
732:                     MicrobiomeZone::Blackout
733:                 } else if n < -0.4 {
734:                     MicrobiomeZone::Holes
735:                 } else if n > 0.85 - (config.tuning.atria as f32 * 0.1) {
736:                     MicrobiomeZone::Atrium
737:                 } else if n > 0.6 {
738:                     MicrobiomeZone::PillarField
739:                 } else if n > 0.4 {
740:                     MicrobiomeZone::Arch
741:                 } else if n > 0.2 && n < 0.25 {
742:                     MicrobiomeZone::RedRoom
743:                 } else {
744:                     MicrobiomeZone::Standard
745:                 };
746: 
747:                 zones.insert(zone);
748:                 grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx] = zone;
749:             }
750:         }
751: 
752:         assert!(zones.len() >= 2, "Expected at least 2 distinct zones");
753: 
754:         let mut same_neighbor_count = 0;
755:         let mut total_neighbors = 0;
756:         for cz in 1..9 {
757:             for cx in 1..9 {
758:                 let z = grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx];
759:                 total_neighbors += 4;
760:                 if grid_zones[(cz - 1) * 10 + cx] == z {
761:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
762:                 }
763:                 if grid_zones[(cz + 1) * 10 + cx] == z {
764:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
765:                 }
766:                 if grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx - 1] == z {
767:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
768:                 }
769:                 if grid_zones[cz * 10 + cx + 1] == z {
770:                     same_neighbor_count += 1;
771:                 }
772:             }
773:         }
774: 
775:         assert!(
776:             same_neighbor_count as f32 / total_neighbors as f32 > 0.6,
777:             "Expected zones to be highly contiguous"
778:         );
779:     }

  38:         :root {
