258: /// Saved backend preference, written by the Settings menu. Query params
259: /// always win so shared links stay exact reproductions.
260: fn stored_backend_pref(window: &Window) -> Option<String> {
261:     window
262:         .local_storage()
263:         .ok()
264:         .flatten()
265:         .and_then(|storage| storage.get_item("vackrooms_backend").ok())
266:         .flatten()
267: }
268: 
269: /// Backend, then renderer, selection.
270: ///
271: /// Backend: `?backend=webgl|webgpu` > saved preference > WebGL2. WebGL2 is
272: /// the compatibility floor (Firefox ESR, mobile); WebGPU stays an explicit
273: /// opt-in. Renderer within the backend: `?renderer=` (surface, splat,
274: /// raymarch, cpu), defaulting to surfaces — on WebGPU without an explicit
275: /// choice, the adapter's own compatibility decides (software adapters get
276: /// the CPU rasterizer).
277: async fn create_renderer(
278:     window: &Window,
279:     canvas: &HtmlCanvasElement,
280:     status_msg: &HtmlElement,
281:     query: &str,
282:     quality: GpuQualityProfile,
283: ) -> Result<DriverRenderer, JsValue> {
284:     let backend = query_param(query, "backend")
285:         .map(str::to_owned)
286:         .or_else(|| stored_backend_pref(window))
287:         .unwrap_or_else(|| "webgl".to_owned());
288:     if backend == "webgpu" {
289:         webgpu_preflight(window, status_msg).await?;
290:         let requested = query_param(query, "renderer").and_then(RendererKind::parse);
291:         return WebGpuRenderer::new_auto(canvas, requested, quality)
292:             .await
293:             .map(DriverRenderer::WebGpu);
294:     }
295: 
296:     let renderer_choice = query_param(query, "renderer");
297:     if renderer_choice == Some("cpu") {
298:         return Ok(DriverRenderer::Cpu(CpuCanvasRenderer::new(canvas)?));
299:     }
300:     if renderer_choice == Some("raymarch") {
301:         return WebGl2Renderer::new(canvas).map(DriverRenderer::Raymarch);
302:     }
303:     if renderer_choice == Some("splat") {
304:         let profile = if quality == GpuQualityProfile::High {
305:             SplatProfile::high()
306:         } else {
307:             SplatProfile::low()
308:         };
309:         match SplatRenderer::new(canvas, profile) {
310:             Ok(gpu) => return Ok(DriverRenderer::Splat(gpu)),
311:             Err(err) => {
312:                 web_sys::console::warn_2(
313:                     &JsValue::from_str(
314:                         "splat renderer unavailable, falling back to surface meshes:",
315:                     ),
316:                     &err,
317:                 );
318:             }
319:         }
320:     }
321:     match SurfaceRenderer::new(canvas) {
322:         Ok(gpu) => Ok(DriverRenderer::Surface(gpu)),
323:         Err(err) => {
324:             web_sys::console::warn_2(
325:                 &JsValue::from_str(
326:                     "WebGL2 surface renderer unavailable, falling back to CPU splatting:",
327:                 ),
328:                 &err,
329:             );
330:             Ok(DriverRenderer::Cpu(CpuCanvasRenderer::new(canvas)?))
331:         }
332:     }
333: }
334: 
335: /// Preflight for the opt-in WebGPU backend: failures inside wgpu's surface
336: /// and adapter glue are unactionable (`getContext` null, or an uncaught
337: /// TypeError when `requestAdapter` resolves to null — seen on mobile
338: /// Chrome), so probe both layers first and put concrete guidance in the
339: /// loading HUD. WebGL2 boots never run this.
340: async fn webgpu_preflight(window: &Window, status_msg: &HtmlElement) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
341:     let gpu = js_sys::Reflect::get(&window.navigator(), &JsValue::from_str("gpu"))
342:         .unwrap_or(JsValue::UNDEFINED);
343:     if gpu.is_undefined() || gpu.is_null() {
344:         // WebGPU only exists in secure contexts, so a plain-http LAN address
345:         // (phone pointed at a dev box) hides navigator.gpu even in browsers
346:         // that fully support it. Distinguish that from a browser gap.
347:         let msg = if !window.is_secure_context() {
348:             "WebGPU requires a secure context and this page was loaded over \
349:              plain HTTP. Serve it via https or localhost, or switch the \
350:              backend setting back to WebGL2."
351:         } else {
352:             "WebGPU is not available in this browser (navigator.gpu is missing). \
353:              Use Chrome/Edge 113+ or Safari 18+, or switch the backend \
354:              setting back to WebGL2."
355:         };
356:         status_msg.set_text_content(Some(msg));
357:         return Err(JsValue::from_str(msg));
358:     }
359:     if !probe_webgpu_adapter(&gpu).await {
360:         let msg = "This device exposes WebGPU but reports no usable graphics \
361:                    adapter. Check hardware acceleration (chrome://gpu), or \
362:                    switch the backend setting back to WebGL2.";
363:         status_msg.set_text_content(Some(msg));
364:         return Err(JsValue::from_str(msg));
365:     }
366:     Ok(())
367: }
368: 
369: /// Asks `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` directly whether any adapter
370: /// exists. wgpu's generated bindings assume the resolved adapter is
371: /// non-null and crash (`null.info`) before our error handling runs, so
372: /// this duplicate one-off request is the only way to fail politely.
373: async fn probe_webgpu_adapter(gpu: &JsValue) -> bool {
374:     let request = match js_sys::Reflect::get(gpu, &JsValue::from_str("requestAdapter"))
375:         .ok()
376:         .and_then(|value| value.dyn_into::<js_sys::Function>().ok())
377:     {
378:         Some(function) => function,
379:         None => return false,
380:     };
381:     let promise = match request
382:         .call0(gpu)
383:         .ok()
384:         .and_then(|value| value.dyn_into::<js_sys::Promise>().ok())
385:     {
386:         Some(promise) => promise,
387:         None => return false,
388:     };
389:     match wasm_bindgen_futures::JsFuture::from(promise).await {
390:         Ok(adapter) => !adapter.is_null() && !adapter.is_undefined(),
391:         Err(_) => false,
392:     }
393: }
394: 
395: pub async fn boot() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
396:     let window = web_sys::window().ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no window"))?;
397:     let document = window
398:         .document()
399:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str("no document"))?;
400: 
401:     let canvas: HtmlCanvasElement =
402:         element(&document, "view").or_else(|_| element(&document, "game-canvas"))?;
403:     let overlay: HtmlElement = element(&document, "overlay")?;
404:     let status_msg: HtmlElement = element(&document, "status-msg")?;
405:     let play_msg: HtmlElement = element(&document, "play-msg")?;
406: 
407:     // ?spec=high -> 20u chunks, 5x5 streaming radius, 0.1u voxels.
408:     // Default is the low-spec profile: 10u chunks, 3x3 radius, 0.2u voxels.
409:     // Generation controls: ?seed=… (number or any text) plus the density
410:     // knobs ?pillars= ?walls= ?atria= ?lights= (multipliers, default 1).
411:     let query = window.location().search().unwrap_or_default();
412:     web_sys::console::log_1(&format!("BOOTING ENGINE: query={}", query).into());
413:     // Renderer optimization switchboard (?rt_<name>=0|1); see
414:     // application::render_settings for the catalog of switches.
415:     crate::init_render_toggles(&query);
416:     // This resolver is also called inside every worker. Keeping the actual
417:     // GeneratorConfig behind one adapter prevents a rejected voxel override
418:     // from producing different worlds on the main and worker threads.
419:     let quality = quality_profile_from_query(&query);
420:     let (resolved_seed, generator_config) =
421:         generator_setup_for_quality(&query, WORLD_SEED, quality);
422:     let high_spec = quality == GpuQualityProfile::High;
423:     // Spawn on the main corridor of region (0,0), looking east down its
424:     // west leg: the first frame is a lit, walled corridor receding into
425:     // fog — the player knows immediately that this is the Backrooms.
426:     let spawn_at = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::spawn_point(resolved_seed);
427:     let spawn = [spawn_at.x, 1.7, spawn_at.z];
428:     // Face east along +X.
429:     let spawn_yaw = -std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_2;
430:     // ?level=34 boots straight into the grassland (debugging any level in
431:     // any renderer without waiting on a noclip roll).
432:     let initial_level = query_param(&query, "level")
433:         .and_then(|v| v.parse::<u32>().ok())
434:         .unwrap_or(0);
435:     let engine_config = if high_spec {
436:         EngineConfig {
437:             chunk_size: generator_config.chunk_size,
438:             chunk_radius: 2,
439:             seed: resolved_seed,
440:             spawn,
441:             spawn_yaw,
442:             // 5x5 footprint: the outer ring (>= 20 units away) stays at
443:             // the coarse LOD, so high spec pays for ~9 fine chunks, not 25.
444:             fine_distance: 25.0,
445:             initial_level,
446:             ..EngineConfig::default()
447:         }
448:     } else {
449:         EngineConfig {
450:             chunk_size: generator_config.chunk_size,
451:             seed: resolved_seed,
452:             spawn,
453:             spawn_yaw,
454:             initial_level,
455:             ..EngineConfig::default()
456:         }
457:     };
458: 
459:     let renderer = Rc::new(RefCell::new(
460:         create_renderer(&window, &canvas, &status_msg, &query, quality).await?,
461:     ));
462:     if let Some((label_rgba, label_w, label_h)) = build_label_atlas() {
463:         renderer
464:             .borrow_mut()
465:             .upload_label_atlas(&label_rgba, label_w, label_h);
466:     }
467:     if let Ok(hud_renderer) = element::<HtmlElement>(&document, "hud-renderer") {
468:         hud_renderer.set_text_content(Some(renderer.borrow().label()));
469:     }
470:     // Names the section the player is standing in (top-right HUD). The
471:     // locator re-derives the deterministic region plan, cached per region.
472:     let locator = Rc::new(RefCell::new(SectionLocator::new(
473:         resolved_seed,
474:         generator_config,
475:     )));
476:     // This pool parallelizes chunk generation/lighting/SVO construction,
477:     // never the renderer. The pure policy reserves the main thread and
478:     // clamps explicit requests to reported hardware. Zero selects the
479:     // synchronous source, which is also the worker-startup fallback.
480:     let worker_preference = parse_generation_worker_preference(&query);
481:     let hardware_concurrency = window.navigator().hardware_concurrency();
482:     let generation_worker_count = worker_preference.resolve(hardware_concurrency);
483:     let source: Box<dyn crate::application::ports::ChunkSourcePort> =
484:         if generation_worker_count == 0 {
485:             web_sys::console::log_1(&"chunk generation: synchronous main thread".into());
486:             Box::new(LocalChunkSource::with_telemetry(
487:                 SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
488:                 resolved_seed,
489:                 generator_config,
490:                 &CONSOLE_TELEMETRY,
491:             ))
492:         } else {
493:             match crate::drivers::worker_source::WorkerChunkSource::new(
494:                 &query,
495:                 WORLD_SEED,
496:                 generation_worker_count,
497:             ) {
498:                 Ok(pool) => {
499:                     web_sys::console::log_1(
500:                         &format!("chunk generation: {} worker threads", pool.pool_size()).into(),
501:                     );
502:                     Box::new(pool)
503:                 }
504:                 Err(err) => {
505:                     web_sys::console::warn_2(
506:                         &JsValue::from_str(
507:                             "worker pool unavailable, falling back to in-thread generation:",
508:                         ),
509:                         &err,
510:                     );
511:                     Box::new(LocalChunkSource::with_telemetry(
512:                         SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
513:                         resolved_seed,
514:                         generator_config,
515:                         &CONSOLE_TELEMETRY,
516:                     ))
517:                 }
518:             }
519:         };
520:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new(
521:         engine_config,
522:         Box::new(SharedRenderer(renderer.clone())),
523:         source,
524:     )));
525:     let input = Rc::new(RefCell::new(InputCollector::new()));
526:     let touch = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TouchState::default()));
527: 
528:     attach_input_listeners(&document, &canvas, &overlay, &input, &touch)?;
529:     attach_touch_listeners(&document, &canvas, &overlay, &input, &touch)?;
530:     run_frame_loop(
531:         window, document, canvas, overlay, status_msg, play_msg, renderer, engine, input, locator,
532:     )
533: }
534: 
535: /// Renders the engine's `§`-sectioned diagnostic report as aperture panels.
536: /// Body lines are escaped; only the fixed panel scaffolding is markup.
537: fn diagnostic_sections_html(report: &str) -> String {
538:     fn escape(text: &str) -> String {
539:         text.replace('&', "&amp;")
540:             .replace('<', "&lt;")
541:             .replace('>', "&gt;")
542:     }
543:     let mut html = String::with_capacity(report.len() + 256);
544:     let mut open = false;
545:     for line in report.lines() {
546:         if let Some(title) = line.strip_prefix("§ ") {
547:             if open {
548:                 html.push_str("</pre></section>");
549:             }
550:             html.push_str("<section class=\"diag-section\"><h4>");
551:             html.push_str(&escape(title));
552:             html.push_str("</h4><pre>");
553:             open = true;
554:         } else if open {
555:             html.push_str(&escape(line));
556:             html.push('\n');
557:         } else {
558:             // Preamble lines before the first section header.
559:             html.push_str("<section class=\"diag-section\"><pre>");
560:             html.push_str(&escape(line));
561:             html.push('\n');
562:             open = true;
563:         }
564:     }
565:     if open {
566:         html.push_str("</pre></section>");
567:     }
568:     html
569: }
570: 
571: fn element<T: JsCast>(document: &Document, id: &str) -> Result<T, JsValue> {
572:     document
573:         .get_element_by_id(id)
574:         .ok_or_else(|| JsValue::from_str(&format!("missing #{id} element")))?
575:         .dyn_into::<T>()
576:         .map_err(|_| JsValue::from_str(&format!("#{id} has unexpected element type")))
577: }
578: 
579: #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
580: fn run_frame_loop(
581:     window: Window,
582:     _document: Document,
583:     canvas: HtmlCanvasElement,
584:     _overlay: HtmlElement,
585:     status_msg: HtmlElement,
586:     play_msg: HtmlElement,
587:     renderer: Rc<RefCell<DriverRenderer>>,
588:     engine: Rc<RefCell<Engine>>,
589:     input: Rc<RefCell<InputCollector>>,
590:     locator: Rc<RefCell<SectionLocator>>,
591: ) -> Result<(), JsValue> {
592:     let document = window.document().unwrap();
593:     // Engine metrics live inside the diagnostic aperture in the redesigned
594:     // shell; the ids are unchanged so older/embedded shells keep working.
595:     let hud_fps: HtmlElement = element(&document, "hud-fps")?;
596:     let hud_chunks: HtmlElement = element(&document, "hud-chunks")?;
597:     let hud_nodes: HtmlElement = element(&document, "hud-nodes")?;
598:     let hud_scale: HtmlElement = element(&document, "hud-scale")?;
599:     let hud_gpu: HtmlElement = element(&document, "hud-gpu")?;
600:     // Top-right section readout and the diagnostic aperture; both are
601:     // optional page elements so older/embedded shells keep working.
602:     let hud_section: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "hud-section").ok();
603:     let last_section_text = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
604:     let debug_overlay: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "debug-overlay").ok();
605:     // The aperture wrapper also holds the always-in-DOM engine channels;
606:     // visibility toggles on it when present (older shells fall back to the
607:     // report element itself).
608:     let diagnostics_shell: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "diagnostics").ok();
609:     let debug_overlay_visible = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
610: 
611:     // Body trace: heart glyph container, pulse figure, step count, carried
612:     // supply ticks. All optional; text/attributes only change when the
613:     // presented value materially changes.
614:     let body_trace: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "body-trace").ok();
615:     let hud_bpm: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "hud-bpm").ok();
616:     let hud_steps: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "hud-steps").ok();
617:     let supply_water: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "supply-water").ok();
618:     let supply_ration: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "supply-ration").ok();
619:     let last_steps = Rc::new(Cell::new(u64::MAX));
620:     let last_bpm_text = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
621:     let last_signal = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
622:     let last_beat_period_ms = Rc::new(Cell::new(0i32));
623:     let last_supplies = Rc::new(Cell::new((u32::MAX, u32::MAX)));
624: 
625:     // Route anchor near the reticle; hidden whenever no real door is known.
626:     let route_anchor: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "route-anchor").ok();
627:     let route_target_el: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "route-target").ok();
628:     let route_bearing_el: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "route-bearing").ok();
629:     let route_range_el: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "route-range").ok();
630:     let route_visible = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
631:     let last_route_text = Rc::new(RefCell::new(String::new()));
632: 
633:     let death_overlay: Option<HtmlElement> = element(&document, "death-overlay").ok();
634:     let last_deaths = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u32));
635:     let death_shown_at = Rc::new(Cell::new(0.0f64));
636: 
637:     let last_time = Rc::new(Cell::new(0.0f64));
638:     let frame_count = Rc::new(Cell::new(0u32));
639:     let hud_window_start = Rc::new(Cell::new(0.0f64));
640:     let was_ready = Rc::new(Cell::new(false));
641: 
642:     // Standard self-referential rAF closure pattern.
643:     let raf_handle: Rc<RefCell<Option<Closure<dyn FnMut(f64)>>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(None));
644:     let raf_handle_clone = raf_handle.clone();
645: 
646:     let loop_window = window.clone();
647:     *raf_handle.borrow_mut() = Some(Closure::new(move |time_ms: f64| {
648:         let dt = if last_time.get() > 0.0 {
649:             ((time_ms - last_time.get()) / 1000.0) as f32
650:         } else {
651:             1.0 / 60.0
652:         };
653:         last_time.set(time_ms);
654: 
655:         // Adaptive resolution: size the backing store to
656:         // window * governor scale * renderer base factor. A non-zero
657:         // user override (settings menu) replaces the governor scale.
658:         {
659:             let scale = effective_resolution_scale(
660:                 &renderer.borrow(),
661:                 engine.borrow().stats().resolution_scale,
662:             );
663:             let target_w = (loop_window
664:                 .inner_width()
665:                 .ok()
666:                 .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())
667:                 .unwrap_or(800.0)
668:                 * scale)
669:                 .max(1.0) as u32;
670:             let target_h = (loop_window
671:                 .inner_height()
672:                 .ok()
673:                 .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())
674:                 .unwrap_or(600.0)
675:                 * scale)
676:                 .max(1.0) as u32;
677: 
678:             if canvas.width() != target_w || canvas.height() != target_h {
679:                 canvas.set_width(target_w);
680:                 canvas.set_height(target_h);
681:                 renderer.borrow_mut().resize(target_w, target_h);
682:             }
683:         }
684: 
685:         let frame_input = input.borrow_mut().take_frame();
686:         engine.borrow_mut().tick(dt, &frame_input);
687: 
688:         // Loading overlay: flip to "click to play" once the spawn chunk is in.
689:         let stats = engine.borrow().stats();
690:         if stats.ready && !was_ready.get() {
691:             was_ready.set(true);
692:             let _ = status_msg.style().set_property("display", "none");
693:             let _ = play_msg.style().set_property("display", "block");
694:         }
695: 
696:         // HUD refresh at a fixed frame cadence.
697:         frame_count.set(frame_count.get() + 1);
698:         if frame_count.get() % HUD_INTERVAL == 0 {
699:             let elapsed = (time_ms - hud_window_start.get()) / 1000.0;
700:             hud_window_start.set(time_ms);
701:             // Engine channels live inside the diagnostic aperture but stay
702:             // current even while it is closed.
703:             if elapsed > 0.0 {
704:                 let fps = (HUD_INTERVAL as f64 / elapsed).round();
705:                 hud_fps.set_text_content(Some(&fps.to_string()));
706:             }
707:             hud_chunks.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
708:                 "{}/{}",
709:                 stats.fine_chunks, stats.resident_chunks
710:             )));
711:             hud_nodes.set_text_content(Some(&stats.atlas_nodes.to_string()));
712:             let effective_scale =
713:                 effective_resolution_scale(&renderer.borrow(), stats.resolution_scale);
714:             hud_scale.set_text_content(Some(&format!("{:.0}%", effective_scale * 100.0)));
715:             let cpu_telemetry = renderer.borrow().cpu_telemetry_string();
716:             if let Some(text) = cpu_telemetry {
717:                 hud_gpu.set_text_content(Some(&text));
718:             } else {
719:                 hud_gpu.set_text_content(Some(renderer.borrow().backend_label()));
720:             }
721: 
722:             // Top-right section readout ("LEVEL 0 · MAIN CORRIDOR · ...").
723:             // The locator caches its region plan, so this is cheap except on
724:             // a region crossing; only touch the DOM when the text changes.
725:             if let Some(hud_section) = &hud_section {
726:                 let (level, pos) = {
727:                     let engine_ref = engine.borrow();
728:                     (engine_ref.level(), engine_ref.player().position)
729:                 };
730:                 let text = locator.borrow_mut().describe(level, pos[0], pos[2]);
731:                 let mut last = last_section_text.borrow_mut();
732:                 if *last != text {
733:                     hud_section.set_text_content(Some(&text));
734:                     *last = text;
735:                 }
736:             }
737: 
738:             // Accessibility switch is a page-level preference; forward it to
739:             // the engine on the same bounded cadence as everything else.
740:             engine.borrow_mut().set_assisted_consumption(
741:                 crate::ASSISTED_CONSUMPTION.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
742:             );
743: 
744:             // Body trace: the beat is driven entirely by CSS (period and
745:             // amplitude custom properties), so the DOM is only touched when
746:             // a presented value materially changes.
747:             let body = stats.body;
748:             if let Some(trace) = &body_trace {
749:                 let signal = match body.signal {
750:                     crate::application::body::PulseSignal::Quiet => "quiet",
751:                     crate::application::body::PulseSignal::Active => "active",
752:                     crate::application::body::PulseSignal::Strained => "strained",
753:                     crate::application::body::PulseSignal::Critical => "critical",
754:                 };
755:                 if *last_signal.borrow() != signal {
756:                     let _ = trace.set_attribute("data-signal", signal);
757:                     *last_signal.borrow_mut() = signal.to_string();
758:                 }
759:                 let period_ms = (60_000.0 / body.bpm.max(30.0)) as i32;
760:                 // Re-time the animation only on a meaningful shift (~4%).
761:                 if (period_ms - last_beat_period_ms.get()).abs() > period_ms / 25 {
762:                     last_beat_period_ms.set(period_ms);
763:                     let _ = trace
764:                         .style()
765:                         .set_property("--beat-period", &format!("{period_ms}ms"));
766:                     let _ = trace.style().set_property(
767:                         "--beat-amp",
768:                         &format!("{:.2}", body.beat_intensity.clamp(0.0, 1.0)),
769:                     );
770:                 }
771:             }
772:             if let Some(hud_bpm) = &hud_bpm {
773:                 // The figure appears only when the body makes it relevant.
774:                 let text = if body.signal == crate::application::body::PulseSignal::Quiet {
775:                     String::new()
776:                 } else {
777:                     format!("{:.0}", body.bpm)
778:                 };
779:                 let mut last = last_bpm_text.borrow_mut();
780:                 if *last != text {
781:                     hud_bpm.set_text_content(Some(&text));
782:                     *last = text;
783:                 }
784:             }
785:             if let Some(hud_steps) = &hud_steps {
786:                 if last_steps.get() != body.steps {
787:                     last_steps.set(body.steps);
788:                     hud_steps.set_text_content(Some(&body.steps.to_string()));
789:                 }
790:             }
791:             // Carried supplies as discrete ticks, never numeric meters.
792:             if last_supplies.get() != (stats.almond_bottles, stats.rations) {
793:                 last_supplies.set((stats.almond_bottles, stats.rations));
794:                 if let Some(el) = &supply_water {
795:                     el.set_text_content(Some(&"▪".repeat(stats.almond_bottles as usize)));
796:                 }
797:                 if let Some(el) = &supply_ration {
798:                     el.set_text_content(Some(&"▪".repeat(stats.rations as usize)));
799:                 }
800:             }
801: 
802:             // Route anchor: shown only while a real resident door is known.
803:             if let Some(anchor) = &route_anchor {
804:                 match stats.route {
805:                     Some(route) => {
806:                         if !route_visible.get() {
807:                             route_visible.set(true);
808:                             let _ = anchor.style().set_property("display", "block");
809:                         }
810:                         let text = format!(
811:                             "{}|{:03}|{:.0}",
812:                             route.target_level, route.bearing_deg, route.range_m
813:                         );
814:                         let mut last = last_route_text.borrow_mut();
815:                         if *last != text {
816:                             *last = text;
817:                             if let Some(el) = &route_target_el {
818:                                 el.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
819:                                     "THRESHOLD / L{}",
820:                                     route.target_level
821:                                 )));
822:                             }
823:                             if let Some(el) = &route_bearing_el {
824:                                 el.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
825:                                     "VECTOR {:03}°",
826:                                     route.bearing_deg
827:                                 )));
828:                             }
829:                             if let Some(el) = &route_range_el {
830:                                 el.set_text_content(Some(&format!("RANGE {:.0} m", route.range_m)));
831:                             }
832:                         }
833:                     }
834:                     None => {
835:                         if route_visible.get() {
836:                             route_visible.set(false);
837:                             last_route_text.borrow_mut().clear();
838:                             let _ = anchor.style().set_property("display", "none");
839:                         }
840:                     }
841:                 }
842:             }
843:             // Death flash: appears on each new death, fades after ~2.5 s.
844:             if let Some(overlay) = &death_overlay {
845:                 if stats.deaths > last_deaths.get() {
846:                     last_deaths.set(stats.deaths);
847:                     death_shown_at.set(time_ms);
848:                     let _ = overlay.set_class_name("shown");
849:                 } else if time_ms - death_shown_at.get() > 2500.0
850:                     && !overlay.class_name().is_empty()
851:                 {
852:                     let _ = overlay.set_class_name("");
853:                 }
854:             }
855: 
856:             // Diagnostic aperture (F3 or the settings switch): the engine's
857:             // sectioned report rendered as structured panels. The section
858:             // split is presentation only; the text itself is authored by
859:             // `Engine::diagnostic_text` and stays natively testable.
860:             if let Some(overlay_el) = &debug_overlay {
861:                 let on = crate::ANOMALY_DEBUG.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
862:                 if on {
863:                     let report = engine.borrow().diagnostic_text();
864:                     overlay_el.set_inner_html(&diagnostic_sections_html(&report));
865:                 }
866:                 if on != debug_overlay_visible.get() {
867:                     debug_overlay_visible.set(on);
868:                     let toggled = diagnostics_shell.as_ref().unwrap_or(overlay_el);
869:                     let _ = toggled
870:                         .style()
871:                         .set_property("display", if on { "block" } else { "none" });
872:                 }
873:             }
874:         }
875: 
876:         // Schedule next frame.
877:         if let Some(closure) = raf_handle_clone.borrow().as_ref() {
878:             let _ = loop_window.request_animation_frame(closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref());
879:         }
880:     }));
881: 
882:     if let Some(closure) = raf_handle.borrow().as_ref() {
883:         window.request_animation_frame(closure.as_ref().unchecked_ref())?;
884:     }
885:     // Keep the closure (and everything it captures) alive forever.
886:     std::mem::forget(raf_handle);
887:     Ok(())
888: }

  49:     pub spawn: [f32; 3],

  51:     /// up looking *down* the main corridor, not at a wall.
  52:     pub spawn_yaw: f32,
  53:     /// Full-resolution chunk loads per tick. 2 balances streaming latency
  54:     /// against frame hitches: one fine chunk costs ~15 ms native (more in
  55:     /// wasm), so higher budgets stall the frame visibly. Coarse loads cost
  56:     /// a fraction of this budget (see `FINE_LOAD_COST`).
  57:     pub max_loads_per_tick: usize,
  58:     /// Screen-space-error proxy: chunks whose nearest point is farther than
  59:     /// this from the player stay at the coarse LOD; nearer chunks refine to
  60:     /// full resolution. A coarse voxel at this distance projects to roughly
  61:     /// the same pixels as a fine voxel at half of it.
  62:     pub fine_distance: f32,
  63:     /// Level to boot into (0 = Backrooms, 34 = grassland). Exposed as the
  64:     /// `?level=` debug query so any level is reachable in any renderer
  65:     /// without waiting on a noclip roll.
  66:     pub initial_level: u32,
  67: }
  68: 
  69: impl Default for EngineConfig {
  70:     fn default() -> Self {
  71:         Self {
  72:             seed: 42,
  73:             chunk_size: 10.0,
  74:             chunk_radius: 1,
  75:             spawn: [5.0, 1.7, 5.0],
  76:             spawn_yaw: 0.0,
  77:             max_loads_per_tick: 2,
  78:             fine_distance: 15.0,
  79:             initial_level: LEVEL_BACKROOMS,
  80:         }
  81:     }
  82: }

  84: /// One frame's worth of user input, already translated to domain terms by
  85: /// the input adapter.
  86: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
  87: pub struct InputFrame {
  88:     pub intent: MoveIntent,
  89:     pub look_dx: f32,
  90:     pub look_dy: f32,
  91:     /// Whether pointer lock is engaged; movement is frozen otherwise.
  92:     pub locked: bool,
  93:     pub flashlight: bool,
  94:     /// Edge-triggered flare drop for this frame (G key / touch button).
  95:     pub drop_flare: bool,
  96:     /// Edge-triggered deliberate drink of one carried almond water (R key /
  97:     /// touch button).
  98:     pub drink: bool,
  99:     /// Edge-triggered deliberate ration meal (T key / touch button).
 100:     pub eat: bool,
 101: }

 103: /// A resolved navigation objective for the route anchor: a real, resident
 104: /// level door. Range is straight-line on the walking plane (there is no
 105: /// route graph, so the presenter labels it RANGE, never PATH).
 106: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 107: pub struct RouteAnchor {
 108:     /// Level id on the far side of the door.
 109:     pub target_level: u32,
 110:     /// Bearing relative to the player's facing, whole degrees 0..=359.
 111:     pub bearing_deg: u16,
 112:     /// Straight-line range, meters.
 113:     pub range_m: f32,
 114: }
